summary: 0-bg grid (h 5-14, w 5-16): row 0 holds color-4 markers on a proper non-empty subset of columns (1..w-2 of them, placement optionally biased left/right/center); rows 1+ hold a body drawn from a palette-kind-controlled set of non-4 colors at a density-controlled rate. Rule: output = body columns under the markers, in order; unmarked columns are dropped.

Bordered (and optionally interior-) walled field of 5s with one color-1 seed and one color-2 seed at even Manhattan separation; rule paints every background cell equidistant (BFS through non-wall cells) from both seeds cyan. Interior walls bend the frontier; seed geometry varies freely across rows and columns.

Separated single-color objects on a 0 background.  Some contain a fully enclosed bbox hole and must be kept; the rest, including leaky C-shaped near-misses, must be erased.  Four scheduled profiles refute frame-only, largest-object, color, and any-bbox-gap shortcuts.
A 0-background grid contains 3-5 halo-separated red polyominoes. All but one are the same free shape under rotation/reflection; output the singleton class as its canonical cyan tight-bbox mask.

Every separated same-color 4-connected object is recolored by exact rectangularity: bbox completely filled -> 4, otherwise -> 1.  Every ordinary scene contains both classes and a missing-corner near miss; non-anchor scenes reuse one non-output input color across both classes so the same input color maps to both 4 and 1, proving input color is irrelevant.

0-bg grid with 2-5 grown-blob objects of strictly distinct sizes; the largest (sometimes only by ONE cell) is kept and recolored 8, the rest are erased. Colors vary freely, may repeat across objects, and a small object may itself be cyan as a red herring.
Any colored grid ≥ 2 × 2. Rule outputs the top-left 2 × 2 corner crop verbatim (preserving colors). Everything else is discarded.

skills: multi-template inputs, selector metadata, conditional search
summary: Four color-9-separated panels contain template A, template B, a selector, and a search board. Selector color 2 chooses A; any other selector color chooses B. Crop the chosen template, match its nonzero cells in the board in the original orientation and exact colors (crop zeros are wildcards), then recolor the union of all matching template cells to 8.

Two to four separated color-2 motifs and a color-1 mask teach the full canonical selector precedence: square-growth overlap, then Manhattan distance, then top-left scan order.  The selected original motif is cropped and recolored 8.

bg=7; infer each colored full H/V/main-diagonal/anti-diagonal line, count the cells hidden by other colored lines, then emit the colors as one row sorted by (hidden-cell count, color value) descending. Ordinary lessons schedule crossings, diagonals, equal-depth tie breaks, and 5/6-line piles.

Row 0 is a sparse per-column legend. It clears in the output. Every non-zero body cell takes the row-0 value at its own column, including 0 when no legend is present there. A linked four-example curriculum separates body-color evidence from erasure evidence and duplicates the comprehensive erasure case for rotation-safe lessons.

3 panels split by full-height color-9 columns: a | b | query, where b = T(a) for T in {rot-cw, rot-180, rot-ccw, flip-lr, flip-ud, none} (rotations use square panels; a is asymmetric enough that T is the rule's first matching branch). Rule applies the same T to the query panel and emits the result.

0-bg grid with one red(2) start, one green(3) goal, color-5 walls forming straight / single-gap / staggered-double-gap layouts; rule marks cyan(8) exactly the bg cells lying on EVERY shortest 4-connected path (verified non-empty, with partially- shared cells present and unmarked on pinch boards).
Dense canonical 7/6 field; the rule recolors every magenta(6) cell to red(2).

0-bg grid with N (1-4) multicolor 2×2 shapes, each composed of 3 body-color cells and 1 special-color cell at one of the 2×2 corners (TL/TR/BL/BR). Each shape's special color is unique. For each shape, a matching singleton in the special color sits elsewhere on the grid. Rule: for each shape, identify which corner is the special. Compute the diagonally OPPOSITE corner and use it as the shape's 'anchor'. Move the whole shape so this anchor lands at the singleton marker. The shape is erased at its original position and redrawn at the new position. Markers and bg cells are unaffected except where the moved shape now lands.

Red(2) markers aligned horizontally or vertically are joined with cyan(8) only when the entire inclusive segment contains black plus exactly those two reds. Constructive h-chain, v-chain, and cross profiles also include a blocked pair and an isolated red to refute canonical-fitting shortcuts.

A 0-background grid contains one singleton marker and 2-4 distinct-color sparse polyominoes. Select the smallest polyomino, breaking size ties by bbox top then left; crop it, upscale 2x, and recolor nonzero cells to the marker color. A four-example schedule exposes unique minima and tied minima.

0-bg grid with one green(3) grown polyomino (5-10 cells) and one gray(5) connected subset of it placed elsewhere (plus optional non-{3,5} decor the rule ignores); rule outputs the normalized set difference green-minus-gray, bbox-cropped, in green.
Two 2-cells (plus optional non-2 decor the rule wipes); rule paints their full rows+cols in 2, fills the bbox interior with 1, and zeroes everything else — output depends ONLY on the two dots.

0-bg grid with 1-3 grown polyominoes (distinct colors, bbox-separated), at least one having a bbox >= 3x3 with an occupied interior cell; rule draws each shape's bbox OUTLINE in its color on a fresh canvas (interiors empty — not a solid fill).

Two to nine separated nonzero objects are sorted by leftmost column and recolored with a right-anchored 2/8 alternation: the rightmost object is 8, its left neighbor 2, and so on. Default lessons mix exact canonical 2x2/color-2 profiles with shape and source-color counterexamples.

Find every 8-connected motif made of two equal NxN color-3 blocks in opposite quadrants. Paint equal NxN color-8 blocks just outside the two empty corners, on the perpendicular diagonal; clip only cells that fall outside the board. All motifs are processed.

Count blue markers in row 0, then retain only the nonblue, non-row-0 object with matching area and recolor it cyan. Alternating canonical and combined-counterexample profiles teach the row-only count and both object exclusions while varying blob geometry, order, size rank, and palette.

Two same-interior hollow frames in colors from {6,7} at varied positions/arrangements; one holds a random motif (colors 4/5/8/9, optionally with 6/7 hole cells the copy drops), the other is empty; a key cell (1=flip-lr, 2=flip-ud, 3=rot-180, absent=copy) sits on the background. Rule: repaint frames on a blank canvas and place the transformed motif in the empty frame.

Column 0 supplies an independent color header for each row. Nonzero payload cells in a headered row take that header color; payload in a headerless row keeps its own color. Default draws contain visible mismatches in every header row plus a retained headerless payload.

Row 0 contains an ordered sequence of transform codes: 1=flip-lr, 2=flip-ud, 3=rotate-cw, 4=rotate-180. Crop the non-zero body in rows 1+ and execute every command from left to right. Body colors, including 1..4, are payload rather than extra commands.
Complete an equal-color diagonal pair into its enclosing 2x2 block only when both missing corners are zero. Blocked diagonals, axis-aligned equal pairs, and unequal-color diagonals remain unchanged.

Color-5 perimeter and divider walls partition the input into chambers. Every 4-connected non-wall chamber has exactly one colored seed, and the output floods the whole chamber with that seed color. Scheduled divider gaps merge neighboring rectangles and make connectivity observable.

A cropped template in colors 6-9 is erased from the scene and copied at isolated command cells colored 1-5.  The command chooses identity, 90° clockwise, 180°, 90° counter-clockwise, or left-right reflection; the transformed template is placed top-left at the command, with transparent zeros and boundary clipping.

8-walled grid (border + 1-2 dividers, optional gaps) with rooms holding one seed color each — sometimes several seeds of that color, sometimes a two-color room that stays unfilled, sometimes an empty room; rule floods each room with its unique seed color.

0-bg grid (h~4-7, w~3-6) with: (a) TOP ROW (row 0): 2-4 TRANSFORM CODE CELLS at random distinct columns, each painted with a value from {1, 2, 3, 4} encoding (1=identity, 2=rotate-CW 90°, 3=rotate 180°, 4=flip-UD). Other top-row cells are 0; (b) ROWS 1..h-1: MOTIF with 3-N scattered non-0 cells (where N is roughly (h-1)*w//2) — usually red, sometimes another color or 2-color mixed, at random distinct positions. The motif is asymmetric so each transform produces a distinct output. Rule (APPLY EACH CODE'S TRANSFORM TO THE MOTIF, OUTPUT SIDE-BY-SIDE): extract the MOTIF (non-0 cells in rows 1..h-1, all color 2), CROP to its bbox. read the TOP-ROW CODES in left-to-right column order. For EACH code C: APPLY the corresponding TRANSFORM to the cropped motif: 1=identity (no change), 2=rot-CW 90°, 3=rot 180°, 4=flip-UD. PRODUCE an OUTPUT where the transformed motifs are STACKED LEFT-TO-RIGHT in the order their codes appeared on the top row, separated by single bg-0 columns. Net: each transform code spawns one transformed copy of the motif in the output gallery.
Row 0 holds an N-color legend at scattered columns (order = column order); below, orange(7) blobs of sizes 1..N are recolored to legend[size-1], while non-7 decor blobs stay unchanged.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~4-6) with 1-3 selected COLUMNS, each containing exactly 2 cells of the SAME non-zero color placed at DIFFERENT rows (separated by ≥2 empty rows); columns may SHARE a color, and near-miss content (mixed-color columns, 3-cell columns, horizontal pairs) stays unconnected. Rule: for each non-empty column, find the two same-color endpoint cells and CONNECT them by drawing a VERTICAL LINE of that column's color through every cell between them (inclusive of endpoints). Net: input has pairs of dots in each non-empty column; output has those dots replaced by solid vertical color segments spanning between the endpoints.

A 0-background grid contains one or two non-zero colors, exactly two anchors per color, with distinct rows and columns. In ascending numeric color order, each color fills still-zero cells in its anchor bounding box; lower colors keep contested overlap cells.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-16) with 1-3 small RECTANGULAR OBJECTS (1×1 up to ~h/4 × w/4) painted in distinct non-zero colors from a palette of 2-5 colors. Objects are placed at INTERIOR positions with 1-cell margin from the grid edges and from each other, so the non-bg content's bbox is strictly smaller than the input grid (the grid is padded with bg). Rule: COMPUTE the BOUNDING BOX of all NON-BG cells (rmin..rmax × cmin..cmax). CROP the grid to exactly that bbox — output is the rectangular subgrid containing only the content, with all bg padding outside the bbox stripped away. Net: input is padded; output is the tight bbox crop of the content (smaller dimensions).

0-bg grid with 2-3 red(2) emitters and 1-2 gray(5) wall segments. Rule: each emitter casts 4 cardinal cyan(8) rays over 0-cells, stopping at ORIGINAL non-zero cells (walls, other emitters) or the edge — rays pass freely THROUGH other rays' painted cells (the stop test reads the input, not the output). Emitters and walls preserved.

Largest magenta/orange components define equal square templates. An independently placed 1..8 index rectangle selects and rotates them; zero slots stay blank. Canonical symmetric and dense asymmetric shapes, 2/3-cell tile sizes, internal gaps, and exterior 9-decor are supported.

0-bg grid with one control cell (2=identity 4=cw90 5=180 6=ccw90), one maroon(9) anchor, the SMALLEST green(3) object (3-4 cells, rotation-asymmetric) and 1-2 larger green distractors. Rule: rotate the smallest green per the control and stamp it in CYAN(8) with its normalized origin at the anchor — ONTO the input (everything else, distractors included, stays).

Place one blue anchor and a uniquely largest solid rectangle or non-rectangular blob, optionally with one smaller decoy. The oracle returns only the largest object's boundary translated so its bbox top-left is the anchor, with edge clipping.

Grid split by a single full color-5 column into 2 panels. Each panel holds a non-zero compact object pattern in some non-bg, non-5 color. Rule: extract left panel and right panel (as subgrids). Normalize each: crop to bbox of non-zero cells, then convert to binary mask. Take XOR of the two binary masks (aligned at (0,0), padded by 0 where dims differ). Output is the bbox-sized XOR with 7 wherever the masks differ, 0 wherever they match.

0-bg grid (h~6-10, w~10-14) with: (a) a 4-conn SHAPE of color 1 (blue), 2-5 cells; (b) exactly ONE color-2 (red) single-cell MARKER 'a'; (c) exactly ONE color-3 (green) single-cell MARKER 'b'. The translated shape stays in-bounds and doesn't overlap existing non-bg cells. Rule: compute delta = (b_row - a_row, b_col - a_col). For every color-1 cell (r, c), paint output[r+dr][c+dc] = 4 (yellow). Original color-1 cells, the red marker, and the green marker stay in place. Net: a color-4 copy of the blue shape appears translated by the red→green vector.

0-bg N x (3N+2) grid: three square N x N panels A | B | C split by two full-height blue(1) divider columns. B = t(A) for t in {1=id 2=cw 3=180 4=transpose 5=flip-lr 6=flip-ud}; C holds an independent shape. Rule: crop each panel to content, find the FIRST t (in 1..6 order) with t(crop A) == crop B, and output t(crop C) — a small cropped grid, NOT the 3-panel layout.
Extend each red-rectangle row and column outward in every unblocked direction; aligned nonzero non-red markers block one direction only.
One to eight independent gray-red-black-red rays lie on a color-7 field. For every ray, the red tail beyond its black pivot rotates perpendicular toward the grid center while retaining its length.

0-bg grid with 1-3 hollow color-2 (red) rectangular FRAMES, each with ODD height and ODD width (so integer center exists). Frames are separated (≥1-cell buffer). Optionally 1-2 decoy cells in other colors (color 5 etc.) that the rule preserves but ignores. Rule: for each color-2 4-connected component, check if it's a hollow rectangle outline with odd dimensions. If yes, set its center cell to color 8. Otherwise leave.

A zero-background grid has one blue source anchor, one or two red anchors, and a multicolour payload. Use the last red in row-major order as the destination, copy each payload offset from blue to that red on a fresh canvas, preserve payload colours, and clip translated cells at the edge.
Full-height col of 9s; left side has 1-3 small shapes; rule mirrors every left cell to the right.

Scattered colored cells (sometimes a color repeats, sometimes a marker is a small 2-3 cell blob). Rule emits a 1xN row of the DISTINCT colors in column-major scan order — a repeated color is listed once, at its first (leftmost, then topmost) occurrence.
In every row with exactly two 8s, paint the empty integer midpoint red(2); odd-distance pairs, three-8 rows, and occupied midpoints remain unchanged.

A connected 4-6 cell template containing one or more 9s and 1-5 singleton 9 markers.  Align the template's last BFS-visited 9 to every marker and render copy coverage on a blank canvas: 1->2, 2->3, 3+->4.  A four-slot teaching schedule anchors canonical scale, then supplies repeated overlap and anchor-selection witnesses plus body-color variation.
Crop the template left of a maroon divider, scan the right board without rotations, and fill the sole missing required cell of every exact one-hole placement.
skills: near-match detection, local repair, exact template completion

summary: A row-major first nonzero seed controls a parity-striped color-4 canopy and drops one row. Alternating later-decoy witnesses make every three-demo rotation refute the canonical-fitting last-nonzero shortcut.

0-bg grid with k magenta(6) markers scattered anywhere (k=0-2) and 3 green objects of 0/1/2 enclosed holes in varied sizes; rule recolors the green object with exactly k holes to orange. k=0 selects the solid object; no-match boards stay unchanged.
Binary two-color complement with a color map: 3→1, 5→4, 8→2, and every other nonzero color maps to itself.

One connected non-0/non-9 template and 1-8 colour-9 anchors.  Start from a blank grid and stamp the template, without rotation or recolouring, at every anchor using the anchor as the template bounding-box top-left.  Erase the source template and all anchors.  Edge examples fit exactly; ordinary examples never rely on out-of-bounds clipping.

Copy every input row into a zero canvas of width w+h-1. Row r begins at column h-1-r, so the bottom row stays at the left edge, the top row moves farthest right, and adjacent rows form a one-column staircase.

A zero-background grid contains two or three separated solid green(3) rectangles. Each rectangle has exactly one red(2) non-corner rim cell. For every red marker independently, project a red centre ray away from its rectangle to the grid edge and paint green side wings whose half-width equals the distance from the marker to the opposite rectangle edge.

Center the full nonzero bounding box on the original zero canvas using floor margins. Mix canonical profiles, broad connected/scattered shapes, and redundant skewed disconnected witnesses against mass, fixed-width, gap-removal and component shortcuts. Exact 6..14 dimensions and 3..8 cells.

0-bg grid with 2-3 isolated components in distinct colors: one LADDER shape with k=2-3 enclosed chambers (varied dims and orientation) plus 1-2 distractors (1-hole rings of varied size, solids); rule crops the component with the most ENCLOSED 0-REGIONS. (Old doc said 'bg cells inside bbox' — the rule counts enclosed REGIONS; and the old shape bank had exactly 2 fixed winners, capping uniq_out at ~13.)

Three horizontal hollow color-1 frames contain monochrome motifs. Classify each binary-cropped motif as asymmetric, left/right-only, up/down-only, or symmetric on both axes; output their 3x3 class-equality matrix using 2 for equal and 0 for unequal.

Three or four separated yellow objects occupy independent corner regions. All but one share a D4-canonical polyomino shape; recolor the unique shape to cyan. A deterministic three-phase size schedule refutes the plausible largest-object shortcut in every ordinary lesson.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 5-7, w ∈ 7-9) with: N ∈ 1-2 ISOLATED NON-BG SEED CELLS, each in a color drawn at random from {2..9}, placed at random positions with MANHATTAN-DISTANCE >4 between any pair (so their radius-2 diamonds don't overlap). Rule (FOR EACH NON-BG SEED CELL AT (R0, C0) WITH COLOR k, PAINT EVERY CELL (R, C) WITHIN MANHATTAN DISTANCE 2 WITH COLOR k — A 13-CELL DIAMOND): For EACH non-bg cell at (r0, c0) with color k: For EVERY (r, c) WHERE |r-r0| + |c-c0| ≤ 2 (in-bounds): PAINT g[r][c] = k. The seed cell itself stays k; the 4 cells at distance 1 (cardinal neighbors) get k; the 8 cells at distance 2 (longer diagonals + outer cardinals) get k. Out-of-bounds cells drop. Net: each seed becomes a 13-cell colored diamond (rhombus); the rest of the grid stays 0.

Separated X-corner motifs (4 equal diagonal corners around an empty center, which the rule fills) plus optional near-miss motifs the rule must skip: 3-corner Xs, mismatched-color Xs, and Xs whose center is already occupied.

0-bg grid with 1-3 grown blobs in distinct colors at VARIED arrangements (either diagonal, horizontal/vertical pairs, or an off-center cluster), sometimes touching a border; rule crops to the bbox of all non-zero cells. (Was: always exactly TL+BR diagonal — the arrangement could be mistaken for the rule.)

0-bg grid with 1-3 magenta(6) dominoes at random positions/orientations plus near-misses the rule must skip: longer 6-lines, single 6-cells, OTHER-color dominoes, and diagonal 6-pairs (two size-1 objects under 4-connectivity). Rule recolors exactly the size-2 color-6 components to orange(7).

0-background grids with one full-width maroon(9) guide row and 2-4 distinct-color polyominoes on both sides.  The output is a fresh canvas containing the guide plus every object reflected across that row; source objects disappear and off-board reflected cells are clipped.

0-bg grid with 4-5 non-touching motifs (distinct colors, sizes 3-6 mostly distinct); rule sorts objects by size DESC (bbox-area tiebreak), takes the TOP FOUR, crops each, and packs them into a 2x2 gallery with 1-cell gutters (biggest top-left). A 5th motif is silently dropped. (Old doc claimed a 'vertical pack'; the old generator emitted 2-3 motif boards which CRASH the rule at (fourth shapes) — 15/24 smoke rejections.)

SAME-COLOR crosses: a horizontal and a vertical line of one color crossing (the crossing cell joins a row-run >=3 AND a col-run >=3 of that color, so the rule paints it 8). Decoy content — different-color crossings (the runs break at the crossing) and non-crossing lines — yields no 8. (The OLD generator gave every line a distinct color and skipped occupied cells, so the rule NEVER fired: every output was an all-zero grid.)
Four to seven monochromatic objects are recolored solely by the number of grid borders touched: 0=blue(1), 1=red(2), 2=green(3), 3+=yellow(4).

Exactly three colored dots: a strictly-farthest pair (either diagonal, vertical, or horizontal — even deltas, integer midpoint) plus a third dot anywhere nearer to both endpoints. Rule paints the farthest pair's midpoint gray(5) and one-step colored spokes from it toward each dot. (Old layout was always the same NW-SE pair + west dot.)

Small grid (h, w ∈ [3, 7]) with 2-6 MARKER CELLS in 1 OR 2 non-{0, 2} colors placed at interior positions via layout (random/cluster/diagonal/scattered/blob/row/column/corners) and position bias (top/bottom/center/spread). Rule (DIAG-SHADOW THEN 3×3 TILE): (i) BUILD a SHADOWED TILE from the input: for EACH (r, c) where g[r][c] == 0, if g[(r+1) % h][(c+1) % w] is NON-ZERO, PAINT (r, c) WITH COLOR 2. Existing non-0 cells stay. (ii) TILE the shadowed input INTO A 3h × 3w OUTPUT by repeating it 3 × 3 times. Net: each empty cell with a diagonal-neighbor non-zero becomes 2; then the whole tile repeats 3 × 3.

On fixed background 0, recolor each same-color four-connected component to 2 when it touches any grid edge, otherwise to 8. Input colors 1..9, including 2 and 8, are legal. Different-color contacts and same-color diagonal contacts do not join components. Every production input has at least one border component and one strictly interior component.
Multi-color blobs on bg=0; rule recolors by border-touching status.

Read key 1 or 2 from (0,0), then erase that cell. Find exactly two single-color 4-connected objects and sort them by bounding box in the canonical order: top row, bottom row, left column, right column. Crop each object tightly and align the two crops at their top-left corners. Overlay them on the smallest common canvas: key 1 makes the first sorted object win overlap cells, while key 2 makes the second object win.

0-bg grid (h, w~12-18) with ≥2 GREEN(3) RECTANGULAR COMPONENTS: (a) ≥1 BORDER-TOUCHING GREEN — a solid 3-color rectangle (h~2-4, w~2-4) anchored to one of the 4 grid edges (top/bottom/left/right); (b) ≥1 INTERIOR GREEN — a solid 3-color rectangle placed in the interior (margin ≥1 from every edge) at a non-overlapping position. Rule (RECOLOR BORDER-TOUCHING GREENS, KEEP INTERIOR GREENS): Find all 4-CONNECTED COMPONENTS of color 3. For EACH component: if ANY cell is on the OUTER BORDER (row 0, row h-1, col 0, col w-1), RECOLOR every cell of that component to a different color (puzzle-specific). Else (fully interior), keep at 3. Net: border-anchored greens get a new color; interior greens stay green.
The uniquely smallest GREEN component is recolored magenta; decoy boards also carry an even-smaller NON-green object the rule must ignore (only greens compete).

Build a 23x23 black scene with two or three separated cyan components whose bounding boxes follow the demonstrated size grammar. Components cycle among solid rectangles, one-hole rectangles, and one-notch rectangles. Repaint only cyan cells: inset center yellow; outer top-left magenta, top-right blue, bottom-left red, and bottom-right green.

0-bg grid with N (2-5) pairs of same-color cells positioned on a DIAGONAL 2-step apart (one cell at (r, c) and another at (r±2, c±2), with the (r±1, c±1) midpoint being 0). Pairs use distinct colors and are separated (1-cell buffer) so the rule's diagonal-midpoint test doesn't accidentally fire on other cell triples. Rule: scan every cell. If g[r][c] == g[r+2][c+2] (non-zero) AND g[r+1][c+1] == 0, set g[r+1][c+1] = g[r][c]. Same for anti-diagonal: g[r][c] == g[r+2][c-2] non-zero AND g[r+1][c-1] == 0 → fill.

The bounding box of color 8 defines a region; the 8s may be a full ring or only its four corners. Every non-zero, non-8 interior cell is a seed. Fill each interior cell with the Manhattan-nearest seed color. If nearest seeds have different colors, leave 0; if they share one color, fill it.

A modal black field contains four structured cells of one target color and two dense distractor colors. Rows and columns containing exactly two target cells become full target-colored lines; for a four-corner rectangle, only the longer rectangle axis is extended.

A compact connected prototype contains exactly one color-8 anchor. One or two isolated 8 markers are destinations.  Copy every occupied prototype cell to each destination using anchor-relative offsets; cells whose translated coordinates fall outside the grid are clipped.  The three-example schedule always includes clipping, a non-top-left anchor, multiple targets, and a multicolor prototype across each sliding window.

Three or four separated, single-color objects have distinct cell counts. The oracle crops them and packs them left-to-right by increasing cell count with one zero gutter. A four-sample schedule preserves exact canonical linked profiles, ranges across free polyominoes through size six, and uses a dedicated size-nine branch to guarantee counterexamples to scan-, color-, bounding-box-, max-span-, boundary-perimeter-, adjacency-edge-, boundary-cell-, descending-size-, and finite-template ordering.

Canonical-size color-8 wall lattices contain empty, one-color, repeated-marker, and two-color regions.  A deterministic three-profile teaching cycle additionally punches one wall so a non-rectangular merged region must be judged by its combined palette, not by marker count or shape.

Draw a square color-8 field with one centered full color-1 row, column, or diagonal. Place two structured object colors wholly on one side: a uniquely least-frequent rare color and a larger decoy. Copy every rare cell across the guide while preserving its source and all decoy cells. Four profiles preserve the complete public linked forms; one profile builds diverse related polyomino scenes.

0-bg grid with 1-3 solid color-6 rectangles (3-6 x 3-6) that get their interiors erased to 0 (borders stay 6), alongside near-miss decoys the rule skips: notched 6-shapes (size != bbox area), thin 2-row/2-col solid 6 rects (empty interior, unchanged), and solid rects in other colors. (Was: 3-4 x 3-5 rects only, solidity check never refuted, plus a fixed green marker at (h-1,0) every board.)

Largest {2,4}-colored blob is the template; every cell colored 6-9 is an anchor. Output is a BLANK grid with the normalized template stamped at each anchor cell (bbox top-left on the anchor) in the anchor's color; out-of-bounds stamp cells clip. (Was: 5 fixed 3-4 cell templates always in the top-left corner, largest-blob selection never contested, no clipping, and two degenerates that CRASH the rule.)

Two panels split by a full color-9 column: left panel holds a small colored template, right panel is a search board with 1-3 D4-transformed exact-color copies plus decoy clutter. Output marks every matched cell with 8 on a board-sized canvas. (Was: 4-7 independent random motif panels — the rule only reads the first two, so 19/20 outputs were blank; all 3 degenerates crashed the rule.)
skills: reflection handling, rotation handling, union of transformed matches

summary: Reduce each solid same-color 4-connected component to its distinct bbox corners; discard non-solid components. Four scheduled demos distinguish solidity, component-vs-color grouping, 4-vs-8 connectivity, and thin/dot corner collapse. Rectangle counts and textures are observable and exact.

Preserve the input and the full-height cyan (8) divider. For every non-{0,8} cell strictly left of that divider, copy its color to the same row at column 2*axis-col when in bounds. Sources remain, clipped copies vanish, copied cells overwrite destination content, and off-axis 8-cells are skipped.

One bi-symmetric (H+V mirror) color-1 component is the template; markers in {2,3,4,5} each get a center-aligned stamp of the template recolored to the marker color, on a blank canvas. asym_decoy boards add color-1 components that are NOT bi-symmetric (selection must check BOTH symmetries); clip boards put a marker near the border. (Was: 2 hardcoded templates, no decoys, and a degenerate that crashed the rule.)

On a dense 16x16 background-0 field using every color, enumerate same-color solid rectangles and keep only the unique maximum-area rectangle at its original coordinates. Winner-colored decoys and, in three demonstrated profiles, one attached same-color tab vanish.

A 0-background grid contains 2-4 well-separated, same-color objects. The output clears every object and keeps one cell in its color at floor((r1+r2)/2), floor((c1+c2)/2). Helpful branches include hollow objects whose center was background, repeated object colors, and even bounding-box dimensions. Placement is exact: the realized object count always equals the keyed draw or explicit override.

Copy 1-8 aligned colored source cells onto the near edge of a solid cyan line or rectangle, keeping sources and ignoring optional diagonal decoys. Exact geometry/count controls; repeated colors and interior sources; four-example lessons distinguish eight executable rivals.

First uniformly-colored full row is the mirror axis; every non-zero cell ABOVE it is copy-reflected to (2*guide - r, c) (sources stay, out-of-bounds reflections vanish, destinations get over-written). Cells below the guide are preserved but never reflected. (Was: guide always mid-grid with full room, nothing below it, guide colors only {5,6,8}, no second uniform row, and a degenerate that crashed the rule.)
Every 8-connected nonzero object grows a clipped green bbox halo of thickness max(bbox side)//2 and a blue vertical stem below that halo.

2-4 isolated components sorted by (hole_count desc, area desc, color asc) and packed left-to-right, top-aligned, with one blank column between crops. Tie textures force the area and color tie-breaks to matter.

Every non-zero cell grows a 3x3 Chebyshev neighborhood, clipped at the borders; the output is the UNION of all neighborhoods painted UNIFORMLY in color 8 on a blank canvas — seed colors are irrelevant and do NOT survive. (Old doc claimed each seed grows in its own color with overlap tie-breaks: fiction. Seeds were also always colors 4/5/6 and always isolated cells.)

Use the connected color-2 object as a bbox-top-left-anchored template. On a blank same-size canvas, stamp it at every color-3..9 marker in the marker color; higher marker colors win overlaps and edge cells clip. Nine-pair, eight-demonstration lessons keep one canonical-style plain pair and duplicate each shortcut-breaking profile, making every held-out query rotation identifiable against the declared competitors; every scene also includes a marker color 6..9 to teach the full marker palette.

Five panels separated by gray columns encode p1 op p2 = p3 for exactly one of union, intersection, or xor; apply that operation to p4 and p5. The sampler schedules every operation twice per six draws, guarantees distinct candidate outputs on both the demonstration and query, and anchors every difficulty band at the canonical 4x24 three-color profile.

Color-6 template + ctrl cell (3 identity / 4 rot90 / 7 reflect-h / 8 reflect-v) + markers 1,2 defining a translation vector; the transformed template is stamped in color 9. All four transforms of every template are pairwise distinct so the control is always inferable. (Was: fixed S-shape at (2,1), ctrl at (0,0), markers in one row so the vector was always horizontal.)

skills: header decoding, panel-wise transforms, voting after alignment
summary: Read the three rotation codes in the first row. Split the remaining input at full color-9 rows into three equal panels, rotate each panel's nonzero occupancy by its code (1=0°, 2=90°, 3=180°, 4=270° clockwise), and output a panel-sized grid whose cells are color 8 exactly where at least two rotated panels are occupied.

Two (or more, ignored) panels split by 9-columns; output is [[onion_depth(p1), onion_depth(p2)]] - depth 1 for thin shapes, 2 for shapes with a fat 3x3 core, 3 for 5x5 cores. Colors merge into one mask (multicolor blobs are ONE component). (Was: 1-3 cell motifs in 4-7 panels - every output was [[1,1]], plus two degenerates that crashed the rule.)
skills: panel parsing, pairwise measurement, reduced symbolic output

summary: Row 0 holds N color-1 count markers; the rule ERASES them (row-0 1s are set to 0 in the output) and recolors EVERY color-3 component of size exactly N to 8. Multiple matches all recolor; 1-cells below row 0 are neither counted nor erased; non-3 blobs are ignored. (Old doc claimed the markers stay - wrong - and the generator never showed multi-match, body 1s, or other-color decoys.)

Cells whose 4 cardinal neighbors share their color produce an X (center + 4 diagonals) on a BLANK canvas; everything else vanishes. The test is cardinal-only, so a solid 3x3 block also fires, and diagonal decor neither breaks a plus nor survives. (Was: perfect pluses only - the cardinal-only check, the vanish behavior, and same-color pairs were never exercised.)

One blob touches exactly TWO grid borders - a corner blob (any of the 4 corners, random grown shape) or a bar spanning top+bottom / left+right - and gets cropped to its bbox. Decoys touch 0, 1, or 3 borders and are ignored; components are color-blind so multicolor targets crop with both colors. (Was: the same 3-cell L at the top-left corner every board - outputs were one 2x2 shape in 8 colors; the 'intrinsic-low' flag was wrong.)

Split at the full gray divider.  Compute (area, enclosed holes, reflection-symmetry class) for the red reference and each right-panel object; crop/recolor the first top-left candidate with the equal triple. The v4 curriculum uses feature twins, one-feature distractors, decisive ties, canonical 10x16/8-color and 11x16/7-color profiles, and exact observable override axes.

Every non-{0,8} border cell fires an inward beam of ITS OWN color (top/bottom borders beam vertically incl. corners, side borders horizontally). Beams stop only at 8-walls, pass THROUGH colored cells without overwriting, and the first writer wins at crossings (vertical seeds trace before horizontal). (Was: all seeds one color, no crossings/pass-throughs/corners exercised.)

Exactly two horizontally separated objects exchange their bounding-box top-left anchors on a blank canvas. Each object keeps its shape, orientation, and color; both translated footprints fit fully and remain disjoint.

Two transform codes (identity/rot90/flip-lr/flip-ud) act on an ASYMMETRIC cyan source; the intersection of the two variants is stamped red at the maroon anchor. (Was: source always PLUS_5 - symmetric under ALL four transforms, so the codes were completely invisible and every output was a full plus stamp; controls/anchor/source at fixed positions; no_source degenerate crashed the rule.)

On a black background, recolor to red exactly the blue 4-connected components that are filled 2x3 or 3x2 rectangles. Preserve blue bars, non-solid six-cell shapes, wrong-size blue solids, and gray shapes. Ordinary lessons stay overwhelmingly on the canonical 11x11/12x12, {0,1,5} manifold and cycle decisive decoy families so the rule cannot collapse to a color-only, count-only, size-only, solidity-only, or shape-only shortcut.

Crop the input to the minimal bounding box containing every color-6 cell. The marker geometry varies between two disconnected diagonal markers, a connected border-L, and a connected interior cross. Small non-6 payloads inside the box must be preserved, while connected non-6 distractors outside the box must disappear.

Normalize the red A-shape and yellow B-shape, compute A minus B in normalized coordinates, and stamp that residue in magenta at the maroon anchor on a blank canvas. The curriculum guarantees partial-overlap, normalized-disjoint, and clipped-stamp counterexamples; empty_diff is an exact boundary override.

Same-color objects; exactly one has a UNIQUE bbox zero-count and is cropped. Shapes mix solids (0), L/S/T pieces (1-2), and rings of several sizes (1-6), so the unique object - and the output dims - vary; the duplicate-count pair can be two DIFFERENT shapes with equal counts. (Was: always two 2x2 solids + one 3x3 ring - output was always a 3x3 ring crop; all_same crashed the rule.)

Count every red (2) cell, independent of position or connectivity, and output one row of exactly that many red cells.  A three-example lesson always includes isolated reds, ignored non-red decoys, and one connected red blob, so neither nonzero-count nor object-count shortcuts fit.

Panels split by 9-columns, each holding a 2-point pair (row / col / diagonal aligned); the majority orientation wins and its longest span is drawn in 8 on a cropped canvas. extra_points panels carry a third point the rule ignores. (Was: random motif scatter with no panels at all - the rule degenerated to the span between two scan-adjacent points.)

The nonzero top-row colours select body objects in header order. The first row-major object of each colour is cropped to its bbox and packed left-to-right with one zero column between pieces. Missing header colours are skipped, repeated colours repeat the same crop, and non-header objects are ignored.
Read the common nonzero color on the complete diagonals belonging to each (row + column) modulo-three residue, then fill the grid with those three diagonal stripe colors.

Cell (0,0) holds rank n; objects sort by (size desc, r1, c1) and the n-th is cropped. 3-5 random grown blobs of strictly distinct sizes 2-7 (tie_break boards share a size so r1/c1 decide); blob colors may repeat and may equal n. (Was: the same square/domino/line trio at fixed spots - outputs were 3 shapes in different colors; no_n and n_out_of_range degenerates crashed the rule.)

Row-0 codes (1=identity, 2=rot-cw, 3=flip-lr, 4=rot-180, duplicates allowed) drive a left-to-right gallery of transformed copies of the LARGEST non-{1-4}-colored motif (colors 5-9). Templates are asymmetric so every code is visually distinct; multi_motif boards add a smaller ignored motif; body_code boards drop a 1-4 cell into the body (neither key nor template).

Rows with EXACTLY two reds and an all-zero span between them fill with yellow; rows with 3+ reds, a blocked span (any non-zero cell between), or one red stay untouched, and vertical red pairs do nothing (the rule is row-only). (Was: every red pair was an active clean row - none of the rule's guards were ever contested.)

Two-colour rectangle-corner dots expand into clipped 3x3 blocks; each ring copies the dot's same-row partner and colour-5 guides join aligned dots. A three-profile schedule teaches partner colour, multiple rectangles, and border clipping while preserving canonical shapes and integer outputs.

Three equal sparse panels are separated by two full-height gray columns. At each aligned position, a nonzero color survives exactly when at least two panels agree on that color; otherwise the output is 0. Every generated input covers left+middle, left+right, middle+right, all-three agreement, and a distinct-color disagreement that refutes the canonical-fitting occupancy shortcut.

Nested concentric frame blocks; the rule reads layer colors down the bbox diagonal, dedups, reverses, and remaps the whole component. Blocks are square OR rectangular, even OR odd sized (single-cell center), with optionally REPEATED layer colors (dedup makes the swap asymmetric). (Was: square even-size blocks with all-distinct layers only.)

Colored dots reflect the entire original blue set. A dot uses the first blue in its column if one exists; otherwise it uses the first blue in its row. The blue-dot pair defines the reflection midpoint. Unaligned dots are inert, out-of-bounds reflected cells are clipped, and dots act in row-major order so later colored reflections overwrite earlier ones.

9-walls carve a varied 2x2..3x3 chamber lattice; chambers hold a single marker / a same-color PAIR (still fills - dedup) / two colors (stays) / nothing (stays). gap_wall merges two chambers through a punched divider. Marker colors may repeat across chambers. (Was: always 2x2 chambers, one distinct marker each - the dedup, multi-color, and merge behaviors were unreachable.)

A sparse 0-background grid contains 2..5 nonzero colors. Count all cells of each color globally, combining disconnected components, and output one row of every color sorted by descending total count with ascending color as the tie break. A three-profile schedule exposes distinct totals, an explicit tie, and a largest-component trap.

Find the unique yellow-4 component decorated with colors 1, 2, and 3. For each plain or red-hinted yellow twin, identify the D4 orientation of the base skeleton and stamp the complete blue/red/green decoration in that orientation; decoration cells outside the grid are clipped.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~10-14) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holding a MARKER COLOR from a 3-color palette (the TARGET INDICATOR); (b) EXACTLY ONE TARGET OBJECT of 3-5 cells in the SAME COLOR as the (0, 0) marker, placed at a random interior position; (c) 1-2 DISTRACTOR OBJECTS in OTHER non-target colors (2-3 cells each, non-overlapping). Objects don't touch each other or (0, 0). Rule: READ marker color at (0, 0). FIND the ONE OBJECT (connected component) elsewhere that SHARES that color. CROP to that object's BOUNDING BOX and RETURN the cropped subgrid (preserving its color and shape). Distractors and marker discarded. Net: marker selects target by color; output is bbox crop of matching object.

0-bg grid (h EVEN ~6-8, w~6-9). UPPER HALF (rows 0..h/2-1) contains 3-6 SOURCE MARKER cells scattered at random positions in various non-bg colors. LOWER HALF (rows h/2..h-1) often contains DISTRACTOR rows — each row painted in a single solid color from 1..9 with ~75% probability — that will be OVERWRITTEN by the rule. Rule: COPY the UPPER HALF into the LOWER HALF using a VERTICAL MIRROR — for each cell (r, c) in the upper half (r < h/2), PAINT (h-1-r, c) with the value of (r, c). The distractors in the lower half are OVERWRITTEN. Net: input has an upper-half pattern + random lower-half noise; output is the grid with vertical mirror symmetry about the horizontal midline.

h x w marker grid tiled 3x3; marker rows fill with color 1; MAIN-DIAGONAL neighbors only ((r-1,c-1) and (r+1,c+1), computed in the tiled space so they cross tile boundaries) fill with color 3 — the anti-diagonal stays empty.

Multicolor blobs slide rightward, rightmost-first, with PER-CELL blocking — non-rectangular shapes INTERLOCK when they pack (each cell scans rightward in the output and the object stops at the minimum). (Was: rectangular blocks only, so packing was always bbox-flush and the interlocking semantics never showed.)

A 9 x w grid contains two four-row occupancy panels separated by one uniform nonzero row.  The output is 4 x w and paints color 3 exactly where one panel cell is zero and the corresponding cell in the other panel is nonzero.

Two full cyan rows and two full cyan columns divide a black canvas into a 3-by-3 zone grid. Preserve the cyan dividers and color the cross zones top red, left yellow, center magenta, right green, and bottom blue.
Two large background zones (the top-2 most-frequent colors) plus sparse minority markers; the rule reassigns every marker cell to its nearest zone color, yielding a two-zone partition.

A command cell at (0,0) is 1 or 2. Every other colour occurring exactly twice marks endpoints on distinct rows and columns. Command 1 draws horizontally from the first row-major endpoint and then vertically to the second; command 2 draws vertically first and then horizontally. Colours with any count other than two, and the command colour itself, remain unchanged.

Scattered row-0 blue cells encode k; among 4-connected green body objects, the first row-major object of area k is retained alone and recolored cyan. Same-area non-green objects, body blue cells, and area decoys defeat color/count/location shortcuts.

Colors with EXACTLY two same-column cells and a clean span fill vertically; 3-cell columns, blocked spans (a non-zero cell between, any color), horizontal pairs, and adjacent endpoints all stay untouched. (Was: every pair was an active clean vertical bridge - no guard was ever contested.)
Infer the unique color-aware binary operation demonstrated by A, B, and RESULT, then apply it cellwise to X and Y. Five equal panels are divided by solid gray separator columns.

BEFORE->AFTER demonstrates a shape growth; the same delta stamps onto the QUERY object in the query's color. diff_query boards give the query a DIFFERENT shape (the delta is positional, anchored at bbox mins, not shape-aware); clip boards push the query so grown cells fall off the panel. (Was: random motif scatter - 10/24 smoke boards CRASHED on empty panel slices.)

Place one connected color-1 object and one connected color-2 object on a zero background. Crop and top-left-normalize both objects, then output color 8 exactly on their symmetric difference. Every sample contains a normalized overlap plus exclusive cells from both objects.
Clear rows or columns containing original zeros, preserving every color-2 cell.

3x3 windows with 4 same-color corners, an EMPTY center, and an uncontaminated border complete into rings. partial_border frames (edge cells pre-filled in the frame color) still complete; center_filled / contaminated / three_corners near-misses stay. (Was: perfect 4-corner frames only - guards never contested.)

Row-0 indicator picks the frame color; the interior motif (bbox up to 5x5, padded to >=3x3) is wrapped in two open-cornered frames at fixed canvas spots. thin/single-cell motifs exercise the padding; big 5x5 motifs fill the frame.

Flood from the first red(2) cell in reading order through the 4-connected component of red(2) and gray(5) cells. Recolor every reachable gray cell red; preserve black background, azure(8) walls, and all disconnected gray/red components.

Color-6 shape + control (1 identity / 4 reflect-v / 7 rot180 / 9 reflect-h) + markers 2,3 defining the vector; the transformed shape stamps in 8 onto EMPTY cells only. collide boards overlap the stamp with existing content that survives (no overwrite); clip boards spill off-grid. (Was: fixed shape/control/markers - the vector was always (3,3) and unique_in=20.)

A color-9 cross forms four quadrants. TL->TR is always a worked solid-to-cardinal-outline example. The BL union is outlined and stamped into BR at the same local offset in the BL row-major first color. Solid, multicolor, pre-filled-BR, and clipped variants rebut whole-copy, per-cell/modal-color, empty-target, fixed-size, and must-fit shortcuts. Version 4.1.0 makes the four decisive profiles match the four-demo lesson budget, and adjacent profiles deliberately overlap their causal witnesses so every allowed query rotation remains identifiable. It preserves the mandatory worked analogy, exact 8..20 dimension envelope, and observable axes.

Scattered markers each stamp a plus in their color. edge boards put markers on borders/corners (arms clip); overlap boards put two markers 1-2 apart so the scan-order LATER plus overwrites the earlier one (even its center); same_color repeats a color; dense packs 5-9 markers. (Was: always-interior markers separated by >=4 - clipping and overlap never fired on the main path, and the overlap degenerate mislabeled last-wins as 'ambiguous'.)
Overlay the horizontal reflection; nonzero reflected cells overwrite destinations.

BG-COLOR (bg ∈ {0, 2..4, 6..9}, excluding 1 and 5) grid (h, w ~ 4-18) with: (a) 1..n_dots COLOR-5 (gray) DOT CELLS placed via one of 8 LAYOUTS (random / cluster / row / column / diagonal / scattered / blob / corners) constrained to a POSITION BIAS region (random / top / bottom / center / spread); (b) optional DECOY CELLS in 0..3 non-{bg, 1, 5} colors scattered at low density (0..0.15). All other cells stay bg. Rule (FOR EACH GRAY-5 DOT, KEEP THE DOT AND PAINT COLOR 1 AT ALL ITS 8-NEIGHBORS): for EACH CELL (r, c) in the input: IF v=5, KEEP it as 5 in the output. ELSE: CHECK if ANY of its 8 surrounding neighbors has value 5. IF YES: PAINT (r, c) with COLOR 1. IF NO: SET (r, c) to bg-0. Net: gray dots survive; each dot grows a halo of 1s in its 8-neighborhood; all other cells (including decoys) are zeroed out.

Color 7 is background; the first full non-7 row/column are reflection axes. Off-axis colored cells paint all in-bounds members of their fourfold orbit in original row-major order, so later sources overwrite earlier ones. Scheduled canonical-core inputs reproduce all four canonical shape/palette profiles. Alternating mixed inputs jointly expose multi-quadrant overwrite order, axis-cell exclusion, and independent clipping; every three-demo lesson and every one-query rotation retains a mixed witness.

Rows with a 1-8 marker pair contribute their between-cells; marker columns and 1/8 order vary PER ROW (the extraction is per-row, not columnar). noise boards bury payload rows in dense 0/2 noise like the original task; near_miss boards add rows with only a 1 or only an 8 (skipped); wider_later boards give later rows a wider gap that truncates to the first row's width. (Was: markers frozen at columns 1/pw+2 in every row on a blank background - per-row freedom and noise never exercised.)

Scattered 6s with one-cell gaps fill orange. wide_gap boards show 6-0-0-6 spans that DON'T fill; filled_gap boards put a non-zero cell between 6s (stays); cross boards fill one cell from both directions and chain 6-0-6-0-6; seven_decoy boards carry pre-existing 7s (7-0-7 does NOT fill - only 6 endpoints count). Decoy color blocks survive. (Was: clean isolated pairs only - every near-miss was absent and degenerates frozen.)

Three color-8-separated panels show BEFORE, AFTER, and QUERY. Normalize the first two supports to their own bbox minima, transfer only AFTER's added relative cells to QUERY in the query color, and clip out-of-panel stamps. Every four-demo lesson includes different-query and partial-clip counterexamples to canonical-fitting shortcuts.

Row-0 count of 1s picks a symmetry class (1: LR-sym only, 2: UD-sym only, 3: both, else: neither); first matching component crops to color 8. Shapes are RANDOM per class (was: 4 hardcoded shapes, unique_out=4 - a false intrinsic-low). multi_match boards carry TWO objects of the wanted class (top-left first wins); both_decoy boards add a both-symmetric object that does NOT match a single-symmetry query; scattered_header spreads the 1s across row 0; code0 boards have an empty header (asym pick, bridge-verified).

Small random grid (up to 10×10) with ≥2 distinct colors. Rule: upscale by 3 — each cell becomes a 3×3 block of the same color. Output dimensions are (3H × 3W). Equivalent to output[r][c] = input[r//3][c//3].

A color with exactly one singleton + one blob gets its blob cropped (raw subgrid: intrusion boards put another color's cell INSIDE the bbox and it shows in the output). Markers sit anywhere (was: frozen at the bottom-right corner). near_miss boards carry colors with 2 singletons or 2 blobs (no hit); two_hits boards have two qualifying colors - first in reading order wins.

Color-8 markers identify a vertical or horizontal reflection axis. Every other colored cell mirrors only into background; occupied targets block the write and out-of-bounds reflections clip.  Exact controls cover all declared dimensions, both orientations, and five lawful textures. Every default three-demo window includes an occupied-target witness and an off-center-axis witness.

A full 5-line mirrors the shape; output is the flipped bbox crop in the FIRST cell's color - multicolor boards collapse to one color (bridge-verified). Divider position and shape side are free (was: centered divider, 5 fixed shapes, top/left side only). both_guides boards have a full row AND column of 5s (the row wins: rule checks guide-col #f via the row-first reflection branch).

Rows AND columns with exactly two 1s and a clear gap fill with 2. Vertical pairs and row+column CROSSING spans now appear (was: row pairs only with column reuse banned, so the rule's whole column pass was dead). blocked boards put a decoy-colored cell inside a span (no fill); three_ones lines don't fill; adjacent pairs have nothing between. Decoy colors scatter like the train's 7s.

Top-left selector color + top-right transform code crop the first matching object (rot-cw / rot-180 / flip-lr / identity). multi_candidate boards carry TWO selector-colored objects (top-left bbox order wins); weird_code boards use codes 5-9 (identity); corner_wins boards deliberately set code == sel so the 1-cell code object wins and the output is [[sel]]; symmetric boards make the transform invisible on a symmetric shape. Frames/blobs in other colors are decoys (the rule has no frame logic).

Crop the first 4-connected glyph whose floor bbox center is inside the bbox of all 7 marks. Connected ordinary glyphs and compound teaching boards distinguish containment, overlap, rounding, scan order, color grouping, connectivity, object masking and fixed-ring shortcuts.

Rotate the complete input grid by 180 degrees: cell (r,c) moves to (h-1-r,w-1-c), with dimensions and colors unchanged.  Every ordinary generated input is asymmetric and distinguishes this rule from identity, horizontal/vertical flips, 90/270-degree rotations, and both diagonal reflections.  A fixed four-draw schedule includes two canonical 3x3 anchors plus rectangular and larger-square generalization witnesses.

Row/column labels in colors 1-3; equal-color intersections paint. invalid_mark boards put colors 4-9 in the headers - those are NOT labels and get erased; body_noise boards scatter content that the rebuild wipes; corner_mark boards color (0,0), which is never a label; multi_match boards light a full intersection lattice. (Was: the SAME hardcoded 6-label layout every board - unique_in=8, RED.)

Sparse extrema markers define a colored rectangular frame around a color-2 center; a color-5 cross is drawn through the center and every non-extreme marker is erased.  Scheduled shared-corner, center-on-edge, and ignored-extra-marker examples refute the canonical-fitting shortcuts.

A 2x2 corner key maps the first non-key body marker colour to the four quadrants of the opposite body rectangle. Exact midpoint cells use the bottom/right key entry. A later second body colour, when present, is a distractor and remains unchanged.

Count maximal horizontal runs of 3 and 2 into a 2x3 row-major tally. Canonical-profile canvases vary the background; every default draw contains a multi-row connected run object and two same-color runs in one row, while alternating draws overflow the six-cell tally.

Rows hold 2-4 runs at free positions; only the longest per row survives. tie boards have two equal-longest runs (LEFTMOST wins, promoted from a mislabeled degenerate); touching boards put different-color runs side by side with NO gap (still separate runs - the split is by color change, not by 0s); single boards mix one-run rows (kept) among multi-run rows. (Was: exactly 2 edge-anchored runs per row.)
A 3x3 mini-grid has one empty row and column; the red marker's position in the remaining 2x2 code selects main- versus anti-diagonal 4x4 blocks.

Color-8 rectangular frames receive the first unused loose component whose cropped bbox exactly matches the frame interior; source components remain. A four-example schedule teaches orientation-sensitive size matching, scan-order tie breaking, value-equality one-use, and multicolor preservation.

Two full-height color-5 columns delimit A, B, and C. Crop all three; take the first exact colored transform in the order identity, rotate-cw, rotate-180, transpose, flip-lr, flip-ud that maps A to B, or identity if none matches; apply that code to C. Four scheduled demonstrations expose priority ambiguity, color-sensitive matching, no-match fallback, and a unique ordinary transform.

An 11-row zero-background grid contains a 5-row upper panel, a full uniform nonzero separator at row 5, and an aligned 5-row lower panel. Each panel uses one nonzero color, with the two panel colors and separator color distinct. The 5-row output keeps each upper cell unless the aligned lower cell is nonzero, in which case the lower value overrides it. Every normal generated scene contains upper-only, lower-only, overlapping, and blank aligned positions. No panel row is full, leaving one unique separator.

One object per mask-symmetry class packs into a 2x2 gallery. Shapes are RANDOM per class with varied sizes (was: 4 fixed shapes at 4 fixed spots). duplicate_class boards add a 5th object doubling one class - the LAST in scan order wins (bridge-verified); same_color boards prove colors don't drive the classification.

Components inside 5-frames fall as whole units (deepest-first, stacking on earlier-dropped ones). stack boards drop two blobs in shared columns (the upper lands ON the lower); settled boards mix an already-grounded blob with a floating one; multicolor_blob boards fall as ONE unit (components are color-blind); outside_decoy content never moves; broken_frame outlines (one gap) are NOT chambers - their contents stay frozen.

A->B cellwise pairs recolor panel C. A/B carry small SHAPES (blocks/diagonals like the original, not lone dots). unmapped boards give C a color absent from A (passes through); erase boards map one color to 0 (B empty at that spot); conflict boards repeat an A color with two different B values - the FIRST scan-order pair wins.

Row-0 legend recolors the body 1s; the paint color is the MAX of row 0, so multi_legend boards with several legend cells use the largest (promoted from a mislabeled 'ambiguous' degenerate). body_decoy boards scatter non-1 colors below (erased); row0_one boards put a 1 IN row 0 (erased, not recolored - the rule only recolors rows 1+).

Blob-shaped holes in 5-containers pull in the single-component color of matching shape. multi_decoy boards add a color with TWO components (one even matching the hole shape) that STAYS - only single-component colors are mobile; wrong_shape boards add a mover whose shape matches nothing (stays); two_containers boards run two distinct hole shapes with two movers. (Was: 1x1/1x2 holes only, one container, no near-misses.)

Wide 6-markers mirror the 4-shape up/down; tall or square markers mirror left/right - the marker's ASPECT picks the axis, its position picks the away-direction, and it is ERASED from the output. fallback boards pin the shape to the wall so the away-mirror would clip and the rule mirrors TOWARD the marker instead; decoy boards scatter other colors (erased - output is 4s only); square_marker boards confirm square = left/right.

Grid (h, w~3-14) with INPUT DECORATION drawn from 5 patterns: all_zero/random (40% density)/sparse (15%)/blob (half-grid solid block)/border_decoy (non-8 colored border). Input colors are irrelevant — only h and w matter for the rule. Output uniq_out=39 (intrinsic — h×w combinations only). Rule (EMIT h×w GRID WITH 0-INTERIOR AND 8-BORDER): COMPUTE h and w from input dims. EMIT a FRESH h×w OUTPUT GRID where: BORDER CELLS (row 0, row h-1, col 0, col w-1) = COLOR-8 (cyan); INTERIOR CELLS = 0. Input contents IGNORED. Net: any grid → same-sized hollow 8-frame.

skills: key detection, lookup dispatch, match-driven value retrieval
summary: Five separator-delimited panels encode KEY1->VALUE1 and KEY2->VALUE2. QUERY contains KEY1 (zero cells are wildcards, no rotations) for VALUE1, or contains KEY2 plus an optional KEY1 decoy for VALUE2.

Corner key picks the color; the LARGEST non-corner blob of that color is cropped. size_contest boards carry TWO key blobs (bigger wins, was never contested); tie boards have equal sizes (first in scan order wins); intrusion boards put a foreign cell INSIDE the winner's bbox (raw crop shows it); corner_attached boards extend a BIG key object from (0,0) (excluded entirely - a smaller detached blob wins).

8->9 vector translates everything else; vectors now point in ANY direction (was: always down-right). clip boards push content partially off-grid; multi_shape boards translate several blobs by the same vector; multicolor blobs keep per-cell colors; extra_markers boards add later 8s/9s (only the FIRST of each counts - all are erased).

Each color-matched loose shape teleports to the CENTER of its frame (floor-half offsets); loose shapes are erased from their original spots. two_pairs boards run two frame+shape colors; odd_center boards use even-size interiors with odd-size shapes (floor-half biases up-left); extra_shape boards add a second same-colored loose shape (only the FIRST in scan order is used, but both are erased).

A cyan(8) rectangle emits yellow(4) horizontal and vertical beams. Non-red colored rectangles clip each beam row or column and are restored on top; red(2) rectangles are transparent and are overwritten where a beam crosses them.

Select the largest non-blue object, erase the input, and stamp its normalized shape centered inside each color-1 exact rectangular border. Smaller objects, malformed blue rings, and connected frame composites are erased; with no exact frame the output is blank.
Restore foreground-only impure color bboxes, then repaint original non-background cells along complete horizontal, vertical, or diagonal color spans in ascending color order.

Rect outlines fill their empty interior with 8. occupied boards carry non-0 cells inside a frame (preserved - only 0s fill); nested boards put a frame INSIDE another's interior (both fill, the inner frame's border survives the outer fill); decoy_mix boards add broken rings / solid blocks (untouched) next to real frames; eight_frame boards use an 8-colored frame (still fills - the rule ignores frame color).

Use the first color-6 cell in row-major order as the pivot. Rebuild an empty canvas, keep that pivot, and rotate every non-{0,6} cell 90 degrees clockwise around it. Clip rotated cells that leave the canvas. Later color-6 cells vanish. Every five consecutive generated examples include plain/canonical, clipping, multiple-object, multicolor, and extra-six witnesses.
For each active row, read the leftmost non-zero color and recolor every non-zero cell in that row to it. Background gaps remain background.

7x7 legend names 4 quadrant colors; each quadrant copies the matching outside shape (normalized, top-left 3x3 window). Legend position free, legend body solid-1 like the original task (was: hollow outline at a fixed corner with shapes at 4 fixed origins). big_shape boards use a 4x4 shape that TRUNCATES to its top-left window; dup_color boards repeat a color in two corners (same shape twice); decoy_one boards add a small 1-object that is NOT 7x7 (skipped by the legend search).

Objects rotate per their color code (1 id / 2 cw / 3 180 / else ccw). identity_one boards include color-1 objects (frozen in place - the code was never generated before); high_colors boards use 5-9 (all ccw, refuting 'code = color mod 4'); nonsquare boards rotate tall/wide crops (dims swap at the same top-left); clip boards push a tall object's rotation off the right edge. Shapes verified rotation-asymmetric.

On the demonstrated compact or 30x30 scene, move each blue dot only when it shares a row or column with its nearest exact 2x2 red square. The dot teleports to hug that square; unaligned dots stay, and a two-square distance tie uses the first square in row-major order.

Green-3 row markers and red-2 column markers paint gray-5 at every intersection. Rich examples add inactive wrong-color header markers, pre-existing body content that intersections overwrite, and an irrelevant noncanonical corner value.

Build a dense 22x22 black field containing one 3x3 blue/cyan template whose yellow cells are blank wildcards. Place one or two exact unmarked copies plus substantial blue/cyan distractor noise. Copy yellow into the wildcard slots of every exact copy; preserve all source content.

1-4 markers stamp transformed copies of the corner proto, and the output COUNTS overlaps per cell - overlap boards cluster markers 2 apart so counts reach 2-4 (the original task's centerpiece, never generated before: old markers were deliberately separated). clip boards stamp at edges; ignored_marker boards add 5-9 cells (not markers); top_band_marker boards put a marker at r<3, c>=3 (legal - only the 3x3 corner is excluded).

Scattered marks copy to their mirrored ROW - sources sit in BOTH halves (refutes 'top-to-bottom copy'; the old generator was top-half only). swap_pair boards put different colors at mutually mirrored spots: they SWAP (mirror writes overwrite, input does not win). on_axis boards use a center-row no-op plus an effective source on odd heights, or an effective source touching the central seam on exact even heights. dense normally packs 8-14 marks while exact mark pins always take precedence.

L-triominoes of 7 complete into 2x2 squares. blocked boards put a non-7 color in the fourth cell (no fill - the slot must be 0); pair_only boards scatter 2-seven dominoes (no window qualifies); chain boards overlap two Ls sharing a column of 7s (both windows fill from the original); decoy boards scatter other colors near the Ls.

Find each maximal vertical magenta (6) run. If its length is at least three, recolor exactly the top and bottom cells blue (1), preserving the interior. Length-one/two magenta runs, horizontal magenta lines, and non-magenta runs are unchanged; separated runs in one column are capped independently.
Multiple colors with distinct frequencies; rule outputs stacked histogram.

Above-divider shapes fold below as 8s. below_blocker boards put content under the line: it does NOT reflect upward and BLOCKS incoming 8s (was a frozen degenerate); clip boards push the divider low so reflections fall off-grid; five_decoy boards put a loose 5-cell above (not reflected - 5s are excluded sources); two_dividers boards have a second full 5-row (the FIRST wins, the second behaves as blocking content).

A zero header row sits above a bottom-aligned one-color skyline. Count each contiguous bar upward from the bottom, ignore empty columns for the minimum, then draw 4 above the RIGHTMOST tallest bar and 9 above the LEFTMOST shortest live bar. Ordinary four-example lessons always include a maximum tie, a minimum tie, a zero-column witness, and a unique-extremes witness; exact linked canonical profiles recur at a controlled rate.

A zero-background odd-width grid has one centered full-height color-8 fold bar. Compare each nonzero left cell with the cell at its exact reflection on the right. Emit a same-size blank grid containing color 2 only at reflected positions where both sides were nonzero. Input colors are irrelevant; left-only, right-only, bar, and all other cells vanish. Two scheduled canonical-profile anchors preserve source support, while three contrast scenes jointly expose both occupancy branches, same- and different-color overlaps, constant-red output, and exact-position logic.

0-bg grid (h, w ~9-14) with 2..4 SOLID FILLED OBJECTS in distinct non-bg colors, at RANDOM non-overlapping positions and VARIED sizes. Most are filled rectangles (≥3×3 so they have interior cells); some are fat irregular blobs (L / plus / random fill) that still enclose interior. Objects are isolated by ≥1 bg cell. Rule: for each object, compute its BOUNDARY cells (a cell with ≥1 4-neighbor outside the object), paint them on a fresh same-size grid in the object's color, interior → 0. Net: each solid object becomes its outline. Object count, sizes, shapes and positions all vary.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-13) with EXACTLY TWO separated 4-connected objects, each a RANDOM polyomino (3-5 cells) of a DISTINCT normalized shape, in distinct non-bg colours (8 reserved for the rule output). Rule (XOR OF THE TWO NORMALIZED SHAPES): sort objects by reading order, take the first two, normalize each to its bbox top-left, output a max(bbox_h)*max(bbox_w) grid painted 8 where EXACTLY ONE shape is filled (symmetric difference), 0 elsewhere. Varied shape pairs -> varied cyan XOR masks.

Four single-color shapes occupy fixed 5-column panels in a 23-column grid. Return a 4x4 matrix with cyan(8) exactly for pairs whose cropped binary shapes are equivalent under rotation; translation and color are ignored, but reflection alone is not equivalence.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holds a LEGEND color C ∈ {1..9, ≠0}; (b) 3 isolated 4-conn shapes (4-cell tetrominoes) in 3 distinct colors placed elsewhere; one of the shape colors equals the legend color C. Rule: read C = g[0][0]. Find the (multi-cell) shape whose color = C. Crop to its bbox. ROTATE 90° CLOCKWISE. Output: the rotated cropped shape (in color C).

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-9, w ∈ 8-10) with: (a) A 2-ROW LEGEND at TOP — for each of 2 DISTINCT COLUMNS (cols sorted, drawn from range(w)): row 0 holds a SRC color, row 1 holds the matching DST color. The 4 colors (src1, dst1, src2, dst2) are drawn distinct from {2..9}; (b) BELOW ROW 1 (row 2 is buffer): TWO BLOBS, each in one of the SRC colors (src1 or src2), built via grow_blob of 2-3 cells, placed at non-overlapping interior positions. Rule (READ THE 2-ROW LEGEND TO BUILD A RECOLOR MAP SRC→DST; FOR EACH NON-BG BODY CELL (R ≥ 2) WITH COLOR V: IF V IS A SRC: PAINT g[R][C] = MAP[V]; ELSE: KEEP AS-IS): PARSE the top 2 rows to build (src1→dst1, src2→dst2) map. For EACH cell (r, c) below row 1: IF g[r][c] ∈ map: PAINT g[r][c] = map[g[r][c]]. Legend rows preserved (or per demos, zeroed). Net: src-colored blobs are recolored to their corresponding dst colors per the legend.

8-wall-bounded grid split into chambers by straight dividers, PLUS scattered interior 8-wall obstacles inside chambers (so the rule's geodesic BFS must DETOUR around them, not just Manhattan-fill). Each chamber holds 1..4 colored seeds. Rule: within each chamber every open cell takes the color of the geodesically-nearest seed (ties → smaller color value). Grid size, divider layout, obstacle count and seed count/positions all vary.

A 0-background grid contains 2..5 nonzero colors. The global total cell counts follow one of four explicit frequency profiles, including ties. Rank colors by descending total count, breaking ties by smaller color, then replace every cell of rank k with k. Geometry and component count are distractors: one scheduled profile splits the most frequent color into two components so largest-component ranking gives the wrong answer.

0-bg grid (h in 4..6, w sized to fit). ROW 0 is a MARKER STRIP: k color-1 (blue) cells encode TARGET AREA = k, m color-2 (red) cells encode TARGET BOUNDARY = m, scattered at random columns. Rows 1.. (the body) hold a RANDOM target polyomino whose (size, boundary-cell count) == (k, m), PLUS 1-3 distractor blobs with a DIFFERENT (size, boundary) pair, each a separate component. Rule: find the unique body blob with size==k AND boundary==m, crop it to its bbox and paint color 8 (cyan). The target SHAPE is random, so the OUTPUT varies; grid size, distractors, colors and all placements vary too (was a single fixed 2x4 blob → k=m=8).

Compact each row independently: delete zeros, preserve the nonzero values' left-to-right order, write them from the left edge, and zero-fill the suffix. Generated lessons mix already-packed rows with rows containing leading or internal gaps, and regularly include a moved row with at least five values.
Place two to four separated solid odd-by-odd rectangles on a zero background. Replace every rectangle by only its geometric center cell, preserving that rectangle's color.
Keep each nonzero cell whose four cardinal neighbours share its colour.
One to four cross-bodied creatures independently move opposite their blue tails to the wall; opposite body colors swap and each observed tail moves intact.
A full color-9 row or column is a reflection axis. Copy every colored cell to its in-bounds mirror, regardless of which side supplied it.
Recolor interior 8s by their row's nonzero left header; preserve all other cells.
2-3 L-trominoes (size 3 in 2×2 bbox) of distinct colors.

Canonical-scale 3x3..5x5 zero-background grid containing one sparse, 4-connected motif in exactly two nonzero colors. Rule: replace EACH input cell by a solid 2x2 block of the same color, so an h x w input becomes a 2h x 2w output. A three-step schedule supplies one square anchor and two rectangular witnesses, while rejecting scenes where whole-grid tiling or transpose-before-upscale would accidentally match the true output.
8-src + 9-dst markers + a colored blob; both blob and shadow in-bounds.

Three panels separated by full-height color-9 columns: A and B form a per-cell color KEY (a->b at matching positions), and a QUERY panel uses the source colors. Rule recolors the query through the A->B map.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 5-8, w = 2*half_w with half_w ∈ 4-6 → w ∈ 8-12 EVEN, by difficulty) with: MARK_COUNT ∈ 4-7 SOURCE CELLS placed ONLY in the RIGHT HALF (cols half_w..2*half_w-1), each in a random color drawn from {1..9}. The LEFT HALF (cols 0..half_w-1) starts EMPTY. Rule (HORIZONTALLY MIRROR THE RIGHT HALF ONTO THE LEFT HALF, OVERWRITING ANY LEFT-HALF CONTENT; THE RIGHT HALF REMAINS UNCHANGED): For EACH cell (r, c) with c in 0..half_w-1: SET g[r][c] = g[r][w-1-c] (its mirror in the right half). The right half preserved. Net: input becomes left-right symmetric across the vertical axis at col half_w; left half is a mirror copy of right.

Color-4 4-connected objects on a 0-bg grid: a mix of hollow 3x3 frames (8 cells, the rule's target), hollow 4x4 frames (12 cells, non-target distractors), and possibly other shapes. Rule fills the single 0-interior cell of each 3x3 frame with color 1; all other shapes (and any 0-cells outside frames) are unchanged.

A zero-background grid contains two or three distinct foreground colors. Each color marks exactly three corners of one axis-aligned rectangle and its fourth corner is blank. Complete every rectangle by painting only that missing corner with the same color.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~7-10) with ONE MARKER FRAME — three corners of an axis-aligned 2×2 local-coordinate system painted in fixed marker colors 5, 6, and 7 (origin at random non-degenerate position via choose_frame helper, basis vectors vx, vy each ±1). Specifically the markers sit at: ORIGIN (color 5), ORIGIN + vx (color 6), ORIGIN + vy (color 7). The FOURTH CORNER at ORIGIN + vx + vy is left 0 and is guaranteed in-bounds. All other cells are 0. Rule (CLOSE THE 2×2 MARKER FRAME): find the three marker cells (colors 5, 6, 7). INFER the local 2×2 coordinate frame: 5 = origin, 6 and 7 along orthogonal axes from origin. COMPUTE the missing fourth corner = origin + (6's offset) + (7's offset). PAINT that fourth corner with a designated FILL COLOR (e.g., the maximum of the three marker colors, or a fixed convention per demos). The three marker cells stay unchanged. Net: the partially-drawn 2×2 marker block is completed into a full 4-corner block with a new color in the previously-empty corner.
skills: frame completion, local neighborhood, same-size output

summary: Move every nonzero, non-9 cell to its 180-degree point reflection around the unique 9 anchor, erasing the source.  Four scheduled layouts include off-center anchors, disconnected sources, anchor-axis cells, and occupied antipodal destinations so each four-demo lesson refutes named shortcuts.
Four fixed 3x3 binary prototypes on a 7..11 by 11..15 canvas. Each row/column pair contributes its intersection, painted 8, to a fixed 7x7 gallery. Prototype colors do not determine their roles.
Color pairs mark endpoints of separated diagonal segments.

A zero-background grid has a FULL header row exposing colors 2..8. Its base is an ascending or descending cyclic sequence; row-1 lessons swap one later object-anchor entry with a non-anchor entry, so the actual lookup cells must be read. The body contains three isolated blue (1) objects. Recolor every object uniformly with the header color above the object's bounding-box LEFTMOST column; preserve the header and all background cells. The body's final column remains blank because the selected rule excludes it from object extraction.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~9-12) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 SEED at (sr, 1) — left edge interior row sr ∈ [2, h-3]; (b) ONE MIRROR at (sr, mirror_c) with mirror_c ∈ [sr+3, w-3] — color either 6 (UP-FROM-RIGHT reflector) or 7 (DOWN-FROM-RIGHT reflector); (c) ONE COLOR-5 WALL at (wall_r, mirror_c) placed in the column the beam will enter after deflection. Rule (LASER BEAM FROM 2-SEED, DEFLECTED BY 6/7 MIRRORS, STOPPED BY 5-WALL): from the 2-seed at (sr, 1), cast a beam to the RIGHT. PAINT every 0-cell along the beam's path with COLOR 8. When the beam hits a 6-mirror: turn LEFT-OF-INCOMING (right → up). When it hits a 7-mirror: turn RIGHT-OF-INCOMING (right → down). When it hits a 5-WALL or grid edge, the beam STOPS. Net: a cyan-painted trajectory traces through the optical system from the seed.
Colored frames sorted by gray-count inside bbox; encoded as padded rows.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~7-10) with 2-4 ISOLATED 2×2 WINDOWS, each containing a same-color DIAGONAL PAIR — either main-diagonal ((0,0)+(1,1)) or anti-diagonal ((0,1)+(1,0)) — with the other two corners of the 2×2 currently 0. Different pairs use distinct colors; windows are spaced with ≥1-cell buffer. Rule: detect each 2×2 window with exactly 2 same-color cells on a diagonal. COMPLETE the 2×2 to a SOLID 2×2 BLOCK by filling the missing anti-diagonal (or main-diagonal) cells with the same color.
Read each foreground directional ring around a background plus, then fill that five-cell plus with the color of the frame side named by the ring orientation.
2-3 L-shaped 3-cell groups of distinct colors, well separated.
Key marker at (0,0) sets a color; one key-colored object + distractor objects; rule crops the key object.
Treat color 9 as hard walls. Flood every zero cell in a chamber that has one colored seed with that seed's color; preserve the walls and any unseeded chamber.

Flood from the reading-order-first red(2) seed through 4-connected blue/red cells, recoloring reached blue(1) cells green(3). Azure(8) walls block the flood and disconnected blue cells remain unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains one connected 5..9-colored object and one isolated control marker.  Marker colors 1,2,3,4 request identity, 90° clockwise, 180°, and 90° counterclockwise transforms.
