Crop the object tightly and apply the requested transform.  Consecutive four-example windows cover all four codes; canonical-size anchors remain in every band.
(a,b) color legend + one 5/6 template in body + K 9-markers; rule stamps the recolored flipped template at each marker.

A 9-10 by 10-12 zero-background grid contains exactly two disjoint hollow yellow rectangular frames and one non-yellow marker. The marker lies immediately above, below, left, or right of a frame border. Select the first adjacent frame in row-major frame order, fill only its zero interior cells with the marker color, and leave the marker, both yellow borders, and the other hollow frame unchanged. Ordinary generated rows make the marker adjacent to exactly one frame; self_check also accepts the canonical tie case because the pinned Racket authority resolves it by first-frame order.

One to four disjoint endpoint pairs define inclusive cyan spans. Axis-aligned lessons include the canonical two-pair crossing profile; perfect 45-degree diagonal variants exercise the same pinned authority.
Grid of small gray(5) blocks defining multiple occupied rows/cols; rule cross-hatches gaps with red/blue.

Independently shaped blue-row and red-column anchors select one connected candidate. Same-area, same-bbox near matches teach both ordered profiles; alternate anchor roles defeat candidate-only incidence. Color and layout vary.

skills: exact matching, coordinate derivation, spatial markers
summary: A three-column template panel and a board are separated by color 9. Find every original-orientation wildcard match of the cropped monochrome template and mark each matched window's bottom-right corner in color 8. Generated scenes include same-color orientation decoys and wildcard-slot clutter; every four-pair lesson also contains two board-only-family refutations, so the template must actually be used.

A yellow five-cell arrow has an apex one column left or right of its three-cell bar.  Read that relative offset, then reflect every cyan(8) cell across the cyan bounding box's indicated vertical edge and paint the reflected copy immediately outside it.  Preserve the input.
Select the largest monochromatic 4-connected component by cell count; retain cells with an absent cardinal neighbor and crop to its bbox.

Square n × n input grid (n ∈ {2..5}) with: (a) g[0][0] = LINE COLOR (a non-0 value drawn from {1..9}); (b) other cells filled by one of 5 DECORATIONS (solid / noise_with_corner / stripes_with_corner / checker_with_corner / blob_with_corner) using a SECOND color (line_color + 1, wrapping). The decoration is decoy — only g[0][0] matters. n encodes the period and line_color encodes the output stripe color. Rule (PRODUCE A FIXED 15×15 PERIODIC LATTICE WITH PERIOD n+1 AND LINE COLOR g[0][0]): EXTRACT line_color = g[0][0] and period = n+1 (where n is the input's side length). PRODUCE a FRESH 15 × 15 OUTPUT GRID. For EACH cell (r, c) with r, c ∈ [0, 14]: IF (r % period == n) OR (c % period == n), PAINT it with line_color; ELSE bg-0. The input's decoration content is DROPPED. Net: a fixed 15×15 grid with horizontal and vertical lines spaced every (n+1) cells in the line color — a lattice pattern. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=31): bounded by 4 period values × 9 colors.
Zero divider rows/columns form rectangular sections; emit a compact grid containing the unique dominant nonzero color of every section.

Nested yellow rectangular frames with row-0 red-count selection. Exact size/count/gap/palette controls; translated and offset stacks; scattered selectors, lawful no-ops, off-row red and protected in-band clutter.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with: (a) ROW 0 cells (0, 1) and (0, 2) hold 2 DISTINCT PALETTE COLORS (from {2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8} — non-1, non-9); (b) a HOLLOW COLOR-1 (blue) RECTANGULAR FRAME at (1, 1)..(h-2, w-2); (c) a COLOR-9 (maroon) SEED cell at (h//2, w//2) (center of frame interior). Rule (ALTERNATING CARDINAL RAYS FROM SEED): READ palette = [g[0][1], g[0][2]]. From the seed at (sr, sc), WALK in all 4 CARDINAL DIRECTIONS (up, down, left, right) STEP-BY-STEP until hitting a 1-wall. At step k (1-indexed), if the cell is 0, PAINT it with palette[k % 2]. The seed and frame stay. Net: alternating-color rays fill the frame interior from seed.
Crop the single body above the last row; read the ordered key cells; map 2/5 to identity, 3 to clockwise rotation, and 4 to 180-degree rotation; then h-stack the results with one-column gaps.

Zero-background 7..15 grids with exactly 2..5 four-isolated sources. Sources expand one step in four cardinal directions, clipped at borders; connected distractor cells remain unchanged. A three-scene curriculum mixes interior sources, boundary sources with a domino, and same-color diagonal sources with a domino. No different-color expansion collisions.
Fill a vertical span only when its column has exactly two matching nonzero endpoints with zeros between; leave mismatched, blocked, and singleton columns unchanged.
Extend the bottom center color upward on the two outward diagonals starting at the endpoints of the centered segment directly above it.

A 19..22 grid has one sparse 3x3 multicolor template: a majority fill color plus two distinct marker-port cells at opposite corners. One to three greedy-nearest pairs of solid marker-colored squares (scales 1..3) occupy corresponding corners of scaled 3x3 footprints. The Racket rule chooses the compatible D4 placement and paints the scaled template fill cells. Consecutive sample_index values cover unit, scale-2, scale-3, multi-pair, mixed-scale, same-diagonal, and opposite-diagonal lessons.

8×10 0-bg grid with: (a) one connected color-1 (blue) TEMPLATE A; (b) one connected color-2 (red) TEMPLATE B; (c) exactly one SINGLETON KEY cell with color ∈ {3, 4, 6} placed somewhere apart. Rule: extract A's cells and normalize → s1; same for B's cells → s2. Detect control color (the one with count == 1 in {3, 4, 6}). Apply boolean op on the two normalized cell-sets: 3 → UNION, 4 → INTERSECTION, 6 → XOR (symmetric difference). If result empty → output [[0]]. Else: normalize result to (0, 0), paint cells color 8 (cyan). Output: small grid sized to result's bbox.

On a color-7 grid, find the solid color-5 rectangle anchored to the bottom. Erase the lone color-2 marker, recolor the lone color-8 marker to 2, and stamp a new 8 on the rectangle's bottom row immediately outside the horizontal side opposite the original 2. The midpoint column counts as the right side.

0-bg grid with: (a) exactly ONE gray(5) cell — the marker; (b) one TARGET non-gray object (some shape, 4-9 cells, in a single color) placed adjacent to the marker (Chebyshev distance ≤ 1 from at least one target cell); (c) 1-4 DISTRACTOR non-gray objects elsewhere (other colors or same target color allowed), NOT adjacent to the marker. Rule: remove the gray cell, find the 8-connected object adjacent to the marker's position, crop to its bbox. The output is just the target's bbox subgrid (no marker, no distractors).

Four separated monochrome 4-connected components on a 0 background. The four-step curriculum crosses unique versus repeated component colors with distinct versus tied component areas. Repeated-color scenes force component extraction rather than global color counting; tied-area scenes force the canonical ascending-color tiebreak rather than position order. The output is one row formed by sorting components by area descending, then color ascending, and repeating each component color by its area.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~9-11 by ~10-12) with 2-3 COLOR PAIRS: each of 2-3 distinct non-zero colors appears EXACTLY 2 times as single-cell markers (not 4-adjacent), positioned NON-COLINEARLY (different rows AND different cols). For each pair, at least one of the two L-elbow routes between the two endpoints is clear of other pair-cells. Rule: for each color, find its 2 endpoints. Try both L-elbow paths (via (r1, c2) corner or (r2, c1) corner). Pick the one whose interior cells don't pass through any other pair's endpoint cells. Paint that elbow path with the pair's color. Output: each pair connected by its clear elbow.

Row 0 is a sparse legend with three or four nonzero colors and one unique frequency winner. Rows 2+ contain two separated objects in that key color plus differently colored distractors. Select the largest key-color object, crop its bounding box from the input, and upscale the crop 2x. Generated examples make the smaller key object occur earlier and make a non-key object larger, so both legend counting and largest-within-key are required.

0-bg grid with N (2-4) connected non-bg components ('blobs'), each in its own color, occupying disjoint column ranges so they can each slide up independently without collision. Rule: for each blob, compute its bbox top row r0. Shift the blob UP by r0 rows (so its new bbox top is at row 0), preserving columns and shape. Output is a fresh grid with all blobs slid to touch the top border.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-16, w ∈ 11-18, by difficulty) with: N_SHAPES ∈ 3-4 OBJECTS drawn from _SHAPES bank (6 variants of sizes 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 — single cell, L, T-pentomino, ring 3×3, solid 3×3), each with a DISTINCT SIZE drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT, each painted in a DISTINCT color from {1..9}, placed via place_no_overlap with 1-cell padding. Total packed width fits within w. Rule (SORT OBJECTS BY (SIZE DESC, BBOX-H ASC, BBOX-W ASC, COLOR ASC); PACK THEM HORIZONTALLY FROM THE LEFT WITH 1-COL BG GAPS, PRESERVING EACH OBJECT'S ORIGINAL SHAPE AND COLOR): EXTRACT every non-bg component. SORT by tuple (-cell_count, bbox_h, bbox_w, color). CROP each to its bbox. PACK left-to-right with 1-COLUMN BG GAPS between, TOP-ALIGNED. Output height = max bbox height across all objects; width = sum_widths + (n-1). Net: largest objects go first, left-aligned packing yields a sorted gallery.
Exactly one object has an enclosed hole; that object is normalized to top-left on blank output.

Read the transform key at (0,0) and the sole non-zero selector colour elsewhere in row 0. Select the largest body component of that colour, transform its tight crop (1=clockwise, 2=left-right flip, 3=up-down flip, 4=180 degrees, 5/6=identity), then center it inside the unique hollow colour-8 frame on an otherwise blank output.

A zero-background grid contains two through four solid, cardinally separated monochrome rectangles, each at least 3x3 and colored from {1..7,9}. For every rectangle independently, paint every strict interior cell cyan 8 and preserve its original colored border. Separate rectangles may share a color; component identity, not color identity, determines which interiors are filled.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-12, w ∈ 10-13) with: (a) TWO EDGE-TOUCHING COMPONENTS of DIFFERENT COLORS at a random interior position, configured per contact_orientation ∈ {horizontal, vertical}: HORIZONTAL: a COLOR-2 (red) vertical 3-cell strip and an ADJACENT COLOR-3 (green) horizontal 2-cell extension touching the middle right of the red strip; VERTICAL: a COLOR-2 horizontal 3-cell strip and a COLOR-3 vertical 2-cell extension touching the middle bottom; (b) ONE ISOLATED COLOR-6 MAGENTA COMPONENT at (h-2, w-3..w-2) — a 2-cell distractor that does NOT touch the other two. Rule (KEEP ONLY NON-BG CELLS THAT EDGE-TOUCH A DIFFERENT-COLORED COMPONENT, RECOLOR THEM TO COLOR 8; OTHERS BECOME 0): For EACH non-bg cell (r, c) with color k: CHECK its 4-neighbors. IF ANY neighbor has a non-bg color != k: PAINT g[r][c] = COLOR 8 (cyan). ELSE: PAINT 0. Isolated components (no different-colored neighbor) are erased entirely. Net: only the inter-color contact boundary survives, painted in cyan.
Stable-sort marker cells by minimum edge distance and paint their colors as concentric output rings from outside inward.
Top + left headers (with a corner color) sharing some overlapping colors; output is the header equality matrix.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-13) with: (a) TWO FULL COLOR-8 (cyan) WALLS — either horizontal (rows 1 and h-2 entirely color 8) or vertical (cols 1 and w-2 entirely color 8); (b) 1-2 COLOR-2 (red) CENTER cells between the walls (≥3 cells from each wall). Rule (PROJECT RED CENTERS TO WALLS WITH LEGS + 3×3 NODES): for EACH COLOR-2 CENTER, PROJECT perpendicular to the walls (if walls horizontal, project vertically; if vertical, project horizontally). DRAW LEGS of color 2 from the center to the nearest walls, AND stamp a 3×3 COLOR-8 (cyan) NODE at the wall intersection points. Net: red centers project to walls, leaving legs + wall-side nodes.

Read cells in row-major order. The last color-2 cell is the source anchor and the last color-3 cell is the destination anchor. Translate every non-{0,2,3} payload cell by that 2→3 offset into a blank same-size grid; drop translated cells that leave the grid and erase all marker cells.

Three square panels are separated by full color-5 columns. Panel B is a unique whole-panel transform of panel A, chosen from clockwise rotation, 180-degree rotation, counterclockwise rotation, left-right reflection, up-down reflection, or transpose. Apply the inferred transform to panel C.

0-bg grid (h~10-15, w~12-17) with: (a) ONE RED (COLOR-2) SHAPE of 2-4 cells with ONE MAROON (COLOR-9) ANCHOR cell embedded; (b) ONE BLUE (COLOR-1) SHAPE of 2-4 cells with its OWN MAROON ANCHOR; (c) ONE CYAN (COLOR-8) TARGET cell at a clear non-adjacent position. All shapes placed with 1-cell padding. Rule (XOR OF RED AND BLUE SHAPES, STAMPED AT CYAN ANCHOR, COLOR 3): identify the RED SHAPE and its 9-anchor; the BLUE SHAPE and its 9-anchor. NORMALIZE each shape by its 9-anchor (offsets relative to anchor). COMPUTE the SYMMETRIC DIFFERENCE (XOR) of the offset sets — cells in red OR blue but NOT BOTH. STAMP the XOR offsets centered at the CYAN anchor in COLOR-3 (green). Source shapes and cyan stay or are task-specific. Net: asymmetric XOR of two anchored shapes paints in green at cyan target.
(0,0)=op key (1..5), (0,cols-1)=transform key (1..6); two component shapes A,B boolean-overlaid (B transformed first).
Cyan(8) maze walls + single 3x3 marker block. Output fills via cardinal ray-expansion bounded by walls, plus wide-axis bridge fill between min/max painted positions in wall-less cols/rows.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 ISOLATED 4-conn motifs (3-5 cells each) in distinct non-zero colors. Motifs separated by ≥1 bg cell. Rule: extract objects. For each object, compute 'grown size' — grow each cell by a square 3×3 stamp (8-conn neighborhood) and count the union size. Pick the object with MAX grown size (ties: tiebreak by scan order). Grow that object's cells by the same square stamp. Output: a small grid sized to the grown bbox, painted color 8 (cyan) at every grown cell, 0 elsewhere.
5-walls divide grid into 4-9 compartments of varied size; each has 1-3 markers of varied colors (chamber floods with max color).

Period-4 8-LATTICE background: at each block offset (rows/cols 1..3 of every 4-cell block) a 3x3 hollow 8-box, with 0 gutters on the lines (r%4==0 / c%4==0) and a 0 center (r%4==2,c%4==2). Scattered markers in 2-3 colors (not 0/8) sit on the 0 cells. Rule: snap each color's markers to the nearest 4-lattice lines, form a bounding rect, paint its border + lattice-center dots (r%4==2,c%4==2) in that color (only over 0-cells; the 8-boxes are preserved); markers are kept. Grid size/colors/positions vary.
Separated objects of varied sizes; objects with ≥4 cells become 6.

N panels separated by full-height color-9 divider columns, each holding a small motif. Rule crops each panel and outputs an NxN matrix with 8 at (r,c) when panel r and panel c are dihedral-equivalent (same shape under rotation/flip), else 0.
skills: pairwise comparison, equivalence classes, symbolic matrix construction

summary: Constructive 0-background object galleries. Generate 2-6 distinct-color 4-connected objects in a 6-14 by 9-22 grid, keep objects disjoint under 4-connectivity, and give every object a unique left bounding-box column. The selected rule sorts by that left edge, crops each object, packs crops left-to-right with one zero column between them, and bottom-aligns them. Every generated input has unequal crop heights so the canonical-only top-alignment shortcut is visibly wrong.
3-4 distinct-color blobs of strictly distinct sizes; rule crops the largest.
Empty diagonal midpoints between yellow pairs are filled cyan. Grids also carry decoy color-5 markers (ignored by the rule) and lone scattered 4s with no diagonal partner (not filled).

Color-7 bg grid. ONE straight line of color-5 cells (the guide, horizontal or vertical). ONE color-9 cell (the marker) on one side of the guide. Several color-4 objects (connected 4-components) scattered. Some objects lie entirely on the marker's side of the guide (preserved). Other objects lie entirely on the opposite side; of these, ≥1 'crosses' the guide projection at ≥2 positions and gets erased. Rule erases such objects to color 7.
Infer the unique dihedral transform mapping the first square panel to the second, then apply it to the third panel.
Preserve every source cell and add a same-color echo at its 180-degree point reflection (h-1-r, w-1-c).

0-bg grid with N (2..6) 4-connected OBJECTS, each in a distinct color, placed apart by >=1 bg cell. Shapes are drawn from a pool of PAIRWISE-DIHEDRALLY-DISTINCT families; some families repeat (each instance independently rotated/flipped) to create dihedral-equivalent pairs. Rule: extract objects, sort by top-left (row, col), binary-crop each (drop color). Output: an N x N MATRIX where cell (r, c) = 8 (cyan) if mask[r] is DIHEDRAL EQUIVALENT to mask[c] (some transform code 1..8 maps one to the other), else 0. Diagonal always 8. Both N and the equivalence block-structure vary (was fixed 3x3).

Ignore zero corners, take the unique strict-majority nonzero corner color, and fill every zero interior cell of every complete color-3 rectangular frame. Three ordinary profiles match exact canonical dimension/palette/frame/corner signatures; a fourth profile supplies zero-corner and three-frame counterexamples to fixed-corner and single-frame shortcuts.

Row 0 holds k color-1 markers (rotation count). Body (rows 1..H-1, cols 0..W-2) has one color-9 anchor + several non-{0,9} colored cells. Rule emits a (H-1) × (W-1) grid: anchor stays at 9, and each colored cell is stamped at every 90° CCW rotation about the anchor for turns = 0..k (k+1 stamps total). Off-bounds stamps drop.
Choose the smallest complete rectangular frame that strictly encloses the red marker, then output a solid rectangle with that frame's size and color.
Use the bounding box of all cyan (8) cells as a recolor zone; change blue (1) cells inside it to green (3), preserving every other cell.
Union the pattern with its left-right mirror.

Grid with VERTICAL color-5 walls (one or more full or partial color-5 columns) dividing the grid into row-segments. Each row-segment between consecutive walls (or wall and grid edge) holds some scattered non-zero non-5 values. Rule: for each row, scan left to right. Preserve color-5 cells in place. Within each segment between walls, collect all non-zero non-5 values in left-to-right order and pack them at the LEFT of the segment, filling the remainder with 0. Equivalent to per-row gravity-left within wall segments.

0-bg grid (size varies). 2-5 color-6 (magenta) OBJECTS of DISTINCT sizes (single connected components, placed apart, all above the marker row), and a color-2 (red) MARKER on the bottom row with blank space to its right. Rule: sort the object sizes descending and draw a BAR on the marker's row — each size = a run of that many color-3 (green) cells, runs separated by one gap, starting right of the marker. The grid size, object count/sizes/positions and marker column all vary freely (was 3 fixed objects, ~11 distinct).

Compact colored grid (h, w in {3..5}) drawn with one of 8 TEXTURES (random/blob_pair/striped/border/quadrants/checker/diagonal/frame_5_inner_8) containing CELLS in COLOR-5 (gray) and COLOR-8 (cyan) at mix_ratio 0.3-0.7. Plus 3-6 DISTRACTOR color cells in non-{0, 5, 8} colors. BG is a non-target color (or task-specific). Guaranteed ≥1 5-cell AND ≥1 8-cell. Rule (SWAP COLORS 5 ↔ 8 EVERYWHERE): For EACH cell with VALUE 5: REPAINT to 8. For EACH cell with VALUE 8: REPAINT to 5. All other colors (distractors, bg) stay. Net: gray and cyan exchange places across the entire grid.

A single full color-8 row and column partition the input into four quadrants. One corner quadrant is exactly a filled 2x2 key using three or four colors outside {0,3,8}; the diagonally opposite quadrant is a 0/3 mask and the two remaining quadrants are empty. Crop the mask quadrant. Each green cell in its top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right half becomes the matching key color; mask zeros remain 0.
Rank every non-7 color by descending frequency, using descending numeric color order for ties, then paint concentric square rings.
Nonzero top-row seeds project downward in their own columns until an optional color-9 blocker; each blocker is column-local and preserved.
Select the first row-major nonzero color, invert the zero mask, and tile 2 by 2.

Three distinct legend colors from 2..8 at row 0 columns 1..3; one closed color-1 rectangular chamber and one interior color-9 seed. Paint eight rays with the legend cycle, stopping at the actual frame. Ordinary three-example windows cover gray 5, deep insets and rays beyond distance 7.
2-3 distinct-color blobs in upper rows of grid (bottom row stays empty).

Fixed 3×3 grid with: (a) MINORITY color (1-2 cells in a randomly chosen color); (b) MAJORITY cells (7-8) in 1-3 OTHER colors arranged in one of 5 layouts (uniform/two_colors/striped/checker/diagonal_split). Minority count must be STRICTLY LESS than every other color count. Rule (SELF-TILE GATED BY MINORITY): identify the MINORITY (least-frequent color). EMIT a 9×9 (3*h × 3*w) OUTPUT grid where each cell at position (R, C) is computed as: if input[R // 3][C // 3] == MINORITY → copy from input[R % 3][C % 3]; ELSE → 0 (or the cell's value if input cell isn't minority — task-specific). Net: 3×3 input self-tiles into 9×9 output gated by minority-color cells.
3 5-wide panels with binary content; pairwise intersection.

0-bg grid (h~7-12, w~7-12) with 2-5 ISOLATED YELLOW L-TRIOMINOES placed at GRID-ALIGNED ANCHORS on a 3-step grid (anchors at rows 0,3,6,9,... × cols 0,3,6,9,...). Each L-triomino is a 2×2 window with EXACTLY 3 of the 4 cells painted YELLOW (color 4) and the FOURTH (missing) CORNER left as 0. Which of the 4 corners is missing is chosen uniformly at random per shape (encoding one of 4 ORIENTATIONS). Triominoes are placed at non-touching positions via the 3-step grid alignment. Rule (PAINT THE MISSING CORNER OF EACH L-TRIOMINO WITH AN ORIENTATION-CODED COLOR): for EACH yellow L-triomino (3 yellow cells in a 2×2 window with one 0 corner): IDENTIFY which of the 4 corners is missing (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). LOOK UP the missing-corner color from a fixed mapping that depends on orientation (e.g., TL→C1, TR→C2, BL→C3, BR→C4 per demos). PAINT the missing-corner 0 cell with that color. Yellow cells stay yellow. Net: each yellow L is closed into a 2×2 block whose new corner has an orientation-coded color.
Translate the unique 4-connected nonzero motif so its bounding-box crop is floor-centered in the unchanged grid; preserve every color, hole, and relative cell position.
Find the object whose row profile reverses the anchor column profile.
Color-3 cells in groups + isolated; rule recolors connected to 8.

On an orange-7 grid, exactly four gray-5 cells define a square: three are square corners and one is a strictly interior distractor. Infer the missing square corner. Paint color 8 on the two square sides incident to that missing corner and on the diagonal joining the other two corners. Paint only orange cells, so all four gray markers are preserved.
2-4 connected motifs in distinct colors; some touch the grid border, some do not.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-12, w ∈ 10-13) with: (a) ONE CORNER KEY CELL — exactly one of the 4 grid corners (0,0), (0,w-1), (h-1,0), or (h-1,w-1) is painted in key_color (drawn from palette[0] ∈ {1..9}); (b) ONE KEY-COLORED BLOB inside the grid — a 3-5 cell irregular blob via grow_blob in the SAME key_color, placed AWAY from any corner (retry if any cell lands on a corner); (c) 1-2 DISTRACTOR BLOBS in OTHER colors (palette[1:] = 2 distinct non-key colors), each a 3-5 cell blob also placed away from corners. Rule (READ THE CORNER KEY, FILTER THE GRID TO KEEP ONLY KEY-COLORED NON-CORNER CELLS, CROP TO THEIR BBOX, OUTPUT): IDENTIFY the unique non-bg CORNER cell — its color is the KEY. FILTER all grid cells: KEEP only cells whose color == key_color AND whose position is NOT a corner. COMPUTE the bbox of the kept cells. CROP to that bbox: OUTPUT a smaller grid containing only the key-colored blob (with 0s where the bbox has no key cells). Net: the corner color picks which blob to extract; the cropped key-blob is the answer; distractors and corner are discarded.
Extend every colored singleton seed to a nearest border.  Equal-distance ties use the authoritative priority top, then bottom, then left, then right.

A 10-12 by 10-12 zero-background binary grid contains one or two exact 3x3 blue(1) hollow frames plus two or three separated non-frame blue objects. Every exact frame is replaced by a red(2) plus (corners erased; side midpoints and center painted red), while all non-frame blue objects remain unchanged.

Place one multicolor connected template above a bottom strip of exactly four transform keys. Smaller isolated cells may distract from the main object, so the unique largest component is selected. Read the four keys left-to-right (repeats are meaningful), apply id/cw90/180/flip-lr, and top-left align the four crops in a 2x2 gallery separated by zeros.

Fixed 7-row × 5-col 0-bg grid with: (a) ROWS 0..4 containing a 5×5 PROTOTYPE SHAPE (4-5 cells) in some source_color, drawn from a curated shape bank; (b) ROW 5, COLS 0..2 holding 3 TRANSFORM CODES (values 0..5 from a code table — each code maps to a specific rotation/reflection: 0=id, 1=cw90, 2=180°, 3=ccw90, 4=flip-lr, 5=flip-ud); (c) ROW 6, COLS 0..2 holding 3 OUTPUT COLORS (distinct from source_color). Rule: construct a CROSS-PRODUCT GALLERY OUTPUT — a 3×3 grid of TRANSFORMED PROTOTYPES, where output panel (i, j) contains the PROTOTYPE shape with TRANSFORM j applied and painted in COLOR i (from row 6). Output dimensions: 3*panel_h × 3*panel_w (each panel cell holds a 5×5 transformed prototype). Net: input teaches one shape + 3 transforms + 3 colors; output is the 3×3 cross-product gallery.

A zero-background grid contains matching red (2) source and green (3) target marker shapes plus one connected yellow (4) object.  The yellow object may partially occlude the red source marker; the complete green marker reveals the hidden source template.  Translate every yellow cell by the vector from the red marker bounding-box top-left to the green marker bounding-box top-left, placing only the translated yellow object on a fresh blank grid.

skills: reduced counting output, symbolic layer profile, histogram encoding
summary: One connected, hole-free shape in a single color 1..8 on background 0. The unchanged rule counts cells REMOVED at each successive cardinal erosion step, writing the counts outer-to-inner in a one-row strip. Each shell count is 1..9; total area may exceed 9. Default lessons cycle axial-detour, dual-concavity, and broad/core examples: five demonstrations plus one query contain two examples of each role.
Count all gray(5) top-row markers and recolor the unique blue(1) 4-connected component with that many cells red(2).

0-background grid with 2-4 distinct single-cell markers in colors 1..4 and 2-4 separated color-5 blobs. Recolor each blob to the color of its unique nearest marker under minimum Manhattan cell distance.
Isolated seeds stamp their color at all eight knight offsets.
1-2 solid 2x2 color-3 blocks with bg margin around them.

0-bg grid (h~11-13, w~12-14) with: (a) ROWS 0 and 1 forming a TWO-ROW LEGEND — row 0 holds 2-3 TRANSFORM TOKENS from {2, 3, 4, 9} at distinct columns (2 = rotate-cw, 3 = rotate-180, 4 = transpose, 9 = identity), and row 1 holds the matching ANCHOR COLORS in the same columns (legend maps anchor-color → transform-token); (b) BODY (rows 2..h-1) contains ONE COLOR-5 (gray) MOTIF (2-4 connected cells, the TEMPLATE shape) plus 2-3 single ANCHOR CELLS in colors matching the legend's anchor colors, placed away from the motif. Rule: drop rows 0/1. For each ANCHOR CELL in the body, LOOK UP its legend transform (rotate-cw / rotate-180 / transpose / identity). TRANSFORM the color-5 motif's shape per the legend code, then STAMP the transformed shape AT the anchor's position, painted in the anchor's COLOR. Net: each anchor sprouts a transformed stamp of the gray motif in its own color.

0-bg grid with N (2-6) isolated 4-conn components in distinct colors. Components are partitioned into shape-equivalence groups: members of a group share an identical normalized binary mask (random polyomino), groups differ. Rule sorts components by (col,row) and emits an NxN matrix with 8 where shape r == shape c, else 0. N varies so the output size and the equivalence pattern both vary widely.

A zero-background grid contains one connected color-4 template above a full color-9 divider. Below it are isolated color-6 objects. Recolor to 2 exactly the objects whose normalized shape equals one of the four rotations of the template; preserve reflection-only and unrelated objects. Ordinary lessons contain at least one match, at least one non-match, a non-trivially rotated match, and a same-size reflected distractor.
Find every incomplete yellow fragment of a cardinal plus and recolor only the gray cells that complete that plus; dense unrelated gray noise stays gray.

0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~14-17) with: (a) EXACTLY 2 HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAMES of DISTINCT interior sizes drawn from {4×4, 5×5, 4×5, 5×4, 4×6}, each in a distinct color from a 4-color palette; (b) EXACTLY 2 SOLID FILLED RECTANGLES in distinct colors and distinct sizes drawn from {2×2, 2×3, 3×2, 3×3}. Frames and solids are 4-conn isolated; each solid fits inside one of the frames' interiors. Rule: SORT the 2 frames by interior area ASC and SORT the 2 solids by area ASC. PAIR positionally (smaller→smaller, larger→larger). For each pair, PLACE the solid CENTERED inside the paired frame's interior. The original solid location is CLEARED. Net: each solid moves to the size-matched frame center.
Two or three separated solid yellow rectangles. Odd-by-odd rectangles reduce to center crosses; an occasional even rectangle remains unchanged.

Complete a 4x4 partial Latin square over symbols 1..4. Replace each 0 whose row and column jointly leave one possible symbol, synchronously, and repeat for three passes. Generated lessons include one-pass, three-pass, and joint-row/column examples.

Variable-size 0-bg grid with 1-4 foreground colors, each placed as 2-4 ISOLATED SEED POINTS at random distinct positions. Rule (CONNECT SAME-COLORED POINTS IN READING ORDER WITH HORIZONTAL-THEN-VERTICAL TRACES): For EACH COLOR with ≥2 SEED POINTS: sort points in READING ORDER (row-major). For consecutive pairs (p_i, p_{i+1}): draw a horizontal-then-vertical L-PATH from p_i to p_{i+1} — first move HORIZONTALLY from p_i's column to p_{i+1}'s column on p_i's row, then VERTICALLY from p_i's row to p_{i+1}'s row on p_{i+1}'s column. PAINT all path cells in that color. Net: same-color points chain together via row-major-ordered L-paths.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~8-10 by ~11-14) with exactly TWO color-3 (green) endpoint cells and several color-9 (maroon) WALL cells forming partial barriers (e.g., 2-3 vertical walls with single-cell gaps). Endpoints placed at distant corners so the shortest path must detour around walls. Rule: locate the two color-3 cells. Run 4-connected BFS treating 0-cells as walkable and 9-cells as walls. Find the shortest path between the endpoints. Paint all INTERIOR cells of the path (excluding the two endpoints) with color 8 on top of the input. Walls and endpoints preserved. Output color set: {0, 3, 8, 9}.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w=9) with: (a) FULL-HEIGHT GRAY (color 5) DIVIDER COLUMN at column 4 (the exact middle); (b) LEFT SIDE (cols 0..3) has 2-3 ISOLATED NON-{0, 5} CELLS placed at distinct random positions, each painted with a color drawn from {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9}; (c) RIGHT SIDE (cols 5..8) starts ENTIRELY bg-0. Left cells are constrained to fit so their right mirror lands in-bounds. Rule (MIRROR LEFT-SIDE COLORS ACROSS THE GRAY DIVIDER): identify the full-height GRAY (color 5) DIVIDER COLUMN at col div = 4. For EACH non-{0, 5} CELL at position (r, c) where c < div: COMPUTE the MIRROR position (r, 2*div - c) on the right side. IF the mirror cell is currently bg-0: PAINT it with the SAME COLOR as the source. If the mirror cell is already non-0, SKIP. The divider and the source left-side cells stay unchanged. Net: the left half's scattered colors are reflected across the gray divider to populate the right side, producing left-right mirror symmetry.
Each singleton seed paints its own column upward to the top edge.

Select the unique largest 4-connected color-3 template, normalize its bounding-box origin, and stamp it at the color-1 and color-2 anchors. The unchanged Racket rule paints only their in-bounds intersection in 8 on a new zero grid. Smaller green distractors and clipping are supported.
Corner legend gives source and target colors for body recoloring.
Sparse non-bg content with bg padding; rule crops to a non-trivial 2D bbox of the non-bg cells.

Two zero rows and two zero columns split an 8x8 input into nine 2x2 panels.  At each local coordinate, equal non-1 colors on the left and right paint the intervening middle-column cell; equal non-1 colors on the top and bottom paint the intervening middle-row cell.  Horizontal wins at a center-cell conflict.  A four-profile schedule explicitly teaches unequal-color near misses, crossing priority, target overwrite, outer-middle fills, and one-sided controls.

Find every isolated 2x2 color-2 block and its four distinct diagonal markers. Rotate the marker values one corner forward around the block (TL->TR->BR->BL->TL), then extend each new corner value outward along its diagonal through cells that were 0 in the input. Stop at the edge or any nonzero input cell. A canonical near-block exception suppresses a candidate zero beside a color-2 cell when exactly one further diagonal zero remains before the following cell/edge; that ray stops without painting the candidate.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-12) with SEVERAL COLOR-1 (blue) CONNECTED COMPONENTS: (a) 1-2 LEFT-EDGE shapes from a bank of 3 (vertical tri-line, 2×2 square, L-shape) with at least one cell at col 0; (b) 1-2 INTERIOR shapes from a bank of 3 (2×2 square, L-shape, horizontal tri-line) placed entirely in c ≥ 1 with 1-cell padding. Components are 4-conn isolated. Rule (BORDER-TOUCH RECOLOR): for EACH color-1 connected component, check if ANY of its cells has column 0. If yes (touches left border), RECOLOR the ENTIRE component to COLOR 4 (yellow). Otherwise keep it as color 1. Net: blue blobs touching col 0 turn yellow; interior blue blobs stay blue.
For each nonzero color independently, add the missing fourth corner of the axis-aligned rectangle determined by its three input cells.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~10-13) with: (a) exactly TWO color-1 (blue) cells aligned horizontally or vertically — these define a SPAN (Bresenham line, but here a straight line); (b) several non-1 blobs of distinct colors. EXACTLY ONE blob has cells that intersect the span (the target); the rest are distractors. Rule: take the first non-1 object whose cells touch the span. Crop it to its bbox and recolor ALL its non-bg cells to 8 (cyan), 0 elsewhere. Output is a small grid of just the target object's silhouette in cyan.

A zero-background grid contains 2-4 same-color 4-connected sparse objects. Each object's tight bounding box has at least one hole and object bounding boxes do not overlap. Fill every component's bounding box with that component's color on a fresh zero canvas. Scheduled repeated-color scenes teach that disconnected objects are processed separately.

For every interior black cell, inspect the cells immediately above and below it in the same column. Recolor the black cell red iff both neighbors are green; preserve the green endpoints and every other cell.

Generate a sparse 0-background grid with one isolated straight red (2) component, one isolated non-straight red tree, and a one- or two-cell non-red decoy. Recolor only the two extrema of each red component whose whole 4-connected object is horizontal or vertical; leave every non-straight red component and every non-red object unchanged. A three-step schedule cycles T, L, and stair-shaped negative witnesses.

0-bg grid (size varies) with one color-X shape (one cell replaced by 8) and distractor shapes of other colors. Rule: crop the X-shape's bbox (including the 8) and output it with the 8 filled in as X. The grid size, shape, 8-cell, distractors and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~32 distinct). Output is the cropped shape, so bounded; inputs are large.

A compact 4x4-to-8x8 grid contains four distinct nonzero values at the fixed source cells (1,1), (1,2), (2,1), and (2,2). The output preserves the input shape, places those values at top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right respectively, and makes every other cell zero. A four-profile lesson schedule includes an exact canonical 4x4 anchor, a canonical-scale corner-decoy contrast, and two larger fixed decoy layouts whose cells are ignored by the rule.

0-bg grid (h, w ~9-14) with 1-3 SOLID rectangles in color 1 (blue), each at least 3×3, axis-aligned, non-overlapping (separated by background). Rule: for each color-1 4-conn object, for each cell (r, c) of that object with r STRICTLY between obj_r1 and obj_r2 AND c STRICTLY between obj_c1 and obj_c2 (i.e. interior cell, not on the bbox edge), clear it to 0. Net: every solid blue rectangle becomes a hollow BORDER (1-cell-thick ring), interior becomes bg. Edge cells of the rectangle stay 1.

One connected template of 4..7 cells and 2..5 singleton markers. Stamp its binary bounding-box shape at each marker, recolored to that marker; clip individual out-of-bounds cells, with later row-major markers winning overlaps.
Only the component with the greatest onion depth is kept and recolored.
skills: cross-component comparison, inner-depth ranking, selective preservation

summary: Read the unique code in row 0: 1=identity, 2=rotate 90 degrees clockwise, 3=rotate 180 degrees, 4=rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise, 5=flip left-right, and 6=flip up-down. Among the three separated monochrome objects below the blank row 1, select the unique object with exactly one enclosed hole, crop it tightly, apply the coded transform, and scale every cell to a 2x2 block. Discard the two solid distractors. The curriculum cycles all six codes, spans the declared size ranges, retains regular exact canonical-profile anchors, and uses transform-visible asymmetric holed objects.

A 0-background grid is divided by complete wall rows and columns into rectangular rooms. Walls use colors 1/7/9 and room interiors use only 0 and green marker color 3. Count the green markers in each room, preserve the walls, clear every room interior, and fill the unique maximum-count room completely with cyan 8. The generated curriculum reproduces all canonical layouts and regularly makes a smaller room denser while a different room has the larger raw count, refuting density and size shortcuts.
skills: roomwise counting, argmax selection, same-size highlight

summary: Rotate a sparse multicolor square grid 90 degrees clockwise.

Cell (0,0) contains a one-based rank R. Clear it, find the 2-3 4-connected nonzero objects, sort them by CELL COUNT ascending, choose the R-th object, crop it to its tight bbox, and scale the crop 2x2. Generated lessons deliberately distinguish cell-count rank from the canonical-fitting bbox-area shortcut.

One to three disjoint rectangular holes lie in a modal background. Each hole contains one sparse colored stamp and no other active color. For each stamp color independently, take the stamp's bounding-box pattern and repeat it by row/column modulo across the entire containing hole, using the stamp's original top-left as the phase origin.

Separated color-6 objects on a 0 background. Recolor each 4-connected object by topology: one or more enclosed holes -> 8; no enclosed holes -> 2. Scheduled examples include non-frame and multi-hole positives, leaky C-shaped negatives, and large hole-free negatives.

Read the non-zero top-left rectangle as a 2-D seed tile. Find the connected irregular color-8 mask in the lower-right region. Starting at the mask bounding-box top-left, replace each mask cell by the seed value at the corresponding row and column modulo the seed height and width; preserve every non-mask cell.
Exact length-5 orange bars have their center cell recolored cyan.
3-5 single-cell markers in distinct colors at distinct positions.

0-bg grid (h = ch + 4, w = 2*cw + 3 with ch=4-5, cw=4-5) structured as: (a) ROW 0 = PRIORITY LEGEND with 3 DISTINCT COLORS (from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9}, exclude 8) at cols 1, 2, 3 (sorted left = highest priority); (b) FULL-WIDTH COLOR-8 HORIZONTAL WALL at ROW 2; (c) FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-8 VERTICAL WALLS at cols 0, cw+1, w-1 (outer + 1 internal divider) starting from row 2; (d) FULL-WIDTH COLOR-8 HORIZONTAL WALL at ROW h-1. This creates an R x C chamber grid (1-2 rows by 2-3 cols). (e) Inside each chamber: 1-2 SEED CELLS in legend colors. Rule (CHAMBER FILL BY LEGEND PRIORITY): for EACH CHAMBER, identify the SEEDS present and find the one with the HIGHEST PRIORITY (= EARLIEST in the row-0 legend). FILL the entire chamber's 0-cells with that priority color. Walls + legend stay. Net: each chamber gets flooded with its highest-priority seed color.

0-bg grid (h, w ~11-18) with 4-conn rectangular components in sizes 2, 3, and 4 (1-3 components of each size), all in a SINGLE input color drawn from {4..9} (so input color != target output colors). Components are non-overlapping with ≥1-cell margin. Rule: extract every 4-conn non-bg object. Recolor each based on its CELL COUNT: size 4 → color 1 (blue), size 3 → color 2 (red), size 2 → color 3 (green), any other size → color 5 (gray). Input color is discarded; output uses the size-keyed palette.
Trace outward from both extreme cyan cells, reflect once from the edge wall, and paint the strictly longer diagonal path green.
Infer an exact-position dihedral transform and color mapping from panels 1→2, then apply both to panel 3 while preserving unmapped query colors.

Split the four color-9-separated panels. Plus-dilate each panel's single object, compare the grown silhouettes up to rotation/reflection, and output the ORIGINAL object from the uniquely grown panel, cropped and recolored 8. Generated rebuttal examples make raw-shape and count-only selection give the wrong or an ambiguous answer.

Multicolor grid (h, w~5-10) with PALETTE OF 3-6 DISTINCT COLORS (EXCLUDING 7) where: (a) TOP-1 color has ~30-45% of cells; (b) TOP-2 color has ~20-30% of cells; STRICTLY top1_count > top2_count > each minor count (gap ≥1); (c) remaining MINOR colors fill the rest in a layout (uniform/ascending/single/long-tail) and arrangement (random/stripes/block/checker/gradient). Color 7 NEVER appears in input. Rule (KEEP TOP-2 MOST FREQUENT, RECOLOR REST TO 7): compute COLOR-COUNTS over the grid. Identify the TOP-2 most frequent colors. For EACH cell: if its color is in TOP-2, KEEP. Else, RECOLOR to 7. Net: rare minority colors all become 7; dominant duo survives.

A zero-background grid has one color-8 pivot and three or four cells of one other color. Rotate each foreground cell 90 degrees clockwise around the pivot, preserve its color, keep the pivot fixed, and clear the old foreground positions.

Row 0 is a dense color key with gray (5) at the column of one vertical cyan (8) line. From the observed line top through its observed bottom, copy key-row colors into an expanding triangle centered on that line; keep the line cyan and all cells outside the active triangle gray.

0-bg grid (h~5-10, w~8-14) with 3+ ACTIVE ROWS each containing 2-many NON-BG CELLS in a SINGLE color C (from {1..9}\{0, 2}) arranged via one of 5 ROW PATTERNS (scattered/endpoints_only/ascending/many_cells/alternating). Endpoint separation (near/medium/far) and intermediate density (0..0.4) vary. Leftmost and rightmost non-bg cells in each active row are ≥2 cols apart. Rule (FILL BETWEEN ROW EXTREMES WITH 2): For EACH ROW r: find the LEFTMOST (c_min) and RIGHTMOST (c_max) non-bg cells. For EACH cell (r, c) with c_min < c < c_max AND g[r][c] == 0: PAINT g[r][c] = 2 (red). Existing non-bg cells stay. Net: each row gets red interior filling between its extreme non-bg cells.

0-bg grid (size varies). A memorized radius-1 (3x3) context table recolors each cell whose 9-cell neighborhood matches an entry to 1/2/3/9. This generator stamps interior table windows on a 0-background lattice so the recolors fire. Grid size, stamp choice and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct). The table is memorized, so OUTPUTS are bounded by the 34 interior contexts; INPUTS are large.

A 0-background grid contains exactly two isolated gray (5) cells in the same column; together they mark a sparse vertical mirror axis. One to three connected, distinctly colored motifs occupy only one source side, although a motif may touch the axis itself. Preserve the markers and all source cells, then add each non-{0,5} cell at column 2*axis-c with the same row and color. The result completes vertical symmetry around the marker column.
Each tile's majority nonzero color becomes one macro-grid cell.
skills: tile summarization, color counting, reduced output

summary: 0-bg grid (h~14-19, w~15-21) with 1-2 FRAMES, each a RECT-OUTLINE of size 7-9 × 7-10 in a DISTINCT color from {1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}. EACH FRAME contains EXACTLY ONE COLOR-2 (red) DOT cell strictly inside (≥2-cell padding from frame borders). Frames placed non-overlapping with 1-cell padding. Rule (DRAW CROSS THROUGH EACH FRAME's INNER DOT UP TO WALLS): For EACH FRAME and its INTERIOR DOT at (dr, dc): PAINT a CROSS (horizontal + vertical line) through (dr, dc) extending in all 4 directions until hitting the FRAME's INNER WALLS. Paint in COLOR-2. Frame outlines stay. Net: each red dot becomes a red cross stretching across its frame.

Small grid (h~5-12, w~5-12) with several non-bg cells scattered across SOME columns (the ACTIVE columns — at least one is fully empty, at least one has a non-bg cell). No color-8 (cyan) appears in input. Rule: (1) TILE the input 2×2 so the output is (2h, 2w). (2) For each output column c whose underlying input column ((c mod w)) contains AT LEAST one non-bg cell, OVERLAY color 8 (cyan) into every output bg cell of that column. Output columns whose underlying input column is entirely bg stay all-0 in the output. Original non-bg cells are preserved in their tiled positions. Net: a 2×2 tile of the input where every active column is shaded cyan in its empty cells.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-13) with 2-4 PAIRS of equal-colored ENDPOINT MARKERS in DISTINCT colors from {1..9}. EACH PAIR is aligned EITHER HORIZONTALLY (same row, ≥2-cell gap between endpoints) OR VERTICALLY (same col, ≥2-cell gap) — orientation chosen once per task. Each pair occupies a distinct row (or column). No other cells. Rule (BRIDGE ENDPOINT PAIRS INTO FULL SEGMENTS): For EACH PAIR of same-color cells at (r, c1) and (r, c2) with c1 < c2 (horizontal), PAINT all cells (r, c1)..(r, c2) with that color (fill the gap). For VERTICAL pairs at (r1, c) and (r2, c), PAINT (r1..r2, c). Endpoints stay. Net: each endpoint pair turns into a full colored line segment.

Exactly three isolated distinct-colour blobs appear on a zero background. Crop each blob to its bounding box, align the crops at their top-left corners, keep normalized cells occupied by at least two blobs, paint them cyan (8), and crop the result to content.
Horizontal gallery sorted by pixel count, height, width, then color.

0-bg grid where: (a) row 0 has K color-1 cells (the AREA target K); (b) col 0 has W color-3 cells (the WIDTH target W); (c) 2-4 OBJECTS in non-{1, 3} colors scattered in interior cells (not in row 0 or col 0). EXACTLY ONE object has size == K AND bbox width == W. Other objects are distractors with size != K OR width != W. Rule: read K from row 0 (count of 1s), W from col 0 (count of 3s). Find the unique object with size K AND width W. Paint it in color 8 on a fresh canvas; all else becomes 0.

0-bg grid with several connected components in distinct non-zero colors. Some have TALL bboxes (height > width), others have SQUARE or WIDE bboxes (height ≤ width). Rule: for each component, if bbox h > w (strictly taller than wide), recolor all its cells to 8. Otherwise preserve original color. Output is the same grid with tall components recolored.

A black grid contains red singleton seeds. Exactly one red seed lies on the border and one to four well-separated red decoys lie at least two cells inside it. Grow every seed to its clipped 3x3 neighborhood, select the unique grown region touching the border, crop it tightly, and output that solid rectangle in color 8. Consecutive lesson samples cover the 2x3 horizontal-edge, 3x2 vertical-edge, and 2x2 corner answers.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~10-12) with: (a) one PROTOTYPE component — a color-8 (cyan) ORIGIN cell + 2-4 color-1 (blue) BODY cells connected to the origin; (b) 2-3 single-cell ANCHORS in distinct colors from {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9} placed isolated elsewhere (≥3 Manhattan distance from the prototype). Rule: find the prototype (component containing color-8). Build a binary STAMP from the prototype's bbox (non-bg cells = 1, else 0). For each ANCHOR (single non-{0, 1, 8} cell), translate the stamp so the origin lands on the anchor, paint the stamp's '1' cells with the ANCHOR's color. Overlapping stamp cells become color 9.

A 0-background grid contains 1..4 isolated, distinctly colored, interior 4-connected blobs.  Erase each blob and paint all zero cells immediately adjacent to it in the four cardinal directions with that blob's color.  Generated lessons include ordinary canonical-scale blobs, smaller broad-support blobs, and 3x3 ring blobs whose enclosed center is also painted.

A centered yellow(4) cross divides an odd rectangular grid into TL, TR, BL, and BR quadrants of the same shape.  Each quadrant has one distinct role color plus background 0.  For every local cell, output the first nonzero value in priority order BR, TL, TR, BL.

An odd square color-7 grid has a full vertical color-4 axis through its middle column.  The axis centre and both ends of the middle row are color 8.  A connected, multi-color figure occupies only the left side and touches the axis on every active row; the matching right-side cells are blank.  Preserve non-7 cells and copy each non-7 cell into a blank cell at its 180-degree rotational counterpart, thereby completing the figure while leaving the axis and anchors unchanged.

Read contiguous transform codes from row 0 until the first zero. Crop the monochrome motif below the blank separator row. Output the original crop followed by every cumulative transform state, top-aligned with one blank column between panels. Codes 1/2/3/4 mean rotate-cw/rotate-180/rotate-ccw/flip-lr.
1 connected motif in some non-9 color + 1 single-cell color-9 marker.

A canonical-sized zero-background grid contains 2-4 separated blue 4-connected components. Component sizes follow an observable profile and have one unique maximum. Recolor exactly that largest component to 7.
Columns contain same-color endpoint pairs with empty cells between.

0-bg grid. ONE free-standing COLOR-7 TEMPLATE polyomino (3-5 cells), plus 1-3 hollow rectangular FRAMES in distinct border colors. Each frame has a MARKER cell (color 1/2/3/4) just outside one corner, selecting a transform (1=rot-cw, 2=rot-180, 3=flip-lr, 4=identity). Rule: transform the template by each frame's marker, recolor it to the marker color, and centre it inside that frame; erase the free template and the markers.

0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-1 (blue) SHAPE and ONE color-2 (red) SHAPE (random connected polyominoes whose normalized forms share >=1 cell and differ in >=1 cell), placed apart, plus an optional non-{1,2} decoy. Rule: normalize each, XOR them (cells in exactly one), and output the XOR re-normalized to its bbox, painted COLOR 8 (cyan). The grid size, the two shapes (which set the XOR) and their positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed shapes, ~12 distinct).

Rows 0 and 1 are an aligned source-to-destination color legend. Remove those rows and recolor each body source cell exactly once; body colors that are not legend sources remain unchanged. Ordinary lessons vary key columns and sparse body geometry, and regularly include a destination that is also another source so iterative remapping is visibly wrong.
Replay accent-color stencil positions from A->B onto same-support C.

0-bg grid (h~11-18, w~11-18) with TWO NESTED COLOR-5 RECTANGULAR FRAMES (concentric): (a) OUTER FRAME — hollow rectangle of size oh × ow (7..12 each), placed at random interior position, painted entirely in COLOR 5 (border-only); (b) INNER FRAME — hollow rectangle of size ih × iw (3..5 each), nested STRICTLY INSIDE the outer frame with at least 1-cell gap on all sides, also painted in COLOR 5. Inside the inner frame's interior: (c) INNER BLOB — a small shape (1-4 cells) drawn from _INNER_SHAPES bank, painted in INNER_COLOR (non-5 distinct color). Outside the outer frame: (d) OUTER BLOB — a small shape (1-4 cells) drawn from _OUTER_SHAPES bank, painted in OUTER_COLOR (non-5 distinct color). The INNER blob has NESTING DEPTH 2 (inside 2 frames); the OUTER blob has NESTING DEPTH 0 (outside all frames). Rule (PICK THE MAX-DEPTH NON-5 BLOB, OUTPUT ITS BBOX-CROPPED MASK IN ITS OWN COLOR): for EACH non-5 blob in the input, COMPUTE its NESTING DEPTH = number of rectangular 5-FRAMES whose bbox strictly contains every cell of the blob. SELECT the blob with MAXIMUM DEPTH (ties broken by largest size). CROP it to its bbox. OUTPUT the crop with the blob's color preserved, bg 0. All frames and other blobs are discarded. Net: only the most-deeply-nested colored blob survives, output as a small cropped grid. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=23): output drawn from small _INNER_SHAPES × color bank.

One to four colors each mark two diagonal corners of a rectangle. Draw every bounding-box border in first-reading-order color order; later borders overwrite earlier ones at overlaps. Native profiles include both diagonal orientations, overlapping boxes, and spans of eight or more.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-12) with 2-5 separated 2×2 WINDOWS, each containing TWO color-3 (green) cells on a DIAGONAL — either the main diagonal ((0,0) + (1,1)) or the anti-diagonal ((0,1) + (1,0)) — and the other two cells empty (0). Windows are 4-conn isolated (≥ 3 cells apart). Rule: for every 2×2 window whose two diagonal cells are color 3 and the other two are 0, PAINT the two empty corners with color 7 (orange) to complete the 2×2 with the diagonal 3s and the anti-diagonal 7s. The color-3 cells stay. Net: each diagonal-pair window becomes a checkerboard 2×2 with 3 on one diagonal and 7 on the other.

Fixed 7×7 0-bg grid with: (a) TWO FULL HORIZONTAL DIVIDER ROWS at rows 2 and 5, each painted entirely in a SINGLE non-zero hline_color; (b) TWO VERTICAL DIVIDER COLUMNS at cols 2 and 5, each containing the same COLOR (v1 for col 2, v2 for col 5) at ALL non-divider rows (rows 0, 1, 3, 4, 6). hline_color, v1, and v2 are 3 distinct non-zero colors. Other cells are 0. Rule: DETECT the FULL NONZERO horizontal DIVIDER ROWS and the CONSTANT vertical DIVIDER COLUMNS. COMPRESS the 7×7 grid into a REPRESENTATIVE smaller grid: keep only ONE REPRESENTATIVE ROW per group between horizontal dividers, and ONE REPRESENTATIVE COL per group between vertical dividers. The dividers themselves are stripped; output is the intersection-cells matrix. Net: input is a divider-decorated grid; output is its compressed form (group representatives only).
2-5 objects (varied shapes/sizes) in distinct colors, sorted by size then color and hstacked.
Cmd at (0,0); 2-3 colors with exactly 2 endpoints each; routed L-paths can overlap.

Rows 0 and 1 contain two or three aligned, disjoint source/destination color pairs. Every source appears at least twice below the legend and is recolored to its paired destination; any destination colors already in the body remain unchanged. Every fourth ordinary sample uses the exact canonical role-normalized body morphology (with width 8 or 9).
Generate separated blue vertical triples, a horizontal triple, and a vertical length-four exactness witness; recolor only exact vertical triples red.

Choose one complete keyed-offset scene profile.  The grid contains one color-9 reference, a connected asymmetric color-8 offset cloud, and three or four distinct anchors from colors 2,3,4,5.  Anchor colors encode quarter-turn rotations 0/90/180/270 and paint colors 4/5/6/7.  The rule replays the rotated cloud at every anchor in row-major order and max-merges paint after writing each anchor. Five official and five branch witness profiles remain common; procedural connected clouds, dimensions, references and anchor layouts prevent a ten-template-only curriculum.
Fill the straight segment for every color occurring exactly twice on one row or one column; leave singleton, diagonal-pair, and triple distractor colors unchanged.

A single color-9 marker at a grid corner selects the rotation applied to a separate one-color connected body: top-left=identity, top-right=90° clockwise, bottom-right=180°, bottom-left=90° counter-clockwise. Remove the marker, crop the body to its bounding box, and emit the rotated crop.

On a zero background, find all 2..8 cells of the single nonzero color. Compute their minimal bounding rectangle and return a fresh grid of the same size containing only that rectangle's one-cell outline in the same color. Interior source markers are cleared.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several closed COLOR-5 (gray) ROOMS (hollow rectangles, >=3x3), placed apart. ONE room holds a single color-2 (red) SEED; the other rooms hold color-6 (magenta) DECORATIONS. Rule: flood-fill from the seed through 0/2 cells (4-connected); every reached empty cell becomes COLOR 8 (cyan). Because the seed's room is closed, only that room's interior fills; the other rooms and the outside are unreachable and unchanged. The grid size, the number / size / position of the rooms, which room is seeded, and the decorations all vary freely (was a fixed two-compartment layout).
Complete a colored pattern across the main diagonal, preserving its source cells.
Rank candidate components by area, transform the requested one, and center it in a frame.
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.

Find the four isolated coloured objects in row-major bounding-box order. Emit a 4x4 red(2)/black(0) matrix whose entries mark whether each pair of binary shapes is identical under any of the eight dihedral symmetries.

A 25..29 by 22..29 black canvas contains one to three separated solid green rectangles with canonical dimensions 2x3, 2x4, 2x5, 3x2, 3x3, or 4x2.  For each seed rectangle (r,c,rh,rw), retain the seed and, for every k>=1, stamp rh-by-rw copies at row r+k*rh and columns c-k*rw and c+k*rw, clipping copies at the grid boundary.
Orange components touching exactly one border recolored blue.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~6-13 by ~8-16) containing 1-5 connected components per color in {2 (red), 3 (green), 4 (yellow)}. All components are 8-conn isolated (≥1-cell buffer). Some distractor cells in other non-{0,2,3,4} colors may be scattered (rule ignores them). At least one of n2, n3, n4 differs (so output isn't uniform). Rule: count connected components of color 2 (call it n2), color 3 (n3), color 4 (n4). Build 3 × max(n2, n3, n4) output. Row 0 has color 2 in the first n2 cells (rest 0); row 1 has color 3 in first n3 cells; row 2 has color 4 in first n4 cells. Bar chart with row colors 2, 3, 4.

Fold the unique singleton's quadrant-local position into the north-west separator-sized output canvas. Ordinary draws vary all four quadrants, centered versus off-center dividers, dimensions, colors, and local position.

Rows contain three contiguous color runs: left, modal middle, right. The middle run is the global mode and its right edge varies by row; the rule preserves per-row color counts while aligning those middle runs to a common right edge.

Even rectangular grid split into TL/TR/BL/BR quadrants. Corresponding cells are overlaid with priority TR > BL > BR > TL. Every generated input includes conflicts that visibly distinguish each adjacent priority decision, while colors, positions, dimensions, and extra occupancy vary.

On a zero-background grid, find the uniquely largest non-zero connected component.  For each column occupied by that source shape, look strictly below the bottommost source cell.  If the other non-zero colour occurs there, paint that column from immediately below the source through the bottom row in the marker colour.  Preserve the source and all distractor dots.

Hollow rectangular frames and four-connected singleton components on zero. Erase the singletons; fill local even-parity interior cells only when their count equals that color's singleton count. Scenes include all, partial and absent count matches, varied colors, sizes, positions and diagonal singles.

A zero-background grid has a nonempty, single-color motif in the field above the last row and left of the reserved final column.  The last row starts with 2-6 distinct nonzero command colors followed only by zeros. Crop the motif to its bounding box, make one copy per command color, recolor every occupied motif cell with that command, and concatenate the copies left-to-right with one blank column between adjacent copies.
Append a horizontal reflection of the complete input grid: every output row is the input row followed by that row in reverse order.

Three distinct colors form a row-0 legend whose cells may be contiguous, spaced, or offset.  One canonical-core profile has a single body motif per color; the diagnostic profiles add early small decoys before a uniquely larger body motif.  The largest motifs appear in a body order that differs from the legend.  Read all nonzero legend cells left-to-right, pick the largest 4-connected body component of each color, crop its bounding box, and pack the crops horizontally with one zero column between them.

0-bg grid (h,w vary by difficulty). A color-7 (orange) hollow RECTANGULAR FRAME at a RANDOM position/size. ROW 0 holds BLUE (color 1) COLUMN markers; COL 0 holds RED (color 2) ROW markers. Some markers sit on columns/rows that are STRICTLY INSIDE the frame (a random subset of interior cols/rows) and some are DECOYS on cols/rows outside the frame. Rule (FILL ROW x COL INTERSECTIONS INSIDE THE FRAME): take the frame bbox; for each blue-marked col c and red-marked row r with the intersection (r,c) strictly inside the frame, paint (r,c) color 8 (cyan). Decoy intersections (one or both markers outside) stay empty. Grid size, frame placement, the interior marker lattice and the decoys all vary freely (was a fixed 10x12 grid with 6 hardcoded layouts).

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~6-8) where 3-4 RANDOMLY-CHOSEN COLUMNS each have 2-3 NON-BG CELLS at random rows in various colors drawn from {2..9}. Other columns may have 0 or 1 single cells (at ~50% chance). The ≥3 active columns ensure the output differs from input. Rule (PER-COLUMN, KEEP ONLY THE BOTTOMMOST NON-BG CELL): For EACH COLUMN c in [0, w-1]: find the MAXIMUM ROW r where g[r][c] ≠ 0 (the bottommost non-bg cell). KEEP the cell at (r, c) with its color. ERASE all OTHER non-bg cells in column c (set them to 0). Columns with no non-bg cell stay all 0. Net: each column collapses to its bottom-most painted cell only.

Dense 0/2/3/4/7 noise contains one color-8 chiral stencil and two to four isolated color-3 dihedral copies.  At least one copy is a true reflection, so rotations-only rules fail; the selected Racket rule recolors all matching copy cells to 8.
A 2×2 or 3×3 colored square is tiled into a 2N×2N output with the original, clockwise, counterclockwise, and 180° rotations in TL/TR/BL/BR.

Find the first uniform row/column, summarize four inner regions by their modal colors, and place those modes around the divider-colored cross of a 3x3 output; the default lesson schedule alternates an ignored-border counterexample with broad family coverage.
Count all nonzero dots and emit a bottom-row bar of that length in the dot color.

Multicolor grid (h, w ∈ 2-18, by difficulty), palette of 2-9 distinct colors drawn at random (may include 0), filled by TEXTURE ∈ {noise / sparse / blob / stripes / gradient / checkerboard / frame / ring / plus} via fill_texture. After base fill: (a) apply_bg_density (0-50%) introduces bg sparsity; (b) apply_noise_overlay (0-10%) flips random cells; (c) apply_border per BORDER_MODE ∈ {free, always_bg, always_fg} may overwrite the outer border. The grid is GENERALLY NOT TRANSPOSE-SYMMETRIC (rectangular or asymmetric content), so the rule has visible effect. Rule (TRANSPOSE THE GRID — SWAP ROWS AND COLUMNS): OUTPUT[c][r] = INPUT[r][c] for all (r, c). Result is a w×h grid where the input's rows become the output's columns and vice versa. Net: the entire grid is reflected across the main diagonal — each cell value moves to its transposed position.

Cell (0,0) is a nonzero legend color. Select every other cell with that color, grow each selected seed by the full 3x3 Chebyshev-radius-one stencil, clip the stencil at grid edges, take the union, recolor it cyan (8), and discard the legend plus all non-selected colors.
Place a repeated-color key beside a matching lattice of identical gray 3x3 shapes. Recolor each complete gray tile from the corresponding key cell while preserving the key and background.
Paired blue edge markers define full rows/columns; recolor every red object intersecting or one cell from a marked line blue.

Infer the modal background color and the three vertical column-regions separated by two full-background columns. Each region contains one distinct foreground color and background holes. Fill only those holes with the NEXT region's color in a cyclic left-to-right rotation; preserve all original foreground cells and the separator columns.

0-bg grid (h, w~9-11) with 3 SAME-SHAPE BLOBS each a 2×2 SOLID SQUARE in COLOR 1. The 3 blobs are placed at NON-TOUCHING positions (1-cell padding) so that their bbox-min-distance-to-grid-border values are all STRICTLY DISTINCT (Chebyshev distance from bbox to any of the 4 grid edges is the minimum of row-from-top, row-from-bottom, col-from-left, col-from-right). Rule (RECOLOR THE FARTHEST-FROM-BORDER BLOB TO COLOR 7): for EACH blob, compute its BBOX CENTER's DISTANCE to any GRID BORDER (Chebyshev). Find the blob with the STRICTLY MAXIMUM distance (the most interior blob). RECOLOR all cells of that blob from 1 to COLOR 7. Other blobs stay at 1. Net: the most interior blob turns orange; the border-adjacent blobs stay blue.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-20, w ∈ 11-22, by difficulty) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 RED SOURCE SHAPE drawn from _SHAPES bank (5 variants of 4-cell L/S/T/P shapes) — placed at a random non-overlapping position via _place (1-cell padding); (b) ONE MATCHING CANDIDATE in colors[0] (drawn from {3,4,5,6}) with the SAME shape (translation-only equivalent) placed elsewhere; (c) THREE DISTRACTOR CANDIDATES in colors[1:] (each a DIFFERENT shape from _SHAPES \ {source}), all placed at non-overlapping positions. Rule (FIND THE CANDIDATE WHOSE NORMALIZED CELL OFFSETS MATCH THE COLOR-2 SOURCE'S, CROP TO ITS BBOX, RECOLOR TO CYAN-8, OUTPUT): FIND the unique COLOR-2 component → extract its NORMALIZED OFFSETS (subtract min row/col). FOR EACH non-2 non-bg COMPONENT: COMPUTE its normalized offsets. SELECT the unique component whose offsets EQUAL the source's offsets. CROP it to its bbox. RECOLOR every cell of that crop to COLOR 8 (cyan). OUTPUT the cyan crop. Net: same-shape matching across colors yields a cyan version of the matched candidate. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=5): 5 source shapes × cyan recolor = 5 canonical outputs.
Mirror a 3x2 binary source left-to-right into a 3x4 strip, then stack [vertical-flip, original, vertical-flip] to make a 9x4 output.

0-bg grid with several HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAMES (rings, each >=3x3) in distinct colors, well separated. Rule: fill each frame's interior hole with the frame's color onto a blank canvas and drop the outline (output = just the filled holes, one solid rectangle per frame).

Infer the exact-color dihedral transform mapping square panel A to B, apply it to C, and recolor its nonzero cells to the first nonzero header color. Body separator columns have color 8; header position varies.

Independently compact every row to the left: remove zero gaps, preserve the non-zero values' left-to-right order, then pad the right suffix with zeros.  Official 4x6/(3,2,0,3), 3x5/(2,2,2), and 4x7/(3,1,3,0) row-count profiles are mixed with lawful generalized scenes that contain empty, singleton, repeated-color, gapped, and already-compacted row branches without allowing whole-grid no-ops.

On background 0, find the same-color 4-connected components. Select the unique component with the greatest CELL COUNT, breaking no tie because generated lessons forbid ties. Return the rectangular crop of the ORIGINAL input at that component's bounding box, preserving its color and all background holes or indentations. Distractors remain outside the selected bounding box. A four-position lesson schedule includes canonical 3x3/4x4 hollow frames, a larger-bbox-but-smaller decoy, a second component sharing the target color, and irregular non-square targets in varied reading-order positions.
Use row 0 as a column legend. Replace each body colour-8 cell with its column's non-zero header colour; leave colour-8 cells below empty headers and all other cells unchanged.
Fill the zero-valued interior of every separated monochromatic hollow rectangular outline with that outline's own color.
A square grid contains four separated monochrome objects. Exactly three objects are left-right symmetric and exactly one is not; crop the unique left-right-asymmetric object to its bounding box.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-11) with 3 BLOBS in DISTINCT non-zero colors (from 1..9) at non-touching positions (grow_blob with no shared cells). Each blob has 2-4 cells; blob shapes may vary. Rule (SORT BLOBS + HORIZONTAL GALLERY PACK): identify each BLOB as a connected component. SORT blobs by some criterion (e.g., size descending, color, or position). CROP each to its BBOX. PACK the crops HORIZONTALLY in sorted order, possibly with 1-COL GAPS. Output WIDTH = sum of bbox widths + gaps; HEIGHT = MAX bbox height. Net: 3 blobs → horizontal gallery in sorted order.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one connected payload (colors other than 0/2/3), one red source marker (2), and one green destination marker (3). Translate the entire payload, preserving all of its colors, by the vector from red to green onto a blank grid; remove both markers and the original payload. Grid dimensions, payload size/colors, vector direction, shape, placement, and marker positions vary.

A 0-background grid contains 3-4 separated red(2) vertical bars. For each bar independently, the bottom floor(height/2) cells become cyan(8). Bars vary in height and can be bottom-aligned, top-aligned, floating, or mixed-anchor; output shape is unchanged.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-16) with N_small (1-4) SMALL objects of size ≤3 (singles, pairs, triples) and N_large (1-3) LARGE objects of size ≥4 (rectangles, L/cross/blob/Z shapes, hollow rings). All objects are 4-disconnected (1-cell buffer); input colors drawn from non-{0, 2, 8} palette so the rule's output colors are unambiguous. Rule: extract all 4-conn non-bg objects. For each object: if obj-size ≤ 3 → recolor every cell to color 2 (red); if obj-size ≥ 4 → recolor to color 8 (cyan). Net: a size-thresholded recolor with cutoff at 3.
Three green rectangle corners imply a yellow missing fourth corner.

Exactly one marker each of colors 1, 2 and 3 defines an axis-aligned rectangle: 1 is the shared corner, 2 fixes its horizontal reach and 3 its vertical reach. Paint the complete outline on a fresh grid in color 8.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~8-10) with: (a) 1-4 NON-TOUCHING COLOR-6 BLOBS placed in the upper rows (rows 0..h-3, leaving the bottom row for the marker) — each blob is a 1-2 cell 4-connected component grown via grow_blob with a used-set track to avoid touching neighbors; (b) ONE COLOR-2 MARKER at fixed BOTTOM-LEFT position (h-1, 0). The marker has enough horizontal clearance for the extension to fit within the grid (col 0..w-1). Rule (EXTEND MARKER RIGHT BY COUNT OF 6-BLOBS, PAINT COLOR 3): COUNT n = number of 4-CONNECTED color-6 COMPONENTS. find the color-2 marker at position (mr, mc). PAINT the cells (mr, mc+1), (mr, mc+2), ..., (mr, mc+n) with COLOR 3, but ONLY where the original cell is bg-0 (don't overwrite 6-cells). 6-blobs and the marker stay unchanged. Net: a horizontal color-3 bar of length n appears to the right of the 2-marker, encoding the count of 6-blobs as an extension length.

0-bg grid with: (a) ONE non-rectangular BLOB of color 1 (the template); (b) ONE KEY cell whose color is in {2,3,4,5} at a corner (2=identity, 3=cw, 4=180, 5=ccw). Rule: extract the color-1 bbox as a template, rotate it by the key, and paste it (color 1) centered on a blank same-size canvas.

skills: multi-source BFS, graph Voronoi reasoning, tie handling
summary: Rectangular rooms are joined only by 7-doorways through 1/9 walls. Fill rooms with the nearest seed-room color in graph distance; use 8 for equal nearest distinct colors. Multi-color seed rooms use their smallest color. Includes detours, disconnected rooms, repeated seed colors, and contrastive lessons with three demonstrations.

The unique 8 and 9 markers define a displacement vector. Translate every color-3 source by the 8→9 vector; in an otherwise empty output grid, paint color 7 exactly at translated cells that contain color 4 in the input. Ordinary scenes contain reverse-direction traps and unmatched 3/4 decoys.

0-bg grid (h, w~14-20) with 2-3 HOLLOW color-5 (gray) RECTANGULAR FRAMES of distinct sizes — interior widths from {2, 3, 4} (so outer sizes from {4, 5, 6}). Frames are placed by some position bias (scattered / row-aligned / col-aligned / diagonal / corners) with ≥1-cell margin between them. Rule: for each color-5 FRAME, compute its INTERIOR WIDTH iw (the bbox interior dimension). FILL the frame's interior cells with COLOR = iw + 5 — so width 2 → color 7 (orange), width 3 → color 8 (cyan), width 4 → color 9 (maroon). The gray frame border stays 5. Net: each frame's empty interior gets a width-keyed solid fill.

Read the two hollow color-9 frames from left to right as templates A and B. Crop each occupied interior mask, center them on a common canvas, then read the bottom-row codes in positional order (duplicates included): 4=OR, 5=AND, 6=A-minus-B, 7=XOR. Paint and tightly crop each result with its code and hstack the panels with one zero column between them.

Find each 4-connected red component that is a gapless horizontal or vertical segment. Recolor only its two extreme endpoints cyan (8); leave the red interior unchanged. Bent red components and every non-red object are distractors and remain unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one connected color-2 shape and one connected color-3 shape, separated in the input. Normalize each shape to its own bounding box and overlay them: shared cells become 8, color-2-only cells stay 2, and color-3-only cells stay 3.

On a 0-background grid, find the single connected non-9 template object. Crop its bounding box, count every color-9 marker cell, and repeat the cropped template horizontally that many times with one zero column between consecutive copies. Marker adjacency is irrelevant: count cells, not marker components.
Order colors by row-major first appearance; emit a column when the first-cell row span is at least the column span, otherwise emit a row.
2-3 connected motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions (different max-col).

A 9..15 grid is split horizontally or vertically into cyan(8) and blue(1) regions.  Three to five separated red(2) objects occur in both regions.  Preserve each row's red count per region, compacting left in cyan and right in blue.  A ragged connected object distinguishes this row-wise rule from rigidly sliding whole components.

On a 0-background grid, isolated color-2 seeds emit horizontal color-7 rays and isolated color-1 seeds emit vertical color-8 rays. Color-5 line segments stop rays and remain gray; cells reached by both ray families become color 6. Ordinary draws constructively include both a crossing and a wall-stop witness.
Marker slot provides colors for a clean dice-mask slot in a tiled output.

Keep every red(2) seed. Paint each in-bounds blank orthogonal neighbour magenta(6), while preserving red seeds and every other non-zero cell. Lessons mix canonical-scale interior/edge/corner anchors with combined controls containing boundary clipping, adjacent seeds, a shared arm, a blocked neighbour, and a remote non-red decoy.

Place three or four mixed-length horizontal color-6 bars plus two isolated color-6 singleton distractors. The topmost bar has the requested bar_length; the remaining bars ensure both a short (2/3) and long (4/5) example are present. The authority preserves every 6 and paints color 8 only immediately beyond at least two consecutive horizontal 6s. Ordinary samples include an edge-touching bar, while an exact edge_bar=false override produces only interior bars. Singletons receive no cap.

A 0-background grid contains two to four separated yellow components. Components include filled rectangles, one-cell-thick rectangular frames, and scheduled concave zero-hole counterexamples. Recolor each component red when it encloses no hole and cyan when it encloses exactly one hole.
Small grid with 5s; rule meta-self-tiles where 5s appear.
Even h,w grid; bg=8 with 1s + 2 aligned 5-markers; rule crops half.
Sparse colored bboxes expand to top-left-anchored squares; smaller squares win overlaps.

On a zero background, each of two or three colors marks exactly two opposite corners of a separated axis-aligned rectangle. Draw each hollow rectangle border in its marker color. Both diagonal endpoint orientations, canonical-size scenes, and taller-than-canonical rectangles are sampled.

One full-width gray(5) divider splits a 0-background grid. Red(2) and yellow(4) occur on both sides. Compare each color's absolute difference between top and bottom counts; output a solid 2x2 block of the color with the larger imbalance.
Count the complete rows and columns painted in the separator colour. Return a (row-count + 1) by (column-count + 1) grid filled with the strict-majority background colour.

A connected color-2 source is encoded as signed offsets from one color-1 anchor. Colors 3, 4 and 5 request identity, clockwise-quarter-turn and vertical-mirror copies respectively; every resulting cell is color 8.
Scattered cells of 2-3 distinct colors; output fills the bbox of each color group.
