The canonical Racket rule keeps every rectangle border and checker-erases its interior in rectangle-relative coordinates.  Default four-pair lessons alternate informative thin-rectangle scenes with broad and canonical-profile scenes.

Split at the full-height 9 column, use the left panel as a non-zero mask on the coloured right panel, and crop the surviving right colours. Generated scenes make masking, colour preservation, and final cropping independently observable.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-9, w ∈ 9-11) with: (a) ROW 0 markers at FIXED cols — g[0][3] = g[0][6] = 1 (COLOR-1 BLUE markers in cols 3, 6); g[0][4] = g[0][7] = 2 (COLOR-2 RED markers in cols 4, 7); (b) COL 0 markers at FIXED rows — g[1][0] = g[2][0] = 2 (red markers in rows 1, 2); g[3][0] = g[4][0] = 1 (blue markers in rows 3, 4); (c) ONE COLOR-6 (MAGENTA) DECORATION at (h-1, w-1). Rule (PAINT 3 AT INTERSECTIONS OF BLUE ROWS WITH BLUE COLS, PAINT 8 AT INTERSECTIONS OF RED ROWS WITH RED COLS): READ row 0 to extract BLUE_COLS = cols where g[0][c] == 1, RED_COLS = cols where g[0][c] == 2. READ col 0 to extract BLUE_ROWS = rows where g[r][0] == 1, RED_ROWS = rows where g[r][0] == 2. For EACH (br, bc) ∈ BLUE_ROWS × BLUE_COLS: PAINT g[br][bc] = COLOR 3 (green). For EACH (rr, rc) ∈ RED_ROWS × RED_COLS: PAINT g[rr][rc] = COLOR 8 (cyan). Net: same-color borders project intersections in distinct colors — blue×blue → green, red×red → cyan.

Create a background-7 grid containing 3-5 distinct colored straight segments. Every scene contains both down-right and down-left diagonals; the with_horizontal profile additionally contains exactly one contiguous horizontal segment on the bottom row. Segment starts have distinct rows. The 5x3 output is background-padded at the top, then repeats each segment color across one row in ascending order of that segment's topmost-leftmost start coordinate.

A 0-background grid contains colors 1, 2, and 4 in horizontally disjoint regions. Color 1 is the anchor. Translate every cell of each nonzero color vertically, preserving its exact shape and columns, until that color's top row equals color 1's original top row.
Append a horizontal reflection of the input to its right, producing an h by 2w grid.

A sparse black grid contains red(2) source cells. Starting from an exact copy of the input, every source red cell paints blue(1) one column to its right when that cell is in bounds. Right-edge reds paint nothing. A blue write may overwrite a red destination, but every source is determined from the original input.

0-bg grid (size varies). A multi-color PAYLOAD (colors 4-9), a color-1 and color-2 marker (their difference is the step vector), and k color-3 counter cells. Rule: stamp the payload k+1 times along the vector (keeping the 1/2/3 markers). The grid size, payload, vector and counter k vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~25 distinct).

Maze grid (walls=5, open=0, start=2, goal=3) with ONE start cell and ONE goal cell. Path consists of: (a) a straight corridor segment from start, (b) one or more rectangular ring bypasses that branch into 2 equal-length paths, (c) a straight corridor segment to goal. Rule: BFS from start and from goal to count shortest-path distance and path multiplicity for every open cell. A 0-cell is UNAVOIDABLE iff dist(s→x) + dist(x→g) == dist(s→g) AND paths(s→x) * paths(x→g) == total_paths(s→g). Mark all unavoidable cells 8; leave others unchanged. Output has 8s on bottleneck corridor cells, 0s on ring branches (where multiple shortest paths exist).

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~8-12) with EXACTLY 3 NON-TOUCHING COLOR-8 (cyan) BLOBS at scattered positions, with STRICTLY DISTINCT SIZES (3 unique values from 2..6, sorted ascending and placed via grow_blob). Blobs are 4-conn isolated. Rule (SIZE-RANK RECOLOR + ERASE OTHERS): identify the 3 COLOR-8 BLOBS. SORT them by SIZE ASCENDING. RECOLOR by rank: smallest → COLOR 2 (red), medium → COLOR 3 (green), largest → COLOR 4 (yellow). Other cells stay 0. Note: output starts from an empty grid (only the 3 recolored blobs remain in their positions). Net: 3 cyan blobs → ranked colors (2, 3, 4) by size; bg cells stay 0.

Preserve a complete broken-blue-frame mask. Within the blue bounding box, paint an empty cell red exactly when its full row or full column contains at least four blue cells. Blue cells remain blue and every other cell becomes background. Published masks anchor the source distribution and a minimal threshold witness refutes the bbox-majority shortcut; D4 transforms and bounded zero padding are nuisance changes.

skills: component ordering, reduced symbolic output, thickness measurement
summary: Order binary foreground components from left to right and output each component's maximum cardinal onion-peel depth as one row.
On a cyan-8 background, find the single non-branching 4-connected path. Walk from either endpoint, reverse the encountered color sequence, and repaint those same coordinates in the reversed order.

Keep nonzero colors confined to one row; erase colors spanning rows. Collision-free mixed inputs include singleton and horizontal keepers, a repeated-row color spanning at least three rows, varied distractor counts and positions, and a canonical-size plus broad-size mixture.
Canonical-scale 21x21 grid with a zero margin around a nonzero rectangle of solid colored blocks; rule downscales by detecting row/col transitions.

Read a 5x5 prototype, then apply four codes cumulatively: 0 identity, 1 clockwise, 2 half-turn, 3 counter-clockwise, 4 left-right reflection, and 5 up-down reflection. Recolor each intermediate panel to the final row color and stamp the four panels left-to-right with blank separators.

Place three through five isolated monochromatic objects. Select the largest by area; equal-largest objects are resolved by uppermost bbox row and then leftmost bbox column. Return the selected object's tight crop. Five-pair lessons demonstrate all three selection branches.

A 7..14 square/rectangular zero-background grid contains 1..5 clear same-color endpoint pairs on perfect 45-degree diagonals.  The reference fills each clear segment inclusively.  Every generated input also contains one different-color diagonal pair crossing a clear pair's endpoint in its interior, so that blocked pair remains unchanged and explicitly teaches the zero-interior condition.

A complete hollow color-8 rectangular frame and one singleton key color appear on a zero background. The key is outside the frame. Paint every strict-interior cell of the frame with the singleton key color, preserving the frame and the key. Optional repeated-color decoys test singleton selection and interior overwrite behavior; seed-phased roles prevent key color, side, decoy mode, and geometry from becoming fixed proxies.
Top-row palette + body of nested color-5 frames recolored by depth.
5-grid (2x2 chambers) with 1 distinct-color seed per chamber.

Three h-by-pw panels (h=3..7, pw=2..6) separated by two gray-5 columns. At each local position, fewer than two nonzero votes produce zero; otherwise select the most frequent nonzero color, with larger color winning a frequency tie. Ordinary draws cycle through 1,2,3,3,1,1,3,3 foreground colors and construct voting counterexamples. Exact count, geometry and palette controls use a separate feasible constructor.

Column 0 is a row guide: keep rows whose guide cell is orange (7), discard every other row, and remove the guide column. Inputs have 2..4 selected rows, at least two rejected rows, observable sparse/medium/dense payloads, and 2..8 payload colors. A four-profile schedule supplies an exact canonical-scale alternating example plus counterexamples to nonzero-guide, alternating-row, fixed-three-row, and any-7-in-row shortcuts.

0-bg grid with N (3-5) connected components in distinct non-zero colors at scattered positions. Each component is a small 4-conn blob (3-5 cells) with varied bbox shape. Components are spaced ≥1-cell apart. Rule: extract each component. Crop to bbox. Sort by height descending (then color asc for ties). Pack the cropped pieces horizontally with 1-col gap between, ALL bottom-aligned. Output height = max cropped height; output width = sum cropped widths + (N-1) gaps.

Grid (size varies) whose top two rows are a key->fill LEGEND (column pairs). The body (rows 2+) has framed rooms, each seeded with a key color. Rule: each room's 0-cells flood with the mapped fill color. The legend pairs, room shapes/seeds/keys, grid size and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~24 distinct).
Fill zero cells inside each complete yellow frame that contains exactly one distinct marker color.
2-5 equally spaced blue cells; continue their row-major step with red cells.

0-bg grid (size varies) with several color-6 shapes of distinct sizes. Rule: extract the largest, crop to its bbox, recolor to 8. The grid size, shape forms/sizes and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct). Output is the cropped largest shape, so its size is bounded; inputs are large.

On a black background, keep every cardinally connected magenta object whose whole shape is exactly a solid 2x2 square; erase every other magenta object, including horizontal/vertical tetrominoes and 2x2 squares with an attached tail.

0-bg grid with 3-5 separated 4-connected objects, each a random polyomino in its own distinct colour and with a DISTINCT cell count (so exactly one is largest). Rule: pick the largest object (ties: topmost then leftmost), crop to its bbox, flip it left-right, and output that crop in the object's colour.

Two color-8 rectangular frames contain gray walls and one colored gate. Flood only gate-reachable zeros with four-neighbor movement. Scheduled open, sealed, and diagonal-wall profiles make reachability and the four-neighbor convention identifiable under every query rotation.

A binary grid contains 2-4 complete blue rectangular outlines, strictly nested with at least one blank cell between adjacent frames. Recolor the outermost frame red(2), the next green(3), then 4 and 5 moving inward, leaving all background cells black(0).
Sparse square grids whose cells are copied across the main diagonal.

0-bg grid (size varies). 3-5 BLOBS (random polyominoes with DISTINCT edge-perimeters, distinct input colors), placed apart. Rule: compute each blob's edge-perimeter, sort the distinct perimeters descending, and recolor every blob by its perimeter rank using the palette [2,3,4,6,8,9,1,5,7] (largest perimeter -> palette[0], etc.). The grid size, the number of blobs, their shapes/perimeters, positions and input colors all vary freely, so the rank recolor (the output) varies too (was 3 fixed blobs + grid padding).
Two 8-cells (src+dst) + a colored blob; shifted blob in-bounds.

Mix of color-1 objects: closed rectangular frames (the 4 border cells of their bbox are all 1) and partial/open shapes (L, T, lines, blobs whose bbox border has gaps). Rule recolors closed frames to color 3; partial shapes stay color 1.

0-bg grid with N (2-5) connected non-bg components, each in its own distinct color. Rule: for each component, compute its max-col-peak (max over columns of the count of cells the component occupies in that column) — equivalently, the longest vertical run within the component's footprint. Pick the component with the STRICTLY LARGEST max-col-peak (ties broken by size, then top-left). Output is that component's bbox crop, recolored so non-bg cells become 8 (bbox holes stay 0).

Cap maximal horizontal yellow length-3 runs with magenta; every generated input also contains uncapped wrong-length yellow runs and uncapped exact-3 runs in another colour, with canonical three/four-colour palette support.

Canonical-scale square input (2x2 through 5x5), with every third sample on the exact public size/palette profile and intervening samples using one fewer or one more visible color. Every color is visible, the arrangement varies in both axes and is not transpose-symmetric. Rule: replace EACH input cell with a solid 2x2 block of the same color.

Two or three colors each mark two non-aligned endpoints. For every color, connect the upper endpoint vertically to the lower row and then horizontally to the lower endpoint. Generated elbow paths are disjoint.

A 0-background grid is enclosed by color-9 walls and partitioned by additional color-9 dividers. Exactly two single-cell seeds, in distinct non-{0,9} colors and different wall-bounded components, each emit four cardinal rays in their own color. A ray paints every non-wall cell until the grid edge or a color-9 wall stops it; walls remain 9. Generated scenes also contain off-ray zeros and an empty compartment so full-region and wall-ignoring shortcuts disagree visibly.

One or two distinct-colored hollow objects appear on background 0. Objects vary in size, position, edge contact, mutual contact, and may be rectangular frames or frames with a two-cell outward stem.  The output is otherwise zero: remove every object border and paint only each truly enclosed zero-region with that object's color.

A 0-background 8..14 by 8..14 grid contains 1..4 separated clear 45-degree endpoint pairs and 0..2 non-diagonal same-color distractor pairs. Each nonzero color occurs exactly twice. For every color whose two cells lie on a clear 45-degree diagonal, fill the inclusive segment with that color; leave non-diagonal pairs unchanged. Default lessons use three foreground colors and regularly include a clear axis-aligned distractor to distinguish the rule from connecting all straight pairs.

One to three disjoint rectangular frames on background 0. Each frame has one or two endpoint colors occurring exactly twice locally; colors may recur in other frames. Connect each pair horizontally from the row-major first endpoint, then vertically. Optional singleton/triple colors stay unchanged. Full routed paths are reserved, so no endpoint is overwritten.
Mix of solid/frame/double-frame objects; recolor by hole count.

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0,0) is a DIRECTION MARKER (1=left, 2=right, 3=up, 4=down). Some color-8 cells form fixed WALLS (random line segments). Several colored polyominoes are scattered as separate components. Rule: drop the marker cell, then slide EVERY non-wall object as a rigid 4-connected component in the marker's direction until it is blocked by a wall, another object, or the grid edge (gravity settling, leading objects move first). Grid size, direction, wall layout and the object set all vary freely, and at least one object always has clear runway so the output differs from the input (was a fixed 9x12 grid with 6 hardcoded variants).

A zero-background grid contains one connected color-2 reference motif and one isolated color-1 marker. Translate the motif so the bottom-right corner of its bounding box lands on the marker, paint the translated cells color 8 on a fresh grid, and discard the source objects.

0-bg grid (h~10-13, w~12-16) with 1-3 ISOLATED color-3 (green) 4-cell T-tetrominoes, each one of 4 orientations (T-up, T-down, T-left, T-right). Each T has the missing plus arm in-bounds. Rule: detect each T-shaped color-3 object, identify which of the 4 plus-arms is missing (the cell opposite the existing stem), and paint that missing cell with color 3 to complete a 5-cell PLUS.

Single asymmetric (non-LR-symmetric) connected blob. Rule crops the input to the blob's bbox, then concatenates that crop with its LR-flip using a 1-column bg separator. Output preserves the blob's color.

h × (3*w+2) grid (0-bg, h=5..6, w=5..6) with THREE same-size w-column panels separated by full-height color-9 (maroon) divider columns. Each panel contains a different count of occupied cells (e.g., 3, 5, 8) in DIFFERENT colors (one color per panel, all distinct from 0 and 9). One panel is the STRICT WINNER (most cells). Rule: split panels at color-9 cols. Count occupied (non-zero) cells per panel. Pick the panel with the most cells. Recolor all its cells to 8 (cyan). Output: just that panel (cropped, w columns wide, h rows tall) with original positions kept and color 8 in non-zero slots.
skills: panel extraction, object counting, argmax selection

summary: Stamp the first 8-row group's pattern in 1 beyond each later group's frontier.
2-3 distinct-color blobs whose bbox-outline differs from the blob shape.

A 2-row x N-col (N=3-6) lattice of square p x p PANELS separated by full color-9 row/col dividers. The QUERY is the 3rd top-row panel. The match is CONSTRUCTED: one bottom-row panel (a chosen index) carries the CW-rotation of the query's occupancy; the others are random non-matching occupancies. Rule: rotate the query CW and output a 1xN one-hot of which bottom panel matches. Output is intrinsically a length-N one-hot.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one closed rectangular frame in color 8 and exactly one non-0/non-8 seed inside it. Fill the complete strict interior with that seed color while preserving the frame and all outside background cells.
Each nonzero seed extends straight downward to the bottom border in its color.
Positional row-0 key, gray separator, and one lower seed for clipped square rings.
Move each object to the nearest singleton marker and recolor by that marker.

On a 10x10 grid with a solid gray-5 border, the interior is a dense, single 4-connected region of black-0 cells with gray-5 blockers. Enumerate every maximal black run in the down-right and down-left directions. Rank runs by length; ties prefer the smaller start row, then for down-left the larger start column and for down-right the smaller start column. Recolor exactly the winning run cyan-8 and preserve every other cell.

0-bg grid (size varies) with a stack of concentric color-1 rectangular frames and k color-2 markers. Rule: rank frames by area, select frame k, and fill its interior with 4 down to the next-inner frame. The grid size, frame count, band widths and k vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~36 distinct).

0-bg grid (size varies) with 3-7 non-touching CONNECTED COMPONENTS in one color (each a polyomino of some rotation class + orientation), placed apart. Rule: sort components by left edge and output an NxN matrix where (i,j) = COLOR 7 if components i,j match under rotation (0/90/180/270, no reflections), else 0. The number of components, their shapes/orientations/positions and the color all vary freely (was 3 fixed components on a fixed 8x14, ~9 distinct).
1-2 horizontal lines + 1-2 vertical lines, all separated.

On background 0, one full-width horizontal bar and one full-height vertical bar cross. Their colors differ. The overlap is uniformly the color of the visually front bar. Recolor the complete overlap rectangle with the other bar color, leaving every non-overlap cell unchanged.
Top-left sketch of single cells (2-3 colors) + matching multi-cell prototypes elsewhere.

skills: transform inference, dihedral/rotation reasoning, candidate selection
summary: Square panels A, B, C and 2..3 candidates are separated by color 9. Infer the first rotation/reflection mapping normalized A to B, apply it to normalized C, then return the unique matching candidate at its original offset recolored 8.
Legend + selector + 2x2 bank entries (3 entries) for palette-lifted horizontal concat.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-9, w ∈ 9-11) with: (a) ONE CMD CELL at FIXED position (0, 0) — value ∈ {1..7} selecting a TRANSFORM (1=identity, 2=cw90, 3=180, 4=ccw90, 5=flip-LR, 6=flip-UD, 7=transpose); (b) ONE SMALL MULTICOLOR BLOB in the LOWER-RIGHT QUADRANT — sub_h × sub_w (sub_h, sub_w ∈ 2-3 with sub_h ≠ sub_w to make transforms visible) at random position (r0 ∈ h//2..h-sub_h-1, c0 ∈ w//2..w-sub_w-1), with each cell painted (with 70% prob) in one of 2 distinct palette colors drawn from {2..9}\{cmd}. Rule (READ THE CMD AT (0, 0), CLEAR (0, 0) TO 0, CROP THE BODY TO NON-BG CONTENT, APPLY TRANSFORM BY CODE — 1=IDENTITY, 2=CW, 3=180, 4=CCW, 5=FLIP-LR, 6=FLIP-UD, ELSE=TRANSPOSE — OUTPUT THE TRANSFORMED CROP): READ cmd from (0, 0). SET (0, 0) = 0. CROP the remaining grid to the bbox of non-bg cells. APPLY the cmd's TRANSFORM. OUTPUT the transformed crop. Net: corner cmd selects 1 of 7 dihedral operations on the cropped multicolor blob.
Three top-row legend colors crossed with three fixed 3x3 mask panels.

Read row-0 keys 1=identity, 2=clockwise, 3=180 degrees, 4=left-right flip; crop one monochrome body template and form a top-aligned strip with one-column gaps. Varied connected templates alternate with asymmetric examples that teach every key and repeated commands.

Canonical-scale 0/1/2 grid with color-1 target windows, color-2 decoy blocks, and isolated noise. Count every sliding 2x2 all-1 window and encode the count as a 1x5 bar. A three-slot lesson cycle contains two overlap counterexamples and one separated canonical-shaped scene.

0-bg grid with N (3-5) isolated 4-connected components, each in a distinct color (sampled freely from {1..9}). The components are scattered so no two 4-touch each other and no two share an 8-edge. Rule: collect all components, sort by their bbox top-left in reading order (row then column). Recolor in order with the palette [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 1]: first → 2, second → 3, third → 4, etc. Output places the recolored cells on a fresh 0-bg grid (positions preserved, only colors changed).

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-10) with 1-3 ISOLATED non-bg SEED cells placed at interior positions (rows 2..h-3, cols 2..w-3) so each has at least 2 cells of bg margin in all 4 cardinal directions. Seeds are pairwise Manhattan-distance ≥ 5 apart so their distance-2 rays do not overlap. Each seed is in some non-bg color from a 2-8 palette. Rule: for every non-zero seed at (r, c) with color v, PAINT the four cells at distance 2 in the four cardinal directions: (r-2, c), (r+2, c), (r, c-2), (r, c+2) — each in color v. Cells out of bounds are skipped. The seed itself stays color v. Net: each colored seed sprouts 4 same-color satellite cells at Chebyshev-2 cardinal positions (like a sparse plus shape).

Exactly two separated solid color-4 rectangles of distinct area, each at least 3x3. The selected rule fills the smaller strict interior with 1 and the larger strict interior with 2 while preserving both color-4 borders.

Count the color-1 markers in row 0. Around the unique color-9 anchor, paint each coloured seed at its original offset and its first k-1 quarter-turn offsets under (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr); discard the header.

A 6-16 cell rectangular 0-background grid contains exactly one local coordinate frame: color 2 is the origin, color 3 marks local (1,0), and color 4 marks local (0,1).  The orthogonal unit basis may use any of the eight directed D4 orientations.  A non-empty subset of the four local offsets (2,0), (0,2), (1,1), and (2,2) is colored 8.  Output is a 1x4 strip in that fixed offset order, using 8 for occupied and 0 for empty. Default episodes use a cyclic 15-mask curriculum whose every three consecutive demonstrations toggle all four strip positions.
skills: symbolic output, local-coordinate lookup, feature extraction

summary: Extract the four-connected non-{0,8} component rooted at (0,0), clear the canvas, and stamp its colored cells at every color-8 anchor. Samples mix canonical-size templates with longer templates, diagonal distractors and three/four anchors; source and stamped bounding boxes stay disjoint.

A zero-background grid contains separated same-color horizontal runs of odd length.  Keep only each run's midpoint cell in its original color and erase every other cell.  Regular draws include singleton and longer runs.

For each occupied column independently, discard marker colors and paint the inclusive topmost-to-bottommost span cyan (8) on a fresh zero grid. The lesson schedule covers canonical color-2 endpoint pairs, adjacent columns with shared colors, mixed-color extremes, extra markers, and singleton one-cell spans.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-18, w ∈ 11-22, by difficulty) with: (a) ONE COLOR-5 (GRAY) MIRROR COLUMN at column OLD_C ∈ 1..(w-2)//2 (constrained so 2*old_c+1 < w), with N_GRAYS ∈ 2-6 GRAY CELLS placed in that column at rows per GRAY_LAYOUT ∈ {scattered / contiguous / edges / evenly_spaced}; (b) N_PROBES ∈ 0-4 COLOR-2 (BLUE) PROBE CELLS placed between cols old_c+1 and 2*old_c per PROBE_LAYOUT ∈ {scattered / vertical / diag} — these probes lie in the 'reflection zone' between the gray column and its mirror position. Rule (MOVE EVERY GRAY-5 CELL FROM COLUMN OLD_C TO COLUMN 2*OLD_C + 1 (THE MIRROR-REFLECTED COLUMN); ANY PROBES IN THE REFLECTION ZONE GET RECOLORED PER A FIXED RULE — PER DEMOS, MAY TURN COLOR 1 OR ANOTHER MARKER): IDENTIFY the gray-5 mirror column old_c. COMPUTE new_c = 2*old_c + 1. CLEAR the gray cells from old_c. PAINT gray-5 at the same rows in column new_c. For each blue-2 probe in cols old_c..new_c: RECOLOR it per the canonical rule (e.g., color 1 to indicate it was 'crossed' by the mirror). Net: the gray column slides to its mirrored position; probes in the swept zone are marked.
A colour-2/3/4 L-frame defines oriented local axes. Count only colour-8 cells strictly inside the four local quadrants and within Chebyshev radius 3; output (++,-+,--,+-) as a 1x4 count strip.

A 7..9 by 9..11 zero-background grid has one control at (0,0): 3=union, 4=XOR, 5=intersection.  Separate connected color-1 and color-2 polyominoes (3..6 cells) are bbox-normalized before the operation.  Their normalized masks may partially overlap or be identical; the result is painted color 8 on the maximum operand bounding box (or [[0]] if empty).

A 14..18 square-ish grid contains exactly two non-background colors: one forms a non-rectangular left-right-symmetric shape and the other a solid rectangular occluder covering the shape's left or right edge. Remove the rectangle and fill only those rectangle cells whose mirror counterparts are visible shape cells.
Yellow emitters paint cyan rightward through zero cells, passing through other colors and stopping before the first maroon blocker or the edge.

A 4..8 by 10..16 zero-background input contains one monochrome path. The rows repeat with the smallest period p in {1,2,3}; after each p-row block the whole motif is translated left, right, or not at all by a constant offset. The output is a width-by-width square that continues the same periodic, translated sequence beyond the input height.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~7-9) containing 2-4 ENDPOINT PAIRS: each pair is two cells of the SAME UNIQUE COLOR in the SAME COLUMN, with at least one empty (0) cell between them. Different pairs use different colors and different columns. Rule: for each column containing exactly two same-color cells at rows r1 < r2, FILL every cell at rows r1..r2 in that column with that color (CONNECT the two endpoints into a solid vertical bar). Other cells are unchanged. Net: each pair of isolated endpoints becomes a continuous colored line spanning its column.
2-3 distinct-color blobs of size ≥3 with bbox centers spaced apart.

0-bg grid (h, w ~ 8-12) with: (a) COLOR-2 MARKER at (base_r, base_c) and COLOR-3 MARKER at (base_r+dr, base_c+dc) where (dr, dc) is drawn from {(1, 2), (2, 1), (-1, 2), (2, -1)} — the marker pair defines a non-zero VECTOR (dr, dc); (b) 4 MOTIF CELLS painted in COLOR 4 at random interior positions chosen so each motif's shifted position (r+dr, c+dc) is in-bounds and not overlapping any marker. Rule (THE 2/3 MARKER PAIR DEFINES A VECTOR — COLOR-4 CELLS ARE KEPT AND COPIED BY THAT VECTOR AS COLOR 8): identify the COLOR-2 MARKER and COLOR-3 MARKER; COMPUTE the VECTOR (dr, dc) = (3-marker's position) - (2-marker's position). For EACH COLOR-4 CELL at (r, c): KEEP it as 4 in the output; PAINT the cell at (r+dr, c+dc) with COLOR 8 (cyan). The original 2 and 3 markers stay. Net: each color-4 cell duplicates to its vector-shifted position in color 8.

A 9..18 rectangular zero-background grid contains 1..4 distinct colors that occur exactly twice. The two cells of every such color are offset in both row and column. The rule lexicographically orders each pair, draws a horizontal-then-vertical L path in that color, and processes pairs by their first endpoint so later paths overwrite intersections. Zero to two additional colors occur exactly three times and are lawful distractors: because they are not exact pairs, the rule leaves them unchanged unless a qualifying path crosses them (the sampler avoids that input ambiguity). A four-position schedule alternates canonical-scale anchors with explicit witnesses against pair-count, occurrence-count, endpoint-order, and overlap-priority shortcuts.

In one simultaneous pass, fill a zero cell yellow(4) exactly when its immediate horizontal or vertical neighbors are both yellow. Preserve blocked midpoints, wider separations, other-color sandwiches, and cells that would become eligible only after an earlier fill.

A sparse 0-background scene contains 2-5 separated connected motifs, including canonical singleton distractors. The output is the normalized union of the two largest motifs, painted color 8; ties use top-left order.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~12-15) with 3-4 small CONNECTED MOTIFS, all in COLOR 6, scattered at non-overlapping positions. The MAJORITY (n-1) of motifs share the SAME normalized shape; one motif may have a different shape (odd-one-out). Rule: identify each color-6 connected motif. NORMALIZE each motif's shape. FIND the MODE shape (canonical normalized shape appearing most). Output: that MOST-COMMON SHAPE in COLOR 2 (red) — the bbox-cropped subgrid. Net: input is magenta motifs; output is the mode shape recolored to red.

Read the single nonzero colour in the bottom row. In the rows above, find the unique 4-connected blob of that colour and return its tight bounding-box crop, preserving the blob's colour and internal zero cells.

Find the unique singleton non-background color and use its column as the scanline reference.  The other non-background color marks row boundaries. On a marker row, fill between the nearest marker strictly left of the seed column and the nearest marker at-or-right of it; a missing side opens to the grid edge.  Rows strictly between the first and last marker rows that have no markers fill edge-to-edge.  Rows above/below inherit the first/last marker-row interval.  Preserve all marker cells.

Create an 11x11 grid split by zero rows and columns at indices 3 and 7 into nine 3x3 blocks. Every block is filled only with colors 1 and 2, and the nine blocks have distinct color-1 counts chosen from 0..9, so exactly one count is omitted. The transformation moves whole blocks: sort them by ascending color-1 count, place the three smallest left-to-right on the bottom macro-row, the next three on the middle row, and the three largest on the top row. Preserve separators and every block's internal pattern exactly.

Row 0 is a color LEGEND (precedence order). The field (rows 1+) has EMITTER cells on its border (non-{0,5} colors on the field's top/bottom rows and left/right columns) and color-5 BLOCKERS inside. Rule: each emitter shoots a ray inward in its color until it hits a blocker or the edge; where rays overlap, the higher-precedence color (per the legend) wins. Output = blockers + emitters + rays.

Match translation-normalized panel supports under ordered D4 transforms; recolor the first matching transformed candidate, preserving its position. Teach same-count decoys, no match, translated matches and first-candidate precedence.

4-separated lattice of noisy 3x3 cells; the unique non-{0,1,4} marker is a 2x-upscaled key bitmap in a walled 8x8 box; lattice cells whose 1-pattern contains the key are recolored to the marker color.

0-bg grid (size varies). 2-5 NESTED color-1 (blue) RECTANGULAR FRAMES, each inset >=2 on every side from the one outside it (so they are separate components; insets vary per side, not necessarily concentric). Rule: for each empty cell, count how many frame interiors enclose it (depth); if depth > 0, recolor it to depth+1 (depth-1 -> color 2, depth-2 -> color 3, ...). The frames stay color 1 and outside cells stay 0. The grid size, the number of frames and their per-side insets all vary freely, so the depth gradient (the output) varies too (was centered concentric frames + grid padding).
Full gray(5) row or column bar; per row/col, extend gray by side dot count; output is binary 0/5 (dot colors discarded).
Generate 2..4 horizontal 5-0-5 sandwiches. Profiles cover distinct rows, multiple sandwiches in one row, both horizontal boundaries, and gray distractors that must remain unchanged.

Split the input at three full-height gray columns into three square prototype panels and one query panel. Match the query occupancy to exactly one prototype under translation and the eight dihedral transforms, then return that prototype in its original position recolored with the query color.

A 0-background grid contains one 4-connected prototype component with one or more color-9 target cells and a single-colored 3-6 cell shape. The first 9 in that component is the origin. Additional 9 targets may be isolated or may touch the prototype, and some targets may lie near an edge. The rule erases every 9 and stamps the prototype's non-9 relative offsets at every 9, clipping cells that fall outside the grid.

A connected cluster of single-cell objects (proper-coloured so neighbours differ) is the largest cluster; the rule outputs its sorted degree sequence (+1) as a 1xN row. Cluster size and shape — hence the degree sequence — vary; isolated decoy cells form smaller singleton clusters.

On a black canvas, retain 2..5 separated monochrome hollow rectangular frames and discard 0..3 solid rectangles. Compare the ranges of frame top-left rows and columns; use a column iff row range is strictly greater, otherwise a row. Sort along that axis and redraw each frame as a fixed 4x4 outline of its color, including repeated colors.

Split an even 6..14 by 6..14 zero-background grid into four equal quadrants. Each non-empty quadrant contains 2..6 cells of one color; the quadrant colors are distinct, and at most one quadrant is empty. Return a 2x2 grid containing the first non-zero color in each quadrant in row-major order, or 0 for the empty quadrant.

Row 0 is a left-aligned palette of K distinct colors. Rows 1+ contain K separate 4-connected color-1 objects. Sort the objects by (cell count ascending, top row ascending, left column ascending), recolor them with the palette in that order, crop each object to its bounding box, and pack the crops left-to-right with one zero column between adjacent pieces. Equal-size objects are intentional: top row, then left column, resolves ties. Five demonstrations preserve the scheduled area, connectivity, and tie witnesses under query rotation.
Components on bg=7; rule shifts each down by its cell count.

A zero-background grid contains exactly three separated monochrome objects. Crop each object to its own bounding box, sort the crops by occupied cell count ascending; ties are broken by color ascending, then original top-left position. Pack the crops left-to-right, top-aligned, with exactly one zero column between neighboring crops, preserving the object shapes and colors.

0-bg grid (h~10-12, w~12-14) with: (a) MARKER GRID — 4 singleton cells in DISTINCT non-{0, 1} colors at positions (0, 0), (0, 2), (2, 0), (2, 2) (top-left 2×2 marker matrix); (b) 4 COLOR-1 (blue) SHAPES — each a 3-cell L-tromino variant placed in a 2×2 LAYOUT at anchors (4, 4), (4, 9), (7, 4), (7, 9). Rule (RECOLOR EACH SHAPE BY ITS POSITIONAL MARKER): compute SORTED UNIQUE ROWS/COLS of MARKERS (marker_rows = [0, 2], marker_cols = [0, 2]) and SORTED UNIQUE ROWS/COLS of SHAPE BBOX TOP-LEFTS (obj_rows = [4, 7], obj_cols = [4, 9]). For EACH BLUE SHAPE at top-left (R, C): find ri = obj_rows.index(R), ci = obj_cols.index(C). LOOK UP MARKER COLOR at marker[marker_rows[ri]][marker_cols[ci]]. RECOLOR all cells of the blue shape to that marker color. Markers stay. Net: shapes inherit colors from the top-left marker grid by their relative (row, col) position.

0-bg grid (panel_h~3-7 rows, w = 4*panel_w+3 cols) with EXACTLY 4 EQUAL-SIZE PANELS separated by 3 full-height COLOR-9 DIVIDER COLUMNS. Each panel contains a DIFFERENT count of non-zero cells in some non-{0, 9} color, ensuring panel cell counts are STRICTLY DISTINCT. Rule: SPLIT into 4 panels. SORT by (CELL COUNT ASC, ORIGINAL INDEX ASC). Build a 2*panel_h × 2*panel_w OUTPUT divided into 4 QUADRANTS (TL, TR, BL, BR). STAMP sorted panels: sorted[0] → TL, sorted[1] → TR, sorted[2] → BL, sorted[3] → BR. All stamped cells painted COLOR 8 (cyan), preserving each panel's binary shape. Net: panels rearranged by ascending count into a 2×2 quadrant layout in cyan.

A sparse grid contains 3-7 non-background colors with pairwise-distinct cell counts. The answer is the three most frequent colors, descending, as a 3x1 column. A periodic 12x12 three-color branch anchors the exact canonical profile; broad lessons include at least one lower-ranked distractor.
Mixed grid; rule paints 0-regions: 2 if border, 5 if interior.
Create 5..7 nonempty rows with distinct non-zero occupancies and two full-palette top rows arranged to refute dominant-frequency and mixed-row-priority shortcuts.
One 9-anchor and one connected 3-4 cell source object; copy each source cell, with its own color, through the anchor by 180-degree point reflection.

0-bg grid (h, w~12-18) with 2-4 COLOR-3 (green) SINGLE-CELL SEEDS at interior positions (edge_margin=2 from borders) separated by min_separation=6 cells. Position bias options: scattered/corners/diagonal/row_aligned/centered. Rule (BUILDING-PROFILE STAMP): for EACH GREEN SEED at (sr, sc), STAMP a 'BUILDING PROFILE' shape centered at (or anchored to) the seed. A 'building profile' is a task-specific fixed motif (e.g., a 3×3 cross, an L-shape, or a house-like silhouette) painted in COLOR 3. The stamp is CLIPPED at grid edges if it extends beyond. Multiple seeds → multiple stamps with no overlap (thanks to min_separation). Net: each green seed expands into a building-shape stamp; min_separation ensures stamps don't collide.

Several colour-3 objects share a common base shape (each with a few extra cells); the rule keeps the cells present in >=2 normalized copies and outputs that consensus shape, coloured 3. Base shape, copy count and extras vary.

Input = three N×N PANELS (N=3..5) separated by full color-8 divider columns. Panel A is a random N×N pattern in source colors c1,c2,c3; Panel B = transform(A) + recolor (one of rot-CW/180/CCW, flip-LR/UD, transpose, anti-transpose, then c1→t1,c2→t2,c3→t3); Panel C = a different random N×N pattern in the same source palette. Rule: infer the transform and color-map from A↔B and apply both to C. Output: the N×N recolor(transform(C)) prediction.

0-bg grid with ONE color-2 (red) PIVOT near the center and a RANDOM connected blob (3-6 cells) in a single color from {1,4,5,6,7,8,9} placed at a random position. Rule: for each non-{0,2} cell, compute its delta (dr,dc) from the pivot and place its color at the 90° CW rotated position (pr+dc, pc-dr); the pivot stays. Net: the blob rotates 90° CW around the pivot.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-11, w ∈ 9-12) with: (a) ONE COLOR-3 SRC ANCHOR at a random position in the UPPER-LEFT region (rows 0..h//3, cols 0..w//2); (b) ONE COLOR-4 DST ANCHOR at a random position in the MIDDLE-RIGHT region (rows h//3..2h//3, cols w//2..w-1) — guarantees src and dst are distinct; (c) ONE COLOR-2 TEMPLATE BLOB — a 3-4 cell irregular blob built by grow_blob random walk, placed at a random non-overlapping position. Rule (COMPUTE THE VECTOR FROM SRC-3 TO DST-4, TRANSLATE THE COLOR-2 TEMPLATE BY THAT VECTOR; PAINT THE TRANSLATED COPY AS COLOR 8 ON A FRESH GRID, PRESERVING DST-4): FIND the COLOR-3 SRC cell at (sr, sc) and the COLOR-4 DST cell at (dr, dc); COMPUTE the vector v = (dr - sr, dc - sc). PRODUCE a fresh same-size grid of 0s. For EACH COLOR-2 template cell at (r, c): PAINT g[r + v.r][c + v.c] = COLOR 8 (cyan). ALSO PAINT the DST cell at (dr, dc) = COLOR 4 (preserving the anchor). Net: template gets translated by anchor-to-anchor vector, recolored to cyan, with dst anchor preserved as a 4-marker.

Place 1..8 distinct nonzero seed colours only on row 0 of a 0-background grid. Seeds are interior and separated by at least three columns. For every seed at column c, paint its colour at c on every even row and at c-1 and c+1 on every odd row. The four-profile lesson schedule preserves single/multi-seed and height-6/taller counterexamples under query rotation.

Full orange(7) divider row/col + magenta(6) cells on one side; reflect each magenta across the divider and paint the destination cyan(8). Ordinary generation reserves those destinations so all other colors survive.

Copy every non-zero cell in the left half to the horizontally mirrored cell in the right half, preserving the left source. Alternating teaching profiles add one unrelated right-half decoy on a non-target cell; that decoy is preserved and is not mirrored back left, exposing that the rule is one-directional.
9-anchor at center + a small blob in upper-left whose reflection lands in lower-right.

0-bg grid with SCATTERED cells of colors 1, 2, 3 at random non-overlapping positions; each color appears 1..cmax times (counts are independent and may repeat). Rule: count cells of each color (1,2,3) and emit a 3-row bar chart: row 0 = n1 cells of color 1 (left-aligned), row 1 = n2 of color 2, row 2 = n3 of color 3. Output dims = 3 × max(n1,n2,n3).

11x11 0-bg grid encoding a BOOLEAN MOSAIC. Cell (1, 1) holds an OPERATION CODE: 1=AND, 2=OR, else=XOR. Two 3x3 ROW TEMPLATES sit at the top at columns (4, 8); two 3x3 COL TEMPLATES sit at the left at rows (4, 8). Each template is a binary mask painted in some non-0 color (the rule is color-blind: any non-0 cell = ON). Rule: for each col-template, hstack the cell-wise boolean combination (AND/OR/XOR per the op code) with each row-template; vstack the two rows into a 2x2 panel layout of 3x3 boolean results (8=true) with 1-cell gaps -> a 7x7 output. Color and exact template pattern are distractors; only the ON/OFF masks and the op code matter.
Repeat the top-row nonzero prefix independently across every row of the cyan rectangle.
One connected orthogonal stroke network partitions black cells into sealed regions and edge-reachable exterior regions.
1-2 hollow rect-frames (e.g. 3x3 ring with 1-cell hole).

Variable-size 0-bg grid (14..30) with: (a) a large RECTANGLE (varied size) in some color (rect_color); (b) one MARKER cell of a different color at the rectangle's center; (c) outside the rectangle: a KEY shape — a marker-colored center cell with 4 ARM segments extending up/down/left/right (each arm is 2 cells of a distinct color: up-color, down-color, left-color, right-color). Rule: detect bg = most common color. Detect rect_color = most common non-bg. Find rectangle objects of that color. Compute marker_color from cells inside the rect that are neither bg nor rect_color (mode). Find OUTSIDE marker cells (same color, not in any rect). The one with most nearby non-bg neighbors = KEY CENTER. Grow the key region from the center via 8-conn non-bg cells outside rects. Then for every marker inside each rectangle, STAMP the key's offsets (relative to key center) at that marker's position, painted in the corresponding key arm colors.
Singleton seeds on distinct main-diagonal offsets.

A 0-background grid is split into 3-5 equal vertical panels by full color-5 divider columns. Each panel contains one monochrome connected object. A strict majority of panel objects share the same row-profile (cell counts from top bbox row to bottom), but the agreeing objects have different normalized shapes. Ignore the outlier profiles and render the majority profile as a left-justified cyan(8) histogram.
Left vertical key bars assign colors to atomic 8-column blocks.
Interior singleton seeds separated enough for hollow plus expansion.

A full color-9 column separates equal left and right panels. The left panel contains one to four nonzero mask components; the right panel is a nonzero multicolor source. Copy each right-panel value through positions where the left panel is nonzero, and output 0 elsewhere.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 12-22, by difficulty) with: (a) ONE LR-SYMMETRIC MULTICOLOR BLOCK at the TOP (sr=1) — sh × sw (sh ∈ 3-5, sw ∈ 3-7, forced odd for exact symmetry), built via _make_sym_block: each row's cells set so row[c] == row[sw-1-c]; painted in colors drawn from a 4-color palette per PALETTE_KIND ∈ {warm, cool, broad, primary}; (b) N_ASYM ∈ 1-3 ASYMMETRIC DISTRACTOR BLOCKS placed BELOW the symmetric block (rows ≥ sr+sh+1) — each 2-3 × 2-4, with corners forced different so LR-symmetry is broken. All blocks placed with 1-cell halo padding via _can_place. Rule (EXTRACT EVERY 8-CONNECTED MULTICOLOR OBJECT; SORT BY (MIN_ROW, MIN_COL) ROW-MAJOR; OUTPUT THE FIRST LR-SYMMETRIC ONE — ITS BBOX CROP IN ITS ORIGINAL COLORS): EXTRACT every non-bg 8-conn object. SORT by (min_r, min_c). For EACH in order: CHECK if its normalized bbox-mask is LR-symmetric (row[c] == row[w-1-c]). SELECT the FIRST symmetric one. CROP to its bbox. OUTPUT the multicolor crop. Net: topmost-leftmost LR-symmetric object extracted; asymmetric distractors discarded.

Read the color at (0,0) as a rotation code. Find the complete gray (5) rectangular frame, crop its interior, and return that crop unchanged for code 1, rotated clockwise for code 2, rotated 180 degrees for code 3, or rotated counter-clockwise for code 4.

Three disconnected monochrome objects appear on black. Crop each object to its bounding box, sort by descending cell area, break equal-area ties by top/bottom/left/right bounding-box order, then concatenate the crops left-to-right, top-aligned, with one black separator column. Scheduled tie scenes rule out color-based tie breaking; sparse shapes distinguish cell area from bounding-box area.

A 0-background grid has a contiguous blue header run in row 0 and exactly three separate, differently colored body components.  Let n be the number of blue header cells.  Scan body components in row-major order and take the first object with exactly n boundary cells.  Crop to that object's full bounding box, erase its interior cells, and preserve its boundary in the object's original color.  Most generated scenes have one match; every fourth sample has two matches so the canonical find-first tie branch is taught explicitly.
Find every three-cell cap whose next row contains its two legs and a zero center; preserve the scene and mark the bottom cell of each gap column orange.
Move the non-marker object by the vector from marker 3 to marker 4.

Three to five sparse colors share a grid. The row-major first nonzero color is the key and survives; all distractor colors are erased. Exact canonical-size anchors and a twelve-slot schedule vary selector position, numeric rank, and frequency rank so those cues cannot replace scanning.
Hollow color-1 object gets exterior-adjacent and interior-adjacent background marks.
An anchored green/red source shape rotates by blue-dot count and stamps at cyan.
Pair ordered color swatches with ordered gray masks, then expand a lower color layout through those masks.

A selector marker at the upper-left names one body object's color and a transform marker at the upper-right names the operation. Crop the unique selector-colored 4-connected body object, apply key 1=identity, 2=rotate-CW, 3=flip-LR, 4=transpose, or 5=rotate-180, then crop to content.
Place two through six isolated, distinct-colored 4-connected objects with strictly distinct areas; output their colors in increasing-area order.
Any colored grid; rule emits a 4-fold kaleidoscope (2h × 2w) of the input.

A zero-background 8..10 by 10..12 grid contains two or three separated, distinct-color, 4-connected asymmetric objects. Each object has 4..5 cells and a local footprint at most 3x3. The answer independently transposes every object's occupied offsets inside its own bounding box, keeps that box's top-left anchor fixed, and paints only the transposed cells on a fresh zero canvas.

Walls partition the input into rooms. Doors (7) induce adjacency edges; green markers (3) are counted per room. Paint a whole room cyan (8) iff its marker count equals its number of neighboring rooms.
skills: mixed local/global reasoning, graph degree, roomwise selection
canonicalization, symbolic output, local neighborhood encoding
summary: Normalize the color-2/3/4 cardinal frame and emit a 3x3 map of only the local color-8 cells; ignore other colors and radius-2 markers.

0-bg grid with several connected objects of varied aspect ratios. At least one TALL (bbox h > w), one WIDE (bbox w > h), and one SQUARE (bbox h == w). Objects in any non-{0, 2, 4, 8} color (avoid output colors). Objects separated by ≥1-cell buffer. Rule: for each object, compute bbox h and w. If h > w → recolor to 2 (tall). If w > h → recolor to 8 (wide). If h == w → recolor to 4 (square). Output preserves grid shape.
The red object whose bounding box reaches lowest is recolored green.

On a background-0 grid, find every solid green (3) axis-aligned rectangle. Recolor exactly its bounding-box perimeter cyan (8), leave strict green interior cells green, and preserve all non-green distractor objects.
Count of red(2) cells = Manhattan distance ring radius around green(3) markers; bg cells at that radius become 8.
Sort separated monochrome nonzero objects by size descending, breaking ties by top-left reading order, and recolor the second object cyan (8).

Distinct keys in row 0 label 3x3 prototypes in rows 1-3.  The nonzero keys in the final row form an ordered query, and the answer galleries the corresponding prototypes with one zero column between copies.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-12) with: (a) cells (0,0) and (0,1) = TWO TRANSFORM COMMAND values in {1..5}; (b) one MOTIF (3-5 connected cells in 2-3 colors) placed in the interior, away from (0,0)/(0,1). Rule: read cmd1 = grid[0][0], cmd2 = grid[0][1]. Clear those two cells. Crop the rest to its non-zero bbox (the motif). Apply cmd1 then cmd2 in order, each chosen by code: 1 = rot-CW, 2 = 180°, 3 = flip-LR, 4 = flip-UD, 5+ = transpose. Output: motif after both transforms applied.

On each row independently, every nonzero color that occurs exactly twice defines a horizontal endpoint pair. Fill the whole interval between those two occurrences with that color. Colors occurring once or three times do not define a span. Multiple non-overlapping color pairs in one row are all processed.

0-bg grid (size varies) with several non-{1,2} shapes (frames and one-side-open C shapes) and a top-left control cell. Rule: if g[0][0]==1 fill each object's per-row span solid, else per-column span. The grid size, shapes/colors/positions and the control axis vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).
Columns with exactly two orange endpoints are filled vertically between them.
Blue marker count selects which yellow nested-frame depth is filled cyan.

0-bg grid (h~8-14, w~8-14) with: (a) A 2-COLUMN × kh-TALL (kh ∈ [3, 5]) KEY TABLE — a solid rectangle at (kr0, kc0)..(kr0+kh, kc0+1) where each row r of the key holds a (LEFT_COLOR, RIGHT_COLOR) PAIR (distinct colors from a palette, encoding the mapping LEFT → RIGHT); (b) OPTIONAL VERTICAL SEPARATOR LINE at col w//2 in COLOR 2 (sometimes present, sometimes not); (c) SPARSE TARGET CELLS outside the key bbox in values drawn from the key's LEFT colors (so they trigger substitution). Rule (APPLY KEY-TABLE SUBSTITUTION TO ALL CELLS OUTSIDE THE KEY BBOX): identify the KEY TABLE (2-column × kh-tall solid multicolor component). PARSE each key row as a MAPPING LEFT_COLOR → RIGHT_COLOR. For EACH CELL OUTSIDE the key bbox: if its color matches any key row's LEFT color, RECOLOR to that row's RIGHT color. Else, keep. Key table stays intact. Net: target cells get substituted color-by-color according to the table's lookup.
1-walls form an n×m grid of compartments; each has 1 marker; output fills each compartment with its marker color.

Panel 1 is a template shape; panel 2 a board with several separated identity copies of it (color-9 column between). Rule: mark color-8 at the centre of every border-clear template match (no rotation). Template, colour, board size and copy count vary.
skills: context-sensitive matching, border inspection, filtered markers

summary: 0-bg grid (h~4-5, w derived) with N=3-4 same-height PANELS each of width 4, separated by FULL COLOR-9 (maroon) DIVIDER COLUMNS of width 1. Each panel holds a CONNECTED MOTIF of 2-4 cells in some non-{0, 9} color (distinct per panel). Output uniq_out=16 (intrinsic — N×N binary match matrices normalize). Rule (BUILD DIHEDRAL-MATCH MATRIX): identify the N PANELS separated by 9-dividers. EMIT an N×N OUTPUT GRID where out[r][c] = 8 if PANEL-r's NORMALIZED MOTIF CELLS match ANY DIHEDRAL VARIANT (8 transforms — 4 rotations × 2 flips) of PANEL-c's MOTIF CELLS. Else 0. Net: pairwise shape-equivalence matrix across panels modulo D4.
skills: pairwise comparison, dihedral normalization, symbolic matrix output

summary: Mode-bg grid (size varies) with a 0-cell SHAPE and one marker. Rule: the marker's offset from the shape center sets a direction and step (manhattan-1); the shape is stamped in the marker's color marching away from center until off-grid. The grid size, shape, marker direction/distance and colors vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~28 distinct).
2x2 colored proto in top-left + 1-3 color-9 markers in the interior.

0-bg grid with an INNER color-5 wall maze: a one-cell zero moat surrounds a rectangular 5-wall frame, and one or two internal 5-wall rows/cols split that frame into 4, 6, or 9 rectangular compartments. Each compartment contains a compact same-color marker blob from {2,3,4}; the marker color is the strict majority for that compartment. The canonical rule visits every non-5 region, ignores regions with no markers, and fills each marked compartment with its majority marker color while preserving the 5-walls and leaving the outer zero moat unchanged.
Several non-touching blobs with varied aspect ratios; output recolors by tall/wide/square.

Find the unique largest same-colour component and crop its bounding box. Every isolated horizontal pair outside that box is read left-to-right as (replacement, source). Recolour all matching source cells inside the crop with their replacements; leave the frame cells unchanged.

A zero-background grid contains colored wall components. Treat all nonzero cells together as walls, find every 4-connected zero region that does not touch the grid border, and output a fresh zero grid with exactly those enclosed cells colored 8. Wall colors and component membership do not matter; multiple components may cooperate to enclose one region.
N panels separated by full color-9 columns, each with a small motif; rule picks the pair with matching shape.
skills: sequence extrapolation, repeated transforms, missing-tile completion

summary: For each 4-connected color-0 region, fill it with its local surrounding color iff the region does not touch the canvas border and its cardinal boundary contains exactly one nonzero color. Open regions and enclosed regions with mixed-color boundaries remain unchanged.

Find the unique blue (1) monochromatic object, follow cardinal contacts between differently coloured objects to its whole contact cluster, crop that union tightly, and recolour every selected cell cyan (8).

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-10, w ∈ 7-10) with: N_PAIRS ∈ 2-3 DIAGONAL ENDPOINT PAIRS — each pair consists of 2 cells of the SAME non-bg color (colors drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT from {1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9}), placed at endpoints of a 45° diagonal of LENGTH k ∈ 2-4 cells: A = (r1, c1) and B = (r1+k*sr, c1+k*sc) where sr, sc ∈ {-1, +1} (any of 4 diagonal directions). The interior cells along the diagonal are RESERVED (occupied set prevents other pairs from using them). Only the 2 endpoints are painted. Rule (FOR EACH COLOR APPEARING EXACTLY TWICE WHOSE CELLS LIE ON A 45° DIAGONAL (|DR| = |DC|), DRAW THE FULL DIAGONAL LINE BETWEEN THEM IN THAT COLOR): GROUP cells by color. For EACH color with exactly 2 cells: CHECK |dr| == |dc| (diagonal). PAINT every cell on the 45° line from endpoint A to endpoint B with that color. Net: endpoint pairs become solid diagonal colored lines.
For each column independently, collect its nonzero cells from top to bottom, clear that column, and place the collected values at the bottom without changing their order. Empty columns remain empty.

Grid with 1-3 solid 2×2 color-3 blocks and 1-3 solid 2×2 blocks of OTHER colors as decoys. Rule: count the number of (overlapping) solid 2×2 sub-blocks of color 3 (sliding 2×2 window). Output is a fresh 3×3 grid: cell (r, r) = 1 for r in 0..count-1, all other cells = 0. So the output is a diagonal of 1s of length = count.

A 2x2 lattice of 3x3 tiles separated by color-9 dividers (7x7). Each tile carries EDGE-CENTER CONNECTOR colors on its inward-facing edges and a CENTER color; the solved lattice matches connectors across every internal seam (4 distinct connector colors, 4 distinct centers, all 8 colors random). The four tiles are then SCRAMBLED — permuted into the 4 slots and each randomly rotated. Rule: search permutations x rotations for the 2x2 arrangement whose touching edge-centers all match, and output that assembled lattice (lex-min valid orientation). The colors drive the OUTPUT and the scramble drives the INPUT, so both vary freely (was 4 fixed tiles with 6 hardcoded scrambles).
skills: search, global arrangement, rotations, combinatorial assembly

summary: A command at (0,0) selects identity/CW/180/CCW. Remove it, crop the single connected monochrome object, and apply the selected quarter turn.

Find the dominant outer-border color and the dominant non-border field color.  The field encloses a rectangular matrix of rooms.  Replace each room by its unique marker color, or by the outer-border color when the room is empty, preserving the room matrix's row/column order.
Recolor each nonzero body cell by the header color in its column.
Canonical-scale colored grid; rule outputs 2h × 2w 4-fold kaleidoscope.

Small grid (h, w~3-6) with n_colors (3-4) DISTINCT NONZERO COLORS at random positions, each with a DISTINCT COUNT determined by a distribution (uniform_gap/increasing/decreasing/polarized/powers). All counts are < total cells; max count ≤ grid_h (so bars fit). Palette kind: warm/cool/broad/primary. Rule (COLOR-COUNT BAR CHART): COUNT cells per COLOR (including 0). SORT colors by COUNT DESCENDING. EMIT OUTPUT GRID: each SORTED COLOR becomes a VERTICAL COLUMN in the output, with a BAR rising from the TOP (top cells = the color, lower cells = 0). The BAR HEIGHT = the color's count. Output dims: max(counts) × n_colors. Net: color-count histogram emitted as a top-to-bottom bar chart.

A 7..14 by 7..14 zero-background grid contains 2..4 isolated monochrome L-triominoes.  There are 1..2 distinct nonzero colors.  Rotate every object 90 degrees clockwise inside its own tight 2x2 bounding box, preserving color and the bounding-box anchor.

A 0-background grid contains 3-5 isolated, distinctly colored objects. For each object, crop to its bounding box and count enclosed 0-regions. Sort objects lexicographically by (hole count, nonzero-cell count, bbox top row, bbox left column), rotate each crop 90 degrees clockwise, then pack the rotated crops left-to-right with one blank column between them and vertical center alignment.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~10-12) with: (a) an INDEX MARKER k at (0, 0) drawn as a single non-bg cell in some color (k ∈ 1..N where N = number of blobs); (b) N=3-4 disjoint CONNECTED BLOBS at random interior positions, each in a distinct non-{0, k} color and each with a distinct size from a small size-pool. Blobs are 4-adjacency-isolated. Rule: (1) CLEAR the index marker at (0, 0). (2) SORT the remaining blobs lexicographically by (size ASC, color ASC, top-row r1 ASC, left-col c1 ASC). (3) SELECT the k-th blob (1-indexed) under that ordering. (4) CROP the original grid to that blob's axis-aligned BBOX and output the cropped subgrid. Net: tiny output that's a bounding-box extract of one rank-selected blob.
Bordered red/green seed fields with open, detour, finite-tie, seedless-chamber, and complete-partition profiles. Open cells use wall-aware BFS distance; ties and seedless chambers remain black.

Extract every same-color 4-connected component with a two-dimensional bounding box, sort those records by bounding-box area, and redraw them inside the largest rectangle from largest to smallest. Hollow or occluded records become frames, solid records stay solid, and each next record is bottom-left aligned within the preceding record.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-10, w ∈ 8-10) with: (a) ONE CMD CELL at FIXED position (0, 0) — value ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} selecting a rotation (per demos: 1=cw90, 2=180, 3=ccw90, 4=identity); (b) ONE SINGLE NON-RECTANGULAR BLOB in a non-cmd color drawn via draw_color: a SIZE ∈ 4-7 cell irregular blob built by grow_blob random walk, placed so NONE of its cells lie in the 2×2 corner around (0, 0) (so cmd stays isolated). Rule (READ THE CMD, CROP THE BLOB TO ITS BBOX, ROTATE BY THE CMD VALUE): READ cmd from (0, 0) → select rotation. FIND the single non-bg blob (excluding the cmd cell). CROP the blob to its bounding box (a small h_bb × w_bb grid with the blob's color where cells are present, 0 elsewhere). ROTATE the cropped grid by cmd (cw90 / 180 / ccw90 / identity). OUTPUT the rotated crop. Net: a single colored shape is extracted and rotated by the corner code, yielding a small output grid.
Read the two transform codes at the upper left, crop the connected color-9 proto, apply code1 then code2, and stamp the transformed shape centered at each isolated anchor in the anchor's color.

Grid is a 2×2 grid of rectangular ROOMS separated by color-1 (blue) WALLS (also color 7 and 9 count as walls in the rule). Each room has bg=0 floor with at most one non-wall non-bg single-cell SEED at the room's center. Rule: extract the rooms (BFS over non-wall cells). For each room, find its seed (any non-bg, non-wall cell). If a seed exists, flood-fill the room's floor cells with that seed's color. Empty rooms stay 0. Walls remain unchanged.
skills: multi-room mapping, local room fill, color transfer

summary: Grid where every column has a SEED of 1-3 non-zero values starting from row 0 (contiguous prefix). Below the seed prefix, all cells are 0 — the area the rule will fill. Different columns may have different seed lengths. Rule: for each column c, find the contiguous-from-top non-zero prefix as the seed pattern. Repeat that seed downward periodically to fill the column for all h rows. Output has the same dims as input but with all 0-cells in each column replaced with the corresponding seed value.
Key motif at top-left + 8-targets; rule stamps key at each target.
Read the nonzero, non-9 colors in row 0 from left to right. For each hollow 9-frame in top-left order, emit that legend color when it is present in the frame interior, otherwise 0.

A 0-background grid contains one or more monochrome 4-connected objects. For EACH object, identify every 4-connected background region enclosed inside that object's bounding box. Output only those enclosed cells, colored with the enclosing object's color; erase all object walls, open cavities, solid objects, and other distractors to 0. The curriculum covers rectangular and irregular enclosures, one- and multi-cell holes, multiple holes in one object, multiple enclosing objects with equal or different colors, and non-enclosing distractors.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holds CONTROL in {1, 2}; (b) 3 SOURCE CELLS in DISTINCT non-{0, control} colors at hardcoded positions depending on control: ctrl=1 (LR mirror) → sources at (1, 1), (2, 2), (h-2, 1); ctrl=2 (UD mirror) → sources at (1, 2), (1, w-3), (2, 1). Some sources may have a 2-cell stripe extension. Rule (MIRROR SOURCE CELLS BY CONTROL AXIS): READ control at (0, 0). For EACH non-{0, control} SOURCE CELL at (r, c): ctrl=1 → PAINT (r, w-1-c) with the same color (left-right mirror); ctrl=2 → PAINT (h-1-r, c) with the same color (up-down mirror). The control + originals stay. Net: source cells mirror across the axis selected by control.
Outline the actual 4-neighbor boundary of 2-4 distinct-color objects; the curriculum mixes rectangles with lawful concave and holed shapes.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-9, w ∈ 7-10) with: SEED_COUNT ∈ 2-4 SINGLE COLORED CELLS, each in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from {1..9}, placed at random positions where: (a) row ∈ 0..h-2 (not the bottom row, so a downward ray has room to extend); (b) col ∈ 1..w-1 (not col 0, so a leftward ray has room); (c) each seed sits on a DISTINCT anti-diagonal (r + c differs across seeds) so rays don't overlap. Rule (FROM EACH SEED, DRAW A DOWN-LEFT (↙) DIAGONAL RAY OF THE SAME COLOR ALL THE WAY TO THE GRID BORDER): For EACH seed at (r, c) with color k: PAINT cells (r+i, c-i) for i = 1, 2, ... until either r+i ≥ h OR c-i < 0 (out of bounds). Each ray cell painted color k. Seeds stay at their original positions. Net: each seed shoots a downward-leftward diagonal of its color to the grid edge.

0-bg grid with ≥2 connected motifs in distinct non-zero colors (≥1-cell buffer, 3-5 cells each, varied shapes). The rule consumes the FIRST TWO components in bbox-top-left sort order; any additional motifs are ignored by the rule but add visual variety. Rule: sort all connected components by bbox top-left (row-major). Take the first two. Crop each to its bbox. Normalize the pair to a common (max-h × max-w) bounding box. Compute symmetric difference between the two binary masks: output cell = 8 if exactly one of the two masks has a non-zero cell there, else 0. Output size = (max-h × max-w).

Keep every source cell and copy it by 180-degree point reflection around the unique color-5 pivot. Canonical two-blob scenes are interleaved with off-center, axis-mixed, and multi-quadrant counterexamples.

Three-color 4x5/3x6 scenes. Every equal nonzero horizontal pair copies its color into the two cells directly below, using the original input for pair detection. A four-slot schedule mixes isolated-pair anchors with overlap, overwrite, vertical-decoy, and bottom-boundary witnesses.

Find every nonzero color occurring exactly twice. If its two cells are row- or column-aligned and the strict interior is all 0, fill the whole inclusive segment with that color. Blocked pairs, nonaligned pairs, and colors occurring three times stay unchanged. Generated five-sample windows contain horizontal and vertical bridges, singleton- and repeated-color blockers, and explicit wrong-count and nonalignment counterexamples.

Fixed 15×15 color-7 (orange) bg grid with: (a) a RED DIAMOND OUTLINE — color 2 cells at all positions where Manhattan distance from a center (red_r, red_c) equals red_radius (2 or 3); (b) a GRAY DIAMOND OUTLINE — color 5 cells at all positions where Manhattan distance from a center (gray_r, gray_c) equals gray_radius (1 or 2). Diamonds are positioned with margin so growth/shrink stays in-bounds. Rule: detect each diamond. RED diamond SHRINKS by 1 (replace red cells with bg, redraw at red_radius - 1). GRAY diamond GROWS by 1 (redraw at gray_radius + 1). Output: bg + shrunk red diamond + grown gray diamond.

7-bg grid (h, w~8-10) with: (a) 2-3 HORIZONTAL PAIRS — two horizontally adjacent cells in the same row in a distinct non-7 color, at distinct rows; (b) 1-2 VERTICAL PAIRS — two vertically adjacent cells in the same col in a distinct non-7 color, at distinct cols. All pair colors are distinct across pairs. Position bias varies (scattered, centered, corners, spread). Rule (EXPAND EACH PAIR INTO ITS FULL ROW/COL): For EACH HORIZONTAL PAIR at row r in color C: PAINT ALL cells in row r with color C (except where another pair's expansion has already painted — specific overlap behavior is rule-dependent). For EACH VERTICAL PAIR at col c in color C: PAINT ALL cells in col c with color C. Cells not on any pair's row/col stay at 7. Net: horizontal pairs grow into full-width stripes, vertical pairs into full-height stripes.

Nonzero-modal-bg square grid (size~12-16) with many separated OUTER-color cells on an interior lattice plus one or two INNER-color markers. The outer color is the most frequent non-bg color; the inner color is present but less frequent. Rule: for every modal-background cell, if it has a diagonal neighbor of the outer color and no cardinal neighbor of the outer color, recolor it to the inner color. Net: sparse outer marks project a diagonal inner-color halo into the background.
Treat 5s as walls; paint each open 0 cell cyan (8) iff its 4-neighbor shortest-path distances from the unique red (2) and green (3) seeds are both finite and equal. Preserve every other input cell.

Split the input at the two solid color-9 columns.  The first two equal panels contain a label at local (0,0) and a monochrome prototype.  The third panel contains a translated D4 transform (rotation or reflection) of exactly one prototype.  Return a blank panel of the same size with the query cells kept in their displayed positions and recolored with the matching prototype's label.

A 0-background grid contains three or four distinct-color clues. Each clue is exactly three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle; complete its missing fourth corner in the same color. Preserve every existing cell, including the unrelated singleton distractor; color 9 becomes an active rectangle once in every three scheduled synthetic samples.
Sparse non-zero cells in the left half; right half is empty.
Two 6-column panels separated by a marker; OR of nonzero-occupancy → 1, else 0.

Treat every 4-connected nonzero component as a color-blind shape, order the components by top-left position, and output an N×N grid with red(2) where two masks are equivalent under any of the eight dihedral transforms and 0 otherwise. Generated scenes use canonical canvas/palette profiles and include explicit same-area/same-bbox/color-histogram near-misses plus reflection-only positive matches.

A noisy {0,1} grid contains 1..4 disconnected color-3 chevrons.  Each chevron is an apex plus at least one marker on each of its two diagonal arms; interior arm markers may be absent and the two arms may be asymmetric.  For every supported chevron, fill its solid triangular wedge with color 8, preserving all color-3 markers and all outside background cells.
A corner color-8 prototype plus singleton transform-code anchors.

Two row-major color-9 markers define a translation vector. Remove both markers and copy only the smallest same-color 4-connected object by that vector; ties are resolved by top row, left column, then color.
Single asymmetric color blob in interior; output is row-count bar chart of its bbox.

Even-width split canvas: left half has detached colored inserts; right half has hollow frames with distinct interior dimensions. Each insert bbox matches exactly one frame interior, sometimes only after 90° rotation.
Hollow frames each holding content; output = horizontal gallery of the interiors.

An inset rectangular frame contains exactly two colored seeds. Paint color 9 on every strict-interior cell equidistant from the seeds in Manhattan distance; opposite-parity seeds lawfully yield an unchanged input.
Interior cells of straight blue segments are recolored red.
Square n×n grid with cells in the lower triangle; rule outputs n×n with diagonal=5, lower triangle=0, upper triangle = transpose(lower) (cell (r,c) ← input[c][r] for r<c).

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~13-16) with 3 HORIZONTAL WIRES at non-touching rows (sampled from {1, 3, 5, 7}). Each wire is: ONE COLOR-2 (red) START cell at (r, c0) followed by a sequence of COLOR-1 (blue) cells at (r, c0+1..c0+length). WIRE LENGTHS are {3, 5, 7} shuffled (strictly distinct, longest is unique). Rule (LONGEST-WIRE RECOLOR): trace EACH WIRE from its RED START. COUNT the length of each wire's BLUE PATH. RECOLOR the entire BLUE PATH of the LONGEST wire to COLOR 3 (green). Other wires' blue cells stay blue. Red start cells stay. Net: longest blue wire becomes green; shorter wires keep their blue color.

A 0-background grid contains one singleton corner marker and two or three other monochrome 4-connected objects in distinct colors. Ignore the marker. Choose the candidate containing the cell with minimum Manhattan distance to the marked corner, requiring a unique winner, and output that candidate cropped to its tight bounding box with internal zeros preserved.
Satellite shape mirrored into other three quadrants around anchor.
Inner tab protrusions cut through inner object and extend through outer frame.

Find the unique blue component and compute its (area, enclosed holes, reflection-symmetry class). Recolor every non-blue component with the same triple cyan (8). The v4 curriculum uses different-shape feature twins, one-coordinate decoys for area/holes/symmetry, a two-match branch, and exact canonical 11x16, 12x16, and 12x17 five-color profiles.

A 12xW zero-background input is four stacked 3-row monochrome masks. Project the four bands onto one 3xW frame and choose the first nonzero cell in priority order band 0, then band 1, then band 3, then band 2; emit 0 only when all four projected cells are 0. Band colors are distinct within a scene and may be reassigned across bands, so color identity is not a substitute for band priority.
Every three-cell 2x2 color corner is completed into a solid block.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-12) with 2-5 BLUE(1) L-TROMINOES (3-cell L-shapes in 2×2 bboxes with one missing corner). L-trominoes are placed at ANCHOR-GRID positions (every 3 cells starting at row 0, col 0), each with a RANDOM MISSING CORNER (one of 4 orientations). Each L-tromino occupies 3 of 4 cells in its 2×2 bbox, leaving the missing corner at 0. Rule (FILL EACH 2×2 WINDOW WITH 3 BLUES + 1 BG CELL → GREEN AT THE BG CELL): scan EVERY 2×2 WINDOW in the grid. For EACH window containing EXACTLY 3 BLUE(1) CELLS AND 1 BG(0) CELL: PAINT the bg cell at (r, c) with COLOR 3 (green). Windows with other blue-counts (0, 1, 2, 4) stay unchanged. Net: every L-tromino completes to a 2×2 solid by adding a green dot in the missing corner.
Intersect each marker-color bounding box with the gray bounding rectangle, filling intersections in ascending color order.

0-bg grid (h, w ~10-16) with: (a) FOUR DOTS at the corners of an axis-aligned rect (rh × rw, rh, rw ~5-8) in a MINORITY color; (b) a BLOB of 5+ cells strictly INSIDE the rect in a MAJORITY color. Two distinct non-bg colors total. Rule: identify the 4 corner-dot cells (minority color = dot color). Find the rectangle they define. Crop the rect's INTERIOR (strictly inside the 4 corner positions). Recolor the blob from majority (big) color to MINORITY (dot) color. Output: the cropped interior with the recolored blob.

0-bg grid (h~7-18, w~8-20) with 2-5 PAIRS (one pair per distinct color). For EACH PAIR: pick a color from a shuffled palette of n_pairs distinct values from {1..9}, pick two cells at OPPOSITE DIAGONAL CORNERS of an axis-aligned rectangle: top-left (r1, c1) and bottom-right (r2, c2) where r2 > r1 and c2 > c1. The bbox rectangles do NOT overlap (overlap check via _bb_overlap). Place these 2 cells in the chosen color; the rest of each rectangle's interior + border are bg-0. Each color appears at exactly 2 cells. Rule (FOR EACH COLOR WITH EXACTLY 2 CELLS, FILL THE SOLID RECTANGLE BETWEEN THEM TREATING THEM AS DIAGONAL CORNERS): for EACH non-bg COLOR in the grid: COUNT its occurrences. IF count = 2 AND the two cells are at distinct rows AND distinct columns (forming diagonal corners of a non-degenerate rectangle): COMPUTE the bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2) from the two corner positions. FILL every cell (r, c) with r1 ≤ r ≤ r2 AND c1 ≤ c ≤ c2 with the pair's color. Colors with count ≠ 2 or with axis-aligned cells stay unchanged. Net: each color-pair grows into a solid filled rectangle.
Rows with exactly two separated 5s and an all-zero interior are filled with 3 between the endpoints; blocked, wrong-color, and three-5 rows stay unchanged.
Each red cell creates a yellow down-right echo if the target is empty.

On a zero background, identify the unique strictly largest 4-connected nonzero component, ignoring color, and crop the whole input to that component's bounding box. Preserve the component's colors and any zero concavities; smaller components are decoys outside the crop.
Tiny L triomino orientations select large output corner placements.

Find every globally largest all-zero square and paint their union color 1. Also paint cells belonging to any side>=2 all-zero square whose entire footprint is disjoint from that maximal union. Preserve the single nonzero obstacle color.

Close vertical holes independently inside every 4-connected non-zero component: in each occupied component column, paint the inclusive span from its topmost to bottommost cell in that component color. Already column-convex controls remain unchanged.

Recolor to 3 the union of all complete color-2 2x2 windows in the original input. Preserve all other cells, including attached red tails and nonred squares. Lessons mix isolated squares with overlapping windows, unequal red components, hollow red rings, and unchanged nonred squares.
Sparse cells; rows with (4,7) or (1,8) pair → pull right cell adjacent.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~7-10 by ~8-12) with exactly 4 non-zero cells all of the SAME color, placed at the 4 corners of an axis-aligned rectangle (r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2). The rectangle has h ≥ 3 and w ≥ 3 (so the border is visible). Rule: collect all non-zero cells, read their common color, compute bbox. Build output: fresh 0-canvas with a HOLLOW RECTANGLE (border only, interior 0) drawn at the bbox in that color. The 4 input corners are preserved; edge cells between them are filled in.

Two or three hollow color-5 rectangular rooms each contain one distinct colored seed. Flood a room interior with its seed only when that room's wall is an isolated color-5 connected component; touching rooms remain unchanged because their merged wall component is not one rectangle.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) containing 3-4 small connected MOTIFS, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color from {2..9}. Each motif is 3-5 cells (small polyomino) generated by random walk. Motifs are scattered at non-overlapping positions with 1-cell padding so each motif remains an isolated connected component. Rule: for each distinct non-bg color, extract that motif's normalized cells. PACK every motif's bbox into a VERTICAL GALLERY OUTPUT — stack the motifs top-to-bottom (or in some canonical ordering, often by color or size) into a smaller composite grid, each in its original color. Output size depends on motif count and dimensions. Net: input has scattered colored motifs; output is a clean vertical pack.

0-bg vertical 2-panel layout (top: template panel; bottom: board panel) separated by a COLOR-9 divider. The TEMPLATE is a fixed 3×3 pattern ([[4,5,6],[7,8,2],[3,4,5]]) placed at (1, 1) in the template panel (h-tall × 5-wide). The BOARD (h × w~9-13) contains 2-4 COPIES of the same template stamped at random non-overlapping anchors. Rule: identify the TEMPLATE in the top panel. SCAN the BOARD: for EACH 3×3 window that EXACTLY MATCHES the template (cell-by-cell, all values match), KEEP those template cells. CLEAR (set to 0) every non-matching cell on the board. Output: the board with only matching template instances kept. Net: template panel teaches pattern; output is board cleared except for exact template matches.
skills: window filtering, exact template detection, preserve original colors

summary: 3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.

On an 8-background grid, erase every isolated colored dot and repaint it at its color-specific destination: 7 up two, 2 left two, 9 down two, and 1 right one. Generated lessons keep all destinations in bounds, unique, and separate from every source dot.
