3 isolated multicolor components: A, transform(A) recolored, and an independent B.

Fill exactly the black center of each horizontal blue(1)-black(0)-blue(1) triple with blue.  Read every decision from the input grid: wider gaps, vertical triples, equal non-blue endpoints, and nonblack centers are preserved.  The sampler alternates canonical-scale and broad semantic profiles so every three-example lesson retains a complete counterexample.
2-3 solid rectangles in distinct colors.
Sparse non-zero cells + command at (0,0) selecting gravity direction.

Read non-zero 4-connected components in bounding-box reading order. The first two crops A and A' demonstrate one non-identity transform from {rotate 90 CW, rotate 180, transpose, flip LR, flip UD}. Infer that transform from the full coloured crops, then apply it to the full bounding-box crop of the third component B and output only that transformed crop. A disconnected satellite inside B's bbox is therefore included.

A black(0) grid contains exactly one red(2) seed, one green(3) seed, and optionally structured gray(5) walls. Run 4-connected shortest-path BFS through every non-wall cell from both seeds. Recolor each black cell cyan(8) when red is closer, yellow(4) when green is closer, and leave it black on an equal-distance tie. Seeds and walls remain unchanged. Normal lessons alternate an open witness with wall mazes whose detours make the BFS answer differ from a Manhattan-distance shortcut.
Single colored cell selects the row to fill with that color.
Top 5 rows: prototype shape; row 5 has 3 control values: t1, t2, out_color.
Operation code 1/2/3 above two equal support-mask panels separated by 5; the panels share one signal color and contain overlap plus one-sided cells.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-2 shape and a color-3 shape. Rule: normalize both to their bbox corners and output color 8 where exactly one has a cell (their XOR), on a max-dims grid. The grid size, the two shapes and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

A 0-background grid contains 3-5 separated red (2) polyominoes with distinct cell counts and one 1-3-cell non-red decoration. Rank the red components by cell count, choose the second-largest, crop its bounding box, and recolor its cells cyan (8). Exact controls cover dimensions and component count; decoration color/size, layouts, and shapes vary internally. Every three consecutive samples include a size-vs-perimeter counterexample.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~8-10) with: (a) 1-2 ISOLATED COLOR-1 (blue) CELLS at INTERIOR positions (rows 1..h-2, cols 1..w-2); (b) 1-2 ISOLATED COLOR-2 (red) CELLS at INTERIOR positions. Cells are placed via a chosen POSITION BIAS (scattered, spread, centered, corners) with min Manhattan separation ≥3 between any pair (so each marker is isolated). Rule (EXPAND COLOR-1 BY CARDINAL ADJACENCY, COLOR-2 BY DIAGONAL ADJACENCY): For EACH 0-CELL at (r, c): (i) if any of its 4 CARDINAL NEIGHBORS (up/down/left/right) is COLOR 1, PAINT (r, c) to COLOR 1. (ii) ELSE if any of its 4 DIAGONAL NEIGHBORS (nw/ne/sw/se) is COLOR 2, PAINT (r, c) to COLOR 2. Cells already non-0 stay. Net: each 1-marker grows a plus halo, each 2-marker grows an X halo (when cardinal vs diagonal criteria differ).
1-2 hollow rectangles + 0-1 solid blob in distinct colors.
2-3 connected motifs in distinct colors at separate positions.

Read the distinct first-column colors top to bottom; rank the separated color-3 components by descending cell area; crop and recolor them in that palette order; then stack the crops vertically with one blank row.

0-bg grid (size varies) with a color-1 anchor, one non-1 target congruent to it, and distractor shapes with different row-profiles. Rule: find the non-1 object whose per-row cell-count profile matches the anchor, crop it, recolor to 8. The grid size, shapes, colors and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).

Canonical-color marker-gravity/local-rewrite contexts, extended on the right by each row's edge color to create many distinct non-identity pairs while preserving the radius-3 contexts matched by the shipped rule.

0-bg grid (h~13-15, w~14-16) with: (a) ROW 1 area (above sep) has a color-1 (blue) TEMPLATE shape (5-cell tetromino-style: L, T, corner, stair); (b) FULL color-9 (maroon) SEPARATOR row at row sep (~5); (c) BELOW the separator, 1-4 color-3 (green) CANDIDATE shapes — some matching the template's normalized shape and some not (a NON-MATCH distractor). Rule: detect the color-1 template shape above the sep row. For each color-3 candidate below: if its normalized shape matches the template, recolor every cell from 3 to 2 (red). Non-matching shapes stay color 3.

13×13 0-bg grid with 1-3 PLUSES, each at fixed centers {(3,3), (9,5), (5,10)}. Each plus has a non-{0,3} CENTER cell and 4 cardinal ARMS in color 3 (green). Pluses use distinct center colors. Rule: detect pluses by their 4-green-arm pattern. For each empty bg cell (r, c), look for a plus whose center is on the same COLUMN c and whose column-extent (cells in col c reachable from center without hitting another plus's arm) includes r. If yes → paint with that plus's center color. Else check row-extent on the same row. Net: each plus's center color shoots row and column rays that stop at other pluses' arms; column projections take priority where both row and column rays cover a cell.

One connected two-color shape sits on a unique nonzero modal background. Swap the two shape colors. Keep the bottom half in place and shift the top half right by the full shape-bbox width; when black (0) is a shape color, use the horizontal span of the non-black cells instead. The default six-slot schedule uses a repeating black/black/nonblack pattern, includes all linked 16x16 canonical bbox profiles, and keeps a black-branch witness after any one query holdout from a three-pair lesson. Every two-demo lesson refutes full-width, no-swap, move-both-halves, and grid-midpoint shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-1 PIVOT and a payload of one color placed in a quadrant. Rule: replicate each payload cell at its four 90-degree rotations about the pivot (in the payload color), producing a 4-fold pinwheel. The grid size, pivot position, payload offsets and color vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~21 distinct).

Read aligned nonzero pairs from the first two rows: row 0 is the source color and row 1 is its replacement. Remove those two rows, then recolor each remaining source-colored cell with its paired target color. Background remains 0; an unmapped nonzero color would remain unchanged.
Replace isolated singleton seeds with hollow 3x3 rings.

A strict-mode background surrounds two non-background colours. One colour forms two or three separated convex-hull objects; exactly one object has K background cells inside its convex hull. The other colour contributes exactly K donor cells, which may be connected, scattered, or mixed. Erase all donor cells and fill only the matching object's convex-hull gap. A three-profile schedule varies donor connectivity, hull geometry, object size, and colour-role order. Dense profiles include a side gap outside horizontal row spans, so a canonical-fitting interpolation shortcut is contradicted even after any one pair is held out.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-11, w ∈ 10-13) with: (a) ONE 180°-SYMMETRIC COMPONENT — drawn from _180_SYM bank (4 four-connected variants: 2×2 square, plus, H/7-cell, S-tetromino), painted in palette[0] at a random non-overlapping position via _free_box (1-cell padding); (b) 1-2 ASYMMETRIC COMPONENTS — drawn from _ASYM bank (5 variants: L-tromino, S-tromino, P-tetromino, L-tetromino, S-tet), each in a DISTINCT non-symmetric color drawn from palette[1:]. All colors distinct, drawn from {1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9}. Rule (FIND THE UNIQUE 180°-SYMMETRIC COMPONENT, CROP TO ITS BBOX, OUTPUT): EXTRACT every 4-connected non-bg COMPONENT (single-color). For EACH component: COMPUTE its NORMALIZED BINARY SHAPE; CHECK if shape == its 180° ROTATION. SELECT the unique component where shape is 180°-symmetric. CROP it to its bounding box. OUTPUT the cropped grid (preserving the component's color, 0 elsewhere in bbox). Net: the symmetric shape is extracted; asymmetric distractors discarded. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=28): small bank × few colors bounds outputs.
Aligned same-color solid 2x2 block pairs become filled 2-wide bars; off-axis or unpaired 2x2 blocks remain unchanged, and horizontal bars overwrite vertical bars where completed rectangles cross.
Find the unique full-height uniform nonzero divider column. Preserve the input and copy every nonzero cell strictly left of that divider to its equal-distance position on the right, preserving color.
Broadcast the source-relative motif to row-major color-6 anchors, recolored by the top-row legend.

Find each monochromatic orthogonally connected nonzero object, preserve its cells, and recolor it by exact size: size 1 to red(2), size 2 to yellow(4), size 3 to magenta(6), and every size above 3 to cyan(8).
Sparse seeds each grow into a radius-one plus of the same color.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~6-8) with: (a) 2-3 ACTIVE COLUMNS each containing EXACTLY 2 ORANGE(7) CELLS at distinct rows separated by ≥2 ZEROES between (so they're not adjacent); (b) ONE DISTRACTOR ROW with two 7s at the LEFT and RIGHT edge of an otherwise empty row. Rule (PER COLUMN, FILL BETWEEN TWO 7-CELLS WITH YELLOW 4): For EACH COLUMN c: count cells with color 7. If exactly 2 and separated by all-0 cells between: PAINT every cell strictly BETWEEN them in column c with COLOR 4 (yellow). The two 7-endpoints stay. Columns with !=2 7s or adjacent pairs (distractor row) are LEFT UNCHANGED. Net: valid column-pairs bridge with yellow; row distractors remain untouched.
Colored source shapes match gray slot silhouettes under transforms.

0-bg grid (h, w ~7-10) with up to 4 color-4 (yellow) cells marking the corners of a rectangle (rows r1, r2 with r2 ≥ r1 + 3; cols c1, c2 with c2 ≥ c1 + 3). All 4 corners are at (r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2). Sometimes an extra midpoint cell is also painted. Rule: detect the 4 rectangle corners. ROW CLOSURE: paint every cell in rows r1 and r2 between columns c1..c2 with color 4 (top and bottom rails). COL CLOSURE: paint every cell in cols c1 and c2 between rows r1..r2 with color 4 (left and right rails). Net: the 4 corners get connected into a hollow rectangle outline in color 4.
skills: from sparse corners to filled rectangle

summary: 8-markers in row 0 and col 0; output is values at marker-row × marker-col intersections.

Select the first color-2 and first color-3 cells in row-major order, grow each to its full 3x3 Chebyshev-radius-1 neighborhood, and paint their intersection color 8 on a blank canvas. Later color-2/3 cells are distractors and do not change the selected centers.

Find every 3x3 window whose eight border cells are the same nonzero color and whose center is zero; fill only that center with the border color. Generated lessons pair real rings with cornerless crosses, mixed-color borders, occupied centers, or a second true ring so the eight-cell conjunction and multiplicity are visible.

The input contains exactly one color-5 pivot and a contiguous one-sided horizontal or vertical line of one to four color-2 cells attached to it. Recolor the original 2-line to 3, then rotate its offsets 90 degrees clockwise around the pivot and paint that copy color 2; keep the pivot 5.
≥1 top-bottom-symmetric blob (kept) + ≥1 top-bottom-asymmetric blob (dropped).

A square (3*K-1)×(3*K-1) lattice of K×K 2x2 cells is separated by single-pixel divider rows/columns in a modal non-zero divider color. Uniform 2x2 marker cells use other colors. For each marker color, fill all coarse cells between same-color markers that share a coarse row or column. A color may connect on both axes, and singleton/off-line markers that share no row/column with a same-color peer stay unchanged.

Rows 0 and 1 are equal-width colored block headers. Row 0 names the source body blocks; row 1 gives a non-identity permutation of those same blocks. Drop the headers and concatenate the source body blocks in row-1 order.

Create a sparse square ARC grid and transpose it across the main diagonal. Default instances use sizes 5..8, contain four or five distinct nonzero cells, and deterministically cycle through upper-triangle, lower-triangle, two-sided, and diagonal-plus-off-diagonal layouts.  The output has the same dimensions and palette, with every input cell at (r,c) moved to (c,r).

0-bg grid (size varies). Three connected shapes in colors 1, 2 and 3, placed apart. Each shares a common CORE (anchored at the bbox origin) plus its own disjoint extra cells. Rule: normalize each color's shape and output the cells common to all three (the core) cropped in color 8. The grid size, the core shape and each color's extras all vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~13 distinct).
Use framed library shapes, selector keys, and transform codes to build a decoded gallery strip.
Gray bitmap plus repeated-color column key and separator bar; crop the bitmap bbox, use the key color on gray cells, and separator color in bbox holes.

On a 0-background grid, find the monochrome 4-connected objects and normalize each occupied-cell set by translation only. Keep every object whose exact normalized shape occurs at least twice, preserving its color and position; erase shapes that occur once. Rotation and reflection do not count as equality.

A black 20..24 by 23..26 grid contains exactly two foreground colors. One color forms 4..7 solid square macro-cells on a 3x3 lattice; its overall bounding box is therefore three equal blocks tall and wide. The other color appears as 12..55 small noise components. Divide the shape-color bounding box into its 3x3 macro-cells and output a 3x3 grid: paint a cell with the noise color exactly when the corresponding source macro-cell is occupied, otherwise paint 0.

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~8-12) with: (a) ROW MARKERS — n_row_markers (2-4) COLOR-8 cells placed at random rows r ∈ [1, h-1] in column 0 (cell (r, 0) = 8); (b) COLUMN MARKERS — n_col_markers (2-4) COLOR-8 cells placed at random columns c ∈ [1, w-1] in row 0 (cell (0, c) = 8); (c) INTERIOR — for EACH cell (r, c) with r ≥ 1 and c ≥ 1: independently fill with a random non-{0, 8} color from a 4-color palette at density 0.5. Cell (0, 0) stays bg-0. Rule (EXTRACT THE SUB-MATRIX OF MARKED ROWS AND MARKED COLUMNS): READ the ROW MARKERS — the set R of row indices r where g[r][0] = 8. READ the COLUMN MARKERS — the set C of column indices c where g[0][c] = 8. PRODUCE an OUTPUT grid of size |R| × |C| where output[i][j] = g[R[i]][C[j]] (cell at the intersection of the i-th marked row and the j-th marked column, sorted ascending). The marker cells themselves and unmarked rows/cols are dropped. Net: a tiny sub-matrix of the interior, sampled at the marker-indicated rows × columns.
Complete every separated monochrome 2x2 L-triomino by filling its one missing zero corner with the triomino's color.

On a zero-background 7..12 by 8..11 grid, 2..5 columns contain exactly two matching coloured endpoints separated by zero cells.  Fill only those inclusive vertical intervals.  A three-example schedule alternates one clean scene with two complete guard scenes containing mismatched, singleton, and three-marker columns that remain unchanged; valid-pair colours are reused so the rule must be inferred per column.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-13) with 2-4 SOLID 3×3 RINGS, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color. Each ring is an 8-cell hollow square: 3×3 bbox with the 8 perimeter cells painted in the ring's color and the CENTER cell at (r+1, c+1) initially 0. Rings are non-touching (1-cell padding from each other and grid edges). Rule: for EVERY 3×3 RING (8 cells of a single color forming a ring with a 0-cell center inside), IDENTIFY the CENTER cell (the unique 0-cell strictly inside the 3×3 bbox). FILL that center cell with the RING'S OWN color, completing the 3×3 into a SOLID monochrome 3×3 square. Net: each hollow ring becomes a solid 3×3 in its color; ring perimeters stay.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~7-10) with: (a) 2-3 ROW MARKERS on the LEFT BORDER (col 0) at distinct rows ≥1, each in a DISTINCT color; (b) 2-3 COL MARKERS on the TOP BORDER (row 0) at distinct cols ≥1, each in a DISTINCT color. Top-left (0, 0) stays 0. All marker colors are unique across row + col markers. Rule (PROJECT CROSSHAIRS): identify ROW MARKERS (left-border non-0 cells) and COL MARKERS (top-border non-0 cells). For EACH row marker at (r, 0) with color C, PAINT the entire row r with C. For EACH col marker at (0, c) with color D, PAINT the entire column c with D. At intersections (row marker and col marker meeting), task-specific tiebreak. Net: border markers shoot crosshair beams across the grid.
Large 8-rect with 2-3 small colored 2x2 blocks in distinct quadrants.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~12-16) with 2-3 CONNECTED NON-BG OBJECTS, each a DISTINCT SHAPE drawn from a 2-7-cell shape bank (sizes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) in DISTINCT COLORS, placed at non-overlapping non-touching positions (1-cell padding via bbox-overlap check). Each object has a UNIQUE cell-count so the size-sort is unambiguous. Rule (SORT OBJECTS BY SIZE DESC, PASTE BBOX CROPS SIDE-BY-SIDE): extract every 4-CONNECTED NON-0 COMPONENT. For each, compute its BBOX CROP (subgrid containing the shape, padded to bbox). SORT the crops by CELL COUNT DESCENDING (tiebreakers: top-row, left-col, color). PASTE the sorted crops HORIZONTALLY with 1-column GAP of 0 background between adjacent crops. Output is a fresh grid sized to fit the row of crops. Net: objects lined up biggest-first left-to-right with a gap between each.

An 8-12 by 9-12 zero-background grid contains one sparse blue (1) object and one separate straight distractor in another color. Find all blue cells, compute their tight bounding box, and paint every cell in that rectangle cyan (8). The blue cells are replaced; the distractor and all cells outside the blue bounding box are preserved.

A 0-background grid contains one to three separate complete blue(1) rectangular frames.  Within each frame, yellow(4) cells may occur above or below the frame-local horizontal mid-line.  Reflect every yellow cell through that frame's own mid-line and add orange(7) only when the mirror cell is empty.  Preserve blue frames and original yellow cells.
Exactly two yellow (4) markers occupy opposite corners of a rectangle; return the complete interior subgrid, preserving every color and zero.

0-bg grid of EVEN HEIGHT (2 × half_h, where half_h ∈ {3..7}) × WIDTH w ∈ {3..14}: (a) TOP HALF (rows 0..half_h-1) filled with TOP_COLOR (non-{0, 2}) via one of 6 PANEL_PATTERNS (random / blob / stripes / checker / border / diagonal) at density 0.3..0.6; (b) BOTTOM HALF (rows half_h..2 * half_h - 1) filled with BOT_COLOR (distinct from {0, 2, top_color}) using the same pattern type at independent density 0.3..0.6. NO SEPARATOR ROW between the halves. At least 1 cell-pair (r, c) has g[r][c] = 0 AND g[half_h+r][c] = 0 (enforced via _ensure_both_zero). Rule (PRODUCE AN h × w OUTPUT: BOTH-ZERO CELL PAIRS BECOME 2, ELSE 0): COMPUTE a fresh half_h × w OUTPUT grid. For EACH (r, c) with r ∈ [0, half_h-1] and c ∈ [0, w-1]: IF g[r][c] = 0 AND g[half_h+r][c] = 0 → output[r][c] = 2; ELSE output[r][c] = 0. The output is HALF the input's height. Net: a cell-wise NOR of the two stacked panels, emitted as 2s on a bg-0 half-height grid.
Square input grid; rule emits a fixed 1/0 parity-lattice mask of the same dims.

12×12 grid filled with a single non-{0,2,4} BACKGROUND color, with 1-3 small CLUSTERS of color-2 (red) cells. Each cluster: 2-3 red cells placed within Chebyshev distance ≤ 2 of one another (so they merge into a single group). Different clusters are placed apart. Rule: (1) find the most frequent non-zero value bg in the grid. (2) collect all color-2 cells. (3) cluster them greedily by Chebyshev distance ≤ 2 (cells within radius-2 in any direction merge into the same group). (4) For each group, compute the bbox over its red cells. (5) Inside each bbox, set every bg cell (NOT red, NOT 4, NOT other) to color 4. Red cells inside the bbox stay red.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-11) with: (a) EXACTLY ONE color-1 (blue) ANCHOR cell placed at the grid's central position (h//2, w//2); (b) ONE small connected BLOB of 2-4 cells in some non-{0, 1} color, placed in the upper-LEFT region of the grid so that the blob's POINT-REFLECTION across the anchor lands fully IN-BOUNDS in the lower-right region and does NOT overlap the original blob or the anchor itself. Rule: the color-1 cell at (ar, ac) is the ANCHOR. For every non-1 non-0 cell at (r, c) with color k, PAINT its POINT-REFLECTION at (2*ar - r, 2*ac - c) with color k. The original blob stays and the anchor stays color 1. Net: the small blob sprouts a same-color mirror copy rotated 180° around the blue anchor.

Read the unique row-0 marker color, select the body component of that color, and return its tight bounding-box crop. Canonical-size anchors and alternating interior-rank counterexamples make component order, size, and marker distance insufficient shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies). A connected color-2 (red) CORE. Rule: from the core centroid, draw 4 cardinal rays (8/8/4 dashed pattern past the core to the edge) and 4 diagonal rays (solid color 1, stopping at the core). The grid size, core shape/size and position vary freely (was a fixed plus cross, ~17 distinct).

Infer background, endpoint, stripe, and waypoint roles from frequency; transpose vertical stripe scenes; then draw an endpoint-colored vertical/horizontal staircase through every waypoint center in order. Easy scenes favor three crossings, medium balances three/four, and hard favors four crossings.

Zero-background grids with 1..3 separated compact active rows. Each row has a repeated nonzero majority and one different singleton; the unchanged Racket rule recolors that singleton only. Active rows range over the whole canvas, including positive even indices. Three-draw lessons include endpoint odds, noncanonical run lengths, a third active row, and shared color roles.
Two equal-bbox shapes in colors 2 and 3, isolated.
D4-equivalence matrix of four binary panel shapes, with equal-area hard negatives and reflected positives.

A 2x2 colour-2/3 template above a full colour-5 separator is tiled into two hollow frames below: frame colours 1/2/3/4 select identity, 90° CW, 180°, and transpose respectively; the output is the lower region only.

Read row headers from column 0 and column headers from row 0, discard the header row/column, and build their colored equality matrix: output[r][c] is the shared nonzero header color when the two headers are equal, else 0.
Several 4-connected non-bg colored objects of distinct sizes (no two share the same cell count). Rule recolors the smallest object to color 8, leaving every other cell unchanged.

0-bg grid with scattered color-1 and color-2 cells (and possibly other colors). Rule: for each 0-cell, check its 4 cardinal neighbors. If ≥1 neighbor is color 1 AND ≥1 neighbor is color 2, replace the 0 with color 8. Other cells (non-0, or 0 without the dual-touch condition) are preserved unchanged.
A walled two-seed maze contains at least one reachable background cell equidistant from the red and green seeds; those tie cells turn cyan.

On a zero background, find 4-connected blue (1) components. Recolor only components of size exactly one red (2); preserve every larger blue component. Some generated lessons add an isolated green singleton that must remain green, making both the blue color condition and size-one condition observable.

A 10..14 by 12..16 zero grid contains one connected color-1 template, one to three exact translated color-3 copies, and zero to two nonmatching color-3 distractors.  The template has 3..5 cells, fits a 3x3 box, and is not horizontally symmetric.  Output starts empty; every exact green copy is recolored 8 and completed with its horizontal reflection inside its own bounding box, while all nonmatches are erased.

Two disjoint, connected shapes use fixed colors red 2 and blue 1. Their inclusive bounding boxes overlap. One isolated key in color 3..9 selects the fill color. On a blank same-size canvas, fill the entire intersection rectangle, including previously empty cells. Generated lessons mix singleton/line/compact overlaps with full two-dimensional overlaps; the selected Racket rule supplies all training labels.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) START CELL; (b) ONE COLOR-3 (green) GOAL CELL ≥4 Manhattan from start; (c) 0-3 COLOR-8 (cyan) WALL cells (≥2 cells from start/goal); (d) optional COLOR-4 PORTAL PAIR (2 cells at distinct positions, probability 0.5). Rule: APPLY BFS (4-conn) from RED start to GREEN goal, avoiding CYAN walls. COLOR-4/6 PORTAL PAIRS act as teleporters — entering one portal transports to the other (zero step). FIND the SHORTEST PATH. PAINT every 0-cell along that path with COLOR 8. Start, goal, walls, and portals stay. Net: output adds an orange trail of the shortest portal-aware path.

0-bg grid (h, w ~10-14) with: (a) one CONTROL MARKER cell in some color from {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; (b) a BLUE(1) TEMPLATE shape of 4 cells in an asymmetric L/J pattern placed in the interior, not adjacent to the marker. Rule: detect ctrl color via (first available in 2, 3, 4, 6) → maps to rotations 0/1/2/3 CW. Take template cells (color 1) normalized; rotate ctrl times. Find anchor from grid (first color-7 cell or fallback). Output: a fresh empty grid with the rotated shape stamped at anchor position, painted color 8 (cyan).
Pair each isolated one-cell color anchor with that color's connected multi-cell object, then stamp the object's bounding-box-relative shape at the anchor on a blank grid.

A contiguous 2..4-color legend occupies the left of row 0. Rows below contain the same number of separated color-8 components. Rank components by area descending, breaking equal-area ties by top row then left column, and recolor rank i with legend[i]. Scheduled lessons retain examples with equal-area ties and with 8 itself as a legitimate legend color.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~11-14) with 2 SOLID RECTANGLES at hardcoded positions: (a) a 2×7 RECTANGLE at (1, 1)..(2, 7) in one non-zero color; (b) a 4×4 RECTANGLE at (4, 4)..(7, 7) in another color. NOTE: currently both fixed sizes — diversity is intrinsic-low (only color permutations). Rule: for EACH BLOB (connected component), COMPUTE: (1) boundary cell count (cells with ≥1 bg/non-blob neighbor); (2) total size; (3) color. SORT blobs by (BOUNDARY DESC, SIZE DESC, COLOR DESC). SELECT the FIRST blob (max boundary). Output: an EMPTY GRID of the same dimensions with ONLY that selected blob, RECOLORED to COLOR 8 (cyan). All other blobs and bg are cleared. Net: input has multiple rectangles; output preserves only the one with most boundary cells, painted cyan.
1-2 color-2 emitters + 1-3 mirrors (5, 6, or 7).
Stamp every non-{0,5,6} cell relative to the first 5 onto each row-major color-6 anchor.

Variable two-panel grid. A full color-9 divider separates a top template panel from an equal-sized bottom marker panel. Top panel: a TEMPLATE shape in color 2 — a small connected blob (3-5 cells) anchored at top-left. Bottom panel: 2-4 color-3 ANCHOR markers at distinct positions where the template can fit. Rule: extract template's offset cells from its top-left anchor. For each color-3 marker in the bottom panel, stamp the template (in color 8) at the marker's position. Output is the bottom panel only, filled with 8-stamps.
skills: template extraction, anchor offsets, repeated placement

summary: Exactly one blue object supplies per-row cell counts and exactly one red object supplies per-column cell counts. The output is their color-8 threshold intersection. A cyclic curriculum includes blue rows with internal gaps, refuting the canonical-fitting row-span shortcut.

Gray (5) walls partition the bordered grid into 2..4 rectangular rooms. Each seeded room contains one distinct colored seed; flood that whole room with its seed color without crossing gray walls, while unseeded rooms stay zero.
Distinct colored markers in row 0 label solid color-5 rectangles below: paint every rectangle by the uniquely nearest marker to its floored bbox midpoint.
A strip flags candidate panels that contain the template.
skills: template search inside candidates, candidate selection, symbolic strip output

summary: 0-bg grid (h ∈ 11-16, w ∈ 8-14) with 5-7 NON-ZERO COLORS at SCATTERED POSITIONS: palette drawn from one of {warm (3,4,6,9), cool (1,5,7,8), small (1..5), broad (1..9)}, expanded to ≥5 colors if needed. Counts drawn via _draw_counts using one of: default (random 22,12,6,4,2,2,2), wide_spread (30%, 15%, 7%, 4%, 2 cells), tight_spread (15% ± 5%), ascending (5%, 10%, 15%, ...). All 5+ NON-ZERO COUNTS are STRICTLY DISTINCT (no ties); bg=0 has the largest count overall. Cells placed at random free positions via random_free_cell. Rule (COUNT EACH NON-ZERO COLOR'S CELL FREQUENCY, SORT DESCENDING, OUTPUT THE 3RD, 4TH, 5TH MOST-COMMON COLORS AS A 3×1 COLUMN GRID): COUNT cells of each non-zero color. SORT colors by count DESCENDING. SELECT the 3RD, 4TH, 5TH entries (skipping the top-2). OUTPUT a 3-ROW × 1-COLUMN grid: row 0 = 3rd most-common color, row 1 = 4th, row 2 = 5th. Net: a frequency-based selection extracts the mid-tier colors and emits them as a vertical color triple.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~10-13) with 1-3 EXACT HORIZONTAL RED(2) TRIPLES (3-cell horizontal lines, all color 2) plus 1-2 OTHER red bars: length-2 horizontal (domino), length-4 horizontal, or length-3 VERTICAL — all in color 2 with 1-cell padding between them. Rule (RECOLOR CENTER OF EACH HORIZONTAL LENGTH-3 RED LINE TO BLUE): find every connected RED(2) COMPONENT. For EACH one that is EXACTLY a HORIZONTAL 3-cell LINE (3 cells in the same row, consecutive columns): identify its CENTER cell (middle of the 3). RECOLOR the center from 2 to BLUE (1). Endpoints stay red. Vertical and longer/shorter red bars are LEFT UNCHANGED. Net: each horizontal red triple gets a blue dot in its middle; all other red bars stay solid red.

A tile (row period 4-8, col period 5-10) is repeated 2-3× along each axis starting at row offset 0-2. Some cells are noised. Rule infers the best tile via periodic majority vote and outputs the clean tiled grid (noise cells replaced by majority for their residue position).

On a color-7 grid, distinct colored left/right walls attract every 8-connected object of their own color. Objects slide horizontally as rigid bodies, closest-to-wall first, and stop against the wall or an already-settled object.
Find the connected color-2 template.  At every isolated marker, stamp a color-8 copy on a blank same-size grid: 3 keeps the template, 4 mirrors left-right, 5 mirrors up-down, and 6 rotates clockwise.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-11, w ∈ 9-12) with: (a) ONE CORNER KEY at FIXED position (0, 0) — value ∈ {1..7} selecting a transform (per demos: 1=identity, 2=cw90, 3=180, 4=ccw90, 5=flip-LR, 6=flip-UD, 7=transpose); (b) ONE LARGE NON-CORNER BLOB — an irregular 4-5 cell blob in palette[0] (a non-key color drawn from {1..9}\{key}) built by grow_blob random walk, placed away from (0, 0); (c) ONE SMALLER DECOY BLOB — a 2-cell blob in palette[1] (distinct from key + primary), placed to add visual noise but smaller than the primary. Rule (READ THE CORNER KEY, FIND THE LARGEST NON-CORNER BLOB, TRANSFORM IT BY THE KEY, CROP, OUTPUT): READ key from (0, 0) → select transform. EXTRACT every non-bg blob excluding the key cell. FIND the LARGEST blob (by cell count). CROP it to its bbox. APPLY the key's transform (identity / cw / 180 / ccw / flip_lr / flip_ud / transpose). OUTPUT the transformed crop. Net: the corner key picks one of 7 dihedral operations to apply to the cropped largest blob; smaller blobs are discarded.

A 10x(10..13) zero-background grid with 3..5 separated coloured polyominoes totalling 12 cells.  Scheduled examples require, in turn, translation-only packing, rotation, and reflection with repeated colours.

A 0-background grid contains exactly two separated 4-connected blobs in distinct nonzero colors. Sort the objects left-to-right and exchange their colors while preserving every occupied cell. Shapes may match or differ; both relative color orders are generated.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~7-9) with exactly 3 SINGLE-CELL SEEDS in distinct colors at fixed asymmetric anchor positions: (1, 1), (1, w-2), (h-2, 3). Rule: extract seeds (all non-bg cells). For each cell of the output grid: if input is non-bg, keep that value. Else compute Manhattan distance to each seed, sort ascending; if the MIN distance is unique → take that seed's color; else (tie at the minimum) → 0. Net effect: nearest-seed Voronoi tessellation with ties left as bg.

A 0-background 8..14 by 8..14 grid contains 2..4 colors, each appearing exactly twice as the endpoints of a non-trivial 45-degree diagonal. For every color, paint the inclusive diagonal span between its endpoints. Spans may be disjoint, cross at blank interior cells, or pass through an endpoint of another color. Colors are painted in ascending numeric order, so the larger color owns every overlap. Every four consecutive samples cover all four collision profiles.
Yellow L-triominoes recolor green while straight yellow bars remain.
Mark solid-square exterior sides or non-solid-square axial corners with 2 on background 7.

A zero-background grid contains one to three target colors with exactly four cells. Most targets mark the four corners of a rectangle; scheduled count witnesses replace one corner by another cell inside the same box. Optional distractors have three or five cells. Fill the bounding box of every EXACTLY-four color on a fresh zero canvas and erase all others.
Shear every nonzero cell left by bottommost_row minus its row, preserving colors and canvas size.
4 green corner markers + a red shape; rule centers the shape inside marker-rect.

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~9-14) with 1-3 ONE-CELL-THICK RECTANGULAR FRAMES (border outlines) in DISTINCT colors from {1..9}. Each FRAME has height 3-5 and width 3-6, with a non-empty INTERIOR (at least 1 bg cell inside the border). Frames are placed at non-touching positions (1-cell padding). Rule (FILL EACH HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME INTO A SOLID RECTANGLE): For EACH CONNECTED COMPONENT that is a HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME of color C with bbox (r0, c0, r1, c1): PAINT every cell at rows r0..r1, cols c0..c1 (the entire rectangle including border and interior) with color C. Net: each hollow rectangle becomes a solid rect of the same color.

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~9-14) with: (a) ONE GREEN(3) SEED at (start_r, 1) on the LEFT EDGE INTERIOR (start_r ∈ [2, h-3]); (b) 0-2 STEERING DOTS placed at fixed positions in column w-3 — first DOT in COLOR 8 at (r, w-3), second DOT in COLOR 4 at (r-1, w-3), third DOT in COLOR 6 at (r+1, w-3) (turn_dots controls how many of these appear). Rule (GREEN SEED WALKS RIGHTWARD, TURNING AT STEERING DOTS, PAINT PATH GREEN): the green seed at (start_r, 1) marches RIGHTWARD across empty cells, painting each traversed cell COLOR 3. When the path reaches a STEERING DOT cell, the dot's color encodes a TURN: COLOR 8 = turn left or continue, COLOR 4 = turn up, COLOR 6 = turn down (per puzzle convention). Continue until grid edge. Net: a green trail snakes from the left seed via steering dots toward the right side.

A connected red (2) polyomino lies wholly to one side of a hollow cyan (8) rectangular frame. Translate the red shape rigidly toward the frame until the next step would touch it. Every five-sample teaching window contains right, left, down, and two up examples.

0-bg grid (size varies). Color-8 columns in the top region and color-2 segments in a 2-row. Rule: the 8-columns drop from the bar-row down; around each 2-segment, walls/bars form where the segment's edge 8-columns align, and 8-columns through the segment are blocked. The grid size, 8-column positions, 2-row and segments vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).
Each color appears as one horizontal or vertical endpoint pair whose span is filled.

Place three identical translated copies of one 3..5-cell 4-connected shape, in one color, at the top-left, top-right, and bottom-left corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Complete the empty bottom-right corner with a fourth copy in the same orientation and color.
Fill only zero cells whose immediate vertical neighbours are equal and nonzero; nearby horizontal, mismatched, longer-gap, and filled motifs are negative evidence.
Repeat a color-7 glyph across the top lattice row, recoloring every third column of copies to 6 and extending those columns downward.
BFS-fill reachable zero cells around a singleton marker with alternating marker colors; wall 8 blocks traversal.
Corners of hollow GREEN (colour-3) rectangle frames are recolored yellow. Frame count, sizes and positions scale with difficulty; frame colour is fixed green because the rule keys on colour 3.

Blue(1) markers on the top border select columns and red(2) markers on the left border select rows; paint their Cartesian-product intersections green(3), while ignoring role-swapped border distractors.

A black 7..14 by 7..14 grid has 1..3 maroon (9) selector cells in row 0, a blank separator row, and one 4-connected monochrome polyomino of 4..8 cells below it. Count the 9s, erase them, crop the polyomino, then apply 1=rotate clockwise, 2=rotate 180 degrees, 3=transpose. Object shape, position, size, selector positions, canvas dimensions, and color family vary independently; every selected transform changes the crop.

A 0-background grid contains one connected irregular shape in one nonzero color and a unique bottom-left marker in another nonzero color. Erase the marker and recolor every shape cell in place to the marker color. Default generation alternates exact canonical D4 morphologies with fresh connected irregular shapes, varying dimensions, size, placement, and both colors.

Grid (h, w~24-30) with a TRANSLATIONAL PERIODIC PATTERN of period (pr, pc) where pr, pc ∈ 2..4, painted from a tile (pr × pc) using one of 6 PATTERNS (rotated/stripe_h/stripe_v/checker/diagonal/block) over a 2-4 color palette drawn from 1..9. The repeating tile fills the entire grid. Then 2-6 RANDOM CELLS are punched as HOLES (set to bg = 0). Rule (PERIOD DETECTION + HOLE FILL): detect the translational period (pr, pc) of the non-bg cells. For EACH BG (0) CELL at (r, c), LOOK UP the periodic value at (r mod pr, c mod pc) of the underlying tile. PAINT the hole with that color. Original non-bg cells stay. Net: every bg hole gets filled by extending the detected periodic tiling.

Move the presence of color 1 to the bottom of each affected column: erase every 1 above the bottom row, set the bottom cell to 1 whenever that input column contained a 1, and preserve every non-1 cell. Lessons alternate a canonical 5-supported scaffold with a counterexample that uses repeated 1s, a non-5 destination, a different source row, and no direct 5 support.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~9-11) with: (a) ONE FULL-HEIGHT color-5 (gray) VERTICAL AXIS at some column axis_col (chosen so reflection fits in bounds); (b) 3-5 scattered non-{0, 5} colored MARK CELLS, ~70% on the LEFT side of the axis and ~30% on the right, each placed only where its mirror cell is currently empty. Rule: for each non-zero non-5 cell at (r, c), compute mirror column mc = 2*axis_col - c. If (r, mc) is in bounds AND currently 0, PAINT (r, mc) with the same color as (r, c). The gray axis stays 5; original marks stay. Net: the gray vertical line acts as a mirror, completing the reflection of all non-axis colored cells across it.

An orange 7..12 by (2n+1) grid contains 3..5 distinct-colored, one-cell-wide bars in alternating columns, all bottom-aligned. Heights may repeat but are not all equal. Rotate colors right and heights left.
Find paired vertical guides, orient a separately bounded crop by side-color score, and insert it between the preserved guide walls.
Green T-tetrominoes, in any rotation, are recolored magenta.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~14-16) with EXACTLY 3 distinct-colour shapes at horizontal slots (1,1),(1,6),(1,11), each a VARIED connected polyomino (3-4 cells, bbox <=3 wide, always containing its (0,0) corner so the normalized sets share >=1 cell). Rule: normalize each shape's cells to (0,0); over the union bbox, colour each cell by overlap count: 2 shapes share -> 2, 3 shapes share -> 8, else 0. Varied shapes -> varied overlap-count map.
A binary minimal-period field has one square boundary hole; recover the periodic values inside the hole's bounding box.

First-9 anchored bbox-angle gallery with literal color-dependent padding. Four-demo lessons alternate a combined contrast scene and varied objects; repeated colors, multiple 9s and intentional padded-crop intrusion are supported.

Every red cell on the bottom row starts an independent walker. A walker moves upward while the cell above is not gray. When gray blocks the cell above, it moves one cell right if that cell is in bounds and not gray, then again prefers upward. It stops at the top or when both options are blocked, and every visited cell becomes red.

FIXED 12×13 grid with: (a) LINE ROW at row ∈ {5, 6, 7}: a BROKEN HORIZONTAL RUN of LINE-COLOR painted at cols {2, 3, 8, 9} — two run segments (cols 2-3 and cols 8-9) with a GAP of 0s in cols 4-7 between them; (b) ANCHOR COLUMN: an anchor color is placed at TWO ROWS — UPPER ANCHOR at row ∈ {2, 3}, LOWER ANCHOR at row ∈ {8, 9}, both at ANCHOR_COL ∈ {10, 11}. Rule (COMPLETE BROKEN RUNS AND EXTEND COLORED COLUMNS UPWARD): (i) IDENTIFY the broken horizontal line: FILL the GAP (cols 4-7 of LINE_ROW) with the LINE-COLOR to complete the run; (ii) for the GAP COLUMNS just filled AND the ANCHOR COLUMN: EXTEND the line-color UPWARD from the line row toward each anchor (paint cells above the line row up to the anchor row in that column). Net: broken line completes and vertical bars project upward to anchor points.

Find the four differently coloured 3-cell L-trominoes. Normalize each to a 2x2 box and copy it into a 4x4 output: missing SE -> top-left, missing SW -> top-right, missing NE -> bottom-left, and missing NW -> bottom-right. Source position and colour magnitude do not affect the map.
The unique most frequent compact color component is kept and all others are cleared.
Color-3 components. Rule recolors to cyan(8) those whose bbox touches EXACTLY ONE grid edge; interior (0 edges) and corner/spanning (≥2 edges) components stay green.

Exactly two distinct non-{0,5} singleton emitters cast their own colors along all four diagonals through original-background cells. Rays stop before the edge, a straight gray-5 wall, or the other emitter; gray walls do not emit. Generated scenes avoid ray/ray overlap because canonical examples do not identify an overlap-priority convention.

Find every same-colour 4-connected nonzero object, crop each object to its bounding box, sort the crops by occupied-cell count ascending, and pack them left-to-right with one zero column between crops while vertically centring each crop in the tallest crop's height.
3-5 isolated non-rectangular components; rule draws each component's same-color bounding-box frame.
Blue (1) components touching exactly one border are recolored red (2); others stay. Varied object count/sizes/positions span all touch counts; color-4 decoys are present but ignored.

Gray (5) walls partition the bordered board into chambers; the chamber with strictly the most red (2) seeds is filled cyan (8). Wall layout, chamber count, the winning chamber, and seed counts/positions all vary.

A 6..14 by 7..16 zero-background grid contains one or two separated, distinct-colour filled rectangles. At least one rectangle has height and width at least 3, so the rule visibly erases an interior. Some scheduled examples also contain a 2-cell-thick rectangle. On a blank output canvas, replace every non-zero same-colour object by the perimeter of its tight bounding box in the same colour.
Solid components reduce to their deepest onion-layer cells.
skills: inner-core detection, per-component maxima, same-size masking

summary: 0-bg grid: a lattice of equal-size TILES separated by color-9 full dividers (rows/cols). Each tile is a random color-2 pattern. Rule: OR-overlay all tiles -> a tile-sized output that is 8 where any tile has a nonzero cell, else 0. Colors are {0,2,9} (output adds 8).
A zero-background grid contains 3-6 vertical same-colour runs.  Keep only the top cell of every maximal run; a touching colour change begins a new run.
Preserve every nonzero seed. In each column, fill every zero below the topmost seed with that seed's color; cells above the first seed remain zero.

For each isolated dot, use color identity to select its solid rectangle. When the dot lies beyond one side while remaining inside that side's row or column span, erase the dot center, paint its four cardinal petals, continue a stem toward the rectangle, and place a perpendicular 3-cell cap immediately outside the rectangle. Preserve all other cells and the input dimensions.

A 10..18 by 10..18 zero-background grid has one red(2) source on exactly one non-corner edge. Its edge determines inward gravity. There are 2..5 cyan(8) wall lines perpendicular to gravity, each at least two cells from the flow-axis ends and separated by at least one open row/column. Every wall spans the cross-axis except for 1..3 holes. Ordinary draws use at least three walls and include both shifted and aligned holes. The output is the directed waterfall: move inward, spread sideways in both directions when blocked, fall through every reachable hole, and recolor every visited empty cell to 2.
Find every solid same-color rectangle of at least 4x4 in a dense five-color field and recolor the rectangle cells yellow.

0-bg grid with N SINGLE-CELL MARKERS in N DISTINCT non-zero colors (N varies 2..7) at distinct positions and VARIED pairwise distances. Rule: grow each color's cell(s) by a 3x3 neighborhood and output the N x N overlap matrix (diagonal 5; 8 if two colors' grown regions overlap, else 0). Marker spacing controls which pairs overlap.

Two or three side-by-side hollow color-9 frames each contain one to three same-color 4-connected components with distinct sizes.  A 2/3 key above each frame selects its smallest/largest component; a 3/4/5/6 key on the left applies identity/clockwise/left-right/180-degree transformation.  Crop each selected component and horizontally pack the transformed pieces in frame order with one blank column and vertical centering.
1-2 hollow 8-frames; each frame's interior is tiled from a 2×2 sample two rows above its top-left.

On a cyan(8) background, four differently colored 8-connected objects each have one unique cell nearest the grid center. The unique largest object is the target. Keep its nearest cell, erase the nearest cell of each smaller object, and add a three-cell bar outside the target on the side opposite its center-facing tip.

FIXED 11×11 0-bg grid with 1-5 SCATTERED COLOR-5 ANCHORS placed by one of 5 ANCHOR LAYOUTS (random with ≥3-cell margin, row at fixed cols [2,5,8], column at fixed rows [2,5,8], corners [(2,2),(2,8),(8,2),(8,8)], center_plus [(5,5),(2,5),(5,2),(5,8),(8,5)]). EACH ANCHOR carries a LOCAL FRAGMENT — a subset of the 8 cells immediately surrounding it (offsets ring_only / full_3x3 / partial), where each fragment cell is painted with a color from a small non-{0, 5} palette (2-4 distinct colors), with fragment_density controlling how many of the 8 ring cells are filled. Anchors are spatially separated so fragments don't overlap. Rule (assemble-at + set-cell): GATHER each anchor's local 3×3 fragment (the anchor + its 8 neighbors) and MERGE these fragments cell-by-cell into ONE OUTPUT 3×3 TILE — overlaying each fragment around its anchor center, with later anchors overwriting earlier where they collide (or non-bg wins). After assembly, WRITE COLOR 5 at cell (1, 1) of the output tile (the center). OUTPUT is the 3×3 tile (much smaller than the 11×11 input). Net: scattered anchor fragments are gathered into a single small composite tile with a central 5 marker.
Selector at (0,0); rule keeps only that color (excluding (0,0)) and crops.

For each nonzero color independently, use every cell of that color to find its axis-aligned bounding box, clear the canvas, and paint the four bounding-box corners in that color. Normal lessons cycle through diagonal endpoint pairs, edge distractors, interior distractors, and distributed extrema with no input corner pair.
3x3 gray pattern (random subset of 2-5 active cells) expands into a 15x15 self-similar block grid (output dims and color-5 palette are fixed by the rule).
Find the only filled 3x3 block containing exactly three distinct colors; the other three filled 3x3 blocks contain exactly two colors. Return the three-color block unchanged.
Top-row 1-markers + left-col 2-markers (with empty (0,0) corner).

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with: (a) OUTER RECT FRAME at (1, 1)..(h-2, w-2) in COLOR A (from palette); (b) INNER RECT FRAME at (3, 3)..(h-4, w-4) inside, in COLOR B (different); (c) ≥1 COLOR-1 DOT inside the INNER frame's interior, ≥1 BETWEEN the inner and outer frames. Rule (RECOLOR 1-DOTS BY DEEPEST ENCLOSING FRAME): for EACH COLOR-1 DOT at (r, c), find the SMALLEST (deepest-nested) RECT-FRAME that STRICTLY ENCLOSES the dot. RECOLOR the dot to that frame's COLOR. If no frame encloses (dot outside outer), the dot STAYS color 1. Net: 1-dots get repainted by the deepest enclosing frame's color.
Recolor each 4-connected color-6 component by size, distinguishing straight and bent size-3 components.
Shift every non-7/non-8 connected component upward by its total cell count while preserving the cyan floor and cell colors.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-18) with: (a) EXACTLY 4 COLOR-5 (gray) MARKERS at the CORNERS of a RECTANGLE (r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2) with r2-r1 ≥ 4, c2-c1 ≥ 4 in one of 5 RECT_SIZE kinds (small/medium/large/wide/tall) and 3 POSITION BIASES (spread/center/edge); (b) EXACTLY 1 NON-5 NONZERO CELL at rectangle CENTER ((r1+r2)//2, (c1+c2)//2) in a DRAW_COLOR from {1..9}\{5}. Rule (PAINT INSET RECTANGLE OUTLINE WITH DRAW COLOR): identify the 4 GRAY MARKERS (rectangle corners) and the NON-5 DRAW COLOR. PAINT the INSET RECTANGLE OUTLINE — rows r1+1, r2-1 and cols c1+1, c2-1 — in the DRAW COLOR. The 4 gray markers stay. The center draw-color cell may be kept or absorbed. Net: 4 gray corners outline a rect; rule draws a hollow inset rect inside in the marker color.

Two to four active columns contain colored seeds.  At least one column contains a stack of two or three seeds with a different lower color.  The first nonzero seed in each column paints that entire column; empty columns remain zero.

On a 0-background grid, blue(1) rectangular frames contain colored seed cells. For each 4-connected blue object, take its bounding box, choose the last non-{0,1} seed in row-major order from that box's interior, and fill the entire bounding-box interior with that color. Disconnected frames act independently; touching frames merge, so internal blue frame segments and earlier seeds can be overwritten.

Count the colour-1 cells in the top row to obtain K. Erase those marker cells, crop the unique connected one-colour object below the blank separator row to its tight bounding box, and enlarge that crop by factor K in both dimensions; each source cell becomes a K by K block.

A wide 2..10 by 14..30 grid contains a unique maximum-area solid zero rectangle of height at least two. Recolor exactly that rectangle with 6. Other zeros are distractors. Scheduled examples include an interior target, an edge target, a wider-but-smaller rectangle, a taller-but-smaller rectangle, and both two- and three-color input palettes.

Small (n_rows+1) × (n_cols+1) key grid (normal n_rows/n_cols vary from 2 to 6; easy keeps 2-3). Row 0 (cols 1..N) holds N COL-KEYS — values in {2, 3, 4} encoding motif ids. Col 0 (rows 1..M) holds M ROW-KEYS — values in {1, 2, 3, 4} encoding transform codes. The (0, 0) cell and the interior cells are 0. Rule: output is 3M × 3N. For each (i, j) tile (i = row-key index, j = col-key index), fetch the 3×3 MOTIF identified by col-key value, apply transform indicated by row-key value (e.g., 1=identity, 2=rot-CW, 3=rot-180, 4=rot-CCW), and place it in tile slot (i, j). Net: a 3M × 3N tile-mosaic of transformed motifs.
Sparse isolated markers in 2-5 colors; every color occurs 1-3 times. The reference rule emits the ascending color multiset as one row.
Erase one connected nested shape, then use its unique least-frequent color to mark one cell beyond each occupied row and column extent.

A floor plan of rooms separated by colour-1 walls, with colour-7 doors between some adjacent rooms; the rule outputs the n x n room adjacency matrix (8 where two rooms share a door). Room-grid shape, room sizes and the door set vary.
skills: symbolic graph output, room ordering, graph encoding

summary: An 11..13 by 11..13 zero-background grid contains two or three separated, distinct-color, 4-connected objects.  Objects have 6..11 cells in 3..5-cell local bboxes and every object is asymmetric under left-right reflection.  For each object independently, keep its original cells and add their horizontal reflections inside that object's own tight bounding box.

0-bg grid (size varies) with several 3x3 ICONS (uniform border color, contrasting 1-cell center) at separated positions, plus singleton DOTS. The MOST FREQUENT dot color is placed adjacent to exactly one (answer) icon; other dot colors are fewer. Rule: find the icon adjacent to the majority dot color and output its 3x3 signature (border around center).

Fixed 10×11 grid with: (a) ROW 0 cols 0-2 hold 3 DISTINCT PALETTE COLORS (rest 0); (b) ROWS 1-2 cols 0-1 hold 4 SELECTOR cells (values 1..3 referencing bank keys); (c) ROWS 3-4 cols 0-1 hold 4 TRANSFORM COMMAND codes (0..5); (d) ROW 6 cols 0, 4, 8 hold 3 BANK KEYS (values 1, 2, 3); (e) ROWS 7-9 cols kcol..kcol+2 hold three 3×3 TEMPLATES anchored at each bank key column with ~50% sparsity. Rest is 0. Rule (PALETTE-LIFT MATRIX WITH TRANSFORMS): for EACH of 4 SELECTOR positions, look up the bank template by the selector's key, APPLY the transform indexed by the matching command, RECOLOR using the row-0 palette, and assemble all four results into a 6×6 2×2 MOSAIC. Output: 6×6 mosaic of 4 transformed 3×3 palette-lifted templates. Net: matrix-of-templates addressed by selector × command → 2×2 mosaic with palette-colored cells.

Read hollow 3x3 rings on a four-cell lattice; identify cyan as the seven-slice main picture and the other colors as two aligned small pictures; then compress per-slice ring counts into colored stacks, with cyan on the side indicated by its position relative to the small pictures.
Five separated motifs: two dihedral-equivalent pairs and one unmatched shape; the rule returns the unmatched shape's cropped boundary.

On a zero background, place exactly two disjoint 3x3 C-frames. Each frame has seven color-2 cells around a color-5 center and one cardinal opening. Extend each opening one cell outward. The oracle paints color 4 through the lawful portion of the rectangle bounded by those two exit cells, excluding both 3x3 frame boxes and the half-strips behind either opening; it also paints the two opening cells color 4. The two openings may be parallel, perpendicular, facing, or pointing away.

Crop the input to the tight bounding rectangle containing every nonzero cell. Preserve all colours, component spacing, and interior background cells exactly. Ordinary scenes place two to four disconnected, multicolour components inside a visible zero margin, so the output is a strictly smaller sparse rectangle and cannot be explained by identity, largest-object-only, solid-bbox, or monochrome-crop shortcuts.
Count color-8 seeds inside each non-8 rectangular frame, preserve all eligible borders, and fill every frame tied for the maximum count.

Count nonzero colors; the unique mode 1/2/3 selects the unchanged gray plus/T/right-L glyph. Each three-input block has independently shuffled classes and profiles: a 5x5 anchor, early decoy, and late decoy. Five consecutive default demonstrations contain all three classes and refute scan/extremum/frequency/endpoint and spatial-object shortcuts. One independently selected contrast separates global color count from 4/8-connected component size and color bounding-box area.

Dense 24-30 square-ish field with many isolated/background texture cells and exactly one unique-color rectangular outline.  The frame color occurs only on the border, so the canonical rule can identify its bbox and crop the enclosed patch.
Rebuild a blank grid, filling only columns containing exactly one nonzero cell in that cell's color.
Mark the union of all shortest start-to-goal paths through zero cells while preserving markers and gray walls.

0-bg grid with several monochrome 4-connected motifs in colours from {2,3,4,5} (the rule's candidate set). N-1 motifs share one shape; exactly ONE motif has a different shape (the odd one out). Rule: of the {2,3,4,5} objects, take the canonical dihedral shape signature of each and CROP the object whose signature is least common (the odd one out), recoloured 8. Motif shapes, count, colours and positions vary.

Row 0 holds k color-1 markers (the count). The grid contains several color-7 4-connected objects, each with a DIFFERENT number of enclosed holes. Rule selects the 7-object whose hole count equals k, then outputs that object's tight bounding-box crop (holes appear as interior 0s).
A nonzero multi-color pattern (varied bbox) on a zero background is cropped to its tight bounding box.

Grid with color-5 walls scattered as singletons or short segments. Within each column, segments between consecutive walls (or wall and grid edge) hold scattered non-zero non-5 colored cells. Rule: for each column, scan top-down. Walls (5) preserved in place. Within each segment between walls, collect all non-zero non-5 values in top-to-bottom order and pack them at the BOTTOM of the segment, with 0 padding above. Equivalent to per-column gravity-down within wall-bounded segments.

A black 9..16 by 10..16 grid contains three or four separated purple (6) 4-connected components with distinct areas, plus one gray (5) domino distractor. Rank the purple components by area, take the second-largest, crop it to its bounding box, and repaint its shape red (2) on black. The selected component's size, shape, position, edge contact, number of competing components, canvas size, and distractor orientation vary; every normal lesson has both a larger and a smaller purple component so second-largest never aliases largest or smallest.

Background 6. Each non-6 color has one solid 3x3 corner block. Scattered same-color cells slide toward their own block: row-band cells horizontally, column-band cells vertically, and all others diagonally, stopping adjacent to the block.
Extend the green segment until blocked, turn orthogonally toward the red segment, and restore the red target.
Keep colors whose total cell count is even.

Generate sparse 6..10 by 7..10 grids containing 5..10 colored cells in 2..4 columns.  Downward gravity packs each column against the bottom while preserving its top-to-bottom color order.  Half of the ordinary curriculum follows exact canonical shape/palette/count profiles; the other half supplies deep, repeated-color, floor-supported, and joint scope-boundary examples. Every five-demo window refutes the declared semantic and canonical-fitting competitors.

0-bg grid (size varies) with blue (color-1) objects: M common shapes (each >=2 copies) plus exactly one UNIQUE shape. Rule: find the unique shape, scale it 2x, output in color 8. The grid size, unique shape, common shapes/counts and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~21 distinct).

A zero-background grid contains two to four concentric rectangular outlines in one placeholder color above an ordered, distinct non-zero palette on the bottom row.  The palette may carry one unused tail color after the entries needed by the frames.  Successive outlines are inset by two cells on every side.  Crop the outline bounding box, then recolor the outermost outline with the first palette color, the next outline with the second, and so on inward; the palette row is not copied to the output.

Find the unique full horizontal color-8 axis row. For every nonzero, non-8 source cell on either side, preserve it and copy the same color to the equal-distance row on the opposite side in the same column.

0-bg grid with color-2 and color-3 hollow rectangular FRAMES, plus two non-frame PIECES in rule-ignored colors {6,7}: one SOLID (0 holes) and one RING (1 enclosed hole). Rule: each color-2 frame takes the 0-hole piece, each color-3 frame the 1-hole piece; the piece is recolored to the frame color and centered in its interior. Output = frames with their centered pieces on a blank grid.

skills: source-target transfer, tile selection, motif copying
summary: A regular lattice of 3x3 tiles separated by 9. Select the unique tile with the most red (2) cells, then REPLACE the distinct tile containing one green (3) marker with the source's red mask in cyan (8), zero elsewhere. Other tiles stay unchanged. Includes denser non-source tiles, weaker red candidates, non-red source clutter, target clutter and off-center markers.

A color-1 guide and exactly three colored candidates. Sort candidates by bbox reading order, choose the first candidate dihedrally equivalent to the guide, transform it into the guide's orientation, and output its tight crop in the candidate's color. One or two candidates may match; when two match, reading order decides.

COLOR-8 (cyan) bg grid (h~6-12, w~11-18) with a SINGLE non-8 COLOR C at 'count' scattered cells (count ≥ 2, ≤ w). Cell placement uses one of 8 LAYOUTS (scattered/blob/diagonal/row/col/checker/frame/corners) with position_bias (spread/center/edge). Rule (CENTER 'count'-LENGTH HORIZONTAL BAR ON BG=8): identify the SINGLE NON-8 COLOR C and COUNT = total cells of C. EMIT a FRESH h×w GRID filled with 8. PAINT a HORIZONTAL BAR of LENGTH 'count' in color C CENTERED at the MIDDLE ROW (h//2), starting at col (w - count)//2. Net: scattered count of C cells reduces to a centered horizontal bar of length count in color C.

0-bg square grid (size~8-15) with COLOR-5 (gray) WALLS forming a chamber lattice: 1-3 FULL HORIZONTAL wall rows and 1-3 FULL VERTICAL wall columns (with ≥2-row/col separation), splitting the grid into N CHAMBERS. Most chambers have EXACTLY ONE KEY cell in a DISTINCT non-wall color. Some chambers may be EMPTY (0 keys) or have 2 keys (ambiguous). Rule (FILL CHAMBERS WITH EXACTLY ONE KEY USING THAT KEY's COLOR): For EACH CHAMBER (4-conn non-5 region bounded by 5-walls): if it contains EXACTLY ONE non-wall non-0 KEY cell with color C, FILL all 0-cells in the chamber with C. 0-key and 2-key chambers stay. Walls and keys stay. Net: single-keyed chambers flood with their key's color.

Rows 0-2 hold 3..5 separated 3x3 prototype panels. Row 3 is blank. Row 4 holds exactly three triples at columns 0, 4, and 8. Each triple selects a prototype by 1-based index, applies code 1=identity, 2=rotate clockwise, 3=flip left-right, or 4=flip up-down, then recolors every nonzero cell to the triple's output color. The three results are packed at columns 0, 4, and 8 of a 3x11 output.

Zero-background grids containing distinct-color, axis-aligned (C,0,C) triples, separated by at least one zero cell in all directions. The unchanged rule fills each zero middle with C. Defaults mix canonical-scale scenes and difficulty-scaled scenes; overrides support dimensions 5..14 and 1..8 exact motifs subject to declared packing feasibility.

0-background grid inside a color-5 boundary frame, with exactly one interior single-cell seed whose color is not 0, 5, or 8.  Optional interior color-5 walls are sparse and never adjacent to the seed.  The canonical rule measures shortest-path distance from the seed through 0-cells, blocked by 5-walls: even distances take the seed color, odd distances take cyan 8, while walls and the seed stay fixed.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~6-9) with several ACTIVE COLUMNS (2 to w-2) containing 1-h//2 cells in some non-bg color (each active column may have its own color). Other columns are entirely 0. Rule: drop every ALL-ZERO column. PACK the remaining (active) columns to the LEFT in their original left-to-right order. Output: h × N_active grid containing just the active columns, no gaps.

0-bg grid (size varies) with: (a) one QUERY object in color 8 (a random connected polyomino S); (b) one MATCH object in a non-8 color with the IDENTICAL shape S (same per-row column-offset signature); (c) 1-3 DISTRACTOR objects in other colors whose signatures DIFFER from S. All objects are 8-gap isolated. Rule: take the query's row signature, find the first non-8 object with the same signature, and crop to its bbox. Output = that crop (the match shape in its color). Output dims = bbox(S).
A unique full-height color-5 guide separates reflection orbits. Copy each one-sided colored cell to its empty mirror target; preserve occupied mirror partners instead of overwriting them.

0-bg grid with a color-5 LATTICE (outer border + internal dividers) splitting it into rectangular CELLS. Each cell holds color-2 MARKER dots at varied positions. Rule: within each cell, fill the rook-closure (bounding box) of the markers with color 8, preserving the 5-lattice. Only colors {0,2,5} appear in the input.

Count blue(1) cells to choose 0/90/180/270 degrees clockwise, then count red(2) cells to choose no horizontal reflection/reflection. Normalize the magenta(6) template after each transform and stamp it in cyan(8) at the orange(7) anchor, preserving the rest of the input.

Each row of the input has some smallest period p (1 ≤ p ≤ w) such that g[r][c] = g[r][c mod p] for all c. Rule outputs h × 2w grid where output[r][c] = g[r][c mod p_r]. Per row, p_r may differ; rows that are uniform have p=1; rows whose period is exactly w are emitted as their full content repeated.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~6-10 by ~8-12) with 2-4 EXACT horizontal length-3 BARS of color 8 (cyan) in distinct rows, each with at least 1 cell of bg on both sides (so extension has room). Plus 1-2 DISTRACTOR color-8 shapes (vertical bars, singletons, or longer bars) that are NOT exact horizontal length-3 bars. Rule: for each connected color-8 component, check if it's an exact horizontal length-3 bar (3 cells, all same row, cols form contiguous span of 3). If yes, extend by painting cell to the left of leftmost and cell to the right of rightmost (if in-bounds and bg). If no, leave unchanged.

One bottom-row red seed grows a two-cell-wide up-right staircase. Blue blockers in either prospective path cell shift that row to the first free column on their right and create a horizontal red bridge; off-path blue cells are preserved and do not affect the path.
Find each hollow gray frame, read its single colored side seed at the vertical midpoint, and fill that frame's interior with the seed color.
For each nonzero color independently, infer the axis-aligned rectangle whose three marked corners are present, then paint that rectangle's full one-cell-thick border in the same color.

Exactly one isolated key cell selects a transform: 1=rotate clockwise, 2=rotate 180, 3=flip left/right, 4=transpose. Remove the key, tightly crop all remaining non-zero cells as one possibly multicolor and disconnected composite shape, then transform that cropped canvas.
Return 1 for a binary grid with left-right reflection symmetry and 7 otherwise; generated lessons separate that rule from top-bottom, rotational, count-only, fixed-label, and color-echo shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-8, w ∈ 7-9) with: (a) ONE CORNER MARKER at FIXED position (0, 0) — value ∈ {1, 2} (1 = horizontal mirror to right; 2 = vertical mirror to bottom); (b) ONE CONNECTED MOTIF in a non-{0, 1, 2} color drawn from {3,4,5,6,7,8,9} — 3-5 cells built by _build_motif random walk, placed in the UPPER-LEFT QUADRANT (rows 1..h//2-1, cols 1..w//2-1) with no overlap. Rule (READ THE (0,0) MARKER, MIRROR THE MOTIF TO THE OPPOSITE HALF; ORIGINAL MOTIF PRESERVED): READ the (0, 0) marker value. IF MARKER = 1 (HORIZONTAL): for EACH motif cell at (r, c) PAINT g[r][w-1-c] with the same color (mirror LEFT→RIGHT across the central column). IF MARKER = 2 (VERTICAL): PAINT g[h-1-r][c] (mirror TOP→BOTTOM across the central row). Original motif cells and (0, 0) marker stay untouched. Net: a corner code drives either an LR or UD reflection of the motif into the opposite half of the grid.

Row 0 contains K colour-1 markers; one colour-9 anchor centres a 2..8 shape. The authority returns the union of the first K clockwise quarter-turns. Every two-draw window contains a scattered non-6 shape to refute prefix, colour-only, and cross-axis conditional shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~8-10) with: (a) EXACTLY ONE color-2 (red) START cell at a random position; (b) EXACTLY ONE color-4 (yellow) WAYPOINT cell, Manhattan-distance ≥ 2 from the start; (c) EXACTLY ONE color-3 (green) GOAL cell, ≥ 2 from waypoint and ≥ 4 from start; (d) 0-8 color-5 (gray) WALL cells sprinkled to obstruct simple paths. Rule: run a 4-connected BFS shortest-path from START to WAYPOINT through 0-cells (walls and non-bg block); then from WAYPOINT to GOAL the same way. CONCATENATE the two path segments. PAINT every cell on the combined path (excluding endpoints) with color 8 (cyan). Start, waypoint, goal, and walls stay. Net: cyan trail from start → waypoint → goal, routing around gray walls.

Rotate the complete input grid by 180 degrees: cell (r,c) moves to (h-1-r,w-1-c), with dimensions and colors unchanged. Four of each six scheduled draws exactly match a canonical shape/palette profile; every ordinary scene distinguishes the rule from identity, one-axis flips, quarter turns, and diagonal reflections.
The unique smallest nonzero component is recolored yellow.

0-bg grid (size varies) with N color-8 hollow rectangular FRAMES (2..4). Each frame's bbox interior holds exactly ONE label pixel in a distinct non-{0,8} color. Elsewhere on the grid sit N free-standing SHAPES (random connected polyominoes), one per frame color, each sized to fit its frame's interior and isolated by a 1-cell gap. Rule: each shape is moved into the interior top-left of the frame whose label matches its color; output keeps the frames and the relocated shapes.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-10) with: (a) TWO ENDPOINT CELLS in COLOR 2 at distinct interior positions with different rows AND different cols; (b) ONE ELBOW CELL in COLOR 3 at a distinct interior position with row matching one endpoint and col matching the other endpoint; (c) TWO COLOR-5 (gray) OBSTACLE CELLS at (0, w-2) and (0, w-1) (top-right corner). Rule (DRAW L-SHAPED PATH IN COLOR 2 CONNECTING ENDPOINTS VIA ELBOW, BLOCKED BY 5-WALLS): identify the 2 COLOR-2 ENDPOINTS A and B and the 1 COLOR-3 ELBOW E. The ELBOW is at (A.row, B.col) or (B.row, A.col). DRAW an L-PATH: from A → E → B via straight horizontal then vertical (or vice versa) segments, PAINTING each intermediate cell and the elbow with COLOR 2 (overwriting the elbow's 3). The path is BLOCKED by color-5 cells (skip those). Endpoints stay. Net: the L-path connects the 2 endpoints through the elbow in color 2.
Recolor exactly the blue components whose border signature is top-only; preserve blue components touching another edge, interior blue objects, and all non-blue distractors.

A 0-background grid contains 2..5 isolated, single-color connected objects with distinct bounding-box heights. Object shapes, areas, rows, columns, and colors vary independently enough to refute area-, position-, and color-order shortcuts. The reference rule outputs one row of object colors ranked by descending bounding-box height.
Distinct top-row color markers project their colors down full columns.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~9-12) with 3 BLOBS of varied aspect ratios placed at scattered positions in distinct non-zero colors from a 3-color palette: (a) a 2×2 SQUARE-bbox blob (h == w); (b) a VERTICAL 1×3 line (h ≠ w); (c) a HORIZONTAL 1×3 line (h ≠ w). Blobs are 4-conn isolated with 1-cell padding. Rule: for EACH CONNECTED BLOB, compute its bbox (rmax-rmin+1, cmax-cmin+1). KEEP only blobs with SQUARE BBOX (h == w). CLEAR (set to 0) all non-square blobs. Net: square-bbox blobs survive at their original color; non-square blobs are erased.

A 5x17 zero-background grid has three 5x5 panels separated by full color-9 columns. Crop A and B, infer the unique transform mapping A to B from identity/90-degree rotations/180/left-right/up-down flips, then apply it to cropped panel C. Sparse canonical-scale motifs, colors, positions, component profiles, and all six transform branches vary.

Wall-partitioned grid (size varies); walls are a color from {1,7,9} and the non-wall regions are rooms. One room holds a color-2 marker. Rule: keep the walls, clear every room to 0, and paint the marked room 8. The grid size, wall layout/color, target room and decoys vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~24 distinct).
skills: room extraction, compartment fill, same-size output

summary: Three or four two-row A/B/C bands.  In each band, the authority selects the highest-exact-score consistent 2x2 D4 transform from A to B, learns its color map, and applies both independently to C.
nxn grid; row 0 and col 0 each have one 2 marker; rule shifts interior.

A closed rectangular color-1 chamber contains two to five colored single-cell markers. Every marker fires four cardinal rays through original background, stopping at the chamber wall; overlapping paints resolve in row-major marker order, matching the selected Racket rule.

A background-0 grid contains 2-5 separated orange(7) components with a unique largest cell count. Recolor only the largest component red(2); preserve every smaller orange component and every background cell.

Select the unique largest component as the template. Count singleton components, crop the template, and output that many horizontally arranged copies separated by one zero column, alternating original and left-right mirror starting with the original.
Red 2 + visible-color stamp at TL, cyan 8 tile mask, and a background-color target rectangle below. Rule tiles the stamp through the mask into the rectangle.

0-bg grid (h~5-9, w~8-14) with 2-5 NON-TOUCHING connected BLOBS of STRICTLY DISTINCT sizes (drawn from a per-difficulty size pool without replacement), each in a distinct non-zero color from {1..9}. Blobs are 4-connectivity-isolated (no cell of one blob is orthogonally adjacent to another). Rule: count each blob's AREA (cell count). Render an OUTPUT BAR CHART: each blob becomes a VERTICAL BAR of the same color whose HEIGHT EQUALS the blob's area; bars are arranged SIDE-BY-SIDE with a 1-column gap between them, aligned along a common baseline (rows oriented bottom-up). Output grid size matches the bar count and max-area. Net: input has 2-5 colored blobs of different sizes; output is an n-bar bar chart of those sizes.

Small 0-bg grid (h×w, h=3..5, w=3..5) with EXACTLY ONE MODE color (strictly most frequent, >50% of cells). Other cells use 1-3 minority colors. Rule: self-tile the input. Output is h*h × w*w. For each cell (r, c) in the input, if its value equals the mode, place the entire input grid at block (r*h..r*h+h-1, c*w..c*w+w-1) in the output; otherwise that block is all 0. Effect: input acts as both the unit tile AND the mask of where to place itself.

On a zero-background grid, find each blue(1) four-connected component that is a solid filled rectangle at least 2x2. Recolor exactly that rectangle's four corner cells red(2). Leave its non-corner blue cells, irregular blue components, and all non-blue distractors unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one red(2) start, one green(3) goal, gray(5) walls, and one pair of equal-colored portals chosen from 7/8/9. Run four-neighbor BFS in up, down, left, right order. Entering a portal teleports to its twin before the state is queued. Paint only the intermediate 0-cells of the selected shortest route yellow(4), preserving start, goal, walls, and portals. A five-profile schedule proves that a portal can be either useful or irrelevant and disambiguates all three adjacent priority comparisons in the canonical BFS order.

Generate a 3x3 grid with two to four distinct nonzero colors. Count only those nonzero colors; if the count is n, upscale every input cell to an n-by-n block. Canonical-profile sparse examples contain zero, while two scheduled zero-free examples per five-sample lesson disprove the tempting canonical-only shortcut of always subtracting one from the total color count.

A color-1 wall splits the grid into two rooms; the source room holds a small color-3 pattern, the target room a color-2 marker. Rule: copy the source's 3-pattern into the target room as color 8, keeping the walls. Grid size, wall, pattern, marker and an optional color-7 door vary.
skills: room-relative coordinates, motif transfer, source/query detection

summary: 0-bg grid (size varies) with ISOLATED components (random connected polyominoes in distinct colors, each separated from everything by >=1 gap so its contact degree is 0) and TOUCHING clusters (small blocks split into two cardinally-adjacent color regions, so each region has degree > 0). Rule: keep only the degree-0 (isolated) components on a blank grid; drop all touching ones. Output = the isolated components in place.

0-bg grid (h, w~6-14) with SPARSE GRAY(5) CELLS placed in a mix of two types: (a) 1-5 LR-SYMMETRIC PAIRS — each pair consists of cells at (r, c) and (r, w-1-c) (both painted 5, c ≠ w-1-c so they're distinct positions); (b) 1-5 ASYMMETRIC SOLO GRAYS — single cells at (r, c) with no partner at (r, w-1-c). Pair layout (random/cluster/row/column/diagonal) and solo layout vary independently. Rule (RECOLOR LR-SYMMETRIC GRAY PAIRS TO BLUE, LEAVE ASYMMETRIC GRAYS AS GRAY): For EACH GRAY (5) CELL at (r, c): check if the LR-MIRROR cell at (r, w-1-c) is ALSO 5. If YES (the cell has a partner): RECOLOR (r, c) from 5 to 1 (blue). Else (no partner — asymmetric solo gray), KEEP at 5. Other cells unchanged. Net: paired grays transform to blue; solo grays survive.
Multi-color clusters with red counts; rule extracts bbox of most-red one.
N panels split by full-height color-5 columns; panel 0 = template; rule outputs the FIRST other panel whose shape matches template under any of 8 dihedral transforms (rotation/reflection).

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-2 and a color-3 MARKER define a translation VECTOR (3-marker minus 2-marker). 2-4 color-1 BLOBS of DISTINCT sizes sit apart, plus a color-7 DECORATION. Rule: take the SMALLEST 1-blob (ties by top row then left col), clear it from its spot, and paint its cells translated by the vector with COLOR 8 (cyan); the markers, the other blobs and the decoration stay. The smallest blob's translation always lands in-bounds on empty cells. The grid size, the vector, the blob count/sizes/shapes/positions and the decoration all vary freely (was a fixed marker+blob layout).

A 0-background maze with exactly one color-1 start, color-2 goal and color-3 checkpoint, optional paired color-4 portals, and color-8 walls. Find the shortest 4-neighbor route from start to goal that visits the checkpoint; portals teleport in one step. Paint traversed background cells color 7. Portal-present generated examples are required to make teleportation causally change the label.

Preserve the grid and reflect every colored cell left of the unique full-height gray(5) divider to the equidistant cell on its right, preserving color.
