The four-profile lesson schedule includes exact canonical anchors, off-center dividers, dense edge/row motifs, and unrelated right-side cells that must remain unchanged.

A square 9..11 zero-background grid contains one copy at most of cue colors 1, 2, 3, and 6. Color 6 grows upward into a seven-cell vertical segment, color 3 grows downward into a four-cell vertical segment, color 1 grows a two-cell right arm with a second 1 above its tip, and color 2 is the right endpoint of a five-cell horizontal segment centered on the rightmost non-2 cue to its left. If that horizontal segment crosses the interior of a 6/3 vertical segment, paint a yellow diagonal down-left from the crossing. Ordinary seven-demo lessons cover every canonical cue configuration before querying the same rule on a new placement.
Recolor yellow components touching exactly two distinct borders to cyan; retain yellow components touching zero, one, three, or four borders.
Equal square blocks separated by full same-color rows/columns; crop the unique block whose nonzero cells all share one color.

Several color-3 plus-shapes (each 5 cells: center + 4 cardinals) on a 0-bg grid. Some pairs of plus-centers are EXACTLY diagonal to each other (|dr| = |dc|). Rule draws color-2 cells in the bg cells between each such diagonal pair (interior diagonal cells fill with 2). Pairs that are not exactly diagonal don't connect.

Place exactly two red (2) markers on an otherwise black grid so they are horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree diagonal endpoints; the rule replaces them with the full inclusive connecting segment in cyan (8) on a blank grid of the same size.

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0,0) holds a ROTATION CODE in {1,2,3,4}. One TEMPLATE object (a random connected polyomino, 3-8 cells, the largest non-{0,9,code} object) sits in the grid, plus 2-4 color-9 MARKER cells positioned with room for the rotated stamp. Rule: rotate the template by the code (1=id, 2=cw, 3=180, else=ccw) and stamp it (top-left anchored) at every color-9 marker on a blank output. Output = the rotated template repeated at the marker positions.

Sparse zero-background grids use seven nonzero colors across 3-4 active rows.  For each row independently, keep every cell whose color appears exactly once in that row and erase every cell whose color appears two or three times.  The curriculum includes singleton-only rows, rows with multiple singleton colors, repeated pairs and triples, and colors that change role between rows so global-frequency and one-answer-per-row shortcuts fail.
Template + layout panel expand two color swatches into self-tiled output.
Keep nonzero contents when every interior color matches its rectangular frame; otherwise erase all nonzero contents inside that frame.

A 0-background grid has 1..3 blue count markers anywhere in row 0. Rows below contain 2..5 isolated, distinctly colored components. Count the enclosed 0-regions in each component, scan components in row-major order, and select the first component whose hole count equals the blue marker count. Crop to that component's bounding box, erase every non-boundary component cell, and recolor the retained boundary cyan (8). Some lessons contain two matching components with different boundary masks, so the canonical first-match tie rule is observable.
Split the zero-separated grid into 5x5 framed tiles, union all interior motif offsets carried by each color, and copy that union into every frame of that same color.

On a black background, recolor only yellow (4) components that are exact three-cell 2x2 L-triominoes to blue (1). Yellow non-L components and same-shaped L-triominoes in other colors remain unchanged.
Target marker frame determines the local diagonal cell to mark.
skills: frame parsing, local coordinates, same-size output

summary: 0-bg grid (h~10-16, w~12-18) with: (a) 1-3 HORIZONTALLY-SYMMETRIC COMPONENTS — each shape drawn from a small bank _SYM_H of LR-symmetric motifs (plus, square, horizontal-3 bar — shapes that satisfy shape ≡ flip_lr(shape)); (b) 2 ASYMMETRIC COMPONENTS — each shape drawn from _ASYM bank (L-triomino, Z-tetromino, T-shape — no LR symmetry). Each component is painted in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {2, 3, 4, 6} (shuffled). Components are placed at non-touching positions with 1-cell padding (_free check). Rule (RECOLOR ONLY HORIZONTALLY-SYMMETRIC COMPONENTS TO COLOR 8): for EACH 4-CONNECTED non-bg COMPONENT in the input: CHECK whether the component's local shape (in its bbox) is HORIZONTALLY MIRROR-SYMMETRIC (flipping its cells left-right produces the same shape). If YES: RECOLOR every cell of that component to COLOR 8. If NO: LEAVE the component unchanged (keeps its original color). Bg-0 cells stay 0. Net: horizontally-symmetric shapes are unified under color 8 (cyan); asymmetric shapes retain their original colors as distractors.

Canonical-scale 5..8 x 10..16 grids with two separated, distinctly colored hollow objects. Enclosed hole unions can be rectangular, nonrectangular, or split into multiple regions; complex profiles also include an exterior bbox corner. The rule extracts only enclosed zero regions, crops each union, recolors it by its object, and packs patterns left-to-right with one background column.
Remove adjacent identical whole rows and whole columns; preserve separated repeats and locally equal cells in globally distinct columns.

skills: legend parsing, layer recolor, same-size conditioned transform
summary: Row 0 contains 2..4 distinct nonzero palette colors, optionally separated by one or two zero gaps. Rows 1+ contain 1..3 separated, monochrome, often non-rectangular 4-connected components in a body color independent of the palette. Repeatedly peel each component's exposed cardinal boundary. Paint depth d with palette[min(d-1, last)], preserving the header and background.
A full-height divider bar mirrors every colored source cell across its column.

A uniquely most-common-colour block mask and a separate dense 3x3 or 4x4 palette share positional coordinates.  Output copies each palette cell iff the corresponding large block is present, else 0.  Defaults cycle through all four canonical size/colour profiles and include connected and disconnected masks plus shape-colour palette witnesses.
Separated top-row legend plus one crop-sized component per legend color.

Colors 1/7/9 are walls; full-height color-9 divider columns split the grid into rooms (one per panel). Top-left room is the query; rule outputs a 1xN strip marking with 8 each candidate room whose motif signature equals the query room's.
skills: roomwise pattern comparison, symbolic selection, query/candidate split
rotation/reflection handling, local transport, same-size output
summary: A sparse 0-background grid contains one SOURCE L-frame: color 2 is its origin, color 3 marks its local u direction, and color 4 marks its perpendicular local v direction. A non-rectangular color-8 motif lies at signed local offsets around that source. A TARGET L-frame similarly uses colors 5,6,7. Copy every source motif offset to the same (u,v) coordinate around the target, so the copied motif rotates or reflects with the target basis. The source, both frames, and all existing cells remain.

A canonical-scale zero-background grid contains four monochrome four-connected objects with one uniquely smallest by cell count. Crop that component exactly to its bbox. A six-step schedule preserves exact canonical dimension/palette profiles and repeatedly contrasts cell count with bbox area, color frequency, color grouping, 8-connectivity, multicolor connectivity, solid-bbox output, and scan-order selection.
Exact solid 2×3 or 3×2 color-2 rectangles → color 8; other shapes/colors ignored.
Paint each blank cell whose wall-constrained distance to the red and green seeds is equal.

0-bg grid (h = dr+8, w = dc+8 with dr, dc ∈ [3, 5]) with: (a) SOURCE GRAY MARKER at (sr, sc) with sr, sc ∈ [2, 3] painted COLOR 5; (b) COLORED MOTIF — 4 cells around the source at offsets (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1) painted in 2 distinct non-{0, 5} colors (alternating); (c) ISOLATED GRAY MARKER at (sr + dr, sc + dc) — a second color-5 cell NOT adjacent to the source motif. Rule (USE GRAY-MARKER VECTOR TO TRANSLATE MOTIF, CLEAR ISOLATED GRAY): identify the TWO GRAY (5) MARKERS. SOURCE GRAY = the one ORTHOGONALLY ADJACENT to colored motif cells. ISOLATED GRAY = the one not adjacent to any non-gray non-bg. Compute DELTA = isolated_pos - source_pos. For EACH non-gray motif cell at (r, c) with color C: PAINT (r + delta_r, c + delta_c) with C (copy translated). ERASE the ISOLATED GRAY (set to 0). Source gray + original motif stay. Net: the motif gets copied to a translated location and the isolated marker disappears.

0-bg grid with exactly one full color-3 row at cross_row and one full color-3 column at cross_col forming a green '+' cross. The cross divides the grid into 4 quadrants. Rule: each quadrant anchor is the inner corner adjacent to the cross. For each non-cross cell (r, c), compute Chebyshev distance from anchor: if dist is ODD → color 4, else → 0. Cross cells (color 3) preserved. Output is 4 quadrants filled with concentric alternating 4/0 rectangles centered on the cross corner.
Count the connected red marker cells. Select the unique blue component with that many cells and output its binary mask cropped to its bounding box.

0-bg grid (size varies). A full COLOR-5 LINE (horizontal or vertical) with a SEED PATCH (sh x sw, a random 2-color pattern) placed directly beside it, anchored at the line's start and narrower than the line. Rule: tile the seed pattern across the line's span (over the seed's height) to fill the rectangle beside the line. Net: the small seed pattern is repeated to fill a strip alongside the 5-line.
Recolor each isolated 2 to 1 and preserve every 2 having at least one orthogonal 2-neighbor.

For an n x n two-color grid, use 0 as the background mask and the sole nonzero color as paint. The n² x n² output is indexed by a block source cell and a subcell source cell from the input; paint exactly when BOTH source cells are 0, otherwise output 0. This is the zero-mask Kronecker self-product. Ordinary lessons schedule 3x3 canonical anchors together with 4x4 and 5x5 cases so the rule cannot collapse to a fixed 9x9 template. The twelve-draw count cycle includes all canonical zero counts 3, 4 and 5.

Find the unique full-height cyan (8) column. Preserve the input, then copy every nonzero, non-axis cell to column 2*axis-c in the same row and color whenever that column is in bounds; ignore clipped reflections.
Find the largest nonzero monochrome rectangular frame with an all-zero interior. Find the other same-sized all-zero interior slot in row-major order and paint that slot's border with the frame color.

Read row-0 rotation commands, select the largest body component with top/left tie breaks, crop the original body through its bounding box, rotate that crop for each command, and pack the copies with one-column gaps.

Color-5 walls enclose 2..6 rectangular chambers. The top-left value 1..6 selects the unique chamber containing exactly that many color-2 cells. The reference fills that chamber with 8 and erases other seeds; walls remain 5. The control becomes 0 except that control 5 remains 5. Canonical crosses alternate with count-disambiguating default inputs.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-12) with 2-4 SAME-COLOR HORIZONTAL ENDPOINT PAIRS, each on a DIFFERENT ROW, at columns (c1, c2) with c2 ≥ c1 + 2 (≥1 bg cell between them). Each pair uses a DISTINCT non-zero color from {1..9}. Active rows have exactly 2 cells in their color; the interval between is initially 0. Rule (FILL ROW INTERVAL BETWEEN ENDPOINTS): for EACH ROW with exactly 2 SAME-COLOR ENDPOINTS, FILL the INCLUSIVE INTERVAL between them (every cell from min_c to max_c in that row) with the pair's COLOR. Rows without endpoints stay 0. Net: each horizontal endpoint pair becomes a solid filled interval.

Place a sparse connected colored pattern inside a square grid. A 1 guide at the top-left selects main-diagonal reflection; a 2 guide at the top-right selects anti-diagonal reflection. Remove the guide and fill empty reflected partners without overwriting original colored cells.
Each horizontal run keeps alternating cells starting from its left endpoint.

Find the solid multicolor template rectangle and the equal-sized solid zero rectangle on the modal nonzero background. Reflect the template left-to-right and write that reflected rectangle into the zero target; leave every other cell unchanged.

A unique full-height gray (5) column is the reflection axis. A connected blue (1) object lies wholly on either side; each blue cell is reflected independently to cyan (8) on an otherwise blank output, with out-of-bounds targets clipped. Non-blue cells, including off-axis gray cells, are ignored.

FIXED 3×3 input grid with 1-8 COLOR-5 TRIGGER cells at positions chosen by one of 8 LAYOUTS (random/cluster/border/row/column/corners/cross/diagonal). Non-trigger cells filled by FILLER PATTERN (zero/sparse_decoy at 30%/mixed_decoy at 60%) using decoy colors from {3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9} (excluding {0, 1, 2, 5}). Rule (STAMP 2×2 [[1, 2], [2, 1]] CHECKER AT EACH COLOR-5 TRIGGER): EMIT a 6×6 OUTPUT GRID (input doubled). For EACH cell (r, c) in the 3×3 input where g[r][c] == 5: STAMP the 2×2 CHECKER [[1, 2], [2, 1]] at output position (2r, 2c). Non-5 input cells produce 0 in the output 2×2 block. Net: each color-5 cell expands to a 2×2 checker; output is 6×6.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with: (a) one HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME (3-4 rows × 3-4 cols, border-only) in one color; (b) 1-2 small DISTRACTOR BLOBS (2-4 cells, irregular shapes) in distinct colors. All components are 4-disconnected. Rule: identify the UNIQUE rect-frame (hollow rectangular outline) among the components. Crop that frame to its bounding box. Output: the cropped rect-frame (h_frame × w_frame grid showing just the hollow rectangle border). Distractors discarded.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~7-10) with: (a) ROW 0 SRC COLORS — at columns 0..n-1 (n=3-5 pairs), row 0 holds SOURCE colors drawn from a palette of n+1 distinct non-0 values; (b) ROW 1 DST COLORS — at the same columns, row 1 holds TARGET colors (each colors[(c+1) % len(palette)] cyclically — paired src→dst mapping); (c) BODY rows 2..h-1 — contain several separated small objects/line-like blobs in the SOURCE colors from the palette[:n] mapping domain, with every source color represented at least once. Rule (APPLY THE TOP-2-ROW COLOR SUBSTITUTION MAP ONLY TO ROWS 2 AND BELOW): READ row 0 and row 1 to build a SRC→DST MAP {g[0][c] → g[1][c] for c with non-0 g[0][c]}. For EACH cell in ROWS 2..h-1: if the cell's value is a SRC in the map, REPLACE it with the corresponding DST. Cells with non-mapped values stay. Rows 0 and 1 (the legend) stay unchanged. Net: the body is recolored by the top-2 legend.
Find nonzero 4-connected components without splitting on color; select the greatest bounding-box height (cell count, then leftmost column break ties), and return its tight color-preserving crop.

0-bg grid (size varies) with: a single RED(2) MARKER cell; a NEAREST object (a random connected polyomino, 3-7 cells, distinct color) placed close to the marker; and 1-2 DISTRACTOR objects placed strictly farther from the marker (so the nearest is unique). Rule: among non-red objects, pick the one with the smallest minimum Manhattan distance to the marker and output it cropped to its bbox. Output shape/dims = the nearest object.
Place 3-5 distinct-color horizontal runs of odd length 1, 3, or 5 on separate rows of a zero-background grid.  Reduce every run to its unique central cell, preserving that cell's color and position.

3×3 grid of equal-sized panels separated by two full color-5 rows and two full color-5 cols. Each panel has 0..k² marker cells in one color. Rule finds the maximum marker count, then fills each panel that reaches that max completely with the marker color. Separators preserved.

Row 0 (colour-1 count) sets a holes-target; row 1 (colour-2 count) sets a symmetry class; the body holds shapes and the rule outputs the one matching both, recoloured 8. The selected (holes, symmetry) combo, shape sizes and positions vary.

A zero-background grid contains either two isolated rectangular gray(5) chambers or three visible rectangles where two touch and merge into one non-rectangular component. Only connected color-5 components that are exact rectangle borders are active. In each active chamber, blue(1) emits a vertical orange(7) ray and red(2) a horizontal ray; gray walls and yellow(4) blockers stop the ray. Seeds and blockers inside the malformed touching pair stay unchanged.

A single red (2) source launches a beam to the right through black (0) cells. A green (3) slash mirror maps (dr,dc) to (-dc,-dr), while a yellow (4) backslash mirror maps it to (dc,dr). The beam stops at the first gray (5) cell or when it leaves the grid; every traversed black cell is painted cyan (8). All mirrors lie on the traced route. One or two straight gray wall components may be present, including an unused distractor wall on the boundary-exit branch demonstrated by the public test example.

A zero-background grid contains 2-4 disconnected hollow rectangular frames in one shared colour and the same number of differently coloured ordinary shapes. Frame interior areas and shape cell counts are each strictly increasing. Rank shapes by cell count, rank frames by interior area, erase the old shapes, and centre each shape in its matching frame.

30x30 nonzero texture with exact 4mm symmetry around the rule's off-center pivot. One to three connected color-9 damage rectangles occlude part of the texture; every damaged cell has at least one non-damaged same-orbit mate, so the canonical rule repairs the grid in place instead of leaving 9s or collapsing to duplicate/no-op pairs.

30x30 zero-background grid with 5-7 separated hollow rectangles, all drawn in color 3.  Rectangles are arranged as a horizontal or vertical chain with small gaps and a shared perpendicular band, matching the canonical task's large fixed canvas and hollow color-3 object style. Rule: connect rectangles along the minimum-gap spanning tree by drawing color-3 corridors and punching doorways through facing rectangle walls.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~9-11) with ONE COLOR appearing as EXACTLY 2 CELLS placed at DIAGONAL positions forming a NON-DEGENERATE BBOX (≥3 rows AND ≥3+ cols span). The two cells are at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) with r2 ≥ r1 + 2 and c2 ≥ c1 + 3 (or other diagonal arrangement). Color chosen from {2..9}. Rule (FILL EACH 2-CELL COLOR'S BBOX RECTANGLE WITH THE COLOR ON A FRESH EMPTY GRID): For EACH COLOR appearing ≥2 times (here, exactly 2): compute its BBOX (min/max row and col). PAINT every cell within the bbox (inclusive) with that color in the output. Other cells stay 0. Net: the 2 cells get filled in to the solid rectangle they define.

A contiguous vertical color-7 source marks a column and bottom row. The output is an upward triangle clipped by the canvas: cells whose horizontal distance from the source column is at most bottom_row-row are 7 at even horizontal distance and 8 at odd distance; every other output cell is 0. Controlled non-7 decoys are outside the triangle and are erased.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-12) with 1-3 HORIZONTAL line objects (single-row runs of length 2-w) AND 1-3 VERTICAL line objects (single-column runs of length 2-h). All in distinct non-bg colors. Lines isolated by ≥1 bg cell. Rule: extract objects. Split into horizontal (all cells share one row) and vertical (share one col). Sort each group by (size DESC, color ASC). Top output row = horizontal lines laid out left-to-right, each painted in its color, separated by 1 zero. Bottom row = vertical lines (laid horizontally as runs of their color), separated by 1 zero. Output: 2-row grid sized to max(top, bottom).
Two 4-column panels separated by col 4; OR of nonzero-occupancy → 8, else 0.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~11-14) with FOUR FIXED-POSITION OBJECTS at the corner-like slots: (a) TEMPLATE OBJECT at (1, 1) — a 4-cell L shape [(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(2,1)] painted in COLOR 8 (cyan, the template color); (b) MATCHING 2-BLOB at (1, w-4) — the SAME 4-cell L shape painted in COLOR 2 (this is the candidate that the rule should recolor); (c) DIFFERENT 2-BLOB at (h-4, 1) — a 2×2 SQUARE shape [(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)] painted in COLOR 2; (d) DIFFERENT-2 2-BLOB at (h-4, w-4) — a 3-cell VERTICAL bar [(0,0),(1,0),(2,0)] painted in COLOR 2. Exactly one 2-blob (b) shares the 8-blob's normalized shape; the other two have distinct shapes. Rule (RECOLOR 2-BLOBS WHOSE NORMALIZED SHAPE MATCHES THE 8-BLOB TEMPLATE TO COLOR 3): find the unique 8-BLOB, extract its NORMALIZED CELLS (subtract min row/col from each cell so the shape sits in its own local coordinates). For EACH 2-BLOB: extract its NORMALIZED CELLS. If the 2-blob's normalized shape EQUALS the 8-blob's normalized shape: RECOLOR every cell of that 2-blob to COLOR 3. Other 2-blobs stay color 2; the 8-blob stays color 8. Net: the one 2-blob matching the 8-shape becomes color-3 (green); the rest remain as color-2 decoys.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE BISYMMETRIC component (a random shape that is both horizontally and vertically mirror-symmetric, built by mirroring a random quadrant into all four quadrants, varied size) plus 1-2 verified NON-symmetric distractor shapes, all in distinct colors, placed apart. Rule: find the unique component symmetric under both H and V mirror and output it cropped to its bbox.

0-bg grid (size varies). The LARGEST object is a 2-wide RING of one color forming a size×size bounding box (size 7-11) with a RANDOM pattern of that color filling its (size-4)×(size-4) INTERIOR. A couple of small distractor clusters in other colors sit elsewhere. Rule: background = most frequent color; cluster non-bg cells; take the largest one-color cluster; shrink its bbox by 2; output the inner region (the color's cells stay, else bg). Output = the ring's interior pattern, dims (size-4)×(size-4).

A 0-background grid contains isolated vertical occupancy blocks. Exact same-color runs of length 3 are targets; the authority recolors only their top and bottom cells to 8. Every default example also contains a mixed-color occupied block of length 3. Defaults alternate same-color length-2 and length-4 distractors, so every three consecutive examples show both boundaries and every four-pair lesson remains identifiable under all query rotations. Three quarters of default draws use one of the canonical (height,width,palette) profiles.

A canonical-scale 0-background grid contains 3-6 separated monochrome components with distinct leftmost columns.  Sort the components by leftmost column (then row), binary-crop each shape, and emit an N x N matrix with 8 when two crops are equivalent under any rotation or reflection and 0 otherwise.  Every ordinary scene contains both a positive off-diagonal match and a negative off-diagonal mismatch.
Highlight the union of every shortest red-to-green path through a gray-walled maze.

An 8-9 by 8-10 zero-background grid has 2-4 red(2) emitters on the top edge and 2-4 blue(1) emitters on the left edge. Gray(5) blockers may lie inside the grid. Top emitters cast downward and left emitters cast rightward; each ray stops before its first blocker. The output is blank except for magenta(6) at cells reached by both ray families.

0-bg grid with: (a) one SOURCE TEMPLATE — a small connected shape in colors from {5, 6, 7} (3-5 cells); (b) 2-3 ANCHOR PAIRS scattered elsewhere — each anchor is a color-9 (maroon) cell with a color-in-{1, 2, 3, 4} cell immediately to its LEFT (at column anchor_col - 1). The left-cell value k encodes the transform: 1=identity, 2=rot-CW, 3=rot-180, 4=rot-CCW. Rule: extract the source — the largest 4-conn component using colors {5, 6, 7}. Normalize to bbox corner. For each anchor (a color-9 cell preceded by a {1..4} cell to its left), apply transform (k - 1) to the source and stamp the result at the anchor's position. Output: empty grid + stamped, transformed source copies at each anchor.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~12-17) with: (a) ONE color-3 (green) TEMPLATE shape — a small polyomino [(0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1)] placed at upper-left (rows 0-2, cols 1-2); (b) THREE CONTROL MARKERS placed at fixed positions ((h-5, 4), (h-4, w-5), (h-2, 2)) in 3 distinct colors drawn from {1, 2, 4, 6} — each marker color encodes a DIFFERENT ROTATION (0°, 90°, 180°, 270° respectively). Rule: extract the green template. For each control marker, decode the rotation from its color and STAMP a rotated copy of the template in color 3 at the marker's position. Original template and markers are DISCARDED. Output: 3 green copies of the template, each rotated according to its marker, at the marker positions. Net: marker colors program rotations; output is the template gallery.
Recolor each color-1 object with the color of the uniquely matching non-1 template object's exact normalized shape.
Several monochrome components. Keep exactly those touching one horizontal and one vertical border; erase components touching only one border or none.

A complete non-gray colored diagonal lies on a black background (with a regular 10x10 canonical-scale anchor among varied sizes). Gray marker cells occupy one or more neighboring parallel diagonals on the left, right, or both sides. Keep the source diagonal and replace the gray region by a colored parallel diagonal exactly two diagonal offsets beyond the farthest gray marker on each occupied side.

A zero-background grid has one command cell in row 0 and one multicolour 4-connected motif below a blank separator. Crop the motif to its bounding box, then apply 2=identity, 3=90° clockwise, 4=180°, 5=left/right flip, or 6=up/down flip.

0-bg grid (h~8-13, w~10-15) with 2-3 BLOBS of 2-4 cells each (4-connected, grown via grow_blob), each in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {1..9}. Blobs are placed STRICTLY IN THE INTERIOR (excluding the outer border row/column — added to `used` set before growing) so their 1-step halos won't extend off-grid. Blobs are spaced apart by ≥2 cells (via 2-cell dilation check) so their halos do NOT touch each other or overlap. Rule (EXPAND EACH BLOB BY ONE CELL IN 4 CARDINALS — PAINT EACH HALO CELL ITS BLOB'S COLOR): for EACH bg-0 cell in the input: INSPECT its 4 ORTHOGONAL NEIGHBORS. IF all neighbors are 0 → leave the cell as bg-0; IF all NON-0 neighbors share the same color C and at least one neighbor is non-0 → PAINT this cell with C (the halo color). IF neighbors have multiple distinct non-0 colors → the rule is undefined (but the input is constructed so this never happens). The original blob cells stay their colors. Net: each blob is dilated by 1 cell in the 4 cardinal directions, growing a single-cell halo around it.

0-bg grid (h~8-16, w~11-19) with: (a) 1-2 (default) VERTICAL FULL-HEIGHT WALLS at columns chosen by one of 5 POSITION BIASES (spread / centered / left_heavy / right_heavy / diagonal), all painted COLOR 2; (b) 1-2 HORIZONTAL WALLS that span only ONE SECTION (between two vertical walls or between a wall and the grid edge), creating DISTINCT 0-REGION SIZES; (c) optional DISTRACTOR cells of color 2 (≤5% density). The 2-walls split the bg-0 cells into ≥3 disjoint 4-CONNECTED REGIONS of distinct sizes (MAX and MIN are unique). Rule (RECOLOR THE MAX-SIZE 0-REGION TO 1 AND THE MIN-SIZE 0-REGION TO 8): extract every 4-CONNECTED region of bg-0 cells (blocked by color-2 walls). RANK regions by cell count. SELECT the LARGEST region — PAINT every cell with COLOR 1 (blue). SELECT the SMALLEST region — PAINT every cell with COLOR 8 (cyan). Other regions stay bg-0. The 2-walls stay color 2. Net: the largest open chamber turns blue; the smallest turns cyan; middle-sized regions stay black.

Read the distinct nonzero colors in the top row from left to right. For each color, tightly crop its separated body component, then pack the crops left-to-right from output row 1 with one blank column between adjacent crops.

One connected monochrome object on zero background; replace it with its tight bounding-box outline in the original color, erasing its interior. Vary canvas, color, occupancy, shape and position. Alternate bent-interior teaching witnesses with unconstrained nonidentity motifs.
Sparse colored cells with at least one exact-two color pair that expands to a rectangle.

0-bg grid (size varies) carved by 1-wide COLOR-8 walls into an nr×nc TABLE of CHAMBERS (2-3 per axis), each chamber an independently varied interior size (2-4 cells per side). Each chamber holds ONE MARKER cell in a non-{0,8} color at a random interior position. Rule: find the 8-walled chambers and flood each with its marker color. Net: each chamber becomes a solid monochrome region of its marker color within the 8-wall grid.
Recolor every exact blue 2x2-square component red while preserving every other blue component.
Swap the two nonzero colors inside the sole gray frame; preserve the same colors outside it.
Swap 9/7 roles and paint red connectors across zero-triggered rows or columns between their global bounding boxes.

A black grid contains two or three separated solid monochrome rectangles in distinct nonzero colours. For each rectangle independently, start a checkerboard at its own top-left cell: retain the rectangle colour where (row - top + column - left) is even and clear the alternating cells to 0. A four-sample teaching schedule alternates two/three rectangles and even/odd rectangle anchors to rule out first-two-only and global-origin checkerboard shortcuts.
Vertical 9-wall on right + 2-3 distinct-color blobs to its left.

0-bg grid with 2-3 compact same-color 3x3 motifs, placed far apart along one dominant axis.  Each nonzero color defines one motif by its bounding box; the motif may be an X with diagonally separated cells, matching canonical examples where color-shapes are not necessarily 4-connected.  Rule: crop each color's bbox, sort motifs by their spatial centers along the dominant axis, and concatenate the crops horizontally or vertically.

0-bg grid (h~5-11, w~6-13) with: (a) ONE HOLLOW RECTANGLE FRAME of size rh × rw (3..5 each) placed at random position (r1, c1) — painted as a complete BORDER OUTLINE (top, bottom rows + left, right columns) in a single non-0 color C0 (palette[0]); the interior cells (rows r1+1..r2-1, cols c1+1..c2-1) stay bg-0; (b) 0-2 SMALL DISTRACTOR SHAPES (1-2 cells each, drawn from _SMALL bank) placed at non-overlapping non-touching positions (bbox padding tracked in placed list), each in a DISTINCT non-{0, C0} color from the palette. Objects don't touch each other. The frame is the only hollow rectangular outline. Rule (FILL EACH HOLLOW RECTANGLE FRAME'S INTERIOR WITH ITS OWN BORDER COLOR): find every RECTANGULAR HOLLOW FRAME (full perimeter outline, ≥3×3, interior cells bg-0). For EACH frame of color C: PAINT every bg-0 cell inside the frame's interior bbox (strictly inside the border) with COLOR C. The border cells stay C. Distractor shapes (non-frame) stay unchanged. Net: the hollow rectangle becomes a solid filled rectangle of the same color; distractors elsewhere are preserved.

Grid laid out as a CELL LATTICE: rows × cols (~4-6 each) DATA BLOCKS, each block a cell_size×cell_size square (cell_size=2), with 1-cell SEPARATOR rows and SEPARATOR columns of 0 between adjacent blocks. Every data block is filled with the BACKGROUND COLOR 1 EXCEPT EXACTLY ONE ANOMALOUS BLOCK, filled with some other non-{0, 1} color. Total grid dims: h = rows*2 + rows-1, w = cols*2 + cols-1. Rule: locate the anomalous block's row-of-blocks and col-of-blocks. REPAINT EVERY data block in that ROW-OF-BLOCKS to the anomaly color, and EVERY data block in that COL-OF-BLOCKS to the anomaly color, leaving separators 0 untouched. Net: the anomalous color spreads to fill the entire row and column of blocks containing it — a 'plus shape' painted across the lattice.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~10-13) with 2-4 ISOLATED 4-conn BLOBS (3-5 cells each) in distinct colors, with NON-RECTANGULAR shapes (so bbox-fill is non-trivial) and non-overlapping bboxes. Rule: extract every 4-conn non-bg blob. For each blob, find its BOUNDING BOX. FILL every cell in that bbox with the blob's color (solid rectangle fill). Net: each blob expands from its sparse shape to a SOLID FILLED RECTANGLE matching its bbox dimensions.
Gray(5) anchor selects checkerboard parity; nonzeros on the OTHER parity are erased.

A zero-background grid contains one cyan outer frame and cyan internal walls that form 2-4 connected chambers. Every chamber has exactly one distinct non-{0,8} seed; fill all zero cells in that chamber with its seed color.

0-bg grid (size varies). A full COLOR-5 ROW divides it. TOP region: a COLOR-2 T (a 3-cell bar + a 2-cell perpendicular stem; stem points down when the bar is on top, up when the bar is on the bottom) plus an 'other'-colored random shape. BOTTOM region: a 'bottom'-colored random shape. Rule: output = the bottom region with the other shape stacked directly BELOW (stem down) or ABOVE (stem up) the bottom shape, column-aligned to it. Output dims = bottom-region dims.

One cyan (8) rectangular frame contains a colored pattern only on the left half (and optionally the centerline) of its interior. Mirror every nonzero non-8 interior cell across the frame's vertical centerline, preserving the source cells and frame.
1-3 emitter cells; rest of the grid is empty.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several DISTINCT blue(1) shapes, each stamped a chosen number of times (same orientation), placed apart, with a mix of odd and even counts. Rule: recolor every instance of an odd-count shape to red(2); even-count shapes stay blue. The grid size, the shapes and each shape's count/positions vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~16 distinct).
Infer the smallest 2-D period of a top-left pattern, shift it one column left, and tile it over the cover region.

Gray walls partition an unframed 0-background grid into 4-connected compartments. Flood a compartment with its seed color exactly when it contains one seed cell from {1,2,3}; clear zero-seed and multi-seed compartments. Canonical full-row/full-column dividers alternate with local separators, and default lessons include a three-seed negative.

Remove the blue (1) drop, follow its column downward through the red (2) open-top containers, and fill the first bounded section whose entire floor is solid red. A floor with any gap leaks, so the drop continues to the next lower container; if every candidate leaks, color the whole bottom row blue. Adjacent red dividers delimit independent sections.

A maroon corner selects one of four rotations; 1-3 orange cells on row 0 select the rank-th smallest ordinary component, which is centered in the cyan frame. Optional orange objects away from row 0 are ignored.

A canonical-profile ARC canvas contains three to five 4-connected red (2) components plus non-red distractors. Return one row containing every red component's cell count in ascending order. Repeated sizes are retained, diagonal contact does not connect components, and lawful sizes can exceed 5.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~8-10) with 2 single SOURCE CELLS in distinct non-zero colors from {2, 3, 4, 5}, placed at hardcoded positions (1, 3) and (4, 2). NOTE: positions hardcoded — diversity is intrinsic-mid. Rule: for EACH EMPTY (0) CELL, FIND all SOURCES that are VISIBLE (same row or column, no non-zero between the cell and the source). For the cell: if EXACTLY ONE color is visible (only one source on its axes), PAINT it that color; if ≥2 DISTINCT colors are visible, PAINT it COLOR 8 (cyan); if zero visible, leave as 0. Sources stay. Net: empty cells fill with the unique visible source color, or cyan for intersections of multiple source axes.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~9-11) with: (a) one RED(2) SEED; (b) one BLUE(3) SEED; (c) a connected PATH of GRAY(5) cells linking them (4-connected through cells with value ∈ {2, 3, 5}); (d) 1-2 ISOLATED GRAY(5) STUB cells elsewhere, not connected to the path. Path orientations vary (horizontal, vertical, L, diagonal-by-stair). Rule: BFS from the 2-seed through cells with value in {2, 3, 5} (4-connectivity). If the BFS reaches the 3-seed → for every 5-cell in the reachable component, recolor it to YELLOW(4). Else output unchanged. Isolated 5-stubs stay as 5 (not reachable, not recolored).
Connected red/green component recolor with a four-profile curriculum that refutes four plausible shortcut rules.

A first all-zero row separates a left-to-right library of 3-5 distinct-color connected prototypes from a dense lower color-index matrix. Each prototype is cropped independently and top-left padded to the common maximum crop size; the lower nonzero rectangle is cropped; each index token is then replaced by its matching padded prototype with no gaps. Scheduled variants include canonical 6/7x11 layouts, vertically shifted prototypes, blank padding around the index, and non-3x3 tile sizes.

One monochrome prototype and isolated anchors: 2=id, 3=cw90, 4=180, 5=ccw90. Stamp bounding-box-normalized shapes in the prototype color on a fresh grid, clipping at edges and taking the union of overlaps. Alternating teaching and broad scenes expose canonical-fitting shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several color-1 BLOBS: 2-4 copies of a COMMON shape (each in ANY rotation/flip — they share a dihedral canonical) plus ONE UNIQUE blob with a different canonical, all separated. Rule: compute each blob's canonical shape under the 8 rotation/flip transforms, find the one whose canonical is unique (appears once), and output its bbox-cropped normalized mask in COLOR 8 (cyan). The grid size, the common shape and its orientations, the unique shape, the copy count and all positions vary freely (was 4 fixed blobs + grid padding).

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~12-14) with 3-4 ISOLATED 4-conn COMPONENTS (1-3 cells each) in distinct non-bg colors, mixed near/far so some pairs share clear row/column line-of-sight while others do not. Rule: extract all 4-conn non-bg components, sort by top-left (r1, c1) ascending. For each pair, scan horizontally/vertically from every cell; if the first non-bg object seen after at least one 0-cell is the other component, they are adjacent. Output is an N×N matrix where N = number of components: diagonal[i][i] = 1 (blue); off-diagonal[i][j] = 8 (cyan) if line-of-sight holds, else 0. Net: a visibility matrix.

0-bg grid (size varies). Row 0 holds n color-9 markers (n in [1, K]). The body (rows 1+) holds K (3-6) connected objects of DISTINCT sizes in distinct non-{0,9} colors at scattered, separated positions. Rule: n = count of row-0 9s; zero them; sort body objects by size descending (tie-break by position); output the bbox crop of the n-th object. The selected object (output shape/size/color) varies with n, the object sizes and shapes.
Sparse values on odd coords expand into block-and-connector diagram.

0-bg grid (size varies). ROW 0 holds a PALETTE: K distinct non-0 colors at K columns (left-to-right palette order). The BODY (rows 1..h-1) holds K connected shapes of DISTINCT sizes (random polyominoes), separated, in distinct colors. Rule: sort the body shapes by size descending and recolor the i-th largest with palette[i]; output the recolored body (dims (h-1) x w). The palette, the body shape sizes and the shapes all vary.

Slide each contiguous color-3 row block left until immediately after the nearest color-8 cell originally to its left, or column zero. Preserve block length. Other rows and all 8s stay fixed. Optional nonmarker distractors are placed outside both initial and final block footprints and survive.

A modal background contains a solid mover, a larger solid facing wall, and a farther same-side distractor. The nearest qualifying mover passes through the wall; its channel is erased from the wall, and the wall grows transversely around that channel. Output dimensions are unchanged.

A grid of 9-walls encloses one or more 4-connected non-9 chambers. Each chamber has colored seed cells and zero cells. Fill every zero from the Manhattan-nearest seed in the same chamber; on an equal-distance color tie, use the smaller color. Walls and seeds stay unchanged.
Several non-touching blobs of distinct sizes/colors; output is colors sorted by size asc.
Find the centered full-height color-5 divider. Preserve the input and copy every non-zero cell from the left panel to the equal-distance cell on the right, keeping its color.
Reflect separate monochrome components in their own square frames; vary shapes, sizes, colors and repeated-color objects.

0-bg grid (h~5-10, w~8-16) with 2-5 ENDPOINT PAIRS placed on distinct rows. Each pair places two SAME-COLOR cells on the SAME ROW at columns c1 < c2 with at least 1 empty cell between them. Different pairs use distinct non-bg colors. Rule: for every row that contains exactly two same-color cells at columns c1 < c2, FILL every cell at columns c1+1 .. c2-1 in that row with the pair's color (CONNECT the endpoints into a solid HORIZONTAL BAR). Endpoints stay; other rows untouched. Net: each pair of isolated row endpoints becomes a continuous colored horizontal line spanning the gap.

A color-8 walled maze has one start (2), goal (3), key (4), locked door (5), and a pair of portals (6). Find the shortest stateful route: collect the key before crossing the door, and entering either portal teleports to the other. Paint only traversed zero cells color 7; preserve all markers.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-11, w ∈ 9-13 FORCED ODD so a center column exists, axis = w//2) with: (a) ONE FULL COLOR-8 (CYAN) DIVIDER COLUMN at col axis (every cell in that column painted 8); (b) COUNT ∈ 5-10 SPARSE SOURCE CELLS placed at random LEFT-HALF positions (cols 0..axis-1), each in a random color drawn from {1..9}\{0, 8}. The RIGHT HALF (cols axis+1..w-1) starts EMPTY. Rule (FOR EACH NON-BG NON-8 CELL ON THE LEFT, COPY IT TO ITS MIRROR POSITION ON THE RIGHT — MIRROR AXIS IS THE COLOR-8 DIVIDER COLUMN; ORIGINAL LEFT CELLS PRESERVED): FIND the full color-8 column → axis position c_axis. For EACH non-bg cell at (r, c) with c < c_axis and color k: COMPUTE mirror position (r, 2*c_axis - c). PAINT g[r][2*c_axis-c] = k. The left source cells and the color-8 divider stay. Net: the left-half pattern is reflected onto the right half across the cyan axis.
Split three square panels at full color-8 columns, infer the unique dihedral transform mapping A to B, then apply it to C.
Scan every original 2x2 window.  Replace its black corner with maroon exactly when the other three cells are yellow; leave all other cells unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains one connected color-2 template and one separate color-1 marker. Normalize the template to its bounding-box offsets, then on a fresh blank grid stamp exactly those offsets in color 8 with the marker as the new bounding-box top-left. The source and marker vanish. Scheduled asymmetric five-cell leftward cases refute mirror-on-left and tetromino-only shortcuts that fit every canonical demonstration.

The top row contains 2-5 distinct nonzero markers. Build a fresh zero grid and fill each marked column with its marker color, erasing all unrelated lower-row input content. Every generated sample includes one lower-row erasure witness in an unmarked column.

On background 0, compare 2..4 same-color endpoint pairs by their aligned span's cell count. Keep only the unique longest span, painted 8. Lessons contrast geometric metrics, winning color ranks, and scan positions.

Use the displacement from the single red(2) marker to the single blue(1) marker. Copy every cell of the connected green(3) tetromino by that vector and paint the translated cells orange(7). Keep the green source, both markers, and the single irrelevant gray(5) decoration unchanged.

A modal-background 13x13 grid contains 2..4 separated irregular color-1 pieces. Marker colors that occur exactly twice, on different pieces, form a connected docking tree. For each pair, infer the outward direction of the first marker and place the other marker one cell beyond it. Assemble every piece without overlap and crop to the completed multicolor object. One extra unmatched marker may remain.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with: (a) ONE COLOR-1 (blue) PROTOTYPE SHAPE drawn from a 5-shape BANK (L-tromino, S-tetromino, T-tetromino, 2×2, J-tetromino); (b) TWO COLOR-2 (red) CANDIDATE SHAPES — ONE is a REFLECTION (identity/flip-lr/flip-ud/rotate-180) of the prototype (equivalent under D2), ONE is a DIFFERENT shape from the bank. All shapes placed non-overlapping with 1-cell padding. Rule (RECOLOR REFLECTION-MATCHING CANDIDATE TO 8): identify the COLOR-1 PROTOTYPE and its normalized cell set. For EACH COLOR-2 candidate: COMPUTE its normalized cell set. CHECK if it equals the prototype under any of {identity, flip-lr, flip-ud, rotate-180}. If YES, RECOLOR that candidate to COLOR-8 (cyan). Non-matching candidates stay color 2. Prototype stays. Net: the red shape shape-equivalent to the blue prototype becomes cyan.

A simple induced four-neighbor path on background 0 has one endpoint 2 and one endpoint 3. Recolor its internal 1-cells by shortest path distance to those seeds; use 4 for equal distances. Exact lengths include both seeds. Orientations, positions, parity and seed order vary.

0-bg grid with: (a) N (1-3) hollow rectangle FRAMES (h≥3, w≥3, cells form only the bbox border); (b) M (1-3) DISTRACTOR shapes — solid rectangles or irregular shapes. All objects in distinct colors. Rule: extract every connected non-bg component. For each, check if it's a frame: h≥3, w≥3, size = perimeter = 2(h+w) - 4, and all cells on bbox border. Keep frames (preserve colors), drop all non-frames. Output: fresh 0-grid with only the frames.
Replace every all-zero row and all-zero column with red 2, preserving all other cells.

On a 7 background, match each cyan(8) left jigsaw piece with the unique colored right piece that completes a solid 3x5 rectangle. Right pieces are permuted across 2-4 bands, with equal-area and row-critical shapes; redraw each completed rectangle at column 0.

Fill a 6..10 by 9..12 grid with a distinct-color 2x2, 2x3, or 3x2 periodic tile, erase one solid interior row- or column-band, then recover the smallest global two-dimensional period and restore every zero cell.

Top 5 rows hold 3 library panels at column offsets {0, 6, 12} (5 cols each); each panel has a distinct non-zero shape in a distinct color. Row 6 has 3 instruction cells: g[6][0]=selector color (matches one library panel), g[6][1]=transform code (1=identity, 2=cw90, 3=180, 4=ccw90, 5=flip-lr), g[6][2]=output recolor. Rule selects the matching library panel, crops to its non-zero bbox, applies the transform, then recolors all non-zero cells to the output color.

A black grid contains two to four cyan local targets with at least two different missing-corner orientations per input. Each target has exactly three cyan corners in a 2x2 window and one black missing corner. Complete every such window by painting only its missing corner cyan. Alternating full-curriculum scenes also contain a cyan line, a complete cyan 2x2 square, and a target joined to one extra cyan tail; those cells do not change unless they participate in an exact three-cyan/one-black 2x2 window.

A 0-background grid contains three or four separated blue objects. Exactly two objects share one shape up to rotation, in visibly different orientations; every distractor has a unique rotational shape class. Normalize all rotations, select the repeated class, render its lexicographically least rotation alone in cyan, and crop to its bbox.
Fill each zero with its nearer red or green Manhattan seed, preserving equal-distance zeros and all nonzero distractors.
Infer a separator-delimited template cell and stamp it into every other cell marked by one or more zero dots.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 12-20, w ∈ 17-26, by difficulty) with: TWO HOLLOW COLOR-5 RECTANGULAR FRAMES each 8×8, anchored at FIXED positions (r0=2, c0=2) and (r0=2, c0=w//2+1) — each frame's interior is 6×6. FOR EACH FRAME: (a) ONE KEY MARKER one row ABOVE the frame's TOP-LEFT CORNER (at row r0-1, col c0+1), value ∈ {6, 7} chosen independently per frame; (b) 2-4 SPARSE INTERIOR CELLS — placed at random non-overlapping interior positions (rows r0+1..r0+6, cols c0+1..c0+6), each painted in ONE non-{0, 5} color drawn per-frame from {2,3,4,6,7,8,9}. Rule (FOR EACH FRAME, USE ITS KEY TO PICK A MIRROR AXIS AND COMPLETE THE INTERIOR PATTERN BY MIRRORING THE CELLS ACROSS THAT AXIS): For EACH color-5 frame: READ its KEY (above top-left). IF KEY = 6: MIRROR each interior cell LEFT↔RIGHT across the frame's vertical center axis (c -> c0 + (c0 + fw - 1 - c)). IF KEY = 7: MIRROR each interior cell TOP↔BOTTOM across the horizontal center axis. The mirrored cell is painted with the SAME color as the source. Original interior cells preserved. Net: each frame's partial pattern is completed into a symmetric pattern across the axis selected by its key.
Multiple red (2) connected components, one uniquely smallest. Rule recolors only the smallest component to blue (1); the others stay red.

0-bg grid with color-5 walls (full divider columns/rows plus connecting segments) carving regions that hold a sparse scatter of color-2 and color-3 markers. Rule: per 4-connected non-5 region, fill its 0-cells with the majority of {2,3} (tie -> 8).

skills: panel splitting, occupancy union, same-size blank output
summary: A full-height maroon(9) divider splits equal left/right panels. Output is cyan(8) exactly where either corresponding panel cell is occupied. Ordinary draws expose blank, left-only, right-only, and overlap cases; same-color overlap periodically distinguishes occupancy union from raw cell-value inequality.
Place 5..10 colored cells in 2..4 columns of a 6..10 grid.  Applying gravity independently to each column packs its cells against the bottom while preserving their top-to-bottom color order.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE connected non-bg blob (a random polyomino, varied bbox 2-7 wide x 2-6 tall, in one color). Rule: crop the blob to its bbox; for each column count the blob's cells; output a grid of width = bbox width and height = max column count, where column c is filled from the bottom with count_c cells of the color (a column-density bar chart). Output dims and the bar pattern both track the blob's shape.

Equal 9x9 panels separated by full color-9 columns. Prototype panels carry distinct key colors at (0,0); the last panel is an unkeyed query. Match the query to the unique prototype with the same complete 4-neighbor onion-layer cell-count histogram and output that prototype's key (1x1). Generated matches are normally non-congruent histogram collisions, with same-area and same-depth distractors to refute shortcut rules.
skills: library lookup, keyed prototypes, histogram matching

summary: On a color-0 background, each active row contains exactly one non-gray seed. The seed paints consecutive zero cells to its right with its own color, stopping at an optional gray (5) wall or at the right boundary. Seeds and walls are preserved. Consecutive sample indices deliberately cycle through mixed, all-blocked, and all-open wall profiles.
Split the even-height input into equal top and bottom halves. For each aligned cell, output yellow (4) when either half is nonzero; output black (0) only when both aligned cells are black.
Draw the rounded DDA line between two red endpoints, mapping path zeros to red and path blues to green.

0-bg grid (h~5-9, w = 2*half_w+1 with half_w~3-5) with: (a) a full-height color-5 DIVIDER column at col = half_w; (b) 3-6 scattered MOTIF cells in some non-{0, 5} color placed strictly LEFT of the divider (cols 1..half_w-1). Rule: detect the color-5 divider. For each non-{0, 5} cell at (r, c), MIRROR it across the divider: paint (r, 2*half_w - c) with the same color. Original cells + divider stay. Net: left motif gets a vertical mirror image on the right side.
Keep only the topmost yellow cell in each column and clear all lower yellow cells.

0-bg grid (h~7-16, w~10-20) with: (a) ROW 0 — n_codes (1-6) NON-ZERO TRANSFORM CODE CELLS at distinct random column positions, each painted with a value 1..4 (transform code); (b) ROW 1 — ALL BG-0 (separator row); (c) ROWS 2..h-1 — a single connected MOTIF (3-5 cell 4-connected blob grown by random adjacency walk) in MOTIF COLOR 8 or 9, placed at a random valid position. Rule (PACK ALL NON-ZERO CONNECTED COMPONENTS INTO A SORTED HORIZONTAL GALLERY): extract every 4-CONNECTED non-bg COMPONENT (including each individual row-0 code cell and the motif). CROP each component to its tight bbox. SORT crops by (WIDTH ASC, HEIGHT ASC, TOP-ROW ASC) — narrowest first, ties broken by shortest, then by original top row position. PACK the sorted crops LEFT-TO-RIGHT with a 1-column bg gap between consecutive crops, BOTTOM-ALIGNED in a tight output grid whose height = max crop height across all components and width = sum of crop widths + (n-1) gaps. Each piece keeps its ORIGINAL COLOR. Net: scattered components and code cells collapse into a horizontal gallery sorted by increasing width.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~11-13) with: (a) TWO REFERENCE BLOBS in 2 DISTINCT non-{0, 8} colors with DISTINCT NORMALIZED SHAPES drawn from {L_TROMINO_NE, L_TROMINO_SE, T_TETROMINO, SQUARE_2X2, V_LINE_3, H_LINE_3}; (b) ONE COLOR-8 (cyan) QUERY BLOB whose normalized shape MATCHES the FIRST REFERENCE blob (placed[0]). All blobs are placed without 4-touching (1-cell padding). Rule (RECOLOR QUERY TO MATCHING REFERENCE, ERASE NON-MATCH): identify the 8-QUERY and the 2 REFERENCE blobs. For each REFERENCE, check if its normalized shape EQUALS the query's. RECOLOR the 8-query in the MATCHING reference's COLOR. ERASE the other (non-matching) reference. Net: query inherits the color of its shape-twin reference; the lone shape vanishes.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-6 shape, a color-8 anchor cell, and one control cell (color 1-4). Rule: rotate the shape (ctrl-1 quarter turns) and stamp it in color 3 at the anchor. The grid size, shape, control rotation and anchor position vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~25 distinct).

An 11x11 color-7 field is divided by color-6 lines into nine 3x3 tiles. Exactly two tiles hold color-2 diamonds. Their relative placement proposes one color-5 and one color-8 diamond, with out-of-bounds proposals clipped, so zero, one, or two diamonds may be added. Any input color-5 or color-8 diamond is contamination and instead yields a 16x16 color-7 output.

Fill a blank cell only when equal nonzero endpoints lie exactly two rows and two columns apart; copy the endpoint color into that diagonal midpoint. Every scene has both diagonal orientations. Consecutive sample indices use overlapping pairs of axis-aligned, wrong-distance/different-color, and blocked-midpoint near misses, so every three-of-four query rotation retains all shortcut witnesses. Every third ordinary sample rehearses a canonical 7x7, 8x8, or 9x9 morphology in every difficulty band; explicit size/count overrides remain authoritative.

Grid with color-5 BORDER (outer ring of walls). Interior is mostly 0-bg with a few scattered 5-walls forming obstacles. Three markers: color-2 (red), color-4 (yellow), color-3 (green) placed at distinct interior positions, all reachable from each other through non-wall cells. Rule: BFS shortest path 2→4 (union of all shortest paths). BFS 4→3. Paint cells on either leg's union with color 8 (only cells that are currently 0). Walls and markers preserved.

0-bg grid (size varies) with N (2-5) separated OBJECTS, each a random connected polyomino of varying SIZE (1-9 cells) in a distinct color, at scattered positions. Rule (SORT BY READING ORDER + ENCODE): sort objects by top-left position (row then col); emit an output grid of N rows x MAX_size cols where row i is the i-th object's color repeated by its size (left-justified, padded with 0). Output dims = (object count) x (max object size), both varying. Rule reads only each object's color and size.

Preserve a connected green (3) template and stamp its untransformed 3x3 or 3x4 binary crop into an isolated matching solid cyan (8) canvas. Template holes become zero in the canvas. Roles follow fixed colors; object positions vary in all four quadrants on a zero background.
Connect the unique red(2) and green(3) cells with an 8-colored L: paint horizontally from red to green's column, then vertically to green.

Four distinct singleton colors mark the four grid corners. Each other monochromatic 4-connected object is recolored by the marker nearest its tight bounding-box center, measured with doubled Manhattan coordinates. Exact ties choose top, then left. Every five-draw schedule includes two canonical-scale examples and three asymmetric center-line witnesses that separate this rule from anchor, centroid, nearest-pixel, and opposite-tie shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-2 SHAPE and ONE color-3 SHAPE, placed apart, defined over a shared k x k frame by a random per-cell membership: every cell belongs to shape-2, shape-3, both, or neither; both shapes span the full frame (so the rule's independent normalization keeps them aligned) and at least one cell belongs to BOTH. Plus a color-4 NOISE cell the rule ignores. Rule: normalize each shape to its bbox, INTERSECT the two cell sets, and output the intersection bbox-cropped in COLOR 8 (cyan). The grid size, the two shapes and their positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed shapes + grid padding).
(0,0) selects a body colour and (0,w-1) selects cw/180/flip-LR/identity; transform the selected tight crop and transparently center it in the hollow colour-8 frame after clearing every other cell.

0-bg grid (size varies) holding 2-4 color-5 RECTANGULAR FRAMES of varied size/position. Each frame has a single KEY color cell in the row just above it; inside, some interior ROWS carry color-2 markers on both inner side columns and some interior COLS carry color-3 markers on both inner top/bottom rows. Rule: per frame, paint each (marked-row x marked-col) crossing inside the frame with that frame's key color.

On a color-0 grid, inspect each row independently and count each non-zero color separately. If a color occurs exactly twice in that row, paint its inclusive horizontal interval in that color on a fresh zero output. Other marks vanish. Multiple disjoint exact-pair colors may fill in one row; blockers inside a qualifying span are overwritten; singleton and triple controls are erased.

Exactly five equal panels separated by single full-height color-9 columns. Panels 1 and 2 demonstrate one support operation by producing panel 3 in color 2; panels 4 and 5 are a new query pair.  Infer the unique operation from union/intersection/xor/A-minus-B/B-minus-A and apply it to the query. Every generated operand pair contains overlap, A-only, B-only, and empty cells, so all five operations are distinguishable and non-empty.

Complete partial monochrome icons after 8-connectivity plus one-cell cardinal bridge clustering. Squares use 4-fold rotation, rectangles use LR/UD reflection in an expanded odd box, and supported odd-square centers are filled. The two-slot curriculum alternates canonical dimension/palette profiles with a six-witness teaching mixture that refutes bridge, rectangle, even-square, center-support, and full-dihedral shortcuts.
Recolor each yellow component by its enclosed-background-hole count: 0 holes -> 2, 1 hole -> 3, 2 holes -> 8; preserve the optional color-6 domino distractor.
1-5 isolated colored cells; rule stamps a plus shape (cell + 4 cardinal neighbors) in the cell's color.
Separated solid 2x2 color blocks reduce to their top-left/bottom-right diagonal.

An 8..10 by 10..13 zero-background grid contains one connected color-1 shape, one connected color-2 shape, and one isolated singleton marker. Normalize each shape to its own bbox. Marker 3 selects intersection, marker 4 selects union, and marker 5..9 selects symmetric difference. Crop the selected nonempty result to its bbox and paint it color 8. Normalized shapes overlap but are nonidentical; both partial-overlap and strict-subset relations are generated, and all three operation outputs are observably distinct.

A 0-background grid contains 1-2 hollow same-color objects in distinct colors: canonical rectangular frames and, in one scheduled profile, an exact rectangular frame with one outward spur. It may also contain one visually similar rectangle with a single non-corner wall gap. Fill every zero cell topologically enclosed by each hollow object with that object's color; preserve existing cells and leave the open decoy unchanged.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-13, w ∈ 9-13, by difficulty) with: N_COLORS ∈ 3-4 DISTINCT non-bg colors drawn from {1..9}, each appearing EXACTLY TWICE as ISOLATED single cells (no two non-bg cells within Chebyshev-distance 1, enforced via _too_close). Generation retries up to 40 outer attempts until all pairs placed cleanly. Rule (FOR EACH COLOR-PAIR, DRAW BOTH POSSIBLE 'ELBOW' PATHS BETWEEN ITS TWO ENDPOINTS (GO HORIZONTAL-THEN-VERTICAL OR VERTICAL-THEN-HORIZONTAL); PER CELL, COUNT HOW MANY ELBOW PATHS PASS THROUGH; OUTPUT A FRESH SAME-SIZE GRID WHERE EACH CELL'S VALUE ENCODES THE OVERLAY COUNT: 1→COLOR 2, 2→COLOR 3, 3+→COLOR 4, ELSE 0): For EACH color pair (p1, p2): GENERATE the 2 elbow paths between p1 and p2 (one with horizontal-then-vertical, one with vertical-then-horizontal). For EACH cell along these paths: INCREMENT its overlay count. PRODUCE output: count=0→0, count=1→2 (red), count=2→3 (green), count≥3→4 (yellow). Net: dense intersections appear in brighter colors; sparse paths in red.
Same-color vertical endpoints with zeros between are bridged.
Complete conflict-free partial main-diagonal symmetry while preserving all source colors.

Sparse 0-background grids teach a local diagonal relation.  Every lawful input has at least one three-cell diagonal chain and remaining two- or three-cell diagonal components in distinct colors, with a contrastive erased pattern.  A four-slot schedule cycles canonical singleton, remote same-color singleton, cardinal same-color pair, and their combination; every three-demo window refutes the declared global-frequency and 8-neighbour shortcuts.

Several hollow gray (5) rectangular frames appear. Exactly one frame contains exactly one colored marker cell; fill only that frame's zero interior cells with that marker color. Frames with zero or multiple marker cells remain unchanged.

Preserve every original non-zero cell and fill each zero cell from its up/down mirror when that mirror is non-zero. A four-example curriculum covers canonical bottom stacks, top sources, both source directions, and multiple conflicting non-zero mirror pairs whose original colors remain fixed.

0-bg grid with h ∈ {3..14} and ODD WIDTH w ∈ {5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15} so the middle column mid = w//2 is well-defined: (a) ACTIVE ROWS — selected by one of 4 distributions (all_active / half_active / few_active / alternating_inactive). For each active row r: set g[r][0] = LEFT_COLOR and g[r][w-1] = RIGHT_COLOR (LEFT ≠ RIGHT, both non-{0, 5}); (b) OPTIONAL DECOY CELLS scattered in interior columns (1..w-2) at density 0..0.2 with random colors. If no rows are active, force row 0 active. Rule (FOR EACH ROW WITH NON-ZERO LEFT+RIGHT EDGES, CREATE LEFT/RIGHT BANDS SPLIT BY COLOR 5 AT THE MIDDLE COLUMN): for EACH ROW r where g[r][0] = lv ≠ 0 AND g[r][w-1] = rv ≠ 0: REPLACE the row: for c < mid: cell = lv; for c == mid: cell = 5; for c > mid: cell = rv. Non-active rows are unchanged (interior decoys stay). Net: each active row becomes a 3-zone band — left color, gray center, right color — replacing any interior decoys in that row.

A 9..26 zero-background grid contains 3..7 complete red diamonds. Consecutive centers sharing a row or column are connected through zero cells by blue lines. Alternating default lessons include an irregular three-arm false-center witness that refutes axis-local marker recognition.

0-bg grid (size varies) with EXACTLY 2 isolated 4-connected MOTIFS in distinct non-0 colors (3-6 cells each), placed apart by >=1 bg cell. The two motifs' NORMALIZED shapes are mutually non-subset. Rule: take the first 2 objects sorted by bbox (col, then row); A = leftmost/topmost. Normalize each; output a max(h_a,h_b) x max(w_a,w_b) grid with A's cells that are NOT in B painted in A's color, rest 0. Net: set-difference A-minus-B of the two aligned shapes, in A's color.

On a 6x12 black grid, find every maximal same-color horizontal nonzero run independently. Recolor its left and right endpoints to 1, including singleton and length-two runs, while preserving every longer interior cell.

Exactly three separated monochromatic 4-connected objects with distinct cell areas. The rule tightly crops the objects, sorts by cell count ascending, and top-aligns them left-to-right with one blank column gap. A five-profile schedule anchors canonical scale and refutes common position, color, bbox-area, alignment, fill, and grouping shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-14) with 6-12 SPARSE COLOR-1 (blue) DOTS placed according to a layout pattern: scattered/clustered/row_focus/col_focus/diagonal/corners. At least one row AND one column has ≥2 blue dots with gap between them. Rule (BRACKETED-FILL WITH COLOR 8): for EACH 0-CELL at (r, c), check if there are COLOR-1 cells on BOTH SIDES in the SAME ROW (i.e., some c1 < c with g[r][c1]==1 AND some c2 > c with g[r][c2]==1) OR if there are COLOR-1 cells on BOTH SIDES in the SAME COLUMN. If yes, FILL the cell with COLOR 8 (cyan). Otherwise leave 0. Blue dots stay. Net: every 0-cell bracketed by blue in its row OR column gets painted cyan.
Keep only the midpoint of each odd-length horizontal run.
Find nonzero 4-connected components, crop them, order by original left edge then top row, and pack the crops left-to-right with one zero column.

0-bg grid (size varies) with: (a) a color-1 MARKER in the top-left 2x2 (its position encodes a rotation k: (0,0)->0, (0,1)->1, (1,1)->2, (1,0)->3); (b) one connected color-2 STENCIL (3-6 cells); (c) one SINGLE color-4 ANCHOR cell. Rule: rotate the stencil's normalized cells by k and paint them in color 8 onto a fresh blank grid at the anchor position. Output dims = input dims; only the rotated stamp (color 8) is drawn.

Mostly-7 grid (size varies) with an all-0 separator row/column and two marker rows holding color-8 markers. Rule: per column, both markers -> clear both to 7 and zero the two opposite-end rows; one marker -> fill the other. The grid size, per-column marker pattern and orientation vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~25 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~11-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-1 SOURCE ANCHOR at (ar1, ac1) (interior) surrounded by 3-4 COLOR-2 STENCIL CELLS at one of 5 hardcoded OFFSET PATTERNS (e.g., [(-1,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)] etc.); (b) ONE COLOR-3 TARGET ANCHOR at (ar3, ac3) far from the source (≥2-cell radius padding) where the same offsets fit in-bounds. Rule (COPY COLOR-2 STENCIL FROM 1-ANCHOR TO 3-ANCHOR PRESERVING OFFSETS): identify the COLOR-1 SOURCE ANCHOR at (ar1, ac1) and its STENCIL OFFSETS = positions of COLOR-2 cells relative to it. Identify the COLOR-3 TARGET ANCHOR at (ar3, ac3). For EACH OFFSET (dr, dc) of color-2 cells, PAINT COLOR-2 at (ar3 + dr, ac3 + dc). Source + target anchors stay. Net: red stencil around 1-anchor replicates around 3-anchor with same shape.
Use the unique modal color as background. Recolor every non-background 4-connected component of size greater than one to cyan (8), while leaving isolated singleton cells unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains exactly two separated 4-connected motifs in distinct non-{0,8} colors. Normalize each motif to its bounding-box top-left and overlay the first two scan-order objects: shared cells become 8, first-only cells keep the first color, and second-only cells keep the second color. Every generated lesson contains all three supports.

0-bg grid where: col 0 has a vertical color-5 SEGMENT (rows 0..gh-1 are 5, rest 0). Cols cs..w-1 (cs ≥ 2) each contain non-{0, 5} color cells (typically full columns). Cols 1..cs-1 are all 0. Rule: detect gh (length of col-0 5-segment), cs (first non-{0, 5} col). Build OUTPUT col oc = cs - 1: for each row r, set g[r][oc] = g[0][cs + (r // gh) % n] where n = w - cs (number of right cols, cycling through them). Output preserves col 0 5-segment, clears other cells.
Sort complete separator-delimited red column groups into their original slots by increasing zero-hole count.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-13) with EXACTLY 3 separated components: the SMALLEST is a VARIED random polyomino (2-4 cells, varied form and colour) and two strictly-larger random objects ensure it is uniquely smallest. Rule: find the smallest connected component by cell count, crop it to its bbox, output that crop (colour preserved). Varied smallest shapes+colours -> varied cropped output.

Count the leading colour-8 cells in the top row (N). Find the sole non-zero data row below the full colour-5 separator. Keep data-row colours occurring exactly N times and repeat that filtered row in the N rows immediately above the separator.

Read header cells (panel index, transform code, fill color, border color); select one of three 5x5 library shapes, crop-normalize it, apply transform code 0..5, recolor every occupied cell to the fill color, and surround the result with a one-cell rectangular border.

7-bg grid whose rows mix three kinds: ACTIVE rows with exactly one color-6 anchor plus other non-7 cells, DECOY rows with non-7 cells but no 6, and EMPTY all-7 rows. Rule: per row, if a 6 is present among the non-7 cells, paint an 8-bar whose length is the non-7 count, starting at c6 - idx where idx is the 6's column-rank among the non-7 cells; everything else becomes 7.
Square grids with sparse content on and above the diagonal.
One-step plus growths from color-2 and color-3 groups overlap into contact cells.

Two color-5 guides share a row or column. Same-row guides select a top-to-bottom full-grid reflection; same-column guides select a left-to-right reflection. A varied motif occupies only the source half and the selected Racket rule completes its mirror while preserving the guides.

15 × w grid (w ~3-14), composed of THREE stacked 5-row PANELS at rows 0-4, 5-9, 10-14. Each panel uses values from {0, 1, 6, 8} in some pattern (random/blob/stripes/checker/border/diagonal/scatter). Rule: output = 5 × w grid. For each (r, c) in output, look at the 3 stacked cells g[r][c], g[r+5][c], g[r+10][c]. Compute the cell by priority OR: if ANY of the 3 is 6 → output 6; else if ANY is 1 → output 1; else if ANY is 8 → output 8; else → 0. Net effect: 3-way overlay with color precedence 6 > 1 > 8 > 0.

0-bg SQUARE grid (n ∈ 7-14, h = w = n, by difficulty) with: N_CELLS ∈ 3-12 NON-ZERO CELLS in 1-4 DISTINCT COLORS drawn per PALETTE_KIND ∈ {warm / cool / broad / primary}, placed per POSITION_BIAS ∈ {scattered (random in upper half) / tight (top-left corner) / diagonal (main diagonal) / row_aligned (one row)}. Cells lie in the upper half of the grid so the rotated copies fit. The bbox center of the non-zero cells is at integer coordinates. Rule (COMPUTE THE BBOX CENTER OF ALL NON-ZERO CELLS; FOR EACH NON-ZERO CELL, PAINT IT AT 4 ROTATED POSITIONS — 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° — AROUND THE BBOX CENTER): COMPUTE bbox center (cr, cc). For EACH non-zero cell at (r, c) with color k: ROTATE (r - cr, c - cc) by 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° → 4 (dr, dc) offsets. PAINT cells (cr + dr_i, cc + dc_i) = k for i ∈ 0..3 (in-bounds). Original cells preserved (as the i=0 rotation). Net: input pattern is replicated by 4-fold rotational symmetry around the bbox center.

For each separated nonzero connected object, erase all of its cells and paint exactly the four corners of that object's bounding box in the object's original color; object identity is determined by connectivity, not merely by color, and the rule applies to L shapes, zigzags, and other connected shapes alike.

Grid h×9 (h~4-6, w=9 fixed) with 0-bg and: (a) ONE FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-5 (gray) DIVIDER COLUMN at col 4 (middle); (b) 2-3 ISOLATED non-{0, 5} CELLS in the LEFT SIDE (cols 0..3) at random rows in random colors from {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9}. Right side (cols 5..8) is all 0. Rule (MIRROR LEFT ACROSS DIVIDER): for EACH non-{0, 5} CELL at (r, c) on the LEFT side (c < 4), COMPUTE its MIRROR position (r, 8 - c) (or equivalently (r, w - 1 - c)) on the RIGHT side. PAINT the mirror cell with the SAME COLOR. The divider stays. Left cells stay. Net: left-side cells are mirrored across the gray divider to the right side.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 4-18, by difficulty) with: each ROW INDEPENDENTLY assigned a KIND per ROW_DISTRIBUTION ∈ {uniform, biased_match, biased_mismatch, alternating}: (a) 'match' → g[r][0] = g[r][w-1] = SAME color drawn from palette; (b) 'mismatch' → g[r][0] = a, g[r][w-1] = b (different colors); (c) 'blank' → both left and right are 0. Palette of 2-6 distinct colors drawn from {1..9}. INTERIOR DECOY DENSITY ∈ 0-20% sprinkles random colored cells in non-edge columns. Generation guarantees ≥1 matching-row exists. Rule (FOR EACH ROW r: IF g[r][0] != 0 AND g[r][0] == g[r][w-1]: FILL THE ENTIRE ROW (ALL w COLUMNS) WITH THAT COLOR; ELSE: KEEP THE ROW AS-IS): For EACH row r: READ g[r][0] and g[r][w-1]. IF both are non-zero AND equal: PAINT every cell of that row with that color. OTHERWISE: row unchanged. Net: matching-pair rows fill solidly with their edge color; mismatch and blank rows stay.

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0,0) holds a COMMAND in {1..7}; the rest of the grid holds ONE MOTIF: a random multi-color pattern with a NON-SQUARE bounding box (bh != bw, each 2-4, 2-3 colors, every bbox edge touched so the crop is exact). Rule: read the command; crop-to-content of the rest; apply the transform (1=identity, 2=rotate-cw, 3=rotate-180, 4=transpose, 5=flip-lr, 6=flip-ud, else=transpose). Output = the transformed motif (dims swap under rotate/transpose). The non-square bbox makes every command distinguishable.

A zero-background odd-width grid has one centered full-height color-8 vertical fold bar. Compare each nonzero left cell with its reflected right-side cell. Emit a same-size zero grid containing only equal-color matches, painted at the reflected right-side positions. Wrong-color pairs, empty mirrors, and right-only distractors disappear. Five scheduled profiles expose those distinctions and refute occupancy, mirror-all, wrong-side, copy-right, global-color-presence, and row-local color-presence shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies). (a) a RANDOM connected SHAPE (4-8 cells) in one main color (not 0/2/3) in the upper/left region; (b) a color-2 (red) FOLD LINE parallel to the shape and offset by a small distance, perpendicular to the reflection axis, with room for the reflected copy. Rule: detect the main-color shape + the red fold line; REFLECT the shape across the fold (axis from the red cells); paint (shape ∪ fold ∪ reflection) the main color and every other cell 3. Output dims = input dims (now vary). Net: the shape folds across the red line, red merges into the main color, background becomes 3.

Read three distinct rank colors left-to-right in row 0. Rank three separated monochrome body components by descending area, then bounding-box top and left ascending. Recolor their crops in rank order and stack with one blank row, centered with floor((maximum width - piece width)/2). Ties, narrow and wide crops, shape variation, and positional tie witnesses are ordinary generated inputs.

0-bg grid with: (a) ONE KEY cell at (0,0) in color {1, 2, 3, 4+} specifying the boolean op (1=union, 2=intersection, 3=xor, else=a-minus-b); (b) EXACTLY 2 connected components A and B in the rest of the grid, in distinct non-{0, key} colors. A is placed leftmost (smaller leftmost col); B is rightmost. Both have the same bbox dimensions (so the boolean op is well-defined). Rule: apply the boolean op (key-determined) on the binary masks of A and B. Output is the resulting shape painted in color 8 (cropped to its bbox).
Recolor every gray 8-connected component containing a diagonal run of length at least three.

A 0-background grid contains two or three differently colored connected objects whose bounding boxes share an overlap. For every output cell, count the object bounding boxes containing that coordinate. A four-profile cycle includes nested frames, nested sparse L-shapes, crossing sparse boxes, and a crossing frame/sparse mixture so frame-only and nesting-only shortcuts are explicitly contradicted.

0-bg grid (size varies). 1-3 color-5 (gray) hollow rectangular FRAMES (>=5 per side so each interior is >=3x3) at random sizes/positions, placed apart. Each frame interior holds one color-2 (red) SEED and 0-2 color-6 (magenta) BLOCKERS; an optional distractor sits outside. Rule: from each seed emit 4 DIAGONAL RAYS painting color 8 (the seed becomes 8 too), bounded by the frame interior and stopping at color-6 blockers (preserved) and the frame border. The grid size, frame count, frame sizes/positions, seed positions and blockers all vary freely (was a fixed 8x15 grid with 5 blocker presets).
Fill every seeded blue frame; vary positive marker counts and preserve exterior red markers.

0-bg grid (h, w = fh+2 × fw+2 with fh, fw ∈ [6, 8]) with: (a) ONE HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME at (1, 1)..(fh, fw) painted in a chosen FRAME COLOR (non-{0, seed_color}); (b) ONE SEED CELL at interior position (sr, sc) inside the frame in a SEED COLOR distinct from the frame color and 0. Rule (CHECKERBOARD-LIKE PARITY-FILL FROM SEED USING SEED AND FRAME COLORS): for EACH 0-CELL INSIDE the frame's interior at (r, c): compute MANHATTAN DISTANCE d = |r - sr| + |c - sc| from the seed. PAINT (r, c) with SEED COLOR if d is EVEN, with FRAME COLOR if d is ODD (or alternate per puzzle convention). The frame border and seed stay. Net: the interior is filled with a checkerboard pattern of seed/frame colors centered on the seed.

Use exact 4-connected orange(7) component membership: recolor an orange component blue(1) iff it contains one of the four grid-corner cells. A color-5 corner marker and near-corner orange decoys remain unchanged.

Split an even grid into four equal quadrants. In every quadrant, choose the uniquely most frequent non-background color (background 0 is ignored), then place the four selected colors in a 2x2 spatial summary.

Five equal-width panels split by four full-height color-8 columns. A, B, and O demonstrate the first matching reachable operation in canonical order union/intersection/xor; apply it to X and Y and emit a binary 0/1 grid. Normal draws contain every binary relation in both operand pairs, making the operation and query answer identifiable.
Orange components touching exactly one outer border are recolored cyan.

A 13..24 by 17..24 grid has an arbitrary top-left background and 3..6 colored corner glyphs.  A glyph's bounding-box maximum dimension assigns it to the smallest available odd ring that fits (loose fits before exact fits, then exact fits largest-first); its longest corner arm controls how much of each output-ring corner is colored.  Shape placement is randomized so row-major appearance does not reveal ring order.

A color-8 background contains exactly two solid rectangular non-8 panels, separated horizontally or vertically. The SOURCE panel contains one non-{0,4,8} marker embedded in a connected yellow shape; the TARGET panel contains a second marker of the same color and no yellow. Crop the target panel and translate every yellow source offset so the source marker aligns with the target marker.
Read the nonzero color at the top-left cell and the first black marker; return the same-size uniform field with both diagonals through that marker painted black.

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0,0) holds a COLOR KEY.
