On a 0-background grid, recolor every 0 whose immediate left and right neighbours are both color 1 to color 2. The test is horizontal, local, and evaluated from the input grid. Longer horizontal gaps, pure vertical 1-0-1 triples, and unrelated colored cells stay unchanged. Generated lessons rotate through isolated targets, overlapping 1-0-1-0-1 chains, left/right boundary targets, and a mixed scene; every scene also contains a wider horizontal-gap control and a vertical control.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 2-3 BLOBS — each a 2-4 cell 4-connected blob grown via grow_blob, painted in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {1..9}. Blobs are placed at non-touching positions with non-overlapping bboxes (tracked in used set). Each blob has bbox ≥ 2×2 (size ≥ 2 ensures the checker pattern is visible). Rule (FILL EACH BLOB'S BBOX WITH A CHECKER PATTERN IN THE BLOB'S COLOR): for EACH 4-CONNECTED non-bg blob of color C: COMPUTE its bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2). For EACH cell (r, c) in the bbox: PAINT (r, c) with COLOR C if (r + c) parity matches the bbox's top-left parity (checker pattern starting with C at (r1, c1)); ELSE leave as bg-0. The original blob cells are absorbed into the checker fill. Net: each irregular blob inflates into a checker pattern within its bbox, in its color.

A rectangular 0-background grid contains exactly one contiguous, single-color bar on row 0, touching either the left or right edge. Let its color be k and length be L. The output is the row-major wrapping of colored run lengths 1,2,...,L,L-1,...,2,1, with exactly one 0 between successive runs; the final output row is padded with 0s to the input width. The input height and bar position do not alter the run sequence.
Recolor each monochrome 4-component by bounding-box aspect: wide->2, tall->3, square->4. Varied connected shapes, repeated colors across aspects, 8..14 by 9..14 canvases, and 3..6 objects.
Fill zero centers with four equal nonzero cardinal neighbors.

Below the full yellow separator, select the uniquely more frequent color as the main shape. Move its complete color mask to the top in the same columns, clear the lower half, and move the other color immediately left of and vertically centered on the main bounding box.
Several solid rectangles; rule replaces each with its perimeter outline (same color).

0-bg grid (h~11-13, w~13-15) with multiple ISOLATED color-3 (green) connected components. EXACTLY ONE is VERTICALLY (LR-mirror) SYMMETRIC — its normalized cells are invariant under flip-lr. The other 1-2 components are ASYMMETRIC under that mirror. Components are buffered by ≥1 bg cell on all sides. Rule: scan color-3 objects in scan order. Pick the FIRST one whose normalized cells are LR-mirror symmetric. Compute its scaled offsets at factor 2 (each cell becomes a 2×2 block). Output is a small grid sized to fit the scaled cells, painted color 8 (cyan).
Generate separated, non-rectangular 8-connected objects, including both an edge-touching and an interior object in every default scene. Fill each object's bounding-box background cells with color 7.

An 8..16 by 8..16 zero-background grid contains two to four separated, monochrome 4-connected components. Exactly one component has the largest area (4..6 cells); every other component is strictly smaller. The output copies only that uniquely largest component in its original position and color and turns every smaller component into background 0.

Each row has an optional header color in column 0 + zero or more color-1 markers in cols 1..w-1. Rule: for rows with header AND exactly ONE marker, recolor the marker to the header color and clear the header. Other rows unchanged.

0-background grid with 2-5 same-color L-trominoes.  Each object has three cells in a 2x2 bounding box; differently colored objects may touch and some draws place one object in another object's missing corner.  Complete every colored L to its 2x2 square using that object's color, overwriting an occupied missing corner when necessary.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-11) with 2-3 color PAIRS — each pair = two cells of the same color at random positions with Manhattan distance ≥3. Pairs may be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal/skew. Different pairs use distinct colors. Rule: for each color appearing exactly twice, draw a BRESENHAM-style LINE SPAN between the two endpoints, painting every intermediate cell along the line with the SAME color. Endpoints stay. Net: each pair becomes a continuous straight or staircase line.
Recolor the uniquely leftmost yellow object green.

Use the connected color-6 object as a template.  At each of the four single-cell anchors, stamp a centered copy rotated according to the anchor color: 1 = identity, 2 = clockwise 90°, 3 = 180°, 4 = counterclockwise 90°.  Output only the four color-6 stamps.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~9-13 by ~11-16) with: (a) a 'WINNING FAMILY' of 2-4 connected components that SHARE the same normalized shape (e.g., all L-shaped, all 2×2 squares), each in a DIFFERENT non-zero color; (b) 1-2 'distractor' components in OTHER normalized shapes (and distinct colors). All components are 8-conn isolated. The winning family is strictly larger than any other family. Rule: group components by normalized shape. Pick the family with the MOST members. Sort the family by bbox top-left (row asc, col asc). Pack them horizontally with 1-cell gaps. Output height = max bbox height of family members. Each member's color is preserved in its slot.

A zero-background grid contains two or three separate 7x7 hollow orange frames. Each frame is an independent workspace: red cells on its left inner axis select rows, green cells on its top inner axis select columns, and a local non-marker color inside the frame is that frame's fill key. Paint every selected-row x selected-column intersection with the local key color, preserving all existing cells.
Exactly three separated, distinct-color 4-connected objects have distinct areas.  Their spatial order varies independently of size rank.
Fill the empty midpoint of every same-color pair separated by (2,+/-2); preserve all existing cells.

A zero-background grid contains two to four separated, non-rectangular red (2) components plus one to three isolated decorative cells. For each red component independently, recolor and fill its complete bounding box green (3), preserving every decorative cell.

Place 2-6 separated monochrome components on a zero background.  Every ordinary draw contains at least one irregular component whose tight bounding box has holes and at least one singleton or straight component whose bounding box is already full.  Some scenes reuse one color on two distant components.  The oracle independently fills each 4-connected component's tight bounding box with that component's color.

Find the unique color-9 anchor. Rotate every other nonzero cell 90 degrees clockwise around that anchor, preserve each cell's color, write the result on a fresh color-0 canvas, and do not copy the anchor.

Rows 0 and 1 are an aligned old-color→new-color key. Drop those two rows and recolor the sparse body once by the column-wise mapping. The curriculum interleaves all three canonical size/palette profiles with scattered late key columns and overlapping mappings so fixed-first-three and cascading shortcuts are explicitly falsified.

Rows 0 and 1 contain aligned nonzero source->target legend pairs; row 2 is all-zero separation. Crop away those three rows. In the remaining canvas replace each legend source color by its paired target and preserve 0 plus any color absent from the legend.
Crop the unique largest multicolor rectangle; paste every smaller multicolor rectangle into it where that piece's shared marker-color pattern aligns exactly, processing pieces largest first.
Sparse colored seeds smear downward through background until the first non-background blocker or the lower edge; color 5 is a passive wall.

Read the command at (0,0). Command 1 overlays a left-right reflection of every other nonzero cell; command 2 overlays an up-down reflection. Preserve the source pattern, every cell color, and the command cell.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~7-10) with 3-6 non-zero cells placed exclusively in the LEFT HALF (cols 0..w//2-1) in varied colors. RIGHT HALF (cols w//2..w-1) is all 0. Rule: for each cell (r, c) in output: if c < w//2 → keep input[r][c]. Else → mirror = input[r][w-1-c] (left-half value at the mirrored column). Net effect: the right half becomes a horizontal mirror image of the left half; result is a horizontally-symmetric grid.
Cross of 8s + TL pattern; rule mirrors 4-fold + replaces colors with 8.
2-3 LR-asymmetric blobs (so flip-lr changes them).
1-2 isolated non-bg cells in distinct colors.
Sparse cells on bg=0; rule applies gravity-down per column (stack at bottom).

A 4..6 by 5..8 grid contains gray(5) walls and exactly two terminals of one other color. Starting from the row-major first terminal, paint the BFS path selected by neighbour order Up, Down, Left, Right on an otherwise black output. Three scheduled profiles cover canonical scale, broad geometry, and a tie that distinguishes the ordered BFS rule. A staggered witness guarantees that rotating any one of four consecutive pairs into the query still leaves a counterexample in the demonstrations.
Non-wall colored cells cast horizontal or vertical shadows to an 8-wall row/column.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~10-14) with 3-5 ISOLATED 4-conn components, each in a distinct non-bg color and with a STRICTLY DISTINCT cell count (sizes drawn from {1..7}). Components are separated by background. Rule: extract all 4-conn non-bg components. Sort them by size DESCENDING (with each size unique by construction). Output is a 1×N row where N = number of components, each cell = the color of the corresponding component in size-rank order. Net: a histogram-by-rank single-row encoding.

A zero-background grid has three to six active columns. Each active column uses its own nonzero color and contains a scattered set of cells. For each column independently, count the nonzero cells and replace them with a solid bottom-aligned bar of the same height and color in that same column; empty columns stay empty.

0-bg grid (h, w ~9-12) with 2 color-1 (blue) 4-conn objects of different sizes plus a color-5 (gray) distractor single cell. Rule: identify all color-1 objects, pick the LARGEST by cell count, compute its bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2), and paint the 4 BBOX CORNERS (r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2) with color 2 (red). Note: those corners may already be color 1 if the object touches its bbox — they get overwritten to 2. Rest of grid stays unchanged.

A zero-background grid contains exactly three separated green objects. Two have the same translation-normalized shape and one is the singleton. Draw a yellow one-cell rectangular border just outside the singleton's bounding box while leaving all green cells unchanged.  A four-profile curriculum cycles a rotation-equivalent singleton, a same-area but shape-different singleton, a smaller singleton, and a larger singleton; the singleton also cycles through first/middle/last spatial order.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-12) with: (a) 2-4 ACTIVE ROWS each containing EXACTLY 2 COLOR-1 (blue) CELLS at distinct columns c0 < c1 with c1 - c0 ≥ 2 (so there's a fillable gap between them); (b) 0 to (count // 2) DISTRACTOR rows each containing exactly 1 blue cell (singleton, not a pair). Active rows and singleton rows are mutually exclusive. Rule: for EACH ROW independently, COUNT its color-1 cells. If COUNT == 2, FILL every cell between the two endpoints (inclusive) with COLOR 1. If COUNT == 0, 1, or 3+, leave the row UNCHANGED. Net: rows with exactly 2 blue endpoints get the gap filled in blue; singleton/empty rows stay; no other colors involved.
Select the unique largest red(2) and green(3) 4-connected components independently, recolor them to 4 and 1, and erase all decoys.

0-bg grid (h~10-16, w~12-18) with: (a) ONE FULL COLOR-4 (yellow) SEPARATOR COLUMN at sep_col (position bias: center/spread/edge); (b) a LEFT SHAPE of width k (3-4) × height left_h (2-4) in some color from the palette (non-4), placed in the left half; (c) a RIGHT SHAPE of same width k × height right_h (2-4) in a distinct color in the right half. Shape density 0.5-0.9 — both shapes have 4 corner cells set + extra cells scattered inside. Rule (VCONCAT CROPPED HALVES): identify the FULL 4-COL SEPARATOR. CROP the LEFT HALF (cols 0..sep_col-1) to its non-bg CONTENT BBOX. CROP the RIGHT HALF (cols sep_col+1..w-1) to its non-bg CONTENT BBOX. VCONCAT (stack vertically) the two crops (left on top, right below). Widths must match (both = k). Output height = left_h + right_h, width = k. Net: 4-separator drives a vertical stack of left then right cropped shapes.
Four square panels: an example transform pair followed by a query merge pair.
Row 0 has 4 markers + body has 4 distinct-size blobs.

Use the top-left 2x2 as a sparse motif, erase every 9-marker, and stamp the motif's nonzero cells at each marker anchor. Default draws preserve the five demonstrated joint profiles while varying colors and positions.
Top key row + one border-touching base blob, with interior distractor blobs.
A central color-5 pivot and 1-3 distinctly colored seeds define disjoint fourfold rotation orbits to complete.

0-bg grid (h, w ~ 8-18) with 4-CONNECTED OBJECTS in 2 categories: (a) BORDER OBJECTS — 1-3 components placed at the GRID BORDER (touching row 0, row h-1, col 0, or col w-1), shapes drawn from a 6-shape bank (L_tromino / rect_2x2 / single / line / L_5cell / blob); (b) INTERIOR OBJECTS — 1-3 components placed strictly INTERIOR (not touching any border), same shape bank, placed via place_no_overlap with 1-cell margin. Each object painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 2, 8} color drawn from a 3-5 color palette. Rule (RECOLOR BY BORDER-TOUCHING STATUS — BORDER OBJECTS → COLOR 2, INTERIOR OBJECTS → COLOR 8): for EACH 4-CONNECTED non-bg COMPONENT: CHECK if any cell of the component lies on the grid BORDER (row 0, row h-1, col 0, or col w-1). IF YES: RECOLOR every cell of the component to COLOR 2 (red). IF NO (fully interior): RECOLOR to COLOR 8 (cyan). Net: border objects unify in red; interior objects unify in cyan; topology of which objects touch the border emerges visually.
Find every nonzero 8-connected object, split its bounding box across the longer axis, and return only its color-9 cells shifted one cell outward from that split.

skills: room graph, neighbor expansion, multi-target highlight
summary: A closed 2-D lattice of rectangular rooms is separated by color-1/9 walls. Color-7 doors define room-graph edges and one room contains a color-2 seed. Preserve the walls, clear all rooms, and fill exactly the rooms one door away from the seed with color 8.

0-bg grid with: (a) exactly one color-1 cell (source anchor); (b) exactly one color-2 cell (destination anchor); (c) one or more shapes in colors other than {0, 1, 2} (e.g. one connected blob in some color, OR multiple separate cells). Rule: compute translation (dr, dc) = pos(2) - pos(1). On a FRESH 0-grid, for every non-{0,1,2} input cell at (r, c) with value v, paint (r + dr, c + dc) with v if in-bounds (else drop). The two anchor cells (1 and 2) do NOT appear in the output; only the translated non-anchor cells are kept.

Find the blue template, rotate it clockwise according to the lone control (2=0 turns, 3=1, 4=2, 6=3), and normalize the rotated shape. The vector from orange 7 to cyan 8 is the repeat step. Starting with the rotated template's bounding-box anchor at the cyan cell, stamp it in maroon 9 repeatedly. Stop before the first placement that touches a color-5 wall or leaves the grid; all input markings disappear.
Extract each two-row strip between paired 2x2 cyan markers and stack the strips in marker-row order, discarding the surrounding nine-color noise field.

Two to four separated, distinct-color 4-connected objects are replaced by one same-colored cell at each object's floor-rounded bounding-box center. Generated lessons vary grid size, object count, palette family, object size, orientation, placement, and whether the center is initially occupied. Every three sequential demonstrations include occupied, vacant, and mixed center profiles.
Row 0 has K 1-cells (K=1..6) + 3 blobs below at distinct sizes, exactly one of size K.
Hollow 3x3 rings of color 1 with zero centers.
A 5x5 top-left exemplar names a normalized binary shape.  Of three same-signature body components, exactly one is an exact shape match; the authority crops it and recolors it 2.

Two color-1 divider columns make three equal square panels.  Crop the colored objects in A and B, infer their consistent one-to-one color map, then recolor the cropped C object with that map.  A and B may be placed at different offsets, and the palette mapping need not preserve order.

7-bg grid (size varies) with pairs of same-color markers placed at exact diagonal offsets. Rule: for each color with two objects, draw a 45-degree diagonal connecting them. The grid size, pair count, diagonal directions/lengths, colors and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).

0-bg grid (h, w~13-15) with: (a) ONE SOLID COLOR-2 (red) RECTANGLE of size bh×bw (bh, bw=2-4) at position (r1, c1)..(r2, c2), placed according to bias (centered/scattered/near_corner/rng); (b) 1-8 COLOR-5 (gray) PIXELS at scattered positions outside the red block (in horizontal, vertical, or diagonal directions). Rule (GRAVITATE GRAYS TO RED BLOCK): for EACH COLOR-5 GRAY PIXEL, MOVE it in a STRAIGHT LINE toward the RED BLOCK. The pixel STOPS at the cell ONE STEP OUTSIDE the block's bbox in the direction of approach. If the gray is directly aligned with the block (same row/col), move axially; if diagonal, move diagonally; if not aligned, move axially to the nearest side. Paint the new position color-5, clear the original. The red block stays. Net: gray pixels migrate to halos the red block's perimeter.

A zero-background grid contains 3-5 separated, 4-connected monochrome objects. For each object independently, replace its occupied cells by the perimeter of its tight bounding box in the same color. Generated lessons include 2xN boxes where the perimeter is the whole box, larger boxes with missing border cells, and larger boxes with interior input pixels that must be erased.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~11-15) with: (a) ONE HOLED COMPONENT — picked from a small bank of HOLED shapes (a 3×3 ring with one center hole, or a 3×4 ring with two center holes), placed in the TOP HALF (rows 0..h/2-sh), painted in a non-key non-bg color C0 from {1,2,3,4,6,7}; (b) 1-2 SOLID NON-HOLED COMPONENTS — picked from a small bank of L/2×2 shapes (3-4 cells each), placed in the BOTTOM HALF (rows h/2..h-ssh), each in a DISTINCT non-{0, key} color; (c) ONE ISOLATED KEY CELL with value 8 or 9, placed at a random bg position with NO non-bg neighbors in any of its 8 surrounding cells. Components are placed with 1-cell 8-conn padding (no touches). Rule (FILL THE HOLED COMPONENT WITH THE KEY COLOR, CROP IT, OUTPUT): scan components in reading order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right by bbox). FIND the FIRST component that contains at least one bbox-interior bg cell (a 'hole'). LOOK UP the KEY COLOR — the unique isolated cell with value in {8,9}. FILL every bbox-interior bg cell of that holed component with the KEY COLOR. CROP the result to the holed component's bbox. OUTPUT that crop (other components and the key cell are discarded). Net: a small rectangular output showing the holed shape with its holes plugged by the key color. Flagged intrinsic-low uniq_out (~21): output crops to a small fixed-shape set × 2 key-color values × a few non-key colors, limiting structural diversity.
Three compact connected 5x5 templates, each paired with a rotation code 1-4; overlay their transformed supports and encode coverage counts as 1->2, 2->4, and 3->8.
Fill the interior of the deepest color-1 frame around each color-2 seed.
Recolor only orange components touching exactly one border; preserve interior/corner orange components and non-orange distractors.
Infer an onion-depth palette from panels 1-2, recolor panel 3, and mark the matching candidate.
skills: analogy, palette inference, candidate selection, panel reasoning

summary: Three 3×3 panels are separated by full cyan (8) columns. Panel B is a uniquely inferable non-identity rotation/reflection of panel A followed by a consistent non-identity recolor. Panel C uses the same source palette; output is C after that same transform and recolor.
3-4 vertical color-2 lines plus a nonvertical color-2 control and color-7 decoration.
2 colors: one with multiple objects, other with 1 unique object.

Irregular color-5 wall fields contain 2..5 distinct single-cell seeds in different 4-connected non-wall regions and at least one seedless region. Flood-fill each seeded region through zero cells; preserve gray walls, seeds, and unseeded background. Canonical 7x7/9x9 profiles occur in every band; larger rectangles extend the same connectivity rule.

A 0-background grid contains 3-8 separated green (3) tree components. Each board includes all three canonical topology classes: degree-3 T-junctions recolor red (2), exactly-two-corner paths recolor magenta (6), and all other paths/junctions recolor blue (1). Canonical-sized profiles and explicit degree-4/three-corner counterexamples prevent position, generic-junction, and at-least-two-corners shortcuts.

Two row-0 keys select a transform of the red source (1=identity, 2=clockwise, 3=left/right reflection, 4=180 degrees) and then a boolean composition with the green source (6=union, 7=intersection, 8=xor). The source crops are center-aligned; the cropped result is painted cyan.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~8-11) with: (a) ONE BORDER-TOUCHING COMPONENT placed flush against one of the 4 grid edges in some random non-zero color; (b) 2-3 INTERIOR COMPONENTS placed strictly inside (rows 1..h-2, cols 1..w-2, with 1-cell padding from each other) in distinct non-zero colors. All components are small polyominoes (2-3 cells from a shape bank: L-tromino, S-tromino, line, domino). Rule: identify each CONNECTED COMPONENT. For EACH component, check if it has ANY cell ON the GRID BORDER. DROP (clear to 0) every border-touching component. KEEP (preserve) every strictly-interior component at its original color. Net: border-touching blobs erased; interior blobs survive.

Split the input at four full-height gray columns. Panels 0 and 1 demonstrate the cellwise merge and panel 2 is their exact result. Apply the same merge to query panels 3 and 4: zero passes the other value through, equal nonzero values remain unchanged, and unequal nonzero values become maroon 9.

Reflect the entire square grid across the anti-diagonal. Every cell at (r,c) moves to (n-1-c,n-1-r); anti-diagonal cells are fixed. Ordinary draws use exactly four foreground colors and include fixed points, singletons, and differently colored occupied mirror pairs so copy/overlay, collision-skipping, color-unique-only, and main-diagonal shortcuts fail.

Fixed 9×11 grid with COLOR-8 (cyan) WALLS forming a 2×2 COMPARTMENT LAYOUT: rows 0, 4, 8 are fully 8; cols 0, 5, 10 are fully 8. This creates 4 INTERIOR COMPARTMENTS at (1..3, 1..4), (1..3, 6..9), (5..7, 1..4), (5..7, 6..9). EACH COMPARTMENT contains 1-2 SAME-COLOR MARKER cells in a DISTINCT color from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9} (different across compartments). Rule (FILL EACH COMPARTMENT WITH ITS MARKER COLOR): For EACH COMPARTMENT (4-conn non-8 region bounded by 8-walls): identify the MAJORITY non-0, non-8 COLOR (the marker color). REPAINT all 0-cells in that compartment with the marker color. The 8-walls stay. Net: each compartment fills with its marker's color.

Color-8 (cyan) background grid (size varies). 1-4 copies of 9x9 BLUE/CYAN boundary PATCHES (from 3 hardcoded anomaly patterns), placed apart so each patch's 9x9 context is clean. Rule (a memorized exact-9x9-context lookup table, radius 4) fixes the single boundary anomaly inside each patch. The grid size, patch count and positions vary freely (was a single patch, ~23 distinct -- the table is memorized so this is the honest ceiling).

Several non-zero cells (in various colors) scattered on a 0-bg grid with non-zero padding on every side. Rule outputs the subgrid bounded by the bbox of all non-zero cells, preserving interior 0-cells within the bbox.
Remove column 0, read the red marker's zero-based row index, and cyclically rotate the remaining rows downward by that many rows.
Trace each color's row-major waypoints with horizontal-then-vertical segments; paint cells shared by both traces with color 9.
Grow every horizontal nonzero run by one cell into each available zero flank.

A connected nonzero/non-9 payload and exactly two maroon (9) markers are placed on a 0 background. Reading the markers in row-major order gives a translation vector. Remove both markers, keep the original payload, and overlay a copy shifted by that vector; the shifted copy wins on overlap and is clipped at the grid boundary. Ordinary draws cover both fully visible and clipped copies and periodically match canonical scale.
Copy the connected source terrain across the paired marker/anchor lines, recoloring the copy with the sparse marker color.
2-3 colors each with 2 cells aligned in row or col.

0-bg grid containing 2 hollow color-6 FRAMES (placed at distinct columns, same row band) and 2 hollow color-7 FRAMES (placed at distinct rows, same column band). All 4 frames have IDENTICAL interior dimensions (ih × iw, ~4-6 each). Each frame's interior holds 3-6 non-bg cells in a single non-{0,6,7} color (the interior pattern). Frames don't overlap. Rule: sort 6-frames by column → COLUMN SHAPES (binary interior masks). Sort 7-frames by row → ROW SHAPES. For each (row-shape, col-shape) pair, compute cell-wise AND of their masks → paint with color 8. Build gallery: hstack horizontally for each row shape with 1-col gap, then vstack the rows with 1-row gap.
Infer union/intersection/xor from an example and apply it to query.

Scan every 2x2 input window. If it contains exactly three equal non-zero cells and one zero corner, fill that zero with the shared colour. Apply all such completions simultaneously and preserve every other cell.

0-bg grid (size varies) with a 1-cell border. ONE grid CORNER holds a non-zero marker; the interior BODY (border stripped) is painted as four distinct-colored QUADRANTS (split at the body's midlines) plus a few scattered accent cells. Rule: read which corner is marked (TL/TR/BL/BR) and output that quadrant of the body. The grid size, the marked corner, the marker color, the four quadrant colors and the accents all vary freely (was a fixed deterministic counter body, ~13 distinct).

Tiny 5×4/5×5 0-bg grid. Row 0 holds 1–2 sparse program tokens: 2 rotates the body 90° clockwise, 3 flips it left-right, and any other token transposes it. Row 1 is an ignored color-8 separator. Rows 2..end hold one connected monochrome body. Output is the transformed body crop.
Collapse each four-connected same-color component to its floor-rounded bounding-box center on zero background; repeated colors remain separate.

On a zero-background grid, keep exactly the nonzero cells having one orthogonal neighbour of the same colour. Scheduled path, branch, isolated-cell, zero-leaf-component, repeated-colour-component, and cross-colour-contact witnesses make the local exact-degree rule visible.

On a square color-7 grid, find the 1..5 red cells. For two or more cells they form one contiguous diagonal; for one cell its quadrant supplies the diagonal. Remove the old red mark/chain, move from its row-sorted lower endpoint by N steps toward the top (or inward for one cell), and draw N+1 red cells continuing along that diagonal.
Single closed frame of one color + 1 seed cell of another color inside.

0-bg grid with 3-4 small, isolated, monochrome connected components in distinct nonzero colors. At least one component touches the outer border and at least one component is strictly interior. Rule: recolor every border-touching component to 2 and every interior component to 8, preserving their shapes and positions.
Center-pack the nonzero values in each row, preserving row order.
Recolor every cell of the sole color that forms exactly one 4-connected component to yellow (4).
Fill each gray-wall room when it contains exactly one distinct seed color; leave empty or multi-color rooms unchanged.

0-bg grid (h, w~5-16) with 2-4 CELLS of a SINGLE NON-BG COLOR from {1..9} placed at the CORNERS of a SQUARE BBOX (side 3-min(h, w)-2, height == width). Always anchors at (r1, c1) and (r1+side, c1+side) with 50% chance of anti-diagonal corners (r1, c1+side) and (r1+side, c1) also set. Rule (DRAW X ACROSS SQUARE BBOX IN ORIGINAL COLOR): identify the 2+ NON-BG CELLS (all same color). COMPUTE their bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2) which is SQUARE (r2-r1 == c2-c1). EMIT a FRESH h×w OUTPUT GRID. PAINT BOTH DIAGONALS of the bbox in the ORIGINAL color — TL→BR diagonal AND TR→BL diagonal, forming an X. Off-diagonal cells stay 0. Net: 2-4 corner markers become an X spanning their square bbox.

A 5..10 by 5..10 zero-background grid contains 2..5 scattered non-zero colors, each occurring 1..4 times. Count every occurrence, sort colors numerically, and emit a one-row strip containing each color repeated by its count; an all-zero input would map to [[0]].

Gray (5) walls partition a bordered grid into rectangular chambers. Count every nonzero, non-wall seed in each chamber, select the unique chamber with the greatest total seed count, find that chamber's unique majority seed color, and fill only its zero cells with that color.

0-bg grid with: (a) exactly THREE color-2 (red) cells positioned as three corners of a rectangle (so exactly 2 distinct row values and 2 distinct col values); (b) 0-3 DECORATION cells in OTHER non-{0, 2, 8} colors that the rule preserves but ignores. Rule: find all color-2 cells. Compute rs = unique rows, cs = unique cols. corners = product rs × cs (4 candidate corner cells). The rectangle has both dimensions at least 3 cells, and may include 0-4 non-{0,2,8} decoration cells away from the red corners. missing = first corner not already in pts. Set missing to 8. Output = input with the missing corner painted 8.
Read row-0 keys left-to-right and output the initial motif followed by every cumulative transform state, packed with one blank column. Keys 1/2/3/4 mean rotate-CW/rotate-180/flip-LR/flip-UD.

Count every color-3 cell, regardless of position or connectivity. If the count is N, emit an N x N solid color-7 square. Canonical-like draws use isolated green cells on black; scheduled shortcut-rebuttal draws add one more-numerous non-green distractor color and connect some green cells in an L, proving the rule is not nonzero-count, component-count, row-count, column-count, modal-color, or fixed-size.

A gray(5) field contains one connected network of walkable zero-cells, one red(2) start, and one green(3) goal.  Some scenes contain a single cycle that supplies exactly two equal-length shortest routes; others contain a unique elbow route plus dead-end branches.  Treat gray cells as walls.  Of all shortest 4-connected start-to-goal paths, recolor with cyan(8) exactly the zero-cells present on every shortest path.  Preserve the red and green endpoints, alternative shortest-route cells, dead-end branches, and walls.

Drop each column of the three-row top object through the obstacle field. Tip-ending columns stop before the first obstacle; body-only columns reach the floor, using the canonical bottom-component landing behavior.

0-bg grid (size varies). One color-4 (yellow) connected BLOB, one color-2 (red) marker and one color-1 (blue) marker; the vector v = blue - red. Rule: translate the blob by v and paint the copy in color-8 (cyan) onto the grid. The copy region is reserved in-bounds and disjoint from the blob, so the cyan ghost is clean. The grid size, the blob shape, the vector and all placements vary freely (was a fixed blob with fixed markers, ~13 distinct).

Three 5x5 monochrome connected panels share a local coordinate system. Their canonical-derived overlap profile contains examples of occupancy counts one, two, and three; lessons move the motif onto the outer border to distinguish the full 5x5 count map from a central-only shortcut.

On a 0-background grid, recolor a 5 to 2 iff its up, down, left, and right neighbours are all 5; preserve every other cell. Lessons cycle through solid rectangles, one-cell border notches, and two-cell deep notches. The notched scenes retain bbox-interior 5s beside the notch, refuting rectangle-fill and bbox-interior shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 1-2 SOLID 3×3 RINGS — each ring is a 3×3 block of cells where the 8 OUTER cells (top row, bottom row, left col, right col of the 3×3) are filled with a single non-bg COLOR, and the CENTER cell at (r+1, c+1) is 0 (empty). Each ring uses a distinct color, and rings are placed with at least 1-cell gap so they don't touch. Rule: for every cell whose all 8 neighbors are NON-ZERO and SAME-COLOR (a ring center), FILL that center cell with the ring's color. Net: each hollow 3×3 ring becomes a solid 3×3 square of its color.

Per color: 3 of the 4 axis-aligned-rectangle corners are present (one is blank). Rule completes each such 3-of-4 rectangle by filling the missing corner with the same color. Multiple rectangles in different colors are independent.
Singleton color-2 objects recolored to 3; larger color-2 objects remain.

Each row keeps its first-cell shift header and cyclically rotates the remaining cells right by that row's header modulo the body width. A four-profile schedule exposes wraparound, modulo identity, large headers, scattered bodies, and row-specific shifts.

On a zero background, transpose each of 2..4 distinct-color, isolated 4-connected objects about its own bbox top-left. Each object has 3..5 cells, is nonrectangular and changes under transpose. All destinations fit and are pairwise disjoint. Paint onto a blank same-size output. Alternate canonical-shaped tetromino lessons with broad lessons that include both a width-four asymmetric pentomino and a three-cell object, on 8..14 by 8..14 grids.

On a zero background, red(2) and blue(1) seeds are joined by a gray(5) corridor tree. Gray cells on the red-to-blue shortest path become yellow(4). Off-path corridor regions entering from the red end become red, regions entering from the blue end become blue, and interior off-path regions become yellow.

A sparse same-size recoloring task. Row 0 contains two to four ordered source/destination color pairs, displayed as source, zero, destination triplets with an optional leading zero offset. Row 1 is a blank separator. Every source color appears in multiple body components below the separator. The output preserves row 0 and all geometry, replaces each body source color with its paired destination color, and leaves background plus at most one unmapped distractor color unchanged.
A black rectangular grid contains several rows of colored seeds and at least one blank row.  Fill each nonblank row with its leftmost seed color; leave blank rows black.

0-bg grid (h~5-13, w~8-17) where each of `target` ACTIVE ROWS (2-9, drawn from h rows without repetition) holds 1-4 SCATTERED NON-0 CELLS at DISTINCT column positions in cols 1..w-1 (col 0 stays bg-0, ensuring leading zero before any non-zero, so packing has visible effect). Cell colors are drawn uniformly from {1..9}, with replacement (so a row may have duplicate colors but at distinct positions). Non-active rows stay all-0. At least one active row has leading or internal zeros (the col-0 bg constraint and sparse placement guarantee this). Rule (PER-ROW LEFT-PACK NON-ZERO VALUES, RIGHT-PAD WITH ZEROS): for EACH ROW r independently: collect every non-zero value in left-to-right order, preserving their RELATIVE ORDER. REPLACE the row with a left-packed sequence: place the collected values in cols 0, 1, 2, ... and fill the remaining right-side cells with 0. Empty rows stay all-0. Row dimensions are preserved. Net: each row is compacted to its left edge — sorted-by-position (not sorted-by-value), with the right side padded by bg-0.
Color-9 dividers split the grid into a lattice of equal tiles; output is the tile-sized grid with 8 where >=3 tiles have a nonzero cell.

Reflect every source color 1..8 across the full-height central 9-axis on a zero background, preserving the source and axis. The right half starts empty. Mix connected monochrome objects with isolated, edge, and varied-color marks; exact count/palette/geometry overrides are honored or rejected.

0-bg grid (size varies) with two non-0 cells aligned in a row or column. Rule: connect them with a segment (horizontal if same row, else vertical at the first cell's column) in the first cell's color, on a blank grid. The grid size, endpoints and color vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct). Output is a single line, so distinct OUTPUTS are bounded; distinct INPUTS are large.
Separated filled odd-size squares reduce to their center cells.

A 0-background grid contains two or three blank centers whose four diagonal neighbors share one nonzero color. The output fills every such center with that color and preserves all other cells. Each generated lesson also contains one controlled non-answer: either only three matching diagonals, four nonzero but mismatched diagonals, or a nonzero center surrounded by four matching diagonals. Positive motifs move across the grid, two of every three examples reuse one color, and one example adds a symmetric orthogonal context pair that must not block the fill.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with: (a) ONE small PROTOTYPE BLOB of 2-4 cells in some non-{0, 9} color, placed at a random position (this is the SHAPE to be stamped); (b) 1-2 color-9 (maroon) ANCHOR single cells placed at positions that have room for the full prototype stamp to fit in-bounds without overlapping existing cells. Rule: extract the prototype's shape cells (the non-9, non-0 connected blob). Build an EMPTY OUTPUT GRID of the same dims. For each color-9 ANCHOR, STAMP the prototype's shape ANCHORED at the anchor's position (with anchor as the stamp's top-left), painted in the prototype's original color. Original prototype + anchors are DISCARDED from output. Net: anchors become stamp positions; output is the prototype replicated at each anchor.

Find all four-connected nonzero components, crop each component to its bounding box while preserving every color and internal zero, and compare the complete crops exactly. Exactly one crop occurs twice; output that duplicated colored crop. Geometry alone, palette alone, cell count, size, position, and modal color are insufficient.

Place one connected non-rectangular red (2) source glyph and two or three green (3) anchor cells on an 8-10 by 10-12 zero-background grid. The source is away from the grid origin. Most anchors hold the full glyph; a scheduled edge branch clips one copy exactly as an official training pair does. The output clears the input, stamps the normalized source shape at every anchor, and recolors all stamped cells green (3).

skills: coordinate transforms, local reflection, orientation-aware rendering
summary: Two 3-cell L-frames in distinct color-triples ({2,3,4} for source with 2 at corner; {5,6,7} for target with 5 at corner). Several color-8 cells are placed near the source. Rule maps the 8-cells from source to target frame via diagonal reflection of their local (u, v) offsets, painting 8 at the corresponding target positions.
Recolor every exact five-cell green X component; preserve distractors.
Read row-length caps from column 0 and column-height caps from row 0. Remove those headers and paint a body cell cyan (8) exactly when it lies inside both the row cap and the column cap.
Left-panel marker count selects the matching-size green object on the right.

Rotate the red asymmetric template according to the blue corner (TL/TR/BR/BL = 0/90/180/270 degrees clockwise), translate it by the green-to-orange vector, and draw the result in cyan on a blank canvas.

Gray 5-cells partition the grid into 4-connected chambers. Fill every zero in a chamber iff that chamber contains exactly one nonzero seed cell; leave empty and multi-seed chambers unchanged. Generated lessons contrast same-color multi-seed conflicts, empty rooms, independent room colors, edge-open rooms, and multiple wall topologies.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-20, w ∈ 7-18, by difficulty) with: TARGET ∈ 2-9 COMPONENTS, each in a DISTINCT color drawn from {1..9}, where: (a) the BOTTOM-MOST COMPONENT is placed at br = h - sh (bottom-aligned) with sh × sw drawn from bottom_shapes bank (L-tromino, corner, 2×2, L-tet, I-tro horizontal/vertical), painted in colors[0]; (b) OTHER components placed STRICTLY ABOVE br (rows ≤ br - 1) with 1-cell padding, drawn from a wider other_shapes bank. Guaranteed: ONE component has STRICTLY LOWEST bottom row. Rule (KEEP ONLY THE COMPONENT WHOSE BBOX BOTTOM ROW IS STRICTLY THE LOWEST; ERASE ALL OTHER COMPONENTS TO 0; KEPT COMPONENT PRESERVES SHAPE AND COLOR): EXTRACT every 4-connected non-bg component. For each: COMPUTE bbox-bottom-row. FIND the MAXIMUM bottom row (strictly unique). PRODUCE a fresh same-size grid of 0s. PAINT only the bottommost component's cells in its original color. Net: the lowest component wins; others vanish.

Paint every zero in the clipped one-cell-expanded bounding rectangle of each multi-cell red component green; preserve red cells and red singletons, with alternating concave witnesses against a per-cell-halo shortcut.

0-bg grid (h, w~5-14) where each ACTIVE ROW has at COL 0 a NON-GRAY, NON-ZERO MARKER COLOR (per-active-row marker; diversity may be same / mixed / all-distinct across rows). The remaining cells of active rows (cols 1..w-1) contain 3-12 GRAY(5) CELLS placed in a chosen layout (random, cluster, one-per-row, column, diagonal, scattered) plus optional decor cells in other non-gray colors. Rule (PER-ROW RECOLOR GRAY → COL-0 MARKER): For EACH ROW r: let M = g[r][0] (the marker color). For EACH cell (r, c) with c ≥ 1: if cell value == 5 (gray), RECOLOR to M. Else, keep. Col 0 stays. Inactive rows normally stay all-bg. Net: gray cells inherit each row's left-edge marker color.

A 0-background grid contains several isolated down-right 4,0,4 gaps and one controlled 4,4,0,4 or 4,0,4,4 diagonal near-miss. Fill only the midpoints of isolated 4,0,4 triples; a candidate that extends a longer diagonal run is deliberately left unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains 3-6 separated monochrome components.  Every normal draw has (1) two differently colored rotation-equivalent shapes, (2) two same-colored non-equivalent shapes, and (3) an unrelated pair.  Some draws also contain a same-color, same-shape pair to show that shape equality takes precedence and still emits 8.  Sort components by bounding-box (top, left); output the NxN relation matrix: diagonal = the component color, else 8 for rotation-equivalent shape, else 6 for equal color, else 0.

Find the unique non-9 object, normalize its cells to its bounding-box top-left, rotate the shape 90 degrees clockwise, and stamp that rotated shape in the template color at every singleton color-9 marker. Build the answer on a fresh black grid and clip stamped cells that fall beyond the bottom or right edge.

Fill a blank cell only when equal nonzero endpoints lie exactly two rows and two columns apart; copy the endpoint color into that diagonal midpoint. Every scene has both diagonal orientations. A four-slot lesson schedule contains one exact 7x7, 8x8, or 9x9 canonical morphology and three overlapping combinations of axis-aligned, wrong-distance/different-color, and blocked-midpoint near misses. Thus every three-of-four query rotation retains all shortcut witnesses. Exact grid-size and pair-count overrides remain authoritative.

skills: pattern extraction from an in-grid legend
summary: A unique 9 anchors an asymmetric constellation of 1s.  Translate the anchor-relative offsets to every 2 seed and paint those target cells 8 on a blank output.  wide_offsets increases the constellation span; edge_seeds makes a lawful stamped copy touch a border.  no_offsets and no_seeds are explicit empty-output degenerates.

A fixed 4×14 input contains three 4×4 same-color sections at columns 0..3, 5..8, and 10..13, separated by zero columns 4 and 9. Each section has exactly one of four zero patterns: none→2, centered 2×2→8, bottom 2×2→4, or the four middle left/right edge cells→3. The output is 3×3; row i repeats the class color of section i.

A 0-background grid has two or more rows containing exactly one maroon (9) anchor and at least one colored source. Each anchored row is solved independently: every nonzero non-9 source is copied to the equally distant cell on the opposite side of that row's 9, preserving the source. Sources occur on both sides across every generated grid. At least one row has no anchor, so the 9s never form a full-height divider; some such rows contain colored pass-through distractors that must remain unchanged.

Five separated, distinctly colored objects on the canonical 12x18 / 6-color profile.  Group objects by (area, enclosed-hole count, row/column reflection-symmetry class) and recolor every member of a repeated class cyan (8).  The v3 curriculum always uses different-outline feature twins plus same-area one-feature decoys, directly refuting exact-shape, area-only, area+holes, and area+symmetry shortcuts.

A zero-corner grid carries nonzero column headers across row 0 and row headers down column 0; the zero interior is replaced by the colored row-by-column equality matrix after both header axes are removed.

An 8-12 by 8-12 zero-background grid contains 1-3 border-touching monochrome 4-connected objects and 1-3 fully interior objects. Objects vary across every border side, sizes, and shapes; some scenes reuse one color across a kept and erased component. Keep exactly the components that touch any outer row or column and erase the interior components.

Read the three-cell header as (shape_code, step1, step2). Match the one body object whose normalized binary crop equals the requested shape class, crop it with its original color, then apply transform step1 and transform step2 in that order. Transform codes are 1 identity, 2 rotate clockwise, 3 rotate 180, 4 rotate counterclockwise, 5 flip left-right, 6 flip up-down, and 7 transpose.

Fixed 5x11 grid. Rows 0-2: a LIBRARY of three 3x3 panels (distinct-color random shapes) at cols 0-2/4-6/8-10. Row 4: four (index 1-3, transform 1-7) tokens at cols (0,1)/(3,4)/(6,7)/(9,10). Rule: decode each token (fetch library[index-1], apply the dihedral transform) and pack the four results into a 3x15 strip. The library shapes/colors and the four tokens all vary freely (was 4 fixed libraries x 5 fixed sequences, ~17 distinct).
Expand every blue cell into a clipped 3x3 blue neighbourhood, filling only black cells and preserving all colored blockers.
Color-7 control count selects an exact graph-distance shell around a seed.

A 0-background grid contains three 4-connected nonzero components and one color-8 marker. Exactly one component has a cell at Manhattan distance 1 from the marker; diagonal-only distractors may also be present. The target component may contain one or two colors. Render only the full multicolor target into its tight bounding box, clear non-target intruders, and upscale the crop by 2 while preserving target colors and holes.

0-bg grid (h~3-5, w~10-14) where EACH ROW r contains a PERIODIC PREFIX: a cycle of length P_r ∈ {1, 2, 3} repeated K_r ≥ 2 times starting at col 0, followed by TRAILING 0-CELLS to col w-1. The prefix length K_r * P_r < w (so trailing 0s exist). Each row's period uses a random selection of colors from {1..9}. Rule (INFER ROW PERIOD, EXTEND PREFIX TO FILL ENTIRE ROW): For EACH ROW r: DETECT the PERIODIC CYCLE by finding the smallest period length P that makes the prefix self-repeating. EXTEND the cycle by repeating the period FROM CELL 0 all the way TO COL w-1. Trailing 0s get filled with cycle continuation. Net: each row's periodic prefix extends to fill the full row width.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-22) containing 1-5 COLOR-6 (magenta) OBJECTS — each a small polyomino (3-4 cells from a shape bank: L, corner, T, S, square, L-tet, J, T-rot). Each object is placed at some interior position with sufficient padding for rotation to stay in-bounds. Each object has a SINGLE CONTROL CELL placed exactly ONE ROW ABOVE its bbox TOP-LEFT (at (r0-1, c0)) with VALUE ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} (the rotation code: 1=identity, 2=cw90, 3=180°, 4=ccw90). Objects + their controls are mutually padded. Rule: for EACH magenta object, READ its control value at (r0-1, c0). ROTATE the object's normalized shape IN PLACE within its local bbox by the control code (1=identity, 2=cw90, 3=180°, 4=ccw90). The object stays color 6; the control stays in place. Net: each magenta polyomino rotates by its overhead control's quarter-turn count.

Fixed 6×16 0-bg grid with 2-4 COLORED 2-CELL VERTICAL COMPONENTS placed at FIXED COLUMN STARTS [1, 5, 9, 13] (one component per slot, separated by 4 columns). For EACH component i: pick a random row r ∈ {1..3}; paint cells (r, starts[i]) and (r+1, starts[i]) in a DISTINCT non-{0, 5} color drawn from {1..9}; with 50% probability ALSO paint cell (r+1, starts[i]+1) with COLOR 5 (a GRAY MARKER cell, signaling this component to be recolored). Other cells stay bg-0. Rule (GRAY MARKERS INHERIT NEAREST COLOR, COMPONENTS PACKED INTO 3-ROW STRIP): for EACH GRAY (color 5) MARKER cell: find the NEAREST non-gray non-bg cell (its color C) — typically the adjacent component. RECOLOR the gray cell to C (so the gray inherits its nearest color, extending the component). Then extract every now-uniform-color component and PACK them into a 3-ROW OUTPUT STRIP (specifically, place each component's crop into a tight 3-row arrangement, preserving color, in order). Net: gray markers absorb into their neighbors and the colored components are gathered into a compact 3-row gallery.

A 0-background grid contains a unique largest color-2 shape and a unique largest color-3 shape, plus 1-3 smaller disconnected distractors of each color. Normalize only the two largest components to their bounding-box origins, intersect their occupied cells, and paint the cropped result color 8. Grid size, shape density, distractor count, shapes, and placements vary while preserving a nonempty normalized intersection.

Generate two or three distinct-color rectangular outlines with one color-1 marker assigned to every color role. Nested scenes require choosing the smallest intact enclosing outline. Overlap scenes draw a later intact frame across an earlier outline, so the earlier color is only an occluded frame fragment and its marker must remain 1.

A 0-background grid contains distinct-colour endpoint groups. Colours appearing exactly twice are bridged only when the endpoints share a row or column; the inclusive straight segment is painted in that colour. Adjacent pairs need no added cells. Misaligned pairs and three-occurrence groups are unchanged and serve as explicit guards against shortcut rules.

A 12..22 square or rectangular zero-background grid contains a diagonal color-1 seed. Extend the seed in both directions. Color-2 line walls reflect the path according to their input-measured orientation; color-3 segments are pass-through distractors. Ordinary draws exercise both true horizontal and true vertical reflection branches.

A 0-background grid contains exactly two hollow rectangular frames and two other connected monochrome objects, all in distinct colors. Sort frames by interior area and objects by cell count; pair equal ranks. Return a fresh 0 grid with every frame redrawn at its original location and each paired object's tight crop centered on that frame. Nonzero crop cells are pasted after the frame, so a crop larger than the interior can overwrite frame-border cells. Original object locations disappear.

0-bg grid with 3-4 ISOLATED 4-conn motifs (3-5 cells each) in distinct non-zero colors at distinct positions, each surrounded by background. Rule: start from an empty grid the same size as the input. For each 4-connected non-bg object, compute its cells normalized to the bbox (0, 0) corner, rotate those normalized cells 90° CLOCKWISE inside the bbox, then paint the rotated cells back at the SAME bbox top-left in the object's color. Net effect: every object is rotated 90° CW in place (anchored at its original top-left corner).

Three disconnected blue components have distinct sizes. Red marker count selects the one-based size rank; green marker count selects identity, 90° clockwise, 180°, or left-right mirror. Stamp the transformed normalized component in orange at the unique cyan target on a blank grid.

A black grid contains exactly one hollow blue (1) rectangular frame and 1-7 yellow (4) cells strictly inside it. For every yellow cell, reflect its column across the frame's vertical axis. If that mirror cell is empty, the Racket rule paints it orange (7); a yellow mirror partner or a yellow cell on the axis is left unchanged. Ordinary draws always include at least one empty, off-axis mirror target. Alternating ordinary draws teach occupied-pair and center-axis preservation; every third draw retains a canonical canvas size in every difficulty band.
N connected components in distinct colors. Components are sorted by color. Output is N×N binary matrix where cell (i, j) = 1 if center_col(comp_i) < center_col(comp_j), else 0 (diagonal is 0).
Exactly one 2-seed + one 3-seed on an otherwise empty grid.

On a zero-background grid, process each row independently. Count its nonzero cells and rewrite the row as that many copies of the row's first nonzero color packed from column 0; empty rows remain empty.

0-bg grid (h, w~6-9) with: (a) EXACTLY TWO color-9 (maroon) MARKERS at distinct positions (a, b sorted by row then col) defining a translation VECTOR v = (b.r - a.r, b.c - a.c) with v ≠ (0, 0); (b) ONE small connected SHAPE (3-4 cells from a polyomino bank) in some non-{0, 9} color, placed in the upper-left region with at least one cell that translates in-bounds. Rule: read the vector v from the two 9-markers. For each non-9 shape, PAINT a TRANSLATED COPY at (cell + v) for each cell in the shape — using the shape's ORIGINAL color, skipping cells that fall OOB. The two 9-markers are ERASED in output (replaced by 0). Original shape stays + translated copy added. Net: each shape sprouts a ghost copy displaced by the 9→9 vector; the 9-markers themselves vanish.

0-bg grid (h~4-6, w~5-7) with: (a) ROW 0 has 2-4 COLUMN MARKERS painted color 8 (cyan) at random column positions; (b) ROWS 1+ contain random non-8 color cells at ~60% density. Rule: detect which columns have a color-8 marker in row 0. Output is (h-1) × N_marked sub-grid: take ROWS 1..h-1 of the input, and KEEP ONLY the marked columns (in their original left-to-right order). Net: filter body cells through the column-marker mask.

Place 2-4 well-separated blue markers on one legal background color. For each original marker, paint its whole row and column blue, recolor the marker red, and recolor its in-bounds diagonal neighbors green.
Singleton same-color objects are erased while larger objects remain.

On a zero-background grid, process each row independently. Keep every nonzero cell in its original left-to-right order, remove the intervening zeros, and right-align the resulting sequence. Empty rows remain empty.
Common colors + 1 unique-color cell; rule outputs unique + halo of 2.

An 8..18 by 10..18 zero-background grid contains three or four diagonally separated monochrome objects with distinct colors and distinct cell areas. Extract each object, crop it tightly, sort the crops by object cell area from largest to smallest, and stack them vertically with one zero row between neighboring crops. Crops are left aligned; output width equals the maximum crop width.
5-frame around interior + 2-3 distinct-color seeds.
Two compact nonzero color components with a strict frequency winner and loser.
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at well-separated positions.

Extract each isolated nonzero object and crop it to its bounding box. Count enclosed zero regions inside each crop, sort by increasing hole count and then by decreasing painted area, and horizontally pack the crops with one black column between them. Exact remaining ties use color as the canonical oracle's deterministic fallback.

A uniform-2x2-block icon occupies the first six rows, followed by one full separator row of color 5 and a 0/2 marker field. Compress the icon to its 3x3 stride-2 values. Create a fresh canvas three times the marker field height and width, then stamp that 3x3 icon at every red(2) marker. Red may also be an icon color; above the separator it is payload, below the separator it is a stamp marker.
Fill each zero cell only when all four cardinal neighbours share one non-zero colour; ignore diagonals and surrounding texture.

Preserve the uniquely largest multicolor 8-connected nonzero object. Every other nonzero cell counts and votes, including small touching groups. The most frequent residual color wins, with row-major first occurrence breaking ties. The unique residual corner selects orientation. Erase all residual cells, then paint a triangle of leg residual-count minus one, overwriting any overlap with the preserved object.

Fill only zero centers with eight color-4 neighbors using fixed color 6. Generate separated 3x3 motifs at varied positions, including edge positions. Canonical-size positive cases alternate with multiple targets and three unchanged distractors: missing corner, non-yellow ring, and occupied center. Exact dimensions and positive-ring counts are honored or explicitly refused.
Read two aligned 3-column panels on either side of a solid separator. Output blue (2) wherever either aligned panel cell is nonzero; otherwise output black (0).

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (2-4) nested concentric color-1 frames and N color-2 markers. Rule: sort frames by area; (N-1) selects one; fill the ring between it and the next-inner frame with 8 (or the whole interior if it is the innermost). The grid size, frames and marker count vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

Read the unique control cell: 2 means identity, 3 one clockwise turn, 4 a half-turn, and 6 one counterclockwise turn. Normalize the connected blue(1) template, apply that rotation, and stamp it in gray(8) with its top-left at the orange(7) anchor on a fresh zero background. Ordinary draws preserve one of the five linked canonical dimension/control/shape profiles while varying role order and horizontal placement.

A zero-background grid contains two to four separated 4-connected magenta (6) objects. For each object independently, paint every cell on the perimeter of its tight bounding box red (2). Existing magenta on that perimeter is overwritten; cells strictly inside each box and all cells outside the boxes are preserved.

Place 1..8 distinct colors as pairs of opposite corners of disjoint 3x3 boxes on a black canvas. Each pair may use the main or anti diagonal. The canonical transformation completes both diagonals of each box, turning every two-corner clue into a five-cell X of the same color.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~8-11 by ~9-12) containing exactly 3 connected blobs in 3 distinct non-zero colors (≠ 8). Blobs have 3, 4, and 5 cells. Their BBOX HEIGHTS are strictly distinct (so the tallest is unambiguous). Blobs don't 4-touch (≥1-cell buffer). Rule: sort all components by bbox-height descending (then by size desc, then top-left row asc, then col asc). Pick the top one. Recolor all its cells from its original color to 8. Other blobs preserved. Output: same grid with the tallest blob's cells now color 8.

A sparse 0-background grid contains 4-8 cyan (8) anchors. For every row and column, fill the zero cells between consecutive cyan anchors. Every ordinary draw includes at least one horizontal and one vertical bridge. Profiles distinguish a shared L-junction, disjoint row/column pairs, a multi-bridge rectangle, and a three-anchor chain whose outer pair is blocked by the middle anchor. A seed-keyed five-slot lesson schedule contains two chain witnesses; extra anchors are isolated distractors.

An alternating zero/nonzero top row is a column legend. Recolor each nonzero body cell under an active header to that header color; preserve zeros, the header row, and optional body cells under empty headers.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~11-15) with: (a) one CENTRAL color-3 (green) cell at random interior position (r, c); (b) 2-3 NEIGHBOR cells adjacent to it in distinct colors {2, 4, 6} (above/right/below the center); (c) 2 DISTRACTOR singletons (color 7, 8) elsewhere with no neighbors. Rule: extract all 4-conn non-bg components. For each, find its neighbor components (any 4-adjacent non-bg cell of a different color). KEEP components whose set of neighbor colors has SIZE ≥ 2; output them on a blank canvas (same dims). Drop components with <2 distinct neighbor colors.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w=9) with EXACTLY ONE FULL-WIDTH color-8 ROW (or full-height color-8 COL — orientation chosen randomly) acting as a DIVIDER. On ONE SIDE of the divider (top half if row, left half if col), 2-3 ISOLATED CELLS in various non-{0, 8} colors are placed at random positions. The OPPOSITE side is all-0. Rule: for each non-{0, 8} cell on the content side, MIRROR it across the 8-divider — paint a copy at the reflected position on the other side, preserving its color. The divider itself stays color 8; originals stay. Net: the empty half fills with a mirror image of the content half, with the cyan row/col as the axis of symmetry.

Zero-background grids contain several colored rectangular frames. Closed frames enclose zero-regions that become cyan (8); open frames have a missing side and remain connected to the exterior. Exact size and scene-profile overrides support ordinary, largest-hole counterexample, and many-hole scenes.

A closed wall of one color 5..9 partitions a 7..18 by 8..20 grid into 2..4 connected chambers. Each chamber contains exactly one seed color 1..4 and at least one zero. The selected rule floods every zero reachable from a seed without crossing another color. Scheduled examples mix canonical straight partitions with stepped and partial dividers; the shortcut-witness and broad slots both carry those decisive contrasts so any query rotation of a four-pair lesson remains identifiable.
Full color-5 vertical column + 2-4 color cells on one side.
N separated monochrome connected objects with varied bounding-box widths; output is the N x N width-comparison matrix (1=equal, 2=greater, 3=less).

Find every distinct-colour solid 2x2 square. Keep each square unchanged and paint its colour into the four diagonal corner cells one step beyond the square. Ignore corners outside the grid. If blooms overlap, the first square in row-major order owns a cell that was still background.

0-bg grid (h×w, h=4..6, w=4..6) with ROW 0 as a TOKEN SEQUENCE: 1-3 tokens at the leftmost columns, each in {1, 2, 3, 4} (1=rotate-cw, 2=flip-lr, 3=flip-ud, 4=transpose). Rest of row 0 is 0. Body (rows 1..h-1) contains exactly ONE connected SHAPE of 2-5 cells in some color != 0 and != {1, 2, 3, 4} tokens (typically 5, 6, 7, 8, 9), placed somewhere with at least one row of bg between it and row 0. Rule: read tokens. Crop body to non-zero bbox. Apply each token's transform in sequence. Output = final transformed shape (variable dimensions).

0-bg grid (h, w ~7-10) with 3-5 distinct non-bg colors, each occupying a DISTINCT cell count drawn from {2..7}, scattered uniformly. Total non-bg cells ≤ 30. Rule: collect (color, count) for each distinct non-bg color. Sort by DESCENDING count, ties broken by ASCENDING color value. Output is a 1×N row (N = total non-bg cell count) where each color appears CONSECUTIVELY repeated by its count, in sorted order. So a histogram-as-1D-bar-chart concatenated by frequency rank.
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.

skills: transform inference, analogy, dihedral action on a query shape
summary: Three panels are separated by full color-9 columns. Panel 2 is a uniquely inferable non-identity D4 transform of panel 1 on generated draws; emit panel 3 after that same transform.
Teach horizontal mirror|input|mirror|input with canonical anchors and varied-width witnesses.
Two or three hollow color-1 frames; crop the unique raw-count winner. Alternating examples refute both density and frame-area shortcuts.

One color-2 tetromino or pentomino source plus 3–7 isolated candidate components in colors 3..6; an exact requested subset matches the source's normalized offsets and the rest are distinct distractors.
Paired row markers between side borders expand into line glyphs. Grid size, marker count and marker rows vary.
A two-color prototype containing one cyan origin plus 1-3 cyan targets; copy the prototype at every target and paint conflicting overlaps maroon.

An EXEMPLAR blob (a colour-1 anchor 4-connected to a colour-3 shape) plus isolated colour-1 TARGET markers. Rule: stamp the exemplar's colour-3 shape (offset from the anchor) at every target. Exemplar shape, target count and positions vary.

A red(2) source and adjacent blue(1) heading launch a beam. Empty path cells become 8; diagonal mirrors 4/6 turn the beam according to their orientation; gray(5) blocks it. Every requested mirror lies on a compact serpentine route; 3+ mirror routes mix relative turn directions.

Find the unique color-1 shape and the unique marker 2..5. Rotate the normalized shape (marker-2) quarter-turns clockwise, crop it to its bounding box, and recolor it 8. Exact public-profile anchors are mixed with translated anchors and moved-marker/new-shape counterexamples so location and lookup shortcuts cannot identify a lesson.
Two equal zero-background panels are split by a full colour-7 row. Emit 8 exactly at aligned positions where both panels are zero; emit 0 for the other three joint cell relations.
A hollow color-1 frame contains a colored source motif. A separate full 2..5 code rectangle is replaced cell-by-cell by the source interior rotated code-2 clockwise quarter turns.

Two colored non-branching orthogonal paths (1..3 turns) and two aligned singleton markers. Extend each path toward its marker and recolor the same number of cells from the opposite endpoint in the marker color.
Rows 0 and 1 define old-to-new color mappings used to recolor the body.

Several colour pairs (two cells each) form horizontal/vertical/diagonal lines; the pair with a unique (orientation, length) signature is the odd one, whose line the rule crops and recolours 8. Pair count, the common signature and the odd pair vary.
Three color pairs and 4-5 color-8 walls teach H-first preference, H-blocked/V-clear routing, both-blocked V fallback, wall preservation, and row-major overwrite order.

A colour-5-9 template plus several isolated marker cells (values 1-4) that encode rotations; the rule stamps a rotated copy of the template at each marker. Template shape, marker count, rotations and positions vary.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~11-16) with: (a) WALLED QUADRANT STRUCTURE — two FULL-HEIGHT (or near-full-height) COLOR-5 (gray) WALL COLUMNS at c1 = w//3 and c2 = (2*w)//3, with small gaps near row h//2 (passable openings); plus a horizontal stretch of color-5 wall cells along row h//2 (sparse, leaving gaps near the wall columns); (b) THREE COLORED SEEDS — color 2 (red) at (1, w//2) in the top region, color 4 (yellow) at (h-2, 2) bottom-left, color 3 (green) at (h-2, w-3) bottom-right. Rule (WALL-AWARE BFS FLOOD WITH TIES → CYAN): For EACH 0-cell, compute BFS DISTANCE through 0-cells (4-connected, blocked by 5-walls) to EACH of the 3 seeds. If one seed has STRICTLY LESS distance, PAINT the cell with that seed's color. If ≥2 seeds TIE for minimum distance, PAINT with COLOR 8 (cyan). Unreachable cells stay 0. Walls and seeds stay. Net: each empty cell goes to its nearest seed's color, ties become cyan.

Find the largest all-nonzero two-colour rectangle. Keep it in place and mirror it into a local 2x2 frame. In each of the other three blocks, indicator positions identify source roles and indicator colours provide that block's recolouring; absent roles become 0 and the first duplicate indicator in row-major order wins.

An odd-height grid contains a sparse colored motif above a full color-5 divider and an empty panel below. Reflect every nonzero motif cell vertically across the divider, preserving its column and color.
Among red objects, crop the one that touches the grid border.
Transform keyed components and pack them into a width-sorted gallery.

0-bg grid with N single-cell objects (each a DISTINCT non-zero color) arranged as a connected polyomino, so cardinally-adjacent cells are separate objects that TOUCH. Rule: sort the N objects by (col, row); output the N x N matrix with 5 on the diagonal, 7 where two objects cardinally touch, else 0 (the polyomino's adjacency graph). N (3-8) and the polyomino shape vary.

A connected 3..8-cell blue shape occupies any one quadrant of a full maroon cross.  The cross can move one cell from the geometric center; the rule reflects the shape across the detected cross, not the canvas center.
Recolor whole red (2) 4-connected components that contain an exact grid corner to green (3); preserve interior and non-corner-border red components, and preserve the inert color-5 distractor.
Yellow (4) emitters cast cardinal rays until a gray (5) blocker or the edge.  Replace the whole canvas by 2 exactly at cells reached by at least two rays; all other cells become 0.

Zero-background grids with 1..4 solid monochrome rectangles, each at least 3x3. Separate components may share a color; different colors may touch. The unchanged Racket rule preserves each component's one-cell border and erases its interior. Three-draw lessons mix canonical-scale, repeated-color and broader scenes, including 5x3 rectangles, edge contact and larger interiors.

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~8-13) with: (a) CELL (0, 0) is the TARGET COLOR LEGEND in some color from {1..9}; (b) ONE NON-LEGEND OBJECT in the TARGET COLOR — drawn from a 4-shape bank (4-5 cell shapes), placed at an interior position with 1-cell padding; (c) 1-4 DISTRACTOR OBJECTS in DISTINCT non-target colors at scattered positions. Output uniq_out=23 (intrinsic — 4 shape banks × ~9 colors normalizes). Rule (CROP LEGEND-COLOR OBJECT): READ TARGET COLOR T = g[0][0]. Identify the BODY OBJECT in color T (excluding the (0, 0) legend cell itself). CROP that object to its BBOX. EMIT the cropped subgrid. Net: (0, 0) color points to the matching body object; output is its tight crop.

A background-colored grid contains one solid monochrome rectangle and 2–5 separated two-color rectangles. Select the widest two-color rectangle, treat its minority color as markers, and create an output the size/color of the monochrome rectangle. Transfer each marker by its distance from the nearest source edges; exact edge ties mirror to both sides, and out-of-bounds projections are dropped.

Keep every solid nonzero full row or column. Erase all other cells, then move each isolated off-line pixel whose color matches a full line to the cell immediately outside its nearest matching line. Compare row and column distance, choosing the row on an exact tie. Off-line colors without a matching line are distractors and disappear.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~10-12) with: (a) ONE connected MOTIF (3-5 cells, polyomino-shaped) in some non-{0, 8} color, placed at a random position; (b) EXACTLY ONE color-8 (cyan) MARKER single-cell, placed elsewhere with no non-bg neighbors. Rule: find the motif (the largest connected non-{0, 8} component) and the marker (the lone color-8 cell). Compute the motif's bbox and CENTER. ERASE the motif from its current location and PASTE its bbox-cropped image onto the grid CENTERED at the marker cell. The marker is OVERWRITTEN by the motif (or remains if not covered). Net: input has a motif + a far-away marker; output has the motif relocated so its center sits where the marker was.

Place three or four isolated, single-color polyominoes on a zero background.  Extract each tight bbox crop and sort the components by (cell count, bbox height, bbox width, color) ascending.  Pack the crops left-to-right with one zero column between them and bottom-align every crop to the tallest one.  Each profile demonstrates two sort keys, so every four-of-five query rotation covers area, height, width, and color.

An 11..14 by 12..16 zero grid contains one connected 3..5-cell color-5 template, one or two exact translated color-2 copies, and one or two same-size color-2 distractors.  At least one distractor is a nonidentical rotation or reflection of the template.  Exact same-orientation copies become color 4; all other candidates become color 1; the template remains 5.

Two equal-width panels are placed horizontally. Output cell (r,c) is 5 exactly when both aligned panel cells are 0, otherwise 0. Normal draws contain all four aligned occupancy states, use distinct non-5 panel colors, and vary dimensions, colors, exact both-zero count, and layout.
One connected monochrome component and one color-9 anchor immediately outside its bounding box; sweep the whole component away from the anchor to the wall, preserving holes and concavities.
Compress nested filled rectangles to one-cell concentric rings in their outside-to-inside color order.

Find every 4-connected nonzero component, even when a component mixes colors. Crop each component, count enclosed black regions inside its bounding box, sort by increasing hole count, increasing painted area, and finally the first row-major component color, then pack the crops left-to-right with one black separator column.

A 0-background grid with two to five active rows. Each active row has one or two separated interior singleton seeds; the canonical rule casts their colors horizontally until an original seed or grid edge.

Grid split by a color-9 cross into square quadrants. A->B demonstrates a dihedral transform (cw/180/ccw/lr/ud); the rule applies it to C in the answer quadrant. The quadrant size, transform, A/C patterns and colors vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~31 distinct). Output is T(C), so bounded; inputs are large.

A non-rectangular two-color template (common cell + accent L) plus 1-3 rectangular seeds (2x2 common block + 2x1 new-color block), placed at random separated positions on a random-sized grid. The rule scales the template at each seed, replacing the accent with the seed's new color.

An asymmetric square tile is expanded into a 3-by-3 block mosaic. Even-numbered block rows flip the tile up/down and even-numbered block columns flip it left/right, so corner blocks are rotated 180 degrees and the center block is unchanged.

Grid (h, w~6-8) with: (a) COLOR-8 (cyan) OUTER WALL — full border of color 8; (b) OPTIONAL INTERIOR WALLS by LAYOUT: none (single room), vertical (full-height color-8 column at random interior col), horizontal (full-width color-8 row), or cross (both a horizontal + vertical wall dividing into 4 rooms); (c) COLORED SEEDS — 2-3 seeds per room placed at random interior cells in DISTINCT non-{0, 8} colors. Rule (BFS FLOOD: EACH 0-CELL GOES TO ITS NEAREST SEED'S COLOR, BLOCKED BY 8-WALLS): For EACH bg-0 cell in any room: compute BFS DISTANCES (through 0-cells blocked by 8-walls) to ALL SEEDS in that room. ASSIGN the cell to its NEAREST seed's color. PAINT it with that color. Seeds and walls stay. Net: each room partitions into Voronoi-like regions colored by nearest seed.

One hollow rectangular frame on a zero background contains exactly two distinct seed colors on one row. The left seed anchors the top-left interior color, the right seed is the alternating color, and both seeds already agree with the checkerboard parity they demonstrate.

Grid split into FIVE n x n panels (n=4 or 5) by 1-col gaps: panel0 = SHAPE1, panel1 = a single LABEL1 cell, panel2 = SHAPE2, panel3 = LABEL2 cell, panel4 = QUERY shape. The query equals a rotation (id/90/180/270) of exactly one of shape1/shape2. Rule: output the query panel recolored to the matching shape's label color. Shape colors are distractors -- only the shape (under rotation) and the label colors matter.

On a fresh same-size color-0 canvas, replace every isolated nonzero seed at (r,c) by a same-color diagonal X containing the center and the four one-step diagonal neighbors (r±1,c±1); clip only the arms that fall outside the grid. Every seed is processed independently.

A 22..24 by 17..20 color-0 grid contains two separated one-cell-wide vertical bars of equal height in green (3), plus an analogous pair in cyan (8), with the two color pairs vertically separated. Each pair emits two bidirectional step-rays from its outer bbox columns: the rays move one column outward per full bar-height of vertical distance. Output cells are green or cyan on one color's rays, magenta (6) at intersections, and 0 elsewhere. Four canonical-anchor profiles are followed by four decorrelated companion profiles, covering both vertical orders, height-1 bars, and both intersection branches without locking independent axes.
Gray frame with a gap; rule fills interior and extends a line through the gap.

Find every 2x2 window with exactly three cells of one non-background colour and one zero, then fill that zero with the same colour. Windows are evaluated from the original input in one simultaneous pass. Scenes include canonical-profile isolated motifs, connected multi-window components, repeated colours, and mixed-colour near-matches.

A grid is almost symmetric left/right or up/down. Count mismatches for both axes, choose the axis with fewer mismatches (left/right on a tie), then restore empty cells from their nonzero mirrors. Patterns may use one or several colors.

Two aligned binary 3-column panels separated by a uniform color 2..9. Racket emits 2 exactly at paired 1/1 positions and 0 elsewhere. Ordinary samples teach all four Boolean inputs; crossed size/separator profiles retain canonical 3x7 gray-separator support in every difficulty band.
Crop the original grid to the first row-major object whose color has minimum global frequency.

Six- to twelve-row grids containing 3-8 same-color vertical runs in 2-3 colors.  Scheduled profiles include canonical sparse bars, multiple runs in one column, touching colors, connected systems, and reused colors.

A one-cell-thick, uniform nonzero lattice partitions the input into a 3×3 through 5×5 array of equal square cells. The first cell of every macro-row contains the same marker mask in a row-specific color. Exactly one non-marker cell contains a larger monochrome template. The answer clears every data cell and stamps that template mask into every cell of each macro-row, recolored with that row's marker color; separators stay unchanged.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~11-13) with 3 BASE BLOBS — H_LINE_3 (1×3 horizontal), V_LINE_3 (3×1 vertical), SQUARE_2X2 — plus 0-2 random EXTRA shapes (4-cell lines, 2×3/3×2 rects, 3×3 squares) placed at non-touching positions in random non-2-3-4 colors (from {5,6,7,8,9} for bases, {1,2,3,4} for extras). Each blob is isolated (no 4-touching). Rule (ORIENTATION-BASED RECOLOR): for EACH 4-CONNECTED BLOB, COMPUTE its BBOX (bb_h × bb_w). RECOLOR every cell of the blob based on bbox shape: bb_w > bb_h → COLOR 2 (red, horizontal); bb_h > bb_w → COLOR 3 (green, vertical); bb_h == bb_w → COLOR 4 (yellow, square). Blob cell POSITIONS preserved; only colors change. Net: every blob recolored by orientation classifier (h-line→2, v-line→3, square→4).
Two frames contain asymmetric interior marks; one odd and one even frame color teach both parity flips.
