0-bg grid (h = block_h = 3-4, w = 2*block_w + 1 with block_w=4-5) structured as TWO EQUAL-SIZE PANELS separated by a full-height COLOR-8 (cyan) DIVIDER column at col bw. (a) LEFT PANEL (cols 0..bw-1) is a BINARY 0/1 MASK with 4-7 color-1 (blue) cells; (b) RIGHT PANEL (cols bw+1..2*bw) contains 4-7 arbitrary non-{0, 1, 8} colored cells from a 5-color palette. Rule: use the LEFT PANEL as a BINARY MASK (color-1 = keep, 0 = clear). For EVERY CELL in the RIGHT PANEL at (r, c), check the CORRESPONDING LEFT cell at (r, c - bw - 1): if it's 1 (blue), KEEP the right cell's color; if it's 0, CLEAR the right cell to 0. Output: the right panel (cropped or in place) after the mask filter. Net: left binary mask filters the right color block, keeping only cells the mask permits.

Fill a 5..18 by 5..18 grid with one background color and place exactly one seed of a color from the fixed cycle 0,5,2,8,9,6,1,3,4. The background may be any nonzero ARC color (the selected Racket mode ignores zero). Color every output cell by Manhattan distance from the seed, advancing through the fixed cycle from the seed's color. Defaults cover corner, edge, center, and interior seeds and include an 8x8 canonical-profile branch in every difficulty band.

0-bg grid (size varies). Exactly TWO blue(1) cells at distinct rows AND distinct cols define BBOX A; exactly TWO red(2) cells likewise define BBOX B. The two bboxes are built around a shared anchor so they overlap. Rule: paint the RECTANGLE INTERSECTION of A and B with COLOR 8 (cyan). A non-{1,2} decoration sits outside both rects. The grid size, the two rects (corner positions / sizes / aspect) and the decoration all vary freely (was a fixed 2+2 cell layout).

Split at the full-height colour-9 separator. Treat every non-zero left-panel cell as a binary keep mask and copy the corresponding right-panel colour into the same-sized output; write zero where the left panel is zero.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~9-12) with 2-4 ACTIVE ROWS, each containing EXACTLY 2 COLOR-7 (orange) cells at distinct columns (c1, c2) with c2 ≥ c1 + 2 (gap of ≥1 bg cell between them). Plus 0-2 INACTIVE ROWS with a SINGLE orange cell (distractor) and 0-3 INACTIVE ROWS with non-orange distractor cells. Spans between endpoints in active rows are initially 0. Rule (PER-ROW HORIZONTAL ENDPOINT FILL): for EACH ROW, COUNT the COLOR-7 cells. If EXACTLY 2 (the endpoint pair) AND all cells BETWEEN them are 0, FILL the ENTIRE INCLUSIVE SPAN (cells from min_c to max_c in that row) with COLOR 7. Rows with 0, 1, or 3+ orange cells unchanged. Net: each row with exactly 2 orange endpoints gets filled between them; single-endpoint rows stay.

A 0-background 6..10 by 8..10 grid contains two or three distinct colors, each used at exactly two opposite bbox corners.  Exactly one pair spans both rows and columns and the remaining pair(s) are collinear.  The pair bboxes are disjoint.  Fill every pair's complete axis-aligned bbox with its own color.
Fill every cell with the color of its Manhattan-nearest corner marker; break distance ties in top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right order.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ [4, 14]) with: (a) ROW-0 TEMPLATE — a set of TEMPLATE COLS (1..w/2 cells) painted DOT COLOR (any non-0 non-2 color) at row 0 using a chosen layout (scattered/left/right/even/endpoints/alternating); (b) MARKER ROWS — for 1..h/2 ROWS r > 0, a MARKER cell of the same DOT COLOR is placed at a MARKER COL (chosen as last/first/random from cols NOT in the template). Rule (EXPAND MARKER ROWS AT TEMPLATE COLS WITH COLOR 2): identify the TEMPLATE COLS (non-0 cells in row 0) and the DOT COLOR. For EACH ROW r > 0: if r has ≥1 non-0 cell at any col NOT in the template (a marker), then PAINT every TEMPLATE COL of row r with COLOR 2 (red). Marker cells stay at dot color. Row 0 (template) stays. Rows without markers stay all-0. Net: each marker-row gets red dots at the template columns, marking the intersection.
Remove border-touching same-color 4-components; preserve all interior components.
Multi-color grid; each non-background color layer is flipped vertically inside its own bounding box without cross-layer overwrite.

Full-height foreground carrier columns mark regularly spaced slots. Sort the following foreground/zero bit columns by ascending foreground population while leaving carriers and zero separators fixed; equal-count columns keep their original left-to-right order.
Place 2..4 distinct-color pairs at opposite corners of disjoint, nondegenerate rectangles on a zero background. Fill each inclusive bounding rectangle with its pair color.
Sparse row markers expand to inclusive horizontal spans, including singleton rows.
1-3 rows each have 2 cells of the same color at separated columns.

0-bg grid (h~12-25, w~12-25) with: (a) RIGHT EDGE GRAY LINE — every cell in column w-1 painted color 5 (the gray edge); (b) 2-6 COLORED BARS placed in the interior (rows 1..h-3, cols 1..w-6), each a small 1×L or 2×L rectangle (L ∈ {1..3}, height 1 or 2) painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 5} color drawn from a palette (warm/cool/primary/broad kinds). Bars are placed at non-overlapping rows (every 3rd row available) so they are disconnected from each other and from the gray edge. Rule (EACH COLORED BAR PROJECTS A RECTANGLE RIGHTWARD TOWARD THE GRAY EDGE — NEARER BARS OVERWRITE OVERLAPPING PROJECTIONS): for EACH non-{0, 5} BAR at rows [r..r+rh-1], cols [c..c+length-1]: PROJECT a RECTANGLE rightward — paint cells [r..r+rh-1] × [c..w-2] with the bar's color (extending from the bar through to one cell before the gray edge). Bars with overlapping projection rows compete — the NEARER bar (higher c value, i.e., closer to the gray edge) OVERWRITES the farther bar's projection in the overlap zone. The gray edge stays color 5. Net: each bar's color streaks rightward to the edge; nearer bars cover farther ones.

0-bg grid with: (a) ROW 0 MARKERS -- K (2-5) color-1 cells at random columns; (b) a random BODY MOTIF (connected polyomino, varied shape/color) below row 0. Rule: count K row-0 markers, crop the body to the motif bbox, tile it horizontally K times with 1-col gaps. The motif shape/color, K and grid size all vary.

A 0-background 9-10 by 10-12 grid contains exactly four distinct-colored monochromatic 4-connected objects. Sort objects by cell count ascending, breaking equal-area ties by lexicographic bounding box, then repaint their unchanged cells 2, 4, 6, and 8 on a blank grid. Different input colors may touch; color, scan order, and the numeric input palette are distractors.
Odd square {0,2,9} scenes contain a central color-9 marker and three of four rotated copies of a color-2 motif; complete the missing quadrant.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 2-4 CONNECTED BLOBS each a 3-5 cell 4-connected component grown via grow_blob, painted in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {1..9}. Blobs are placed at non-touching positions (tracked in used set) AND have STRICTLY DISTINCT BBOX CENTERS (integer division: center = ((rmin+rmax)//2, (cmin+cmax)//2)). Blobs are size ≥ 3 so the reduction rule is non-identity. Rule (REPLACE EACH BLOB WITH A SINGLE CELL AT ITS BBOX CENTER): for EACH 4-CONNECTED non-bg BLOB of color C: COMPUTE its bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2). COMPUTE the BBOX CENTER cr = (r1+r2) // 2, cc = (c1+c2) // 2. CLEAR every cell of the blob to bg-0. PAINT the single cell (cr, cc) with COLOR C. Other blobs are reduced independently. Net: each multi-cell colored blob collapses into a single-cell marker at its bbox center, preserving color.

One connected single-color object on zero background: frames and lattices alternate with irregular rails, sparse bottom rows, and left/right clipping witnesses. Translate each occupied row by (0,-1,0,+1) indexed by its distance above the LAST NONEMPTY row. Preserve its exact holes and details. Default lessons use four demonstrations; explicit controls are research draws and are checked against the same Racket authority.
Move a colored pattern to the missing corner using one diagonal bracket for row alignment and the other bracket for interior-column alignment.
Horizontal color-2 runs of EXACT length 3 + distractor runs of other lengths (2, 4, 5, …). Rule recolors exactly-length-3 horizontal runs from 2 → 7; other runs stay 2.

Some objects are exact rectangle outlines (frames), others are filled plus shapes. Rule keeps each object in its own columns; frames slide UP and pluses slide DOWN until they hit the top/bottom edge respectively, packing densely without overlap. Colors preserved.
Draw a cyan outline through two opposite green corners while preserving every occupied cell.

0-bg grid scattered with n1 color-1 cells, n2 color-2, n3 color-3. Rule outputs a 3-row bar chart (rows = colors 1,2,3) of width = max count, each row left-filled with its count. The three counts, positions and grid size vary.

0-background grid with an exact requested count of horizontal same-color runs. Each ordinary run is a contiguous nonzero segment in one row, has length 2-5, and no row contains two abutting runs. At least one run has length at least 3, so endpoint reduction is observable. The canonical rule creates a fresh empty grid and paints only each run's first and last cells in its original color; all run interiors become 0. Explicit degenerate textures (blank, vertical-only, singleton-only) are dimension-honoring negative probes rather than ordinary samples.

Every separated three-cell L emits a same-color diagonal ray away from its missing 2x2 corner, beginning one cell beyond that missing corner. The distribution covers all four directions, repeated and distinct object colors, 1..5 pieces, 8..16 dimensions, varied positions and ray lengths, with collision-free rays and a 10x10 repeated-color canonical anchor.

A 6-8 by 9-11 zero-background grid has one full gray (5) vertical axis, 2-7 colored source cells on its mirrorable left side, and optional right-side distractors. Rebuild a clean grid: preserve the gray axis and left sources, reflect every source across the gray column, erase unrelated right marks, and overwrite occupied mirror targets with the source color.

0-background grid with three equal panels separated by two full-height color-8 columns. Panel B is panel A after at least one addition and one deletion. Apply that edit stencil to differently colored panel C: additions take C's color and deletions become 0. Every generated lesson makes both operations visibly affect C.

Three or four equal-width boxes are separated by full-height border columns.  The same connected marker appears at one shared horizontal offset while its top row advances by a constant signed step.  Output one new framed box and extrapolate the marker one more step; add one extra blank row only when the positive step exceeds the marker height.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-11) with 2-4 ISOLATED diagonal DOMINOES — each is 2 same-color cells at diagonal adjacency: (r, c) and (r+1, c±1). Different dominoes use distinct colors and have ≥2-cell buffer. Rule: for each cell (r, c), for each diagonal direction (dr, dc) ∈ {(1,1),(1,-1),(-1,1),(-1,-1)}: if input[r][c] is a non-bg color c0, input[r+dr][c+dc] is also c0 (forming a domino in that direction), input[r+2dr][c+2dc] is 0 (open end), and (r-dr, c-dc) is NOT c0 (so r,c is the outer end) → set output[r+2dr][c+2dc] = c0. Net effect: each diagonal domino grows by 1 cell at its OPEN END (the end not next to a same-color neighbor).
Erase every globally unique nonzero color; retain repeated colors.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~12-14) with: (a) 2 closed color-1 (blue) FRAMES at fixed positions (1, 1)-(4, 4) and (5, 7)-(8, 11); (b) each frame's INTERIOR contains exactly ONE non-{0, 1} MARKER cell in a distinct color; (c) one color-5 DECORATION cell at (0, w-1) outside frames. Rule: for each closed color-1 frame, find any non-{0, 1} cells strictly inside its bbox. If exactly ONE unique color is found, FILL the frame's strict interior with that color. Outside-frame decorations stay; frames stay color 1.

Fixed 11×11 0-bg grid structured as a 3×3 MACROGRID of 3×3 MACRO CELLS separated by 1-cell SEPARATORS (rows 3, 7 and cols 3, 7 are separator gaps). Each macro cell at (tr, tc) for tr, tc ∈ {0, 1, 2}: occupies rows tr*4..tr*4+2 × cols tc*4..tc*4+2 (3×3). One CLEAN TEMPLATE macro cell (the top-left at (0, 0)) contains a 3×3 PATTERN using TWO COLORS (majority_color and minority_color, both non-{0, 5}). The TEMPLATE variant ∈ {diag, corner, bar}. ALL OTHER 8 macro cells are filled with COLOR 5 (gray) — i.e., the template is the only non-5 macro cell. Rule: identify the TEMPLATE (the macro cell that contains NO COLOR 5 — the 'clean' template). For EACH OTHER macro cell (currently all-5), STAMP the template's pattern at the corresponding macro-cell position — where template has MINORITY color (the 2 in the encoding), KEEP that macro cell as 5; where template has MAJORITY color (the 1), CLEAR the macro cell to 0. Net: template controls which macro cells stay 5 and which become 0 across the 3×3 macrogrid.

Split the grid into exactly four equal panels at the three full color-5 separator columns. The first panel is a one-cell query-color key. Count that color in each of the three candidate panels and return the unique candidate with the largest count; other colors are distractors.

Scattered cells of 2-4 colors where one color is uniquely most-frequent. Rule outputs a single row of length N (total nonzero cells) all in the majority color. Total count N (output width), the majority color, and grid size all vary.

A 3x3 to 5x5 multicolor grid has one strict most-common NONZERO color. Its lead may be clear or only one cell over the runner-up. Zero is absent, sparse, or more common than every nonzero color, so the solver must ignore zero when taking the mode. Fill an output of identical dimensions entirely with that unique nonzero mode color.

On a zero background, each separated nonzero singleton seed expands on a fresh same-size output into its Manhattan-radius-1 diamond: the seed cell plus its up/down/left/right neighbours, all in the seed's own colour.  Out-of-bounds arms are clipped.  Ordinary lessons alternate between canonical anchors and scenes containing both an edge-clipped seed and two separated seeds that reuse a colour.

29x29 input containing 25 five-by-five tiles separated by solid lines; 24 tiles are identical and one erases 1..5 consensus foreground cells to the tile background. Output is the consensus tile with every disagreement coordinate replaced by color 1.

A red(2) source and adjacent blue(1) heading launch a beam. Empty path cells become 8; diagonal mirrors 3/4 turn the beam according to their orientation; a canonical-scale gray(5) border frame blocks the final leg. Every requested mirror lies on a compact serpentine route; 3+ mirror routes mix relative turn directions, and optional interior blocker cells add exact wall-count variation.
Extract a one-row palette in first-appearance order.
Hollow 3-color plus signs with zero centers for the rule to fill.
1-2 small 3x3 4-frames each with a single non-4 center color.

Find the unique full row or column of color 8.  For every color-7 cell, paint its reflection across that line color 7 while preserving the original 7 and the divider. Reflection targets become 7 even when occupied; all other cells, including distractors, stay unchanged. Out-of-bounds reflections are skipped without deleting their sources.
Rotate each isolated straight odd-length component 90 degrees around its center on an orange canvas.

0-bg grid with exactly two ISOLATED connected objects that share a common normalized sub-shape T (a random polyomino) plus disjoint extra cells. Rule: take the first two objects, normalize each, output the bbox of their cell intersection painted 8 -- which equals T. The target T, the two shapes' extras, colors and grid size all vary.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-9 / 10-14, w ∈ 8-11 / 12-16, depending on difficulty) with: MULTIPLE L-SHAPED 3-CELL GROUPS — n_shapes ∈ 1-6 placements, each shape is an L-tromino (3 of the 4 cells of a 2×2 block) drawn from LSHAPES (4 rotations: NE / NW / SE / SW). Each L is painted in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from a 1-6 color palette. Placements use a spread-rejection of 4 cells between origins (no two L origins within 4 cells of each other). The 4th cell of each 2×2 block is 0 by construction (since only 3 cells of the L were painted). Rule (ITERATIVELY FILL THE 4TH CELL OF ANY 2×2 WINDOW WHERE 3 CELLS SHARE A NON-BG COLOR AND THE 4TH IS 0): REPEATEDLY SCAN every 2×2 WINDOW of the grid. When a window has EXACTLY 3 non-bg cells SHARING THE SAME COLOR c AND the 4th cell is 0: PAINT that 4th cell = c. CHAIN: the newly-filled cell may complete adjacent 2×2 windows, cascading further fills. ITERATE UNTIL no 2×2 window still has a fillable corner. Net: each L-tromino becomes a 2×2 solid block; cascading growth may extend beyond the initial Ls when filled cells complete adjacent triples.

A 1-shape (5-9 cell random polyomino) and a 2-shape (a proper subset of it) placed apart. Rule: output normalized(1-cells) minus normalized(2-cells), cropped to bbox and painted 3. The 1-shape, the dropped subset and grid size vary.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-14) with 3-5 BLOBS each of a DISTINCT SIZE (sampled from ascending/wide-spread/tight-spread distributions over sizes ~1-9) in DISTINCT COLORS from {1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} (NOT color 2, since 2 is the rule's output). Blobs are non-touching (4-conn separation). The SMALLEST BLOB has a STRICTLY UNIQUE size (no tie at minimum). Rule (FIND SMALLEST OBJECT BY SIZE, RECOLOR TO 2): find every 4-CONNECTED NON-0 COMPONENT. COMPUTE the CELL COUNT of each. IDENTIFY the COMPONENT with MINIMUM size. RECOLOR ALL its cells to COLOR 2 (red). Other components stay unchanged. Net: the smallest blob turns red; all others keep their colors.

A sparse top-row palette recolors distinct-area color-8 components after sorting them largest-to-smallest; normalized shapes are bottom-aligned and packed with one blank column between them on the minimal canvas.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-11, w ∈ 11-13) with: (a) ONE HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME of size fh × fw (fh, fw ∈ 3-4) drawn at a random non-overlapping interior position in palette[0] color; (b) 1-2 SOLID 2×2 BLOBS in palette[1:] colors (distinct from frame color), placed at random non-touching positions (no 4-adjacency with other blobs or the frame). Palette drawn from {1..9}\{0}. Rule (KEEP BLOBS WHOSE BBOX INTERIOR HAS AT LEAST ONE 0-CELL FULLY ENCLOSED BY THE BLOB (HOLEY OBJECTS); DROP BLOBS WITH NO HOLES (SOLID OBJECTS)): EXTRACT every 4-connected non-bg COMPONENT. For EACH: COMPUTE its bbox; CHECK if any 0-cell inside the bbox is fully enclosed by the component's cells. IF YES (holey): KEEP. IF NO (solid): ERASE every cell of the blob to 0. Net: hollow frames survive; solid blobs vanish.
Horizontal same-color one-cell gaps are completed amid multiple targets, longer same-color spans, different-color flanks, busy rows, and vertical decoys.
Remove the unique color-9 anchor and copy every other colored cell to its 0, 90, 180 and 270 degree rotations around that anchor.
Recolor yellow tips green and extend yellow/cyan/red bands across a full separator in triggered lanes.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-1 2-cell segment and a color-2 point define a bounding box; one TARGET object sits inside it and DECOY objects sit outside. Rule: output the object fully inside the box, cropped to its bbox in color 8. The grid size, box, target shape/color and decoys all vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~18 distinct).
Mark the top-left cell of every solid same-color non-background 2x2 window, including overlapping windows.

0-bg grid with a full color-5 divider (either a complete row or a complete column). Orange (color 7) cells lie on ONE side of the divider; the OTHER side may carry decorations in colors ≠ {0,5,7,1}. Rule: detect whether the divider is row-shaped or col-shaped (full rows tried first); for each color-7 cell at (r,c), compute its reflection across the divider: if row-divider at row d, mirror to (2d-r, c); if col-divider at col d, mirror to (r, 2d-c). Paint color 1 (blue) at the reflected position IF in-bounds AND the cell is currently 0 (existing decorations are preserved, not overwritten). Original 7s and all other cells are kept as-is.

Rows 0 and 1 are independent sparse color lists: scan each row left-to-right and discard zeros. Pair the first min(source_count, target_count) entries. Rows 2+ are the body. The output removes both header rows, recolors paired source values, and preserves zeros, unpaired sources, target-colored distractors, and other unmapped body values.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with: (a) one BASE motif in color 3 (green), 3-4 cells, placed in the upper-left region; (b) 2-3 MARKER PAIRS in the right region: each pair = a CODE cell (color in {2, 4, 6, 9}) immediately to the LEFT of a color-1 (blue) MARKER cell. Rule: extract base = normalized cells of color 3. For each color-1 marker at (r, c), look at code = g[r][c-1]. Decode code → rotation count: 2→0, 4→1, 6→2, 9→3. Rotate base CW that many times. Stamp the rotated base at the marker position (anchor at marker's (r, c)), painted color 8 (cyan). Original base, markers, codes all replaced by 0 in output except where stamped cells overwrite.

A black grid contains exactly two one-cell rectangular frames: a yellow (4) outer frame and a blue (1) inner frame separated uniformly by one or two blank cells. Fill the annulus inside the outer frame but outside the inner frame's bounding box with cyan (8), preserving both frames and the empty interior of the inner frame.

On a zero-background grid, every nonzero color appearing exactly twice in different rows and columns marks opposite corners of a rectangle. Paint that rectangle's complete border in the same color while preserving all other input cells. Exactly-two collinear colors and colors with other multiplicities are distractors. Intersecting borders are processed in row-major first-occurrence color order, so the later qualifying color wins.

A 3xW strip (W is 19 or 29) has all-zero outer rows. Row 1 contains 2 or 3 distinct seed colors at the first triangular columns: [0,1] or [0,1,3]. Read those colors left-to-right as a sequence. For k=0,1,..., paint row 1, column k(k+1)/2 with seed[k mod n] while that column fits. All non-triangular cells remain unchanged (and are zero in lawful inputs).

A rectangular grid has four distinct nonzero border colors: top, bottom, left, and right, with zero corners. Sparse interior pixels sit at least one blank cell away from the border. Pixels matching a border color move to the adjacent inner wall while preserving the perpendicular coordinate; one-off non-border distractor colors are removed.
Read the unique nonzero marker in row 0. Preserve that marker, erase every cell of the same colour below row 0, and leave every other cell unchanged.
Each nonzero color marks two diagonal corners. In row-major first-appearance order, draw that color's bounding-box border on a fresh background-0 canvas; later borders overwrite earlier ones.
Three separated monochrome components become horizontal bars. Rows are ordered by increasing component color; each bar length is that component's cell area, and the output width is the largest area.
Hollow gray frame; rule fills interior with cycling distance-from-border colors.
Select the top glyph compatible with sparse frame-interior evidence and expand it blockwise inside the cropped frame.

A 0-background grid contains two to four singleton markers. All markers share one nonzero color and occupy distinct rows and distinct columns. For every marker, paint its entire row and entire column in that marker color. The output is the union of all such full crosses; every other cell remains 0.
Small 2-color template + 1-2 rect-frames in other colors (large enough to fit centered template).
Magenta components touching exactly one border are recolored yellow.
Complete every 3x3 perimeter that has seven equal nonzero cells and one missing perimeter cell; ignore the center and leave mixed-color near-rings unchanged.

On background 4, two or three separated multicolor source templates each contain a globally unique accent cell. Isolated dots matching an accent stamp that template with the accent aligned to the dot; isolated colors absent from all templates are decoys and vanish. The output contains only the stamped copies, not the source templates or original dots.
Sparse 0/3 grid with explicit 3x3 empty blocks; rule paints them 1.

Split the 9x3 input into three stacked 3x3 panels. Return the first panel from top to bottom that differs from its main-diagonal transpose. Ordinary lessons include two-asymmetric-panel counterexamples so first match, rather than unique or last match, is identifiable.

A 0-background grid contains one or two hollow color-6 rectangular frames and one or two filled color-6 rectangular distractors, all as separate components, plus a short non-6 decoration. Fill the strict interior of every hollow frame with color 8; leave filled rectangles unchanged. Canonical-size profiles are sampled densely, frame aspect and scale vary constructively, and all declared numeric controls are exact.
Color-1 src + color-2 dst markers define a translation vector; rule translates each non-{0,1,2} cell by (dst-src) on a fresh empty grid (markers erased).

n panels separated by full color-9 columns; panel 0 holds a proto motif. Each later panel is either a rotation of the proto (matches) or a different-size motif (doesn't). Rule outputs a 1x(n-1) row with 8 where panel k's onion-depth-map matches panel 0's under rotation. Panel count, proto shape, match pattern and colors vary.
skills: normalized comparison, rotation reasoning, candidate selection

summary: 0-bg grid (size varies) with n scattered blue(1) cells plus optional ignored decoy-color cells. Rule: output a 3x3 count display -- the first min(n,4) positions of a fixed T-order are colored 2. The blue count, blue/decoy positions, decoy colors and grid size vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~23 distinct). Output is a 3x3 count display, so distinct OUTPUTS are bounded (~5: n=0..4+); distinct INPUTS are large.

Overlay a square zero-background grid with its anti-diagonal reflection. A nonzero cell at (r,c) writes the same color to (n-1-c,n-1-r) while the original remains. If both reflected partners are occupied, their values swap because the reflection is read from an immutable snapshot.

A 7..16 by 9..16 zero-background grid contains 2..5 color-2 emitters and 1..4 disconnected color-5 wall components. Wall geometry varies between singleton/two-cell blockers and longer horizontal or vertical segments. Each emitter becomes color 8 and casts color-8 rays up, down, left, and right until the first color-5 wall cell or the grid edge.
Recover the smallest periodic tile consistent with all non-magenta cells, then replace magenta (6) noise by repeating that tile across the grid.

A zero-background grid contains exactly one green(3) anchor, a cyan(8) template represented by offsets from that anchor, and 1-5 red(2) destination markers.  Clear the input and stamp the exact cyan offsets at every red marker.  The default curriculum alternates all four linked 13x13 canonical profiles with asymmetric templates, includes single and multiple destinations, and includes both overlapping and separated copies so fixed-shape, horizontal-mirroring, first-marker-only, local-3x3, bbox-fill, XOR-overlap, and marker-as-answer shortcuts are visible.

Sparse 0-background grids contain 2-6 exact horizontal [2,3,0] triggers, 1-2 reversed [3,2] negative witnesses, and optionally 0-3 blocked [2,3,3] near-matches. Scan every row left to right: for each exact [2,3,0], recolor only the trailing 0 to cyan 8. Reversed and blocked arrangements are unchanged. Layouts deliberately vary edge positions, multiple triggers in one row, and trigger/reverse motifs in the same row so row-count, fixed-position, and one-match shortcuts fail.

n (3-5) non-touching blobs in distinct colors with one repeated-size pair and at least one differently-sized blob; output is the nxn matrix with 8 where two objects share size, else 0. Object count, sizes and positions vary.

0-bg grid (size varies). A SOURCE L-frame: color 2 at the origin, color 3 one cardinal step along basis vector vx, color 4 one perpendicular cardinal step along vy. A small color-8 (cyan) MOTIF sits within Chebyshev radius 3 of the origin. ONE MATCHING candidate frame (color 5/6/7) uses the SAME oriented basis (vx,vy); 1-2 DISTRACTOR candidate frames use a DIFFERENT ordered basis. Rule: read the source basis + motif (in local coords), and copy the motif into every candidate whose basis matches — here exactly the matching frame. Distractors stay untouched. The grid size, the basis orientation (8 options), the motif, and all frame positions vary freely (was a fixed 13x25 layout with only 3 origins x 3 motifs).
skills: orientation matching, candidate selection, frame-relative copy

summary: 0-bg grid (h, w~7-12) with 2-5 SEPARATED COLOR-2 (red) L-TRIOMINOES, each fitting in a 2x2 box with EXACTLY ONE CORNER MISSING (3 cells of color 2 painted in 3 of the 4 corners of a 2x2 window, the 4th corner is 0). The missing corner varies per L (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). L-triominoes are spaced with ≥3-cell padding so they remain isolated. Rule: for every 3-cell L-triomino of color 2, IDENTIFY the single MISSING CORNER (the 4th cell of its 2x2 bbox that is 0). FILL that missing corner with COLOR 3 (green). The original 3 red cells STAY red. Net: each red L gains a green completion-corner, forming a 2-color 2x2 square.

Find every 4-connected blue(1) object, normalize its bounding-box crop, sort the objects by cell area from smallest to largest (normalized shape breaks an area tie), recolor the object cells cyan(8), and pack the crops left-to-right, top-aligned, with exactly one background(0) column between successive crops. Ignore the single orange(7) distractor object.
Top two rows encode 3-4 source→target color pairs; body motifs use the source colors so the rule recolors them by column-wise lookup.
Cyan dots on bg=0; rule paints red one cell below each cyan.

0-background grid split into 3-4 equal panels by full-height color-9 divider columns. Each panel contains four color-2 rectangle corners. Complete every panel by row-then-column closure and output one panel-sized grid, painting 8 wherever at least two completed rectangles overlap.
Color-7 size-three 2x2 L objects recolored to 8.

Read the main diagonal of the square nested-L staircase. Strip an optional trailing zero padding band, then double the input height and width. Output cell (r,c) is active_diagonal[max(r,c) modulo period]. Repeated active colors are lawful and the final zero is optional.
Fill only blue hollow frames whose outer height and width both equal four.

Keep each nonzero cell iff it has a same-colour cardinal neighbour. Alternating canonical-linked and counterexample-rich profiles teach that the condition is local, same-colour, and 4-connected rather than a global colour-frequency, 8-neighbour, arbitrary-contact, or one-axis rule.

0-bg grid (h~7-12, w~8-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) MARKER at (r, c1) and ONE COLOR-3 (green) MARKER at (r, c2) — same row r (random interior), with c2 ≥ c1 + 3; (b) SCATTERED COLOR-5 (gray) WALL CELLS at ~18% density in OTHER rows (NOT row r), placed at random rows for each column. The direct horizontal route between markers is unblocked. Rule (BFS SHORTEST PATH FROM RED TO GREEN, PAINT CYAN): from the COLOR-2 red marker, BFS through all 4-conn 0-cells, AVOIDING color-5 walls and the markers themselves, to find the SHORTEST PATH to the COLOR-3 green marker. PAINT every cell on that path with COLOR 8 (cyan). Markers and walls stay. Net: cyan shortest-path connects red→green across the grid.

2x2 lattice of THxTW tiles separated by color-9 dividers; the bottom-right tile is blank. Rule: output a THxTW tile marking cells with odd occupancy among the 3 visible tiles. Tile dimensions (2..5 each), density and colors vary; output is THxTW (incl non-square).
skills: matrix reasoning, boolean composition, reduced output

summary: Keep every component touching any outer border; erase all interior components.

Place cyan 8 markers on one edge and red 2 markers on a perpendicular edge. Each cyan marker emits a ray inward. Whenever the ray reaches a red marker's row or column, it steps one cell away from the red edge before continuing. All four cyan edges and both deflection directions are generated, including bottom-origin and red-on-top counterexamples that the canonical demonstrations omit.

0-bg grid (h, w~14-16) with: (a) ONE SOLID RECTANGLE (3×4 to 5×6) in some non-zero rect_color at a random interior position; (b) 2-4 SMALL DOT CELLS placed OUTSIDE the rectangle at positions that are HORIZONTALLY or VERTICALLY ALIGNED with the rectangle's edges (with ~3-cell gaps). Dots use distinct non-{0, rect_color} colors from a 4-color palette. Rule: for EACH dot, determine its ALIGNMENT direction to the rectangle (does it share a row or col with the rectangle's boundary?). CAST a BEAM from the dot's position TOWARD the rectangle in the dot's color, filling every bg cell along the straight-line path between the dot and the rectangle's nearest face. The rectangle and the dots stay. Net: each dot shoots a colored beam toward the largest rectangle.
Two to four separated red objects occupy the left half of an odd-width grid; scheduled non-red controls teach that only red is mirrored as 7.
Read a palette mapping and geometric command from the two-row header, then remap, transform, and tightly crop the object below.

Compact 0-bg grid with 4-7 columns. Each nonempty column is a single color, bottom-justified vertical stack with count 1..h; some columns may be empty. Rule: column count -> left-justified horizontal bar row in that column's first nonzero color.

0-bg grid with a WINNER cluster (random connected blob colored with 4 distinct colors) and 1-2 distractor clusters (fewer distinct colors), all separated. Rule: among adjacency-clusters of touching objects, pick the one with the most distinct colors and output its cell-union cropped, recolored to 8. Winner shape, colors, positions and grid size vary.

Three aligned width-4 panels are separated by two full-height color-5 columns.  A panel-local position becomes color 8 in the output exactly when at least two of the three panels are occupied there.  Generated instances include observable one-panel negatives, two-panel positives, and three-panel positives so common union/intersection/copy shortcuts are contradicted in every example.

Scan rows independently. Each active row has two separated endpoints of one color; fill the inclusive segment between them. Singleton distractors stay unchanged, and the same pair color may be reused in several rows.

Fixed 12×13 0-bg grid with: (a) ROW 0 HEADER — holes encoded as (holes+1) COLOR-1 cells at cols 0..n; (b) g[0][4] = 2 if vertical SYMMETRY required, else 3; (c) g[0][6] = TARGET COLOR. BODY contains 4 OBJECTS at FIXED POSITIONS spanning the 4 (holes, symmetry) combos in {(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)}, each in a DISTINCT non-target color from {2..8}. Output uniq_out=25 (intrinsic — fixed object positions × 4 spec combos × colors). Rule (SELECT MATCHING OBJECT, SCALE 2× + RECOLOR): READ HOLES = (count of 1s in row 0 - 1); SYMMETRY = (g[0][4] == 2); TARGET_COLOR = g[0][6]. SELECT the BODY OBJECT matching (holes, symmetry). UPSCALE 2× and RECOLOR to TARGET_COLOR. EMIT the result. Net: header drives object selection by (holes, sym); output is upscaled in target color.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-13) with 2-4 PAIRS of SAME-COLOR ENDPOINTS, each pair on a DISTINCT ROW. Each pair: cells at (r, c0) and (r, c1) with c1 - c0 ≥ 2 (gap of ≥1 cell). Pair colors are DISTINCT across pairs from {1..9}. No other cells. Rule (BRIDGE SAME-COLOR ENDPOINTS WITH SOLID LINE): For EACH ROW r containing TWO SAME-COLOR ENDPOINTS at columns c0 and c1 (c0 < c1): PAINT every INTERIOR cell (r, c) with c0 < c < c1 in the same color. Endpoints stay. Net: each horizontal endpoint pair becomes a solid colored line.

Color-1 markers on the left border select rows and color-2 markers on the top border select columns.  Return a zero grid with color 8 at every Cartesian-product intersection.  Generated boards use gapped selected coordinates and at least one role-swapped border decoy by default, so a solver must attend to both color and border role rather than treating all border marks alike or filling their bounding rectangle.
Several 1-seeds at different positions + 8-walls; output marks cells reached by exactly 2 rays.

0-bg 5x6/5x7 grid with one small non-rectangular motif (3-5 cells) in a single non-bg colour. Rule: crop that motif and build a 2hx2w 4-fold KALEIDOSCOPE — top-left = motif, top-right = flip-LR, bottom-left = flip-UD, bottom-right = rotate-180.

Grid split into N panels (~5-6) by 1-wide full-height color-9 (maroon) separator COLUMNS. Panel 0 = SOURCE motif; panel 1 = TARGET motif; panels 2..N-1 = CANDIDATES. Each panel has 1-3 cells in some non-{0,9} color. Rule: split panels. Compute source cells (panel-relative positions where panel value != 0); same for target. For each candidate panel, compute its cells, union with source's cells, then check if the UNION (sorted, deduped) equals target's cells. The FIRST candidate matching that test is selected. Output: that candidate panel with all non-zero cells recolored to 8 (cyan). If no match → empty (zeros) grid of candidate size.
skills: inverse boolean reasoning, candidate search, set union

summary: Rewrite each filled monochrome 2x2 block to its anti-diagonal.

Every colored source paints down to the bottom edge. Scheduled stacked, bottom-boundary, and repeated-color profiles teach overwrite and boundary behavior that the canonical distinct-column examples do not expose.
Red singleton cells grow blue cardinal halos into empty neighbors.

A 0-background grid contains two through six pairwise separated nonempty rows and at least two all-zero rows.  Delete every all-zero row while preserving each nonempty row, its order, and the original width.
Red runs define parity toggles for filling cells with alternating 3 and 5.

Generate the canonical 4x19 four-section layout with green divider columns.  Every input constructively includes zero fallback, all four solo-section cases, and all six pairwise overlaps, so the section priority 2 > 3 > 0 > 1 is identifiable.  Five extra aligned cells vary from simple to three/four-way overlaps with difficulty.  Section colors are distinct nonzero non-divider colors and are randomized away from the fixed public color-to-priority mapping unless explicitly overridden.
Remove noise from colored bands: compare column-mode and row-mode coherence, then fill every column or row with its mode on the more coherent axis.

A 0-background grid contains exactly three monochrome 4-connected objects with distinct contour-cell counts. A contour cell is an object cell missing at least one 4-neighbour. Rank objects by contour length ascending, breaking ties by top-left position, and repaint them on a blank grid with 2, then 3, then 4. Canonical rectangle profiles are mixed with area- and bounding-box-inversion scenes so size proxies fail; non-shared canonical anchors include cross-colour contact so colour-blind connectivity also fails.

Find the unique color-7 rectangular outline. Ignore cells outside it, crop the non-zero cells in its interior to their bounding box, remove the frame, and paste that crop centered on a zero canvas of the original height and width. Centering is relative to the whole canvas, not the frame interior; internal zero holes and all content colors are preserved.

Grid (h×w, h=3..15, w=6..15) with bg color ∉ {4, 6} and scattered color-4 (yellow) cells in various layouts (random, cluster, column, row, diagonal, scattered). Optional decor cells in other colors. At least one yellow cell sits at a column where col % 3 == 0. Rule: for each cell, if color == 4 AND column index % 3 == 0, recolor to 6 (magenta). Otherwise keep original. Output: yellows in trigger columns become magenta; yellows elsewhere stay 4.

Expand every red seed into an orthogonal plus, every green seed into a diagonal X, and every yellow seed into a filled 3x3 square; combine all independent color-specific stencils on the original canvas.
Given an asymmetric n x n color bitmap, output a 2n x 2n tiling with TL=180-degree rotation, TR=vertical flip, BL=horizontal flip, and BR=the original bitmap.

0-bg grid with one color-1 marker and one color-2 marker (defining vector v = p2 - p1) plus a color-4 payload shape. Rule: translate the color-4 cells by v (dropping out-of-bounds), then fill the moved bbox solid with color 4. Output is input-sized. Grid size, vector and payload bbox/position vary.

Split the fixed 4x14 input into three 4x4 color-6 masks. Build a 3x3 ordered gallery whose tile (i,j) is panel_i XOR panel_j in color 7, with one-cell black separators; diagonal tiles are blank and opposite off-diagonal tiles are equal.

On a 10x10 black canvas, place two or three separated solid rectangular 8-connected objects using colors 1, 2, and 8. Count red (2) cells in each object. Exactly one object has the largest red count. Return that object's complete bounding-box crop, preserving its internal colors.

h × w grid (small examples plus medium/large hard examples, up to 24×13) with bg = 7 (orange) and sparse non-7 cells in colors 5 and/or 9 (~25-55% density). Various layouts (scatter, blob, stripes, diag, frame, checker). Rule: rotate input 90° CCW → core. Output dimensions: (2*core_h + 3) × (core_w + 2). For each output cell (r, c): let period = core_h + 1. If r % period == 0 → it's a SEPARATOR ROW: cells at col 0 and col core_w+1 are 7, else 1. If r % period != 0 → it's a CORE ROW: cells at col 0 and col core_w+1 are 1 (side border), interior cells are core[r%period - 1][c-1]. Net effect: rotate-CCW the input, then frame in 1-border with 7-corners and tile vertically twice.

In a color-8 maze, trace the shortest lawful path from start 2 to goal 3 in (position, key-4-held, key-5-held) state space. Key 4 unlocks door 6 and key 5 unlocks door 7. Paint every path coordinate 9 on an otherwise zero grid; return all zeros when the goal is unreachable.

skills: panel aggregation, denoising, numeric depth output
summary: Three same-size color panels separated by color-9 columns; noisy panel disagreements are majority-repaired by the rule.
3 horizontal color-1 frames; each has a transform token (2/3/4/9) above its TL corner.
Complete multicolor reflection about the axis of a movable rectangular frame.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-10) with: (a) ROW 0 containing a LEGEND of K=3 colors placed left-aligned at fixed columns 0, 2, 4 (with 0-gaps between them); (b) BELOW row 0: K=3 CONNECTED SHAPES at distinct positions, each in a DIFFERENT non-legend color, each with a DISTINCT SIZE drawn from sizes {1, 2, 4} (one 1-cell, one 2-cell line, one 4-cell L-shape). Shapes don't touch each other or row 0. Rule: SORT the 3 shapes by size ASCENDING. RECOLOR shape with rank-i (0-indexed by size) to LEGEND[i] (the i-th row-0 color). CLEAR row 0 (set to 0). Net: shapes get repainted with legend colors according to size-rank; the legend itself is erased.

One to three color-2 seeds occupy canonical-scale chambers bounded by a single color from 6/7/8/9. Cardinal BFS may cross only 0/2 cells. Every reachable cell is recolored by distance mod 3 as 3/4/5; walls and unreachable chambers remain unchanged. A closed outer barrier makes wall blocking answer-changing in every ordinary example; a three-slot wall-color schedule also refutes the canonical-fitting color-8-only shortcut.
Schedule linked official anchors, isolated negative witnesses, and a mixed counterfactual that composes both unchanged branches.

skills: coordinate transforms, multicolor motifs, rotated transport
summary: Rotate source-local 8/9 markers a quarter-turn into a second local frame.
Horizontal gray line; blue extends away and red extends toward it.

A 7..12 by 7..12 zero-background grid contains one to three distinct nonzero colors. Each color appears exactly twice at different rows and columns, marking opposite corners of a rectangle at least 3x3. Rectangle borders do not intersect, although one rectangle may be nested inside another. On a fresh zero grid of the same size, draw all four border edges of every marked rectangle in its pair color; interiors remain zero.

A sparse 8..10 by 10..12 grid contains a connected red (2) object, a blue (1) marker, a green (3) marker, and one preserved distractor. Move the red object by the blue-to-green vector: erase its source cells to background 0 and paint its translated cells cyan 8.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-9, w ∈ 9-13) with: TARGET ∈ 2-4 ACTIVE ROWS picked at random; FOR EACH active row: (a) ONE COLOR-9 ANCHOR CELL at an INTERIOR column (2..w-3); (b) 1-2 COLORED OFF-AXIS CELLS — placed at random offsets 1..k from the anchor (where k = min(anchor, w-1-anchor) so reflections stay in-bounds), all on ONE SIDE of the anchor (sign chosen per row from {-1, +1}), painted in colors drawn from {1..8} (not 9). Inactive rows stay all-0. Rule (FOR EACH ROW WITH A 9-ANCHOR, MIRROR THE NON-9 COLORED CELLS ACROSS THE ANCHOR TO THE OPPOSITE SIDE): For EACH row r: FIND the color-9 cell (if any) at column ac. For EACH non-{0, 9} cell at (r, c): COMPUTE c' = 2*ac - c (reflection across the anchor column). IF c' is in-bounds AND g[r][c'] is 0: PAINT g[r][c'] with the same color as g[r][c]. Original cells, anchor, and other rows preserved. Net: each anchor row becomes horizontally symmetric across its 9-marker; colors are duplicated on both sides.

0-bg grid with K (2-3) hollow rectangular FRAMES in distinct border colors, each containing a small centered interior content (a 2-4 cell shape in a distinct content color, bbox <= 2x2 so it fits any frame). Rule: keep the frame outlines but redistribute the interior contents in REVERSED frame order, re-centering each. Frame count/sizes/positions, contents and colors all vary.
2-3 components; exactly one is a (procedurally varied) LR-mirror symmetric shape.

0-bg grid (h~6-10, w~7-11) with: (a) ONE FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-8 (cyan) DIVIDER COLUMN at col `guide_col` (random 2..(w-1)//2 — left of center so the mirror fits on the right side); (b) 4-(guide_col*h/2) non-{0, 8} CONTENT CELLS on the LEFT SIDE ONLY (cols 0..guide_col-1) at random positions in ONE random color from {1..9} minus {0, 8}. Right side starts all 0. Rule (REFLECT LEFT ACROSS 8-DIVIDER): identify the cyan VERTICAL DIVIDER at col `guide`. For EACH non-bg non-8 CELL at (r, c) with c < guide, PAINT the MIRROR position (r, 2*guide - c) on the right with the SAME COLOR. Divider stays. Net: left content reflected across cyan column to right side.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with: (a) cell (0,0) = KEY (some non-bg color); (b) one 3-5 cell BLOB of the KEY color placed elsewhere on the grid (away from (0,0)); (c) 1-2 DISTRACTOR blobs in different colors. Rule: read key = grid[0][0]. Clear (0,0) to 0 (temp). Find all cells in temp matching the key color. If none → output [[0]]. Else: compute bbox of those key-color cells. Output: temp cropped to that bbox (small grid containing the key blob plus any distractor cells that happen to lie inside the same bbox).

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 2-4 DIAGONAL ENDPOINT PAIRS — each pair: TWO SAME-COLOR cells at diagonal offset ±1 from a MIDPOINT (r, c), at (r-dr, c-dc) and (r+dr, c+dc) where (dr, dc) ∈ {(1, 1), (1, -1)}. Midpoint is initially 0. Pairs are DISTINCT colors from {1..9}, placed non-touching (3×3 neighborhood padding). Rule (FILL MIDPOINT OF EACH DIAGONAL ENDPOINT PAIR): For EACH PAIR of same-color cells at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) with |r2-r1| == |c2-c1| == 2 and the midpoint cell (r1+r2)//2, (c1+c2)//2 == 0: PAINT the midpoint with the pair's color. Endpoints stay. Net: each diagonal endpoint pair becomes a filled 3-cell diagonal.
Row 0 has k color-1 markers. Below it are distinctly sized, distinctly colored body objects; exactly one has area k. Select that object, keep its 4-neighbor outline, and crop to its bounding box.

0-bg grid with several 2×2 windows where exactly 3 of 4 cells are color 4 (yellow) and 1 is 0 (missing corner). Optional decoration cells in other colors elsewhere. Rule: scan all 2×2 windows. For each window where exactly 3 cells are color 4 and exactly 1 cell is 0, set the 0-cell to color 2 (red). All other cells preserved unchanged. Output: each L-shaped yellow pattern is completed with a red corner.

A 10-18 by 10-18 zero-background grid contains one to four separated hollow yellow (4) rectangular frames, each 4-6 cells tall and wide. Every frame interior contains exactly one marker whose color is neither 0 nor 4. One to four non-yellow distractor cells also lie outside all frame boxes. For each frame independently, fill only its zero-valued interior cells with that frame's marker color; preserve marker cells, yellow borders, and every exterior cell.
Trace the right-launched red(2) ray, paint every traversed cell cyan(8), reflect on slash(4) and backslash(5) mirrors, and stop before magenta(6).
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.
Separated 2x2 windows each contain exactly 3 same-color cells and 1 blank (zero) corner. Rule fills the blank corner of each such window with that window's color, completing it into a solid 2x2.

Count non-zero colors, select every color tied for the maximum count, sort the selected colors by their leftmost input column, and emit a max-count-tall solid bar for each selected color. Generated colors are single connected objects; lower-count distractors and 1/2/3/4-way winner branches are all represented.

A 7..14 rectangular zero-background grid contains one connected color-1 shape. Its occupied bounding box is 5..7 rows high and five columns wide; five morphology families and free lawful placement provide visual variation. The rule finds the minimum and maximum occupied rows and recolors each color-1 cell strictly below their arithmetic midpoint to color 2. A four-position schedule reserves half of draws for exact canonical canvas profiles and half for broader dimensions, while odd shape heights supply explicit counterexamples to the tempting but wrong inclusive-midpoint interpretation. Odd notched frames additionally distinguish the occupied bounding-box midpoint from the pixel centroid.

0-bg grid (size varies). Bottom two rows are the SHELF (a shelf color); the row above the bottom has K gaps (runs of 0) of DISTINCT widths separated by shelf cells. Above the shelf sit K solid blocks in distinct non-shelf colors, block i sized gap_i.width x h_i (so sizes are strictly increasing and block_i.size is divisible by gap_i.width). Rule: sort gaps by width and blocks by size, pair them, and drop each block into its gap. Grid size, gap widths/positions, block heights and count all vary.

Color-5 walls + non-{0,5} seed cells. Rule: from each seed, cast 4 cardinal rays through 0-bg cells, painting them with the seed's color. A ray stops at the first 5-wall or grid edge. Seeds and walls stay; opposite-side cells (across a wall) are NOT painted.

Sparse 0-background grids with 2-3 colors. Same-color markers may form a single row/column pair, a gapped collinear triple, several row/column spans, a lowest-color overlap, or an unaligned distractor. Fill every background cell between same-color markers sharing a row or column; keep existing markers, and let the numerically smallest eligible color win overlaps.

On a blue (1) field, the unique most numerous foreground color is a complete sparse template. For each other color, first treat all of its cells as one translated fragment and complete that single template footprint. If the whole color cannot fit one footprint, split it into 8-connected components and complete one footprint per component.

A 0-background grid contains two to four separated nested rectangular color-1 frames, optionally inset from the canvas, plus zero to two isolated color-1 singleton components. Recolor every nonzero cell to 1 plus the number of rectangular-frame components whose bounding boxes contain it.

A 0-background grid contains one connected color-2 template and 2..7 isolated color-3 mask cells. Tight-normalize the template by its bounding box. On a fresh blank canvas, stamp that shape in color 8 with offset (0,0) at every mask cell; keep the union when stamps overlap. Discard the original template and mask cells.
Read transform tokens 1..4 from the top row, crop the nonzero body below the blank separator, and apply the transforms in left-to-right order.
Recolor the blue component whose normalized vertical-symmetry status is unique among all blue components.

Place exactly three separated objects: two translation-identical shapes and one different shape with matched area and bounding box. The rule returns the uniquely shaped object cropped in its original color.

Read the two nonzero selector colors from row 0 in left-to-right order. Below the blank separator row, locate the single component of the first selector color and the single component of the second selector color; ignore the one or two larger distractor components. Crop both selected components to their bounding boxes, rotate the second crop 90 degrees clockwise, align the crops at their top-left corners on a canvas large enough for both, and overlay them. First-only cells keep the first color, second-only cells keep the second color, and overlaps become color 8.
A 3x3 motif in the lower-left is repeated under the row-0 transform command sequence.
0-6 solid 2x2 blocks; rule encodes count n (capped at 5) as a 3x3 X-pattern. Output is f(n): distinct ceiling is 6 (n in {0,1,2,3,4,>=5}); output is always 3x3 (rule-fixed).

One monochromatic 4-connected object on a zero background. Preserve its tight shape, holes, color and orientation while translating it to the nearest canvas corner, measured by bounding-box center. Equal distances choose top, then left. A three-profile teaching cycle distinguishes center/anchor rules, tie handling and independent canvas dimensions.

0-bg grid (size varies). A top-left CONTROL cell (2->wide, 3->tall, else->square) and several solid color-1 rectangles. Rule: output the first rectangle whose aspect matches the control, as an h x w grid of 1s. The control/aspect, target rect dims, distractor rects, grid size and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~21 distinct).

Zero-background grids with 2..5 separated monochromatic objects of size 1..9. Output their cell counts in top-left reading order. Exact dimension, count, maximum-size, palette-size, position, and texture controls are validated and realized.

Color-9 rectangular frame on a 0-bg grid, with a single color-2 seed inside the frame's interior. Rule does 4-connected BFS from the seed through cells of value {0, 2}, then paints all cells at ODD Manhattan-walk-distance from seed with color 8. Seed stays 2, walls stay 9, even-distance cells stay 0.

A zero-background grid contains two or three separated horizontal green (color-3) runs. Append exactly one red (color-2) cell immediately to the right of each run when that cell is in bounds and zero. Do not alter horizontal non-green runs, vertical green objects, green runs ending at the right edge, or green runs whose right neighbour is occupied.

0-bg grid with N (3..6) connected objects of STRICTLY DISTINCT sizes (random polyominoes) at random separated positions. Rule: sort objects by ascending size and repaint each with a rank color (smallest=2, next=3, ...). The output colors are rank-derived (input colors irrelevant), so diversity comes from the shapes, positions, and object count.

A color-1 rectangular frame contains two or three distinct singleton seeds. Zeros take the unique nearest seed color by wall-aware 4-neighbor BFS; equal-distance ties remain zero. A three-example schedule guarantees an open tie and horizontal/vertical one-gap wall detours.
Select the first rectangular frame matching (0,0), crop its interior to content, and apply the command at (0,1).

A square 0-background grid contains a uniquely smallest colored template object, one or two larger differently colored distractor objects, and isolated color-9 markers. Stamp the normalized smallest-object shape in its color at every marker on a fresh blank grid.

Square grid of side k*(k+1)-1 (k in 2..4), single non-bg color, with color-0 separator lines (r%period==k or c%period==k) and ONE hole per k x k block at a RANDOM local position. Rule: normalize every block's hole onto the block diagonal (local (br,bc)). The k, color and the per-block hole positions all vary freely (was holes at fixed transposed spots, ~16 distinct).

0-bg grid with: (a) ROW 0 holds N legend cells (distinct colors, in order) at cols 0..N-1; (b) N body blobs below row 0, one per legend color, each a random polyomino, 4-conn isolated. Rule: for each legend color in order, crop its body blob and hconcat the crops with 1-col gaps. N, blob shapes and positions, and grid size all vary.
Two clusters: color-2 motif + color-3 motif at separate positions.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-9, w ∈ 9-13) with: ROW_COUNT ∈ 3-5 ACTIVE ROWS, each with: (a) ONE ROW MARKER at EITHER LEFT EDGE (col 0, color 1) OR RIGHT EDGE (col w-1, color 2) — chosen randomly per row; (b) ONE COLORED SEGMENT of length 2-min(5, w-3) painted in a distinct color drawn from {3..9}\{1, 2}, placed at a random middle column position (NOT at the same edge as the marker). Inactive rows stay all-0. Rule (FOR EACH MARKED ROW, DOCK ITS COLORED SEGMENT AGAINST THE MARKER'S EDGE — MARKER=1 (LEFT) → SEGMENT MOVES LEFT TO TOUCH COL 0 (JUST AFTER MARKER); MARKER=2 (RIGHT) → SEGMENT MOVES RIGHT TO TOUCH COL W-1): For EACH row with a marker: CLEAR the segment's current cells to 0. REPLACE with the segment STARTING at col 1 (if marker is at left/color 1) OR ENDING at col w-2 (if marker is at right/color 2). The marker stays at its edge. Net: each row's segment is pulled toward the row's edge-marker, docking against it.

Two or three distinct-color exact rectangular outlines are strictly nested. Every operative outline owns a visible zero region, and four scheduled profiles teach smallest-enclosing-frame ownership independently of color rank.

0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~12-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-1 (blue) TEMPLATE — a 3-5 cell shape (L-tromino/2x2 square/T-tetromino) placed at some interior position; (b) 2-3 ISOLATED SINGLE-CELL MARKERS in DISTINCT non-{0, 1} colors at scattered positions with enough room for template stamping. Rule (STAMP TEMPLATE AT EACH MARKER, RECOLORED TO MARKER): identify the COLOR-1 template and its anchor (top-left of bbox). For EACH MARKER cell at (mr, mc) with color C, STAMP the template shape at (mr, mc) (as the anchor or offset position) in COLOR C. Net: each marker becomes a copy of the template recolored to that marker's color.
1-3 distinct colors, each with exactly 2 markers in a shared row or column.

0-bg grid (size varies). 1-4 SOLID color-6 (magenta) RECTANGLES of random sizes/positions, each kept >=1 cell from every grid edge and placed apart (a 1-cell gap all around, so the diagonal-corner cells are in-bounds, empty, and never shared). Rule: for each solid 6-rect, paint COLOR 2 (red) at the four cells diagonally one step outside its bbox corners. The grid size, the number of rects and their sizes/positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed rects).

Three distinct legend colors occupy three consecutive cells in row 0. Rows below a blank separator contain color-5 walls forming rectangular chambers. Count color-1 dots in each chamber: counts 1, 2, and 3 select the corresponding legend entry, while count 0 selects the last entry. Flood-fill the whole chamber, replacing dots as well as background. Generated scenes vary grid size, legend position/order, horizontal band split, chamber partition, and the row-major permutation of counts 0..3.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~6-9 by ~7-10) containing: (a) a 2-color BLOB (a few connected cells in 2 distinct non-{0,8} colors) placed in the upper-left area; (b) exactly ONE color-8 (cyan) ANCHOR cell placed elsewhere, with room for the blob's bbox to fit when re-anchored. Rule: detect the color-8 anchor (must be exactly 1). Detect all non-{0,8} cells (the blob). Crop the blob to its bbox. Build a fresh 0-canvas. Paste the cropped blob such that its top-left corner aligns with the anchor position. Output: blob translated to anchor; original blob position cleared.

Overlay a square zero-background grid with its main-diagonal transpose. Unpaired nonzero cells are copied to (c, r); if both transpose partners are occupied, their original values swap because the transpose is read from an immutable snapshot.
Color every minimum-size zero room 3 and every larger zero room 4 while preserving the wall lattice.
One or two separated 9-frames with paired axis markers; repeated colors require frame-local crosses.

A zero-background grid contains one full-height vertical line and one full-width horizontal line in distinct nonzero colors. Either line may win at their interior intersection. Paint all eight surrounding cells yellow (4), overwriting both background and line arms; preserve the intersection and every cell outside its 3x3 neighborhood. Sample square and rectangular grids, margin-one crossings, all line colors, and both overlap winners.

0-bg grid (h, w~4-18) with n_rows_with_dots active rows containing COLOR-1 (blue) DOTS in one of 4 LAYOUTS (endpoints / scattered / regular_spacing / triple_anchors), with DOT_COUNT distribution sparse_2/cluster_3plus/dense_5plus/mixed. Row distribution: top_only/bottom_only/spread/alternating/all_rows. Plus optional 0-3 DECOY COLORS in non-trigger rows. At least one row has ≥2 dots with bg between them. Rule (PAINT RED BETWEEN BLUE DOTS PER ROW): for EACH ROW, find the COLUMNS of all COLOR-1 cells. If ≥2 dots, find LEFTMOST and RIGHTMOST. PAINT every BG (0) CELL strictly BETWEEN them in that row with COLOR 2 (red). Rows with <2 dots stay. Decoys (non-1) cells stay. Net: each row with ≥2 blue dots fills its bg span between leftmost and rightmost dots with red.

Grid split by full color-8 columns into three panels (masks). Rule: output a per-cell boolean combination of the three supports, recolored to C's dominant color. The panel size, masks and colors vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~37 distinct). Output is a small mask, so bounded; inputs are large.
Color-2 rectangular frame + interior color-5 (gray) bbox region. Rule fills all frame-interior cells outside the gray bbox with color 2; frame and gray bbox unchanged.

Small grid (3..6 rows × 11 cols) split into THREE 3-col panels by full-height color-5 (gray) divider columns at cols 3 and 7. Panel A (cols 0-2) and Panel B (cols 4-6) share the SAME color (call it color X) — B's binary shape is some dihedral transform t of A's shape. Panel C (cols 8-10) uses a DIFFERENT color (color Y). C's shape is independent. Rule: split panels at 5-columns. Infer the dihedral transform t such that t(A.shape) == B.shape (search id, rot90, rot180, rot270, flip-lr, flip-ud, diag, anti-diag). Apply t to C (preserving C's color). Output = t(C), 3×3.
Recolor only orange components touching exactly one border to gray; preserve interior/corner orange components and all non-orange distractors.

Three isolated distinct-color components with canonical distinct-size profiles. Sort their cropped shapes by increasing cell count and pack them top-aligned from left to right with one zero column between shapes.

Horizontal panel layout (panel_h ∈ [4, 5], 5-6 PANELS each of width 4) separated by FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-9 (maroon) DIVIDER COLUMNS between panels. Total width = 4*n_panels + (n_panels - 1). Each panel contains a SMALL MOTIF (1-3 cells, connected blob) in a color from {2..7}. Panels may share motifs by chance. Rule (FIND THE MATCHING PANEL PAIR AND ISOLATE / MARK): scan all panels and find which TWO PANELS share the SAME MOTIF SHAPE (up to color/translation matching, per puzzle convention). Mark or extract the MATCHING PAIR — e.g., isolate those two panel crops side by side, or paint a marker on them. Net: among n panels, identify the two whose motifs match.
Sparse pixels paint full row/column crosses; only intersections reached by different colors become red (2).
Move isolated magenta cells one step down-right while gray cells remain fixed.

A gallery of three to five separated hollow color-9 frames. Each contains one connected single-color shape, and the output is the cyan pairwise rotation-equivalence matrix over frames ordered from left to right.

0-bg grid (h, w~15-18) with: (a) THREE NESTED RECTANGULAR FRAMES of COLOR 6 — drawn at offsets (0, 2, 4) from a centered anchor (frame 0 outermost at margin 2, frame 1 nested 2 cells inward, frame 2 innermost 4 cells inward), all in color 6; (b) ONE CONTROL CELL in COLOR ∈ {1, 2, 3} placed at one of the 4 GRID CORNERS. The control encodes a band index k. Rule (FILL THE k-TH BAND WITH CYAN, FROM OUTER INWARD): identify the SINGLE CONTROL CELL — its color k ∈ {1, 2, 3}. The nested-frame structure has 3 BANDS: BAND-1 = ring between frame 0 and frame 1; BAND-2 = ring between frame 1 and frame 2; BAND-3 = interior inside frame 2. SELECT the k-th band (outer-in). PAINT every BG-0 cell in that band with COLOR 8 (cyan). Frame cells (6) stay. Control cell stays. Net: the control color picks one nested ring and fills it cyan.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-13, w ∈ 11-16) with: n ∈ 2-5 SCATTERED MULTI-CELL CONNECTED MOTIFS, each a 3-5 cell motif (built via _build_motif random adjacent-step walk), each in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from {2..9}, placed at random non-overlapping positions via _free check (1-cell padding). Per-task semantics aim at tile-the-component-with-most-holes: motif with the largest enclosed-area is the target. Rule (FIND THE COMPONENT WITH THE MOST HOLES — IE, MOST ENCLOSED BG-CELLS WITHIN ITS BBOX OR CONVEX HULL — TILE IT OR EMIT IT AS THE ANSWER PER DEMOS): For EACH motif: COMPUTE the number of HOLES (interior bg cells trapped within the motif's bbox/region). SELECT the motif with the MOST holes. CROP it to its bbox. TILE / EXPAND / EMIT per the rule's canonical output for this task. Net: most-holed motif is extracted and emphasized as the answer.

Read nonzero column labels from the top border and nonzero row labels from the left border. Remove those borders; at each output coordinate write the row label when it equals the column label, otherwise 0.

Two separated connected tetrominoes, red 2 and green 3, are normalized independently. The output is their symmetric difference in cyan 8, rendered from shared normalized origin (0,0), including any leading blank row or column created by cancellation.

A 9..11 by 11..14 zero-background grid contains exactly three separated, distinct-color, monochrome 4-connected objects. Crop each object's bbox, sort by CELL AREA descending and then COLOR ascending for equal areas, and pack the true crops left-to-right with one zero separator column. The versioned four-sample schedule alternates canonical 5/5/4 ties, distinct-area bbox conflicts, a second tie family, and distinct-area shape variation so area, tie-break, crop, and packing semantics are visible. One cell also includes the canonical horizontal 1x4 crop and overlapping object column ranges, defeating disjoint vertical-band segmentation.
A complete color-8 rectangle encloses 6 or 7 colored markers. Each interior column is packed upward independently, preserving vertical order.

0-bg grid with: (a) ROW 0 BLUE HEADER of k color-1 cells (k = rank); (b) K random body polyominoes with STRICTLY DISTINCT areas, in distinct colors, 4-connected isolated, placed below the header. Rule: count k blue cells in row 0; among body objects sorted by AREA DESCENDING (ties by top-left), select the k-th; crop to bbox and recolor to 8. Object shapes, areas, count and rank all vary.
Two or three non-overlapping rectangular frames with a unique largest interior.

In each column whose last nonzero marker is 5, fill from row 0 through successive markers using the current/lower marker's color. Leave other columns and rows below a floating terminator unchanged. A four-profile curriculum covers all canonical size/palette profiles and includes distractor columns, internal-5 traps, top gaps, and floating terminators.

0-bg grid (size varies). 1-3 BAR-PLUS configs, each a color-8 (cyan) centre with a color-1 (blue) VERTICAL bar at distance d above and below and a HORIZONTAL bar at distance d left and right (near end at exactly d, bars extend away). Rule: a centre becomes 4 (yellow) iff all four first-hit 1s are equidistant and correctly oriented (vertical rays -> vertical bars, horizontal rays -> horizontal bars). Each config qualifies. The grid size, config count, and each config's distance/bar-lengths/position all vary freely (was one centre on a sized-to-fit grid, ~13 distinct).

Dense 0/5 field containing a small color-2 template. Several empty footprints of that template are carved into the field; odd center-hole templates also keep a color-5 center marker. Rule: greedily stamp the template into every non-overlapping valid footprint.

Sparse 0-background row scenes. A qualifying row contains one distinct non-{0,9} color plus one or more 9s; every 9 in that row adopts the companion color. Canonical-profile inputs mirror the published examples. Alternating teaching-profile inputs add a 9-only row, a two-color row, multiple 9s, and repeated companion cells; those distractors stay unchanged and make the exact predicate and all-occurrences replacement identifiable from each consecutive lesson.

A 7..16 by 9..18 zero-background grid contains 1..5 clear same-color axis-aligned endpoint pairs. The reference draws only their inclusive segments on an otherwise empty output. Scheduled examples may also contain one different-color aligned pair blocked by an endpoint of a clear pair, explicitly teaching the zero-interior precondition while clear-only anchors preserve canonical palette roles.

0-bg grid with N (2-5) distinct colors. Each color appears at exactly 2 cells positioned as OPPOSITE CORNERS of a rectangle (so the bbox of those 2 cells defines a rectangle with width and height both ≥3). Different colors' rectangles may overlap or nest. Rule: for each color c with ≥2 cells, compute the bbox of ALL cells of color c, draw the border (outline) of that bbox in color c on a fresh 0-grid. Colors with <2 cells are ignored. Output: only the rectangle border outlines appear, no interior fill.

Split three 3..5 square panels at full color-8 columns, infer the unique D4 transform mapping A to B, then apply it to C. Panel size, transform, foreground counts, shapes, and source/target colors all vary exactly.

On a 0-background grid, each color occurring exactly twice at positions in distinct rows and columns marks opposite rectangle corners. Paint that rectangle's outline in the marker color. Ignore singletons, aligned exact pairs, and colors occurring three or more times. Outlines may cross and overwrite existing cells; qualifying colors are applied in row-major first-occurrence order, matching the canonical Racket authority.

Two or three differently colored 4-connected objects occupy disjoint row bands and begin strictly right of column 0.  Every sample contains a nonrectangular object so demonstrations teach that each object moves to the left border without changing its rows or internal shape.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-9) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holding a DIRECTION CODE ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} (1=up, 2=right, 3=down, 4=left); (b) 2-3 INTERIOR CELLS placed at rows 1..h-2, cols 1..w-2 in distinct non-zero colors. Rule: READ the CODE at (0, 0) and determine shift vector (dr, dc): 1→(-1, 0), 2→(0, +1), 3→(+1, 0), 4→(0, -1). Build an EMPTY OUTPUT GRID. For EVERY non-(0,0) cell, COMPUTE its shifted position (r+dr, c+dc) and PAINT that cell with the marker's value. The code cell is consumed. Net: code at origin dictates direction; marker cells shift uniformly by 1 cell in that direction.
Move every reflected 2/5 endpoint pair across its adjacent 6-bar, preserving the full 9 mirror row.

Three separated monochrome objects are shown on black. Select the unique largest by cell count and output its top-justified cyan column-count histogram. Every four-sample lesson includes canonical-scale anchors and counterexamples to leftmost, widest, and largest-bounding-box shortcuts.

Sparse colored objects are completed by row closure followed by column closure. Colors are sorted ascending and the output is a KxK overlap matrix with diagonal 5 and off-diagonal 8/0. A deterministic four-profile cycle preserves canonical 3- and 4-color scenes, includes a counterexample to the bounding-box shortcut, and varies five-object relation graphs.
1-marker + 2-marker (defining a translation vector) + a small shape to translate.

Five border fragments (a top-left corner, a top bar, a bottom-left and bottom-right corner, and a side piece) in distinct colours are SCATTERED at random non-overlapping positions on a nonzero modal-background grid. Rule: classify each fragment by edge type (shape-based) and repack them into a compact square frame. Fragment colours, background, positions and grid size vary.

Tall grid with three equal-height vertical panels. Every panel has the same nonzero common background plus many repeated common decorative components. The top two panels contain a payload bar in one non-common color; panel 2 is panel 1 grown by one cell horizontally. The third panel has only the common pattern, so the canonical rule outputs the extrapolated next panel.

The first two nonzero cells of the top row encode a boolean operation (3 union, 4 intersection, 6 xor, 7 red-minus-blue) and a clockwise quarter-turn count (1 identity, 2/3/4 = 90/180/270 degrees). The first red object and first blue object are normalized, blue is rotated, the masks are combined, and the minimal result is rendered in cyan.

A four-color stencil in colors {1,2,7,8,9} is normalized to its bounding box. Marker colors encode identity (3), horizontal reflection (4), vertical reflection (5), and clockwise rotation (6). The transformed colored stencil is stamped with its bounding-box top-left at each marker onto an otherwise blank output.

Any rectangular colored grid (H rows × W cols, W ≤ 15) with ≥2 distinct colors. Rule: output is hconcat(g, g) — duplicate the input horizontally to produce an H × 2W grid where the right half is the SAME as the left half. Equivalent to output[r][c] = input[r][c mod W].

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~10-13) with: (a) ONE 3-BLOB TEMPLATE — a connected blob of COLOR 3 (size 2-4) grown randomly and placed at a non-touching position; (b) 1-3 COLOR-4 SINGLETON ANCHORS — single 4-cells at positions where the TEMPLATE'S BBOX would fit without going out of bounds or overlapping the template. Rule (STAMP TEMPLATE (IN COLOR 8) AT EACH 4-ANCHOR ON A FRESH GRID): identify the TEMPLATE (largest COLOR-3 connected component) and its NORMALIZED SHAPE (cells with min row/col offsets = 0). PRODUCE a NEW BLANK h × w GRID. For EACH ANCHOR (COLOR-4 cell) at (ar, ac): STAMP the template's shape with the anchor as top-left corner, painting each stamped cell with COLOR 8 (cyan). The original template and anchors are discarded. Net: a fresh canvas with cyan copies of the template at each anchor's location.

Treat each same-color 4-connected nonzero component independently. Keep it in place when any cell touches the top, bottom, left, or right grid border; erase components that remain strictly inside the grid.

A 0-background grid contains 2-7 separated solid rectangular objects. Every object has a blue (1) body plus one or more non-blue marks. Exactly one rectangle has the fewest marks. Select that rectangle and return its bounding-box crop unchanged.

A cyan (8) rectangular frame encloses 2-4 distinct single-cell seeds. A seed may use any nonzero color except cyan, including gray (5). For each empty interior cell, copy the color of its nearest seed by Manhattan distance; when two or more seeds are tied for nearest, paint gray (5). The frame and the original seeds stay unchanged.

A 7-14 by 9-14 zero-background grid contains one or two hollow color-7 rectangular frames and one or two solid color-7 rectangles, separated by blank rows/columns.  At least one hollow/solid pair has the same bbox dimensions.  Recolor each 7-component independently: a bbox with an empty interior cell becomes yellow (4); a fully filled bbox becomes red (2).

Exactly three nonzero colors appear twice each. Every pair is separated and row- or column-aligned; the inclusive pair segments are disjoint and the scene always contains both horizontal and vertical examples.

For each row, ignore colors 0 and 7 and find the uniquely most-frequent remaining color mc. Replace cells equal to mc with 0; replace every other cell, including 0, 7, and arbitrary colored noise, with mc.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~4-6 by ~6-9) with: (a) one MARKER cell in color 8 (cyan) or 9 (maroon) placed at the top of the grid; (b) one connected non-rectangular BLOB of 3-4 cells in some color ≠ {0, 8, 9}, placed below the marker. Rule: detect marker color. Extract blob, crop to bbox. If marker == 8, apply rotate-cw; else (marker == 9), apply flip-lr. Output = transformed cropped blob.

A 12-15 by 12-15 black grid contains two or three complete blue (1) rectangular frames, strictly nested with at least one black cell between adjacent outlines. Frames may be concentric or deliberately offset. Keep the blue outlines; for every black cell, count how many frames strictly contain it and paint depth+1 when depth is positive. Cells outside every frame remain black.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~11-16) with: (a) ONE DIRECTION-CODED SOURCE at (h-2, 1) — a single cell with COLOR 2 (direction index in [1..4]: 1=right, 2=down, 3=left, 4=up per puzzle); (b) ONE SLASH MIRROR (COLOR 6) at (h-2, mirror_c) with mirror_c ∈ [4, w-4]; (c) ONE WALL (COLOR 5) at (2, mirror_c) blocking upward travel; (d) OPTIONALLY ONE BACKSLASH MIRROR (COLOR 7) at (h-2-3, mirror_c+2). Rule (TRACE CYAN BEAM FROM SOURCE THROUGH MIRRORS UNTIL EDGE/WALL): the source's value encodes a direction. Cast a beam from source's position in that direction. The beam traverses 0-cells (painting them COLOR 8 cyan). When it hits a SLASH MIRROR (6), the beam reflects right-angle per the slash convention (e.g., right→up, down→left). When it hits a BACKSLASH MIRROR (7), it reflects the other way (e.g., right→down, up→left). GRAY WALL (5) STOPS the beam. Edges of the grid also stop it. Source/mirrors/walls stay. Net: a cyan-painted trajectory traces through the optical system.
3 objects with distinct sizes (1, 2, 3, or 4 cells).
Each active row has two equal-colored endpoints at an even distance; replace every pair by one same-colored dot at its integer midpoint.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~10-13) with 3-4 NON-TOUCHING BLOBS at scattered positions, each in a DISTINCT color from 1..9. Blob sizes are MIXED — 2 from PRIMES {2, 3, 5, 7} + 1-2 from COMPOSITES {4, 6}. So at least one prime-sized and one composite-sized blob exist. Rule (RECOLOR BY BLOB SIZE PRIMALITY): for EACH BLOB (4-conn connected component), COUNT its cells (size). If the SIZE is PRIME (2, 3, 5, 7), RECOLOR the blob to COLOR 2 (red). If COMPOSITE (4, 6), RECOLOR to COLOR 8 (cyan). Net: blobs get binary-recolored by primality of size — prime→red, composite→cyan.

Decode three indexed library shapes (random polyominoes in 4x4 panels), transform each, recolor, and pack as a centered strip with 1-cell gaps. The 8x14 canvas is rule-intrinsic; library shapes, program triples and colors vary.
