Square n×n grid (n~7-11) with: (a) ONE FULL-ROW COLOR-2 (red) DIVIDER ROW at row sep (interior, 2..n-3) with random density (some cells = 2, others = 0); (b) COLOR-8 (cyan) CELLS scattered in ODD COLUMNS (c = 1, 3, 5, ...) above and below the divider at random densities. Rule (NORMALIZE ALTERNATING BARS): identify the DIVIDER ROW (the row with color-2 cells). For EACH ODD COLUMN, count the 8-cells ABOVE and BELOW the divider. NORMALIZE — paint a FULL ALTERNATING BAR pattern: paint every cell in odd columns (except divider row) with COLOR 8, then leave even columns 0. Or apply task-specific normalization based on the divider partition. Divider row stays color 2. Net: scattered odd-col 8s normalize into alternating vertical bars.
Two or three red sources emit orange cardinal rays through zeros; every three-sample lesson includes a two-color obstacle probe showing that rays stop at every nonzero cell and only red cells emit.

Read the two distinct nonzero role colors from the two uniform input rows (equivalently from column 0), then fill the same 2xW canvas with those colors in checkerboard phase: output[r][c] uses role (r + c) mod 2.

For each colour, find its largest filled rectangle. A complete straight one-cell-wide tail of length 2+ launches that rectangle by the tail length in the tail direction and then vanishes. Otherwise fill the shape's bounding box in place. Paint all settlers before all jumpers, so moved rectangles overwrite settled boxes on collisions.

Several connected components; exactly one is left-right (horizontal-mirror) symmetric in its bbox crop. Rule outputs that component's crop scaled 2x in its own color. The symmetric target is a random mirror-symmetric polyomino; distractors are verified non-symmetric.

Four colored edge markers (2 horizontal, 2 vertical) + one separate color-8 polyomino. The rule frames the 8-shape's bbox, coloring each interior 8-cell by its nearest edge (ties stay 8); output dims = (eh+2)x(ew+2). The 8-shape, the marker colors and the grid size all vary.
Fill only zero centers with eight equal nonzero neighbors; include decisive near-misses.

0-bg grid with 2-4 hollow rectangular FRAMES in distinct non-zero colors. Each frame is ≥3×3 (so it has an interior). Frame interiors are bg (0), forming HOLE REGIONS enclosed by the frame color. Frames don't overlap or touch. Rule: find all 0-regions (connected groups) that are ENCLOSED (not reachable from grid border through 0-cells). For each enclosed region, find its adjacent frame color. Build a small grid showing the region cells in that color. Sort regions by (size DESC, height ASC, width ASC). Pack the grids horizontally bottom-aligned with 1-col gap. Output is the packed gallery.
A 2x2 motif uses red (2) cells as diagonal direction markers; recolor the motif to its other color and launch that color from all four motif cells toward every marked quadrant.
Turn each isolated red singleton into a green diagonal X while preserving larger red components and unrelated colored objects.

Two-panel grid: LEFT panel (cols 0..fw-1) is mostly filled with frame color (5 or 8) with 2-3 'hole' regions (small 0-shapes punched out). RIGHT panel (cols fw+1..w-1) has 2-3 small shapes in distinct non-frame colors, separated by zero rows. Each hole shape (normalized) matches exactly one right shape. Rule: detect hole sections in left frame. For each hole, find right shape with matching normalized pattern. Fill the hole with that shape's color. Output is left panel only (cropped).
Top row holds a transform-code sequence (codes 1..4); bottom-left cell names the selected object color; the rule crops that object and applies the sequence. Shape, sequence and grid size vary.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~13-15) with: (a) ROW 0 holds k COLOR-2 (red) CELLS (k=4-5) at random distinct columns; (b) TWO HOLLOW COLOR-4 (yellow) RECT-OUTLINE FRAMES — FRAME A at (1..5, 1..k) with WIDTH = k (matches); FRAME B at (2..6, w-other_k-1..w-2) with WIDTH = k+1 or k-1 (mismatches). Rule (FILL 4-FRAME INTERIOR WITH 8 IF FRAME WIDTH EQUALS k): COUNT k = number of COLOR-2 cells in row 0. For EACH COLOR-4 FRAME: if frame WIDTH equals k, FILL its INTERIOR cells with COLOR-8 (cyan). Non-matching frames stay empty. Frame outlines stay 4. Net: only the frame whose width matches the red count fills with cyan.

On a zero background, retain the center of EVERY solid nonzero monochrome 3x3 window. Larger rectangles and corner-notched 4x4 patches yield overlapping centers. Other patches include recolored corners/edges, holes, small squares, and attached tails.

Full-height column of 9s acts as a vertical mirror axis. Colored cells (non-0, non-9) on the LEFT of the guide get mirrored to the RIGHT via mc=2*guide-c, only when the mirror target is in bounds and currently 0. Rule preserves input + adds mirror copies.
First two broken near-full separator rows/cols bound the cropped subgrid.
2-3 components; exactly one is a random holed polyomino (arbitrary outer shape enclosing >=1 bg cell). Rule crops that component and fills its holes -> output shape and content vary.
Read the 4x14 input as three 4x4 panels separated by full color-8 columns. Infer the D4 transform mapping monochrome panel A to panel B, then apply that same transform to differently colored panel C.

On a background-0 grid, recolor an interior nonzero cell to cyan (8) exactly when its two opposite diagonal neighbors have the same color as the center. Both down-right and down-left triples count. Endpoints, axis-aligned triples, diagonal pairs, and mismatched-color diagonals stay unchanged.
Extract the color matrix from divider-bounded blocks and flip that matrix left-to-right.
Same-color diagonal endpoint pairs define filled diagonal spans.

A 0-background grid contains either two or three separated, monochrome, 4-connected components with strictly distinct cell counts. Rank all nonzero components by ascending area and repaint them on a blank grid: smallest to 2, next to 3, and (for three-component scenes) largest to 4. Input colour, position, and shape do not determine the rank.

A sparse color-3 rectangular lattice is stretched outward to boundaries implied by exterior color-6 markers. Boundary rows/columns move, internal complete rows/columns stay fixed, and markers remain color 6. Exact canvas, lattice, and marker profiles are observable from every returned input.
Reverse the order of adjacent two-column tiles without reflecting the contents inside each tile.
One random connected blob; the rule histograms its per-column fill counts (output height = max count, width = bbox columns). Blob shape, span and per-column counts all vary.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 2-3 SOLID FILLED RECTANGLES of size rh × rw (3..4 each, so each rect has a strict INTERIOR), each painted entirely in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from a shuffled palette {1..9}. Rectangles are placed at non-touching positions with 1-cell padding via _free (no two rectangles share cells or 4-edges). Rule (REPLACE EACH SOLID FILLED RECTANGLE WITH ITS BBOX-OUTLINE — KEEPING THE BORDER, ERASING THE INTERIOR): for EACH solid rectangular blob of color C: identify its bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2). KEEP the BORDER CELLS (top row r1, bottom row r2, left col c1, right col c2 of the bbox) in color C. CLEAR the INTERIOR (cells (r1+1..r2-1, c1+1..c2-1)) to bg-0. Other rectangles outside the current blob's bbox stay unchanged. Net: solid filled rectangles become hollow outlines of the same color and size; interiors become bg-0.

0-bg grid (size varies) with TWO color-4 (yellow) BLOBS (a left of b) defining a translation VECTOR (b.bbox_topleft - a.bbox_topleft, with the column delta > 0), and ONE color-3 (green) BLOB. Rule: translate the green blob by that vector and paint it on a fresh grid. The green blob is placed so its translation lands fully in-bounds. The grid size, the two yellow blobs' positions (hence the vector), and the green blob's shape/position all vary freely (was fixed diagonal blobs, ~11 distinct).

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-13, w ∈ 10-14, by difficulty) with: N ∈ 1-2 HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAMES, each fh × fw (fh, fw ∈ 4-5) drawn at non-overlapping positions via _free check, each in a DISTINCT FRAME_COLOR drawn from a 2N-color palette (so 4 distinct colors when N=2). INSIDE EACH FRAME: ONE SINGLE SEED CELL at a random interior position, painted in a SEED_COLOR (the OTHER half of the palette, distinct from the frame color). Rule (FOR EACH RECT-FRAME, FIND THE SINGLE NON-FRAME SEED INSIDE; FILL ALL OTHER 0-CELLS OF THE FRAME'S INTERIOR WITH THE SEED'S COLOR; FRAME OUTLINE AND SEED CELL PRESERVED): For EACH rect-frame: COMPUTE its INTERIOR (cells strictly inside the outline). READ the unique non-frame-color seed cell inside → seed_color. PAINT all 0 cells in the interior with seed_color. Outline stays frame_color. Net: each frame's interior floods with its seed's color.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one yellow (4) border light and one or more non-yellow interior caster cells. The light may occupy any edge or corner; at corners, the selected rule gives left/right borders priority. The Racket authority casts a yellow ray from every caster cell away from the light and clears the original light. Generated scenes include separated collinear casters so a canonical-fitting farthest-caster-only shortcut is visibly wrong.

Place 3-4 ordinary-draw colors as separated solid rectangles on a zero background. Each color has a distinct number of 4-connected objects. Rectangle areas vary independently of those counts, and the colored-cell ranking conflicts with the object-count ranking. The Racket rule counts objects per color, sorts counts descending, and emits a right-aligned staircase with one row per color.

Small 0-bg grid (h, w~2-4) with 2-4 SINGLE-CELL MARKERS at distinct positions in random non-zero colors from {1..9}. Other cells are bg. Rule: UPSCALE the grid by FACTOR 2 — every cell at (r, c) with value v becomes a 2×2 BLOCK of color v at output positions (2r, 2c), (2r, 2c+1), (2r+1, 2c), (2r+1, 2c+1). Output dimensions: 2h × 2w. Net: input is a small markered grid; output is the same pattern but each cell expanded to a 2×2 block (2× upscale).

A 5x17 zero-background grid contains three cropped shape panels separated by blank columns. Panels A and B share one color; panel C uses a distinct color. Infer the first transform in code order {identity, rotate-cw, rotate-180, rotate-ccw, flip-lr, flip-ud, transpose} that maps A to B, then apply it to C and preserve C's color. Ordinary generated examples make the A->B transform unique, make C discriminate all seven transforms, vary connectedness, and cover every branch in each seven-sample window.

Full color-8 wall rows and columns partition a 0-background grid into two to four rectangular chambers. Each chamber contains exactly one nonzero, non-8 seed cell; fill every non-wall cell in that chamber with its seed color. The curriculum covers vertical, horizontal, and 2x2 wall layouts at canonical and expanded scales, and alternates globally distinct versus deliberately reused seed colors.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-2 template shape and a color-1 marker. Rule: rotate the template (op 3 = (r,c)->(c,h-1-r)) and stamp it in color 8 at the marker, on a blank grid. The grid size, template shape and marker position vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~24 distinct).

A full-height cyan(8) bar separates equal-width halves. For every left cell, compare whether it and its reflected right-half partner are occupied (nonzero). Return a fresh all-zero grid and paint orange(7) only at the reflected RIGHT-HALF position when exactly one side is occupied. The input bar and source colors are not copied to the output.

Fixed 7×14 0-bg grid with: (a) ROWS 0..3 (the LIBRARY): THREE 4×4 PROTOTYPE PANELS at column offsets (0, 5, 10), separated by 1-column gaps. Each panel holds a motif drawn from one of 4 _LIBRARIES sets (each set has 3 distinct prototype shapes), each panel painted in a DISTINCT non-0 color from {2..9}; (b) ROW 5 (INDEX ROW): sparse INDEX CODES placed at specific columns (drawn from one of 5 _PROGRAMS layouts), where each index ∈ {1, 2, 3} selects one of the 3 prototypes; (c) ROW 6 (TRANSFORM ROW): TRANSFORM CODES at the same columns as the index codes, where each code encodes a dihedral transform (1=identity, 2=rot90, 3=flip-LR, 4=flip-UD per canonical rule (not rot180). Rule (DECODE THE PROGRAM — FOR EACH (INDEX, CODE) PAIR, SELECT THE INDEXED PROTOTYPE, APPLY THE TRANSFORM, PACK THE RESULTS): scan ROW 5 left-to-right for INDEX CODES. For EACH column c with g[5][c] = idx and g[6][c] = code: LOOK UP the idx-th library prototype panel. APPLY the transform code to that panel. PACK the transformed panels LEFT-TO-RIGHT into an OUTPUT GRID with 1-cell gaps between, preserving each prototype's color. Library rows, index/code rows, and gaps are discarded. Net: the output is a sequence of transformed prototype panels decoded by the index/transform program.

One color-9 anchor and one monochrome asymmetric connected template. Crop the template and stamp its 0/90/180/270-degree rotations in the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right anchor quadrants.

Among several separated components, the one with the strictly highest row-occupancy peak is cropped and recolored to 8. The target is a random polyomino (peak >= 3); distractors have strictly lower row-peaks.
An odd square grid; the rule rotates 90° CW and crops the top-left quadrant.

A zero-background grid contains one connected color-4 template, one color-7 start marker, and one non-branching color-1 wire. Follow the wire from the start; at every direction change, stamp the normalized template with top-left alignment onto a fresh output grid. Grid size, template size/shape, exact turn count, start orientation, path signs, segment lengths, and placements vary.
Recolor nonzero objects by bounding-box aspect: tall to 2, wide to 8, square unchanged.

A q×q motif (q=3..5) selects both macro blocks and micro cells on a q×q lattice with one-cell zero separators. One complete macro row or column is overpainted green, hiding some motif copies. Remove green and form the motif's self-product; output cyan where macro/micro row-major ranks match and red elsewhere.
Two separated gray rectangle rooms, each with one distinct-color seed in its strict interior.
Top template (color 2 cells) + full-5 row separator + bottom canvas with transform-command markers.

0-bg grid (size varies) with THREE PANELS separated by blank zero-columns, all one color. Panel A is a random D4-ASYMMETRIC shape (unique transform); panel B is A under a chosen detectable transform (code 1-5: rot-cw / rot-180 / transpose / flip-lr / flip-ud — NOT rot-ccw or anti-transpose, which this rule cannot infer); panel C is another asymmetric shape. Rule: infer the A->B transform and output it applied to C. Each panel has no internal blank column. The shapes, transform, positions and color all vary freely (was a fixed 6x13 layout with 2 transforms x ~8 colors, ~16 distinct).

On a color-9 background, several disconnected color-1 objects are shown. An object changes to color 8 iff a complete background-9 region is wholly strictly inside that object's bounding box; no-hole objects stay color 1. Generated lessons include irregular hole-bearing objects and open-bbox decoys, not only rectangular frames.
Collect every non-black cell, sort the cells by column ascending and then row ascending, and place the ordered colors into a 3x3 output whose middle row runs right-to-left. Missing entries are black.

Grid (h 6..18, w 8..14) textured with a random 5/7 mix, carrying 1..8 rectangular zero holes (along-edge span 1..6, perpendicular depth 1..6), each touching exactly one edge and placed clear of corners (margin >=1). Rule: every edge-touching zero component is mirrored to the opposite edge (row-flip for top/bottom holes, col-flip for left/right holes), then the hole's full column band (top/bottom) or row band (left/right) is painted 7; mirrored zeros take precedence over the sweep. Floating holes are not mirrored but may be consumed by other sweeps.

Erase each same-color 4-connected object touching any outer border; keep every fully interior object. Zero is the background. Shapes, edge positions, dimensions and colors vary, including one color in both erased and surviving objects, diagonal-only same-color contacts and cardinal different-color contacts.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-1 (blue) SOURCE on the left emits a ray moving RIGHT. 1-3 single-cell DEFLECTORS (color-3 '/' or color-4 '\') sit at the ray's TURN POINTS, and a color-5 (gray) WALL sits where the ray finally stops. Rule: trace the ray from the source — '/' turns right->up / up->right etc., '\' turns right->down / down->right etc., the wall stops it — and paint every traversed 0-cell COLOR 8 (cyan). The whole path is built by tracing forward so every deflector is actually hit and the ray ends at the wall; grid size, source position, deflector count/placement/type and wall position all vary freely (was one fixed ray config + padding).
Exactly 2 cells of one color, both at non-trivial bbox corners.

On a fresh same-size color-0 canvas, process every isolated nonzero seed in row-major order. Paint its center and four one-step diagonal neighbours with the seed color, clip arms at the border, and let later seeds overwrite earlier colors where X footprints overlap.

Find the three hollow gray frames and read each singleton key above its top midpoint.  Match key 1/2/3 to the loose object with 0/1/2 enclosed holes, erase all loose source objects, and center each matched crop on the corresponding frame interior without recoloring it.

Read the fixed 3x11 input as three 3x3 panels A, B, C separated by all-zero columns 3 and 7. A and C use the same source color; B uses a different target color. Infer the unique geometric transform that maps A's occupied-cell support to B's support from the canonical family {identity, rotate-90-CW, rotate-180, flip-left/right, flip-up/down}. Apply that transform to C's support and paint every occupied output cell with B's target color. Ordinary generated lessons schedule only the four non-identity branches and use asymmetric masks so the transform is unambiguous and shortcut-rebutting.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one full-height grey (5) divider. All coloured source cells begin left of that divider. Copy every source cell to the same row at the equal-distance position on the right, keeping its colour and preserving the input. Production lessons include canonical 7x11, 8x9, and 7x13 profiles plus larger profiles, and deliberately vary connected/scattered geometry, palette size, source count, and an off-centre divider so midpoint and exactly-five-cell shortcuts cannot solve a lesson.

Four 5x5 panels are separated by color-9 columns.  Exactly one of the first three colored source shapes maps to the last-panel query under one of the seven distinct transforms implemented by the frozen authority; paint the query cells with that source color.  A scheduled same-size, same-bounding-box decoy refutes the strongest canonical-fitting shortcut.

A zero-background grid contains 2–4 orthogonally isolated 3×3 tiles. Every tile is filled by color 1 and one shared nonzero fill color, and the color-1 counts are distinct. Return the tile with the most color-1 cells.

Two separated monochrome source shapes are cropped and top-left aligned; the output is a four-panel gallery of union(2), intersection(3), xor(4), and left-shape-minus-right-shape(6), with one-cell black separators.

Colored legend shapes in a top band, an all-zero separator row, then gray(5) copies below; the rule recolors each gray copy to the legend color whose normalized shape it matches. Grid size, shapes and colors vary.
Two or three separated single-color objects are replaced by the border of each object's bounding box on an otherwise blank output.

Grid (h~11-13, w~16-18) with: (a) 2-3 hollow rectangular FRAMES (5×5, 5×6, or 6×5) in distinct non-{0,5,8} colors, isolated; (b) 2-3 small 4-conn MOTIFS (3-5 cells) in the SAME distinct colors as the frames (one motif per frame color), placed elsewhere. Rule: detect frames and motifs. For each color, find its frame and its motif. Move/center the motif INTO its matching frame (paint motif cells at the centered position inside the frame's interior). Empty motif's original position back to bg.

A 3×3 mosaic repeats a 2×2, 2×3, 3×2, or 3×3 base tile, with two uniform separator rows and columns.  At least two local cells disagree across the nine copies: one has exactly one outlier and one has two to four outliers.  Compress to one tile, preserving unanimous values and painting every non-unanimous local cell blue (1).

Three or four distinct-color connected motifs occupy distinct source quadrants. The rule classifies each motif by its centroid, crops it, and reassembles the occupied quadrants as a normalized 2x2 mosaic with one background row and column between mosaic cells.

Split the 9-row input at its solid middle row into aligned 4-row top and bottom panels. For every aligned cell, output green (3) when either panel cell is nonzero; output black (0) only when both cells are black.

Crop the inclusive bounding box of all color-9 markers, preserving every cell inside. Sparse diagonal pairs, reverse-diagonal pairs and scattered side extrema vary the box. Exterior payload distinguishes marker-defined cropping from trimming all nonzero cells; varied payload multiplicities supply counterexamples to the declared frequency shortcuts.

On a color-7 field, one vertical 8/9 source rail has an end-aligned color-9 block and one unique all-8 target rail is exactly two cells longer. Several additional all-8 vertical rails reproduce the canonical rail field. Move the block to the target's matching end and grow it by one cell. Non-half source blocks refute the canonical-only shortcut of painting half the target.
Remove singleton noise and recolor each 8-connected object by top-bottom, left-right-only, or asymmetric shape class.
Fill the corner, edge, and interior regions of a color-3 divider lattice by their matrix position.
2-3 colored shapes; each has a distinct token (1..4) directly above its bbox top-left.
Three or five isolated, single-color blobs with strictly distinct areas; a five/five/three schedule keeps every two-demo lesson identifiable.

Two or three disconnected blue(1) room-and-corridor networks each have one unique marker color.  Within each network, repaint every cell whose eight neighbours are all nonzero with that network's marker color.

2-4 distinct-color pairs, each color appearing exactly twice and aligned in a row or column (>=3 apart, clear segment) so the rule fills the segment; plus an optional diagonal (non-aligned) distractor pair that stays.

One to three interior markers of one color emit same-color rays along all four diagonals. Markers remain present; generated markers are separated and never block one another. A 45-slot color/count schedule covers every legal pairing while repeatedly refuting canonical-fitting multiplicity shortcuts; exact 7x7, 15x15, and 17x17 anchors preserve profile support.

One connected blue shape (1) and one connected red shape (2) are placed apart on a zero background. Their independently normalized masks overlap and each contributes exclusive cells. The output top-left-aligns the two masks, takes their union, and paints it green (3). Alternating lawful lessons add a distant color-7 decoy pair that the rule ignores.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-11) with: (a) 1-2 GRAY (COLOR-5) WALLS — each wall is a near-full row or column with 1-2 GAPS (openings) at random positions; (b) 2-3 SINGLETON SEED CELLS in DISTINCT colors from {2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9} placed at BG positions with Manhattan distance ≥ max(3, min(h, w)//2) between any pair. Rule (GEODESIC VORONOI FILL AROUND GRAY WALLS): For EACH BG cell at (r, c): compute GEODESIC (4-conn, non-wall) distance to EACH SEED. PAINT the cell with the COLOR of the NEAREST seed by geodesic distance. Ties broken task-specific. Walls stay 5. Net: each connected region partitions by nearest seed (geodesic Voronoi), with walls blocking shortest paths.

Zero-background 7..12 by 9..14 grids contain 1..2 border-touching and 1..2 interior orange(7) polyominoes plus 0..2 non-orange distractor objects. Recolor every whole border-touching orange component green(3); leave interior orange and all distractors unchanged.

Read the five wall-enclosed rooms from left to right as key1, value1, key2, value2, and query. Compare the query's nonzero colored cells with the two keys at exact room-relative coordinates, including color. Return the entire interior grid of the value room paired with the unique match.
skills: library lookup, key/value pairing, room-interior matching

summary: 0-bg grid (h~4-6, w~7-9) with 1-3 LONG HORIZONTAL COLOR-2 RUNS (length ≥3, up to 5) plus 1-3 SHORT DISTRACTOR RUNS (length 1 or 2). Each run is placed at a random row and random starting column with 1-cell padding so they don't merge. No two runs share a row. Rule (RECOLOR ENDPOINTS OF LONG RUNS): scan each ROW LEFT-TO-RIGHT for HORIZONTAL RUNS of COLOR 2 (maximal contiguous sequences). For each run with length ≥3, RECOLOR its FIRST and LAST cells to COLOR 8 (cyan); INTERIOR cells stay 2. Runs of length 1 or 2 stay color-2 (no change). Vertical 2-runs unaffected. Net: long horizontal runs get cyan-tagged endpoints; short runs stay 2.

0-bg grid (size varies) with full color-8 lattice lines and colored dots. Rule: dots map to coarse lattice cells; same-coarse-row/col same-color dot pairs fill the coarse cells between them (color conflicts -> 6); output expands each coarse cell's fill (8 lines stay 8). The grid size, lattice and dot colors/positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~25 distinct).

A centered maroon cross separates a visible TL-to-TR clockwise example from a BL source and empty BR target. Rotate the BL bounding box clockwise, preserving its offsets and color; generate full-fit shapes on 9..15 grids.

0-bg grid (size varies) with 0/2/4 cells. A memorized radius-3 (7x7) context table recolors each cell whose 49-cell neighborhood matches an entry to 0 or 4. This generator stamps the 3 interior table windows on a 0-background lattice so recolors fire. Grid size, stamp choice and positions vary, but normal examples stay near canonical scale instead of expanding to large 20x20+ canvases. The table is memorized and edge-dominated, so the per-cell transform variety is 3; whole-grid inputs/outputs stay diverse via placement.
On every row and column, fill the inclusive span between exactly two same-color cells when the original span contains only zero and that color; row fills happen before column fills.
Recolor each color-8 object by its bounding-box zero-region count, mapping four regions to 7.

0-bg grid (size varies). Row 0 holds k color-1 markers; below are color-3 rectangles with distinct hole counts. Rule: recolor the rectangle with exactly k holes to 2 and clear the markers. The grid size, k, target/distractor shapes and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).

Grid where the MODE color is the background (often 2, sometimes 5 or 0). The most-frequent non-bg color is the FRAME color. The grid contains 2-4 solid frame-color rectangular blocks at non-touching positions. Each block has 1-3 marker cells inside in OTHER colors (replacing frame-color cells). The frames may have different sizes; the largest determines the output bbox. Rule: output is sized to the LARGEST frame's bbox; start filled with frame_color. For each frame, overlay each marker at local coords (r-r0, c-c0) within the output canvas. Markers from different frames may be at different local coords; they merge onto the shared canvas.

0-bg grid (size varies) with color-7 objects. Rule: recolor to 6 every object touching EXACTLY 2 grid borders (corner or edge-spanning); objects touching 0/1/3/4 borders stay 7. The grid size, object shapes, border-touch counts and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~24 distinct).

Split at the full color-9 column. Read the right panel's first-column legend top-to-bottom. Repaint the left panel's distinct-size color-8 components from smallest to largest with that ordered legend, and output only the recolored left panel.

Rows contain color-5 cells plus ordinary 0/background and 2-4 signal colors.  In each row, every 5 is replaced by that row's first non-5 value; later zeros and colored distractors stay unchanged, and an all-5 row stays all 5.  Lessons include variable-depth interior keys, zero-valued keys, separated 5-runs, and different keys across rows so fixed-column, first/last/nearest, first-nonzero, global-color, and whole-row shortcuts fail.

0-padded grid (size varies). Row 0 is a LEGEND (non-0 cells in column order); a fixed 3x3 template (rows 2-4, cols 1-3) uses some symbols. Rule: the i-th smallest distinct template symbol maps to the i-th legend color; output is the remapped 3x3 template. The legend colors, template symbols/arrangement and grid size vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~24 distinct). Output is 3x3, so distinct OUTPUTS are bounded; distinct INPUTS are large.

Generate a 3x3..7x7 square pattern with 2..4 colors and a visible quarter-turn change.  The output tiles identity, 90-degree CCW, 180-degree, and 90-degree CW copies into the four quadrants.  A deterministic four-profile curriculum per difficulty band includes a canonical 3x3 binary profile, multicolor cases, full rotation orbits, and lawful half-turn-symmetric cases.

0-background grid with 2-6 distinct endpoint colors, each appearing exactly twice.  The rule connects each row-major endpoint pair with the canonical horizontal-then-vertical elbow, overlays the paths, and maps coverage counts 1/2/3+ to colors 3/6/9.
Five or six distinctly colored objects arranged in scheduled Manhattan-2 contact graphs that cover touch degrees 0 through 5.

0-bg grid (h = sum(row_bands)+dividers, w = sum(col_bands)+dividers) with COLOR-5 (gray) DIVIDERS forming an odd 5×3, 3×5, or occasional 5×5 macro-cell lattice. Thin bands on the 5-side keep color 5 as the majority like the canonical demos, so zero macro-cells are separate counted objects. Cell grid has odd row × col count so a CENTER macro-cell exists. Rule (FILL 3 DIAGONAL MACRO-CELLS): identify the 3×3 cell grid split by color-5 dividers. Fill the TOP-LEFT macro-cell's 0-cells with COLOR 1 (blue), the CENTER macro-cell with COLOR 2 (red), and the BOTTOM-RIGHT macro-cell with COLOR 3 (green). The 6 non-diagonal macro-cells stay 0. Dividers stay color 5. Net: 3×3 lattice of macro-cells with main diagonal filled blue/red/green.

Treat each same-color 4-connected nonzero component independently. Keep a component unchanged when any of its cells touches the top, bottom, left, or right grid border; erase every component wholly in the interior.

Two separated connected objects have distinct colors and unequal sizes. Normalize both masks to the same top-left origin, remove the smaller mask's exact cells from the larger mask, and paint the remainder in the larger object's color on the maximum of their normalized bounding boxes.

A zero-background grid contains one to three hollow rectangular frames. Each frame has exactly one differently colored seed strictly inside it. On a fresh zero-background canvas, replace each frame by one cell at its floor-center, using that frame's seed color.

Split the grid into nine zones: four singleton corners, four border strips with the corners removed, and the interior rectangle. Scan each zone in row-major order. Output a 3x3 grid containing the LAST NON-ZERO value seen in each zone, or 0 for an empty zone. Generated lessons use rotating empty-zone masks and multicolor scan conflicts so first-hit and occupancy-only shortcuts are refuted.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-15) with 2-3 PAIRS of SAME-COLOR CORNER MARKERS — each PAIR consists of TWO cells in a DISTINCT non-0 color, placed at diagonally OPPOSITE CORNERS of an axis-aligned rectangle (both row-span ≥3 and col-span ≥3). Pair rectangles are SEPARATED (≥1-cell gap between bboxes). Rule (EXPAND EACH CORNER PAIR INTO ITS RECTANGLE PERIMETER): For EACH COLOR C appearing as exactly 2 cells at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) (diagonally opposite corners of an implicit rectangle): PAINT the entire PERIMETER of the axis-aligned rectangle from (min(r1, r2), min(c1, c2)) to (max(r1, r2), max(c1, c2)) — i.e., all cells on the top row, bottom row, left col, right col of that bbox — with color C. Net: each pair of corner markers grows into a rectangle outline.

Create 2-4 horizontally separated monochrome shape panels. Crop and binarize each panel, compare shapes up to all rotations and reflections, and output an N x N matrix with 5 on the diagonal, 2 for equivalent off-diagonal pairs, and 0 otherwise. The sampler includes canonical 5-8-cell classes plus compact 3-4-cell classes and guarantees lessons that refute identity-only, rotation-only, and equal-size shortcuts.
Sparse square-grid cells are echoed across the anti-diagonal.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 5-14, w ∈ 5-14, by difficulty) with: SPARSE NON-BG CELLS in 1-4 DISTINCT COLORS, placed at density 15-40% via fg_layout ∈ {random / cluster (Manhattan-centered) / row (one full row picked) / column / diagonal / blob (Chebyshev) / scattered (every other (r+c))} in candidates filtered by row_bias ∈ {top / bottom / spread}. The grid is INTENTIONALLY UD-ASYMMETRIC — at least one cell exists where the UD mirror position (h-1-r, c) is currently 0 (so the rule has visible effect). If natural placement happens to be UD-symmetric, the generator forces one asymmetric cell. Rule (COMPLETE TOP-BOTTOM (UD) SYMMETRY — FILL EVERY BG CELL WHOSE UD MIRROR IS NON-BG WITH THE MIRROR'S COLOR): For EACH (r, c) where g[r][c] == 0: COMPUTE the UD mirror (h-1-r, c). IF the mirror cell is non-bg: PAINT g[r][c] with the mirror's color. ORIGINAL non-bg cells preserved. Net: every cell gets the color of itself OR its UD mirror (whichever is non-bg first); the grid becomes UD-symmetric — gaps in the top half are filled from the bottom half and vice versa.
N (2..4) distinct-color blobs of strictly distinct sizes; output packs them horizontally by descending area.

5-row, 23-col grid with THREE 5x5 binary SOURCE PANELS in non-0 colors plus a BLANK 4th (answer) panel, separated by single color-9 (maroon) columns at cols 5, 11, 17. Rule: split into the 5-wide panels; for each of the 25 cells the result is 8 (cyan) where at least 2 of the 3 source panels are ON (per-cell MAJORITY vote), else 0. The output rejoins the 3 source panels plus this 5x5 majority panel in the 4th slot. Colors are distractors -- only the ON/OFF masks and the per-cell majority matter.

A marker at (0,0) selects identity, flip-lr, or rotate-cw for an asymmetric source panel left of a unique all-9 separator. The transformed panel fits into the initially blank right region. Every advertised scalar override is exact and recoverable from returned pixels.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one connected red(2) shape and one connected green(3) shape in opposite regions. Normalize each shape to its own bounding-box origin, then overlay the normalized cell sets: shared cells become cyan(8), red-only cells stay 2, and green-only cells stay 3. Generated pairs always have a nonempty overlap and at least one exclusive cell on each side, so all three output colors are required.
Fill each gray-wall chamber containing exactly one colored seed; leave zero- and multi-seed chambers unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains separated same-colour connected components. Recolour each component 8 exactly when it encloses one or more 4-connected background regions inside its bounding box; otherwise recolour it 4. Open U/C/L-shaped concavities have no enclosed hole and therefore become 4.

Preserve each same-color 4-connected object in place and recolor it only by the number of enclosed complement regions in its own bounding box: 0 holes -> 2, 1 -> 3, 2 -> 4, 3 -> 6, and 4 or more -> 9. A four-example profile schedule includes canonical scenes, equal-area/equal-bbox objects, 4/8-connectivity contrasts, procedurally varied connected masks, and 3/4/5/6-hole extensions. Twelve explicit rivals are checked; this is finite evidence, not universal identifiability.
One color-1 rectangular frame contains distinct colored seeds; fill each interior cell from its uniquely nearest seed by Manhattan distance and leave cross-color ties black.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~8-10) containing: (a) ONE SINGLE-CELL KEY MARKER in some unique non-{0, 3} color (this color appears EXACTLY ONCE in the grid — it's the distinguishing marker); (b) 1-2 L-TRIOMINOES (3-cell L-shapes, all 4 rotations) painted in color 3 (green), placed at distinct positions, isolated from each other and from the key (8-neighborhood clearance). Rule: identify the KEY COLOR (the unique single-cell color that's not 0 or 3). For every L-triomino painted in color 3, RECOLOR all 3 of its cells to the KEY COLOR. The key marker itself stays. Net: green L-triominoes get recolored to match the single key cell's color.

Grid (h×w, ~3-10 by ~3-10) with at least one color-7 (orange) cell + 1-4 DISTRACTOR colors (not 7) in various textures (scattered, blob, line, border, rect, L-shape, diagonal, checker). Background usually 0. Rule: recolor every cell of color 7 to color 5 (gray). All other cells preserved unchanged. Output: same shape and structure as input with 7s replaced by 5s; distractor colors remain as-is.

Rows 0..h-2 hold one TEMPLATE shape; the LAST ROW is a sequence of transform-code markers (1=identity, 2=rotate-CW, 3=rotate-180, else=flip-LR). Rule: render the template in each marker's orientation, hstacked with 1-col gaps. Template shape/colour, marker count and codes vary.

Preserve the nonzero key row. In the framed area, find the unique most-frequent non-border interior color. Recolor the outer frame with that winner, draw a hollow winner-colored frame around all winner cells' bounding box, and clear the remaining interior.

Periodic 4-spaced lattice task. On zero-based coordinates, output 0 when r%4==0 or c%4==0; otherwise erase input color 8 to 0 and paint every other value red (2). Default lessons alternate a canonical {0,8}, clean-lattice profile with a joint counterexample profile containing interior decoys and nonzero values on every periodic row/column.

Recolor whole degree-one monochrome components to 8. Construct chains or branches with isolated contrasts, repeated colors and lawful input 8; two of every four default samples distinguish ten explicit rivals.
Read transform keys 1..4 from the four corners, tightly crop the remaining colored body, transform one copy per key, and pack the copies into a 2×2 top-aligned mosaic with one-cell gaps.
Colored concentric template + uncolored target; output colors the target's onion layers with the template palette.
skills: palette inference, example-to-target transfer, component pairing

summary: A 0-background grid contains two or three blank centers whose four diagonal neighbors share one nonzero color. The output fills every such center with that color and preserves all other cells. Each generated lesson also contains one controlled non-answer: either only three matching diagonals, four nonzero but mismatched diagonals, or a nonzero center surrounded by four matching diagonals. Positive motifs move across the grid, two of every three examples reuse one color, and one example adds a symmetric orthogonal context pair that must not block the fill.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-11) with 1-3 HOLLOW 3×3 SAME-COLOR RINGS — each a 3×3 region where the 8 BORDER cells are painted in ONE NON-0 COLOR and the CENTER CELL is ZERO (a hollow ring). Ring centers are placed on a 4-cell stride grid (rows 1, 5, 9; cols 1, 5, 9) so rings don't touch. Each ring uses a distinct color from {1..8} (color (i%8)+1). Rule (FILL EACH HOLLOW 3×3 RING'S CENTER WITH RING COLOR): For EACH 3×3 WINDOW where all 8 BORDER CELLS are the SAME COLOR C and the CENTER cell is 0: PAINT the center cell with COLOR C. Cells outside such windows stay. Net: every hollow ring completes into a solid 3×3 patch of its ring color.
Fill horizontal intervals between matching row endpoints.

A zero-background grid contains a target-color selector at (0,0), one full color-5 guide row or column, 2..7 further target cells on the selector side, opposite side, or both sides, 2..6 distractors in one or two other colors, and optional isolated color-5 noise. Reflect every target-color cell except the selector across the guide when its mirror is in bounds. A six-profile schedule supplies canonical-size examples, both guide orientations, clipped identity cases, and opposite-side witnesses.

Read the transform key at (0,0) and the ordered nonzero legend across row 0. For each legend color, crop its body component, apply the shared key, and pack the transformed crops into a one-row gallery in legend order.

Split the input at its solid color-5 divider into equal MASK and SOURCE panels. Find panel-relative positions that are nonzero in both panels, take their tight bounding box, and return the entire SOURCE crop inside that box, preserving source colors and zeros.

On a modal-background square canvas, find every 3x3 uniform ring with a distinct centre.  Connect each motif toward the nearest separate object of its centre colour that overlaps the motif's row-band or column-band; paint a ring-colour 3-wide corridor and repeat the centre marker every third cell along its middle line.  Multiple motifs, all four directions, shared partners, and same-colour candidate distractors are represented.

A row-0 color-5 marker selects a column. Alternating monochrome bars write squared length codes there; one repeated non-5 length changes the code for the other lengths, while color-5 bars are excluded from the repeated-length census.

Find the unique color-8 source marker and unique color-9 destination marker. Translate every non-{0,8,9} payload cell by the exact 8→9 vector onto a fresh background grid. Remove both markers and clear every original payload position. Scheduled lessons include negative and axis-aligned vectors, disconnected payloads, and multicolor payloads so positive-only, first-component-only, modal-color-only, marker-preserving, and fixed-vector shortcuts are contradicted.
Fill each repeated color's row-local span; sample endpoints, multi-hit and disjoint-color rows.
Fill each zero chamber with its unique plurality boundary-marker color; ties stay zero.

Canonical-size zero-background grids contain two to four active rows. Each active row has exactly two nonzero endpoint markers; the authoritative output drops those markers and paints only zero cells strictly between the row's leftmost and rightmost marker with color 8. Ordinary lessons mix the canonical color-2 palette with same-color and mixed-color endpoints, and include lawful adjacent pairs whose bridge is empty.
Read the contiguous four-color legend, then rotate the monochrome source motif by quarter turns around the gray pivot and recolor the four turns in legend order; later turns win at overlaps.

Count color-1 header markers, select the uniquely area-matched monochrome body object, crop its original-grid bounding box, and upscale 2×. Four scheduled profiles vary canonical scale, non-1 header distractors, and touching different-color objects.

Union the corners of every solid monochrome nonzero 3x3 window onto a zero output. Teach repeated colors, attached nonmatching foreground, and overlapping windows as well as separated canonical-size squares.
Sparse 0-bg with 1-2 full rows + 1-2 full cols of distinct colors and 3-5 scattered 3-cells.
Color-2 target shape + several distractor shapes; rule outputs the FIRST distractor whose shape is dihedrally equivalent to the target, in the distractor's own color.
Cyan divider line + magenta cells on one side; rule reflects magenta across divider.

Small SQUARE 0-bg grid (n~3-5, h == w) with 2-4 distinct non-zero colors in a TEXTURE pattern (noise / sparse / blob / stripes / gradient / checkerboard / frame / ring / plus) — NOT 4-fold symmetric (so rotations differ visibly). 4n ≤ 30 constraint. Rule: TILE the input grid into a 4n × 4n OUTPUT GRID structured as a 2×2 ARRAY of BIG QUADRANTS, where each big quadrant is itself a 2×2 of small n×n TILES, and each tile uses a DIFFERENT ROTATION (identity, cw90, 180°, ccw90). The output thus has 16 small n×n tiles total, each a different rotation of the input. Net: n×n input becomes 4n×4n output as a self-tiled 4-rotation kaleidoscope.

A 7x7 input: col 0 (rows 1,3,5) = 3 transform codes, row 0 (cols 1,3,5) = 3 colour codes, rows 4-6/cols 4-6 = a 3x3 prototype. The rule builds an 11x11 cross-product gallery (transform i x colour j of the prototype). Codes and prototype vary.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~8-10) with 2-3 HORIZONTAL COLOR-4 (yellow) PAIRS — each pair is 2 adjacent color-4 cells at (r, c) and (r, c+1) where 1 ≤ c ≤ w-3 (so both flanking cells c-1 and c+2 are in-bounds and remain 0). Each pair occupies a DISTINCT ROW (no two pairs share a row). Rule (FLANK WITH 9s): for EVERY (r, c) where g[r][c]==4 AND g[r][c+1]==4, set g[r][c-1] = 9 (maroon) AND g[r][c+2] = 9 — but only if both target cells are in-bounds AND currently 0. The color-4 pair stays. Net: each horizontal yellow domino gets flanked left+right by maroon cells.
Project each external color-7 marker through its complete color-5 frame as an interior color-3 stripe.

A 0-background grid contains separated color-3 simple orthogonal paths with varied lengths, orientations, and one- or multi-turn geometry. Recolor to 6 exactly the green cells having two green 4-neighbors split across the horizontal and vertical axes. Endpoints and straight degree-two cells remain 3.
2-5 separated non-5 motifs plus a color-5 blocker with payload above and below.
Three corner-rectangle panels; return the unique completed shape in color 8.
Fill the rectangle from the lone colored cell to its nearest corner, resolving ties in UL/UR/LL/LR order.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several solid COLOR-4 (yellow) objects of DISTINCT bbox areas, scattered apart, plus k blue(1) marker cells (1<=k<=#objects). Rule: recolor the k-th LARGEST object (by bbox area) to color 3 (green). The grid size, object count/sizes/positions, the selector k and the marker positions all vary freely (was several nested frames, ~16 distinct).

Fixed 3×11 grid with: (a) cols 0-2 = QUERY panel containing a 3-cell L-shape (after some dihedral transform) in q_color; (b) col 3 = full color-8 separator; (c) cols 4-6 = first CANDIDATE (the L-shape in hit_color, normalized orientation); (d) cols 7 = blank gap; (e) cols 8-10 = second CANDIDATE (a 4-cell distractor in other_color). Rule: extract the query shape and each candidate shape's binary support; for each candidate test all 8 dihedral transforms — the candidate whose support matches the query under some D4 transform is the WINNER. Output: the winner cropped to its bbox, recolored to the query's color.

A zero-background grid has exactly one full-height cyan (8) divider column and one small connected, single-color shape entirely on its left; the right side is empty. Preserve the divider and source shape, then reflect every non-{0,8} source cell across the cyan column to (row, 2*axis-col), preserving its color.

A 0-background grid contains exactly three separated solid 2x2 objects in distinct non-cyan colors. Compute Manhattan distance from each object's bounding-box center to the full-grid center, choose the unique closest object, and recolor all four of its cells to color 8.

Two adjacent aligned 4-column panels.  Output color 4 appears exactly at aligned 00 positions; 10, 01, and 11 positions map to 0.  Ordinary draws contain every occupancy state, exclude color 4 from the input, and alternate same/different foreground palettes to refute raw equality.
Pack each row's nonzeros left while preserving their original order.

A 1xN strip (N = number of rooms, in top-left scan order) flags with color-8 each rectangular room that contains a color-4 token. Room-grid layout (R x C), room size, and which rooms are flagged all vary.
skills: room order, symbolic strip output, presence detection

summary: Grid with bg = color 7. Contains: (a) 1-3 ANCHOR cells (color 9); (b) 2-5 OBJECTS, each a small connected blob (2-4 cells) in some non-{7, 9} color. Anchors and objects are separated (≥1-cell buffer). Rule: for each object O, find the nearest color-9 anchor cell (Manhattan). Compute dominant direction (whichever axis has larger offset; ties go to row). Slide O entirely until its bounding box touches the grid edge in that direction. Anchors stay put; bg preserved.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 3 BLOBS, each in a DISTINCT non-zero COLOR (drawn from 1..9 without replacement) and with STRICTLY DISTINCT SIZES (3 unique sizes from range 2..6). Blobs are 4-conn connected components grown via grow_blob with no touching. Rule: identify all NON-BG BLOBS. SORT them by AREA DESCENDING (largest first). STACK them VERTICALLY in a new output grid, LEFT-ALIGNED, with a 1-ROW GAP between consecutive blobs. The output's WIDTH is the MAX BBOX WIDTH of the largest blob; the HEIGHT is the SUM of blob heights + gaps. Net: 3 blobs become a vertical stack sorted largest-to-smallest, left-aligned with 1-row gaps.
Infer a 5x5 0/8 lattice, then expand anomalies into below-right zero masks.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-10, w = 2*half_w + 1 with half_w ∈ 4-6 → w ∈ 9-13 ODD so there's a center column at w//2) with: TARGET ∈ 3-8 SPARSE NON-BG CELLS placed at random LEFT-HALF positions (cols 0..half_w-1), each in a random color drawn from {1..9}. The RIGHT HALF (cols half_w+1..w-1) and the AXIS COLUMN (col half_w) start EMPTY. Rule (COMPLETE VERTICAL MIRROR SYMMETRY ACROSS THE CENTER COLUMN AXIS = W//2: FOR EACH NON-BG LEFT-HALF CELL AT (R, C) WITH COLOR k, PAINT g[R][W-1-C] = k; ALSO COPY BACK FROM ANY EXISTING RIGHT CELLS TO LEFT; CENTER AXIS COLUMN STAYS 0): For EACH non-bg cell at (r, c) with color k: COMPUTE mirror position (r, w-1-c). IF that mirror is bg (0): PAINT g[r][w-1-c] = k. The original left cells stay. Net: left-half pattern is reflected onto the right half across the central column axis.

Small H × W binary grid (bg=0 + 1 fg color, H, W ≤ 9). Rule: self-tile — produce H² × W² output. For block at (br, bc) in [0, H) × [0, W): if input[br][bc] is fg, copy input into that block; if input[br][bc] is bg, leave that block all 0. The input thus serves as both a mask and a template.

Maroon dividers form two rows by three equal square panels. The top row demonstrates union, intersection, or XOR on occupancy masks; the bottom row supplies a new pair and a blank answer panel. Operand pairs use one non-divider color each (including red on some draws), computed masks are red, and generated demo/query pairs each contain 00, 10, 01, and 11 witnesses.

On a 0-background grid, every color appearing exactly twice marks two opposite corners of a nondegenerate rectangle. Fill each such inclusive bounding rectangle with that color. Other non-zero colors may be present with non-pair multiplicities and remain unchanged. Qualifying rectangles do not overlap or contain distractor cells.

Hollow rectangular frames in colors {1,2,3}; non-frame components have hole counts 0/1/2; rule matches each component to the frame whose color = holes+1, center-places the crop into that frame's interior.
A full row and column of 1s split the input into four quadrants. Overlay aligned quadrant cells with zero transparent and priority TL, then TR, then BL, then BR.

A grid of rooms (R x C, total >=2) built by rectangular_rooms with COLOR-1 (blue) walls and uniform room interiors (size 3..6). The SEEDED room holds one COLOR-2 (red) cell at a random interior cell and has EXACTLY ONE COLOR-7 (orange) DOOR to a neighbour (the target). 0-2 extra distractor doors connect OTHER room pairs (never the seed room). Rule (DOOR-DIRECTED FILL): find the seeded room, follow its single door to the adjacent room, and output walls+doors with that target room filled COLOR 8 (everything else 0). The layout, room size, seeded room, door direction and distractor doors all vary freely (was a fixed 1x2 layout x 3 sizes).
skills: door interpretation, room adjacency, one-step transfer

summary: Place exactly two isolated, differently colored straight dominoes on a 0-background: one horizontal and one vertical.  The rule scans all length-three row and column windows in the original input; 0,v,v fills the leading zero and v,v,0 fills the trailing zero.  Boundary dominoes therefore become length-three segments, while interior 0,v,v,0 motifs extend on both sides and become length-four segments.  Lessons alternate boundary and interior layouts so a one-extension shortcut is refuted.

A 0-background grid contains distinctly colored 4-connected components. For each component, count its cells in every occupied row. Components with a constant per-row count are recolored to cyan(8); components whose row counts vary keep their source color. Generated lessons contain both classes and at least one constant-row-profile shape that is not a solid rectangle.

On a zero background, place 2..5 separated gray components. Keep exactly the gray cells with one orthogonal gray neighbor; erase all other cells. A four-example schedule covers paths, a branch, a cycle, and an isolated cell so the lesson identifies the local degree-one rule.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~9-11) with 3 CONNECTED MOTIFS at distinct non-touching positions: sizes {2, 4, 6} (strictly different, shuffled), each painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 7} color from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9}. Motifs are 4-conn random walks, placed with 1-cell padding. Rule (RECOLOR MEDIAN MOTIF TO 7): identify all CONNECTED COMPONENTS. SORT them by SIZE (ASCENDING). The MEDIAN motif (middle one, position 1 in the sorted list of 3) gets RECOLORED to COLOR 7 (orange). The smallest (size 2) and largest (size 6) keep their original colors. Net: 3-blob input → median-size blob becomes orange; small/large blobs unchanged.

A tr x tc lattice of s x s tiles separated by single full color-9 divider rows/cols. Each tile holds a small pattern in {0,2..8}. Rule: split on the 9-dividers, replace each tile by the lex-smallest of its 4 rotations, and reassemble with the 9-dividers. At least one tile is non-canonical so the rule visibly rotates it (output != input).
Border-touching blobs → 2, interior → 8.

0-bg grid (h~9-18, w~9-18) with: (a) a DOMINANT BARRIER — a single LONG straight LINE segment (6-8 cells long, horizontal at random interior row, or vertical at random interior col) in some non-zero barrier_color (the most frequent non-zero color); (b) 2-4 PAIRS of single DOTS on OPPOSITE SIDES of the barrier — each pair shares a column (or row, by orientation) with one dot 2 cells above the barrier and the matched dot 2 cells below (opposite side), in 4 distinct dot_colors. Rule: identify the BARRIER line and its orientation. For EACH (column/row) that has a dot above AND a dot below the barrier, SWAP the two dots: above-dot moves to a cell JUST BELOW the barrier (on the bottom side); below-dot moves to a cell JUST ABOVE the barrier (on the top side). Net: each matched pair of opposite-side dots swaps positions, ending up flush against the barrier on the opposite side.

Use the four uniform non-corner border sides as a color-to-direction key. Clear the interior to its modal background, then move every interior cell matching the top, bottom, left, or right side exactly one cell toward that side. A matching cell already adjacent to its side remains in place, and interior colors matching no side are stationary distractors.
Scattered non-adjacent nonzero cells (count varies) read into a single 1xN row in row-major scan order; output width = number of nonzero cells.

On a zero background, recolor every zero to 4 exactly when its immediate vertical neighbours are both 7.  Horizontal 7-0-7 patterns, wider vertical gaps, occupied midpoints, and matching endpoints of any other color remain unchanged.
Read the first nonzero color in row 0, clear the header and all distractors, and recolor exactly the blue (1) cells below the header with that color.

16x16-ish orange(7) grid with exactly two other colors: the MARKER color (least cells: one 5-cell plus shape) and the BLOCK color (most cells: 4..12 solid squares, side lengths 1..max_block_size, canonically 1..7). Rule: if odd-sided blocks outnumber even-sided ones, the plus is kept, else it is erased to 7; either way every odd-sided block's center cell is painted with the marker color. keep_cross (the parity decision) is an exact observable axis; both branches are witnessed at healthy rates.

Two separated 4-6 cell rectangular frames, each with one differently colored interior marker. Fill every interior with a top-left-anchored checkerboard using that frame's local marker and border colors.

Count all blue cells in the top row. Select the unique body component whose tight bounding-box height equals that count, crop it, and recolor its occupied cells cyan (8). Header placement varies so count, not run length or left packing, is required.
Solid colored anchors emit center-row/column crosses; distinct-color overlaps cancel to zero.

A 0-background grid contains two or three hollow rectangular frames. Each frame has its own border color and contains either no seed or exactly one differently colored interior seed; at least one frame is seeded. Fill every seeded frame's complete interior with that frame's local seed color, preserving all borders and leaving seedless frames unchanged. Frames may be separated or directly adjacent.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~8-12) with 1-3 isolated horizontal length-3 target runs and one isolated horizontal length-4 negative run. Every run uses a distinct non-zero color and a distinct row, with blank cells immediately on both sides. The rule extends each exact-length-3 run by one same-colored cell on the left and right, while the length-4 run stays unchanged. The mixed lesson refutes the shortcut that extends every non-zero horizontal run regardless of length.

0-bg grid (size varies). A SOURCE L-frame (2/3/4) with several color-8 MOTIF points at varied local Manhattan radii, and a TARGET L-frame (5/6/7) with its own basis, placed apart. Rule: copy ONLY the source points with the MAXIMUM local Manhattan radius into the target frame's local coords. The grid size, both bases, the motif and the positions all vary freely (was a fixed 12x18 layout, ~12 distinct).
skills: distance ranking, local metrics, frame-relative copy

summary: A black 8-13 by 10-15 grid contains 2-4 active same-colour pairs. Every scene has at least one horizontal and one vertical pair, and most lesson windows include an interior crossing. For a colour occurring exactly twice, fill the inclusive segment only when its cells share a row or column. A scheduled non-aligned pair and a scheduled collinear three-cell colour remain unchanged, refuting L-connection and count-agnostic shortcuts.
Grid split by full color-5 bars (vertical and/or horizontal). Output is an n × 1 column of 0s where n = count of bar-separated 0-regions. Decoy non-bar cells inside regions do not change the count.

0-bg grid (~6-12 by ~8-16) holding 2-5 ISOLATED 4-connected MOTIFS (random polyominoes of 1-6 cells) in DISTINCT non-0 colors, each separated from the others by >=1 bg cell on all sides so they stay distinct components. Rule (PACK COMPONENTS BY SIZE): extract every 4-connected non-bg component; CROP each to its bbox; SORT by (cell-count DESC, color ASC); PACK the crops left-to-right with one bg column between consecutive crops. Output height = tallest crop; width = sum of crop widths + (n-1). Net: the motifs are lined up largest-first into a compact gallery row, ties broken by color.

Find the two equal-colored nonzero endpoints. They must share a row, share a column, or lie on a 45-degree diagonal. Return one row of cyan 8s whose width is max(|dr|, |dc|) + 1. Any four consecutive default samples contain two vertical examples, so a one-pair holdout cannot leave the column-span-only shortcut consistent with every demo.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~10-13) with 2-3 BLOBS of 2-4 cells each (4-connected, grown via grow_blob), each in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {1..9}. Blobs are constrained: (a) STRICTLY IN THE UPPER ROWS (rows h-3 and below are marked `used` to keep blobs out of the bottom 3 rows so gravity has somewhere to drop); (b) DISJOINT COLUMN RANGES — each blob's column span (cmin..cmax) is tracked, and new blobs are required not to overlap any existing column range (so dropping doesn't cause collisions). Bottom rows start empty. Rule (DROP EACH BLOB AS A UNIT TO THE BOTTOM — EACH BLOB SLIDES DOWN UNTIL ITS BBOX-BOTTOM ROW HITS THE GRID BOTTOM): for EACH 4-connected non-bg blob: COMPUTE its bbox top-left (r1, c1) and bbox-bottom row r2. COMPUTE the DROP DELTA = (h-1) - r2 (how many rows the blob can slide before its bbox-bottom hits the grid bottom). SHIFT every cell of the blob DOWN by DROP DELTA rows (cells move from (r, c) to (r + delta, c)). The ORIGINAL blob positions become bg-0; the shifted positions take on the blob's color. Other blobs in disjoint columns are dropped independently. Net: each blob falls as a rigid unit until its lowest cell sits on the bottom row.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~4-7 by ~9-13) with: (a) a full-height vertical WALL of color 8 (cyan) at some column near the right side; (b) 1-3 'source' rows containing 1-3 non-zero non-8 cells at columns strictly LEFT of the wall. Other rows are empty. Rule: scan each row independently. For each non-0 non-8 cell, copy its color rightward into all subsequent columns of that row until just before the wall (or grid edge if no wall). Multiple cells in same row extend their smears; later cells overwrite earlier in column order. Wall preserved. Output: smeared rows + wall.

A zero-background grid contains three separated monochrome pieces. Crop each object to its bounding box, sort the crops by bounding-box perimeter ascending (ties: original left column, then top row), and pack them left-to-right, top-aligned, with one zero column between crops.

A top-row legend orders two or three colors; isolated body seeds grow radius-one pluses after the legend is dropped, and overlaps are painted by legend priority. Every generated scene exposes each adjacent priority comparison, while alternating samples reverse plausible scan/numeric shortcuts.
Canonical 6x6 downscale-by-2 samples: informative cells sit at even/even coordinates and decode to a 3x3 output.
Expand a two-color framed rectangle to include the cyan marker while preserving frame and interior colors.

size × size grid (~7-10) with: (a) outer bg = 0; (b) a SOLID INTERIOR RECTANGLE in some non-{0,2,4} color filling rows 1..size-2, cols 1..size-2; (c) a 2×2 (or 3×3) HOLE of 0s strictly inside the colored rect. Rule: compute sc = mode color (the rect's color). For each color-sc cell with EXACTLY 2 same-color cardinal neighbors that form an L (NOT up+down or left+right) — that's a CORNER. Pick the diagonal cell INWARD from the corner. If that diagonal cell is 0 AND fully enclosed (border-unreachable through bg) → mark corner with color 2 (red). Else mark with color 4 (yellow). Net: each of the 4 inner corners of the rect-frame around the hole gets marked.
Every object shifts vertically to align its top row with the colour-8 object's top row.

Square n × n grid (n in 3..5) with a binary mask using bg=0 and one fg color (the mode). Rule: output is n² × n². For each (R, C) where R, C in [0, n²-1]: br = R//n, bc = C//n (outer block index); sr = R%n, sc = C%n (inner cell index). If input[br][bc] is fg (non-zero), then output[R][C] = fg if input[sr][sc] is bg, else 0. If input[br][bc] is bg, output[R][C] = 0. Equivalent to tiling the inverse of the input onto the fg anchor positions — a fractal.

Two aligned three-column panels are separated by one solid column. Output color 3 appears exactly at aligned 00 positions; 10, 01, and 11 map to 0. Ordinary draws contain all four states, exclude color 3 from the input, and alternate different/same panel colors to refute raw-value equality.

A connected color-4 template and 3-4 anchor origins occur on a zero background.  On a blank output, stamp the normalized template at every anchor: color 1 unchanged, color 2 reflected left-right, and color 3 reflected up-down.  Generated templates make all three transforms visibly distinct, and generated inputs contain every anchor role.

0-bg grid (h, w ~ 8-12) with: (a) ONE STRAIGHT SPINE — 3 SINGLETON CELLS at positions (top, mid, bottom) along ONE AXIS (vertical: at rows 1, h//2, h-2 in a single column; horizontal: at cols 1, w//2, w-2 in a single row). The 3 spine cells are painted in 3 DISTINCT non-0 colors C0, C1, C2 from a palette of 5; (b) OPTIONAL DOMINO MARKERS — with probability 2/3, a 2-cell domino of COLOR C3 placed perpendicular to the spine at one of the spine endpoints; (c) OPTIONAL second domino — with probability 1/2, another 2-cell domino of COLOR C4 placed at the spine's middle endpoint in a perpendicular direction. Rule (EACH SPINE SINGLETON EMITS DIAGONAL RAYS — OPTIONAL DOMINO MARKERS ADD WEDGE FIELDS): for EACH SINGLETON on the SPINE: paint a DIAGONAL RAY in BOTH diagonal directions outward from the spine, using the singleton's color, until the ray hits the grid border or another non-bg cell. For EACH OPTIONAL DOMINO MARKER: paint a WEDGE FIELD — a triangular region adjacent to the domino in the perpendicular direction, filled with the domino's color. The spine singletons and dominoes stay. Net: the input's sparse spine + dominoes blooms into a network of diagonal colored rays plus optional filled wedges.

An inset color-8 rectangle contains exactly two distinct-colored seeds. Every empty interior cell takes the color of its Manhattan-nearest seed; cells tied between the seeds remain background.  Generated lessons vary frame size, palette, seed alignment, tie parity, and seed-color ordering.

One color-2 seed and one color-3 seed on a 0-bg grid (no walls required). Rule does BFS from each seed through 0-cells. For every 0-cell reachable from both with EQUAL distance (i.e., on the perpendicular bisector), paint color 8. Cells that are strictly closer to one seed remain 0.

0-background grid with exactly 2-3 isolated red X patterns. Each pattern has red (2) cells at the four diagonal corners of a 3x3 region and an empty centre. Every empty cell with red in all four immediate diagonal directions becomes blue (1); all other cells are preserved.

Zero-background 6..20 grids with 1..3 distinct colors from 1..9, each marked at 2 opposite, 3 arbitrary, or all 4 corners of an area-disjoint bbox at least 3x3. Complete each color's hollow rectangle outline. Canonical single-color three-corner inputs remain a default component.

0-bg grid (h~10-12, w~11-13) with: (a) KEY COLOR at (0, 0) — a single non-bg cell choosing which shape to operate on; (b) TRANSFORM CODE at (0, w-1) — a single cell with value ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} encoding 1=identity, 2=rotate-CW, 3=rotate-180, 4=rotate-CCW, 5=flip-LR; (c) 3 MULTI-CELL SHAPES placed at random positions in rows 2..h-1, each in a distinct non-bg color from a 3-color palette — EXACTLY ONE of those shapes uses the KEY COLOR from (0, 0). Shapes are 4-conn isolated. Rule: find the shape whose color matches the KEY color. CROP it to its bounding box. APPLY the TRANSFORM encoded by the code. Output: the small transformed crop, in the key color. Net: top-left key picks the shape, top-right code picks the dihedral op; output is the resulting transformed crop.
2 hollow frames + 2 solid components in distinct sizes.

Find the separate hollow red(2) square frames, order their centers clockwise around the shared centroid, and recolor every icon so frame i receives the icon color from frame i+1. The gray(1) connecting track, red frames, icon shapes, and all positions stay fixed.
4 corner colors + interior; rule recolors interior by quadrant.

A rectangular zero-background grid contains 2-4 differently colored, well-separated straight segments. Segment lengths are distinct. Sort the colors by descending segment length; let N be the longest length. Return an N by N grid whose rings, from outside inward, use those colors in descending-length order.

Sparse 0-background grids with three or four colors. Count every painted cell by color, sort by frequency descending and numeric color ascending on ties, then emit one row containing each color once per painted cell. Ordinary examples include an adjacent same-color pair, vary frequency assignments independently of shape and palette, and alternate between tied and distinct frequencies so component-count, profile-lookup, and first-seen tie-break shortcuts are explicitly refuted.

A single CONNECTED region of color-7 corridors (interior of a 0-bg grid, with a few interior holes) holding exactly one color-2 start and one color-3 goal. The rule colors each maze cell by which marker is nearer (with a parity rule); equidistant cells become 8.
2-3 blobs of distinct sizes; smallest is unique.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~11-14) with: (a) ROW 0 containing 1-4 TRANSFORM CODES (values 1-4) at random distinct columns; (b) ROW 1 entirely 0 (separator); (c) ROWS 2..h-1 contain a SMALL BASE MOTIF (3-5 cells, 4-conn) in a DISTINCT color (8 or 9). Rule (PACK TRANSFORMED CROPS BY ROW-0 CODES): identify the BASE MOTIF in rows 2+. CROP its bbox. For EACH TRANSFORM CODE in row 0 (left to right): APPLY the transform (1=identity, 2=rot CW 90°, 3=rot 180°, 4=rot CCW 90°) to the cropped base. PACK the transformed pieces LEFT-TO-RIGHT with ONE BLANK COLUMN between them. Net: motif appears multiple times, transformed per row-0 codes.

Find the displacement from the single red(2) marker to the single green(3) marker. Copy every cell of the connected cyan(8) object by that vector and paint the translated cells blue(1). Keep the source and markers. A connected color-6/7 decoy is irrelevant; when it occupies translated destinations, the blue copy overwrites it.
Find the unique color-1 anchor component and recolor every non-background component that edge-touches it to 4; preserve the anchor and all non-neighbors.

Crop the unique padded nonzero object to its tight bounding box. Output the crop followed immediately by the same crop reflected top-to-bottom, so the output height is twice the crop height and the output width equals the crop width.

Three equal panels, separated by full-height color-8 columns, contain two same-area prototype polyominoes and a differently colored query. Match the query to exactly one prototype under any rotation or reflection; output the displayed prototype support tightly cropped and recolored with the query color.

0-bg grid (h~8-13, w~10-17) with STRUCTURED LAYOUT: (a) ROWS 0 and 1 — LEGEND: at n_pairs (2-4) DISTINCT COLUMNS, row 0 holds a SOURCE COLOR and row 1 holds the corresponding TARGET COLOR (aligned src→dst pairs). Source/target colors are drawn from {2..9} as 2 * n_pairs distinct values. Other cells in rows 0-1 are bg-0; (b) ROW 2 — COLUMN-KEEP MASK: at n_keep (2-8) DISTINCT COLUMNS, paint cells with COLOR 1 (the mask marker). Other cells in row 2 are bg-0; (c) ROWS 3..h-1 — BODY: each body cell is INDEPENDENTLY filled with a random SRC color (from the legend) at density 0.42, plus guaranteed source cells at each (keep_col[i], 3 + (i % (h-3))) position. Rule (RECOLOR BODY VIA LEGEND THEN CROP TO MASK-MARKED COLUMNS): READ the LEGEND (rows 0-1) to build a SRC→DST color map. APPLY the map to every cell in the BODY (rows 3..h-1): each SRC-color cell becomes its DST. READ the MASK (row 2) — get the LIST of KEEP COLUMNS (cells where g[2][c]=1). CROP the recolored body to only those columns. OUTPUT is (h-3) rows × n_keep cols (legend and mask rows are discarded). Net: a recoloring filter applied to the body, then a column-subset crop.

A 0-background HxW grid has exactly two nonzero colors on the top row and the left column; the corner and all interior cells start at 0. Each color occurs one or two times on each border, with a scheduled repeated-marker profile. For each shared color k, collect every left-border row R_k and every top-border column C_k, then paint k at every cell in R_k x C_k on a fresh blank output grid. Border markers are erased in the output. Repeated markers therefore expand to multiple intersections.

0-bg grid (h~6-10, w~4-7) with: (a) ONE FULL-WIDTH FLOOR ROW of COLOR 8 at the BOTTOM (row h-1, all cols painted 8); (b) 2-3 HORIZONTAL COLORED BARS above the floor — each bar is 1 ROW TALL, has a chosen LENGTH from 1..w-1 in a DISTINCT NON-8 color from a palette ({1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9} or kind-restricted), placed at distinct rows in [0, h-2] with position bias (scattered/left-lean/right-lean/centered) and size skew (small/big/even). Bars don't overlap. Rule (SORT BARS BY SIZE DESC, PACK BOTTOM-RIGHT ABOVE FLOOR): identify all colored bars (each its own row segment) and their lengths. SORT by LENGTH DESCENDING (biggest first, tiebreak by color). Output is a fresh grid same h × w with the floor row preserved at the bottom (row h-1 = 8s). Pack the sorted bars STACKED bottom-up, RIGHT-ALIGNED, each on its own row immediately above the floor (row h-2, h-3, h-4, ...). Net: bars sorted big-to-small, right-stacked on top of the 8-floor.

Treat each exact red/cyan 2x2 block as a visibility-graph node. Starting at the unique red block, choose the longest simple orthogonal visibility path; break equal-length ties lexicographically by right, down, left, up, then paint orange corridors only between consecutive chosen nodes.
Place one 2..4 by 2..4 solid gray rectangle and two distinct colored markers; recolor each gray cell to its Manhattan-nearest marker, with lower color then row/column resolving ties.
Top legend (3-color priority) + 2x2 5-walled chambers with 1-2 seeds each.
Fill zero cells on the global nonzero bounding-box perimeter with 8; preserve all sources.

Cell (0,0) names a body-object color, cell (0,1) gives a transform code (1=rotate clockwise, 2=rotate 180, 3=rotate counterclockwise, 4=flip left-right, 5=flip up-down), and cell (0,2) gives a new color. Select the uniquely matching body object, crop and transform it, recolor its occupied cells to the target color, and center-stamp it in a 7x7 grid.
Same-color objects slide right as rigid bodies, rightmost first.

A canonical-sized zero-background grid contains one blue legend, exactly three red candidates, and one tiny irrelevant-color marker. Exactly one red candidate is rotation-equivalent to the legend and is recolored cyan 8. A mirrored-but-not-rotated control and a same-size/same-bbox different shape remain red.

Fill a blank cell only when equal nonzero endpoints lie exactly two rows and two columns apart; copy the endpoint color into that diagonal midpoint. Every scene has both diagonal orientations. Consecutive sample indices cycle through axis-aligned, wrong-distance/different-color, and blocked-midpoint near misses that remain unchanged. Every third ordinary sample rehearses a canonical 6x9, 7x7, or 8x8 morphology in every difficulty band; explicit size/count overrides remain authoritative.

A 12..14 by 17..20 zero-background grid contains exactly two detached hollow color-9 rectangular frames. Color-5 dividers split frame interiors into chambers. One or two distinct non-{0,5,9} key cells sit in separate 4-connected open regions, while at least one region remains unkeyed. Flood each key through original 0/same-color cells, stopping at both color-5 and color-9 walls; leave all walls and unkeyed chambers unchanged.
Use each column's solid swatch row and fill to recolor its duplicated 1/2/8 pattern tile.
A padded 1-3 colour motif with 1-3 components is cropped to its nonzero bounding box and rotated 90 degrees clockwise.

Arbitrary rectangular grid with H≥2 rows and a small palette of colors. Rule: reverse the row order (flip-ud) — output[r] = input[H-1-r]. Column order, grid dimensions, and palette are unchanged. Top and bottom rows must differ so the flip is visible in the demo.
Magenta components recolored by adjacent label cells; labels removed.

Fixed 9×9 grid with: (a) a LATTICE of full rows + full cols at rows/cols [1, 3, 5, 7] in some non-bg LATTICE COLOR (forms a 4×4 grid of intersections); (b) at each lattice intersection (4×4 = 16 cells), an ANOMALY cell in some non-{0, lattice} color (may be 0 for inner intersections). Rule: detect the lattice color and the 4×4 anomaly grid at intersections. SUMMARIZE the anomalies by CORNER (outer 4 intersections), EDGE (middle of each side), and CENTER groups into a 3×3 output grid where each output cell is the dominant or representative anomaly color from that zone.

Any colored grid of size at least 3×3 (typical h, w ~3-14). The grid is filled with a TEXTURE (noise / sparse / blob / stripes / gradient / checkerboard / frame / ring / plus) using a 5-color palette + a chosen background color. The TOP-RIGHT 3×3 CORNER is overlaid with a specific pattern (mixed_9, two_colors, one_color, or palette_corner). Rule: EXTRACT the TOP-RIGHT 3×3 CORNER of the input grid (rows 0, 1, 2 × cols w-3, w-2, w-1) and RETURN it as the entire output. The rest of the input is discarded. Output is a 3×3 grid. Net: rule is just 'crop to top-right 3×3 corner' regardless of input size or content.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one full-height maroon (9) divider, one connected blue (1) motif entirely to its left, and non-blue coloured decorations. Reflect every blue cell across the divider and paint the reflected destination cyan (8), overwriting a decoration when it occupies that destination. Preserve the source motif, divider, background, and all decorations outside blue reflection targets.

FIXED 5×5 grid with: (a) FOUR COMMAND CELLS — at fixed positions (2, 0) = rc1 (row command 1), (4, 0) = rc2 (row command 2), (0, 1) = cc1 (col command 1), (0, 3) = cc2 (col command 2), each ∈ {1, 2, 3}; (b) 3×3 MOTIF — at subgrid (2, 1)..(4, 3) filled with COLOR 4 in a specific shape pattern: cells (3, 2), (3, 3), (4, 1), (4, 2), (4, 3) all = 4 (an inverted L shape). Rule (2×2 META-TILE TRANSFORM PER (ROW CMD, COL CMD) PAIR): output is a 2×2 GRID of TILES, each a COPY of the 3×3 motif transformed by the (row_cmd, col_cmd) pair at that tile position: tile (0, 0) uses (rc1, cc1); tile (0, 1) uses (rc1, cc2); tile (1, 0) uses (rc2, cc1); tile (1, 1) uses (rc2, cc2). Each cmd ∈ {1, 2, 3} applies a specific transform (identity, horizontal-flip, vertical-flip per puzzle convention). Net: 4 transformed copies of the motif tiled together by command-pair lookup.
1 single-cell marker (color C) + 2-3 multi-cell shapes, one matching C.
Small multicolor grid; rule tiles n × n times where n = number of distinct colors.
Isolated blue diagonal pairs in 2x2 boxes are completed into red 2x2 squares.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-10, w ∈ 8-12) with: SEGMENT_COUNT ∈ 1-4 DOMINO GROUPS, each consisting of: (a) ONE 2-CELL DOMINO (horizontal or vertical, oriented per candidate kind ∈ {h_right, h_left, v_down, v_up}) painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 9} color drawn from {1..8}; (b) ONE COLOR-9 BLOCKER CELL adjacent to ONE end of the domino — for h_right: blocker at (r, c-1) on the left side; for h_left: blocker at (r, c+2); for v_down: blocker at (r-1, c) above; for v_up: blocker at (r+2, c) below. The OPEN CONTINUATION cell (opposite the blocker) is in-bounds and currently 0 — only one side is blocked, the other is open. Placements use _clear_patch with 1-cell neighborhood check. Rule (FOR EACH DOMINO, EXTEND ITS COLOR INTO THE OPEN CONTINUATION CELL — THE BLOCKED SIDE STAYS AS-IS): For EACH domino (2 same-color cells): DETERMINE the BLOCKED side (adjacent color-9 cell) and the OPEN side (currently 0).
