PAINT the OPEN cell with the domino's color, EXTENDING the domino by 1 cell. Blockers stay 9. Net: each domino grows by one into its open continuation, becoming a 3-cell line.
Stamp the unique marker-cell pattern into every lattice cell sharing both source row parity and source column parity, clipping at partial edges.
Each blob whose shape is a hollow rectangle outline gets its interior filled with the frame color. Non-frame blobs (irregular shapes, solid blocks) are left unchanged.

Scan monochrome 4-connected components in row-major order, select the first component whose bounding-box crop is left-right symmetric, crop it, and recolor every nonzero cell to cyan(8). A four-step schedule covers the canonical three- and five-component scene counts; three-component lessons anchor the canonical 11x11 four-color profile, and five-component lessons add a later same-color symmetric competitor so order, not size or color alone, determines the answer.

Extract each nonzero 4-connected object, crop it to its bounding box, sort by bounding-box width descending, then height descending, then color ascending, and vertically pack the left-aligned crops with one zero row between neighbors.
Color-2 and color-3 endpoint segments intersect at one cell.

Build a contact graph of differently colored four-connected objects and paint only its unique articulation object cyan on a blank same-size grid. Disconnected distractors and a scheduled biconnected contrast refute color, area, and maximum-degree shortcuts.

Find the first all-zero column; it ends the left source prefix. Preserve that prefix, copy it in the same orientation to the right edge, and fill the intervening columns of each row with that row's column-0 color.

A control at (0,0) selects a local transform of one separated, connected, single-color 3-6-cell motif: 1=90cw, 2=180, 3=flip-lr, 4=flip-ud. The motif and its transformed footprint both fit; the selected transform changes the motif. Other symmetries are allowed, including canonical T shapes. Paint on a fresh zero canvas at the original bbox top-left; discard the control.

Row 0 cells 0..2 are (prototype color, transform code, output color). The transform map is 1=identity, 2=flip left-right, 3=flip up-down, 4=rotate clockwise, 5=rotate 180 degrees, and 6=rotate counterclockwise. Select the matching object from a three-object color library, transform and recolor it, then center it inside the cropped 6x7 cyan frame.
Separated top-row run lengths map gray body-object sizes to recolor targets; every instance contains exactly three gray objects.
Exact hollow 3x3 yellow-ring components receive cyan centers.

A color-9 cross forms demonstration panels A and B, query panel C, and an empty answer panel.  B is a strict bbox-aligned superset of A.  Copy C to the answer panel and stamp exactly the relative B-minus-A cells in C's color.  Ordinary four-pair lessons schedule within-bbox, right-expanding, down-expanding, and two-axis-expanding edits; they also include query shapes that differ from A so copying B's silhouette is not a valid shortcut.
Gray walls forming compartments; red seed inside one + green distractor in another; flood with 8.

A 0-background 7..10 by 8..12 grid contains 2..4 singleton seeds in exactly two nonzero colors. Scan seeds in row-major order: each seed paints itself and every in-bounds chess-knight destination in its color, with later seeds overwriting earlier paint. Ordinary draws include an overlap where a later lower color defeats an earlier higher color, while also varying clipped and fully visible halos.

Horizontally-tiled grid: panel_h × W where panel_h ∈ {3-5} and W = 3 * n + (n-1) with n ∈ {4, 5} panels. Layout: (a) n PANELS each panel_h rows × 3 cols, arranged left-to-right; (b) FULL color-9 DIVIDER COLUMNS between panels; (c) PANEL 0 holds the TEMPLATE — a 2-3 cell connected motif in a single non-{0, 9} color drawn from {2..7}; (d) PANELS 1..n-1 hold CANDIDATE MOTIFS: 50% of candidates are a DIHEDRAL VARIANT (rotation or reflection) of the template (also in the template's color); the rest are random non-template shapes in the same color. Rule (MARK THE MISMATCHED PANELS — THOSE WHOSE MOTIFS ARE NOT A DIHEDRAL VARIANT OF THE TEMPLATE — WITH COLOR 8 STRIP MARKERS): READ the TEMPLATE in panel 0. COMPUTE its DIHEDRAL VARIANTS (8 rotations + reflections). For EACH CANDIDATE PANEL (panels 1..n-1): CHECK if its motif (normalized) matches ANY template variant. IF the motif does NOT match (mismatch): MARK that panel — e.g., paint a COLOR 8 (cyan) VERTICAL STRIP at the panel's rightmost interior column or above the panel's index per demos. Matching panels stay unchanged. The template panel and 9-dividers also stay. Net: each candidate panel either keeps its motif (dihedral match) or gets a cyan strip marker (mismatch). Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=21): output normalizes across small motif and marker permutations.
skills: dihedral normalization, candidate comparison, odd-one-out selection

summary: A 6..12 by 6..12 zero-background grid containing exactly 3..12 nonzero cells in 1..3 separated, monochrome components. Different components use distinct colors, and at least one component contains an orthogonal corner. The edge_mode axis is either in_bounds (every cell has a valid (+1,+1) destination) or mixed (at least one cell clips at the bottom/right edge while at least one cell moves). The output rule starts from a fresh zero canvas and shifts each nonzero cell by (+1,+1), dropping out-of-bounds destinations.
Move the central ring's 9 one coarse step toward 6 and recolor the destination marker 9.

On a 0-background grid, treat each nonzero monochrome 4-connected component as an object. Normalize each object to its bounding box and keep it in place exactly when its occupied cells are invariant under left-right reflection; erase every other object. Generated lessons pair vertical-only and horizontal-only reflection cases and match object sizes and bounding boxes across roles so color, position, prototype, size, aspect-ratio, and horizontal-symmetry shortcuts fail.
1 ref (color 2) + 1 target (color 3) + a small template shape; translate by ref→target.

On a black background, identify the complete one-cell rectangular outline frames, ignore any non-frame singleton/domino inside them, and keep only the frame nested inside the greatest number of other frames.

Given a dense square grid, inspect its width. If the width is odd, copy the top-left 2x2 crop. If the width is even, copy the top-right 2x2 crop. Both candidate corners are varied and non-degenerate, so parity—not corner content—selects the answer.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) containing 3-4 small connected MOTIFS, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color from {2..9}. Each motif is 3-5 cells (random-walk polyomino) at scattered non-overlapping positions with 1-cell padding (isolated connected components). Rule: identify each distinct non-bg COLOR and extract its motif's normalized cells. PACK every motif's bbox into a VERTICAL GALLERY OUTPUT — stack the motifs top-to-bottom (or in canonical order by color or size) into a smaller composite grid, each motif in its original color. Output size depends on motif count and dimensions. Net: input has scattered colored motifs; output is a clean vertical pack.

A 6x8, 7x9, or 8x10 zero-background grid has exactly three keyed rows. Each keyed row begins with a nonzero, non-cyan color and contains one to three cyan (8) markers. The selected rule recolors only those cyan cells whose row has a nonzero key; scheduled cyan markers in zero-key rows are preserved and distinguish the rule from an erase-empty-row shortcut.

Distinct colors in row 0 define a left-to-right directed cycle. Every body cell whose color occurs in the strip changes to the next strip color; the strip, background, and out-of-strip body colors remain unchanged.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-9) with: (a) ONE COLOR-3 (green) CELL at (r3, c3); (b) ONE COLOR-4 (yellow) CELL at (r4, c4). Cells are placed so Manhattan distance ≥ min_separation (2-4) and direction (relative placement) is one of 8 cardinal/diagonal directions (n/s/e/w/nw/ne/sw/se). No other cells. Rule (SHIFT COLOR-3 ONE STEP TOWARD COLOR-4): identify the 3-cell at (r3, c3) and the 4-cell at (r4, c4). COMPUTE delta = (sign(r4 - r3), sign(c4 - c3)). ERASE the 3-cell (g[r3][c3] = 0). PLACE the 3-cell at (r3 + dr, c3 + dc) (one step toward the 4-cell). The 4-cell stays. Net: green cell takes one step toward the yellow target.

Find the free multicolor template and every hollow gray frame. Read the single nearby key for each frame, transform the template by 1=identity, 2=rotate clockwise, 3=flip left/right, or 4=flip up/down, and center the transformed stamp inside that frame. Remove the source template and keys.

0-bg grid (h, w~11-15) with: (a) ONE FULL-WIDTH HORIZONTAL DIVIDER ROW at random row div_r and ONE FULL-HEIGHT VERTICAL DIVIDER COL at random col div_c, both painted in a single non-zero div_color — carving the grid into 4 BLOCKS (TL, TR, BL, BR); (b) ONE of the 4 blocks (randomly chosen) contains CONTENT — scattered cells in 3 non-divider colors at fill density ~0.4 plus an anchor cell at (sr0, sc0); the other 3 blocks are EMPTY. Rule: identify the ONE FILLED BLOCK. EXTRACT its pattern (cells and colors). COPY that pattern into each of the other 3 EMPTY BLOCKS at corresponding LOCAL positions (matched offsets from each block's top-left). The dividers stay. Net: 4 blocks all show the same pattern; the one filled block is replicated to complete the layout.
A connected multicolor source blob and one color-9 marker. Crop the source to its tight bounding box, clear the source, and stamp the crop with the marker as its top-left destination cell.
Multiple vertical bars with one unique tallest bar.

On a zero background, find monochromatic four-connected components, rank them by cell count with row-major order as the tie break, and recolor only the first smallest component to maroon (9). Vary canonical dimensions, object count, connected shapes, positions, minimum size, minimum ties, repeated colors, and target position relative to larger objects.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with TWO COLOR PAIRS: pair 1 is two cells of color A on row r1 at columns c1 and c2; pair 2 is two cells of color B on row r2 at the SAME columns c1 and c2 (aligned, parallel bars). r1 < r2, and ≥1 interior row between them. Rule: find color groups appearing exactly TWICE. Get pair 1 and pair 2. Determine orientation (horizontal here). Compute the rectangular BAND between the two parallel bars — bbox (min row, c1, max row, c2). Output: fresh empty grid with that rectangle painted color 8 (cyan).

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~10-14) with OBJECTS of THREE FIXED COLORS (2, 3, 4): for each color c ∈ {2, 3, 4}, place counts[c] (1-5) INSTANCES at slot positions from a fixed slot list (sparse rows × sparse cols). Each instance is a single cell, with 35% probability extended to a 2-cell horizontal pair by painting the cell to its right. Counts per color are INDEPENDENT and may vary 1-5. Rule (COUNT OBJECTS OF COLORS 2, 3, 4 — EMIT GROUPED COLOR RUNS SEPARATED BY ZEROS): COUNT the number of 4-CONNECTED color-2 components → n2. Same for color-3 → n3 and color-4 → n4. PRODUCE a SINGLE-ROW OUTPUT: emit n2 cells of COLOR 2, then a bg-0 separator, then n3 cells of COLOR 3, then bg-0, then n4 cells of COLOR 4. Output length = n2 + n3 + n4 + 2 (the separators). Net: the input's scattered colored objects collapse into a single-row count encoding. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=20): bounded by 5³ count combinations.
Reflect a multicolour upper-left motif across both full-grid midlines.
Wall-bounded room with 2-5 colored seeds; zeros fill by nearest seed, ties become 9.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 2-5 SINGLETON SEEDS — single non-0 cells placed at positions on a 3-cell stride grid (rows 0, 3, 6, ...; cols 0, 3, 6, ...) so their 2×2 expansions don't conflict. Each seed uses a DISTINCT color from {1..8} (color (i % 8) + 1). Rule (EXPAND EACH SINGLETON INTO A 2×2 SAME-COLOR BLOCK, ANCHORED AT THE SEED AS TOP-LEFT): For EACH SINGLETON SEED at (r, c) with color C: PAINT the cells (r, c), (r, c+1), (r+1, c), (r+1, c+1) with color C. The seed stays. Net: every non-0 cell becomes the top-left corner of a 2×2 solid block in its color.

0-bg grid with a small cluster of color-2 (red) cells and a separate cluster of color-3 (green) cells. Rule: expand a manhattan radius from both sets simultaneously and stop at the first radius where their neighborhoods overlap; the output paints that meeting region in 8 (cyan) -- the manhattan-bisector between the two sets. Positions, counts and grid size vary freely.

15×16 grid (0-bg) with 2-3 hollow rectangular FRAMES (border-only rectangles) in distinct non-zero colors. Each frame's interior contains 2-4 non-zero pattern cells in a color DIFFERENT from its frame color (and different from any other frame's color). Frames don't overlap. Rule: detect all rectangular hollow frames. Sort them by frame color ascending. For each frame, extract its interior (cells strictly inside the border): keep cells whose color is not 0 and not the frame color. Crop the interior to its bounding box. Build a gallery: stack all cropped interiors LEFT-TO-RIGHT, TOP-ALIGNED, with a 1-cell gap between them. Output height = max of crop heights; width = sum of crop widths + (n-1) gaps.

0-bg grid with two separated colored polyomino objects of distinct areas. Rule: extract the non-bg objects, normalize each shape to its bbox origin, sort objects by descending area (scan-order tie break), and pack the normalized shapes horizontally with one blank column gap.
A top-row tile library maps key colors to 2-motifs; bottom query tiles name keys.
skills: tile library lookup, key-value matching, source-to-query transfer

summary: A 9x9..17x17 background-0 grid is split into a 3x3 array of panels by exactly two full color-8 rows and two full color-8 columns. Each panel contains a controlled number of color-6 cells. The output is a 3x3 binary mask whose entry is 1 iff the corresponding panel contains at least two color-6 cells. Every generated profile includes counts 1, 2, and 3 to teach the threshold rather than an exact-count shortcut.

0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~12-16) with: (a) ONE FRAME of border_color drawn as a full rectangle outline at (r0, c0)..(r1, c1) of size frame_h × frame_w (6-8 × 5-7), placed by POSITION_BIAS (centered/corner/near_edge/anywhere); (b) NOISE CELLS in palette colors (warm/cool/broad/primary) at density 0.3-0.55, EXCLUDING the border. The border color uniquely forms a ≥80%-complete rectangular border ≥8 cells. Rule (FIND FRAME COLOR + CROP INTERIOR): SCAN colors 1..9 in order. For each color, COMPUTE its cells' bbox. CHECK if the cells form ≥80% of the bbox perimeter (border match count * 5 > 4 * perimeter) AND have ≥8 cells. The FIRST color satisfying this is the FRAME COLOR. CROP to the INTERIOR of the frame's bbox (excluding border cells). Output: the cropped interior of the frame's bbox. Net: locate the boundary color, crop out its interior.
A 3x3 binary-colour mask is self-tiled into a 9x9 output: each foreground mask cell selects an exact copy of the input, while each background mask cell selects a blank 3x3 block.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~8-12) with 2-4 SINGLETON SEED CELLS at scattered positions with Manhattan distance > 2 between any pair (so radius-1 diamond footprints don't overlap). Each seed in a random color from {1..9}. Rule (EXPAND EACH SEED INTO RADIUS-1 CARDINAL DIAMOND): For EACH SEED at (r, c) with color C: PAINT the 4 CARDINAL NEIGHBORS — (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1) — with COLOR C, clipping at grid edges. The seed cell stays. The result is a 5-cell plus-shape (or smaller if at border) in color C per seed. Net: each seed becomes a + diamond of its color.

Three or four separated monochrome objects are recolored from their tight-mask reflection signature: both left-right and up-down symmetric -> 8, left-right only -> 2, up-down only -> 3, and neither -> 4. Canonical-scale profiles recur in every difficulty band, while alternating teaching profiles use unseen masks to refute exact canonical-mask memorization.

0-bg grid (h~7-14, w~8-16) with 1-3 ISOLATED non-bg cells, each in a distinct color (no color-2 in input). Cells are placed at distinct rows AND distinct columns. Rule: for each non-bg cell at (r, c) with color v, PAINT a full CROSS — every cell in row r and every cell in column c — with color v. Where TWO CROSSES OVERLAP (a cell sits on row(a) ∩ col(b) or row(b) ∩ col(a) for two different seeds), PAINT that intersection cell with color 2 (red) — the conflict marker — OVERRIDING the per-seed color. The original seed cells stay their own color. Net: input has isolated colored dots; output has full cross shapes per dot with red marking where two crosses cross-intersect.

A black 7..16 by 7..16 grid contains 2..3 distinct colors, each in exactly two diagonally opposite cells of an axis-aligned rectangle. Rectangles are either spatially disjoint or form a strictly nested chain; their outlines never overlap.  At least one rectangle is hollow and at least one is two cells thick.  Draw every rectangle outline in its corner color on a fresh black canvas.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~8-11) with 2-4 isolated PARTIAL PLUS motifs. Each plus: a center cell + 3 same-color cardinal arm cells (up, down, left, right minus one). The missing 4th arm cell is bg (0), in-bounds, and the remaining 3 arms are all the same color. Different pluses use distinct colors; motifs isolated by ≥2 bg cells on all sides. Rule: scan every cell. For each non-bg cell, count how many of its 4 cardinal neighbors have the same color. If exactly 3 → identify the missing cardinal direction and paint that neighbor with the cell's color (if in bounds and currently 0). Net effect: complete each partial plus by filling its missing arm.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-14) with: (a) ONE FULL-LENGTH COLOR-2 (red) EDGE LINE on ONE of the 4 GRID EDGES (top row, bottom row, left col, or right col); (b) 3-5 CONNECTED COLORED OBJECTS in DISTINCT non-{0, 2} colors, each a 1-3 cell shape from a small bank, scattered in the INTERIOR (not touching the red line). Objects are placed at non-touching positions (1-cell 8-conn buffer). Rule (SLIDE OBJECTS TOWARD THE RED LINE, STACKING): DETECT the red line's EDGE → DIRECTION (up/down/left/right TOWARD the line). SORT objects by DISTANCE to the line (closest first). For EACH object in that order: SLIDE the entire object (as a rigid group) toward the line by max amount until it hits the RED LINE or a PREVIOUSLY-PLACED object's cells. The line stays. Net: objects stack against the red line in distance-order.

A zero-background grid has 2-4 separated monochrome objects above a bottom-row key of the same length. Read the nonzero key colors from left to right, sort the objects by left edge and then top edge, recolor object i with key color i, and erase the key row.

Square 5..12 grids with 3..9 colored off-diagonal sources. Distinct transpose orbits keep every destination empty; positions span multiple rows and columns and occur on both sides of the main diagonal, so each lesson teaches bidirectional additive transpose without collision semantics.

0-bg grid (h~8-12, w~10-15) with: (a) ONE CORNER MARKER — a COLOR-1 cell at one of the four corners {(0, 0), (0, w-1), (h-1, 0), (h-1, w-1)} encoding WHICH ROTATION to apply (TL/TR/BL/BR → 0°/90°/180°/270°); (b) OPTIONAL FLIP MARKER — a COLOR-3 cell at (0, w//2) with 50% probability, requesting a horizontal flip in addition to rotation; (c) ONE ASYMMETRIC RED (color 2) SHAPE — a fixed 5-cell shape placed at the vertical center column (col w//2), spanning rows 2..5. All other cells are bg-0. Rule (CROP-TRANSFORM THE RED SHAPE BY THE CORNER+FLIP CONTROLS, OUTPUT AS CYAN ON A FRESH GRID): READ the CORNER MARKER (color 1) — its position determines a ROTATION code. READ the FLIP MARKER (color 3, present or absent) — its presence determines a horizontal FLIP code. EXTRACT the RED SHAPE (color 2) and CROP to its bbox. APPLY the chosen ROTATION (and FLIP if requested) to the cropped shape. OUTPUT the TRANSFORMED CROP as COLOR 8 (cyan) on a fresh bg-0 grid sized to the transformed shape's bbox. Original markers and red shape are discarded. Net: a small cyan output showing the red shape transformed by the corner/flip controls. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=4): 4 corners × 2 flip × 1 shape = 8 possible outputs, bounded by the fixed shape.

Read the distinct nonzero colours across row 0 from left to right. For each listed colour, find its unique same-colour body component, crop that object to its bounding box, and pack the selected crops left-to-right with one zero column between them. Ignore unlisted distractor objects. Default lessons include distractors and cases where body position disagrees with the header order.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-10, w ∈ 8-12, by difficulty) with: N ∈ 2-4 CONNECTED MOTIFS, each a 3-5 cell connected motif built via _build_motif random adjacent-step walk, painted in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from {1..9}. Each motif's bbox is ≥2×2 (single-row or single-col motifs filtered out). Motifs placed at non-overlapping positions via _free check with 1-cell padding. Rule (FOR EACH 4-CONNECTED NON-BG COMPONENT, PAINT THE 4 EDGES OF ITS BBOX (TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT) WITH THE COMPONENT'S COLOR — TURNING THE BBOX INTO A HOLLOW RECTANGULAR OUTLINE; INTERIOR REMAINS PARTLY PAINTED FROM THE ORIGINAL MOTIF): For EACH component with color c and bbox (rmin, cmin, rmax, cmax): PAINT all cells (rmin, c) and (rmax, c) for c in cmin..cmax, and (r, cmin) and (r, cmax) for r in rmin..rmax with COLOR c. Interior cells keep their original (motif or bg) values. Net: each motif gets wrapped in its color's rectangular bbox outline.
N non-touching blobs of distinct sizes; output is NxN size-comparison matrix.
A large rectangular frame surrounds interior content; rule extracts the interior.
A 10..12 by 11..14 grid contains crossing near-full 5/6 guides and a 6..9-cell, two-color motif in one quadrant. Reflect the motif across both guide axes into all four quadrants.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 connected MOTIFS at distinct non-touching positions, each in a DISTINCT color from {2..9} and each of size 3-5 cells (4-conn random walk). Motifs have 1-cell padding from each other and grid edges. Rule (VERTICAL GALLERY PACK): identify each MOTIF as a connected component. CROP each motif to its BBOX. STACK the cropped motifs VERTICALLY in canonical order. Output WIDTH = MAX bbox width; HEIGHT = SUM of bbox heights. Net: scattered motifs → vertically packed gallery.

Place three or five isolated color-6 objects with distinct cell areas. Select the median-area object, transpose its normalized shape, and return the tight color-6 crop. A five-slot schedule varies count, median area, reading order, shape, position, and dimensions while retaining canonical 12x12/13x13 anchors.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 8-13, by difficulty) with: (a) BOTTOM ROW (row h-1) ENTIRELY filled with COLOR-1 (FLOOR); (b) N_WALLS ∈ 0-5 additional COLOR-1 cells placed at random interior positions (rows 2..h-3) acting as walls/floors splitting columns; (c) N_MARKERS ∈ 2-10 scattered NON-1 COLORED MARKERS (colors 2..9) placed at random non-1 positions in rows 0..h-2. Rule (COLUMN GRAVITY: FOR EACH COLUMN, NON-1 SEGMENTS BETWEEN ADJACENT 1-CELLS COLLECT THEIR NON-0 NON-1 MARKERS AND PACK THEM AT THE BOTTOM OF EACH SEGMENT; 1-CELLS AND THE FLOOR STAY): For EACH column c: SPLIT it into segments separated by COLOR-1 cells (walls + floor). For EACH segment: EXTRACT its non-0 non-1 markers in order; CLEAR the segment to 0; PACK the markers at the BOTTOM of the segment (just above the next 1). Net: every marker falls down its column until it lands on a 1-cell.

Crop the input to the tight bounding rectangle containing every nonzero cell. Preserve all colours, component spacing, and interior background cells exactly. Canonical anchors include the lawful one-component, one-colour case; the surrounding schedule deliberately supplies sparse multi-component and multicolour witnesses that refute shortcut rules.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-12) with 2-4 SAME-COLOR ENDPOINT TRIPLES — each TRIPLE consists of two cells of a DISTINCT non-0 color separated by EXACTLY ONE ZERO CELL between them, either HORIZONTAL (r, c), (r, c+1)=0, (r, c+2) or VERTICAL (r, c), (r+1, c)=0, (r+2, c). Triples don't overlap or touch each other (via 8-conn clearance check). Colors are distinct across triples. Rule (BRIDGE THE MIDPOINT OF EACH DISTANCE-2 SAME-COLOR PAIR): For each pair of same-color cells at axis-aligned distance 2 (one 0 between them): find the MIDPOINT cell (the 0-cell between) and PAINT it with the pair's color. The endpoints stay. Net: each distance-2 axis-aligned same-color pair becomes a solid 3-cell line.

One to three separated color-5 boxes contain colored cells in separate, stacked, or mixed columns. Gravity acts independently inside every box; the output also repairs an optional non-5 overwrite on a box border.

A unique border 2 launches a beam through interior / (3) and \ (4) mirrors. Paint traversed zeros 8, preserving objects; stop at a wall 5 or exit. Four scheduled profiles teach walls, long routes and repeated mirror orientations, with occluded and off-path distractors.

0-bg grid (h, w ~6-10) with 2-4 isolated color-2 (red) ANCHOR cells placed at well-spaced positions (rows/cols at multiples of 3, so halos don't conflict). Rule: for each color-2 anchor at (r, c), KEEP the anchor at value 2, and PAINT each of its 4 DIAGONAL neighbors (r±1, c±1) with color 7 (orange). Cardinal neighbors stay 0. Net: each red anchor grows into a 5-cell X pattern — red center + orange diagonal halo.
Canonical 3×3 non-zero grid with 1, 2, or 3 distinct colors; rule emits one of three count-keyed 5-patterns.

0-bg grid with N (3-5) connected color-2 components of STRICTLY DISTINCT sizes (the smallest must be unique). May include 0..1 decoration cells in other colors (e.g. color 5 in a corner). Rule: extract all color-2 components, sort by cell count ascending, take the first (smallest), recolor its cells to color 8. Other 2-blobs and decoration cells preserved.

A unique color-9 pivot copies one connected monochrome motif across the pivot column when the motif is wholly left/right; otherwise it copies an above/below motif across the pivot row. Column priority is exercised explicitly when both conditions hold.
A 3x(3N) strip of 3x3 zones; each zone is relabeled by gray-cell count, with three-cell top/bottom/other shapes mapping to different colors.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~10-12) with 4 BLOBS each a 2-4 cell 4-connected blob grown via grow_blob, painted in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from a shuffled palette {1..9}. Each blob's BBOX WIDTH is STRICTLY DISTINCT from the other 3 (seen_widths set ensures no two blobs share width). Blobs are placed at non-touching non-overlapping positions via used-cell tracking. Rule (SORT BLOBS BY BBOX WIDTH ASCENDING, GALLERY-PACK HORIZONTALLY): extract every 4-CONNECTED non-bg COMPONENT. CROP each to its tight bbox. SORT crops by BBOX WIDTH ASCENDING (since widths are strictly distinct, sort is unambiguous). PACK the cropped blobs LEFT-TO-RIGHT in sorted order with a 1-column bg gap between consecutive crops, into a horizontal output grid. OUTPUT HEIGHT = max bbox_h across blobs; shorter crops are bottom-aligned (or top-aligned per demos). Net: 4 scattered blobs collapse into a horizontal gallery ordered by increasing width.
A small 7-frame interior is transplanted into a larger 7-frame.

Input is 13 × w (w ~3-14). Rows 0-5 = TOP panel, row 6 = solid-color separator, rows 7-12 = BOTTOM panel. Each panel filled with some pattern (random/blob/stripes/checker/border/diagonal) at a chosen density in some color. Rule: output is 6 × w. For each (r, c) with r ∈ [0,5]: output[r][c] = 3 (green) IFF (input[r][c] == 0) XOR (input[r+7][c] == 0) — i.e. exactly ONE of the two panels has a zero at that cell (equivalently: the cells differ in zero/non-zero). Otherwise 0.
Move the red object along each separated axis until its bounding box abuts cyan.
One to three colors each appear exactly twice. Their two endpoints define a row segment, column segment, or rectangle outline.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holding a KEY COLOR from a 3-color palette; (b) ONE KEY-COLOR BLOB (2-4 cells, connected polyomino) placed AWAY from the (0, 0) corner in the same key color; (c) 1-2 DISTRACTOR BLOBS in the other 2 palette colors (2-3 cells each, non-overlapping). Rule: READ the KEY at (0, 0). Find the UNIQUE BLOB of matching KEY COLOR that's NOT at the corner. CROP that blob to its BBOX and OUTPUT the cropped subgrid (preserving key color and shape). Distractors and the corner-key are discarded. Net: corner-key selects the target by color; output is bbox crop of the matching non-corner blob.

Rectangular frame in one color + guide lines in another color (one row through and one col through the frame interior). Rule moves the guide lines so the horizontal guide aligns with the TOP frame row (r1) and the vertical guide aligns with the RIGHT frame col (c2); cells outside the frame on those new lines are line-colored, others become 0. Frame border preserved.

A 0-background grid contains 3-6 isolated, monochromatic, 4-connected objects with at least two different areas and at least one non-rectangular object. Replace each object by a one-column vertical bar of the same colour and height equal to its cell count. Sort bars by descending area; break equal-area ties by object top row and then left column. Pack bars left-to-right with one zero spacer column and bottom-align them. Separate objects may share a colour and still produce separate bars.
Sparse 2-cells; rule fills 0s bracketed by 2s with 2 below.

Exactly four yellow cells mark the corners of a rectangular crop. A connected three-colour key lies below the crop. Two or three complete same-colour square blocks already appear inside the crop at positions consistent with selected key cells. Infer the common block size from those references, scale every key cell to that square size, align the key to the references, and return only the completed corner-marked rectangle.
Flood reachable black cells cyan from the red seed without crossing gray walls.

A square 16-22 grid has a color-1 upper field and color-6 lower field. A connected color-5 rectangular-mask patch is flush with the left or right edge and ends immediately above the split. Move the entire source rectangle to the opposite edge, preserve its mask, and shear rows after the first three one column inward per row; paint the exposed part of the first color-6 row color 9.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~5-12 by ~5-14) with 2-4 color-2 SEED cells in scattered positions (≥2-cell separation so diagonal decorations from one seed don't collide with another). Seeds preferably in interior so all 4 diagonal neighbors exist. Rule: build fresh 0-canvas. For each cell (r, c), check its 4 diagonal positions for a color-2 seed: if (r+1, c+1)=2 paint cell 3; if (r+1, c-1)=2 paint 6; if (r-1, c+1)=2 paint 8; if (r-1, c-1)=2 paint 7. (Priority TR/TL/BR/BL.) Each 2-seed at (sr, sc) produces a diamond of colors around it: (sr-1, sc-1)=3, (sr-1, sc+1)=6, (sr+1, sc-1)=8, (sr+1, sc+1)=7.

A sparse green (3) wall network partitions black (0) cells into one or more sealed 4-connected regions plus border-reachable exterior. Fill every sealed black region yellow (4), preserving all green walls and every exterior black cell. Open wall fragments and irregular holes make bounding-box, rectangle-only, and largest-hole shortcuts visibly wrong.

Use the unique modal background. For each other color independently, leave a single connected component unchanged; when the color is split, keep its largest component (equal sizes choose the lower/right top-left corner), erase its other components, and fill the winner's bounding rectangle together with one column on the left.

A 0-background grid contains 1-3 non-overlapping monochrome hollow 3x3 rings with zero centers.  Each ring uses a distinct color.  A separate small concave same-palette distractor is not a complete ring and must remain unchanged.  Fill only each ring center with its ring color.

Exactly one color-9 marker is at a corner and exactly one connected, single-color motif is strictly inside the border. Remove the marker, crop the motif tightly, then rotate that crop according to the marker: top-left identity, top-right clockwise 90°, bottom-right 180°, bottom-left counter-clockwise 90°.

Read a unary blue selector from row 0 columns 0..3, transform code 1..5 from column 5, and target color from column 7. Select one of four 4x4 monochrome panels, crop its nonzero support, apply identity / clockwise / 180 / counter-clockwise / left-right reflection, and recolor the result.

A 0-background grid ordinarily contains 2-6 distinct-colored singleton seeds from {2,3,4,6,7,9}; the strict n_seeds override also supports the one-seed boundary. Seeds are at pairwise Manhattan distance at least 3, so their radius-one orthogonal halos do not overlap or erase another seed. Preserve the seeds and paint every in-bounds orthogonal background neighbor cyan (8). Position profiles exercise interior, edge, corner, and mixed clipping cases.

Sparse 0-background grids contain 1-3 separated X motifs.  Each X has four same-color diagonal corners around a zero center, which the rule fills with that color.  Every generated input also contains exactly one scheduled near-miss: either only three matching corners or four corners split 2+2 across two colors.  These controls teach that all four corners must be present and must agree.

Generate color-5 wall mazes containing exactly two matching colored endpoints.  Four consecutive samples cover an edge-hugging route, a deep serpentine detour, an interior endpoint pair, and a multiple-shortest-path case.  The authority paints the first U,D,L,R BFS shortest path through zero cells with the endpoint color.

On a zero-background grid, count all occurrences of each nonzero color. Keep every cell whose color occurs exactly twice and erase every color occurring once, three times, four times, or five times. Ordinary non-anchor samples contain count-1, count-4, and count-5 witnesses, while exact canonical anchors retain the public count profiles.

On a black grid, inspect each row independently.  If and only if the row contains exactly two nonzero cells and those two cells have the same color, fill every cell between them, inclusive, with that color.  Leave mismatched pairs, rows with extra nonzero cells, and all other rows unchanged.
Rows with non-bg run; rule shifts run right + fills 5.

A 4..15 by 4..6 dense nonzero multicolor tile with a visible left-right asymmetry. The output is five horizontal tiles alternating original and left-right mirror, beginning and ending with the original. Canonical 4x4 two/three-color inputs are a dominant curriculum profile; broader sizes and four-color textures remain represented in every difficulty band.

Grid is split into 3 panels by 2 full color-5 separator columns. Each panel holds exactly one connected non-bg shape. Panels A (left) and B (middle) share the SAME shape and color; the shape's position differs — the translation vector (dr, dc) = bbox_top_left(B) - bbox_top_left(A) is the rule's only learned quantity. Panel C (right) has a (possibly different-colored) shape. Rule output is a C-panel-sized grid containing C's shape translated by (dr, dc); cells that would translate outside C's panel are silently dropped.

0-bg grid with: (a) ROW 0 holding a LEGEND of 3 distinct non-{0, 5} PRIORITY COLORS at columns 1, 2, 3 (left-to-right priority order, leftmost = highest priority); (b) ROWS 2..h-1 forming a 5-WALLED REGION — color-5 (gray) outer FRAME (row 2 = top wall, row h-1 = bottom wall, cols 0 and w-1 = side walls) plus an INTERNAL VERTICAL WALL at col cw+1 that splits the region into 2 CHAMBERS; (c) each chamber holds 1-2 SEED CELLS (single pixels) using colors from the legend. Rule: for EACH CHAMBER independently, find all seeds and determine the SEED COLOR WITH HIGHEST PRIORITY (leftmost legend position). FILL every empty (bg) cell inside that chamber (not the walls, not the seeds) with that highest-priority color. Net: each chamber flood-fills to its dominant seed-priority color; walls and legend stay.

Find each 4-connected nonzero object and compare its exact normalized shape with every other object. Recolor a singleton shape class red (2) and a repeated shape class blue (1); leave background 0. Rotation and reflection do not count as the same shape.

Square 5-14 grids on background 0 contain 3-9 colored source cells in distinct transpose orbits. Sources may lie above, below, or on both sides of the main diagonal; their transposed targets start empty. The output keeps every source and copies its color to (column,row), producing the union of the input and its transpose.
Mark every black cell lying on any shortest non-wall path between red and green.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~9-11) containing color-1 (blue) cells arranged as: (a) 2 T-SHAPES (each = a 4-cell T: 3-cell horizontal or vertical bar + 1 stem cell, where the stem cell has exactly 3 cardinal blue neighbors); T-shapes vary in orientation (up, down, left, right T's); (b) at least 1 DISTRACTOR — a straight 3-cell BAR of color 1 (no cell has 3 neighbors). All 1-shapes are non-touching with their neighborhoods. Rule: for every cell (r, c) with VALUE 1, COUNT its CARDINAL neighbors that are also 1. If the count is EXACTLY 3, RECOLOR that cell to color 4 (yellow). Otherwise leave it as 1. Net: T-shape CENTERS become yellow (one cell per T), arms stay blue, distractor bars stay fully blue.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~9-13) with 2-4 ACTIVE ROWS, each containing a LAUNCHER — at column c, a COLOR-1 (blue) MARKER immediately followed by a COLOR CELL at (r, c+1) in a non-{0, 1, 9} color drawn from {2..8}. Some rows ALSO have a COLOR-9 (maroon) STOPPER somewhere to the right at (r, c+k) where k ≥ 3. Other rows have no stopper. Rule (EACH 1/COLOR LAUNCHER FIRES A RIGHTWARD RAY OF ITS COLOR UNTIL STOPPER OR EDGE): For EACH ACTIVE ROW r: locate the LAUNCHER — a color-1 cell at (r, c) immediately followed by a non-{0, 1, 9} color C at (r, c+1). PAINT cells (r, c+2), (r, c+3), ... with COLOR C, extending RIGHTWARD, stopping just before a COLOR-9 STOPPER or the grid right edge. Launcher and color cells stay. Net: each row's launcher paints a rightward tail in its color until a 9-stopper or the right edge.
Color-8/9 rectangular frames; each holds a 1/2 key + several distinct-size objects; rule centers the smallest (key 1) or largest (key 2) object in the frame (rotated 180 for color-9).

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 scattered SMALL MOTIFS in distinct non-bg colors. Canonical rule layout (NOT yet matched by this generator): the grid is split HORIZONTALLY by FULL-HEIGHT color-5 (gray) DIVIDER COLUMNS into THREE 5×5 panels (left, middle, right). Left and middle carry colored cells; right is empty in input. Rule: for each cell (r, c) ∈ (5 × 5), compute the right panel as: if BOTH left[r][c] and middle[r][c] are non-zero, output 8 (collision marker); if only ONE is non-zero, output that color; else output 0. Re-join the three panels with color-5 separators. Net: a 3-panel layout where the right panel is the COLORED OR-OVERLAY of left and middle, with cyan marking conflicts.

0-bg framed grid (h~7-12, w = 2*panel_w+3 with panel_w=5) containing TWO PANELS separated by a vertical FRAME-COLOR divider, plus a full FRAME-COLOR outer border. LEFT PANEL contains 1-2 small colored OBJECTS (each 2-3 cells, in distinct non-frame colors c1, c2) placed at distinct row spans. RIGHT PANEL is initially blank (the projection canvas). NOTE: object positions are currently hardcoded — diversity is mid. Rule: for EACH OBJECT in the LEFT PANEL, determine its ROW SPAN (rmin..rmax) and color c. PROJECT a stretched HORIZONTAL BAR of color c into the RIGHT PANEL spanning those same rows, filling the entire right-panel column range (with horizontal margin convention). Net: left-panel shapes become projected colored bars in the right panel.

Use the unique blue(1) cell as the source and the first red(2) cell in row-major order as the target. Translate every other non-zero cell by the source-to-target vector, including later red cells, clip translated cells at the canvas boundary, then crop the surviving payload tightly.

0-bg grid (size varies). A FILL color fc at (0,0); 1-2 full green(3) interior rows; one red(2) row carrying >=2 periodic red blocks (width w, period p). Rule: read the block width + period and tile the whole grid into a periodic stripe pattern -- stripe columns filled with fc, red rows -> 2 inside stripes, green rows -> full 3, else 0. Built horizontally then optionally transposed. The orientation, grid size, fill color, green/red positions, block width and period all vary freely (was a fixed 11x12 layout, ~13 distinct).

On a canonical-size canvas, connect exactly two blue endpoints in every row or column only when all cells strictly between them are background. Generated lessons contain clear horizontal and vertical positives plus a non-colour-5 blocked negative witness; easy layouts are separated, medium layouts mixed, and hard layouts cross the clear pairs.
Four equal sections separated by full gray rows show a changing pattern; predict the next section by shifting the latest cell diff and carrying a prior row diff when the latest step skipped that row.

A fixed 5x11 input holds four commands at row 0 columns 1,3,7,9 and two connected asymmetric 3x3 templates at rows 2-4, columns 1-3 and 7-9. Commands 1-4 select the left template and 5-8 the right; their residue selects identity, clockwise rotation, horizontal flip, or 180° rotation. A four-profile schedule preserves exact canonical support and teaches source decoding, full-frame transforms, and multicolor fidelity.

A 0-background grid has one red (2) marker on the top or left edge and a gray (5) object. The marker selects a vertical or horizontal mirror axis. In-bounds reflections onto background become orange (7); occupied or out-of-bounds targets are left unchanged. A six-profile curriculum covers both orientations, both source sides, occupied targets, and out-of-bounds targets.

Stack two equally sized panels with distinct nonzero foreground colors. Output 6 exactly where one aligned cell is zero and the other is nonzero, otherwise 0. Every ordinary input covers all four occupancy states. Three-demo lessons alternate canonical/broad sizes and canonical/varied palettes; textures and densities are proposals, xor_target is a lower bound.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-12) with 2-4 STRAIGHT LINE SEGMENTS (horizontal or vertical, length 2-4 cells) in DISTINCT colors. Lines are placed at spaced positions so they don't touch. Rule (MARK LINE ENDPOINTS WITH COLOR 8): for EACH non-zero CELL, COUNT its same-color CARDINAL (4-conn) NEIGHBORS. If the count is EXACTLY 1 (the cell has only one same-color neighbor — it's a line endpoint), RECOLOR it to COLOR 8 (cyan). Interior cells (2 same-color neighbors) keep their color. Singletons (0 neighbors) keep their color. Net: each line segment's two endpoints become cyan.

A connected green (3) motif and one hollow rectangular frame of another color appear on a 0 background. Erase the motif, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise, and stamp the normalized result at the frame's top-left interior coordinate. The stamp wins on contact with the frame border.

On a zero background, fill the zero interior of every exact hollow orange (7) rectangular frame with cyan (8). Preserve the orange outline, broken orange near-frames, non-orange frames, and all unrelated cells.

Exactly one corner is non-zero and acts only as a color key. Clear all four corners, find the single connected body object of that key color, and return the raw subgrid at its tight bounding box. Distractors use other colors; some samples place one distractor cell in an empty cell inside the selected bbox, so the foreign cell remains in the output.

A centered color-9 anchor and one connected single-color motif occupy one quadrant of an odd square grid. Remove the anchor and complete the other three quadrants by horizontal, vertical, and 180-degree reflection.
2-4 horizontally-aligned equal-color pairs with empty cells between.

A 16x11 grid of six 4x4 pattern SLOTS (fixed canonical origins). Two slots hold RANDOM color-2 source patterns whose UNION exactly equals a third slot; the other three slots hold RANDOM DECOY patterns chosen so NO other union relationship exists (the triple is unique). The six patterns are placed in a RANDOM permutation of the slots. Rule: find the slot that is the union of two others, color it green (3), color the two source slots cyan (8), leave the decoys red (2). The patterns, their union, the decoys and the slot assignment all vary freely (was 3 hardcoded union styles x a transpose flag = ~6 inputs).
Replace every zero by the left-to-right rank of its global zero-containing column.
The overlap of blue- and red-corner implied rectangles is filled green.

A zero-background grid contains two to five strictly nested hollow yellow(4) rectangular frames and k red(2) marker cells outside the outer frame. A separate color-6 triomino is an irrelevant distractor. Order the frames by bounding-box area from largest/outermost to smallest/innermost and recolor the k-th frame border cyan(8).
(0,0)=op key; color-2 cluster + color-3 cluster.
Crop the lexicographically smallest qualifying patterned object by area, orientation, symmetry, row, and column.
Several plus-shaped (center + 4 cardinals) color-4 patterns. Rule recolors the CENTER cell of each plus to 8; arms stay color 4.
Isolated 6-0-6 horizontal gaps are bridged with 8.
A red component touches several neighbors; the largest red neighbor is kept as 8.

0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-2 (red) SHAPE and ONE color-1 (blue) SHAPE (random single-component polyominoes whose normalized forms share >=1 cell and differ in >=1 cell), placed apart. Rule: take the largest blob of each color, normalize both to their bbox, and output their XOR (cells in EXACTLY ONE of the two normalized sets) bbox-cropped, painted COLOR 8 (cyan). The grid size, the two shapes (which set the XOR) and their positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed shapes whose XOR was always the same 4-cell pattern).
Top-row color markers paint their entire columns.

0-bg grid with a single connected motif (3-6 cells) in one non-zero color, surrounded by bg padding. The motif's bbox is strictly smaller than the grid (so the rule's crop produces a smaller output). Rule: find the bbox of all non-zero cells. Output = the subgrid bounded by min/max row and col of non-zero cells. Output dims = (max_r - min_r + 1) × (max_c - min_c + 1).

0-bg grid (h~8-14, w~14-22) with 2-4 HORIZONTAL SOLID BARS, each 3 rows tall and 5-16 cols wide, painted in distinct non-bg colors. Bars are vertically separated (≥1 row gap between bars). Each bar's MIDDLE ROW has cells equal to the cells DIRECTLY ABOVE and DIRECTLY BELOW (since the whole bar is solid). Rule: scan every cell at (r, c). If the cell ABOVE and the cell BELOW share the SAME non-zero value v (i.e., the cell is in the middle row of a 3-tall bar), find the LEFTMOST such matching cell in this row-group and HOLLOW OUT alternate cells starting from there: every OTHER middle-row cell (parity from leftmost) becomes 0. The top and bottom rows of each bar stay solid. Net: each solid 3-tall bar gets its middle row turned into a dashed pattern of alternating filled/empty cells.

Rows 0-1 form a sparse source→target color legend.  Below it are 1-4 separate hollow color-5 rectangular rooms.  Every room contains exactly one source-colored seed.  Read the legend by column, use the seed to select its target color, and repaint the room's whole interior—including the seed cell—with that target while preserving the color-5 outline and all cells outside room interiors.  Default draws repeatedly revisit the canonical 10x12/11x13/12x14 scale while also exploring larger layouts.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-11, w ∈ 12-14) with: (a) TWO HOLLOW COLOR-5 (GRAY) RECTANGULAR FRAMES, each height 4-5 and width 4, drawn via draw_rect_outline at FIXED corner regions: FRAME 1 at top-left (1, 1)..(fr, fc), FRAME 2 at bottom-right (h-fr2-1, w-fc2-1)..(h-2, w-2); (b) IN EACH FRAME'S INTERIOR: ONE MARKER CELL of a distinct non-{0, 5} color drawn from {2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8} (palette[0] for frame 1, palette[1] for frame 2), at a random interior position; (c) ONE COLOR-6 NOISE CELL at (0, w-1). Rule (FOR EACH CLOSED 5-FRAME, FILL EVERY 0-CELL INSIDE THE FRAME'S INTERIOR WITH THE MARKER COLOR INSIDE THAT FRAME): EXTRACT every COLOR-5 frame outline. For EACH frame: READ the unique non-{0, 5} MARKER COLOR inside. PAINT every interior 0-cell with the marker color. The frame outline stays gray; the marker cell stays its color. Net: each frame's interior floods with its marker color; gray outlines and noise cells preserved.

Find the hollow rectangular frame. Among all other same-color 4-connected components, select the last component in row-major discovery order. Erase every non-frame component, crop the selected component to its bounding box, and paste that shape unchanged at the floor-centered position inside the frame's interior.
Boundary lines crop; interior scatter matching one wall grows into bars.
An n × n grid (n in 3..5) with a unique most-frequent color; mode cells receive tile copies.
Several green-3 blobs of distinct sizes plus distractors; recolor the largest green to 8.

Green (3) markers on the top edge shoot downward and red (2) markers on the left edge shoot rightward. Maroon (9) cells stop rays. Horizontal-only and vertical-only cells become 2 and 3; crossings become cyan (8).
Key rows map source colors to fill colors around each source color bbox.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-16) with: (a) 1-3 LARGE OBJECTS (size ≥ 3 cells) in some non-{0, 3} fg_color, shaped as rect / L / cross / random_blob / line_h / line_v; (b) 2-5 SMALL OBJECTS (size 1 or 2 cells) in the SAME fg_color — singletons or pairs (pair_h / pair_v / pair_diag). Large and small objects are 4-conn isolated with 1-cell padding. Rule: for EVERY 4-CONN OBJECT, compute its CELL COUNT. If size < 3 (singletons or pairs), RECOLOR every cell of that object to COLOR 3 (green). If size ≥ 3 (large), KEEP fg_color unchanged. Net: small objects turn green; large objects stay.
Gray diagonal staircase recolored by cycling legend with saturation.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-13, w ∈ 10-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-1 (BLUE) TEMPLATE SHAPE drawn from base_shapes bank (4 variants of 3-4 cell shapes: S, Z, T, L) placed at a random non-overlapping interior position via _free check; (b) ONE MATCHING COLOR-3 (GREEN) SHAPE — same variant as the template — placed at another random position; (c) WITH 70% PROBABILITY ONE ADDITIONAL DIFFERENT COLOR-3 SHAPE — a different variant from base_shapes (acts as a distractor). Rule (FIND THE UNIQUE COLOR-1 TEMPLATE; AMONG COLOR-3 SHAPES, KEEP ONLY THOSE WHOSE NORMALIZED BINARY MASK EXACTLY MATCHES THE TEMPLATE; RECOLOR KEPT ONES TO COLOR 8): EXTRACT the COLOR-1 component → normalize its cells (subtract min r/c). EXTRACT every color-3 component. For EACH: normalize its cells; CHECK if EQUAL to template's normalized cells. IF YES: RECOLOR every cell of that component to COLOR 8 (cyan). ELSE: ERASE it to 0. The color-1 template stays. Net: the matching green copy becomes cyan; non-matching green distractors vanish.

Generate two equal panels separated by one full color-8 column.  For each aligned cell, the output keeps the source color when exactly one panel is nonzero and writes 0 when both or neither are nonzero.  Default draws alternate a canonical 4x9 input profile with a band-specific expanded profile, use exactly two or three panel colors, and include left-only, right-only, both-zero, same-color overlap, and different-color overlap witnesses in every scene.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with: (a) cell (0, 0) holds a CONTROL CODE in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; (b) EXACTLY ONE isolated ASYMMETRIC SHAPE (3-6 cells from a bank of 9 asymmetric tetro/pent shapes) in some non-control color elsewhere in the grid (rows 2+, cols 2+) with 1-cell padding. Rule (CONTROL-CODE TRANSFORM CROP): CLEAR cell (0, 0). CROP the remaining grid to its non-zero CONTENT BBOX (the shape's bbox). APPLY the TRANSFORM indexed by the control code: 1 = identity, 2 = rotate CW 90°, 3 = rotate 180°, 4 = rotate CCW 90°, 5 = flip horizontal. OUTPUT: the cropped, transformed shape. Net: code cell at (0, 0) picks the geometric transform applied to the cropped asymmetric shape.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 2-3 BLOBS in distinct non-bg colors. Each blob is a connected polyomino of 3-5 cells with a NON-TRIVIAL bbox (min bbox dimensions 2×2, so corners are not collinear). Blobs are 4-conn isolated. Rule: for each blob, compute its axis-aligned BOUNDING BOX (rmin, cmin, rmax, cmax). REPLACE the entire blob with EXACTLY 4 CELLS at its bbox CORNERS — (rmin, cmin), (rmin, cmax), (rmax, cmin), (rmax, cmax) — painted in the blob's original color. ERASE all other cells of the blob to 0. Net: each blob becomes 4 corner dots marking the bbox extremes; the blob's interior + edges vanish.

Fill a zero cell exactly when its four cardinal neighbors share one nonzero color. Preserve exact canonical-size two-plus examples while mixing horizontal-only, vertical-only, three-arm, mixed-arm, occupied-center, and diagonal decoys that distinguish plausible shortcut rules.

Three square panels A, B, C are separated by two solid non-background columns. B is one uniquely identifiable non-identity D8 transform of A; apply that same transform to C. Generated C panels make the transform visible and never contain the answer already.
Partial motif completed by 90/180/270 degree rotations around its center.

Grid (h, w ~12-18) filled with background color 8 (cyan) and 2-3 SOLID RECTANGLES of distinct non-bg colors. Rectangles have distinct AREAS (so a sort is unambiguous). Rectangles are placed without overlap. Rule: bg = color at (0, 0). Find non-bg, non-zero color components. Compute each component's bbox dimensions (bh, bw) and area = bh*bw. Sort by area descending. The LARGEST = canvas (oh × ow). Output: oh × ow grid where each cell (r, c) takes the color of the SMALLEST rect whose dims still cover (r, c) (i.e., (r, c) is inside the smaller rect's dims). Rects stack at top-left from largest to smallest.

Grid (h~9-13, w~10-15) with: (a) color-5 (gray) WALLS forming a central vertical wall (with a gap) and horizontal cross-walls; (b) exactly ONE color-2 (red) seed on the left side and ONE color-3 (green) seed on the right side. Rule: do BFS-shortest-path distance from all red cells (d2) and from all green cells (d3), treating color-5 cells as impassable. For each cell: if input != 0 → keep it. Else compare d2 vs d3: if d2 < d3 → paint 2; if d3 < d2 → paint 3; tie → 0. Net: wall-aware nearest-seed Voronoi between red and green.

One 9-anchor and one connected monochromatic 2-5-cell shape on background 0. Keep the original and add its point reflection through the anchor, clipping individual out-of-bounds cells. Mix copied-interior plus witnesses, partially clipped asymmetric witnesses, and broad complete or symmetric shapes; retain canonical-size support in every difficulty band.

Two opposite borders have distinct colors. Each color-1 marker projects the color of its matching border into the adjacent cell toward that border: up/left in the first half and down/right in the second half.
Control 2/3/4 selects nested color-6 frame band to fill cyan.

A 21..23 by 19..22 grid is a primitive 3x3 or 4x4 periodic pattern using three or four colors. Two or three other colors each form one solid rectangle and occlude the pattern. Exactly one rectangle has the largest area. Output the largest rectangle's bounding box with every occluded cell replaced by the periodic value for its global phase.
2-3 distinct-color blobs of strictly distinct sizes.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-12) with 2-5 BLUE(1) L-TROMINOES (3-cell L-shapes in 2×2 bboxes with one MISSING CORNER) placed at non-touching anchors (min Chebyshev distance 3 between anchors). EACH tromino occupies 3 of 4 cells in its 2×2 bbox, with the missing corner randomly chosen from the 4 positions. Rule (FILL EACH 2×2 WINDOW WITH 3 BLUE + 1 BG → COMPLETE WITH RED): scan EVERY 2×2 WINDOW in the grid. For EACH window containing EXACTLY 3 BLUE(1) CELLS AND 1 BG(0) CELL: PAINT the bg cell with COLOR 2 (red). Windows with other blue counts (0, 1, 2, 4) stay unchanged. Net: each L-tromino gains a red dot in its missing corner, completing it to a blue-3 + red-1 2×2.
On a zero-background grid, process each column independently: preserve only its topmost nonzero cell with its original color and erase every lower nonzero cell. Empty columns remain empty.
Expand each isolated interior nonzero marker into an empty-centered hollow 3x3 ring in the marker's own color.

0-bg grid (size varies). A top band of K (2-4) color-1 rectangular FRAMES, each holding a distinct th x tw TEMPLATE in its interior; the interior's top-left (first-nonzero) color is that template's CODE. A solid CR x CC CODE GRID below uses those codes. Rule: expand each code cell into its template and tile -> a (CR*th) x (CC*tw) grid. Template count/size/patterns, the codes and the code-grid shape all vary freely (was 3 fixed monochrome 5x5 templates, ~17 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~11-13, w~13-16) with 3 ISOLATED 4-CONNECTED COMPONENTS in distinct colors from {1..9}, each with a DISTINCT ENCLOSED-HOLE COUNT: (a) SOLID BLOCK — 2×2 / 2×3 / 3×2 with 0 holes; (b) HOLLOW RING — 3×3 / 3×4 / 4×3 outline with 1 enclosed hole; (c) DOUBLE-HOLED RING — 3×5 / 3×6 / 5×3 with an extra divider line creating 2 enclosed holes. Components are placed at non-touching positions. Rule (SORT COMPONENTS BY (HOLE-COUNT DESC, AREA DESC, COLOR ASC), PACK BBOX CROPS HORIZONTALLY): for each 4-CONNECTED COMPONENT: crop to BBOX, compute HOLE-COUNT (# enclosed zero regions inside the crop). SORT by (hole_count DESC, area DESC, color ASC). PACK the crops LEFT-TO-RIGHT with 1-column BLANK GAP between adjacent crops. Output dimensions = max(crop rows) × (sum(crop cols) + gaps). Net: components stacked left-to-right by complexity (holes first, then area).
Copy every orange (7) source cell across the horizontal midline, preserving the original source and its column.

A complete gray color-5 row or column separates a red color-2 L-shape from empty space. Reflect only the red cells across the divider and paint their blank mirror positions color 3. Preserve the red source, divider, background, and one unrelated non-red distractor object.

0-bg grid with: (a) a multicolor template — connected colored cells using palette {2, 3, 4, ...} (no 0, no 1); (b) exactly one color-1 marker cell elsewhere. Rule: normalize the template's cells to top-left = (0, 0), then stamp the template at the marker position on a FRESH 0-grid (preserving each cell's color). The marker and original template do NOT appear in the output.

Split an even grid into top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right quadrants. For each quadrant output its most frequent non-zero color, or 0 when the quadrant is empty. Ordinary lessons mix single-color, empty, and multi-color quadrants, including count winners that are neither the first nor the numerically largest visible color.

0-bg grid with several disjoint-color 2-color blocks (each fills its rectangle with two colors, both present in every row & col so each color's support = the block). Rule crops to the largest such paired block.
Red singleton cells fall downward until blocked by the border or obstacles.

Find every 4-connected zero region. Preserve border-connected exterior zero. Recolor each enclosed zero region independently by its cell count: size <=8 with 8, size <=24 with 4, and size >24 with 3; preserve red boundaries and interior red dividers.

A 21x21 zero-background grid contains one largest monochrome source template and two or three smaller monochrome marker fragments.  Each marker is a proper subset of the source translated to the first slot in one of eight directions.  Repeat the full source shape outward in the marker color, using stride (source bbox height + 1, source bbox width + 1) on the active direction components and preserving all existing cells.

0-bg grid (h, w ~ 9-17) with 3-5 (or up to 6 hard) SOLID 2×2 BLOCKS placed at random non-overlapping non-touching positions (1-cell padding via _free). Each block is painted entirely in a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from a shuffled palette {1..9}. Block top-left positions may share rows, share cols, or be all distinct (per position_bias). Rule (PROJECT 2×2 BLOCKS TO A MINI GRID — ROWS = SORTED UNIQUE BLOCK TOP-ROWS, COLS = SORTED UNIQUE BLOCK TOP-COLS): scan the grid for SOLID 2×2 monochromatic BLOCKS. For EACH block, record its top-left (top_row, top_col) and color. EXTRACT SORTED UNIQUE top_row values → rows[0..M-1]. EXTRACT SORTED UNIQUE top_col values → cols[0..N-1]. PRODUCE an M × N OUTPUT grid where output[r][c] = block_color whose (top_row, top_col) = (rows[r], cols[c]), or 0 if no block sits at that intersection. Net: the scattered 2×2 blocks become a small mini grid encoding their projection onto unique row/col positions.

8-bg grid (h, w ~ 8-18) containing MANY independent color-7 markers. Each marker has a clear ray of color-8 background cells in one of four directions and then a visible adjacent 1/6 pair. The input deliberately puts the near/far pair as 1 then 6; the canonical rule scans from each marker through 8s and rewrites the visible pair to 6 then 1 in the viewing direction. This matches the real task, whose examples are dense 8-background fields with multiple 7 markers and multiple 1/6 pairs, not a sparse 0-bg single-corridor scene.
Read nine fixed cells from a 5 x 5 grid into a 3 x 3 output; all other cells are decoys.
Template panel and board panel separated by a full color-9 column; board contains recolored template copies.
skills: structural pattern matching, color-equivalence reasoning, symbolic detection

summary: 0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~13-16) containing two kinds of CONNECTED COMPONENTS, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color: (a) 1-2 HOLED OBJECTS — frame-shaped polyominoes with an ENCLOSED 0-CELL HOLE inside (3x3 donut, 3x4 rect outline); (b) 2 SOLID DISTRACTOR objects — small polyominoes without enclosed holes. Objects are non-touching with 1-cell padding. Rule: for EACH connected component, check if it has an ENCLOSED 0-CELL inside its bbox (a bg cell that cannot reach the grid border via 4-conn through other 0 cells without crossing this component). If YES (holed), RECOLOR every cell of that component to COLOR 8 (cyan). If NO (solid), leave it unchanged. Net: holed blobs become cyan; solid blobs keep their color.

A rectangular grid has a solid TOP-COLOR first row, a solid BOTTOM-COLOR last row, and a third modal BACKGROUND color. Interior 8-connected objects use only the two marker colors. Every TOP-COLOR object is erased and shifted vertically so its top edge becomes row 1. Every ordinary BOTTOM-COLOR object is erased and shifted so its bottom edge becomes row h-2. A BOTTOM-COLOR object that both touches the right edge and is at least three rows tall is instead extruded downward: every column occupied by that object is filled from the object's original top row through row h-2. Generated lessons keep same-color object destinations disjoint so every source object's effect remains visible. Object shapes, counts, positions, dimensions, and colors vary.

0-bg grid with one or more color-2 diagonal emitters and color-8 blocking walls.  At least one emitter has an open diagonal ray so the canonical wall-aware visibility overlay fires.  Normal examples use only colors 0, 2, and 8 to avoid confusing motifs with emitters/walls.

Grid (h~6-10, w~7-12) with bg = 7 (orange). At the BOTTOM there are exactly TWO vertical BARS: one in col col_8 of color 8 (cyan), one in col col_2 of color 2 (red). Each bar's height = how many cells from the bottom up are non-7 in that column. Bars have DIFFERENT heights. (col_2 + 2) must be in-bounds. Rule: scan bottom row to find bar columns. Compute height_8 and height_2 by counting non-7 cells in each bar's column. gray_h = |height_8 - height_2|. new_col = (rightmost bar col) + 2. Paint a color-5 (gray) bar in column new_col, occupying the bottom gray_h rows. All other cells preserved.

Fixed 11×9 0-bg grid with HARDCODED LAYOUT: (a) TWO HOLLOW 3×3 RINGS in TARGET COLOR (from {1..8}) at (1..3, 1..3) and (5..7, 4..6); (b) ONE HOLLOW 3×3 RING in OTHER COLOR at (8..10, 1..3); (c) ONE SOLID 2×2 BLOCK in OTHER COLOR at (2..3, 6..7). Hardcoded positions × ~8 × ~7 color choices = ~31 unique configs (HARDCODED-LOW). Rule (MOST-COMPONENTS COLOR's HOLES → 9): identify the COLOR with the MOST 4-conn COMPONENTS (target color has 2 components, other has 2). With tiebreak picking target. For each COMPONENT of that color, fill its ENCLOSED HOLE (interior 0-cells) with COLOR-9 (maroon). Other components, solid blocks unchanged. Net: most-component color's hollow rings get maroon centers.
Place exactly two color-4 endpoints on a horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree segment with an even coordinate span. Return only the segment midpoint as color 8 on an otherwise blank grid.

A 1/7/9 wall lattice contains row-major rooms. Color 7 is a doorway; match the first room's exact (area, door-degree, #2, #3) signature and mark the unique matching candidate in a one-row color-8 strip.
skills: compound room signatures, degree + area + counts, symbolic selection

summary: Complete every adjacent 2x2 whose opposite corners have the same nonzero colour, overwriting either companion corner; unequal-colour diagonals are controls and remain inactive.

Use the unique modal colour as background. A non-background row-0 cell fires only when it differs from row 1 in its column. Down each firing column, marker-colour cells turn into background and every other body cell turns into the marker colour. Non-firing top decoys and all cells outside firing columns remain unchanged.

Exactly one non-zero top-row marker supplies guide color G. Rows 1+ contain three distinct-color connected objects, exactly one colored G. Return the raw tight bounding-box crop of all body cells colored G. Non-guide cells inside that box remain in the output.

Find monochrome 4-connected objects, compare their occupied-cell sets after translation normalization only, and paint the sole shape occurring once cyan on a blank grid. Every other exact shape occurs in a matched pair; rotation and reflection do not count as equality.

Count 4-connected non-zero/non-9 components by maximum onion-peel depth 1..4. Generated scenes mix solid and non-rectangular exact-depth shapes, randomize positions, and sometimes reuse colors across components.

skills: boundary peeling, same-size recolor, component-wise depth
summary: Two or three separated monochrome components on background 0. Components are solid squares/rectangles, diamonds, rounded squares, or thick crosses; each has a nonempty interior. The rule recolors exactly the exposed outer 4-neighbor layer to 8 and preserves the inner core color.

(0,0) holds the target color. Target-color rings (or other components with bg interiors) get their interior holes filled with target color. (0,0) is cleared in output. Non-target components untouched.
In a zero-separated array of identical framed cells, propagate every non-common interior color across the span between matching local-offset anchors in each cell-row and cell-column.

3 isolated small shapes (each ≤3×3 bbox) in distinct non-bg colors. Rule: for each shape, compute bbox edge-cell counts (cells on each of top/bottom/left/right side of bbox). If shape's bbox height < 3, anchor toward the side with more cells. Compose all 3 into a single 3×3 output, overlaid by position score order.

Pack every column's non-zero cells at the top in their original vertical order. Ordinary lessons retain the official two-layer histogram family: one foreground layer spans a contiguous set of columns above a second foreground layer, with empty vertical gaps that disappear in the output. A rolling four-sample schedule also includes a floating upper layer and an interleaved A-B-A column, refuting lower-object-only, fixed-color, and numeric-sort shortcuts.

0-bg grid (size varies) with EXACTLY 4 non-touching BLOBS, each a connected polyomino in a distinct color, placed so their bounding boxes don't overlap. Rule: sort the blobs by color ascending, crop each to its bbox, and assemble a 2x2 grid (tl/tr/bl/br in color order) with a 1-cell gap between quadrants. The grid size, the 4 shapes, their colors (which set the quadrant order) and positions all vary freely (was 4 fixed shapes, ~9 distinct).

Zero-separated panels each contain a unique-largest colored component and a same-color distractor; largest components are overlaid largest-first with conflict-avoiding shifts on one 8-background panel.
The first two nonzero top-row codes transform the cropped motif below the header.

0-bg grid (h,w ~10-20) with a hollow RECTANGULAR FRAME (>=3x3) in an OUTER color and a small MARKER (1-4 cells) in a distinct OTHER color placed inside the frame's interior. The frame is positioned so its four corners have clear OUTWARD DIAGONALS. Rule: every L-corner of the outer color (a cell with exactly two orthogonal same-color neighbors forming an L bend) shoots a DIAGONAL RAY in the OTHER color outward (away from the frame) along the open diagonal, provided that diagonal is unobstructed.
1-4 directional emitter cells (1=up,2=right,3=down,4=left) + 1-2 color-5 blocker line segments; each emitter shoots a ray of its value through empty cells until a 5-blocker or grid edge.

Find each 4-connected monochrome nonzero component. Keep the entire component exactly when at least one of its cells touches the outer grid border; replace every fully interior component with background 0. Four-example teaching windows include non-top and edge-only border objects, multiple kept components, and a repeated color split across a kept and erased component so position/connectivity—not color, count, or corner membership—identifies the rule.

Place one 4-connected green(3) component, four to six cells large, on a black(0) grid. The component is offset from both top and left borders. Translate every green cell by the negative of the component bounding-box top-left so the same shape begins at row 0 and column 0; preserve the input grid dimensions and clear every other cell to black.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-9) with 1-2 COLORS each appearing EXACTLY TWICE as ALIGNED PAIRS — same-row pair with EVEN col-distance ≥2 OR same-col pair with EVEN row-distance ≥2. Plus 1 DISTRACTOR ISOLATED CELL in another color. Rule: for EACH COLOR appearing EXACTLY TWICE, check if its 2 cells are SAME-ROW with EVEN col-distance OR SAME-COL with EVEN row-distance. If yes, COMPUTE the MIDPOINT and PAINT it with COLOR 8 (cyan). Net: each even-distance aligned pair gets a cyan dot at its midpoint.
Full color-5 divider (row or col); red(2) marker is on the source side; rule mirrors all non-marker, non-divider cells on the marker's side across the divider, erases marker in output.
2-3 colors each with exactly 2 cells at distinct rows/cols.

Dense color grid (h~4-9, w~6-12) where each ROW is a CYCLIC SHIFT of one base color sequence: row 0 = the base sequence (a length-w row drawn from a rich 4-9 color non-0 palette by default), and every other row is an independent non-zero cyclic shift of the base (so it differs from row 0). Rule: replace every row with row 0 (broadcast the top row to all rows). The output is therefore w-wide and entirely row-0's pattern repeated; its diversity comes from the base sequence in row 0.

Complete a 2x2 square only when one diagonal contains the same nonzero colour and both opposite corners are empty; apply the symmetric main- and anti-diagonal cases simultaneously without overwriting occupied cells.

Match each intact monochrome frame to its external same-color insert. An isolated interior key selects identity (1), clockwise (2), half-turn (3), or counterclockwise (4). The unchanged reference clears the input, retains complete frames, and pastes transformed insert subgrids at each frame's interior top left. Generated transformed inserts fit completely. One-frame 7x12 three-color scenes alternate with varied multi-frame scenes.

COLOR-7 (orange) background grid (h ∈ 5-7, w = 3*sw + 2 with sw ∈ 5-6) split into 3 SECTIONS of WIDTH sw separated by 2 FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-6 (MAGENTA) DIVIDER COLUMNS at cols div1=sw and div2=2*sw+1. WITHIN EACH SECTION: N_MARKS ∈ 1-5 COLOR-1 (BLUE) CELLS scattered at random positions; PLUS ONE COLOR-5 (GRAY) CELL placed in exactly ONE of the 3 sections at a random row/col. Rule (RIGHT-TO-LEFT STACK ALL NON-BLANK ROWS FROM EACH SECTION INTO A SINGLE OUTPUT GRID OF SECTION WIDTH; PER DEMOS: OVERLAY/COMBINE USING THE COLOR-5 MARKER AS ANCHOR): IDENTIFY the 3 SECTIONS (separated by 6-dividers). For EACH SECTION, EXTRACT its non-blank ROWS (rows containing any non-7 cells). STACK them right-to-left into a single output of DIMENSIONS h × sw, combining the cell values per a fixed stacking rule (e.g., last-wins, majority, or per-position OR). The single color-5 cell may act as a special marker. Net: 3 sections collapse into 1 by stacking; the unique 5 may anchor the layout.
Erase each component's strictly bbox-interior cells while preserving its bbox-edge cells.
Find every yellow-centered plus whose four petals share one nonzero, non-background color; output the most frequent petal color as a 1x1 grid.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-6 block and scattered color-8 cells. Rule: each 8 stays 8 if aligned with the 6 block's bbox row/col band; otherwise it stays 8 or becomes 4 by a diamond-support condition on the all-0 separator rows/cols between it and the block. The grid size, 6-block and 8 positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

Color-5 walls form an outer frame plus complete interior divider rows and columns. Treat every wall-separated room independently. In each room column, move all nonzero markers downward into the lowest available cells while preserving their top-to-bottom order; keep every wall fixed.

Choose the most frequent nonzero color as background. Count every other color; turn the largest repeated count and the next repeated count into solid squares whose side lengths are their integer square roots, and preserve an optional singleton. Place the big square at the upper right, the smaller square at the lower left, and—when present—the singleton at the bottom-left corner.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~11-13) with: (a) cell (0,0) = an OP KEY value in {1, 2, 3}; (b) one connected color-4 (yellow) motif (3-5 cells); (c) one connected color-6 (magenta) motif (3-5 cells). Both motifs placed apart from each other and from (0,0). Rule: read key = grid[0][0]. Take largest color-4 component → mask-crop to its bbox (1=cell, 0=bg). Same for color-6 → mask b. Pad both to max(h_a, h_b) × max(w_a, w_b) at top-left. For each cell: key=1 → cell non-zero in EITHER (UNION); key=2 → non-zero in BOTH (INTERSECTION); else → non-zero in exactly ONE (XOR / symmetric difference). Paint result cells color 8 (cyan). Output: crop to content.

For each color pair, sort endpoints in row-major order, draw horizontally from the upper endpoint to the lower endpoint's column and then vertically to the lower endpoint; later-read colors overwrite earlier colors at crossings.

0-bg grid (size varies) with a 3x3 TEMPLATE in the upper-left (values 0/7/9, center 0) and 1-4 ANCHOR cells elsewhere (distinct colors from {1..6,8}), each with a clear 3x3 footprint. Rule: for each anchor, stamp the template centered on it — template 9-cells become the anchor's color, 7-cells stay 7, only empty cells are painted. The grid size, the template pattern, and the anchors' count/positions/colors all vary freely (was a fixed X-template + 2 fixed anchors, ~9 distinct).

For each row independently, extract every monochrome nonzero run, sort those runs by descending length, preserve each run's color and length, then rebuild the row from column 0 with one 0 separator between runs. Generated lessons combine a genuine sorting witness with already-sorted, single-run, and blank controls so both row-wise scope and left-packing are identifiable rather than inferred from homogeneous rows.

Connect each same-colored endpoint pair through background cells. Cyan 8 is an impassable wall. Process colors in ascending order and paint the right/down/left/up BFS shortest path while treating foreign terminals and already-painted earlier paths as blocked.
Top row + left col hold codes; rule marks interior cells where row code = col code AND rays from edges are clear of walls.

A fixed 7x9 zero-background grid contains four monochrome five-cell panels in the 3x3 slots TL, TR, BL, and BR. The four panel colors are distinct nuisance labels. Crop each binary panel to its content. Output a 2x2 matrix with 8 at (r,c) exactly when top panel r and bottom panel c are equivalent under the full D4 group (rotation or reflection), else 0. The default sample-index schedule covers every output position, singleton and multi-match relations, reflection-only matches, and offset-only matches.

0-bg grid (h = 2*sh + 4, w = 2*sw + 4 with sh, sw ~3-4) with: (a) ONE isolated KEY CELL in {4 (OR), 6 (AND), 8 (XOR)} placed alone with 8-neighbor buffer; (b) ONE color-2 (red) shape A at (1, 1) with sh × sw bbox; (c) ONE color-3 (green) shape B at (sh+3, sw+3) with matching sh × sw bbox. A and B are connected within the sh × sw bbox but have DIFFERENT cell patterns. Rule: detect op key, A, B. Compute per-cell boolean combine of A and B (both normalized to bbox), with op = OR (key==4), AND (key==6), or XOR (key==8). Output: the combined pattern painted in color 7 (orange) at A's position. Other cells = 0.
Three equal maroon frames contain red/blue shapes with overlapping bounding boxes and local key colors; repeated keys are lawful, and every draw teaches vertical centering in the output gallery.
0-bg grid (9..18) with 2-3 color-6 polyominoes (6..10 cells, bbox <= 4x4) and equally many distinct-color singleton markers near their shapes. Rule: recolor each shape by its nearest marker.

Read the nonzero codes in row 0 from left to right.  Crop the motif below the all-zero separator row to its bounding box, then apply every code to the previous state (1=identity, 2=rotate-CW, 3=flip-LR, 4=rotate-180).  Pack all intermediate states left-to-right with one zero column between them.  Motif colours are preserved; they may overlap the script colours.

0-bg grid (h,w ~ 9..14) holding exactly THREE things: ONE color-9 PIVOT cell at an interior position; ONE TOKEN cell of color in {1,2,3,4} (token-1 = the number of 90deg CW quarter-turns); and ONE 4-connected OBJECT (2-6 cells) in a color from {5,6,7,8} (disjoint from pivot 9 and tokens 1-4). The object sits within a radius of the pivot small enough that ALL quarter-turns about the pivot stay in bounds. Rule: erase token and object, ROTATE the object about the pivot by (token-1) quarter-turns, repaint it in its color, and restore the 9 pivot. Net: the object swings around the pivot by the token-selected angle.

0-bg grid (h=4, w=7-8, canonical-sized). The BOTTOM ROW carries TOKEN cells of colors {1,2,3,4} at scattered columns (each token = a transform KEY: 1=rotate-cw, 2=rotate-180, 3=flip-lr, 4=transpose).
