Above the bottom row (the FIELD, last column excluded) sit N_MOTIFS = 2 small 4-connected blobs in DISTINCT colors drawn from {5,6,7,8,9} (NOT the token colors), each grown by random adjacency walk and placed with an 8-conn 1-cell buffer. Tokens are placed so each motif's nearest token varies (keys differ across motifs). Rule: extract every 4-connected field component, crop to bbox, TRANSFORM by the key of the NEAREST bottom token (by horizontal center), then PACK the transformed crops left-to-right into a small center-aligned gallery with 1-cell gaps.

Find every nonzero monochrome 4-connected object, sort the objects by their left bbox column, and paint each solid bbox rectangle on a fresh same-size zero grid. The first rectangle starts at (0,0). After painting a rectangle of height h and width w, advance the next top-left by (h-1,w-1), so consecutive rectangles share exactly one corner and the later color overwrites that shared cell.

mix_weight_reason: Owner restores inherited zero weight after exact-source reviewer repair and fresh original/base-generation protected-Racket preflight. Imported notes describe old off-manifold failures; current source/rule review is valid and no active veto remains. Native qualification and fresh acceptance are still required.
summary: 0-bg SQUARE grid (size 10-30). Top half holds a BLUE (color 1) WALL spanning exactly 3 consecutive rows and the full width. The wall contains 1-3 OPENING pockets: 0-cells with blue somewhere above them inside the wall rows and blue somewhere on both sides in their row (gap shapes: dominoes, squares, L/T/S pieces, ...). Below the wall (>= 1 blank row) sit 3-6 GRAY (color 5) PIECES — 4-connected blobs such as bars, L-shapes, 2x2 blocks, T/plus clusters. Rule (GRAY KEYS THAT FIT A WALL OPENING OR BRANCH TURN RED): every gray piece turns RED (color 2) iff (a) it BRANCHES — some cell has 3+ gray 4-neighbors — or (b) its top rows, taken as tall as some opening, match that opening's shape directly or left-right mirrored. All other cells stay unchanged. Net: keys that fit a lock (or that branch) are marked red; the rest stay gray.
Separated 2x2 L-shapes have one missing square corner.

Close each occupied row from its leftmost to rightmost marker, compare the inclusive span lengths, and output the longest span as cyan (8) on a blank same-size grid. If maximum spans tie, choose the topmost tied row.

A 0-background grid contains 2-6 isolated monochrome objects spanning solid blobs (0 holes), hollow rings (1 hole), and sometimes double rings (2 holes). Sort objects by hole count descending, then occupied area descending, and pack their crops left-to-right with one-column gaps.

Row 0 holds a 3-color LEGEND. Below: several COLOR-5 shapes of varied size/position, each with a hole count of 0, 1, or 2 (solid blob / single ring / double ring). Rule: recolor each shape by its hole count -> legend[min(holes,2)]. Shapes, sizes, positions and legend colors vary.
Use the row-zero maroon count to select the kth component in canonical size-and-position order.

Place 2-4 disconnected green(3) objects.  Each object has one distinct colored key at (bbox_top-1,bbox_left); recolor the object to that key.  Every generated input contains at least one empty bbox-corner object so the bbox anchor is taught rather than merely asserted.

N (3-5) small 4-connected components in distinct colors. Some pairs are 4-touching (immediate cardinal adjacency), others are separated. Rule outputs an N×N adjacency matrix sorted by bbox top-left: diagonal cells = 1, off-diagonal (i, j) = 2 if components i and j are 4-touching, else 0.

A p x p periodic color TILE (period p in 2..5) tiled over a grid (rows and cols may differ), with some cells punched to 0 (holes). The first p rows keep the full tile so the period is recoverable. Rule: detect the period p, then fill each 0-cell from the matching periodic position. Output is the fully restored periodic grid.

Use (0,0) to select the largest same-colored source component and (0,w-1) as a 1/2/3/4 rotation command. Normalize and rotate the source, then center a recolored copy inside every hollow rectangular frame.

0-bg grid (h, w~14-18) with: (a) ONE HOLLOW COLOR-5 (gray) RECTANGULAR FRAME (5-7 × 5-7) drawn at random interior position; (b) INSIDE the frame (with 1-cell buffer from walls), a TEMPLATE SHAPE (3-4 cells from a bank of 8 templates) painted in TEMPLATE_COLOR (random non-{0, 1, 5}); (c) OUTSIDE the frame, 2-5 BLUE (color-1) CANDIDATE SHAPES — at least one with normalized cells matching the template, and at least one with a different shape. Rule (MATCH TEMPLATE → RECOLOR CANDIDATES): identify the gray FRAME and TEMPLATE inside. NORMALIZE the template's cells. For EACH BLUE CANDIDATE outside the frame, NORMALIZE its cells and compare. If they MATCH the template's normalized pattern, RECOLOR the candidate to TEMPLATE_COLOR. Non-matching blue candidates stay color 1. Frame + template stay. Net: blue shapes matching the framed template get template's color; others stay blue.

Zero-background grids containing both singleton and multi-cell same-color 4-connected components.  Singletons are erased; larger components are preserved.  A three-sample schedule covers canonical 5-row shape/palette profiles and includes mixed-color cardinal contact plus same-color diagonal singletons, refuting multicolor-component and 8-connectivity shortcuts.

0-bg grid with 1-3 PAIRS of same-color rectangular BLOCKS. The two blocks of each pair sit at OVERLAPPING ROW BANDS with a horizontal COLUMN GAP between them; different pairs use distinct colors and sit in different row bands. Optionally a non-overlapping decoy pair (same color, disjoint rows) that the rule leaves alone. Rule: for each color with exactly two objects whose row ranges overlap, FILL the gap rectangle between their facing edges (over the overlapping rows) with that color, bridging the pair into one bar.
Key-dot lookup; rule expands each dot into 3x3 block.

0-bg maze bordered by color-5 walls, with extra interior color-5 walls, and two seeds (color 2 and color 3) at random distinct open interior positions. Rule: BFS distance from each seed through open (non-5) cells; each open cell is painted by its NEARER seed's color (2 or 3), or 8 on a tie. Seed positions and the interior wall layout vary freely.

0-bg grid with several BORDER EMITTERS (non-0,non-5 cells on the outer edge, spread across all 4 edges) and several interior COLOR-5 BLOCKERS. Rule: each border emitter shoots a ray inward (perpendicular to its edge) through 0-cells, painting them its color, until it hits any non-0 cell (a 5-blocker or another ray's tip) or the far border.

A color-0 grid contains exactly two equal-width panel columns and 2--4 row bands. Each panel has a modal nonzero background and one monochrome non-background mask. In every row band, reset both panels to their own backgrounds, move the right mask to the same relative coordinates in the left panel painted with the RIGHT background, and move the left mask to the right painted with the LEFT background. Foreground input colors are ignored; equal panel backgrounds can make both swapped masks vanish.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several closed COLOR-1 (blue) RECTANGULAR FRAMES (hollow outlines, >=3x3), placed clear of one another. Each frame's interior holds 1-3 cells of a SINGLE distinct non-{0,1} marker color (frames use different colors); optional decoy frames have an empty interior. Rule: for every hollow color-1 frame whose interior contains exactly ONE non-{0,1} color, recolor the frame's cells to that color; frames with no interior color (or more than one) stay blue. The grid size, the number / size / position of the frames and their marker colors all vary freely (was 2 hardcoded frames, ~6 configs).

0-bg grid with COLOR-5 cells acting as FLOORS/WALLS (some full-height 5-columns plus scattered 5-cells inside other columns) and SCATTERED SINGLE non-{0,5} colored cells. Rule (PER-COLUMN SEGMENT GRAVITY): the output keeps every 5-cell in place; within each column, the 5-cells split it into segments, and each segment's non-{0,5} values fall to the BOTTOM of that segment preserving their top-to-bottom order. Net: loose colored cells drop within their 5-bounded segment.

A 0-background grid contains one complete gray(5) rectangular frame with a blank interior and exactly two distinct singleton colored markers in corner regions outside it. Read markers row-major. Split the frame interior into four quadrants. Quadrants with the same parity as the first marker's corner receive its color; the other two receive the second marker color. The frame, markers, and all exterior cells are preserved.

0-bg grid (h~8-14, w~10-16) with: (a) ONE MIRROR AXIS COLUMN at axis_col (3..w-4) — 1-3 COLOR-8 (cyan) CELLS placed at random rows on this column (NOT a full 8-column, just markers); (b) 5-10 SCATTERED NON-ZERO CELLS in colors from palette (warm/cool/broad/primary) on ONE SIDE of the axis (left OR right). Cells are not on the axis column. Rule (IDENTIFY 8-AXIS, MIRROR NON-ZERO CELLS, FILL AXIS): identify the AXIS COLUMN (unique col containing ≥1 color-8). For EACH 0-cell at (r, c) with c ≠ axis_col: COMPUTE MIRROR position (r, 2*axis_col - c). If the MIRROR cell is non-zero, COPY it to (r, c). AXIS COLUMN becomes ENTIRELY COLOR-8 (every cell on the axis col is filled with 8). Net: scattered cells reflect across the 8-axis; axis column becomes solid cyan.

A zero-background grid contains at least two nonzero colours whose two cells are diagonally opposite corners of separate axis-aligned rectangles. Fill every cell of each implied rectangle with that pair's colour. Some lessons also contain a different colour appearing twice on one row or one column; that collinear pair stays unchanged because it is not diagonal.
Bridge two separated solid rectangles with color 8 inside the shrunken overlap of their facing spans.
Split at the centered full-height 5-divider, mirror the right half, and overlay nonzero right cells over the left half.

0-bg grid (~10-13 × 12-15) split into 4 QUADRANTS by EXACTLY ONE full-width color-9 (maroon) ROW and EXACTLY ONE full-height color-9 COLUMN. The LOWER-LEFT QUADRANT contains EXACTLY ONE HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME (border-only, ~3×3 to 5×5) in some non-{0, 9} color, with its strict interior all-0. Other quadrants are empty. Rule: identify the hollow object in the lower-left quadrant. COMPUTE its bbox CROP and SOLID-FILL its interior (replace 0 cells inside the bbox with the object's color). PASTE the now-SOLID rectangle into the LOWER-RIGHT QUADRANT at the same relative bbox position. The lower-left frame STAYS hollow. The 9-dividers and the original frame stay. Net: the hollow frame in the bottom-left gets duplicated as a solid filled rectangle in the bottom-right.

A unique token 1..4 appears in any corner, independently of its value. A connected 5..9-cell motif in 2..5 colors from 5..9 appears in the interior. Crop the motif and transform it according to the token: 1=identity, 2=rotate clockwise, 3=rotate 180 degrees, 4=transpose.
Count K maroon cells, select the K-th smallest of three blue components by area, tightly crop it, upscale 2x, and recolor nonzero cells cyan.

On a 0 background, each color occurring exactly twice is completed into an inclusive horizontal or vertical segment when its two cells are aligned. Every generated input has at least one pair of each orientation. A scheduled counterexample profile also includes an unaligned two-cell color and a three-cell color with one aligned subpair; both must remain unchanged, making the exact-count and alignment predicates learnable.

Several connected components form a contact graph (touching components are adjacent). A central HUB is a random connected polyomino touched by several singleton leaves (high degree); isolated singleton distractors sit elsewhere (degree 0). Rule finds the component with the highest contact degree (ties broken by size, then top-left), then outputs its bbox crop painted color 8. Hub shape/size varies, so the cropped output varies.

Three or four isolated 4-connected objects occupy a 0-background grid. Objects contain five or six cells and use two or three foreground colours, so disconnected objects can share a colour. Replace each object—not each colour—with one same-colour cell at floor((r1+r2)/2, (c1+c2)/2) of its tight bounding box. A three-profile schedule alternates canonical 3x3 objects with repeated-colour asymmetric 2x4 witnesses.

0-bg grid (h, w~9-16) holding a RANDOM CONNECTED BLUE(1) BLOB that is (nearly) 180-degree symmetric about an interior cell center (cr, cc): the blob is grown on one side then mirrored through the center, and a FEW cells are then DELETED so their symmetric partners are unmatched. Rule (COMPLETE 180-deg SYMMETRY, MARK NEW CELLS RED): SEARCH all candidate centers for the one that best maps the blue set onto itself while sending at least one blue cell onto a BG-0 cell; for each blue cell whose partner about that center is BG-0, PAINT the partner RED(2). Existing blue cells stay. Net: the missing symmetric partners fill in red. Blob shape, size, center and number of deletions all vary.

A four-row dictionary contains 3-4 compact multicolor prototypes, split by full color-9 columns.  Each prototype's unique minimum color is its key and anchor.  Below a full color-9 divider, every key-colored marker is replaced by the complete anchor-relative prototype on a blank body.

Rows 0/1 map colors to modes above a color-9 divider: 1 closes rows, 2 closes columns, 3 closes rows THEN columns ONCE, and 4 keeps only new row bridges, erasing its seeds. Rebuild the scene from original color supports; overlaps prefer mode 1 > 3 > 2 > 4, then the larger color.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with: (a) one PROTOTYPE — one color-8 (cyan) ANCHOR cell adjacent to (or inside) a small RANDOM CONNECTED POLYOMINO (2-7 cells) painted in 1-3 varied non-{0,1,8} colors; (b) 1-4 single color-1 (blue) TARGET cells scattered apart from the prototype, each with room around them for a full stamp. Rule: find the anchor (the 8 cell). Targets = all color-1 cells. Offsets = for every non-{0, 1, 8} cell in the input, compute (r - anchor_r, c - anchor_c, value). For each target, stamp those offsets at the target's position (target becomes new 'anchor'), each cell painted with the original value. Output: a fresh empty grid with all stamped cells. The original prototype, anchor, and target markers all DISAPPEAR in the output.

An 8..30 rectangular maze has one start(2), one goal(3), a complete gray wall barrier(8), one to three paired portals colored 4/5/6, and up to eight extra walls. Start and goal lie on opposite sides and no ordinary route crosses the barrier; at least one portal pair is required.

Split the input at the two full-height color-9 divider columns. Use the THIRD/rightmost panel as the query, convert its color-1 shape to a binary mask, add one cardinal (up/down/left/right) boundary layer, then crop to the grown mask's occupied bounding box. Output the cropped mask in color 1.
skills: analogy, inverse peeling, one-step dilation, reduced output

summary: A contiguous row-0 header contains 2..4 distinct colors.  Each header color has either one matching dot on the left/right edge or, for at most one color, no side dot.  The rule extends each header vertically to its matching dot and then horizontally to that edge; a header without a dot extends vertically to the bottom row.

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (2-4) hollow color-2 frames, each enclosing one hole, of distinct cell counts. Rule: take the largest one-hole frame and paint its hole cells 8 on a blank grid. The grid size, frame count and sizes/positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

A black canvas contains one padded, completely filled rectangular body using exactly two foreground colors. One color is the strict majority; the minority color forms a sparse horizontally asymmetric motif. The output crops the nonzero bounding rectangle and flips that crop left-to-right. A period-8 alternating anchor/witness curriculum retains canonical profiles and teaches explicit black background and all-color cropping.

0-bg grid (h, w~5-8) with SPARSE NONZERO CELLS scattered at 4-7 random positions using a 3-5 color palette drawn from 1..9. Cells are placed at random distinct positions; no spatial structure or invariant. Always at least one nonzero mark. Rule (SCAN-ORDER EMIT): READ the grid in ROW-MAJOR SCAN ORDER (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). COLLECT every nonzero value in ENCOUNTER ORDER into a list. EMIT them as a SINGLE-ROW OUTPUT (1 × N grid where N is the number of nonzero cells). Output preserves: (a) the scan order, NOT the input positions; (b) repeated colors appear as separate entries (no dedup); (c) sorted order is irrelevant. Net: scattered marks → 1-row sequence in scan order.
Find the two equal-colored aligned markers. Return a blank same-size grid with only the strict segment interior recolored cyan (8); omit both endpoints.

Find the one solid color-3 square. For every nonzero/non-3 singleton marker lying left/right on a square row, or above/below on a square column, paint the zero-cell gap to the nearest square edge in that marker's color. Preserve the square, the markers, and all diagonal decoy markers.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-12) with color-1 (blue) WALLS splitting the canvas into 2 (horizontal split at row h//2) or 4 (cross split at row h//2 and col w//2) ROOMS. Each room contains exactly one MARKER cell in a distinct non-{0, 1} color at a random interior position. Rule: detect color-1 walls dividing the grid. For each ROOM (connected bg region bounded by walls), find its marker color. FLOOD the room (every bg cell of that room) with the marker's color. Walls stay color 1.

EVEN-DIM grid (h, w~12-18, both even) split into 4 QUADRANTS (TL/TR/BL/BR). Each QUADRANT filled with one of 4 DISTINCT BASE COLORS from a palette (warm/cool/broad/primary, excluding noise color). Each quadrant has scattered NOISE (COLOR-4 by default) cells: 7-10 noise cells in the WINNING quadrant, 1-3 in the others. EXACTLY ONE quadrant has the highest noise count (unambiguous winner). Output uniq_out=8 (intrinsic — output is a 1×1 grid of the winning quadrant's color, with ~8 palette × few winner colors). Rule (EMIT 1×1 OF MOST-NOISY QUADRANT's COLOR): For EACH non-zero, non-noise color C in the grid: COUNT noise cells in C's filled region. Pick the C with MAX noise count. EMIT a 1×1 grid of color C. Net: most-noisy quadrant's color wins; output is a single cell.

A solid ORANGE(7) rectangle lies in a nonzero 5/8/9 background. Exactly one RED(2) head and a straight MAGENTA(6) tail are embedded in the rectangle. The arrow points away from the adjacent tail cell in any of the eight compass directions. Follow that ray through one or more orange cells and recolor the first non-orange cell to 7; only that single boundary cell changes.

A 0-background grid contains 3-4 halo-separated objects in distinct non-zero colors. All but one share a free-polyomino shape under rotation and reflection. Output the singleton object's observed pose and color, cropped to its tight bounding box.

skills: symmetry filtering, local reflections, frame-relative copy
summary: Two independently oriented color tripods define source (2/3/4) and target (5/6/7) coordinates. Copy source-local 8-markers within radius 3 exactly when their reflection (u,v)->(-u,v) exists, including axis self-mirrors. Other cells, including distant 8-distractors, remain unchanged.

A unique corner marker in {1,2,3,4} selects up/right/down/left. Every other non-{0,5} cell casts a same-color beam in that direction, stopping at the first color-5 blocker or the edge. Production draws contain both an active blocker and an irrelevant blocker.

Full-height color-5 walls split every row into independent horizontal segments. In each segment containing markers, replace the complete span from its first through last non-zero marker by color 8; preserve walls and leave empty segments at 0.
Place 3-5 separated monochrome objects left-to-right with a nontrivial shape-equivalence partition; compare translation-normalized shapes into an N x N 8/0 equality matrix.
Separated 2x2 windows have one missing same-color corner.
Marker at (0,0) is the target color; rule outputs the cropped bbox of the LARGEST multi-cell object with that color (excluding the singleton marker).

A zero-background 8-11 by 11-13 grid contains exactly two or three spatially separated, uniformly colored 4-connected components. Component colors and sizes are distinct, and one component is uniquely largest (6, 8, or 12 cells). The largest component may be a filled rectangle or an irregular/hollow polyomino and appears in varied positions and colors. Select the component with the greatest cell count and return the exact input subgrid spanning its bounding box. Smaller components lie outside that box and disappear from the crop.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-10, w ∈ 8-11) with: 4 NON-OVERLAPPING COMPONENTS each in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from {1..9}: (a) ONE LARGE 6-CELL component (L-pentomino: (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0)) at fixed position (1, 1) in colors[0]; (b) ONE 2-CELL pair at (0, w-3..w-2) in colors[1]; (c) ONE 3-CELL L-tromino at (h-2..h-1, 0..1) in colors[2]; (d) ONE 2-CELL vertical at (h-2..h-1, w-2) in colors[3]. The 6-cell component is STRICTLY LARGER than any other (unique-largest). Rule (KEEP THE UNIQUE LARGEST CONNECTED COMPONENT, ERASE ALL OTHERS): EXTRACT every 4-connected non-bg component with cell count. FIND the component with MAXIMUM cell count (unique). PRODUCE a fresh same-size grid of 0s. PAINT only the largest component's cells in its original color. ALL OTHER components erased to bg. Net: noisy multi-component input becomes a clean single-component output.

Copy a connected multicolor source bounding box, including its zeros, into each gray rectangle at its top-left corner; retain gray beyond the stamp. Alternate fresh canonical-size examples with explicit shortcut witnesses.
Order four scattered 8-connected objects by upper/lower row group and left/right column, then assemble their normalized crops into a 7x7 quadrant grid.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~7-11 by ~10-16) with 2-3 FULL-HEIGHT vertical color-8 (cyan) WALL columns dividing the grid into chambers. Each chamber has 2-5 SCATTERED non-zero non-8 'pebble' cells at various rows (above the bottom). Rule: walls preserved. For each non-wall column independently, collect all non-zero non-8 values top-to-bottom. Stack them at the BOTTOM of the column with the topmost-original at the top of the stack. Other cells become 0. Walls divide gravity into chamber-local computation (each column processes alone).
Horizontal runs separated by zeros; odd-length >=3 runs reduce to centers, even/short runs erased.
Recolor cyan cells red when the cell at the same column in the top-bottom mirrored row is cyan; recolor every other cyan cell gray.

0-bg grid (h, w~5-25) containing a SINGLE FOREGROUND SHAPE in some non-zero fg_color, with shape_kind ∈ (rect / L_shape / hollow_ring / random_blob / line_h / line_v / cross / scatter / diagonal) filling a smaller bbox (shape_h × shape_w, 2-12 each) inside the canvas, padded by ≥1-3 bg cells on each side. The shape's bbox is strictly smaller than the grid in at least one dimension. Rule: APPLY CROP-TO-CONTENT — compute the BOUNDING BOX of all non-bg cells (rmin..rmax × cmin..cmax). CROP the grid to exactly that bbox — output is the rectangular subgrid containing only the content, with all bg padding outside the bbox stripped away. Net: input is padded shape; output is the tight bbox crop of the foreground.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 9-16, by difficulty) with: ONE COLOR-8 (CYAN) SEED PIXEL placed at a position per POSITION_BIAS ∈ {center (rng), top_left (3, 3), top_right (3, w-4), bottom_left (h-4, 3), bottom_right (h-4, w-4)} with ≥3-cell margin from all edges. Rule (FROM THE CYAN SEED, EMIT A CLIPPED GRAY (5) STAIR PATTERN: ONE ARM GOES UP-RIGHT IN STAIR STEPS, ONE ARM GOES DOWN-LEFT IN STAIR STEPS; THE STAIRS ALTERNATE ONE-CELL HORIZONTAL AND ONE-CELL VERTICAL MOVES, PAINTED IN COLOR 5; SEED CELL PRESERVED AS COLOR 8): FIND the COLOR-8 seed at (sr, sc). EMIT UP-RIGHT ARM: walk alternating up-1, right-1, up-1, right-1 ... until hitting the grid edge, painting each cell COLOR 5. EMIT DOWN-LEFT ARM: walk alternating down-1, left-1, ... until edge, painting color 5. Seed stays cyan. Net: cyan dot grows a 2-arm gray stair pattern.

A zero-background 8..18 by 8..18 grid contains one nonzero color. The occupied cells span a non-solid bounding box. Crop that box and concatenate the crop with itself horizontally. Even sample indices use the canonical 8x8 / 3x3 scale; odd indices use a non-3x3 bounding box so lessons explicitly refute a fixed-3x3 shortcut.
Row 0 holds k color-1 markers (rotation count, 1-4). Body has one maroon(9) anchor + non-{0,1,9} object cells. Rule rotates each object cell up to k times around the anchor.

A simple 2..6-turn orthogonal channel reaches two grid boundaries and is enclosed by exact orange side walls plus the outer corner at every bend. Examples cycle through no marker, a straight maroon marker, and a marker at a turn. The authority fills the selected channel cyan: all of it for no/straight markers, or only the larger side when a turn marker splits it.

A 3-row x 2-col grid of n x n panels separated by full color-9 dividers (rows n and 2n+1, col n; n varies by difficulty). TOP pair (left=template, right=transformed) demonstrates ONE of 5 geometric transforms (rot-cw / rot-180 / rot-ccw / flip-lr / flip-ud) on a RANDOM ASYMMETRIC color shape (all 8 dihedral images distinct, so the transform is uniquely inferable). MID pair demonstrates a RANDOM color RECOLOR MAP (k source colors -> k distinct targets). BOTTOM-LEFT holds a RANDOM query in the source colors; BOTTOM-RIGHT is blank. Rule: read the transform from the top pair, the recolor from the mid pair, apply both to the query, paint the result into the blank. Panel size, shape, transform, color sets and all three layouts now vary freely (were 5 hardcoded inputs).

A rectangular grid has a closed one-cell gray (5) frame, zero interior background, and three or four distinct non-{0,5,8} seed colors. Fill each interior zero with the color of its uniquely nearest seed by Manhattan distance; if two or more seeds tie for the minimum distance, paint cyan (8). Preserve the seed cells and the gray frame.
Use the unique red cell as a rotation pivot. For every blue marker, paint all in-bounds 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° rotation images; clipped images are skipped and the red pivot remains red.

Place one horizontally and vertically symmetric colored shape on background 0. Its even bounding box is 6..10 rows by 6..10 columns; the selected rule returns the top-left quadrant, preserving its colors and internal zeros.

skills: within-tile transforms, regular tiling, same-size output
summary: Mirror each equal-sized tile left-right in place, preserving the color-9 divider lattice. One foreground color on background 0; 1..3 tile rows, 2..5 tile columns, tile height/width 2..5. Canonical 1x3, 3x3-tile examples alternate with shortcut witnesses and independent broad draws.
Trace color-6 markers upward; roll right across orange ledges or stop when the roll is blocked or reaches the edge.

Two equal-height, coordinate-aligned binary masks are separated by one full-width color-5 row. The top and bottom foreground colors are distinct non-{0,5,8} colors. Output cell (r,c) is 8 iff both aligned input cells are nonzero, otherwise 0. Every generated input exposes 00, 10, 01, and 11 occupancy states; a four-profile schedule preserves canonical 5x8, colors-2/3 support while varying palette, shape, spatial texture, and foreground-color roles.

Crop the uniquely smallest monochromatic 4-connected object. Vary target size 1..7, polyomino shape, colors, position and distractor sizes. Include sparse/compact ranking inversions, repeated colors, different-color edge contacts and same-color diagonal contacts; retain canonical-scale draws.
Compact each row's nonzero cells flush left while preserving their original left-to-right order.

A zero-background grid has three to six active rows. Each active row's first cell is its non-cyan color key, and one or more cyan(8) markers appear later in that row. Recolor every such row-local 8 to the row key. Scheduled variants also include a cyan marker in a headerless row, which must stay 8, and non-cyan body distractors, which must remain unchanged.
3-5 distinct-color blobs of varied sizes/shapes (incl non-square bboxes).

0-bg grid (size varies) partitioned into rooms by color-5 wall lines, every room a distinct area. Rule: fill the smallest room 7 (orange) and the largest 8 (cyan); the rest stay 0. The grid size, room count/areas/layout vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~21 distinct).

Grid = 3 equal-width panels separated by single color-5 columns. panel0 is a binary MASK (some color on bg 0), panel1 (A) and panel2 (B) hold colored content. Rule: output[r][c] = A[r][c] where mask non-zero, else B[r][c].
Connected components in colors 1, 2, 3. Output is a 3×6 bar chart: row r (r=0,1,2) has color r+1 painted in the first n cells, where n = number of (r+1)-colored components in the input.

On a colour-0 background, each colour-2 marker casts a one-cell colour-5 shadow diagonally down-right only when that destination is in bounds and still 0. The marker and every other input cell are preserved. The teaching schedule includes blocked destinations, inert non-2 decoys, and clipped boundary markers so canonical-fitting shortcut rules are falsified.

A closed color-5 frame contains two or three distinct-colored seeds. Zeros take the unique nearest seed color by wall-aware 4-neighbor BFS; finite ties and seedless chambers remain zero. Three scheduled profiles guarantee tie, wall-detour, and unreachable-component evidence.
Find the same-colour 4-connected nonzero components, keep the unique component with the most cells unchanged, and erase every smaller component to background 0.
Recolor each 0-pocket by its size: 1->3, 2->2, 3->1, >=4 stays 0.
Top region + 5-separator + empty bottom; rule emits mode at last-row middle.

0-bg grid with a bottom row of 1-3 marker cells (colours 1/2/3) at distinct columns, and for each marker one upper label digit (the same 1/2/3) sitting just left of a coloured shape (colour 4..9). Rule moves each labelled shape to its marker's column, bottom-aligned above the bottom row, in the shape's colour; markers stay.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 SMALL MOTIFS (connected polyominoes of 3-5 cells each) scattered at distinct positions, each in a distinct non-bg color, with 4-adjacency isolation between motifs. Rule: ignore motif identity/shape and INSTEAD find the four EXTREMAL non-zero cells: NORTH (lowest row), SOUTH (highest row), WEST (leftmost col), EAST (rightmost col). Compute CENTER (cr, cc) = (midpoint of north/south rows, midpoint of west/east cols), and RADIUS = Manhattan distance from NORTH to CENTER. PAINT a blank canvas of the same dims, filling every cell whose Manhattan distance to (cr, cc) is ≤ RADIUS with color 8 (cyan). Net: the scattered colored motifs are replaced by a single cyan DIAMOND whose center and size are derived from the motifs' bounding extents.
Keep exactly the nonzero 4-connected components with even cell count; erase odd-area components while preserving each kept cell's color.

A zero-background grid contains one connected four-cell red (2) template, one to three isolated blue (1) anchor cells, and sometimes one smaller singleton red distractor.  Normalize the largest red component by its bounding-box top-left and copy those offsets in blue at every anchor, preserving the input.  Therefore an anchor is part of the copied shape when the template contains normalized offset (0, 0), but remains as an extra marker when that offset is absent.
Preserve colored source cells and copy each color across the anti-diagonal (r,c) -> (n-1-c,n-1-r).

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with exactly 3 ISOLATED 4-conn BLOBS in distinct colors with strictly distinct sizes (drawn from {2..6}). Blobs are non-touching. Rule: identify all 4-conn non-bg objects, pick the one with the SMALLEST cell count (unique by construction), crop to its bounding box, and UPSCALE by factor 2 (each cell becomes a 2×2 block of the same color). Output dimensions = (2 * bbox_h) × (2 * bbox_w).

Grid of size (3*N) × (3*M) divided into N×M sub-blocks of 3×3 cells each. Each block contains some cells in a dominant color plus stray distractor cells. Rule outputs an N×M grid where each output cell = the most frequent value in the corresponding 3×3 block.

0-bg grid with: (a) one PROTOTYPE shape in a non-{0, 9} color (a 4-connected blob, 3-5 cells); (b) 2-4 ANCHOR cells in color 9, scattered. Anchors and prototype are isolated (1-cell buffer). Rule: the prototype defines a binary stamp pattern. For each anchor 9, stamp the prototype's binary pattern at the anchor's position (with overlap counts). Output uses color 1 for stamps + per-cell overlap count visualization; the anchor's own cells become part of the stamp pattern. Original prototype and anchors are not preserved in output.
3×3 tiles in a 9-divided lattice; rule paints an 8 at center of every tile whose top-left AND bottom-right corner are nonzero (main-diagonal corners set).
skills: tile-local condition checks, same-size output, corner reasoning

summary: A large 8-colored sidebar panel (5-6 cols, near full height) carries 2-4 KEY MOTIFS carved into it in distinct non-{0,1,2,8} colors. The field beside it holds isolated 5x5 tiles: SOLID tiles in key colors and PATTERNED tiles (base color 2 + 1-cells at some key's motif positions). Rule: solid key-color tiles become base-color tiles stamped with that key's 1-motif; patterned tiles whose 1-motif matches a key (under the 8 dihedral transforms) become solid tiles of that key's color.

Several 4-connected non-bg components on a 0-bg grid: solid blobs, hollow frames, plus-shapes, etc. One component has STRICTLY highest exposed-cell perimeter (cells with ≥1 non-component-cell neighbor or grid edge). Rule outputs the cropped bbox of the winner with all non-zero cells recolored to 8 (holes preserved as 0).

On a two-color grid, treat 2 as background and find the 4-connected color-0 components. Sort whole components by their leftmost column. Recolor every third component starting with the first (indices 0, 3, 6, ...) completely to 4. The curriculum alternates the canonical 3-row zigzag with irregular multi-cell shapes and a row-order trap, so neither a fixed 3x12 pixel stencil nor 'every third black pixel' can solve it.

0-bg grid (h, w ~7-10) with 3-5 ACTIVE COLUMNS, each containing 1-4 non-zero cells at random rows in rotating colors from a 6-color palette. At least one column has multiple non-zero cells. Other columns are fully zero. Rule: for each column c, find all non-zero cells in that column; keep only the one with the LARGEST r (bottommost) — clear every other non-zero cell in that column to 0. Net: each column collapses to at most one cell, located at the bottommost row where it originally had a value.

A 5..9 by 5..9 color grid uses background 0 and all foreground colors 1..9. Every column contains one to three nonzero values. The rule packs each column's nonzero values upward into rows 0,1,... while preserving their original top-to-bottom order. A deterministic four-example teaching schedule includes dense canonical-scale scenes, a below-top singleton that must move, and an A-B-A column whose order must remain A-B-A.

0-bg grid with N (3-5) connected blobs in distinct non-zero colors. Each blob has a strictly distinct size from all others (so the size-rank is unambiguous). Blobs are placed with ≥1-cell buffer so they don't 4-touch. Rule: sort all 4-connected non-bg components by (size ASC, then top-row ASC, then left-col ASC). Recolor the i-th component to palette[i] where palette = [2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9]. Output: same shapes, new colors based on size-rank.

A hollow framed object and a different-colored solid square have equal bounding-box size. Transfer every enclosed zero region of the hollow in local coordinates by carving those cells from the solid; preserve all other cells. Ordinary draws contain a connected divider that creates multiple holes and therefore refutes whole-interior and largest-hole-only shortcuts. Three-example lessons also refute a rightmost-target positional shortcut.
Find the first and last nonzero rows, treat that contiguous row block as one vertical period, and tile the period over the full grid with the phase anchored at the original first nonzero row.

Dense color-8 mazes with start 2, goal 3, checkpoint 5, and one or two required portal pairs (6/7).  The selected BFS tracks whether checkpoint 5 has been visited; generated lessons refute goal-first, direct-path, and ignore-portals rivals.

0-bg grid (h~4-6, w~8-10) with: (a) the RIGHTMOST column filled entirely with color-9 (maroon) cells — the DOCK; (b) one connected BLOB of 3-4 cells in some non-{0,9} color, placed on the LEFT side with empty space to its right. Rule: extract dock cells and blob cells. While the blob can be shifted east by 1 (all next-column cells in bounds AND either 0 or in the blob itself), shift it east. Stop when shifting would hit the dock or wall. Output: empty grid + dock(9) + blob in original color at final position (abutting the dock).

0-bg grid with ONE marker cell (colour 1=TL/2=TR/3=BL/4=BR) and ONE connected object (colour 5..9). Rule: crop the object and paste it into the marker-indicated corner of an empty grid; the marker is dropped.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~10-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) CONNECTED COMPONENT placed at the LEFT side (col c0 ∈ 0..2) of the grid, drawn from a 3-shape bank (small L/T-tetro shapes); (b) blocker_kind ∈ {wall, edge}: if WALL, a full-height COLOR-8 (cyan) WALL is placed at col wall_c (at least 2 cells right of the red); if EDGE, no wall, the grid edge acts as the right boundary. Rule (SLIDE RED RIGHT UNTIL BLOCKED): identify the COLOR-2 component. SLIDE it RIGHTWARD as a rigid body until ANY of its cells WOULD HIT (a) the GRID's RIGHT EDGE (col w) or (b) a COLOR-8 WALL cell. STOP at the first contact (translated cells stay in bounds and don't overlap walls). Walls stay. Net: red component shifts right as a unit until obstructed.

A 0-background grid contains exactly two equal-color markers at opposite diagonal corners of a rectangle. Return a same-size grid whose inclusive marker bounding box is filled solidly with that color and whose remaining cells are 0. Ordinary lessons vary both diagonal orientations, rectangle shape, color, grid size, and edge/interior placement.

Three to five isolated green components with distinct cell counts; scale the second-smallest shape 2x at its bounding-box origin in cyan. Mix random polyominoes with explicit ranking, shape and anchor witnesses.

Find the single color-8 pivot. After temporarily removing it, select the unique largest 4-connected nonzero component. Preserve each source cell's color and paint that component in all four reflection-related positions around the pivot: original, left/right mirror, up/down mirror, and both. Return a fresh background-0 grid with the pivot restored; smaller disconnected components are distractors and are omitted.

0-bg grid (h~10-14, w~11-16) with: (a) a RADIUS INDICATOR at (0, 0) = value in {1, 3} (encoding radius 1, 2, or 3); (b) a VERTICAL COLOR-5 (gray) WALL at random col wall_col (4..w-5) with ONE GAP at row gap (3..h-3); plus a partial HORIZONTAL gray wall at row h-3 with select gap columns; (c) a CONNECTED L-SHAPED COLOR-2 (red) SEED of 3 cells in the lower-left chamber. Rule (DILATE RED SEED BY TOP-ROW RADIUS THROUGH NON-WALLS, PAINT CYAN): identify RADIUS R from (0, 0). DILATE the RED SEED COMPONENT by R cells through 4-connected non-5 (wall) cells (BFS depth ≤ R from any seed cell). PAINT all reached non-seed cells with COLOR-8 (cyan). The radius indicator, walls, and seed stay. Net: red seed grows cyan halo of radius R, blocked by gray walls.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several DISTINCT blue(1) shapes, each stamped once (unique) or several times (duplicated, same orientation), placed apart, with a mix of both. Rule: recolor every UNIQUE shape to 8 (cyan) and every DUPLICATED shape to 2 (red). The grid size, the shapes and each shape's count/positions vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~16 distinct).

5 SQUARE panels separated by full color-9 divider columns. Panels 1->2 are related by a geometric TRANSFORM (id/rot90/rot180/rot270/flip-h/flip-v/transpose); panels 3->4 by a COLOR RECOLOR of the same shape; panel 5 is a fresh motif using panel 3's source colours. Rule: infer the transform from 1->2 and the recolor from 3->4, apply both to panel 5, output the result.

Sort the three distinct-color connected objects by four-neighbour perimeter descending (color ascending on ties), then output their colors as one row. Every draw refutes area order and row-major position order.

0-bg grid (variable size ~10-14) with 1-3 COLOR-1 (BLUE) random-walk WIRES of length 4-8 with occasional turns; each wire has ONE adjacent COLOR-2 (RED) START cell. Rule: from each start, follow the attached non-branching color-1 wire and count its turns (direction changes); the wire with the MAXIMUM turn count (ties broken by length) is RECOLORED to COLOR 3 (green). Other wires and all start cells stay. Multiple wires per grid exercise the turn-count selection.

skills: reduced output, numeric depth encoding, bounding-box cropping
summary: A zero-background grid contains one or two thick 4-connected binary components grown around guaranteed 3x3 cores. Foreground colors are semantically ignored; scheduled striped multicolor components explicitly teach that adjacent colors belong to one shape. The rule peels cardinal boundary layers, writes each cell's onion depth, and crops the combined map to the foreground bbox.

SQUARE grid (n × n with n ∈ [6, 9]) with 3-6 NON-BG CELLS placed EXCLUSIVELY on or ABOVE the ANTI-DIAGONAL (positions (r, c) with r + c < n - 1). Cells use various non-0 colors. Rule (ECHO EACH NON-BG CELL ACROSS THE ANTI-DIAGONAL): For EACH CELL at (r, c) with value V (non-0): PAINT its ANTI-TRANSPOSE position (n - 1 - c, n - 1 - r) with the SAME VALUE V. Cells on the anti-diagonal (where r + c == n - 1) echo to themselves. Existing cells stay. Net: the upper-anti-triangle pattern is mirrored across the anti-diagonal into an anti-transpose-symmetric grid.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~6-9 by ~8-12) with 3-5 horizontal RUNS of non-zero cells. Each run: a contiguous horizontal segment of length 2-5 in a single non-zero color. Runs are placed in different rows or with ≥1 zero gap between same-row runs. Different runs use distinct colors (or repeat). Rule: for each cell, output the cell's color if it's the LEFTMOST of its same-color horizontal run (i.e., either col=0 or the cell to its left has a different color), else 0. Output: only the leftmost cell of each horizontal run survives.
Paint three color-8 copies of the first color-2 object along the vector from the first color-3 cell to the first color-4 cell.

0-bg grid (h, w~12-18) with: (a) ONE CONTROL CELL at (0, 0) — a singleton color from {1, 2, 4, 6} encoding a ROTATION (1=0°, 2=CW, 4=180°, 6=CCW); (b) ONE GREEN(3) TEMPLATE near top-left — fixed 4-cell L-shape at cells (2, 1), (2, 2), (3, 1), (4, 1) (an asymmetric L); (c) ONE HOLLOW GRAY(5) RECTANGULAR FRAME near bottom-right at (h-7, w-7)..(h-2, w-2). The template fits inside the frame after the indicated rotation. Rule (ROTATE THE GREEN TEMPLATE BY THE CONTROL CODE, PLACE INSIDE THE GRAY FRAME): READ the CONTROL color → rotation. ROTATE the green template's cells by the indicated angle (0°/CW/180°/CCW). PLACE the rotated template's cells INSIDE the gray frame (centered or at a canonical position within the frame interior), painted GREEN. The control cell, original template, and frame all stay. Net: the template gets cloned into the frame interior at the orientation indicated by the control color.
3-6 distinct-color non-touching blobs of varied sizes.
One to three separated color-1 rectangular outlines each have one non-corner gap. Fill every interior with 2 and extend a 2-beam outward from each gap to the grid edge.

A non-{0,5} template lies in the top-left 3x3 chamber, whose bottom row and right column form a seven-cell gray L-frame. Outside the cue are 3..5 colored objects. Exactly one object has the template's exact translation-normalized shape and orientation; recolor only that object to gray (5). Rotated/reflected and different-size objects are decoys.
Crop-to-content yields a square n×n motif. Output tiles the grid in checkerboard with motif (even parity) and rotate-cw(motif) (odd parity).

Use the largest magenta(6) component's occupied cells relative to its bounding box as a mask. Find the solid green(3) rectangle with the same height and width, clear it, and redraw the mask there in cyan(8). Keep all magenta components unchanged.
Dense ten-color fields containing both zero components adjacent to color 1 and zero components isolated from color 1; only the adjacent components are absorbed.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-9) with: (a) ONE MULTI-COLOR SHAPE drawn from 3 hardcoded SHAPE VARIANTS (each 3-6 cells in 2-3 distinct colors from {1, 2, 4, 6}) placed in the UPPER-RIGHT quadrant; (b) ONE COLOR-5 (gray) MARKER cell at a non-adjacent position in the LOWER-LEFT quadrant. Rule (TRANSLATE SHAPE TO ALIGN CENTROID WITH 5-MARKER): identify the SHAPE (non-0 non-5 cells) and compute its CENTROID (mean of cell positions, rounded). Identify the 5-MARKER's position. COMPUTE translation delta = (marker - centroid). For EACH SHAPE cell at (r, c) with color C: ERASE the original, PAINT g[r + dr][c + dc] = C. The 5-marker is absorbed (or kept per task). Net: shape moves so its centroid lands on the gray marker.

0-bg grid with ≥2 blue (color-1) markers and optional decoration cells in other colors (the rule ignores them). Rule: enumerate all pairs of color-1 markers (in first-found order). For each pair (a, b), check if they share a row OR column AND their separation along that axis is EVEN and ≥2. The FIRST qualifying pair gets its midpoint cell set to color 2. All other cells preserved as-is.

A narrow grid is partitioned into 8..16 maximal groups of 1..3 identical rows. Groups alternate between nonempty 0/1 rows and nonempty 0/8 rows. Scan groups from zero: in groups 0,3,6,... recolor every nonzero cell to 2; preserve all cells in the other groups.
Solid colored rectangles are reduced to their bounding-box outlines.

A 7..10 by 8..10 grid contains 7..10 directional emitters (1=up, 2=right, 3=down, 4=left) and 4..6 color-5 walls. Rays include their emitter, pass through emitters, stop before walls, and add in a fresh count map. Constructive layouts include all four directions, a ray overlap, and a downward wall-stop witness.

On a 0-background grid, every isolated maroon (9) source casts a gray (5) echo exactly one cell down-left. In-bounds background targets are painted; occupied targets and out-of-bounds targets are skipped. Each scene retains at least one paintable source and includes one unrelated color-1/3/4 bar, domino, or 2x2 block matching the canonical distractor grammar.

Sparse zero-background grids use the same shape/palette signatures as the five canonical examples.  Every four-example lesson cycles through two aligned pairs, three aligned pairs, a diagonal repeated-color near miss, and singleton/aligned-triple cardinality near misses.  The rule connects only colors appearing exactly twice whose endpoints share a row or column; all other cells are preserved.

FIXED 3×11 grid with: (a) THREE 3×3 PANELS separated by FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-8 (cyan) DIVIDER COLUMNS at cols 3 and 7. Panels A (cols 0-2), B (cols 4-6), C (cols 8-10). PANEL A is a fixed L-shape (cells (0,0), (1,0), (1,1)) recolored in random non-{0, 8} A-COLOR. PANEL B is the same L-shape transformed by a chosen transform CODE (r1=rot90CW, r2=180, r3=CCW, fh=flip LR, fv=flip UD, tr=transpose, atr=anti-transpose) recolored in B-COLOR. PANEL C is a different fixed shape (cells (0,2), (1,1), (1,2)) recolored in C-COLOR. Rule (INFER TRANSFORM FROM A→B, APPLY TO C, UNION WITH ORIGINAL C): compare the support (cell positions) of PANEL A and PANEL B — infer which dihedral transform T maps A's support to B's. APPLY T to PANEL C's support. OVERLAY the transformed C cells (painted in C's color) onto the original C panel — nonzero transformed cells overwrite bg in C. Net: C panel gets enriched with T-transformed copies of itself. Flag: INTRINSIC-LOW DIVERSITY — fixed shapes × 7 transforms × small color set → ~19 distinct outputs.

Read every nonzero, non-blue color on the main diagonal in top-to-bottom order. Keep the blue rectangular frame, then fill its interior with those marker colors as nested rectangles from outside to inside.

For each blue (1) 4-connected component that is a straight horizontal or vertical segment of odd length at least 3, recolor only its middle cell red (2); leave even blue segments, bent blue objects, nonblue segments, and every other cell unchanged.

A canonical-size 0-background grid contains one colored rectangular frame with one contiguous gap on exactly one side. Yellow (4) pours from that mouth through the cavity band and continues diagonally beyond both arm tips. Arm lengths include canonical 2/2 cases and scheduled 1/1, 1/3, and 3/1 counterexamples to the strongest canonical-fitting shortcut. Every draw shows a diagonal continuation; explicit large profiles scale the frame and expose longer spouts while ordinary profiles remain canonical.
One color-2 + one color-3 single-cell markers + color-7 path cells; rule recolors each 7 to whichever marker is closer (BFS distance through 7-cells); equal distances → 8.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several color-6 (magenta) objects: one UNIQUE shape plus 1-3 other shapes each duplicated 2-3 times (same orientation), all placed apart. Rule: output the shape that appears exactly once, cropped to its bbox, in color 6. The grid size, the unique shape, the duplicate shapes/counts and all positions vary freely (was five fixed blobs, ~13 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with 2-3 distinct non-bg colors. For EACH color, EXACTLY TWO isolated single cells (the MARKERS) are placed at random non-adjacent positions (8-connectivity isolation between any two cells, so each cell is its own 4-component). Rule: for each color that appears in exactly TWO cells, treat the two cells as endpoints. PAINT an ELBOW PATH between them — an L-shaped 2-segment path going through some corner point (typically the cell at (r1, c2) or (r2, c1)) — in that color. The two endpoint cells stay. Net: each colored pair gets connected by an L-shaped path of its own color.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-9) with 2-3 HORIZONTAL endpoint TRIPLETS: each is a (color, 0, color) pattern in some row at consecutive cols (c, c+1, c+2). Plus 1-2 isolated DISTRACTOR cells that have no matching neighbor. Different triplets use varied non-bg colors. Rule: for each (r, c) with input == 0, check: HORIZONTAL match — (r, c-1) and (r, c+1) are equal non-bg → fill (r, c) with that color. Else VERTICAL match — (r-1, c) and (r+1, c) are equal non-bg → fill with that color. Horizontal precedence (if both match with different colors, horizontal wins).

Find every closed rectangular color-1 frame. Recolor each color-2 cell strictly inside any such frame to color 4, while preserving color-2 distractors outside all frames and leaving every other cell unchanged.

A full-height gray divider separates a magenta source from empty mirror destinations. Copy every magenta cell across the divider as cyan while preserving all source cells and unrelated colored distractors. Generated lessons include singleton, two-cell, and oversized magenta components in the same inputs plus a left distractor whose mirror remains blank, refuting canonical-fitting component-size and reflect-all shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~6-8) with 2-4 SPARSE SEED cells placed at random positions, each in a distinct non-bg color (the seed colors are simply 2, 3, 4, 5 in placement order). Rule: for each non-bg seed cell at (r, c), STAMP a 5-cell PLUS shape in color 8 (cyan): the center (r, c) and the four cardinal neighbors (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1). Cells that fall outside the grid are clipped. The seed cells themselves are OVERPAINTED to color 8 (their original color is replaced). Net: every colored seed dot becomes a cyan plus-sign on a black field; the original seed colors disappear.
Move each active gray marker to the penultimate cell of its adjacent green route while preserving inactive markers, endpoint green, zeros, and unrelated cells.

One color-1 source (treated as laser start, moving right). Mirrors at color 2 reflect via (dr,dc) → (-dc,-dr); mirrors at color 3 reflect via (dr,dc) → (dc,dr). Color 8 is a wall (stops the beam). The beam paints empty cells along its trajectory color 7. Source + mirrors + walls preserved.

A 0-background grid contains one connected color-2 template and two colored rectangular frame outlines.  Frames may be disjoint or one may occlude cells of the other, splitting a frame color into multiple same-color components.  The output is a fresh 0 canvas containing every non-2 component plus a centered, frame-colored copy of the normalized template inside each such component; the source template disappears.
Color-5 wall grid of 0-chambers (5 outer ring); border markers (non-0/5) flood the adjacent chamber with their color.
Four distinct colors form a 2x2 source. Each color paints a clipped 2x2 patch in the diagonally opposite quadrant, measured from the source block.

0-bg grid (size varies). 2-3 colors from {2,3,4}, each with exactly 2 ENDPOINT cells aligned in a row or column (the cells between them are empty). Rule: fill the segment between each aligned same-color pair with that color. Line footprints are reserved so they don't cross. The grid size, which colors are used, and each pair's orientation/length/position vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~13 distinct).

A full separator row or column divides a sparse source side from an aligned key row or column. Matching source dots move to the edge next to the separator; non-matching dots move to the far outer edge.

On a zero background, expand every isolated interior colored singleton into a five-cell plus by painting its four cardinal neighbours with the same color. Every generated lesson contains 2-3 differently colored markers with disjoint plus footprints.

Use the blue object as a reference shape. Recolor each red object cyan exactly when its normalized cells match the reference under a rotation or reflection; preserve the reference, decoy, marker, and background.
Red seeds cast cyan rays along all diagonals until gray blockers.

Grid laid out as a 4×4 MACRO-GRID of cell_size × cell_size (cell_size ∈ {1, 2}) macro-cells, separated by SEPARATOR rows/cols painted color `sep` (drawn from non-bg). Each macro-cell is one of: TARGET color, SUPPORT color, or empty. The input is configured so one TARGET macro-cell at (1, 1) has a distinctive SUPPORT neighborhood (its 4 cardinal macro-cells colored support); other TARGET macro-cells appear elsewhere without support. Rule: detect the target-color macro-cell with the strongest support neighborhood. Propagate that pattern (paint matching support neighbors) to every other target macro-cell.

A complete color-1 border plus connected internal color-1 walls split a 7..14 by 8..16 grid into two to four rooms. Each room has one distinct seed color from 2..9 and at least one zero. Fill every room's zeros with its seed color while leaving all color-1 walls unchanged.

A 30x30 zero-background grid contains 2..4 spatial rows of exactly three spatially varied solid 3..8-cell-side colored rectangles using a canonical-scale target palette, plus dense two-color small-object noise whose colors are absent from the rectangles. Return the rectangle colors as an n-by-3 table in spatial row-major order.
Stamp a template and its mirrored/rotated variants into the 4 interior corners of a 4-frame.

Treat color 1 as walls. For every 4-connected non-wall region, fill its zero cells with the region's unique marker color when exactly one distinct marker color is present; leave seedless and mixed-color regions unchanged.

A centered color-5 cross divides an odd square grid into four equal quadrants. Exactly three quadrants contain the same connected colored shape under the horizontal/vertical reflection appropriate to their position; exactly one quadrant is empty. Fill only the missing quadrant.

On a 0-background grid, inspect each 4-connected red (2) component in its own bounding box. Recolor the whole component to green (3) exactly when its shape is left-right symmetric. Leave asymmetric red components and gray (5) distractors unchanged.

On a zero-background grid, find every complete same-colour hollow rectangular frame. Preserve its border. Fill every zero cell strictly inside that frame with colour 7 when the number of interior columns is odd, and with colour 2 when the number of interior columns is even. Frames are handled independently; border colour, position, height, and the number of other frames do not determine the fill colour.
Count every nonzero cell in the one-row input. Build a width/2 by width output whose row r is a left-aligned prefix of count+r cells in the same nonzero color; all remaining cells are background 0.

Fixed 9×10 grid with 6 cells (2×3 macro grid), each cell is 3 rows × 2 cols, separated by all-0 row 4 and all-0 cols 3 + 6 + border. Each cell has a majority color + possible distractor cells. Rule outputs a 4×5 grid: 0-border + each interior position = mode color of corresponding 3×2 cell.
Grid with distinct color frequencies; rule outputs 3 × 3 of the 3rd-ranked color.

A connected magenta (6) payload and one direction marker appear on a black grid. Marker colors 1/2/3/4 mean left/up/right/down. Shift every payload cell one step in that direction and output only the shifted payload on a blank grid.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-16) with: (a) 1-2 RECTANGULAR FRAMES (perimeter outlines) of size 5×6 to 8×9, in some FRAME_COLOR (the most frequent non-zero color), placed by bias (right_lean / centered / corner / scattered). At least one frame is LARGER than the other (the largest is the target); (b) 3-5 SCATTERED DOT CELLS in a SECOND non-frame color (DOT_COLOR) outside the largest frame, plus 1-2 dots INSIDE the largest frame's interior. Rule: identify the MOST FREQUENT COLOR (FRAME_COLOR) — its cells form the rectangular frames. PICK the LARGEST FRAME component (by bbox area). CROP the grid to that frame's bbox. REPLACE the frame's perimeter cells with the DOT_COLOR. Net: output is the largest frame cropped, with its perimeter recolored to the dot color and its interior dots preserved.
Erase a colored cue outside a purple frame, then copy the cue's full bounding-box edges to the corresponding inner frame edges; if all four cue edges are full, fill the complete frame interior.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~12-14) with 3-4 ISOLATED 4-CONN COMPONENTS, each a 2-or 3-cell shape (L-tromino/I-domino/square-corner) in a DISTINCT color from {1..9}. Components placed at scattered positions with varying Manhattan-2 neighborhood degrees (some isolated, some touching others). Rule (RECOLOR EACH COMPONENT BY ITS MANHATTAN-2 TOUCH DEGREE): For EACH COMPONENT: COUNT the number of OTHER COMPONENTS within MANHATTAN-2 distance (any pair of cells in different components with Chebyshev ≤ 2 or Manhattan ≤ 2). MAP DEGREE → COLOR: 0→2, 1→3, 2→4, 3→5, 4→6, ≥5→7. RECOLOR all component cells to the mapped color. Net: each shape repaints by how many neighbors it has within Manhattan-2.
Cyan dots; rule fills between 2 cyans in same col/row with green.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~7-10) with 2-4 TWO-CELL DIAGONAL COLOR CHAINS: for each chain, pick a distinct color from {1..9}, choose diagonal direction (down-right or down-left), pick a starting cell (r, c) so that the chain plus its one-step continuation fit in bounds. PAINT both chain cells (r, c) and (r+1, c±1) with the chain color. The THIRD cell at (r+2, c±2) is reserved (invariant: in-bounds and bg-0). Chains use disjoint cells; no two chains share any cell or extension cell. Rule (EXTEND EACH DIAGONAL CHAIN ONE MORE STEP): for EACH color C with exactly TWO cells forming a one-step diagonal (offset (+1, +1) or (+1, -1)): COMPUTE the continuation cell by extending one more step in the same diagonal direction. PAINT that continuation cell with COLOR C. Original two chain cells stay unchanged. Net: each two-cell diagonal becomes a three-cell diagonal of the same color, extending downward in the natural direction.

0-bg grid (h, w varies by difficulty: 9×11 / 10×13 / 14×16) with: N_COMPS ∈ 2-4 SEPARATED 4-CONNECTED COMPONENTS, each painted in a DISTINCT color drawn from {1..9}, each as a solid rectangle filling a subset of size cells (rectangle dimensions chosen to approximately match each component's size). The LARGEST component has size LARGE_SIZE (6-14 by difficulty); other components have strictly smaller sizes (decreasing by 2 per component). Components placed with gap ≥2 between bboxes. Rule (FIND THE 4-CONNECTED COMPONENT (UNDER 'NON-ZERO' PREDICATE) WITH THE LARGEST CELL COUNT; TIE-BREAK BY EARLIEST BBOX TOP-LEFT (SMALLER R, THEN SMALLER C); CROP THE INPUT TO THAT COMPONENT'S BBOX; OUTPUT THE CROP — CELLS IN THE COMPONENT PRESERVE THEIR COLORS, BBOX HOLES ARE 0): EXTRACT every non-bg component. SORT by (-cell_count, min_r, min_c). PICK first. CROP input to its bbox. OUTPUT. Net: largest component extracted with its original colors in a tight bbox crop.

On a literal orange-7 canvas, two to four parallel full-span black strips are exactly three cells thick. One to three strips carry a same-colored cap in the three-wide block at a common source end, while at least one strip is unmarked and inherits that direction. Clear every strip and copy its complete source-end 3-wide block to the opposite end. Same-colored markers outside all strips are stationary decoys.
An 8-background rectangle contains one monochrome cyclic segment on its outer-border ring.  Keep the source segment and repeat it around the ring at stride 2N, where N is the number of colored cells.
Sparse upper-half cells are copied across the horizontal axis.
Count wholly empty rows inside a gray U-shaped container; paint a 3x3 clockwise cyan spiral.
Single gray(5) blob of 2x2 rooms linked by bridges plus dangling arms/tips; oracle recolors 3-cell arm runs to 2 and remaining gray to 8.
Recolor every nonzero cell with no orthogonally adjacent nonzero neighbor to 9; preserve all multi-cell foreground components.
A full row or column of 8s acts as a mirror guide; isolated colored cells appear only on the source side.

Top-row color-4 markers select payload columns and left-column color-5 markers select payload rows. Return the ordered submatrix at their intersections. Nonselected left-border cells include colored distractors, and colors 4/5 also occur as ordinary payload values.
Colored singleton seeds with one-step nearest-border motion.
The input expands a small color grid by independently repeating each logical row and column; the output samples the first cell of every run detected along the input's first column and first row.

A gray field contains three or four separated rectangular 0/2 chambers. Count red cells in each chamber; paint the unique maximum chamber cyan on a blank output. Scheduled examples refute exact-three, largest-room, and highest-density shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h, w~6-10) with: (a) TOP ROW (row 0) containing 2-5 COLOR HEADERS at random distinct columns, in DISTINCT non-{0, 8} colors; (b) BODY (rows 1..h-1) with 1-3 COLOR-8 MARKER CELLS in each header column at random rows. Columns without headers stay 0. Rule (HEADER-DIRECTED RECOLOR): for EACH COLUMN c where row 0 contains a NON-ZERO HEADER COLOR header_c, find all body cells in that column with value 8 and RECOLOR them to header_c. The top-row header stays. Cells in header-less columns and non-8 body cells stay. Net: top-row color tags propagate down their column to repaint every 8-marker.
Crop the original grid to the bounding box of the first smallest same-color 4-connected component when color 2 alone is excluded.

Grid n × n (n = 2*cell_size + 1, cell_size ∈ {3, 4}) with: (a) full color-4 (yellow) SEPARATOR row at row cell_size and full color-4 separator column at col cell_size — splits grid into 4 SECTIONS; (b) one MARKER cell in distinct non-{0, 1, 4} color in each of two sections (top-left, bottom-left). (c) BLUE (color-1) cells scattered in the right-column sections. Rule: for each blue cell, look at its section's row position relative to separator and inherit the marker color from the same-row left-column section (top → m1's color, bottom → m2's color). Output: blue cells replaced by their section-paired marker color.

A zero-background grid contains two or three distinct nonzero colors. For each color, exactly three cells occupy three corners of one axis-aligned rectangle and the fourth corner is blank. Complete every rectangle by painting only its missing corner with the same color.
1-2 solid 8-blobs in left half of grid, leaving room to shift right.

On a 0-background grid, read the single connected color-2 source as exact offsets from its own top-left corner. Find the single solid color-3 target rectangle and stamp those offsets at the target's top-left corner in color 8 on an otherwise blank same-size output. Source orientation is preserved; unused target cells, the source, and the original target disappear.

0-bg grid (h~6-12, w~10-16) with: (a) ONE LARGE ASYMMETRIC OBJECT (4-8 cells) drawn from a hand-curated shape bank in some big_color; (b) 1-(big_size-2) ISOLATED SINGLETON CELLS as distractors in a different small_color. The big object is strictly larger than all singletons (size delta ≥2). The big object is horizontally ASYMMETRIC (so mirror differs from original). Objects are 4-conn isolated (no shared neighborhoods). Position bias varies (big_left/right/top/bottom_small or big_any). Rule: identify the LARGEST object (the big asymmetric one). NORMALIZE its cells. MIRROR HORIZONTALLY. COMPUTE the UNION (original cells ∪ mirrored cells). CROP to that union's BBOX. PAINT in the big object's color. Output: the cropped mirror-union subgrid. Singletons are discarded. Net: largest object gets symmetrized via horizontal mirror-union.

0-bg grid with 3-6 ISOLATED 4-connected components in distinct colors. Rule: extract all 4-connected components and sort by top-left (r1, c1). Output is an N×N MATRIX: out[i][j] = 1 if i == j; = 2 if shape[i] is rotation-equivalent to shape[j] under a 90° rotation; else 0. Net: encodes the pairwise rotation-equivalence relation among the components.
Use the gray legend's ordered colored cells to recolor ordered external objects of the outside-dominant source color.

A 0-background grid contains two differently colored hollow objects and optionally one larger solid distractor. Select the hollow object with the greatest number of colored cells, fill every enclosed zero region of that object with its own color, and leave every other object unchanged.

0-bg grid (size varies). THREE shapes in colors 1, 2 and 3, placed apart. They are defined over a shared k x k frame by a random per-cell MEMBERSHIP: each cell belongs to some subset of the three shapes, every shape spans the full frame (so the rule's independent normalization keeps them aligned), and at least one cell belongs to EXACTLY 2 shapes. Rule: normalize each color's cells to its bbox and output the cells that appear in exactly 2 of the 3 normalized sets, bbox-cropped, in COLOR 8 (cyan). The grid size, the three shapes and their positions all vary freely (was 3 fixed shapes + grid padding).
Use a two-count legend to select the component with matching graph-cluster size and degree.
Count each active color's monochromatic 8-connected components on a 7-background grid.  Emit a bottom-aligned histogram whose fixed columns are colors 5, 2, 8, 9, and 6.

A zero-background grid contains a source local frame marked by colors 2 (origin), 3 (+u), and 4 (+v), and a target frame marked analogously by 5, 6, and 7. Three or four cyan (8) source points lie within local radius 3. The output preserves the input and stamps into the target frame every cyan point whose source-local u coordinate is maximal. Coordinates are transferred frame-relatively, and every tie on the maximum-u tier is copied.

Preserve the input grid and fill with color 7 every 4-connected zero region that cannot reach the outer border. Border-connected zeros stay 0; wall color, wall component identity, and hole shape do not matter.

One connected color-8 source is rotated around the unique color-9 pivot. The unique control value 1,2,3,4 means identity, 90 degrees clockwise, 180 degrees, or 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Stamp the transformed cells as color 2 while preserving the source, control, pivot, and unrelated color-5/6/7 objects except where a red stamp overlaps them.
Control marker (4/6/8) selects boolean op (union/intersect/XOR) of color-2 and color-3 normalized templates; output painted color 9.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~9-14) with 2-3 RECTANGLE-CORNER PAIRS — for each rect: 2 same-color cells placed at DIAGONALLY OPPOSITE CORNERS of an implied axis-aligned rectangle (either main-diagonal (r0,c0)+(r1,c1) or anti-diagonal (r0,c1)+(r1,c0)). Each pair uses a DISTINCT color (2-3 colors total). Implied rects are 3..5 rows × 3..6 cols, with 1-cell buffer between rects (no overlap). Rule: for EACH PAIR of SAME-COLOR CELLS, INTERPRET them as DIAGONALLY OPPOSITE CORNERS of an axis-aligned rectangle. FILL the entire rectangle interior (all cells in (min_r..max_r) × (min_c..max_c)) with the pair's COLOR. Net: each diagonal corner pair becomes a filled rectangle in its color.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~8-11) containing a small GLYPH in 2 distinct non-bg colors: a connected 5-cell motif (L-tetromino-like) in colors[0] plus 1 isolated cell of colors[1] placed near it. The glyph is fully interior — ≥1 full blank row above/below AND ≥1 full blank col left/right. Rule: crop the grid to the bbox of all non-zero cells. Output = a small grid containing only the glyph.
Exact vertical green triplets have their centers recolored yellow.

A 0-background grid contains one or two single-orange target rows plus unchanged counterexamples: a partial row with multiple orange cells, a singleton non-orange row, and a row containing one orange cell together with another color. Only rows whose nonzero list is exactly [7] fill completely with orange.

Canonical-scale 0-background grids contain one irrelevant non-green corner marker plus green objects. All but one green object are the same shape under rotation/reflection; the unique dihedral class is recolored to 8. The outlier quadrant is scheduled independently of matched/exploratory roles. Three-demo default lessons retain a matched shape witness after any single query holdout.

Extract and remove the unique blue (1) template. For every gray connected component that is itself a hollow rectangular frame, read its local key: 2 keeps the template, 3 rotates it 90 degrees clockwise, 4 rotates it 180 degrees, and 5 rotates it 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Center the transformed copy in that frame's 5x5 interior and recolor it to the key color. Preserve all frames and keys. Touching frame borders merge into a non-frame component, so the selected oracle preserves that group without adding copies.

On a zero background, inspect each 4-connected cyan (8) component. Recolor it orange (7) exactly when it has three cells forming one straight horizontal or vertical line; leave every other cyan component unchanged.

0-bg square grid (h, w ~ 6-9) with: (a) THREE NON-0 TOP-ROW MARKERS at fixed column positions {1, w//2, w-2} in 3 distinct non-0 colors C0, C1, C2 drawn from a 4-color palette {1..9}; (b) TWO DISTRACTOR cells in COLOR C3 (the 4th palette color) — one at (h-1, 0) and one at (h//2, w-1). Distractors occupy lower rows / right edge where the rule will overwrite them. Rule (PROJECT TOP-ROW COLORS DOWN THEIR COLUMNS): for EACH non-0 cell (0, c) in the top row of color C: PAINT every cell (r, c) for r in 1..h-1 with COLOR C. Cells in columns without a top-row marker stay unchanged. Distractor cells in marker columns are OVERWRITTEN; distractors in non-marker columns stay. Net: vertical color stripes descend from each top-row marker, painting their columns downward; distractors outside marker columns remain as scattered noise.

0-bg grid (h, w~6-17) with 3-10 SINGLETON MARKER cells in COLORS {2, 3, 4} at interior positions (1..h-2, 1..w-2) so their keyed shape stays in-bounds. Each marker's footprint (keyed shape + 1-cell guard) doesn't overlap other markers' footprints. Rule (EXPAND EACH MARKER TO ITS KEYED SHAPE ON FRESH CANVAS): EMIT a FRESH h×w OUTPUT GRID. For EACH SINGLETON MARKER at (r, c) with color: color 2 → STAMP HORIZONTAL BAR cells (r, c-1), (r, c), (r, c+1); color 3 → STAMP VERTICAL BAR (r-1, c), (r, c), (r+1, c); color 4 → STAMP PLUS-5 (centered + 4 cardinals). All stamped cells keep the marker's color. OOB cells are clipped. Net: each color-2/3/4 singleton becomes its keyed shape on a fresh canvas.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~8-12 by ~9-12) with: (a) EXACTLY 2 color-9 (maroon) MARKER cells at distinct positions defining a translation vector (the markers are sorted by reading order, vector = second - first); (b) a connected SHAPE of 2-4 cells in some non-{0, 9} color near one of the markers. Translated copies must fit in-bounds. Rule: locate the 2 color-9 markers. Compute (dr, dc) = marker_2 - marker_1. For each non-0 non-9 cell, paint that cell color at original position AND at (r+dr, c+dc) on a fresh canvas. Markers do NOT appear in output.

0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-2 (red) BLOB and ONE color-3 (green) BLOB, built as rectangles minus their shared corner so their BBOXES overlap but their cells do not, plus a color-6 (magenta) decoy. Rule: intersect the red bbox with the green bbox and output a fresh grid with COLOR 8 (cyan) over that intersection rectangle. The grid size, the intersection rectangle, the blob extents and the decoy all vary freely (was a fixed 2-blob layout, ~12 distinct).
Copy every sparse nonzero singleton marker to its vertical-axis mirror position, keeping the original marker.
For each color occurring at two aligned endpoints, fill only the exact midpoint when the distance is even and the whole interior segment is zero; blocked or odd-distance pairs remain unchanged.
A top-left color swatch selects one separated component; crop that component and rotate the crop 90 degrees clockwise.
Centers of yellow diagonal X patterns are filled cyan.

A noisy non-zero background (one color, scattered with random 0s) plus a few rectangular all-0 holes punched in. Rule paints the MAXIMUM-AREA all-zero rectangle inscribed inside each 4-connected zero component (size ≥ 4) with color 2; ties (multiple equal max-area rects in one component) all get painted. Background and small/non-rectangular zero regions stay.
Sort nonzero component crops by (-size, top, left), then stack their raw bounding boxes left-to-right with one zero-column gap.
Preserve row 0 and column 0. For every interior (r,c), copy the left row key iff it equals the top column key; otherwise write background 0.
Small + large shapes; rule recolors large by small's shape kind.

2-3 distinct-area hollow color-8 frames and equally many distinct-color objects whose cell counts match those areas; center each matched object's bounding box in its frame and clip cells outside the interior.

On the original zero-background grid, scan each row and column independently. When a color occurs exactly twice on that line and every strictly interior cell is zero, fill the inclusive span with that color. Leave blocked and off-axis pairs unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains one blue seed, a seed-connected contact graph with explicit distance-0/1/2/3+ layers, and at least one detached object. Six replayable graph profiles cover long bent paths, branches, and a cycle. Component colors are assigned independently of distance, including the same input color at different output layers, while rotations, reflections, padding, palette size, and detached-object placement vary.

Color-7 (orange) background grid (size varies). A zero LOLLIPOP — a solid 3-4 cell rectangular body plus a thin 1-2 cell STEM at its facing-edge midpoint — points toward a color-5 (gray) object on one side. Rule: clear the stem (to 7) and paint the body edge facing the color-5 object with COLOR 6 (magenta). The grid size, orientation, body size, stem length and positions all vary freely (was a fixed 13x13 with fixed positions, ~12 distinct).
Sparse single-cell markers (1-3) at distinct corners or edges of grid.
0-bg 23x23 with ONE solid color-1 rectangle (2..3 interior color-4 ports) plus 17..47 scattered color-4 cells; the rule stamps the template's 1-cells wherever a D4 transform aligns >=2 ports.
Tiled tiles w/ separator; rule keeps unanimous, writes 1 for disagreements.

Build the intended output first: a corner triangle plus a connected multicolour pattern in the opposite quadrant. Remove the triangle and encode its corner, side length, and colour with isolated markers. The unique corner marker is intentionally not the majority marker colour.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~11-13) with EXACTLY 3 NON-TOUCHING CONNECTED BLOBS at hardcoded positions: (a) a 4-cell L-tetromino at (1, 1); (b) a 4-cell T-shape at (1, 5); (c) a 3-cell corner at (h-4, w-4). Each in a DISTINCT non-zero color from {2..9}. NOTE: shapes/positions hardcoded — diversity is intrinsic-low. Rule: identify each non-bg CONNECTED COMPONENT. SORT them by COLOR ASCENDING. For each blob, CROP to its bbox. CONCATENATE the cropped bboxes HORIZONTALLY from left to right with 1-COL GAPS between them. Output: max-height-among-blobs × sum-of-widths + gaps. Net: input has scattered colored blobs; output is them side-by-side sorted by color in a horizontal pack.
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.
Code at (0,0) ∈ 1..4 + asymmetric shape elsewhere.
Decode a 2x2 template id grid and a 2x2 transform code grid into a transformed gallery.

0-bg grid (size varies) with 1-3 color-8 PIVOTS, each with a nearby connected BLOB (a distinct color, within Manhattan distance 3 of its pivot, in its own reserved region so the nearest pivot is unambiguous and the rotation fits in-bounds). Rule: rotate each blob 90 degrees clockwise about its nearest pivot. The grid size, the pivot count, and each blob's shape/color/placement all vary freely (was a fixed 2-pivot layout, ~9 distinct).

On a square background-0 grid, inspect every cell together with its main-diagonal transpose partner. If the transposed cell is nonzero, write that value here; otherwise preserve the current value. One-sided cells are therefore copied to both positions, while different nonzero values across the diagonal swap positions.

FIXED-SIZE 15×15 grid divided into 9 sub-grids of 5×5 each (arranged 3×3). BG = bg_color drawn from {1..9} (non-zero) — the entire grid starts filled with bg. N_ZERO_SUBS ∈ 1-7 RANDOMLY-CHOSEN sub-grids (out of 9) each get N_PER_SUB ∈ 1-4 ZERO CELLS placed per ZERO_POSITIONS_KIND ∈ {scattered (random), cluster (Manhattan around random center), border (perimeter), diagonal (main diag), single (one random)}.
