Rule (OUTPUT A 3×3 GRID WHERE EACH CELL (SR, SC) IS 0 IF THE CORRESPONDING 5×5 SUB-GRID AT rows SR*5..SR*5+4, cols SC*5..SC*5+4 CONTAINS ANY 0; OTHERWISE THE CELL IS BG_COLOR): DETERMINE bg_color = g[0][0]. PRODUCE a 3×3 output. For sub (sr, sc) in 0..2 × 0..2: SCAN cells in rows sr*5..sr*5+4, cols sc*5..sc*5+4; IF any cell is 0: OUTPUT[sr][sc] = 0; ELSE: bg_color. Net: 15×15 summarized to 3×3 zero-presence matrix in bg color.
3 isolated components with 0, 1, and 2 enclosed holes; output packed left-to-right by ascending hole count.
Clear all nine lattice interiors, then copy the marker's 3x3 source pattern to the macro-cell encoded by the marker's local position.

Complete every same-color three-of-four 2x2 window in one simultaneous pass. Alternating canonical and witness profiles expose overlapping windows and distinguish one-pass behavior from iterative closure.

BG-color filled grid (h~11-15, w~11-16) with BG = 1st of 3 random distinct colors. Layout: (a) ONE PLUS_5 SHAPE (5-cell + sign) at random interior position (r0, c0) with 4 BODY cells in the BODY COLOR (2nd of palette); (b) ONE INDICATOR cell at one of the 4 cardinal PLUS_5 arms in the INDICATOR COLOR (3rd) — direction (up/down/left/right) determined by which arm cell is the indicator. Rule (SHOOT DOTTED TRAIL + EDGE BAR FROM INDICATOR OUTWARD): identify the BG, BODY, and INDICATOR colors. Locate the SHAPE and the INDICATOR's DIRECTION (which arm of the plus). PAINT a DOTTED TRAIL of INDICATOR color outward from the indicator cell in the direction (every other cell). At the GRID EDGE in that direction, PAINT a FULL EDGE BAR (row or column) in the INDICATOR color. Net: indicator's arm direction sends a dotted ray and a edge bar in indicator color.
A unique-color cell has exactly one open cardinal neighbour. Paint that singleton color through zero cells on the opposite ray, skipping the monochrome support shape rather than overwriting it.

Independently placed connected red/green shapes: any 7 selects their normalized intersection; otherwise XOR. Color 9 is irrelevant. Exact overlap, unequal areas, empty answers and tight cropping are supported.
Place exact horizontal dominoes with a zero cell to their right.

The blue(1) corner encodes 0/1/2/3 clockwise quarter-turns for the red(2) object. Ignore the differently coloured corner singleton, rotate and normalize the red object, crop it, and recolour it cyan(8).

Row 0 has color-1 column markers at some columns; column 0 has color-2 row markers at some rows. Rule paints color 4 at every (r, c) where row 0 has a 1 at column c AND column 0 has a 2 at row r. Markers preserved.
Grow marker-tipped color-1 columns upward from a marked horizontal bar: height three for color 8 and four for color 2.

A zero-background grid contains one solid color-1 rectangular panel. One cell in from its four corners are four distinct logical markers: three non-blue colors and blue (1).  The panel also contains a nontrivial one-color body motif, connected or fragmented.  Outside the panel, exactly three dots occupy three corners of a second bounding box; the missing fourth corner is interpreted as blue.  Match that four-corner key signature to the panel's logical corners and apply the corresponding one of all eight D4 symmetries to the entire panel, including its body motif.

Fixed 8×26 0-bg grid with: (a) 2 FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-5 (gray) DIVIDER COLUMNS at col 8 and col 17, splitting the grid into 3 PANELS of width 8 each; (b) TWO PANELS each contain a 3-COMPONENT CONTACT CHAIN (3 2×2 blocks at (3, 1), (3, 3), (3, 5)) — degree pattern [1, 1, 2]; (c) ONE PANEL (odd_panel ∈ 0..2) contains a 4-COMPONENT CHAIN drawn from 3 hardcoded shapes — degree pattern [1, 1, 2, 2]. Each panel uses 4 distinct colors from {1..9}\{0, 5}. Output uniq_out=3 (intrinsic — 3 odd chain shapes, output recolored to 8). Rule (FIND ODD PANEL BY DEGREE MULTISET, CROP & RECOLOR TO 8): identify the 3 PANELS (separated by 5-divs). For EACH PANEL, compute the contact-chain DEGREE MULTISET. Find the ODD panel (unique degree multiset). EMIT the ODD panel's cluster cropped and RECOLORED uniformly to COLOR 8. Net: odd-out panel's shape, in cyan.
Right-pack each row's nonzero values while preserving order.

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (2-4) NESTED concentric hollow FRAMES of distinct non-8 colors (gaps so no border crosses). Rule: paint color 2 on the cells strictly inside every frame -- the innermost frame's interior. The grid size, frame count, nested sizes/margins/colors and position vary freely (was a fixed nesting, ~20 distinct).

On background 0, take the bounding boxes of all color-2 cells and all color-3 cells. Emit a solid color-8 rectangle with the height and width of their nonempty intersection. Sparse points, relative box ownership, overlap aspect ratio, containment and canvas scale vary.

A 3..20 by 3..20 grid uses exactly 2..6 colors. Reverse every row left-to-right while keeping the row order unchanged. Normal lessons contain at least two asymmetric rows and are rejected when identity, vertical reflection, rotation, or transpose would give the same answer.

Fixed 7×11 0-bg grid laid out as TWO ROWS of THREE 3×3 PANELS each, separated by COLOR-9 LINES: (a) 9-DIVIDERS — full vertical column-9 at cols 3 and 7, full horizontal row-9 at row 3 (so the grid splits into a 2×3 panel grid with 9 borders); (b) TOP ROW (DEMO): three 3×3 panels showing _A, _B, and (_A op _B) where op is one of 5 fixed binary set ops {union, intersection, xor, A-B, B-A} chosen for this sample; (c) BOTTOM ROW (QUERY): bottom-left panel = _D (fixed mask), bottom-middle panel = _E (fixed mask), bottom-right panel is BLANK (the target). All masks painted in a single random non-{0,9} color drawn from {1..7}. Rule (INFER THE BINARY OCCUPANCY OP FROM TOP DEMO AND APPLY TO BOTTOM-LEFT × BOTTOM-MIDDLE INTO BOTTOM-RIGHT): read the TOP ROW to determine which of the 5 ops produces the third panel from the first two. APPLY that same op to the bottom-left and bottom-middle 3×3 occupancy masks. PAINT the resulting cells (in the same color) into the bottom-right 3×3 panel. Top row, dividers, and the two bottom operand panels stay unchanged. Net: the blank bottom-right panel gets filled with the inferred op of the two bottom operands.
Row 0 holds key colors; the 2 cells below each form its 2x1 stamp. Body cells (rows>=3) holding a key color are replaced by that key's stamp.
Row 0 holds per-column thresholds and column 0 per-row thresholds; the rule fills interior cell (r,c) with 8 where both thresholds are met (a staircase intersection of the two bars).

A zero-background grid contains exactly one full blue row or column and a connected shape using exactly two non-background colors on one side. Reflect the shape across the blue separator into the empty side. At the original location swap the shape's two colors; the reflected copy keeps the original colors and the separator remains blue.
Read 3 or 4 top-row legend colors; recolor equally many 1-components by minimum-column rank.
Manhattan nearest-seed fill in a 7-frame, with numeric color ties and preserved interior 7s.
Solid 3x3 block of mixed colors at interior position; rest empty.
Color-2 seeds get a Chebyshev-1 halo of 1; other non-zeros preserved.

Scatter two to seven cells of one nonzero color so their bounding box spans at least 3x3 without covering the whole canvas. Replace the sparse input by a solid rectangle filling that bounding box in the same color.

Count color-1 cells in row 0, rank eligible color-3 four-connected components by descending cell count then first occupied cell, and recolor rank k to 2. Default lessons interleave joint counterexamples with varied lawful shapes, including ties, singleton and endpoint ranks.
A 3x3 or 4x4 separator lattice contains one or more adjacent 2x2 tile blocks with exactly one missing patterned tile; the rule fills each missing tile by the appropriate horizontal/vertical flip.
Repeat the first two color-major dots as alternating row or column phases, using period twice the selected coordinate separation.

0-bg grid (h~6-10, w~9-14) with: (a) EXACTLY ONE FULL-HEIGHT color-9 (maroon) DIVIDER COLUMN at some column gc placed in the right half of the grid (gc ∈ [w//2..w-2]); (b) scattered non-{0, 9} content cells in 2-3 distinct colors placed ONLY on the LEFT side of the divider (cols 0..gc-1), at random row positions. The RIGHT side (cols gc+1..w-1) is initially EMPTY. Rule: for each cell (r, c) on the LEFT side with non-zero non-9 color k, compute its MIRROR column mc = 2*gc - c. If (r, mc) is in bounds, PAINT (r, mc) with color k. The 9-divider stays; original left cells stay. Net: the maroon column acts as a vertical mirror, reflecting all left-side content into the right half.

0-bg grid (h~5-8, w~6-9) with EXACTLY FIVE NON-ZERO CELLS placed at fixed positions: (0, 1), (1, w-2), (h//2, 2), (h-2, w//2), (h-1, w-1). Colors are drawn from a palette of 3 distinct non-0 values C0, C1, C2 from {1..9} and assigned: position (0, 1) = C0 (the FIRST color in row-major scan order), positions (1, w-2) and (h-2, w//2) = C1, positions (h//2, 2) and (h-1, w-1) = C2. So C0 appears once and C1, C2 each appear twice — 5 cells total. Rule (COUNT ALL NONZERO CELLS, OUTPUT A ROW REPEATING THE FIRST-SEEN COLOR THAT MANY TIMES): COUNT n = total number of non-zero cells in the input. SCAN row-major to find the FIRST non-zero cell's color C0. PRODUCE a 1-row × n output where every cell holds COLOR C0. Net: input has scattered colors; output is a horizontal bar of length n=count, all in the first-scanned color. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=9): output is one of 9 possible {color × length=5} bars.
Outline in red the first non-red component touching the first red marker, clearing markers, interiors, and distractors.

A 0-background grid contains 4-6 isolated monochrome polyominoes. Objects are compared after rotation but not reflection.  Sorted by top-left position, the output relation matrix uses 9 on the diagonal, then 6/4/2/0 for same-shape+same-color / same-shape-only / same-color-only / neither.
Rank three 4-connected components by exposed-edge perimeter; stable row-major ties; recolor 2,3,4.

A 6..16 by 6..16 zero-background grid contains 2..8 blue(1) anchor cells. Anchors may be interior or lie on any outer edge. For every original blue cell, the rule paints its in-bounds cardinal neighbors: up=2, left=7, right=6, down=8, while retaining the input elsewhere.

Find every 5/6/7 L-frame, express nearby 8-cells in that frame's ordered local coordinates, and select the sole candidate whose signature occurs once. Return a 1xN strip with 8 at its row-major candidate index. The 2/3/4 frame is a non-authoritative distractor whose motif varies independently across the curriculum.
skills: candidate comparison, canonical local signatures, symbolic output

summary: WALL-BG (color 5) grid (h~7-16, w~8-18) with: (a) ONE OPEN CORRIDOR of color-0 cells carved through the wall in one of 6 SHAPES (straight_h / straight_v / rect / L / T / rect_with_branch). The corridor may have non-trivial geometry including dead-end branches; (b) TWO ENDPOINT MARKERS — COLOR 2 (start) at one corridor end; COLOR 3 (goal) at the opposite end. Start and goal are 4-connectable through the open corridor (D = shortest-path distance < ∞). Rule (OUTPUT THE UNION OF ALL SHORTEST PATHS FROM START TO GOAL, IN COLOR 8 ON A FRESH BLANK GRID): RUN BFS from the COLOR-2 START over 4-conn non-5 cells to get d_start[r, c]. RUN BFS from the COLOR-3 GOAL similarly to get d_goal[r, c]. Let D = d_start[goal] (the shortest-path distance). For EACH cell (r, c): IF d_start[r, c] + d_goal[r, c] == D, it lies on SOME shortest path → PAINT it COLOR 8 (cyan) in the output. ELSE: output is bg-0. The walls, original start/goal colors, and dead-end branches off the shortest path are DROPPED. Net: the union of all shortest paths from start to goal appears as a cyan blob on a blank grid.

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (3-4) nested concentric color-4 frames and a control cell (1 or 2). Rule: outer = frames[control-1], inner = frames[control]; fill the ring between them (strictly inside outer, not inside inner) with 8. The grid size, frames and control value vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

A small 0-bg grid with 2-4 maroon-9 markers in row 0 and one single-color connected body object below. The marker count k drives horizontal repetition of the cropped body with one blank spacer column.

Find all green (3) cells, fill their complete axis-aligned bounding box with green on a fresh same-sized black grid, and erase every other color. A four-slot lesson schedule includes canonical two-color anchors, split-extrema marker layouts, and a dominant non-green decoy outside the green box so all-nonzero and modal-color shortcuts are observable.

On a 0-background grid, color 5 cells are inert blockers and every other nonzero color marks exactly two endpoints in different rows and columns. For each endpoint pair, try the two possible L-shaped Manhattan paths. Exactly one route is clear of blockers and other endpoints in generated lessons; paint that route in the endpoint color and never connect color 5.

0-bg grid (h~6-10, w~9-14) with 2-3 PAIRS of SAME-COLOR CELLS, each pair on a DIAGONAL (|dr| == |dc| ≥ 2), direction drawn from {nw_se, ne_sw, mixed}. Each pair color is DISTINCT from a palette (warm/cool/broad/primary). Pairs don't share cells. Rule (CONNECT DIAGONAL SAME-COLOR PAIRS WITH DIAGONAL LINES): For EACH COLOR C with EXACTLY 2 cells (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) where |r2-r1| == |c2-c1| (diagonal): PAINT every cell along the DIAGONAL LINE between them in color C (Bresenham/step-1 diagonal). Endpoints stay. Net: each diagonal endpoint pair becomes a solid colored diagonal line.

On a zero background, fill with orange (7) every zero that has red (2) immediately to its left and right in the same row. Leave vertical 2-0-2 patterns, adjacent red pairs, isolated red cells, and horizontal gaps of two or more zeros unchanged.
A colored motif is placed away from the outer border and then cropped to content.

Read and clear the top-left control: 1 recolors hollow rectangular 7-frames to 8, while 2 recolors filled 7-rectangles. Generate 2..4 separate objects with both kinds, varied sizes and positions, and larger-solid counterexamples.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 ISOLATED motifs in distinct non-{0,5} colors AND a few color-5 (gray) BLOCKER cells scattered around. Motifs and blockers are separated. Rule: collect blockers (color-5 cells). Extract non-5 components, sort by leftmost column ascending. Start with a fresh empty grid containing only the blockers. For each component in left-to-right order: slide its cells LEFT (dr=0, dc=-1) until they hit a blocker, an already-placed cell, or the grid's left edge. Paint the slid cells with the component's color. Net: gravity-left with both stationary blockers (5) and stacking dynamic blockers from earlier-placed objects.

Odd-height 0-background grids contain a centered full row of maroon 9s. Two to four source colors occupy 4..12 cells above the separator, with witness cells at both vertical extremes. The unchanged rule reflects the entire top half into the bottom half in reversed row order.

Canonical-scale 9x18..21 zero-background input. Three hollow 5x5 color-9 frames occupy rows 4..8 and form a left-to-right library; each 3x3 interior is a full-bbox 5..7-cell colored payload, and color 9 may also be payload. Rows 0/1 contain 3..4 aligned command pairs: row 0 is selector 1..3 and row 1 is rotation code 1=id, 2=90CW, 3=180, 4=90CCW. Execute commands left-to-right and hstack the transformed cropped payloads with a one-column zero gap, vertically centered.

Extract the color-1 template. Replace each code-grid cell by a recolored template transform: 2 = identity, 3 = 90° clockwise, 4 = 180°, and 5 = horizontal flip; preserve zero code gaps and center tiles with one-cell spacing.

Connect every nonzero color that appears exactly twice when its two cells share a row or column. Fill only the inclusive segment between the two endpoints. Process colors in ascending order, so the numerically larger color wins at an interior crossing. Diagonal pairs and aligned triples remain unchanged.

FIXED 10×w grid (w ∈ [13, 15]) with: (a) COLOR-1 (blue) TEMPLATE — a fixed 5-cell shape {(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1), (2, 2)} painted at (1, 1); (b) MATCHING CANDIDATE — same shape transformed by one of 8 DIHEDRAL TRANSFORMS (rotations + reflections), in a CANDIDATE color from {2..9} (excluding 1), placed at (1, match_left) where match_left is chosen to fit; (c) TWO DISTRACTOR shapes with DIFFERENT normalized shapes (different dihedral class), each in a DISTINCT color, placed at bottom-left and bottom-right. Rule (FIND THE CANDIDATE MATCHING THE TEMPLATE UP TO DIHEDRAL SYMMETRY, CROP, RECOLOR TO 8): identify the COLOR-1 TEMPLATE. For EACH non-1 candidate: check if its normalized shape matches any of the 8 dihedral variants of the template's normalized shape. Find the UNIQUE match. CROP it to its BBOX. RECOLOR ALL its cells to COLOR 8 (cyan). Output is the cropped matching candidate in cyan. Flag: INTRINSIC-LOW — fixed template × 8 variants → 4 distinct cropped shapes.

On a 0-background grid, each color occurring exactly twice is joined inclusively when its two cells share a row or column. Singleton colors, three-cell colors, and diagonal pairs are unchanged controls.
(0,0)=rotation count + color-9 pivot + a small motif in some other color near the pivot.
Move one connected nonzero object straight down by a single shared offset until its lowest cell touches the bottom row; preserve shape and colors.

0-bg grid (size varies). Row 0 is a control row: (0,0)=1-based panel selector, (0,1)=transform command (0..5). The body (rows 1+) holds N single-color connected motif panels separated by blank columns. Rule: take the selected panel, crop to content, apply the command. Panel count/shapes/sizes, selector and command vary while preserving the canonical one-color-per-panel distribution.

Transpose a sparse square grid across the main diagonal. Normal inputs contain 3-8 uniquely colored cells with at most one cell per row and column; moving cells may lie above, below, or on both sides of the diagonal, and an optional single diagonal cell is a fixed point.
Two separate connected shapes in colors 2 and 3 are translated to a common top-left origin; output paints their normalized intersection in 8.

0-bg grid assembled from N=3-4 SIDE-BY-SIDE PANELS (each h×w ~ 5-6 × 5-6) separated by FULL COLOR-9 (maroon) COLUMNS of width 1. Each panel is filled with cells in a DISTINCT panel color (2, 3, 4, …): 3-5 SHARED cells appear in ≥2 panels (threshold-2 overlap positions), plus 3 panel-unique cells. Rule (MAJORITY-VOTE MASK AT THRESHOLD 2): identify the N PANELS (separated by 9-rows). For EACH INTERIOR (r, c), COUNT how many PANELS have a non-0 cell at (r, c). EMIT an h×w MASK where out[r][c] = 8 (cyan) if COUNT ≥ 2, else 0. Net: cells lit in ≥2 panels form an 8-mask.
skills: panel voting, coordinate-wise counting, same-size synthesis

summary: Rows with nonzero cells contain a strict majority color that controls the row.
Variable same-colored blobs docked beneath matching top-row marker cells.
Key at (0,0) + a key-color blob away from corner + 1 distractor.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~7-9) with 2-4 ACTIVE COLUMNS, each containing exactly TWO same-color cells separated by EXACTLY 2 rows (cells at (r, c) and (r+2, c)), with the middle cell (r+1, c) initially 0. Different active columns use distinct colors. Rule: for each column with a same-color vertical pair exactly 2 rows apart, fill the MIDDLE cell (r+1, c) with the same color. Net: each vertical pair becomes a solid 3-cell column segment.

A 6-9 by 8-10 zero-background grid contains 4-8 colored source cells strictly above the horizontal midline.  The source uses two or three nonzero colors, reaches both the top row and the row immediately above the midline, and leaves the entire lower half empty.  Copy each nonzero cell (r,c) to (h-1-r,c) with the same color while preserving the source.
Iterate over multiple multicolor templates; same-count standalone anchor objects receive translated template fragments, while unique source colors move.

0-bg grid (size varies). The upper-left 3x3 is a TEMPLATE: a color-2 center with a random set of color-3 ARM cells among the 8 surrounding cells. Elsewhere sit 1-4 single color-2 ANCHOR cells (clear of the template and of each other so their stamps don't overlap). Rule: stamp the template centered on each anchor, painting every empty cell under a template ARM with that arm's color; the anchor stays color 2. The grid size, the template arm pattern, and the anchor count / positions all vary freely (was a fixed plus template + 2 fixed anchors).

A full red top row and a shallow red band contain several blank, shape-specific sockets. Three or four disconnected gray polyominoes are bottom-anchored below. The rule clears the gray sources, processes them largest-first, and paints each normalized shape blue in its first supported blank placement.

A dense gray-5 surround encloses a large irregular zero field containing one marker color. Replace exactly the zero cells whose row parity and column parity both match the marker; preserve gray blockers, the marker, and every other zero cell.
Cells of {2,3,8}; rule paints color-paired rings around each.

A zero-background grid contains 2-3 distinctly colored connected objects. Each object color also appears exactly once in the top row and once in the left column. Move each object's unchanged crop so its bounding box is centered at the intersection of the matching color's row and column markers; erase the markers and original locations.

A zero-background grid contains 1-4 colored single-cell centers. Treat all nonzero cells as one seed set. Paint cyan(8) exactly where the minimum Manhattan distance to that set is 2, on a fresh zero canvas. Input center colors are irrelevant and centers disappear. Close-center lessons expose the union-distance behavior: a cell at distance 2 from one center is suppressed when it lies within distance 0 or 1 of another.
Isolated interior seeds bloom into radius-one plus signs.

0-bg grid (h~5-12, w~6-14) with: (a) 2-4 COLOR-8 (cyan) CELLS all in a SINGLE COLUMN col8 at DISTINCT ROWS (excluding row2); (b) 2-4 COLOR-2 (red) CELLS all in a SINGLE ROW row2 at DISTINCT COLUMNS (excluding col8). Positions for col8 and row2 are biased center/spread/edge. No other non-bg cells; no color-4 anywhere. Rule (CROSS COMPLETION + INTERSECTION COLOR-4): identify the COLOR-8 COLUMN and COLOR-2 ROW. PAINT the ENTIRE col8 column with COLOR 8 (every cell in that column, top to bottom). PAINT the ENTIRE row2 row with COLOR 2 (every cell in that row, left to right). At the INTERSECTION cell (row2, col8), PAINT with COLOR 4 (yellow). Net: scattered evidence in one row and one column → full cross with yellow intersection.
On a zero-background grid with 3-6 separated, uniquely colored objects, copy exactly the objects whose bounding boxes touch one grid border. Erase interior objects and corner/multi-border objects.

0-bg grid (size varies). K (2-8) connected color-1 BLOBS with distinct bounding-box areas, scattered apart. Rule: rank the color-1 blobs by bbox area (descending) and recolor them on a blank grid -- largest 2, next 3, next 4, ... The grid size, blob count, blob shapes/sizes and positions vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~17 distinct).
Scatter upper-half colored cells for horizontal midline reflection.
Exactly four same-color cells occupy the corners of an interior rectangle; the rule fills that rectangle solid.
Vertical 5-divider; output highlights cells where left/right halves differ.
2x2 quadrant holes filled with the color missing from each quadrant set.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with 3-4 distinct non-zero COLORS, each appearing in exactly 2 isolated cells (8-conn non-adjacent). Rule: for each color with exactly 2 cells, compute a STAIRCASE PATH between them (monotone diagonal/L-step path). Collect all path cells across all color pairs. For each output cell (r, c), encode the count of how many path cells map to (r, c) via s17b-encode-count — a per-cell count map painted with specific colors per count level.
Color-5 frames; fill complete square bbox interiors with color 2.

On a zero-background grid with gray(5) wall objects and one checkpoint each of colors 2,3,4,7, find shortest 4-neighbor paths 2->3, 3->4, and 4->7 through non-wall cells. Resolve equal paths in up/down/left/right BFS order, then paint every interior route cell cyan(8), even when that cell was another checkpoint.

Input is (N+1) × (M+1). Row 0 cols 1..M hold M col-key colors; col 0 rows 1..N hold N row-key colors. (0,0) is 0. Rule emits a 2N × 2M grid: at output (r, c), use row-key[r//2] if (r+c) is even, else col-key[c//2]. The output is a 2-cell-thick checkerboard mixing the row and col keys.

A 0-background grid contains 2..5 independent vertical endpoint pairs. A fillable pair is exactly two equal non-zero cells in one column with one or more zeros between them; the output fills that inclusive span in the endpoint color. Optional negative-control columns contain either different endpoint colors or a non-zero blocker and therefore remain unchanged.

Three strictly nested, disconnected color-4 rectangular frames plus a singleton control marker and an irrelevant singleton distractor. Rank the frames by area, largest first; control 1/2/3 selects outer/middle/inner. Fill zero cells inside the selected frame with 8, excluding the complete bounding box of the next inner frame when one exists.

Extract the isolated same-color objects in top-left order and compare every ordered pair. Emit 1 on the diagonal, 8 for the same exact row/column symmetry class, 4 for equal enclosed-hole count when symmetry differs, and 0 otherwise. Four scheduled profiles distinguish exact reflection class, hole-region count, relation precedence, and top-left object order from six canonical-fitting or otherwise plausible shortcut families.

Green objects on black: recolor only complete rectangular frames from 3 to 7. Every three-example schedule includes a canonical small scene, a large open non-frame, and complementary hollow decoys, so size, bbox, generic-hole, closed-loop, and rectangular-hole shortcuts are falsified.

Count 8-connected monochrome components separately for each nonzero color. Choose the unique color with the most components, take its first object in reading order, and copy that color's cells from the object's top-left 3x3 window into a 3x3 output; every other output cell is zero.

Grid (h, w~3-14) FULLY COLORED with one of 9 TEXTURE patterns (noise/sparse/blob/stripes/gradient/checkerboard/frame/ring/plus) drawn from a palette of 2-6 non-0 colors, plus 0-0.05 noise overlay. Any remaining 0-cells are filled with palette[0]; if monochrome after that, two corners are forced to different colors. Every cell is guaranteed non-zero. Rule (ADD MIRRORED 1-CELL BORDER): EMIT an (h+2)×(w+2) OUTPUT. PASTE the input at rows 1..h, cols 1..w. For BORDER rows/cols: TOP row (row 0) cols 1..w mirror ROW 0 of input. BOTTOM row mirrors row h-1. LEFT col mirrors col 0. RIGHT col mirrors col w-1. The 4 CORNERS stay 0. Net: input grows by 1-cell mirrored frame around all sides, corners left as 0.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-13) with 2-4 ISOLATED color-2 (red) T-TETROMINOES — each is a 4-cell T shape in one of 4 orientations (T-up, T-down, T-left, T-right). T's spaced apart with ≥3-cell distance. Rule: detect each color-2 component as a T-tetromino. Find its 2×3 or 3×2 BOUNDING BOX. FILL the entire bbox with color 3 (green), replacing the original red T cells. Net: every red T expands into a solid green rectangle matching its bbox.

Exactly one full vertical color-9 guide and a 3..8-cell, 1..3-color source wholly on one side. Preserve the input and copy every source cell to its equal-distance mirror. A balanced four-profile lesson schedule covers centered/off-center guides, left/right sources, connected/split sources, and guide-adjacent/gapped sources.

0-bg grid (h ~ source_rows + tail_rows + repeat_rows, w~5-10) with three row bands stacked top-to-bottom: (a) SOURCE BAND (top source_rows ∈ {2..4}): each row's col 0 = GRAY (5) marker; cols 1..w-1 hold a scattered non-{0,5} colored PATTERN drawn by one of 6 SOURCE_LAYOUTS (scattered / blob / diagonal / stripes / left_biased / right_biased) using a 2-5 color palette and fill density 0.3-0.7; each source row has ≥1 non-gray colored cell; (b) TAIL BAND (next tail_rows ∈ {1..3}): more sparse colored cells (no gray markers); (c) REPEAT BAND (final repeat_rows ∈ {4..10}): ALL-BG ZEROS, ready to receive the cycled pattern. Rule (CYCLICALLY REPEAT SOURCE ROWS — WITH GRAY MARKERS ERASED — INTO THE REPEAT BAND): the gray-marked top rows define a SOURCE CYCLE. for EACH ROW r in the REPEAT BAND (below the source+tail band): COPY source row (r mod source_rows) into row r, ERASING the col-0 gray-5 marker (set to 0). The colored non-gray pattern is replicated cyclically. Source and tail bands stay unchanged. Net: the bottom repeat band fills with cyclic copies of the gray-marked source rows minus the markers.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-11, w ∈ 8-12, by difficulty) with: (a) ONE COLOR-1 MARKER at (r1, c1) drawn from r1 ∈ 0-1, c1 ∈ 0-2 (top-left region); (b) ONE COLOR-2 MARKER at (r2, c2) drawn from r2 ∈ 2-3, c2 ∈ 3-4 (offset toward bottom-right) — these define a translation vector (dr, dc) = (r2-r1, c2-c1); (c) ONE CONNECTED MOTIF — a 3-5 cell motif built via _build_motif random walk, painted in a non-{0,1,2} color drawn from {3..9}, placed in the LOWER HALF (rows ≥ h//2). Rule (COMPUTE TRANSLATION VECTOR FROM COLOR-1 TO COLOR-2 MARKER; FOR EACH NON-{0,1,2} CELL, PAINT THE SAME COLOR AT (R + DR, C + DC); ORIGINAL MOTIF AND MARKERS PRESERVED): LOCATE markers; COMPUTE v = marker2 - marker1. For EACH non-{0,1,2} cell at (r, c) with color k: PAINT g[r+v.r][c+v.c] = k (if in-bounds). Net: motif is duplicated by the marker vector to a new position; original kept.
One to three separate arbitrary-colour rectangular frames each contain one differently coloured seed; fill each entire interior with its own seed colour.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~12-16) with 2-3 SOLID RECTANGLES drawn from a dims bank {(2,1),(1,3),(2,2),(2,3),(3,3),(3,4),(4,3)} — each rect has a DISTINCT cell count (e.g., 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12). Each rect uses a DISTINCT color from random_palette. Rects are non-overlapping with 1-cell padding. Rule (SORT BY SIZE ASC, HORIZONTAL GALLERY PACK): identify all SOLID rectangles. SORT by SIZE ASCENDING (color ASC as tiebreak). CROP each to its BBOX. PASTE the crops HORIZONTALLY with 1-COL GAPS in sorted order. Output WIDTH = sum of widths + gaps; HEIGHT = MAX height. Net: solid rects sorted small→large, horizontally packed.
2-3 L-trominoes in distinct colors, plus distractor singletons.

Count blue cells in row 0, crop the one connected nonzero prototype below the header, and repeat the entire colored crop horizontally that many times with one blank column between copies. The body may contain blue, multiple colors, holes, and arbitrary padding. Generated K is 1..4.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~8-10) with 2-3 HORIZONTAL SOLID RUNS — each run is a single horizontal sequence of length L (3..min(w, 6)) of identical non-0 color C, placed at a unique row chosen from h rows without repetition, starting at a random column c0 in [0, w-L]. Each run uses a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {2..9}. No two runs share a row. Outside cells are bg-0. Rule (DASH EACH HORIZONTAL SOLID RUN — KEEP EVEN-INDEXED CELLS, ZERO OUT ODD-INDEXED CELLS): For EACH horizontal contiguous run of identical non-0 color C spanning columns [c0..c0+L-1] in a row: KEEP the cells at even RUN-RELATIVE positions (offset 0, 2, 4, ...) with their color C; SET cells at odd RUN-RELATIVE positions (offset 1, 3, 5, ...) to bg-0. Other rows and outside cells stay unchanged. Net: each solid horizontal stripe becomes a 'dashed' pattern of alternating color/zero cells starting with color at the run's left endpoint.

0-bg grid containing exactly THREE separated same-color components with strictly distinct cardinal perimeters. Rule: rank components by perimeter from smallest to largest, then recolor them 2, 4, and 8 respectively.

skills: panel splitting, overlap detection, same-size output
summary: Split two equal panels at the vertical 9 divider and paint color 8 only where both aligned panel cells are nonzero.
Mirror each guided multicolor component from its modal-payload denser side across the rounded yellow-guide axis.

A multi-cell template blob anchored by a color-9 cell, plus several isolated single marker cells in distinct colors. The rule stamps the template shape at each marker, recolored to the marker's color.

skills: exact matching, window geometry, rectangular border rendering
summary: A color-9 divider separates a cropped monochrome template from a board. Find every original-orientation placement matching the template's nonzero cells (template zeroes are wildcards), then outline each matched bounding window in cyan(8) on a board-sized zero grid.

0-bg grid with several isolated color-2 cells scattered (≥3 cells), each separated by ≥2 Manhattan from another so their diagonal-painting regions don't overlap-conflict. Rule: for each color-2 cell at (r, c), paint the 4 diagonal neighbors at (r±1, c±1) with color 6 IF in-bounds AND currently 0. Color-2 cells preserved; non-bg cells already in place are preserved.

Color-5 walls bound four-connected regions. A regular 2-3 by 2-3 lattice is refined by 1-3 local wall segments, so some nominal cells split into smaller regions as in the canonical examples. Each region contains 0-4 color-2 keys. The whole non-wall region, including its keys, becomes 0 for zero keys, 8 for an odd count, or 7 for a positive even count. Profiles deliberately include 3- and 4-key regions to separate parity from the canonical-compatible one-versus-many shortcut.

Every non-zero input cell is a colored seed. Preserve each seed and paint its up, down, left, and right neighbours with that seed's color; cells outside the grid are simply clipped and all other background stays 0. Generated lessons contain two or three separated, distinctly colored seeds. A four-profile schedule alternates interior canonical anchors with mixed boundary scenes, so every three demonstrations show a complete five-cell plus, a one-edge clip, and a two-edge corner clip.
Replace every same-colour 4-connected component by the same-colour outline of its own axis-aligned bounding box on a fresh zero background.
Every gray 3x3 ring receives a cyan center cell.

0-bg grid (h~11-13, w~12-14) with TOP-ROW anchor cells and 3-4 BODY COMPONENTS: (a) cell (0, 0) = k (1-indexed selector in [1..n]); (b) cell (0, w-2) = t1 (transform code 1-4); (c) cell (0, w-1) = t2 (second transform code 1-4); (d) remaining row 0 = 0; (e) BODY (rows 1..h-1) has n (3-4) isolated 4-conn components, each in a DISTINCT color from {2..9} with STRICTLY DISTINCT SIZES from {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}. Rule (RANKED COMPONENT + COMPOSED TRANSFORM): SORT body components by (AREA DESC, COLOR ASC). PICK the k-th component in sorted order. CROP to its BBOX. APPLY transform t1 then t2 (transform codes: 1=rotate CW 90°, 2=rotate 180°, 3=flip-LR, 4=flip-UD). Output: the transformed crop. Net: k picks ranked blob, t1∘t2 applies composed geometric transform.

A colour-keyed library of shapes above a last-row token sequence of (key, transform 1-7, recolour) triplets; the rule decodes each token (look up, transform, recolour) and galleries them. Library, token count and codes vary.

0-bg grid (h, w ~8-13) with 2-5 ACTIVE ROWS, each containing EXACTLY TWO color-2 (red) ENDPOINT cells at columns c1 and c2 (c2 ≥ c1 + 2), with the span between them all 0. Different rows use distinct column-pairs. Other rows are entirely 0. Rule: for each row with exactly two red endpoints, paint the cells BETWEEN them (strictly inside, not endpoints) with color 3 (green). Net: each red pair becomes red endpoints + green bridge segment between.
Color 7 is an irregular target mask; 3-5 other colors are sparse marker sets whose horizontal closures compete by overlap, extra cells, then color.

A 7..10 by 8..10 zero-background grid contains exactly two distinct nonzero colors, each in exactly two cells at different rows and columns. Each same-color pair is the pair of opposite corners of a rectangle; the two rectangle bounding boxes are disjoint and at least one rectangle has a nonempty interior.  On a fresh zero grid of the same size, draw each rectangle's four border edges in its pair color and leave every interior cell zero.
Cell (0,0) keys a boolean op (1=union, 2=intersection, 3=xor); two shapes sharing a common core (plus per-shape extras) are combined by that op and painted 8. Key, core shape and extras vary.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~9-11). ROW 0 contains k=2..3 color-1 (blue) cells at random distinct columns (the COUNT/target-size). BODY (rows 1..h-1) contains EXACTLY 2 color-3 (green) BLOBS of DISTINCT sizes (one with 2 cells, one with 3 cells), positioned at fixed slots (rows 2, cols 1 and 6). EXACTLY ONE color-2 (red) ANCHOR cell at fixed (5, 5) with room for the translated blob. Rule: count color-1 cells in row 0 → k. Find the green BLOB whose cell count equals k. TRANSLATE that blob so its bbox top-left lies at the red anchor's position. PAINT the translated cells with color 8 (cyan) on the existing grid. Original green blobs, the red anchor, and row-0 count stay. Net: the count selects the matching blob; output adds a cyan copy at the anchor.

A single color-2 start cell on the left and one or more non-zero stopper cells (e.g., color 5 to the right) on a 0-bg grid with sparse decorations. Rule: starting from the 2-cell, fire a rightward ray painting color 2 along the path. When the ray hits any non-{0,2} cell, the path branches perpendicular (up and down) and continues; further branches stop at the next obstacle. All traversed cells are painted 2 (decorations stay).

Repeat the bottom guide row into every output row. Preserve every gray 5 at its input position. When a gray 5 lies above a bottom-row red 2, clear that red column above the blocker and continue it one cell right from the top through the row below the blocker. Gray cells outside red marker columns are preserved distractors and do not bend a column.
Endpoints of exact length-4 cyan line segments are recolored red.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-11, w ∈ 11-13) with: N ∈ 3-4 DISTINCT-COLOR BLOBS, each a 3-5 cell irregular blob built via grow_blob random walk, painted in DISTINCT colors drawn from {5,6,7,8,9}, placed at non-overlapping positions where each blob has a STRICTLY NEAREST border (no tie among top, bottom, left, right) — _nearest_unique check enforces this. Rule (FOR EACH BLOB, COMPUTE THE DISTANCE FROM ITS BBOX TO EACH OF THE 4 GRID BORDERS (TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT); RECOLOR THE BLOB BY THE NEAREST BORDER: TOP→COLOR 1, BOTTOM→COLOR 2, LEFT→COLOR 3, RIGHT→COLOR 4; TIES KEEP ORIGINAL COLOR): For EACH blob with bbox (r1, c1, r2, c2): COMPUTE distances (r1, h-1-r2, c1, w-1-c2). FIND the UNIQUE minimum (top=0, bottom=1, left=2, right=3). RECOLOR every cell of the blob by that border index (0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→4). On tie: keep original color. Net: blobs recolored by which grid border is closest.

A color-1 template motif plus several color-5 rectangular frames, each with one non-{0,5} interior marker. Rule: clear each marker and stamp the template into that frame's interior, recolored to the marker's color.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~9-13) with 2-4 ACTIVE ROWS, each containing: (a) ONE COLOR-9 (maroon) ANCHOR cell at column p (3..w-3); (b) 1-3 COLORED MARKER cells on the LEFT side of the anchor (cols max(0, p-3) to p-1) in random colors from {1..8}. Non-active rows are 0. Rule (MIRROR LEFT-SIDE MARKERS ACROSS 9-ANCHOR): For EACH ROW r containing a COLOR-9 ANCHOR at col p: For EACH non-0 non-9 cell at (r, c) with c < p, PAINT the MIRROR position (r, 2p - c) with the same color (if in-bounds). The anchor stays. Source cells stay. Net: each row with a 9-anchor reflects its left-side markers to the right side.

Wall-geodesic Voronoi with 4-6 seed cells, 2-4 seed colors, varied barriers, different-color ties, and repeated-color nearest-seed witnesses. Two repeat-color profiles in each four-draw cycle support query rotations.

Several HOLLOW color-8 frames with DISTINCT interior dimensions, plus detached inserts in distinct non-{0,8} colors; each insert's bbox matches exactly one frame's interior. Rule: move each insert into its matching frame's interior; the original insert position is cleared.
Place same-color endpoint pairs in separate columns for vertical interval filling.
Mirror eligible cells left of the first full-height color-5 guide, preserving originals and clipping off-canvas targets.

Every active input column contains 4 or 9 scattered colored cells. Its total determines a 2- or 3-layer odd-width pyramid; its bottom-to-top distinct-color order and exact color counts determine complete consecutive layers. The output moves those layers to the grid bottom, centered on the same column. Canvas and structure vary independently; every nine consecutive samples cover all four canvases and all five structures, including both 5+4 and 8+1 grouped-layer partitions.
For each nonzero color, find its four cells at the corners of one axis-aligned rectangle and fill that entire rectangle with the same color.  Treat colors independently.

A color-7 outer frame encloses a color-5 guillotine wall network. One or two spanning backbone walls form two or three strips; compartment-local perpendicular branches split selected strips, producing 3-6 rectangular rooms and genuine T-junctions. Every seeded room has exactly one distinct non-{0,5,7} seed; either all rooms are seeded or exactly one is seedless. Fill each seeded room's zeros with its seed color, preserving walls, seeds, and the seedless room.

0-bg grid (size varies) with 2-5 ARROWS (colors 1/2/3/4 = up/right/down/left) at random positions, plus 1-4 COLOR-5 (gray) WALL segments. Rule: each arrow shoots a ray in its direction, painting empty cells COLOR 7 (orange) until it hits a 5-wall or the grid edge (rays pass through other arrows). The grid size, the arrows' positions/directions and the walls all vary freely (was a fixed full-column wall + 3 fixed arrows, ~9 distinct).

A zero-background grid has a contiguous row-0 script and one connected, single-color template below a blank separator row. The fixed script legend is 1=clockwise quarter-turn, 2=half-turn, 3=left-right reflection, 4=transpose. Apply codes cumulatively to the current cropped template. Pack the resulting states left-to-right, top-aligned, with one blank column between states. Codes 5..7 supported by Racket are outside this sampler's declared 1..4 vocabulary. Templates use colors 5..9. Default three-demo lessons interleave asymmetric full-legend witnesses with canonical-profile and symmetric/rectangular examples.

A canonical-size zero-background grid contains one or two isolated, monochrome, hollow right-slanting parallelograms. For each object, keep the cells on its bounding-box bottom row or rightmost column fixed; shift every other object cell one column right.

A 6-30 by 6-30 zero-background grid contains exactly one monochrome, 4-connected blob of 2-6 cells and exactly one color-9 marker. Crop the blob to its tight bounding box, clear the canvas, and paste the crop with its top-left corner at the marker. Marker direction varies across all four diagonal quadrants.

A hollow rectangular frame is the template; several smaller solid rectangles are fillers whose total area equals the frame's interior. Output is the frame's bbox with the fillers packed into the hole.

0-bg grid: n_panels (4-6) of 4-WIDE x h-HEIGHT (panel_h 4..5), separated by FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-9 (maroon) DIVIDER COLUMNS, each panel holding a SMALL MOTIF (1-3 cells) in a color from {2..7}. Rule (VERIFIED from the canonical Racket): crop the joint bounding box of ALL motif cells, remove the color-9 dividers (-> 0), and STAMP that motif-collage crop at each former divider-column position. It does NOT identify or emit a matching motif pair — see the docstring MISMATCH flag (the canonical rule and the generator's 'find-pair' design disagree; likely a bad conversion).
Hollow 5x5 8-frames; each interior's majority non-8 color read into a 1xK row (K=frame count), ordered by column then row.
Add green only at empty fourth corners supported by three original red corners, simultaneously.

On a sparse 0-background grid, every nonzero color appears at exactly two axis-aligned endpoints. Fill the inclusive horizontal or vertical span between each pair with its endpoint color. Perpendicular spans may cross; row-major first-appearance order determines which later color occupies a blank crossing cell.
Copy each nonzero cell into its blank transposed partner across the main diagonal, while preserving originals, diagonal cells, and already occupied transpose pairs.

Preserve odd-area same-color 4-connected components; erase even-area components on background 0. Inputs include singletons, areas 1..9, repeated colors, same-color diagonal contact and cross-color edge contact.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~13-15) with: (a) FOR EACH of colors {2, 3, 4}, EXACTLY 2 CELLS placed at DISTINCT ROWS AND DISTINCT COLUMNS (i.e., diagonal corners of a rectangle); (b) 1-4 DECOY cells in colors from {1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} at random empty positions. Each color may overlap rectangles but rectangle-outline paths can clobber decor — that's fine. Rule (PAINT RECT OUTLINES BETWEEN DIAGONAL CORNER PAIRS): For EACH color C ∈ {2, 3, 4}: if C has exactly 2 cells at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) with r1 ≠ r2 AND c1 ≠ c2, PAINT the RECTANGLE OUTLINE through those 2 corners in color C — outline = top row, bottom row, left col, right col of the bbox (min, max)(rows/cols). Interior of the rect stays. Other colors (non-{2, 3, 4}) untouched. Net: each diagonal pair in 2/3/4 becomes a hollow rectangle outline.
One solid 4-connected object on background 0 is replaced by its same-colour 4-neighbour boundary; interior cells become 0.

On a zero-background grid, recolor a blue(1) cell red(2) exactly when its up, down, left, and right neighbours are all blue. Generated scenes contain one or two separated blue line crosses with varied arm lengths, plus a straight-line or T-junction decoy that must remain unchanged.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-10) with: (a) ROW 0 holds K NON-ZERO MARKER cells (K=1..3) at random distinct columns in COLOR-2 (red); (b) BELOW ROW 1 (in rows ≥2) ONE NON-RECTANGULAR BLOB of 3-5 cells in a random color from {3..8}. The blob is non-rectangular (bbox area > cell count) so rotation changes its shape. Output uniq_out=35 (intrinsic — K mod 4 × few blobs × colors normalizes). Rule (ROTATE BLOB BY K MOD 4): COUNT K = number of non-zero cells in row 0. COMPUTE rotation = K mod 4 (0=identity, 1=90°CW, 2=180°, 3=270°CW). CROP the BLOB to its BBOX. APPLY the rotation. EMIT the rotated crop as output. Net: row-0 count drives the blob's rotation.
Several motifs in distinct colors; the rule outputs ONE selected motif (most holes, then most mirror-symmetry axes, then largest area, then top-left), cropped to its bbox and recolored to 8.

Three or four separated solid rectangular patches use cyan 8 with green 3 overlays. Ignore patches taller than eight rows; among the remaining patches crop the one with the most green cells, breaking ties by smaller bounding-box area and then top-left position. Default scenes include a taller higher-green decoy, larger-area and denser valid decoys, and alternating equal-count area-tie witnesses.
Scale a separate marker's binary shape independently in height and width to fill a hollow rectangular frame interior.
2-3 columns each have exactly 2 cells of one color (all-0 between).
Recolor every four-connected orange-7 component touching both the top and left borders to cyan 8; preserve all other cells.
Keep each color-6 4-connected component only when an occupied cell, not merely its bounding box, lies on the main diagonal; recolor kept cells 2.
Treat every nonzero cell as a seed, grow its clipped orthogonal plus mask, count cells in the union of all masks, and output one row of that many 8s.
Exactly one marker each of colors 2, 4, and 3. Connect 2 to 4 and then 4 to 3 with gray paths that move horizontally first and vertically second; preserve all marker colors.

0-bg grid (size varies). A color-2 (red) shape, a color-3 (green) shape, and a color-5 rectangular FRAME. Rule: stamp the XOR (symmetric difference) of the normalized red and green shapes in color 8 at the top-left of the frame's interior. The grid size, red/green shapes (hence their XOR), frame size and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~23 distinct).
Bridge midpoint-aligned same-color object boxes across their full gap and overlap interior, unless a third same-color box blocks the bridge.

6..12 by 6..12 zero-background grids with 2..5 sparse nonzero seeds. A deterministic five-scene curriculum alternates canonical interior color-3 seeds, non-cyan edge seeds, mixed-color interior seeds with overlapping X footprints, non-cyan corner seeds, and cyan interior seeds. Every nonzero cell grows into a cyan diagonal X on a fresh grid; out-of-bounds cells are clipped and overlaps are unioned.

0-bg grid (h, w~13-17) with: (a) CONTROL CELL at (0, 0) in color ∈ {1, 2, 3} encoding a BAND INDEX; (b) THREE NESTED COLOR-5 (gray) RECTANGULAR FRAMES drawn at offsets (0, 2, 4) from a centered anchor — outermost (frame 0), middle (frame 1, 2 cells inward), innermost (frame 2, 4 cells inward). Rule (CONTROL 1-3 SELECTS WHICH GRAY NESTED-FRAME BAND BECOMES CYAN): READ the CONTROL cell's color k ∈ {1, 2, 3}. The 3 nested frames define 3 BANDS: BAND-1 (ring between frame 0 and 1), BAND-2 (ring between 1 and 2), BAND-3 (interior inside frame 2). PAINT every bg-0 cell in the k-th BAND with COLOR 8 (cyan). Gray frames and control cell stay. Net: control color picks one nested ring to fill cyan. Flag: HARDCODED-LOW DIVERSITY — 3 controls × ~9 grid sizes → ~26 distinct.

A 12-14 square color-0 canvas contains three to five separated solid color-1 rectangles, always including at least one square, one wider rectangle, and one taller rectangle.  Most draws also contain one separated non-rectangular color-1 component, which is a decisive negative witness: it must remain color 1.  One four-cell non-rectangular color-6 distractor is always preserved.  Every fourth sample is a linked canonical anchor with exactly four solid blue rectangles and no blue non-rectangle.  The canonical Racket rule is the sole output authority: solid blue squares become 8, wider rectangles 2, taller rectangles 3, and every other cell is unchanged.

Scan rows top-to-bottom. Skip empty rows; from each non-empty row take the first non-zero cell from the left and append that color as one row of a one-column output. Mixed-row witnesses distinguish first non-zero from modal/last-row-color shortcuts, and repeated heads prove duplicate output values are preserved.
3-4 motifs in distinct colors at distinct positions.

0-bg grid (size varies). 2-4 connected color-2 (red) shapes sharing a common CORE (each = core + its own disjoint extras), plus one color-9 (maroon) ANCHOR cell. Rule: intersect the normalized color-2 shapes (the core) and stamp it at the anchor in color 3 (green) on a blank grid. The grid size, the core, each shape's extras and the anchor position all vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~13 distinct).
Read the four corner cells as transform commands, crop the non-corner motif, transform it once per corner in reading order, and pack the four variants into a 2-by-2 output.

A 0-background grid contains 2..14 blue (1) markers.  The three-slot default curriculum cycles through canonical interior-separated layouts, boundary markers whose orange X is clipped, and nearby markers whose orange X stamps overlap by union.  The rule emits a fresh same-size grid and paints color 7 at each marker and its four in-bounds diagonal neighbours.

h×w grid (h, w~3-6) with foreground non-bg cells in some PALETTE (warm/cool/broad/small) arranged in a LAYOUT (scattered/blob/diag/row/col/checker/frame). Column 0 is conditionally all-zero (col0_has_nonzero=false) or has at least one non-zero. ≥2 fg cells and ≥1 bg cell guaranteed; color 8 is never used in input (rule writes 8 for output). Rule (TASK-SPECIFIC OUTPUT NORMALIZATION): if column 0 of input has ANY NON-ZERO, produce a 2w-wide output with the LEFT HALF showing color-8 wherever the input has a 0 (a mask of zeros), and the RIGHT HALF being the original grid. ELSE (col 0 is all-zero), produce a 2w-wide output with the LEFT HALF being the original grid and the RIGHT HALF being the horizontal mirror. Net: input grid is doubled horizontally with color-8 mask of bg cells or its mirror, depending on col 0 contents.

Find each 4-connected monochrome nonzero component. Keep the entire component exactly when at least one cell touches the outer grid border; erase every fully interior component to background 0. Four-example teaching windows include canonical 7x7 anchors, non-top edge-only border objects, multiple kept objects, opposite kept/erased fates for one color, and both size-order directions so color, count, corner, side, and size shortcuts do not identify the query answer.
Read the selector color at (0,0), exclude that key cell, and crop the original grid to the joint bbox of every remaining selector-colored cell.

Use the color at (0,0) as a selector.  For each other 4-connected object of that color, fill its bounding-box interior only when the object is exactly a complete rectangular perimeter; preserve all nonselected objects and malformed or merged selector-colored objects.

Select the first singleton control in priority order 2,3,4,6; apply identity, clockwise rotation, top-bottom reflection, or 180-degree rotation to the largest blue component; translate it by vector 7->9; and stamp its empty in-bounds landing cells cyan.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-10) with: (a) TWO MULTI-CELL BLOBS — an L-tromino [(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)] in upper-left area (rows 0-1, cols 0-2) in palette[0]; and a 2-cell horizontal bar [(0,0),(0,1)] in middle-right area (rows 2-4, cols w-4..w-3) in palette[1]; (b) TWO ISOLATED SINGLETONS — one in the bottom-left corner (row h-1, cols 0-1) in palette[2]; another in the middle-left interior (rows 2..h-3, cols 2-3) in palette[3]. The 4 colors are distinct non-{0} values from {2..9}. Rule (KEEP ONLY NON-BG CELLS THAT HAVE AT LEAST ONE SAME-COLOR CARDINAL NEIGHBOR — ERASE SINGLETONS): for EACH cell (r, c) with value v ≠ 0: CHECK its 4 CARDINAL NEIGHBORS. IF at least ONE neighbor also = v: KEEP the cell (stays color v). IF NONE of the neighbors = v (cell is isolated by color): SET the cell to bg-0. Net: multi-cell same-color blobs survive intact; isolated singletons are erased to bg-0.

Color-5 (gray) WALL-FILLED grid (h~7-12, w~8-14) with a CORRIDOR of passable 0-cells carved through, with one COLOR-2 (red) START cell at one end and one COLOR-3 (green) GOAL cell at the other end. Corridor topology varies: straight horizontal, straight vertical, L-bend (h-then-v or v-then-h), or 2-route rectangle PERIMETER (two equally-short paths around a box). Passable cells are 0, 2, or 3; walls are 5. Rule: find ALL SHORTEST PATHS from the red start to the green goal through passable cells (4-connectivity, walls 5 block). Compute the INTERSECTION — every cell that lies on EVERY shortest path. PAINT those cells with COLOR 8 (cyan). Red start and green goal stay. For single-corridor topologies the whole path becomes cyan; for rectangle-perimeter topology only the start/goal corners (intersection cells) get painted. Net: intersection of all shortest paths highlighted in cyan.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE color-8 (cyan) ANCHOR, ONE color-9 (maroon) TARGET, and a MOTIF of 3-7 cells in colors from {1..7}. Rule: translate the motif by (target - anchor) and paint it on a fresh grid (anchor + target consumed). The motif is placed so its translation lands fully in-bounds. The grid size, the motif shape/colors, and the anchor/target positions (hence the vector) all vary freely (was a fixed motif + fixed anchor/target, ~9 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~9-11) with: 2-3 cells of color 2 (red), 2-3 cells of color 3 (green), and 1-3 scattered distractor cells (colors {1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9}). All cells are placed at random distinct positions. Rule: produce a FRESH same-shape grid where each cell (r, c) is 8 (cyan) if: (a) input[r][c] == 0; (b) there exists a 2-cell at (r, c2) on the same row with all cells strictly between c and c2 in that row equal to 0 (horizontal LoS to a red); (c) there exists a 3-cell at (r2, c) on the same column with all cells strictly between r and r2 equal to 0 (vertical LoS to a green). Else cell is 0. The 2/3/distractors do NOT appear in the output.

A single magenta(6) marker in column 0 selects one nonempty payload row. Output that row without the marker column. Every generated row is nonempty and payload rows are pairwise distinct, so the marker is the only stable selector.

A binary 0/1 grid has a least row period of 2..6 with at least two repeated-row cues. Continue that period to h + floor(h/2) rows and replace every 1 by 2 throughout the output. First-row repetitions inside a motif and either top-left color are lawful. Default lessons interleave canonical-size, broad, and randomized distinguishing inputs.

Dense field (h 12..22, w 12..22) of noise colors 0/1/8 with magenta-6 cells at ~6..16% and exactly one 3x3 template (yellow-4 body + magenta-6 markers, 3..5 markers, yellows spanning the bbox; yellow appears nowhere else). Rule: for every dihedral orientation of the template, stamp its yellow cells wherever its magenta pattern matches grid 6s (>=2 hits, no conflicts; bottom/right 1-cell overhang allowed). The generator plants 1..3 guaranteed match windows in the noise so the rule always fires; emergent noise matches add more, matching the canonical 3..18 stamped-cell range.

Ignore non-square distractors, count monochrome solid-square components by side length, conditionally remove one excess smallest square as the size key, then emit count-layered top-left nested-square tally glyphs.

0-bg grid (h ~ 11-19, w ~ 10-22) with FG CELLS in one color drawn from {1..9}: (a) several CONNECTED CLUSTERS of varying shape (rect / L_shape / blob / cross / line_h / line_v) and size (small / medium / large / mixed) — each cluster's cells are 8-connected with at least one same-color neighbor; (b) many ISOLATED SINGLETON CELLS placed via one of 5 LAYOUTS (random / corners / row / column / scattered) at positions where their 8-neighborhood is clear of any other fg cells (so they're truly isolated). All fg cells share the same color. Rule (ERASE ISOLATED SAME-COLOR PIXELS — KEEP ONLY CELLS WITH AN 8-CONNECTED SAME-COLOR NEIGHBOR): for EACH fg CELL (r, c): CHECK its 8 SURROUNDING NEIGHBORS. IF at least ONE neighbor has the SAME COLOR: KEEP the cell. IF NO neighbor has the same color (isolated singleton): SET the cell to bg-0. Bg-0 cells stay 0. Net: connected clusters survive intact; isolated singletons are erased to bg-0.

On a 0-background grid, inspect each row independently. If and only if a row has exactly two nonzero cells, paint the inclusive interval between them cyan (8) on a fresh same-size output; every other row remains zero. The default three-slot schedule includes strict canonical anchors, mixed-color qualifying pairs, and singleton/triple/four-marker decoys.

0-bg grid with: (a) ONE color-1 (blue) SRC anchor cell; (b) ONE color-2 (red) DST anchor cell at a different position; (c) one TEMPLATE blob of 2-5 cells in color 3, placed adjacent to or around the src anchor. Rule: compute translation vector (dr, dc) = (dst.r - src.r, dst.c - src.c). Translate the 3-blob by (dr, dc). On a fresh 0-canvas, paint the translated blob in color 2. Anchors are removed in output. Blob's translated position fits in-bounds.

0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~12-15) with: (a) ONE COLOR-9 (maroon) ORIGIN cell at interior position (nine_r, nine_c) (within rows 2-4, cols 2-4); (b) 2-3 COLOR-7 (orange) CELLS placed at fixed OFFSETS from the origin (one of 4 templates: small L-shapes / corners). These define the TEMPLATE; (c) 1-3 single ANCHOR cells with values from {2, 3, 4, 5} (the rotation codes: 2=0°, 3=90°, 4=180°, 5=270°), placed at scattered interior positions with sufficient margin from the origin and each other so rotated stamps stay in-bounds. Rule: extract the TEMPLATE as the color-7 offsets relative to the COLOR-9 origin. For EACH ANCHOR cell with rotation code v, ROTATE the template's offsets by v's rotation (2=0°, 3=cw90°, 4=180°, 5=ccw90°), then STAMP COLOR-7 cells at (anchor + rotated_offset) positions. The anchor stays, the origin stays, and original templates stay. Net: each rotation anchor pulls a rotated copy of the template into its position in orange.
Single-color motif stamped with rotations and reflection into a larger square.
Move an arbitrary connected object crop to the unique color-9 marker.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~14-20 by ~14-20) with TWO non-overlapping regions of distinct non-zero colors: a BIG region (color A, high density, larger bbox, more cells) and a SMALL minority region (color B, fewer cells). Regions placed in separate quadrants/halves of the grid with ≥1 empty row/col between them. Color B's cell count is STRICTLY less than color A's. Rule: scan colors 1-9. Find the non-zero color with the FEWEST cells (the minority). Compute its bbox. Crop the input to that bbox. Output: cropped subgrid, preserving both majority and minority cells inside the bbox.

Rows contain independently placed color-8 walls and ordered colored pebbles.  Within every maximal non-wall segment, the canonical rule packs pebbles rightward while preserving their left-to-right order.

A color-0 grid contains two or three same-color endpoint pairs on opposite corners of length-3 diagonals.  The output fills each blank midpoint with the endpoint color.  Scheduled control scenes additionally contain one axis-aligned distance-2 pair, one length-5 diagonal pair, and one length-3 diagonal whose midpoint is already occupied; those controls remain unchanged and distinguish the exact local rule from broader rivals.

Fixed 13×15 grid. Background is a 2-COLOR CHECKERBOARD with even color (e) at (r%2==0 or c%2==0) and odd color (o) at (r%2==1 and c%2==1). The pattern is DISRUPTED by: (a) a RECTANGULAR FRAME (drawn in some FRAME color) at fixed coords for one of two ORIENTATIONS (horizontal: (3..8, 3..12) or vertical: (2..11, 4..10)); (b) TWO CONTENT BLOCKS in distinct colors A and B placed at fixed offsets relative to the frame. Rule: RESTORE the checkerboard everywhere EXCEPT INSIDE the frame, where the two content blocks are kept CENTERED. The frame border stays. Net: input has a noisy backdrop with a framed layout; output restores the checkerboard outside the frame, centering content blocks inside it.

Three non-background colors appear on a zero background with pairwise distinct global cell counts. Count cells of each color, choose the unique most-frequent color, then output a fresh same-size zero grid whose bottom row begins at column 0 with a bar in that color; the bar length is exactly the winning global count. Generated lessons vary winner color rank, count gap, and local connectivity so color identity, first occurrence, and largest connected component cannot replace global counting.

For each separated nonzero connected component, erase all of its cells and paint exactly the four corners of that component's bounding box in its original color. Components are determined by connectivity rather than color, including when two separated components deliberately share a color.
3*bh × 3*bw grid; rule emits 3×3 of first non-zero per sub-block.
Apply row-0 transform codes 1..5 to a base motif and pack the pieces.

Find the equally spaced green guide cells. Infer their positive row/column interval, erase the red 3x3 ring, and translate every red cell forward by one guide interval while leaving the green guide unchanged.

On a 0-background grid, select the largest blue (1) object and the largest red (2) object. Normalize each selected object's cells to its own top-left bbox origin, take their symmetric difference, tightly crop that mask, and paint its occupied cells cyan (8). Smaller same-color objects and the singleton unrelated-color distractor are ignored.
Exact horizontal length-2 dominoes are extended one cell to the right (same color). Singletons, vertical pairs, and longer runs are not extended.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-13) with: (a) A SINGLETON MARKER — single cell at (1, w-2) (top-right interior) in a chosen shared color C from {2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9}; (b) A LARGER OBJECT of the SAME color C — a 4-5 cell shape drawn from a shape bank, placed near the bottom-left at anchor (h-5, 1); (c) A DISTRACTOR L-tromino of COLOR 5 at fixed top-left (rows 2-3, cols 2-3) in a different color. Rule (CROP LARGER OBJECT MATCHING THE MARKER COLOR, CENTER ON BLANK CANVAS OF ORIGINAL SIZE): find the SINGLETON MARKER (a single cell) — its color is C. Find the LARGER OBJECT (≥2 cells) sharing color C (4-connected component). EXTRACT its bbox crop, then PAINT it CENTERED on a fresh blank canvas of the ORIGINAL h × w dimensions (centered at ((h - bbox_h)//2, (w - bbox_w)//2)). Marker and distractor objects are discarded. Net: only the matching larger object survives, centered on a blank canvas.
Two or three isolated colored dominoes complete the 2x2 square extending downward from a horizontal domino or rightward from a vertical domino.
Complete nested square rings from corner colors and optional paired side-color witnesses.

0-bg grid (h, w ~10-13) with 3 SEPARATED 4-cell objects in distinct colors at fixed origins (1, 1), (1, w-5), (h-5, 2). Each object is an L-tetromino-style shape (3-4 cells) with asymmetric bbox. Rule: for each 4-conn non-bg object: crop to its BBOX (bbox_h × bbox_w). Rotate the cropped subgrid 90° CLOCKWISE. Paste the rotated subgrid back at the SAME origin (top-left of original bbox) — note rotated bbox is bbox_w × bbox_h, may extend differently than original. Net: each object appears rotated 90° CW in place at its bbox top-left anchor.
Use the left prototype-to-swatch legend to recolor every shape-matching neutral target on the right of the central blank separator.

≥3 4-connected color-2 (red) blobs of strictly distinct sizes, plus optional non-2 decoration cells. Rule sorts the 2-blobs by (cell count DESC, then top-left ASC) and recolors the second blob's cells to color 8. Other blobs (largest, 3rd+) stay 2.

0-background grid (h in [6, 14], w in [6, 16]) holding 1-4 FULLY-FILLED 3x3 OBJECTS that each use EXACTLY TWO colors in an interlocking pattern (checkerboard, row/column stripes, center or column markers, random mixes), plus 0-2 NEGATIVE objects (solid 1-color blocks or 3-color blocks). Objects stay 8-separated. Rule (SWAP THE TWO COLORS OF EVERY 2-COLOR OBJECT): within every 8-connected non-bg object that uses exactly two distinct colors, swap those two colors; objects with 1 or 3+ colors stay unchanged. Net: the two-color blocks invert their pattern; solid and 3+ color blocks are untouched.
Crop to non-zero content, then return its upper-left floor-half in each dimension.
Find color-6 objects that occupy three cells in a 2x2 box and recolor them to 1.

Two to four rigid colored pieces fall straight down around one fixed vertical color-8 wall; canonical-scale anchors occur in every difficulty band, and ordinary draws include wall support plus floor or piece-on-piece support.

A source panel and several candidate panels (color-9 columns between); exactly one candidate is an identical copy of the source, the rest have a different cell count. Rule: recolour the matching candidate to color 8. Source shape and candidate count vary.
skills: rotation matching, panel selection, normalized comparison

summary: Sparse non-zero cells occupy the left side of a zero-background grid; on odd widths the center column may also contain a source.  Widths may be even (midline between columns) or odd (center-column axis).  The rule preserves every source and copies its color to column w-1-c, completing left/right mirror symmetry.  Off-axis mirror destinations are blank in the input.
Infer a unique nonidentity D4 transform from two 3x3 panels, apply it to a query panel, then merge with a fourth panel using color 9 exactly for unequal nonzero overlaps.
Independently recolor the 2nd, 4th, ... nonzero cell on every constant-(row-column) diagonal to yellow.

Split the 5-row input into 5-column panels separated by one zero column, crop each panel to its nonzero bounding box, and binarize nonzero cells. Return an N×N matrix with 8 on the diagonal and 2 off diagonal exactly when the destination panel is the left/right or up/down reflection of the source panel; all other off-diagonal cells are 0. Ordinary draws contain a real reflection pair plus a 90-degree rotation decoy, and larger draws also contain an exact-copy decoy whose off-diagonal relation remains 0 for asymmetric motifs.

A zero-background grid contains an arbitrary connected blue source shape, one control singleton (4 identity, 6 clockwise rotation, 7 top/bottom reflection), and red/green singleton markers defining a nonzero vector. Normalize the transformed source and stamp it in cyan from red along the red-to-green vector until the next complete copy leaves the grid.

Vertically-assembled grid with 3 SAME-SIZE PANELS (each panel h × w, h ∈ {5, 6} and w ∈ {5, 6}) separated by FULL-WIDTH COLOR-9 SEPARATOR ROWS. Layout: (a) PANEL 0 at top, painted in COLOR 2 (red); (b) PANEL 1 in middle, COLOR 3 (green); (c) PANEL 2 at bottom, COLOR 4 (yellow). The occupancy patterns (which cells are non-bg) are: ONE REPEATED PATTERN (6 cells) appears in EXACTLY 2 of the 3 panels (the pair chosen via repeat_pair ∈ {'01', '02', '12'}); the THIRD ODD PANEL has a DIFFERENT pattern (5 cells, ensured distinct from the repeated set). Each panel's occupied cells use that panel's designated color. Rule (FIND THE REPEATED OCCUPANCY PATTERN AMONG 3 PANELS, OUTPUT IT RECOLORED TO 8): COMPUTE each panel's OCCUPANCY MASK (which cells are non-0, ignoring color). FIND the TWO panels that share the SAME occupancy mask. OUTPUT is a single panel of dimensions h × w where the SHARED OCCUPANCY CELLS are painted COLOR 8 (cyan) and all other cells are bg-0. The third panel and the 9-dividers are discarded. Net: the repeated-pattern panel emerges as a single cyan-occupancy panel.
skills: exact panel comparison, majority agreement, same-size output

summary: A zero-background grid contains 1-5 separated colored singleton seeds. Preserve every seed and paint each original empty cell at Manhattan distance exactly two with that seed's color. Seeds are processed row-major and only still-empty output cells are painted. The ordinary teaching grammar keeps closed radius-two influence zones disjoint.

Use cyan panel masks on a uniform-divider lattice. Exact outside-mask matches select target panel rows and columns for a Cartesian-product stamp; when no such match exists, a full cyan row invokes a same-column modal-uniform-row fallback with an exactly-one-hit guard.

Extract the three to five isolated same-colour motifs. Crop each motif; rotate a crop 90° clockwise only when it is taller than wide. Sort the resulting crops by motif size descending and colour ascending, then pack them left-to-right with one zero column between adjacent crops.

Two separated color-5 framed rooms contain one or two distinct-colored seeds each. Zero cells take the color of their unique nearest seed by four-neighbour shortest-path distance through non-wall cells; ties stay zero. Some lessons include an attached interior wall that makes geodesic distance disagree with a Manhattan shortcut.
Redraw every filled two-color object as a dominant-color frame with a rare-color edge-distance X and centered extension.
11x11 lattice; replicate the unique 3x3 block without cyan(8).

0-bg grid (h~8-13, w~9-15) framed by a COLOR-5 (gray) OUTER WALL BORDER (entire row 0, row h-1, col 0, col w-1 painted 5). Inside: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) SEED at (r, mid-2); (b) ONE COLOR-3 (green) SEED at (r, mid+2) where r is a random interior row and mid = w // 2 (seeds separated by 4 cols). Otherwise the interior is empty. Rule: APPLY WALL-AWARE BFS from EACH SEED through bg cells (4-conn, walls 5 block). Compute distance to RED and distance to GREEN for every open cell. PARTITION cells: closer to RED → paint red color; closer to GREEN → green color; TIE → tie marker color. Seeds and walls stay. Net: maze interior gets partitioned by BFS distance to seeds, with ties marked separately.
Reflect nonzero cells across the main diagonal; a reflected nonzero value replaces its counterpart.

Exactly one red start and one green goal lie on a 6-30 square/rectangular zero canvas with optional gray walls. The canonical BFS paints only the interior of a shortest wall-avoiding orthogonal path cyan. Four scheduled profiles guarantee obstacle-relevant teaching support in every lesson.
Read row 0 as adjacent old->new color pairs, drop the legend row, and replace each body source color once while preserving unmapped cells.

Canonical 3x3 grid where MOST cells share one non-{0,5} color (the MODE, 50-85% density) — call it keep. Remaining cells are 1-3 distractor colors (chosen from {1..9} ∖ {0, 5, keep}), optionally including bg(0). Rule: compute mode = most-frequent non-zero color in the input. For every cell (r, c): if cell value == mode, keep it; otherwise (including bg cells) → set to 5 (gray). Output: same shape as input, with the dominant color preserved and everything else recolored gray.

A sparse grid contains gray(5) cells on both alternating column parities. Recolor only the gray cells in columns with c % 2 == (width + 1) % 2 to green(3); preserve gray cells in the other columns and preserve every non-gray cell. Ordinary lessons alternate even and odd widths so the right-edge anchoring, rather than a fixed left-column parity, is visible.

0-bg grid with exactly two color-2 cells at diagonal corners of a non-degenerate rectangle, exactly two color-1 cells at diagonal corners of another non-degenerate rectangle, and 0..2 decoration cells in colors not in {0, 1, 2, 3, 8}. Rule: for color 2, paint the bbox border (perimeter) of its two cells with color 3. For color 1, paint the bbox border with color 8. Markers themselves become part of the painted perimeter; interior bbox cells stay unchanged (0 or decoration color). Other cells preserved.

A zero-background grid contains 2-5 disjoint hollow blue rectangular frames, each strictly inside the previous frame with at least one blank cell of separation. Recolor the outermost frame 2, the next frame 3, then 4, 5, and 6 moving inward, leaving every other cell 0.

Keep the input grid. Read command 1 or 2 at (0,0). In row-major first-appearance order, connect every color that has exactly two cells with an L path of that color: command 1 uses horizontal then vertical; command 2 uses vertical then horizontal. Singleton colors stay unchanged, and later pair colors win where paths overlap.

A black 8..10 by 11..13 grid contains exactly three mutually separated green(3) four-connected components with strictly distinct cell counts. Sort them by cell count and recolor smallest->red(2), middle->yellow(4), largest->magenta(6), preserving shape, position, and grid dimensions.

Filler-framed grid split into two touching rectangular containers (colors BG1/BG2), each holding a solid blob of the shared inner color IN with a margin. Each blob carries 1-3 tab dominoes: IN protrusions into the background or background dents into the blob, on straight edge segments away from corners. Rule: every tab is recolored to the OTHER container's background color. Both containers always carry at least one tab (the rule needs both backgrounds among the tab pairs).

Cap each straight, monochrome 4-connected yellow component of exactly three cells with color 8 at each independently available endpoint. Nonzero and off-grid cap positions, other colors, and other components stay unchanged. Ordinary scenes supply contrasting distractors.
Row 0 has key-color markers; rule crops the bbox of all matching-color blobs in the body, discarding distractors and row 0.

A color-0 grid contains 2..3 independent horizontal endpoint pairs. A fillable row has exactly two equal non-zero cells with at least one zero between them; the output fills that inclusive row interval in the endpoint color.  Optional negative-control rows contain two different endpoint colors, equal endpoints plus a different-color blocker, or three separated same-color markers; all controls remain unchanged.
Sort three separated objects by their left edge, transpose each cropped object, then stack the pieces vertically with one blank row between them.
Preserve each row's column-zero shift header and move every nonzero content cell right by that row's header value, clipping cells that leave the grid.

A 0-background 10..16 x 13..20 grid contains one or two separated color-1 rectangular frames. Each frame has exactly one token in {2,3,4} and one seed in {5,6,7,8,9}. Token 2 paints a plus, token 3 an X, and token 4 a full 3x3 footprint in the seed color, clipped to the strict frame interior. Default scenes use two frames with distinct tokens and seed colors and mix centered and clipped footprints.
Mark each blank cell that lies on every shortest non-wall path from the red start to the green goal.

0-bg grid split by one full color-9 divider column. The left panel holds a cropped color-3 template with internal 0 wildcard cells; the right board contains 2-4 separated same-orientation occurrences of that template. Rule: crop the left template, scan the board with zeros as wildcards, and render the union of matched occupied template cells as color 8 on a board-sized output.
skills: exact motif search, union of matched cells, same-size blank output

summary: Use a 0/4 reference panel for output positions and ordered special rows, and a colored template panel for line colors plus special fill variants.
One or two exact hollow rectangular frames recolor every connected object strictly inside them; same-color objects outside remain unchanged.
20-tall grid with 3 indicators + uniform-color rect at row 7+.

0-bg grid (panel_h~4-5) structured as 5-6 vertical PANELS each of width 4, separated by full-height COLOR-9 DIVIDER columns of width 1. Each panel contains a small CONNECTED MOTIF (1-3 cells) in some non-{0, 9} color, placed at a random position within the 4×panel_h area. Different panels may use different colors. Rule: identify all panels. FIND the PAIR of panels whose motifs MATCH (identical shape + color or shape modulo rotation/reflection). Output: the matched panel's 4×panel_h subgrid. Net: gallery 'find the matching pair' selector — output the duplicated panel.
skills: panel parsing, histogram comparison, candidate selection

summary: 0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~8-12) with 2-4 VERTICAL RUNS of COLOR 5 (gray), each of length 3 or 5 (alternating between lengths). Plus 1-2 DISTRACTOR runs of length 2 or 4 (even lengths, also color 5). All runs are placed at DISTINCT COLUMNS with ≥1 column padding between them. Rule: identify each VERTICAL COLOR-5 RUN (vertical line of consecutive 5-cells). If a run has ODD LENGTH ≥ 3 (3 or 5), RECOLOR ONLY ITS CENTER CELL (the middle cell of the run) to COLOR 2 (red).
