The other cells of the run stay 5. EVEN-length runs (2, 4) are left entirely as 5 (no well-defined center). Net: odd-length vertical 5-runs get a single red center pixel; even-length runs stay solid gray.

Start with a square image that is symmetric across the horizontal and vertical axes (and therefore under 180-degree rotation). Rectangular yellow regions are missing data. Keep every non-yellow cell unchanged; for each yellow cell, copy the first non-yellow value found at its 180-degree, horizontal, then vertical mirror counterpart.

Square 0-bg grid (n×n, n~6-9) with 3 single-cell MARKERS in distinct colors placed off the main diagonal at positions (0, 2), (1, n-2), (n-3, 1). Rule: for every cell (r, c) with input != 0, ALSO paint the TRANSPOSED position (c, r) with the same color (keeping the original cell as well). Cells already on the main diagonal don't move (since (r, r) == (r, r)). Net: every off-diagonal mark gets mirrored across the main diagonal, doubling the non-bg cell count.

Read command 1..5 from (0,0), clear that command cell, tightly crop all remaining nonzero content, then apply clockwise rotation, 180-degree rotation, transpose, left/right reflection, or up/down reflection respectively. The output is the transformed crop, never the full canvas.

A 7..10 by 10..12 zero-background grid contains two or three colored endpoint pairs.  Each pair lies on one slope -1 anti-diagonal, has a length of 2..5, and has an empty interior.  Different spans use different anti-diagonals.  Colors may be reused across separate anti-diagonals.  The rule independently fills every color+anti-diagonal span between its two endpoints.

Top row contains a left-to-right transform script using codes 1,2,3. Row 1 is blank.  The body below contains one connected multicolor object in colors 4..9, offset from the origin.  The canonical rule crops the body object and applies the script: 1 rotate-cw, 2 flip-lr, 3 flip-ud.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-12, w ∈ 10-14) with: (a) ONE LEGEND MARKER at FIXED position (0, 0) — value ∈ {4, 5, 6} (legend codes that map to a target color, e.g., 5→2, 6→3, 4→4); (b) THREE COLOR-PAIRS scattered — for EACH color ∈ {2, 3, 4}: place 2 cells of that color at axis-aligned endpoints (horizontal or vertical, ≥3 cells apart, both cells initially 0). All 3 pairs placed via _try_pair with non-overlap check. Rule (READ THE LEGEND AT (0, 0), MAP TO A TARGET COLOR, FIND THE PAIR OF THAT COLOR, DRAW A COLOR-8 SPAN BETWEEN THE TWO CELLS): READ the (0, 0) LEGEND. MAP legend → target color (per demos: 5→2, 6→3, 4→4, etc.). FIND the two cells of the TARGET color (axis-aligned). PAINT every cell on the line segment between them (inclusive of endpoints) with COLOR 8 (cyan). Other pairs stay as-is. The legend cell stays. Net: legend selects which color-pair to connect; that pair becomes a cyan line.
Exact length-2 vertical green runs turn orange; length-1 and length-3+ controls stay green.
Detect rectangles from four L-corners, mirror each enclosed blue motif across its missing axis, and remove blue distractors outside frames.

A 7-row color-5 arena contains two to four singleton seed cells. Zeros take the unique nearest seed COLOR by wall-aware four-neighbor BFS; different-color ties and seedless chambers stay zero. Four scheduled profiles guarantee evidence for ties, wall detours, unreachable cells, and equal-distance same-color seeds. Seven demonstrations provide one spare copy of every profile so any of the eight pairs can be held out as query.

Place a sparse one- to three-colour pattern inside a black border. The nonzero content may be connected or disconnected and may be tall, square, or wide. Crop to the tight bbox of every nonzero cell, preserving internal zeros, then transpose that crop.

0-bg grid with: (a) one KEY cell at the TOP-RIGHT corner (0, w-1) in some non-bg color cK; (b) 2-3 NON-RECTANGULAR blobs in distinct non-cK colors, placed in the interior. Each blob is 4-connected with bbox dims ≥2×2 and SHAPE differs from its bbox (so the rule's bbox-fill is visible). Rule: read key = g[0][w-1]. For each non-key blob, compute its bbox. Paint all cells in the bbox (including any bg holes) with the key color. Key cell preserved.
3x3 cells with markers 1..4; rule fills each block with marker+5.

Zero-background scenes with exactly three monochromatic 4-connected objects. The reference crops each object, sorts by (leftmost column, top row), and left-aligns the crops in a vertical gallery with one blank separator row. A five-profile schedule preserves canonical 3-cell L motifs while exposing ordering, width/alignment, tied-left, and same-color grouping shortcuts.

A zero-background grid has a transform key at (0,0), one asymmetric main object, and zero to three strictly smaller disconnected objects in the same foreground color. Clear the key, select the unique largest four-connected object, crop its bounding box, then apply key 1=clockwise quarter-turn, 2=left-right reflection, 3=top-bottom reflection, or 4=half-turn. The four-example schedule covers all keys and all distractor counts, so both transform dispatch and largest-object selection are observable.

Read the first top-row control in {1,2,3,4}. Select the first row-major 4-connected red(2) component, normalize it, rotate it by 1=identity, 2=clockwise, 3=180 degrees, or 4=counterclockwise, and stamp the result in green(3) at the cyan(8) anchor on a blank grid. When the control is 2, the red control singleton itself is the selected component.
Pair vertical bars by color and exact row span, in left-to-right disjoint pairs. Includes multiple same-color pairs and unmatched span/odd-bar witnesses.

0-bg grid (h, w~9-12) with 2-4 NON-TOUCHING BLOBS, each in a DISTINCT color drawn from 1..9 (shuffled), each of size 3-6 cells (4-conn random growth). Blobs are BBOX-ISOLATED (no bbox overlap with each other) and at least one blob is ASYMMETRIC (differs from its diagonal transpose). For each blob, the bbox transpose-within-grid is validated to fit in bounds. Rule (TRANSPOSE-WITHIN-BBOX UNION): for EACH BLOB, COMPUTE its BBOX (r1, c1, r2, c2). For each cell (r, c) of the blob, its TRANSPOSED POSITION within the bbox is (r1 + (c - c1), c1 + (r - r1)) — i.e., swap row and column OFFSETS from bbox top-left. PAINT both the original blob cells AND their transposed positions with the blob's COLOR. UNION the original and transposed cells. Other 0-cells stay 0. Net: each blob gains its bbox-local diagonal-transpose copy in the same color.

A 0-background 10..18 x 10..18 grid contains one or two vertically separated color-1 rectangular frames. Each frame has exactly one non-corner notch on its top or bottom edge and exactly one interior dot in color 2..9, aligned to the notch column. The output fills the frame interior and notch with the dot color and paints one full-width row immediately outside the notched edge. The color-1 wall remains.

Find the only nonzero 4-connected shape. Its color names the destination edge: 3 means left, 4 bottom, 6 top, and 8 right. Translate the complete shape as one rigid object until its bounding box is flush with that edge; preserve grid size, color, orientation, and every occupied-cell offset.

TOP 3-row LEGEND of 3 proto panels (pw wide, separated by single cols): each proto has a CENTER colour at local (1,1) + a small same-colour support pattern. Row 3 is an all-8 divider. BODY (rows 4+) holds single colour markers from the legend colours. Rule: stamp each body marker with its colour's proto support pattern. Output = the body region with markers expanded.

A 0-background 11..20 x 13..22 grid contains one connected color-2 template of 4..7 cells and one to four control pairs. Each pair is a code 1..8 immediately left of a color-9 anchor. The output is otherwise empty and stamps the corresponding identity/rotation/reflection of the normalized template in color 3 at each anchor.
Count 1..3 red markers in canonical-weighted 2..3 variable yellow frames.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~7-10) with 2-4 HORIZONTAL ENDPOINT PAIRS — each pair is 2 same-color cells in the SAME ROW at columns (c1, c2) with c2 ≥ c1 + 2 (gap of ≥1 bg cell between them). Each pair uses a DISTINCT non-zero color. Pairs occupy DISTINCT ROWS. Cells between endpoints start as 0. Rule: for EACH ROW that contains EXACTLY 2 SAME-COLOR CELLS, FILL the ENTIRE SPAN between them (all cells at columns min_c..max_c in that row) with the PAIR's COLOR. The two endpoints stay; the 0 cells between become the same color. Net: each same-color horizontal endpoint pair becomes a solid horizontal line connecting them.
Input is h × 2*half_w (two equal-width halves stacked horizontally, no separator). Output is h × half_w: cell (r, c) = 6 if either left[r][c] or right[r][c] is non-zero, else 0.
Equal panels split by color 4; paint 2 iff exactly one aligned cell is nonzero.

Grid laid out as N PANELS (5-6) of size panel_h × 4 (panel_h~4-5), side-by-side, separated by full-height color-9 (maroon) DIVIDER columns. Each panel contains a small 4-conn motif (1-3 cells) in some non-{0, 9} color. Rule: detect the panels by splitting at the color-9 divider columns. Find the MATCHING PAIR (two panels with the same shape modulo color or rotation). Output: a compact representation.

Variable-size 0-bg grid with: (a) one ORANGE(7) rectangular block (rh∈3-4 × rw∈3-5) at a random interior position; (b) one GRAY(5) strip of THICKNESS t spanning exactly one side of the block (top/bottom/left/right) so the rule's push = t ∈ {1,2,3}; (c) one isolated 2×2 orange block in the top-left corner (no gray contact). Rule: first recolor every gray(5) cell → yellow(4) and every orange(7) cell → gray(5) into a base result. Then for each orange block in the input, find total gray contact size and contact direction. Push = floor(gray_size / perpendicular_dim) cells from the contacted side. Re-paint that side's slice of the orange block back to orange(7); the remaining slice stays gray(5). Isolated orange blocks (no gray contact) revert entirely to orange(7) — staying unchanged from input.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~11-15) with: (a) ONE COLOR-3 (green) BLOB of 3-5 cells at a random clear position (the TEMPLATE); (b) ONE COLOR-7 (orange) ANCHOR cell at a non-adjacent position with enough room for the rotated template; (c) k COLOR-1 (blue) CELLS at scattered positions (1 ≤ k ≤ 4) — k counts the rotation. The template, anchor, and 1-cells are mutually 4-non-adjacent. Rule (ROTATE TEMPLATE BY k, STAMP AT ANCHOR IN COLOR 8): COUNT k = number of color-1 cells. Identify the LARGEST COLOR-3 BLOB (the TEMPLATE). NORMALIZE the template (shift to origin). APPLY transform: k=1 identity, k=2 90° CW, k=3 180°, k=4 horizontal flip. Find the COLOR-7 ANCHOR. STAMP the TRANSFORMED template at the anchor position in COLOR 8. Template, anchor, k-markers stay. Net: blue-count picks rotation, applied to green template, stamped in cyan at orange anchor.

0-bg grid (h~8-13, w~8-13) with: (a) 2-5 COLOR-2 (red) SINGLETON CELLS placed at positions with no cardinal red neighbor (diagonal-neighbor pairs are allowed and used to pin CARDINAL, not diagonal, connectivity); (b) ONE FIXED MULTI-CELL COLOR-2 CLUSTER at bottom-left (a 3-cell L-shape at (h-3, 0), (h-2, 0), (h-2, 1)) — a non-singleton red blob that should NOT be recolored. Rule: for EVERY COLOR-2 (red) CELL, check its 4 cardinal neighbors. If ALL 4 cardinal neighbors are NON-RED (any non-2 value), RECOLOR that cell to COLOR 3 (green). If ≥1 cardinal neighbor IS red (part of a multi-cell component), KEEP it as 2. Net: cardinally isolated red singletons become green; multi-cell red blobs stay red.
Cyan cells defining a bbox; rule draws perimeter as 1.
A marker direction slides the colored object rigidly until blocked.
A direction marker makes every non-control object slide rigidly until stacked against the wall or another object.
A 2x2 template sits left of one black separator column; a 2x2 command matrix sits on the right. Commands 1/2/3/4 tile the template unchanged/clockwise/180-degrees/counter-clockwise into a 4x4 output.

Grid (h~7-10, w~5-8) with 3 COLORED ROWS interleaved with all-zero rows. Each colored row has 2 non-zero cells at specific positions (col i and col w-1-i) in 3 distinct colors. Rule: filter the rows — keep only rows with at least one non-zero cell. Output: a 3 × w grid consisting of the original colored rows in their order, with all-zero rows DROPPED.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~12-17) with COLOR-5 (gray) WALLS: (a) FULL-HEIGHT VERTICAL WALL at col w//2 with a GAP at random row (in 3..h-4); (b) SHORT HORIZONTAL WALLS at row h//2 scattered on both sides at random columns (random True/False); This creates 2 CHAMBERS. THREE SEEDS placed at fixed corners: COLOR-4 at (1, wall_col-2), COLOR-3 at (h-2, 2), COLOR-2 at (h-2, w-3). Rule (WALL-AWARE VORONOI + TIE MAP): for EACH 0-CELL, compute the SHORTEST BFS DISTANCE to each of the 3 SEEDS through walkable (non-5) cells. If one seed is strictly closest, MAP its color to {2 → 6, 3 → 7, 4 → 8}. If MULTIPLE seeds tie for closest, MAP to COLOR 9. Unreachable cells (separated by walls) get COLOR 9 or 0. Net: 3-seed wall-aware Voronoi, ties = 9.

A 0-background grid is split into four rectangular chambers by one full horizontal and one full vertical color-5 wall.  Each chamber contains sparse 2/3/4 seeds.  Preserve walls and seeds; fill only zeros with 6/7/8 for the chamber-local unique plurality of 2/3/4, or 9 when the largest count is tied.  Every normal draw includes all winner mappings, a tie, and a plurality-without-majority counterexample.
Recolor every nested component to the color of its outermost enclosing rectangular frame; preserve independent uncontained components.

A sparse zero-background grid contains 2..4 same-color horizontal or vertical one-cell x 0 x gaps. Repair every such gap by painting its middle cell with the endpoint color. Some curriculum samples also contain unequal, diagonal, and two-cell-gap negative controls that must remain unchanged.

Pair 2-4 hollow frames by increasing interior area with equally many loose connected shapes by increasing cell count. Center using signed floor-half offsets, including border overlap. Shared or distinct frame colors, unequal rectangular interiors, and variable shape counts occur in ordinary lessons.

Read the rank key at the top-left and the transform key at the top-right. Sort body components by area, breaking equal-area ties by bounding-box position, select the indicated 1-based rank, crop it, and transform the crop (4 identity, 5 clockwise, 6 left/right reflection, 7 rotate 180).

On a 0-background grid, the unique pair of red (2) cells sharing a row or column forms a trunk. Join the trunk endpoints with green (3), then connect every remaining red perpendicularly to the trunk in green. Generated scenes vary dimensions, orientation, trunk placement/span, branch count (1..5), branch rows/columns, and both branch sides.

Color-5 wall field (size varies) with rectangular 0-ROOMS, each ringed by sparse {1,2,3} markers. Rule: each room fills with the strict-plurality marker color (the winner itself; tie -> 8; no marker -> empty). The grid size, room count/sizes/positions and per-room marker mix vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~21 distinct).
Small multicolor seed grid; rule rotates 180° and applies a 4-quadrant kaleidoscope.

A 10..20 square-ish canvas contains one dense 3..6 square bitmap in colors 1/8, one yellow source marker at an expanded bbox corner, and a separate three-cell yellow L cluster in the target quadrant. Rotate the colored bitmap by target-source quarter turns and mark the target corner yellow.
1-marker (src) + 2-marker (dst) + a 3-blob; translation lands in-bounds.

Generate exactly four equal nonzero cells at the corners of one axis-aligned rectangle.  Default draws cycle the five linked canonical (grid height, grid width, rectangle height, rectangle width) profiles, while color and placement vary deterministically.  The canonical Racket rule draws only the complete rectangle border in the marker color.
A 5+ row grid; rule swaps rows 0/1 and 3/4.

Zero-background 6..20 grids containing 1..5 distinct-colored rectangle clues.  Each color has exactly one axis-aligned rectangle with three of its four corners present; selected teaching profiles also include one same-color interior marker that shares neither clue row nor clue column. Complete every color's missing fourth corner and preserve all other cells.

A 3..15 by 3..30 grid using 2..4 colours.  The authority stacks the vertical reflection above the unchanged input.  Default lessons alternate canonical-profile 3x4 binary inputs with broader non-three-row inputs, and adjacent broad slots have opposite height parity so teaching witnesses survive duplicate rejection. All ordinary draws make the reflection visible.
The second onion layer of each solid component is extracted as 8.
skills: selective masking, depth thresholding, same-size extraction

summary: Separated color-8 objects are recolored by their enclosed 0-region count: 1->1, 2->3, 3->2, 4->4, else stays 8. Every lesson includes component-size counterexamples and cycles through counts 2, 3, 4, and 0.

skills: header decoding, panel-wise boolean operations, same-size output
summary: A color-5 header corner selects union, intersection, XOR, or A-minus-B over two same-size occupancy panels. Four-example lessons cover every corner, and every operand pair makes all four outputs distinct.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~12-14) with: (a) RANK-KEY at (0, 0) — a color encoding rank ∈ {1, 2, 3} (1-indexed size rank ascending); (b) TF-KEY at (0, w-1) — a color encoding transform ∈ {4, 5, 6, 7}: 4=IDENTITY, 5=ROTATE CW, 6=FLIP LR, else=ROTATE 180; (c) BODY (rows ≥1) — 3 CONNECTED COMPONENTS in DISTINCT SIZES (2..6) drawn from a shape bank in 3 distinct BODY COLORS (excluding rank-key and tf-key colors). Components are non-touching with 1-cell padding. Rule (SORT BODY COMPONENTS BY SIZE ASC, PICK RANK-KEY-TH, APPLY TF-KEY TRANSFORM): identify the 2 corner key cells. SORT all body components by CELL COUNT ASC. PICK the rank-key-th (1-indexed). CROP that component to its BBOX. APPLY the TF-KEY transform (identity / cw90 / flip-lr / rot180) to the crop. OUTPUT is the transformed crop. Net: rank-key selects which size-ranked blob to pull, tf-key selects how to rotate/flip it.
Gray 5 walls form two to four chambers; flood only the four-connected chamber containing the single red 2 seed with cyan 8.

Find every same-colour 4-connected nonzero object. Recolour objects of exactly six cells red(2), and recolour all other object sizes blue(1). Four-slot lessons contain two 10x10 gray anchors and two non-gray six-cell witnesses that refute the strongest canonical colour shortcut.

A 3-column two-color template panel is followed by three 7- or 8-column candidate boards, separated by single full-height maroon columns. Count exact-color occurrences of the cropped template in all four rotations inside each candidate (template zeroes are wildcards). Output marks every candidate tied for the positive maximum in a 1x3 cyan strip.
skills: counting transformed matches, candidate comparison, symbolic argmax output

summary: N non-touching objects drawn from a few exact-shape classes; output is the n x n shape-equality matrix.

A canonical-sized zero-background grid contains 2-4 separated green 4-connected components and 0-2 isolated gray markers. Component sizes follow an observable profile with one unique minimum. Recolor exactly that smallest green component to 4.
2-3 X-shapes (center + 4 diagonal corners) of distinct colors, well separated.

9x9 0-bg grid with exactly one non-zero corner marker. The marker color names the target color. Usually a same-color target object is placed in the body and 1-2 non-marker distractor objects are placed outside its bbox; sometimes the corner marker is the only cell of that color, yielding the canonical 1x1 fallback answer. Rule: choose the non-zero corner color and output the tight crop of cells with that color, excluding the corner when body cells exist.
Start 2, goal 3, color-5 maze walls, optional paired portals 6/7/9; output path uses 8.
2 hollow rect frames in distinct colors + 1 lone marker matching one frame's color.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~8-10) containing 2-4 CONNECTED MOTIFS of 2-4 cells each, all painted in COLOR 4 (yellow). Half of them (ceil(n/2)) TOUCH the GRID BORDER (any cell at row 0, row h-1, col 0, or col w-1); the other half are placed in the INTERIOR (no border contact). Motifs are non-touching (separated by ≥1 cell padding). Rule: for every CONNECTED COMPONENT, check if any of its cells touches the grid BORDER (row 0, row h-1, col 0, or col w-1). If YES, RECOLOR every cell of that component to COLOR 2 (red). If NO (entirely interior), leave the component as color 4 (yellow). Net: border-touching motifs become red; interior motifs stay yellow.

Fill a zero cell only when all eight original neighbors share one nonzero color. Sample 1-6 full rings with inert near-rings, nonzero centers, and optional singleton colors. Preserve distractions and original colored cells.

A zero-background grid contains one or two separated same-color pluses. For every nonzero center whose north, south, west, and east neighbours all equal the center, fill its entire 3x3 neighbourhood with that color. Preserve every other cell. A four-profile schedule includes clean canonical anchors, an unchanged five-cell monochrome L distractor, an unchanged multicolor false cross, and repeated-color pluses with a border-touching footprint. All nonzero colors may trigger; distractors reuse true-plus colors so neither absolute palette IDs nor per-color filtering solve it.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~11-14) with 1-3 (default 2) HOLLOW COLOR-5 (gray) RECTANGULAR FRAMES (4-5 × 4-5) at non-overlapping positions. INSIDE EACH frame's STRICT INTERIOR (rows r1+1..r2-1, cols c1+1..c2-1), place EXACTLY ONE MARKER CELL in a DISTINCT non-{0, 5} color. Rule (FLOOD FRAME INTERIOR WITH MARKER COLOR): for EACH color-5 RECTANGULAR FRAME, identify its INTERIOR cells. If the interior contains EXACTLY ONE non-{0, 5} marker color, FILL the entire frame's INTERIOR (all 0-cells inside) with that color. The marker stays. Frame walls stay color 5. Net: each gray frame's interior gets flooded with its marker color.
Crop every same-color 4-connected component, sort the crops by enclosed hole count descending with reading-order ties, and top-align them with one blank column between adjacent crops.

A 0-background 4..14 by 4..14 grid contains exactly three cells of one nonzero color at three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Rows and columns may be adjacent, and the rectangle may touch any grid boundary. Complete the unique missing row-column combination with the same color.

summary: 0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with 3-4 connected MOTIFS at distinct non-touching positions, each in a DISTINCT color from {2..9} and each of size 3-5 cells (4-conn random walk). Motifs have 1-cell padding from each other and grid edges. Rule (VERTICAL GALLERY PACK): identify each MOTIF as a connected component. CROP each motif to its BBOX. STACK the cropped motifs VERTICALLY in a new output grid (task-specific canonical order — color/position/size). Output WIDTH = MAX bbox width; HEIGHT = SUM of bbox heights. Net: scattered motifs → vertical gallery.

Square N×N (6 ≤ N ≤ 9) 0-bg grid with 3-5 non-zero source cells in distinct colors at scattered positions. Each source cell's anti-diagonal mirror image is blank (so the rule can fill it). Rule: for each cell (r, c), if v == 0 AND the anti-diagonal mirror cell (N-1-c, N-1-r) has value ref != 0, then fill with ref. Otherwise preserve. Effectively each non-zero source cell gets reflected across the anti-diagonal.
Select the unique largest 4-connected color-3 component, recolor it 9, and erase every other component.
Square grid; rule tiles z*N × z*N where z = N² - nz.
N (2-5) isolated components from random rotation-classes; output N×N rotation-equivalence matrix (1 diag, 2 if rotation-equal, 3 else).

0-bg grid (h ∈ 11-13, w ∈ 14-18) with: (a) ONE ISOLATED MARKER CELL — random position, value ∈ {4, 5, 6} (op_marker, with 4=OR, 5=AND, 6=XOR), placed with 1-cell padding from all other non-bg cells; (b) TWO HOLLOW COLOR-9 FRAMES — each is a rectangular ring of color 9 with the same interior dimensions (ih × iw, ih ∈ 3-4, iw ∈ 3-4), placed at non-overlapping positions with 1-cell padding; each frame's INTERIOR is sprinkled with 3 to (interior_size - 1) cells of one non-9 color (the two frames use DIFFERENT interior colors drawn from {1,2,3,7,8}). Generation retries until the op result has ≥1 hit cell. Rule (READ THE MARKER, COMPUTE THE BOOLEAN COMBINATION OF THE TWO FRAMES' INTERIOR MASKS, OUTPUT AS COLOR 8): READ the marker value (4/5/6) → choose op ∈ {OR, AND, XOR}. BUILD binary mask A from frame 1's interior (1 where non-bg, 0 else) and binary mask B from frame 2's interior. COMPUTE the elementwise boolean combination A op B. OUTPUT an ih × iw GRID: PAINT COLOR 8 where the result is true, COLOR 0 elsewhere. Net: marker selects an operator; two frame interiors are unioned/intersected/xored into a small cyan-8 mask.

Complete only red (2) same-color components that are exact three-cell L-triominoes in a 2x2 box. Paint the entire box green (3), overwriting even a non-red cell in the missing corner. Red lines, dominos, and full squares, plus non-red Ls and other components, remain unchanged. Four linked profiles expose shape, color, occupancy, count, and edge contrasts.

An 8..14 square has contiguous color runs on its right and bottom borders. Their ordered colors agree while their run lengths may differ; fill an interior cell exactly when its row and column labels agree.

Read the nonzero cells of row 0 from left to right as an ordered palette. Find the nonzero 4-connected body objects below the blank separator row, sort them by area, crop and recolor each object with the corresponding palette color, then pack the pieces left-to-right with one zero-column gap. Ignore any unused palette tail after the last object.

0-bg grid with difficulty-scaled h/w with 2-4 HOLLOW BLUE (COLOR-1) 3×3 RECT-OUTLINE FRAMES at non-overlapping interior positions (≥4-cell anchor separation). Each frame's 3×3 window has its 8 outline cells in color 1 and CENTER CELL = 0 (empty). Rule (FILL CENTER OF EACH HOLLOW 3×3 BLUE RING WITH CYAN): identify each HOLLOW 3×3 BLUE FRAME by detecting 8-cell rings of color 1 with empty center. For EACH FRAME at (r, c): SET g[r+1][c+1] = 8 (cyan). Frame walls stay 1. Background stays 0. Net: each blue ring gets a cyan center dot.

Four distinct colors mark four sparse point sets.  Complete each color by filling row segments and then column segments, normalize the completed shapes up to translation, sort objects by color, and output a 4x4 equivalence matrix with diagonal 5, matching pairs 8, and nonmatches 0. Generated lessons make raw-marker, bounding-box, and area-only shortcuts fail even though all three fit every canonical pair.
0-grid with exactly two 8 endpoints; oracle draws diagonal-first and straight-first L-paths (3) between them. Canonical family: unequal >=2 row/col deltas, endpoints anywhere incl. borders.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~7-9 by ~9-11) with EXACTLY 2 pairs of cells: one VERTICAL pair of color A (2 cells in same column, different rows) and one HORIZONTAL pair of color B (2 cells in same row, different columns), where A ≠ B and A, B ≠ 9. The two spans (vertical line A, horizontal line B) cross at exactly one cell. Rule: for each non-bg color with exactly 2 cells, compute the SPAN (inclusive line of cells from one endpoint to the other, horizontal if same row, vertical if same column). Paint each span cell with that color. If any cell is in 2+ spans (intersection), overwrite with color 9 (maroon). Output: a cross pattern with 9 at the intersection.
Draw separated hollow monochrome rectangles whose interiors get filled.
Use the top color-to-2x2-mask legend to paint matching cells of the lower separated 2x2 tile lattice.

0-bg grid (h~6-8, w~6-8) with 2-4 ISOLATED L-TRIOMINOES — each is a 2×2 window with EXACTLY 3 of the 4 cells painted in ONE non-0 color from {1..9}; the FOURTH (missing) CORNER is 0. Which of the 4 corners is missing is random per triomino. Triominoes are placed at non-touching positions with 1-cell 8-conn padding (so each L-shape sits alone in its 2×2 window, no shared cells between any two). If random placement fails entirely, generator emits a single fallback L at (1,1)-(2,1). Rule (FILL MISSING CORNER OF EACH MONOCHROME L INTO A 2×2 SQUARE): For EACH 2×2 WINDOW where exactly 3 cells share ONE non-0 color C and the fourth cell is 0: RECOLOR the missing-corner 0 cell to C, completing the 2×2 monochrome square. Other cells (already filled with C, or outside any active 2×2 window) stay unchanged. Net: every L-triomino is closed into a solid 2×2 monochrome block of its own color.

Place a unique largest 4-connected monochromatic component together with smaller distractor components and crop to that component's bounding box. Alternating scenes make either a distractor color or the target color globally dominant through disconnected fragments, refuting aggregate and conditional color-ranking shortcuts.

Mode-color background grid (12..16 x 12..14, canonical prior on the exact official dim pairs). 1..2 4-connected compounds, each exactly two colors stacked vertically: an upper blob (1..5 rows, 2..7 cols, possibly L-shaped or 1-cell notched) touching a lower blob; both color classes 4-connected. Rule: each compound's top color shifts left 1, its bottom color shifts right 1, onto a fresh background. Compounds keep collision-free separation (row-disjoint or >=2 empty bbox columns when rows overlap) and every cell keeps shift room.

A canonical-sized 0-background grid contains 2-4 mutually separated 4-connected red (color-2) components. Their largest cell-count is unique, but smaller components may tie. One connected non-red distractor is preserved. Recolor exactly the unique largest red component to color 8.

0-bg grid of 5 equal PANELS (each ph x pw) separated by single 0-columns: a, b, result, c, d. a/b/result are colour A; c/d are colour B. a and b overlap partially; result = OP(a,b) for OP in {union, intersection, xor} (unambiguous because all three differ). Rule: infer OP from a,b,result, then output OP(c,d) recoloured to colour B. Output is ph x pw.

One or two corner-disjoint yellow rectangles, optionally with up to three isolated yellow distractors; fill every strict rectangle interior red. A four-slot schedule alternates canonical anchors and interleaved-row counterexamples to the adjacent-row-pair shortcut.

A color-1 wall maze contains start 2, end 3, and one to four distinct waypoints from colors 4..7. Visit present waypoints in ascending numeric order between 2 and 3. For each leg, take the deterministic shortest four-neighbor path through non-wall cells (neighbor order up, down, left, right) and paint only path cells that were color 0 with color 8. Preserve all walls and markers.
One colored full-row/full-column cross plus 1-3 gray markers; count every gray cell and move the cross center by (+N,-N), erasing the markers.

0-bg grid with one to three CYAN(8) rectangular frames (hollow outlines) of size 5-9 per side. Inside each frame interior, 1-3 RED(2) cells are placed (not on border), preferably in the top-left quadrant so the rule's mirror operations are visible. Rule: for each color-2 cell at (r, c) inside the frame, compute mirror positions: horizontal mirror (r, 2*cc - c), vertical mirror (2*cr - r, c), both (2*cr - r, 2*cc - c) where (cr, cc) is frame center. Paint each mirror position with 2 (if currently 0 and within frame). Output preserves frame + original reds + adds mirrored reds.

Sort same-color 4-connected components by true exposed-edge perimeter descending, breaking equal-perimeter ties by ascending color; crop and left-align them in a vertical stack separated by one background row. A four-profile schedule explicitly refutes bbox, area, input-order, and descending-color tie shortcuts.

8-bg grid with one full row of 2 (the line) and color-1 shapes above it. Thin shapes (vertical bars, incl. singletons) fall through the line to the last row and punch 8-holes in it; wide shapes fall until their lowest wide row rests just above the line (thin tails may overlap the line); originals erase to the 8 background. Grid size, line row, thin/wide mix, shape sizes and positions vary; canonical dims 7..18 sit inside the generated envelope.

On a sparse 11..16 by 15..24 zero background, the unique 2/3/4 cardinal corner is a SOURCE coordinate frame and the unique 5/6/7 corner is a TARGET frame.  Read the sparse color-8 motif in signed source-local coordinates, take its complete local bounding rectangle, and fill that rectangle with 8 through the target frame.  Canvas size, both ordered bases, motif quadrant, motif shape, and placement vary.
skills: local bounding boxes, abstraction, frame-relative rendering

summary: Each seed cell mirrors its group's main shape across the indicated bbox side.
Paint each blank cell whose wall-constrained distance to the red and green seeds is equal.
2x2 color template at columns 0..1, vertically centered; output is the exponentially doubling staircase (block widths 2,4,8,16) built rightward from the template's quadrants.

Grid with FULL-ROW SEPARATORS in some uniform non-bg color, partitioning the canvas into horizontal BANDS of equal height N. The border rows (top and bottom) are also separator-colored. Each band's height equals the SQUARE BLOCK SIZE N for that band. Inside each band, 2 SOLID N×N SQUARES are placed in two distinct colors against a noisy filler of other colors (any color except the separator color and the square colors). Rule: scan band-by-band top-to-bottom. For each band, DETECT the K solid N×N SQUARES inside (each in a distinct color) in left-to-right order. EMIT a 1-row sequence of those K square-colors. Output: BANDS rows × K cols, one cell per square's color. Net: the separator-bound bands get reduced to a compact (bands × K) lookup table of solid-square colors.

skills: relational output, pairwise comparison, matrix construction
summary: Color-9 columns split the grid into panels.  Each panel contains one connected monochrome object whose onion-peel depth is its thickness.  The output is the square pairwise equality matrix: 8 for equal depths, 0 otherwise.  Equal-depth panels intentionally vary in silhouette, area, color, and position.
Colors as staircase rows whose lengths = connected-object counts.

Count the four-connected components of colors 1, 2, 3, not their areas. Random connected shapes, diagonal contacts, border contacts and optional colors 4..9 break pixel-count, eight-connected and color-blind shortcuts. Output is a three-row left-aligned histogram of width max(1, counts).

8-bg grid with a connected zero field and one connected 2-region. The 0s are distributed unevenly: at least one ROW has the maximum 0-count (≥ all other rows), and at least one COL also has the maximum 0-count. Rule: count 0s per row → max-rz. Count 0s per col → max-cz. For each 0-cell at (r, c), if row r has count max-rz OR col c has count max-cz, replace it with color 3. Otherwise leave it as 0. Other cells (8, 2) are preserved. The generator keeps 8/2 as low-component regions like the canonical examples instead of scattering 2s as independent speckles.

Find each separated solid rectangle, clear the input, and paint exactly the rectangle's four bounding-box corners cyan (8). Generated rectangles span the demonstrated 2..4 side lengths but exclude 2x2 identity cases.
Find every singleton red(2) component. Replace its center and four cardinal neighbors with yellow(4), while preserving larger red components and all differently colored distractor objects.
Two header commands 0..5 are composed in order on one translated 2..5 by 2..5 multicolor motif; the output is the transformed crop.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~7-9, w should be ODD for a centered divider) with: (a) FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-5 DIVIDER at col w//2 — every row of col w//2 painted gray; (b) LEFT BLOB — 2-4 CELLS in a single non-{0, 5} color placed at random positions on the LEFT side (cols 0..w//2-1) where the mirrored target on the right stays in bounds; (c) RIGHT SIDE (cols w//2+1..w-1) is INPUT-EMPTY. Rule (MIRROR LEFT BLOB CELLS ACROSS THE GRAY DIVIDER TO THE RIGHT): identify the FULL-COLUMN GRAY (5) DIVIDER at col div. For EACH NON-0 NON-5 CELL at (r, c) with c < div: PAINT (r, 2*div - c) on the RIGHT with the SAME COLOR. Divider and original cells stay. Net: left blob appears mirrored across the gray divider on the right side.

Generate 3-6 separated blue components: horizontal- and vertical-edge examples, a distance-one interior decoy, optional deep/inter-edge components, one preserved decoration component, and count-varying lesson schedules. Recolor whole blue components iff they touch any grid border.

A centered full-height gray divider separates two independently placed monochrome connected objects.  Count object cells per row in each object's own bounding box, zero-pad the shorter row profile, take elementwise absolute differences, and draw that list as a left-justified cyan histogram.

A black canonical-scale grid contains exactly one blue control in a corner, one connected red polyomino, and one connected green polyomino. The control maps TL/TR/BR/BL to 0/1/2/3 clockwise quarter-turns. Normalize red, rotate then normalize green, take their symmetric XOR, normalize that mask, and emit its tight cyan(8) crop.

Find every same-color 4-connected nonzero component, sort components by cell count from largest to smallest, and recolor the i-th component with color i. Generated lessons use distinct component sizes and include non-rectangular counterexamples to height, bounding-box-area, reading-order, input-color, smallest-first, and identity shortcuts.

Nonzero non-gray cells on the four borders cast straight rays inward. Gray (5) cells stop and preserve rays, interior colored distractors do not emit or block, and crossing rays keep the larger color number.
Grid with one full-color axis column; rule mirrors non-zero cells across it.

On a zero background, keep only complete cyan(8) rectangular frames. Treat each filled non-cyan rectangle as an insert. If an insert's exact height and width equal a surviving frame's interior dimensions, fill that interior with the insert color. Clear source inserts, unmatched inserts, and incomplete cyan frame candidates. Generated lessons vary object order and include a canonical-style occluded candidate.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~9-14) with: (a) color-1 (blue) MARKER at (0,0); (b) color-2 (red) MARKER at offset (dr, dc) from blue — defines the translation VECTOR; (c) a small MOTIF (3-5 cells) in some non-{0,1,2} color placed apart from markers, with room to fit several translated copies. Rule: find p1 = color-1 cell, p2 = color-2 cell; vector = (p2 - p1). Extract motif cells (non-{0,1,2}). Output: fresh empty grid. For k = 0, 1, 2, ... while all translated cells (shifted by k*vector) stay in bounds, stamp the motif (with original colors). Stop when out-of-bounds. Markers DISAPPEAR in output.

Read transform code grid[0][0] and output color grid[0][1]. Clear those two controls, crop the single 4-connected monochrome body, apply the canonical six-code transform table (1 identity, 2 left-right reflection, 3 up-down reflection, 4 clockwise rotation, 5 half-turn, 6 counter-clockwise rotation), and recolor the transformed body to grid[0][1].
Select the unique component with the widest bounding box, crop its exact mask to that box, and recolor the selected cells to 8.

Crop the grid to the tight joint bounding rectangle of every nonzero cell, preserving colors, zero holes, and gaps between disconnected components. Two of every four scheduled inputs match canonical canvas/palette profiles; the alternating inputs contain two differently colored components.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~7-11) with 3-5 SINGLETON SEEDS at random positions, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color (drawn via distinct_colors). Seeds are placed with a 3-cell HORIZONTAL BRUSH neighborhood guard ((r, c-1..c+1)) so brushes don't overlap. Rule (HORIZONTAL BRUSH EXPANSION): for EACH SINGLETON SEED at (r, c) with color C, PAINT a HORIZONTAL 3-CELL BRUSH at row r, cols c-1, c, c+1 — i.e., paint (r, c-1), (r, c), (r, c+1) with color C. CLIP at grid edges (cells outside 0..w-1 are dropped). Net: each singleton dot expands into a 1×3 horizontal stripe in its color.

A color-5 rectangular hollow frame (≥4×4) and one connected blob in a non-{0,5} color, placed OUTSIDE the frame. Rule emits a FRESH same-size grid where the blob is translated so its bbox top-left aligns with (frame_r1+1, frame_c1+1) (the interior top-left). The 5-frame is DROPPED in the output; only the relocated blob remains.

0-bg grid (size varies). A red (color-2) frame defines the reflection box. VERTICAL axis: a full rectangular frame (solid top bar) with 1-3 gray (color-5) markers ABOVE/BELOW it. HORIZONTAL axis: only the LEFT and RIGHT vertical walls (top bar not solid) with markers to the LEFT/RIGHT. Rule: detect the frame bbox; if the top bar is solid reflect each gray vertically across the near top/bottom edge, else reflect horizontally across the near left/right wall; the original gray is removed and the reflection drawn (always in-bounds, landing in the box interior). Grid size, axis, frame size/position and the markers all vary freely (was a fixed 12x12 frame with one marker).

0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-1 (blue) SHAPE and ONE color-2 (red) SHAPE (random connected polyominoes whose bbox masks are NOT identical), placed apart. Rule: bbox-crop each color's cells into a binary mask, align both masks at the top-left, and XOR them on a max-dimension grid — cells in exactly one mask become COLOR 7 (orange). The grid size, the two shapes (which set the XOR) and their positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed shapes, ~9 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-11) with HARDCODED POSITIONS for 2 DISTINCT colors: (a) COLOR_A (random from {2..7}) at fixed positions (1, 1) and (h-3, w//2+1) — defining bbox A; (b) COLOR_B (distinct) at fixed positions (2, w//2-1) and (h-2, w-2) — defining bbox B. Hardcoded positions × color pair choices ≈ ~50 unique. Output uniq_out=15 (intrinsic — intersection rect dimensions × colors normalize). Rule (PAINT INTERSECTION OF BBOXES IN 8): For EACH NON-0 COLOR: COMPUTE BBOX from its cells. COMPUTE bbox_A ∩ bbox_B — the RECTANGULAR INTERSECTION. PAINT every cell inside that intersection rect with COLOR-8 (cyan). Original color cells stay. Net: bbox overlap rect becomes cyan.

Replace every monochrome 4-connected object by its same-color filled bounding rectangle. This is equivalent to the authority's occupied-row × occupied-column closure because a 4-connected object's row and column projections cannot contain gaps.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-11) with: (a) 1-2 color-2 (red) EMITTER cells at interior positions; (b) 1-2 short straight color-8 (cyan) WALL SEGMENTS — horizontal or vertical lines of length 3-5 cells. Walls and emitters are placed so they are NOT 4-adjacent. Rule: for each color-2 emitter at (r, c), CAST FOUR RAYS in the cardinal directions (up, down, left, right). Each ray walks one cell at a time, painting that cell color 2 (red), until it either steps onto a color-8 wall cell (stop and do NOT paint the wall) or steps out of the grid. Walls stay 8; emitters stay 2. Net: each red dot emits red rays in all four directions that terminate at cyan walls or the grid border.
Tightly crop the global nonzero pattern, preserving all colors and internal zeros, then paste it at the top-left of an equal-size zero canvas.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-12, w ∈ 9-14, by difficulty) with: TARGET ∈ 1-3 HOLLOW ONE-CELL-THICK RECTANGULAR FRAMES, each of size rh × rw (rh ∈ 3-5, rw ∈ 3-6) drawn at non-overlapping interior positions (via _free padding check), each in a DISTINCT color drawn at random from {1..9}. Each frame's INTERIOR (cells strictly inside the outline) starts EMPTY (0); each frame is non-touching with others. Rule (FILL EACH HOLLOW RECTANGULAR FRAME'S INTERIOR WITH THE SAME COLOR AS THE FRAME — TURNING IT INTO A SOLID RECTANGLE): For EACH color-c frame: COMPUTE its bbox. For EVERY (r, c) inside the bbox (including interior and outline): PAINT g[r][c] = c. The frame outline stays color c (no change); the interior 0-cells become c. Net: each hollow frame becomes a solid same-color block of identical dimensions.

Connect every repeated non-background/non-8 color into one obstacle-aware L-path tree; choose the shortest available attachment, use the existing same-color row/column to choose an open bend, and preserve color-8 walls and singleton distractor colors.

Build a 30x30 modal-background scene from one of five demonstrated multi-motif grammars. Each 5x5 motif has a majority body and singleton core; corner markers select core-matched motifs for stamping after the body/core swap. Palettes, D4 orientations, positions, and marker corners vary independently, with a bounded literal-public prior.
3 square-ish panels separated by full-column color-8 dividers; cropped B is a unique non-identity D4-style transform of cropped A; output is the same transform applied to cropped C.

Fixed 6×23 grid, 0-bg. PROTOTYPE shape drawn at (0..4, 0..4) — a small polyomino in some color proto_color. THREE CANDIDATE PANELS at columns [6..10, 12..16, 18..22] each spanning rows 0..4, in distinct candidate colors. EXACTLY ONE candidate's shape is a ROTATION (90°/180°/270°) of the prototype; the other two are unrelated shapes. A TARGET COLOR is placed at (5, 0). Rule: find the candidate panel whose normalized binary mask matches the prototype under some rotation (0°/90°/180°/270°). CROP that candidate, RECOLOR all its cells to the TARGET COLOR at (5, 0). Output: the small recolored crop. Net: prototype + rotation-match selector + target color → output is the matching panel recolored.

A 0-background grid contains two or three blank centers whose four diagonal neighbors share one nonzero color. The output fills every such center with that color and preserves all other cells. Each generated lesson also contains one controlled non-answer: either only three matching diagonals, four nonzero but mismatched diagonals, or a nonzero center surrounded by four matching diagonals. Positive motifs move across the grid, two of every three examples reuse one color, and one example adds a symmetric orthogonal context pair that must not block the fill.

0-bg grid (h 10..19, w 12..22) with 2-4 4-connected same-color components, each a distinct color (different-colored components may touch edge-to-edge, as in canonical train pair 2; their bboxes never overlap). Each component is one of: solid rect (0 holes), open/notched rect (0 holes but zeros inside the crop touch the crop border), ring (1 enclosed hole), or double-ring (2 enclosed holes). Rule: crop each component to its bbox, count ENCLOSED interior 0-regions, sort by (hole_count asc, reading-order index asc), and pack the crops LEFT-TO-RIGHT with one blank column between consecutive crops. Output height = max crop height; width = sum of crop widths + (n-1) gap columns.

A non-corner red 2 marker on the top edge fires a stream downward; a left-edge marker is the transposed rightward case. On each blue 1 or green 3 bar, the stream slides above the bar and exits just beyond one end: blue turns to the stream's left hand and green to its right. Transposition flips chirality. Unhit length-3 bars are inert distractors.
Onion layers are recolored by odd/even depth parity.
skills: layer parity, same-size transform, depth labeling

summary: Two to four colored rectangles each have one bbox corner replaced by 8; replace the markers and move every full rectangle one diagonal step toward its marked corner on background 7.
A 9-anchored colored shape is completed across four rotations.
Sort distinct-color components numerically and emit an area-winner matrix, using zero on the diagonal and for tied areas.

A border-walled maze uses color 8 for walls and color 0 for open cells. It contains exactly one start marker 2, one end marker 3, checkpoints 4 and 5, and optionally checkpoint 6. Visit markers in numeric order 2 -> 4 -> 5 -> [6] -> 3. For each consecutive pair, take its unique shortest four-neighbor path through non-8 cells and paint only the zero cells on the combined path color 7. Preserve walls and all markers.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~10-18 by ~13-22) with THREE CORNER ANCHORS: (0, 0) = SEL color (color of the object to select); (0, w-1) = CODE (transform 1..4: id/rot-cw/rot-180/flip-lr); (h-1, 0) = FRAME color (color of the target hollow rectangular frame). Body contains: (a) ONE hollow rectangular frame in FRAME color (6-7 per side); (b) ONE connected object (2-4 cells) in SEL color (NOT at (0, 0)). Rule: read 3 anchors. Find sel-colored object (excluding (0, 0)) and frame-colored rectangular frame. Transform object by CODE. Fresh 0-canvas with only the frame redrawn. Center-paste transformed object inside the frame interior.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~6-8) containing exactly 2-3 single SEED cells in distinct non-zero colors from {2..9}, placed at interior positions with Manhattan distance > 3 between any two seeds. Rule: build an empty output grid; for every seed at (r,c), paint the surrounding 8-cell frame (all neighbors in the 3x3 box except the center) with that seed's color. Out-of-bounds neighbors are silently dropped.

N (2-5) small, well-separated, distinct-color shapes drawn from random rotation-classes (distinct-size base polyominoes, each placed at a random rotation). Rule: sort objects by (color, r1, c1) and output the N x N matrix where (i,j)=8 if objects i and j match under any rotation, else 0.

Exactly two distinct nonzero interior dots: one at row < floor(h/2) and one at row >= floor(h/2).  The selected rule paints the top edge, the upper dot row, and upper side columns in the upper dot colour; it paints the lower dot row, bottom edge, and lower side columns in the lower dot colour.

0-bg grid (h~6-14, w~8-16) with: (a) ONE COLOR-7 AXIS MARKER at column axis ∈ [2, w-3] (interior, with ≥1 col on each side), placed at random row axis_row ∈ [0, h-1] (cell (axis_row, axis) = 7); (b) 3-10 NON-BG NON-7 SOURCE CELLS placed at random distinct positions on EITHER side of the axis column (one side or scattered), each painted in a color cycling through a shuffled palette {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9}. For each source cell at (r, c), its mirror position (r, 2*axis-c) is bg-0 and in-bounds (constraint enforced). Rule (REFLECT EACH NON-BG NON-7 CELL ACROSS THE VERTICAL 7-AXIS COLUMN): find the COLOR-7 cell — its column is the AXIS. For EACH non-{0, 7} cell at (r, c) where c ≠ axis: COMPUTE the MIRROR position (r, 2*axis - c). PAINT the mirror cell with the SAME COLOR as the source (only if currently bg-0). The 7-axis marker and source cells stay. Net: every colored cell off the axis gets a mirror copy on the other side, producing left-right symmetry around the 7-axis.

Split the 5-row input at blank separator columns into N=3..5 width-5 panels. Crop each panel to its nonzero bounding box and compare binary support, ignoring foreground color and placement. Output an N×N matrix: 8 on the diagonal, 1 for exact normalized support, 2 for a non-identity rotation, 3 for a reflection/other dihedral image, and 0 otherwise.
Keep only the unique largest 4-connected nonzero object.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-12) with 2-5 GREEN (COLOR-3) L-TRIOMINOES — each a 3-cell L-shape in one of 4 ORIENTATIONS (NE/NW/SE/SW), placed at non-touching positions (≥3-cell separation). L-triominoes have a clear BEND CELL — the corner cell where two arms meet (4-conn degree 2 in the tromino). Rule (RECOLOR L-TRIOMINO BEND CELLS TO RED): For EACH GREEN L-TROMINO of 3 cells: identify the BEND CELL (corner of the L — the cell where both arms meet, with 2 non-zero neighbors in the tromino). RECOLOR that cell to COLOR-2 (red). The two arm cells stay green. Net: each L-tromino's corner pixel turns red; arms stay green.
Nested hollow color-9 rectangular frames contain same-colored marker cells. Recolor each marker by its strict frame-containment depth, while leaving every frame and background cell unchanged.
Dense rows of mixed colors with a clear majority per row.

Keep every red seed and paint each in-bounds blank orthogonal neighbour blue. Lessons include interior, clipped-edge, and shared-arm layouts; the latter two co-occur often enough to make every three-demo window identify the local four-neighbour rule.
Infer periodic long-run spacing, then extend full columns or choose the maximal nested-L completion; fill non-path cells gray.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~8-10) with 4 BLOBS at hardcoded border positions: (a) 2-cell vertical bar TOUCHING TOP BORDER at column tc; (b) 2-cell vertical bar TOUCHING LEFT BORDER at row lr; (c) 1-cell bar TOUCHING RIGHT BORDER at row rr; (d) 2-3 cell INTERIOR BLOB growth in the middle. Each in a DISTINCT color from {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Rule (RECOLOR BY BORDER CONTACT): for EACH BLOB, check which BORDER its cells touch: (a) blob touching ROW 0 (top) → RECOLOR to COLOR 2 (red); (b) touching COL 0 (left) → COLOR 4 (yellow); (c) touching COL w-1 (right) → COLOR 6 (magenta); (d) fully INTERIOR (no border) → COLOR 8 (cyan). Net: blobs recolored by which border they touch.

Two to seven distinct-color, solid, separated rectangles on background 0. In top/left order, output their pairwise row/column projection matrix: both=3, row only=1, column only=2, neither=0. Alternate teaching inputs that distinguish ordering and one-cell overlaps with varied layouts.

Two to four isolated, differently colored objects with distinct occupied cell counts. The selected rule sorts by occupied cells and packs bbox crops; two of every three ordinary samples refute the canonical-fitting bbox-area shortcut.

FIXED 15×15 grid with COLOR-7 (orange) BACKGROUND. (a) ONE ASYMMETRIC RED(2) SHAPE drawn from a shape bank of 4-cell tetrominoes (L, J, T, S, Z, etc.); (b) ONE 2×2 GRAY(5) BLOCK. The two are separated along ONE DOMINANT AXIS (horizontal: red and gray on same rows, different columns; vertical: same columns, different rows) with the SLIDE DIRECTION from red toward gray being one of {right, left, down, up}. Rule (SLIDE RED TOWARD GRAY, DOCK; REPLACE GRAY WITH REFLECTED RED): DETECT slide axis (red position vs gray position). SLIDE the red shape as a rigid group toward gray until they are adjacent (red's leading cell touches gray's bbox). REPLACE the gray block with a REFLECTED COPY of the red shape (LR reflection if sliding horizontally, UD reflection if vertically) painted in red. Bg-7 preserved. Net: red shape docks beside gray, gray transforms into the red's mirror image.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-13) with 3-5 SEPARATED 3-CELL STRAIGHT LINES, each either HORIZONTAL (cells at (r, c..c+2)) or VERTICAL (cells at (r..r+2, c)), each in a DISTINCT non-zero color (random from 1..9). Lines are 4-conn isolated with ≥1-cell gap between them (guard neighborhood enforced during placement). Rule: identify EACH 3-CELL STRAIGHT LINE (connected component that is exactly 3 cells in a row or column). COLLAPSE each line to its CENTER CELL ONLY — keep the middle cell of the 3, ERASE the two endpoint cells to BG (0). Endpoint cells: for a horizontal line at (r, c..c+2), erase (r, c) and (r, c+2); for vertical, erase (r, c) and (r+2, c). Net: each 3-line shrinks to its single center-cell dot in the same color.

Mirror every colored cell left of one full-height color-9 divider to the equal-distance cell on the right, preserving each source color. Lawful inputs vary dimensions, source count, palette cardinality, connectedness, and centered/off-center divider placement.

skills: symmetry detection, tile classification, symbolic output
summary: A one-row strip of 3x3 tiles is classified by vertical mirror symmetry; the output contains 8 for symmetric tiles and 0 otherwise.
Fill a zero exactly between equal nonzero horizontal neighbours; generated scenes include wide-gap, mismatched, and vertical negatives.

Fill horizontal gaps independently inside every same-color four-connected object.  A four-scene schedule preserves canonical one-object examples and adds disconnected same-color witnesses and row-varying object boundaries that separate the intended rule from color-merging and right-alignment shortcuts.

On a 0-background grid, locate the unique color-1 source marker, the unique color-2 destination marker, and the unique monochrome non-marker object. Translate every object cell by marker2-marker1 onto an otherwise empty grid. Paint translated 4-neighbor boundary cells orange (7) and strict interior cells cyan (8); clip translated cells that leave the canvas. Ordinary five-example windows include canonical-scale full and clipped rectangles, all vector quadrants, overlap, and a concave object that distinguishes topological boundary from bounding-box border.
Place isolated T-shapes whose degree-3 centers are highlighted.

Color-1 (blue) background grid (~12-22 per side) with non-bg OBJECTS arranged in a regular N×M GRID LAYOUT (N, M = 3..5 each). All objects share a single non-1 color, each 1-2 cells, separated by ≥1 cell of bg. Rule: detect all non-bg objects (bg=1). Determine each object's row-index ri (in sorted unique top-rows) and column-index ci (in sorted unique left-cols). If object is on the BORDER of the layout (ri == 0 OR ri == N-1 OR ci == 0 OR ci == M-1), recolor its cells to color 2 (red). Otherwise (interior of layout), recolor to color 3 (green). Background stays 1.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~8-10) with 2-3 ACTIVE ROWS each containing EXACTLY 2 COLOR-1 (blue) cells at distinct columns separated by ≥2 col gap, PLUS 1 DISTRACTOR ROW with ONE ISOLATED color-1 cell. Other rows are 0. Rule (FOR EACH ROW WITH EXACTLY 2 COLOR-1 CELLS, FILL ALL CELLS BETWEEN THEM INCLUSIVE WITH COLOR 1): For EACH ROW r: COUNT non-bg color-1 cells. If EXACTLY 2 at columns (c1, c2): PAINT every cell in row r from min(c1, c2) to max(c1, c2) (inclusive) with COLOR 1. Rows with 0, 1, or ≥3 color-1 cells stay unchanged. Net: 2-cell rows fill in to solid blue bars; 1-cell distractors remain as singletons.
Isolated cyan singleton cells gain a magenta cell immediately to the right.

A single source in color 3/4/6/7/8/9 sits on a non-corner border cell and launches a beam inward. Color 1 is a slash mirror, color 2 a backslash mirror, and color 5 a wall. The beam paints traversed black cells with the source color, turns at reached mirrors, and stops at a wall or boundary. Every ordinary draw reaches at least one mirror; optional off-route mirrors and walls teach that only objects encountered by the beam matter. One cyclic lesson role crosses an earlier beam cell and visibly continues afterward.

Read the three-colour priority legend at row 0, parse the cyan-wall chambers below it, and fill each chamber with its highest-priority present seed colour.  Lessons vary horizontal, vertical, and 2x2 wall layouts, including unequal partitions that defeat midpoint shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-11, w ∈ 11-13) with four singleton marker cells in colors 2, 3, 4, and 6 at randomized non-overlapping positions, plus one connected color-1 template (line or L triomino) and one non-cyan decoration in color 7 or 9. Rule: compute v = (pos(3)-pos(2)) + (pos(6)-pos(4)); for each color-1 template cell, paint color 8 at the translated cell when it is in-bounds and background. Normal generation guarantees the translated template cells are in-bounds/background so the cyan copy is fully visible.

Place 3-8 separated colour-{2,3,4} objects of equal cell count. Exactly one shape occurs twice, while another object is a rotated or reflected version that is not exactly equal. Sort objects row-major and output the pairwise translation-normalized exact-shape equality matrix (8/0).

On a 0-background grid, every color that appears exactly twice on a non-trivial 45-degree diagonal fills its inclusive span. Colors are processed in row-major first-appearance order, so the later color owns crossings. A five-sample schedule covers disjoint and crossing spans, both endpoint outcomes, plus axis-pair/singleton/triple controls.

Read rank k from the upper-left and a transform command from the upper-right. Remove both commands, rank the three separated body objects by area descending/color ascending, crop the k-th object, and transform it.
Separated singleton markers expand into horizontal bars of length three.

Read three equal square panels separated by full color-5 columns. Infer the D4 transform mapping panel A to panel B, then apply it to panel C. Ordinary lessons cover all eight transforms with connected asymmetric motifs and preserve a recurring canonical 5x17 profile.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 9-14, w ∈ 11-16, by difficulty) with: EXACTLY TWO COLOR-3 (GREEN) CONNECTED MOTIFS of STRICTLY DIFFERENT SIZES — drawn from SIZE_PAIR (e.g., (2, 4) for easy/medium, (3, 6) for hard) shuffled, each motif built via _build_motif random adjacent-step walk, placed at non-overlapping positions via _free check (1-cell padding). Both motifs painted in COLOR 3 only. Retries up to 40 outer × 120 inner attempts. Rule (FIND THE SMALLER OF THE 2 COLOR-3 MOTIFS, SCALE IT 2× (EACH CELL → 2×2 BLOCK), RECOLOR THE SCALED COPY TO COLOR 8 (CYAN); LARGER MOTIF DISCARDED): EXTRACT both COLOR-3 components and compute their cell counts. SELECT the SMALLER one (with fewer cells). UPSCALE its cells by factor 2: each (r, c) in the original becomes a 2×2 BLOCK at (2r..2r+1, 2c..2c+1). PAINT every cell of the upscaled shape with COLOR 8 (cyan). OUTPUT the scaled cyan crop (on a fresh canvas sized to the scaled bbox). Net: smaller motif is enlarged and recolored cyan; larger motif is gone.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~7-10) with 2-4 ENDPOINT PAIRS in distinct non-bg colors. Each pair is AXIALLY ALIGNED (horizontal or vertical) with an EVEN SPAN between the two endpoints (span ∈ {2, 4, 6}, so there is a SINGLE integer MIDPOINT cell between them). Pairs don't overlap. The cells between the endpoints are 0. Rule: for each color appearing exactly TWICE at axially-aligned endpoints with an even span between them, COMPUTE the MIDPOINT cell (((r1+r2)/2, (c1+c2)/2)). PAINT that single midpoint cell with the pair's color. Endpoints stay; other cells in the span stay 0. Net: each endpoint pair gets its exact midpoint marked in the pair's color — no full bridge, just the center dot.
One 3-frame with one interior 3-marker; fill the interior with Chebyshev rings from the marker (even=2, odd=4).

Rooms separated by colour-1 walls each hold a motif; the rule marks (1xN strip, colour 8) the rooms whose motif is dihedral-unique. N-1 rooms share a motif (up to dihedral); one is the odd one out. Room count, motifs and odd position vary.
skills: shape normalization, dihedral equivalence, odd-one-out detection

summary: 1 single-cell anchor + 1 connected motif in another color.
1 color-1 template + 2-4 scattered key cells in {2, 3, 4, 5}.

Color-9 markers (either 4 corners or a full rectangular frame) define a bbox. Rule outputs the INTERIOR rectangle: rows (r1+1)..(r2-1), cols (c1+1)..(c2-1), where (r1,c1,r2,c2) is the bbox of all 9-cells. The interior contains content cells; the 9-cells themselves and the cells outside the bbox are dropped.

Three square panels of size n∈{3,4,5} separated by full color-8 divider columns. Panel A is a random asymmetric 3-color support; panel B is a visible transform of A with a consistent recolor; panel C uses only A's source colors. Rule: infer the transform and recolor from A→B, then apply both to C and emit the transformed/recolored query panel.
Place a monochrome 2x2 body on background 0 with one to four diagonal corner tails; the rule extends every tail diagonally away from the body through the grid edge.
Single horizontal 2-bar at left edge; rule expands triangles above/below.
Two 4-row panels separated by row 4; aligned both-zero cells become 3.

Place two to four rotation-classes of separate red polyominoes; exactly one class occurs once or three times and every other class occurs twice. The rule fills every odd-class object's bounding box with orange.

Two equal-size panels are stacked vertically. Output cell (r,c) is 2 exactly when both aligned panel cells are 0, otherwise 0. Normal draws contain all four aligned occupancy states, use distinct non-2 panel colors, and vary dimensions, colors, positive-mask count, and layout.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 7-14 / 5-18, w ∈ 8-16 / 6-20, by difficulty) with: (a) ONE HOLLOW COLOR-8 RECTANGULAR FRAME — fr × fc outline drawn at (r0, c0) with frame_size_kind ∈ {small / medium / large / wide / tall} (fr, fc both ≥4); position bias center (anchored) or spread (random); (b) 0-3 INTERIOR COLOR-8 NOISE CELLS — n_interior_8s additional 8-cells placed at random positions strictly inside the frame's bounding box (rows r0+1..r0+fr-2, cols c0+1..c0+fc-2). No color 2 in input. Rule (FIND ALL COLOR-8 CELLS' BBOX, FILL EVERY 0 INSIDE THAT BBOX WITH COLOR 2): COMPUTE the BOUNDING BOX of all color-8 cells (rmin, cmin, rmax, cmax). For EVERY (r, c) with rmin ≤ r ≤ rmax AND cmin ≤ c ≤ cmax: IF g[r][c] == 0: PAINT g[r][c] = COLOR 2 (red). Color-8 frame and interior 8s stay 8. Cells OUTSIDE the bbox stay 0. Net: the 8-frame's interior fills red; interior 8-noise cells punch holes in the red fill.

A gray(5)-walled maze contains exactly two same-colored portals. Read the portals in row-major order and BFS from the first through 0-cells using neighbor priority right, down, left, up. On a fresh 0-grid preserve the walls and paint the first-discovered shortest path, including both portals, with the portal color. Consecutive samples schedule a unique route plus ties that separately expose R>D, D>L, and L>U priority.

0-bg grid with K rows each holding EXACTLY two non-zero markers at distinct columns (>=2 apart, so a gap exists), in varied colors; other rows empty. Rule: for each row with exactly two non-zero cells, fill the inclusive span between them with color 8. Net: each marker pair becomes an 8-colored bar.
Small bg=7 grid with 3-cell triangle in one corner of one non-7 color.
Among several green components, the unique odd-area component recolors blue.

Place one full gray row, one full gray column, or their intersection as walls. Scatter red seeds in the resulting two or four chambers with one strict count winner. Fill only that chamber's black cells with cyan.
Cells on the left of a full color-8 vertical bar are mirrored to the right.

0-bg grid (h, w~9-14) with: (a) CELL (0, 0) holds the TARGET COLOR (a value in {1..9}); (b) ONE LARGEST TARGET OBJECT in the TARGET COLOR — a random connected polyomino (sizes 4-9, varied bbox) at random interior position; (c) optionally ONE SMALLER TARGET OBJECT (size 1..target_size-2) in the same color, strictly smaller; (d) 0-3 DISTRACTOR BLOBS in DISTINCT non-target colors, each strictly smaller than the target. All blobs with 1-cell padding. Output crops vary by random target shape, bbox, and color. Rule (CROP LARGEST TARGET-COLOR OBJECT TO BBOX): READ TARGET COLOR T = g[0][0]. Identify all OBJECTS in color T (excluding (0, 0)). Find the LARGEST. CROP to BBOX. EMIT the cropped subgrid. Net: (0, 0) names color; biggest object of that color is extracted.
Sparse non-zero cells; gravity pulls them down to the floor.

Rows 0-1 hold a contiguous top-left source→target color legend with 2..4 distinct, disjoint pairs spanning aligned, crossed, and noncyclic rank pairings. Rows 2 onward contain 4..10 source-color cells (every source appears) and 0..4 unmapped value/neutral distractor cells. Output clears the legend, applies the aligned substitutions, and preserves unmapped body colors in place.

Fixed 6×6 grid with: (a) ROW 0 cells (0, 3) and (0, 5) hold COLUMN command codes (1..8); (b) COLUMN 0 cells (3, 0) and (5, 0) hold ROW command codes (1..8); (c) rows 3-5 × cols 3-5 hold a 3×3 SOURCE MOTIF with 3-6 cells in a single non-zero color. Rule (2×2 TRANSFORM MOSAIC): build a 2×2 grid of 3×3 mosaics. For each output position (r, c) in the 2×2: APPLY col_cmd[c] to the source, then row_cmd[r]. PACK the four 3×3 panels with 1-cell gaps. Output dims: 7×7 (2×3 + gap). Codes: 1=identity, 2=rotate CW, 3=rotate 180°, 4=transpose, 5=flip-LR, 6=flip-UD, 7=transpose (canonical duplicate), 8=anti-transpose. Net: row × col cmd grid yields a 2×2 transform mosaic of the 3×3 source.
1 random asymmetric source shape (color 5-9) + 2-4 marker cells with distinct codes in {1,2,3,4}; rule stamps the source rotated (code-1)*90deg CW (recolored to the code) at each marker.

Maze grid (h×w, ~8-13 by ~9-15) with color-5 (gray) BORDER walls around the entire perimeter and 0 interior. EXACTLY ONE color-2 (red) marker and ONE color-3 (green) marker placed in the interior at distinct positions. Optionally, 5-8 INTERIOR wall cells (color 5) scattered in the interior, creating asymmetric path obstacles (not blocking either marker from anything else). Rule: BFS from red and from green through 0-cells, avoiding 5-walls (4-conn). For each 0-cell reachable from BOTH markers, if dist_red == dist_green, paint it color 8. Output: markers + walls preserved, plus a 'perpendicular bisector' of color 8 cells.

Square 5..12 grids with 3..9 colored off-diagonal sources. Distinct transpose orbits keep destinations empty; source positions span multiple rows and columns and occur on both sides of the main diagonal, so the additive transpose rule cannot be learned as an upper-triangle-only shortcut.

0-bg grid (h 10..20, w 12..22) with 2-4 hollow gray(5) rectangle frames (distinct interior areas) and 2-4 arbitrary-shaped movers (distinct non-5 colors, distinct cell counts 1..5; singletons, dominoes, bars, L/S/T tetrominoes, plus/T/V/W pentominoes). Rule: rank frames by interior area and movers by size, then stamp each mover's normalized shape centered into the same-rank frame's interior on a blank canvas.
Find the single nonzero hollow axis-aligned rectangle.  Keep its bounding box and color, but paint every cell in that box on a fresh zero grid.

0-bg grid (h~11-14, w~14-18) with 3 ISOLATED COMPONENTS each in a DISTINCT color from {1..9}\{0}, each with a DISTINCT HOLE COUNT from {0, 1, 2}: (a) SOLID rect (0 holes); (b) HOLLOW RING (1 hole); (c) DOUBLE-RING with 2 holes. Components placed non-touching with 1-cell padding. Rule (SORT BY (HOLE_COUNT ASC, AREA ASC, COLOR ASC), PACK CROPS LEFT-TO-RIGHT WITH 1-COL GAPS): identify all 4-conn COMPONENTS. For EACH: CROP to BBOX, COUNT enclosed-zero holes (regions of 0 inside the bbox that don't touch the rim). SORT by (hole_count asc, area asc, color asc). HCONCAT the cropped components left-to-right with 1-COL GAPS in sorted order. Net: components rearranged by hole complexity, packed horizontally.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 6-8, w ∈ 7-9) with: 2-3 NON-OVERLAPPING BLOBS, each a 2-3 cell irregular blob built via grow_blob random walk, each in a DISTINCT color drawn from {1..9}. Blobs placed with shared used-set tracking. Each blob's bbox checker-fill differs from the input (since blobs are non-rectangular or small). Rule (FOR EACH NON-BG COMPONENT, FILL ITS BBOX WITH A CHECKER PATTERN IN THE COMPONENT'S COLOR — CELLS WHERE (R - R1 + C - C1) % 2 == 0 GET THE COLOR, OTHERS STAY 0): For EACH blob with color c and bbox (r1..r2, c1..c2): For EVERY (r, c) in the bbox: IF (r - r1 + c - c1) % 2 == 0: PAINT g[r][c] = color; ELSE: PAINT 0 (overwriting the blob's interior). Net: each irregular blob expands to a checker-filled rectangle in its color.
Find same-color 4-connected nonzero objects, count how many other objects touch each one cardinally, and recolor the whole object by degree: 0->3, 1->4, 2->6, and 3+->8.

Place one hollow blue frame containing a connected yellow prototype. Place one to four isolated orange anchors elsewhere with room for the complete prototype footprint. Stamp every prototype offset at every anchor in cyan.
Random color-1 source shape + a control marker (2=id,3=rot90,4=reflect-h,6=reflect-v) + a color-9 anchor; the rule stamps the transformed source (color 8) at the anchor.

Color-5 walls form rectangular chambers (2×2 grid). Each chamber has 1-3 colored seed cells. Rule fills each bg (0) cell within a chamber with the color of its NEAREST seed (Manhattan); ties broken by lower color value. Walls and seeds stay.
Exactly one color appears twice; its two cells define a filled rectangle.

Nonzero modal-bg grid (default h~12-22, w~12-22) with a SOLID BOTTOM BAND of band_h~3-7 rows containing a PATTERN (even_cols / odd_cols / halves / thirds / diagonal / checker / frame / scattered) painted in one or more colors distinct from the field/background color. Above the band, all rows are entirely the modal background. Rule: extract the band's pattern. TILE the band UPWARD by REPEATING the band's row sequence (or row-by-row period) through the empty rows above, filling them with the same band pattern until the entire grid is covered. Net: input has modal-bg top + a patterned band at bottom; output is the band's pattern REPLICATED upward to fill the whole grid.
On a zero background, replace every separated interior point marker by a same-color five-cell orthogonal plus, preserving grid size.

A black 8..10 by 11..14 grid contains three or four isolated red (2) 4-connected components with distinct left bounding-box columns. The strictly leftmost RED component is selected, all other cells are erased, and the selected shape is repainted cyan (8) in place. Some scheduled lessons include one non-red distractor further left; it is never selected.

Orange(7) field with ONE line (straight or diagonal, 2 endpoints) in line-color and 2-4 GLYPHS (all the same shape, including canonical X/I forms) in stamp-color, all separated. Rule: connect every pair of glyph centers with line-color lines, and stamp the glyph shape (stamp-color) centered at each of the line's two endpoints. Net: line endpoints <-> glyph stamps; glyph centers <-> a line network.
Small random template (non-0/non-8) + the matching 8-frame (interior == template bbox) + 1-2 distractor 8-frames of different interior size; the rule stamps the template into the matching frame only.
5 × 9 grid with key cells + right-panel mask; rule outputs 3 × 3 colored mask (fixed I/O dims, faithful to canonical).

0-bg grid with exactly 4 separated single-color objects (random polyominoes, 1-5 cells, distinct colors) at random positions. Rule: sort objects by (size, bbox-h, bbox-w, color), take the first 4, and arrange them in a 2x2 quadrant gallery separated by one blank row + column, each in its own color. Net: scattered objects gather into a compact 2x2 layout.
Select the remote object matching the top-left color and return its original tight bounding-box subgrid.
Canonical 3x3 row-repeated grids over swap colors; rule applies fixed permutation 1↔5, 2↔6, 3↔4, 8↔9 (colors 0, 7 unchanged).

A zero-background grid contains two to nine independent motifs. In each motif, two cells of one unique non-zero color lie exactly two cells apart in the same row or column, with a zero midpoint. The output fills every such midpoint with the matching endpoint color while preserving all endpoints. A different-color gap stays zero in every generated input/output pair. Horizontal and vertical negative gaps alternate, while positive modes cycle mixed/horizontal/vertical/mixed. Residues 0 and 3 use official-scale 7x7 or 8x8 scenes with two motifs; exact overrides remain available.

A zero-background grid contains one to three true rectangle-corner colors and one to three deliberately nonqualifying colors.  In first-appearance order, a color with exactly four cells at exactly the corners of its bbox fills that bbox into a fresh output; all other colors disappear.

An 8..22 by 8..22 zero-background grid contains 1..8 isolated interior colored pixels.  For each pixel at (r,c), the output keeps the pixel and draws one vertical arm to its nearer top/bottom edge plus one horizontal arm to its nearer left/right edge.  Exact center ties on odd dimensions resolve toward bottom and right, matching the canonical strict-less-than rule.  Generated complete L-ray footprints are pairwise disjoint, so each lesson has a unique answer without relying on unshown overlap precedence.

0-bg grid (size varies). A SOURCE L-frame (colors 2/3/4) with a color-8 MOTIF in its local frame, and 3-5 candidate L-frames (colors 5/6/7). Exactly ONE candidate's local motif equals the source motif ROTATED 90 degrees ((u,v)->(-v,u)); the rest are distractors with different signatures. Frame orientations vary freely (signatures are in local coords). Rule: output a 1xN strip with COLOR 8 at the matching candidate's index. The grid size, the source motif, the matching candidate, orientations and positions all vary freely (was a fixed 13x25 layout, ~9 distinct).
skills: transformed matching, candidate selection, symbolic output

summary: Transpose the whole sparse rectangular grid across its main diagonal: output[c][r] = input[r][c].  A four-profile curriculum mirrors the canonical one-color points, two compact blobs, and one blob plus two same-color singleton distractors, while each input refutes every other dihedral transform.

0-bg grid with one full-width color-9 separator row. Above it is a library of 3-4 distinct-color prototype polyominoes; below it is one key cell whose color selects a prototype and one color-8 anchor with room to stamp that prototype. Grid size, separator row, prototype shapes/positions, selected key, and anchor position all vary.

A 0-background grid contains 2-4 same-size rectangular frames and 1-3 differently sized distractor frames, all in distinct colors and separated by background. Exactly one same-size frame is the template: its interior contains a non-empty, non-solid pattern in its own color. The oracle keeps all frames matching the template's interior height and width, copies the relative pattern into each in that frame's color, and erases every mismatched frame.

Replace every 4-connected, same-color nonzero object by the frame of its tight bounding box on a fresh zero grid. Draw 2..4 separated objects with 1..4 distinct colors, varied positions and shapes, including fixed points. Disconnected objects may share a color; their frames stay separate.

A single color-2 border emitter sends a laser inward. The laser paints empty cells 7, reflects differently at color-4 and color-5 mirrors, and stops at color-8 walls or the boundary. A five-profile cyclic curriculum covers corner precedence, one- and two-reflection paths, active walls, boundary exits, and off-route mirror decoys.

A 6..10 by 7..12 grid has a complete color-8 outer border and 2..5 pairwise-distinct colored singleton seeds in its otherwise-zero interior. Fill each blank interior cell with the color of its Manhattan-nearest seed. On equal distances, choose the seed appearing first in row-major reading order. Preserve the border and all seed cells.
Row-0 legend (3 colors) + three 8-shapes of distinct sizes (1-5 cells) elsewhere; rule recolors each by its size-rank to the matching legend color.

Use the single blue (1) component as a shape template. Among green (3) components, keep exactly those matching the template under translation and any of four rotations, recoloring them cyan (8); drop the template, green nonmatches, and matching components in other colors. Generated lessons include rotated positives, equal-area/reflected negatives, and color-role distractors while retaining frequent canonical-profile inputs.

A 9..10 by 9..12 zero-background grid contains 3..5 singleton seed cells in pairwise-distinct colors excluding 0 and 8.
