Fill each zero with the color of its uniquely nearest seed under Manhattan distance; if two or more seeds tie for minimum distance, paint the cell cyan (8). Preserve all seed cells.

On a 0-background grid containing green(3) sources and blue(2) blockers, inspect each green source independently. If its one-step down-right cell is in bounds and 0, paint that destination gray(5); if the destination is already nonzero, leave it unchanged. Preserve all original 2s and 3s.

A zero-background grid contains one or more disjoint solid square nested frames. Each frame has a uniform nonzero outer ring and a distinct uniform nonzero inner fill. The canonical output expands every frame about its center into a larger rounded nested frame motif.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~12-17) with: (a) a CONTROL CODE at (0, 0) drawn as a single non-bg cell with color ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} (each code corresponds to a different dihedral transform of the template); (b) a small color-6 (magenta) TEMPLATE polyomino (L-tetromino-like) placed near the top-left; (c) a single color-7 (orange) ANCHOR cell placed near the bottom-right indicating the stamp position. The template and anchor do not overlap. Rule: read the control code at (0, 0) and select the corresponding TRANSFORM (e.g., 1 = identity, 2 = rotate-CW, 3 = rotate-180, 4 = rotate-CCW or similar). Apply that transform to the magenta template. PAINT the transformed shape in color 8 (cyan) at the anchor's position on the original grid. Original template and anchor stay. Net: a cyan copy of the template (transformed per the control code) is stamped at the anchor.

Grid h × (3*pw + 2) (h~4-5, pw~4-5) with: (a) two full-height color-8 (cyan) DIVIDER columns at col pw and col 2*pw+1, splitting grid into 3 equal panels (A, B, C). Panels A and B share the SAME 3-4 cell shape (but in different colors); panel C uses a different shape (and color). Rule: extract the 3 panels by subgrid; binarize each (non-bg → 1). Output is a 3×3 PAIRWISE MASK-EQUAL MATRIX where out[i][j] = 1 if panels[i].binary == panels[j].binary (under normalization). With the generator's A==B, A!=C, B!=C structure, output is always [[1,1,0],[1,1,0],[0,0,1]].

Two separated 4-connected fragments each contain one red(2) connector. Sort the fragments by connector position, translate the second so its connector lands on the first, and paint the aligned union in color 6 (magenta) on a fresh same-size zero canvas. Ordinary draws use canonical canvas sizes and partial overlaps that refute one-fragment, bbox-alignment, solid-bbox, and in-place-recolor shortcuts.

Separated gray objects on black.  Recolor exactly the 1x2 horizontal components cyan; leave a vertical domino and a horizontal-adjacency near miss gray.  Four scheduled profiles retain every canonical shape.

0-bg grid (size varies) with N identical frame-color lattices (an R x C array of single-cell slots). Each slot's color appears in some lattices; the rule completes every empty matching slot with that color. The lattice dims, template count, colors and positions vary freely (was a fixed 8x14 setup, ~38 distinct).

0-bg grid (h×w, ~7-10 by ~6-10) with 3-6 'active' columns. Each active column has 1-3 SCATTERED non-zero cells at various rows (NOT all at the top — at least one cell below the top row). Cells use random colors. Inactive columns are entirely 0. Rule: for each column c independently, collect all non-zero values top-to-bottom (preserving order). Pack them at the TOP of the column starting at row 0. Remaining cells become 0. Equivalent to upward gravity.

5-panel grid (size varies) split by all-8 columns: ea, eb, eo demonstrate a binary set op (union/intersection/xor by support, eo in one color), then ta, tb are the operands. Rule: output OP(ta, tb) recolored with ta's dominant color. The operation, panel patterns/sizes and output color vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).

Row 0 and column 0 are label headers over a color-0 interior. For each interior cell, copy its column header exactly when that color equals the row header; otherwise keep 0. Preserve both header strips.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~13-15) with: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) GUIDE SHAPE — a 3-5 cell shape chosen from a shape bank, placed at random non-touching position; (b) 1-3 COLOR-9 (maroon) ANCHOR CELLS placed at random positions with room for stamping; (c) TWO CANDIDATE SHAPES in DISTINCT non-{2, 9} colors — one shape is a DIHEDRAL VARIANT (rotation/reflection) of the GUIDE; the other is a DIFFERENT shape. Rule (FIND THE DIHEDRALLY-MATCHING CANDIDATE, STAMP IT AT EVERY 9-ANCHOR): identify the GUIDE (color-2) and the 2 CANDIDATES (non-{0, 2, 9})). For EACH CANDIDATE, check if its normalized shape matches any rotation/reflection of the guide's normalized shape. Pick the MATCHING CANDIDATE. CROP it. Produce a FRESH BLANK output grid; STAMP the matching candidate's crop (in its color) at each 9-ANCHOR position. Guide, non-matching candidate, and 9-anchors are DISCARDED.

Place one to three separated, distinctly colored, solid odd-by-odd rectangles on a zero background. Replace every rectangle by the union of its geometric middle row and middle column on a fresh zero canvas.

A zero-background grid contains several rows with exactly two equal nonzero endpoints separated by at least two zero cells. Fill each such interval inclusively with its endpoint color; blank and explicitly non-qualifying distractor rows stay unchanged.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-12) with 3 DISTINCT NON-0 COLORS scattered at distinct positions: (a) MAJORITY color appears 6-10 times (strictly highest count); (b) TWO MINORITY colors each appear 1-3 times. Cells placed at random positions without overlap. Rule (KEEP ONLY THE NONZERO MAJORITY COLOR): identify the NON-0 COLOR with STRICTLY HIGHEST FREQUENCY in the grid (the majority). KEEP all cells of the majority color. ERASE all other non-0 cells (set to 0). Net: minority colors vanish; only the dominant color survives.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-12) with 2-4 DIAGONAL PAIRS — each pair is two SAME-COLOR cells along the MAIN DIAGONAL (slope +1): pick length L ∈ {2..5}; pick start (r0, c0); endpoint at (r0+L, c0+L). PAINT only the two endpoints in the pair's color; cells (r0+k, c0+k) for k ∈ [1..L-1] are bg-0 (the diagonal span). Each pair uses a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn from {1..9}. Diagonal spans don't overlap (placement tracked in reserved set). Rule (FILL EACH MAIN-DIAGONAL SPAN BETWEEN SAME-COLOR ENDPOINTS WITH THAT COLOR): for EACH color C that appears at exactly TWO cells (r0, c0) and (r0+L, c0+L) on the SAME MAIN-DIAGONAL LINE (slope +1, equal row-step and col-step): PAINT every cell (r0+k, c0+k) for k in [1..L-1] with COLOR C. Endpoints stay. Anti-diagonal pairs and non-pair cells are unchanged. Net: each diagonal pair becomes a solid diagonal colored line.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-13) with 2-4 ISOLATED HOLLOW 3×3 COLOR-4 (yellow) RINGS at scattered positions, each with ≥4 cell separation from the others (no overlap of 3×3 windows). Each ring is an 8-cell outline (3×3 - center) with a 0 center cell. Rule (FILL RING CENTERS WITH COLOR 2): identify each HOLLOW 3×3 RING (8-cell color-4 frame with 0 center). For EACH ring, PAINT the CENTER CELL (at (r0+1, c0+1)) with COLOR 2 (red). The 8 ring cells stay color 4. Net: each yellow ring gets a red dot painted in its center.

0-bg grid containing one rectangular cyan(8) frame. The top row of the frame has 2-3 color-2 markers replacing 8s at interior columns {cm}. The left column of the frame has 2-3 color-2 markers replacing 8s at interior rows {rm}. The frame interior is all 0. Rule: for each (row r in left-markers, col c in top-markers), if g[r][c] is 0, set it to color 3. Output is the input with those intersection cells filled in.

Three equal square panels are separated by full color-5 columns. Crop A, B and C to their nonzero bounding boxes; choose the first transform in identity/rot-cw/rot-180/transpose/flip-lr/flip-ud that maps binary(A) to binary(B); apply it to C and recolor every foreground cell with B's color. A four-profile schedule includes two ambiguous first-match cases and independently translates A and B, refuting uncropped-panel matching.

Orange(7) background field with one full grid edge maroon (9). Cyan (8) cells move one step toward the maroon edge each application. Cyan cells whose entire 4-neighborhood is red (2) or cyan (8) are enclosed and become red. Red and background unchanged.

Extract the bbox of the largest eligible left-right symmetric object. Objects use same-color four-connectivity; eligibility requires width > 1 and exact color equality of every mirrored bbox pixel. Size counts object cells, not bbox area. Default four-draw lessons distinguish larger ineligible objects, varying occupied-size rank, smaller symmetric decoys, scan order, bbox area, width-one bars and disconnected objects sharing a color. Half the default profiles use canonical 10x10 grids with three nonzero colors; two profiles refute the canonical-fitting bottommost-eligible shortcut.

0-bg grid (h×w, h=4..6, w=7..9) with SPARSE non-zero cells. 3-4 columns are 'active' (have ≥1 non-zero cell at random rows in random non-zero colors). Other columns are entirely zero (the columns-to-drop). Active cell colors drawn from varied palette. Rule: iterate over columns. Keep only columns where at least one cell is non-zero. Output: each row projected to the kept columns only (in original column order). Output height = h (unchanged); width = number of active columns.

0-bg grid of 3 PANELS (each panel_w wide, panel_h tall) separated by single DIVIDER COLUMNS (color 5). panel0=BEFORE (a base shape in color A), panel1=AFTER (base + a connected DELTA of extra cells, color A), panel2=QUERY (the SAME base shape in color B). Rule: read the object in each panel; DELTA = cells AFTER has that BEFORE lacks (both normalized); output = the QUERY panel with DELTA painted in color B at the query's top-left. Net: before→after growth applied to query (before:after :: query:output).

On a black grid, identify complete color-3 cardinal plus centers. Connect every diagonal-aligned pair, painting only intervening zero cells red (2). Inputs include two-plus pairs, three-plus collinear/bent/skipped-pair scenes, and five-plus crossing networks with green arms on both bridges. A three-demonstration curriculum retains a compound witness under each single-query rotation. The canonical Racket authority is unchanged.

0-bg grid with a SOURCE L-frame (color-2 origin, color-3 along one cardinal axis vx, color-4 along a perpendicular axis vy), SATELLITE cells of color 8 and/or 9 scattered within Chebyshev radius 3 of the origin (in source-local coords), and a TARGET L-frame (color-5 origin, color-6 along vx', color-7 along vy') of independent orientation placed clear of the source. Rule: copy each satellite to the TARGET frame at the SAME local coordinates (so the constellation is re-placed around the target, rotated/reflected to the target's orientation). Source frame + satellites stay.
skills: multicolor transport, local coordinates, orientation change

summary: Echo every nonzero source across the main diagonal, retaining the originals.
Place one to six separated red L-triominoes in all orientations, plus optional red non-L and non-red shape distractors. Recolor only each qualifying red L's elbow yellow.

On a black background, every cardinally isolated red (2) singleton with an empty in-bounds right neighbour moves exactly one column right. Multi-cell red components and non-red distractors stay fixed. Default lessons deliberately include canonical-only and shortcut-rebutting scenes.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~11-13) with 1-2 HOLLOW RECTANGULAR COLOR-8 (cyan) FRAMES — each a rectangle outline of width × height 4-5 (interior is 0). EACH FRAME strictly CONTAINS EXACTLY ONE SEED CELL at a random INTERIOR position (inside the frame, not on the border) in a SEED COLOR distinct from 0 and 8. Frames are placed at non-touching positions (≥1-cell padding). Rule (FILL EACH ENCLOSED INTERIOR WITH ITS SEED'S COLOR): For EACH COLOR-8 FRAME: find the bg-0 cells strictly INSIDE the frame's border (the enclosed region NOT border-reachable). IDENTIFY the SEED — the lone non-0 non-8 cell inside the frame's interior; its color is C. PAINT every BG-0 cell in the interior with COLOR C. The frame border stays at 8. The seed stays at C. Net: each frame's interior becomes solid in the seed's color.

Exactly two magenta (6) markers share a row or column with at least one empty cell between them. Paint only those strict-interior cells cyan (8), preserving both magenta endpoints and every off-segment decoration.

0-background grid with 1-3 distinct-color odd-by-odd hollow rectangular frames and one distinct-color hollow even-dimension decoy, all separated by at least one background cell. Rule: add one same-color cell at the exact bbox center of each frame whose height and width are both odd; leave the even-dimension decoy unchanged.
Keep only the unique smallest 4-connected nonzero component.
Colored objects slide rightward until they pack against a gray wall.

skills: room boundaries, wall extraction, boundary rendering
summary: A one- to four-row by one- to four-column lattice of rectangular rooms is separated by color-1 walls, optionally with color-7 door cells. One or more rooms contain a color-2 seed, centered or off center. Paint on a blank grid the color-1/color-7 wall cells immediately adjacent to every seeded room.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~9-11) with: (a) TRANSFORM CODE at (0, 0) in COLOR ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} encoding rotation/flip (1=IDENTITY, 2=ROT CW, 3=ROT 180, 4=ROT CCW, 5=FLIP LR or similar); (b) TARGET COLOR at (0, w-1) in some non-{0, code, body_color} color (the destination color for the transformed body); (c) BODY SHAPE — one ASYMMETRIC SHAPE from a small bank (L-tetromino, T-tetromino, S-tetromino) in a DISTINCT non-{0, code, target} color at random interior position. Rule (CROP THE BODY SHAPE, TRANSFORM PER CODE, RECOLOR TO TARGET COLOR): READ the CODE from (0, 0) and TARGET COLOR from (0, w-1). CROP the body shape to its BBOX. APPLY the transform encoded by CODE. RECOLOR all non-bg cells in the transformed crop to TARGET COLOR. OUTPUT is the transformed + recolored body. Code, target, and original body are discarded. Net: the body is rotated/flipped per code and painted in the target color.

0-bg grid of 3 SQUARE panels (each s×s, s∈3..6) separated by single DIVIDER COLUMNS (color 5) at cols s and 2s+1; total width 3s+2, height s. panel0 holds a BASE MOTIF (random asymmetric cell set in base_color). panel1 holds T(base) where T is a chosen DIHEDRAL TRANSFORM ∈ {id, rot90, rot180, rot270, flip-lr, flip-ud, transpose, anti-transpose}. panel2 holds an INDEPENDENT QUERY MOTIF (random cell set in query_color). Rule (DIHEDRAL ANALOGY): split into 3 panels; INFER the transform T such that T(panel0)==panel1 exactly; APPLY T to panel2 and EMIT it. Net: panel0:panel1 :: panel2:output is a transform analogy; output is s×s.

Each color-5..9 object has one touching code cell. Codes 1/2/3/4 mean up/right/down/left. Remove every code, then paint a same-color ray from each original object cell in its coded direction through the grid edge.

0-bg grid (h~5-12, w~9-16) with: (a) ONE FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-8 (cyan) DIVIDER COLUMN at col gc (mid-grid so mirroring fits both sides); (b) 2-6 NON-{0, 8} MARKER CELLS scattered on the LEFT side of the divider (c < gc), each in a color from {1..9}\{0, 8}. RIGHT side (c > gc) starts all 0. Each left marker has a valid in-bounds mirror position. Rule (MIRROR LEFT-MARKER CELLS ACROSS 8-DIVIDER): For EACH LEFT-side non-{0, 8} marker at (r, c): COMPUTE mc = 2 * gc - c (mirror position on the right). PAINT g[r][mc] with the same color (overwriting the 0). Left markers, divider stay. Net: left-side markers reflect across the cyan divider to the right side.

A zero-background grid contains 2-4 separated, distinctly colored objects with asymmetric square bounding boxes. For each object, overlay its three clockwise quarter-turns inside its own bounding box. Every ordinary input contains a diagnostic object that rules out a 180-degree-only shortcut.

A 0-background grid contains 2-5 distinctly colored 4-connected objects. Sort objects by (bounding-box left column, bounding-box top row), tightly crop each object, and pack the crops horizontally with exactly one black column between neighbors. Vertically center every crop in an output whose height is the maximum crop height.

A command token at (0,0) selects a transform. Remove the token, crop the single connected interior object, and apply command 1=id, 2=cw, 3=180, 4=transpose, 5=flip-lr, 6=flip-ud, 7=transpose, or 8=anti-transpose.

BG-colored grid (h ∈ 7-30, w ∈ 7-30, by difficulty) painted uniformly with one bg color fixed to 0, containing: (a) ONE SOLID RECTANGLE of size rh × rw (rh ∈ 5..h-2, rw ∈ 5..w-2, both ≥5) at random interior position (rr, rc) with ≥1-cell margin from all grid edges, painted in rect_color (distinct from 0). (b) AT THE RECTANGLE'S FOUR INSIDE-CORNER CELLS — (rr+1, rc+1), (rr+1, rc+rw-2), (rr+rh-2, rc+1), (rr+rh-2, rc+rw-2) — paint 4 DISTINCT non-{0, rect_color} colors drawn from {0..9}. Rule (CLEAR THE FOUR INSIDE CORNERS (SET TO BACKGROUND 0) AND PLACE THE 4 CORNER COLORS AT THE FOUR DIAGONALLY-OPPOSITE OUTSIDE CORNERS OF THE RECTANGLE): IDENTIFY the rectangle (solid rect_color region) and its 4 inside-corner cells with their distinct colors c0, c1, c2, c3 (TL, TR, BL, BR of inside). CLEAR the 4 inside-corner marker cells to background 0, leaving four holes in the rectangle. PAINT the 4 OUTSIDE-CORNER cells of the rectangle: (rr-1, rc-1)=c3 (diagonally opposite TL→BR-corner), (rr-1, rc+rw)=c2 (TR→BL), (rr+rh, rc-1)=c1 (BL→TR), (rr+rh, rc+rw)=c0 (BR→TL). Net: inside colors jump to the diagonally-opposite outside corners while their former cells become background.

Fixed 12×14 0-bg grid with: (a) RANK CELL at (0, 0) painted with a value rank ∈ {1, 2, 3} encoding which size-ranked object to select; (b) ONE COLOR-9 MARKER placed in the lower-right region at (6+jitter, 8+jitter) (random ±1 perturbation); (c) THREE SOURCE OBJECTS at fixed positions sorted ASCENDING BY SIZE — _OBJECTS[0]=2-cell horizontal pair at (2, 1); _OBJECTS[1]=3-cell L-shape at (5, 1); _OBJECTS[2]=5-cell pentomino at (2, 5). Each object painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 9} color drawn from {2..8}. Sizes are strictly distinct: {2, 3, 5}. Rule (THE RANK AT (0, 0) PICKS A SIZE-RANKED SOURCE, UPSCALE IT 2×, PASTE AT THE 9-MARKER): READ the RANK at (0, 0) — 1→smallest, 2→middle, 3→largest. SELECT the corresponding source object. CROP it to its bbox. UPSCALE the crop by factor 2 (each cell → 2×2 block in same color). find the COLOR-9 MARKER position (mr, mc). PASTE the upscaled crop with its top-left at (mr, mc) on a FRESH OUTPUT GRID. The rank cell, marker, and original source objects are discarded. Net: a 2×-enlarged copy of the rank-selected object appears at the marker's location. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=33): 3 ranks × 3 fixed objects × marker positions × colors.
2-4 isolated single-color components with varied sizes/perimeters.
Paint cyan doubled-coordinate Manhattan auras around red bars, using each bar's bounding-box length as the threshold.

0-bg grid with EXACTLY TWO nonzero cells at OPPOSITE CORNERS of an axis-aligned rectangle (>=4x4). Rule: interpret them as opposite corners and paint the full rectangle BORDER with color 8 (the corner color is ignored -- any nonzero works; canonical uses 1). Corner color, rectangle size/position and grid size vary.

0-bg grid (size varies) with one non-5 PROTOTYPE shape and several color-5 hollow rectangle frames. Rule: frames whose interior matches the prototype's bbox get the prototype stamped inside (in its color); other frames stay empty. The grid size, prototype shape/color and frame sizes/positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~4-12, w~7-16) with 2-4 PAIR ROWS — each pair row holds EXACTLY 2 cells of COLOR 2 (red) at distinct columns (c_left, c_right), with a GAP = c_right - c_left. Gaps are assigned by one of 6 DISTRIBUTIONS (uniform / increasing / decreasing / min_at_top / min_at_bottom / alternating), starting from min_gap (2-3) and extending by up to extra (2-4). At least ONE row has the UNIQUE MINIMUM GAP (strict). Other rows (non-pair rows) have 0 cells of color 2. Pair-row positions are random (sampled without replacement). Rule (FILL CELLS BETWEEN THE TWO 2s IN EVERY ROW WHOSE GAP EQUALS THE OVERALL MINIMUM GAP): for EACH PAIR ROW r: COMPUTE its GAP = c_right - c_left. find the GLOBAL MINIMUM GAP across all pair rows. For EACH row whose gap = min_gap: FILL every cell (r, c) with c_left < c < c_right with COLOR 2 (the interior between the two 2s). The endpoint 2s stay; the other (larger-gap) pair rows keep just their endpoints unchanged. Net: the tightest pair row(s) become solid horizontal red bars; wider-gap rows stay as their two endpoints.

Three square n x n panels A | B | Q (n = height) separated by single divider columns (grid n x (3n+2)). Rule: output n x n where each cell is Q if A==B at that cell else B. Panels are filled so A and B partially overlap (both branches fire); panel size, colors and density vary.
Top-right target color, one color-1 reference, and two or three equally sized candidates; exactly one candidate is a requested rotation match.
Decode four selector-color and transform-code pairs into a 2x2 transformed template gallery.

Two aligned 3-column binary panels, separated by one nonzero marker column.  Output color 8 appears exactly at aligned 00 positions; 10, 01, and 11 positions all map to 0.  Normal draws contain every state, exclude answer color 8 from the input, and vary height, colors, count, and spatial layout.

A randomly oriented 5..10 square-or-rectangular perfect maze uses color 1 for walls and color 0 for walkable cells. Exactly two color-2 endpoints have one unique wall-forced shortest path with 2..4 turns, while unused walkable branches remain as distractors. Four-pair lesson windows cover all three canonical sizes and turn counts while repeating 10x10/four-turn evidence for query rotation safety. Fill only that shortest path with color 4 and preserve both endpoints as color 2.

One green(3) seed anchors a fixed stencil made of a 49-cell spiral path and a disconnected 11-cell lower bar. With no color-2 blockers, every in-bounds zero stencil cell is painted green. If any color-2 blocker exists anywhere, only the blocker-free stencil component 4-connected to the seed is painted: an on-path blocker cuts the spiral, while even an off-stencil blocker suppresses the disconnected bar. Scheduled lessons cover the no-blocker mask, the global off-mask switch, early/late cuts, varied blocker counts, shifted anchors, clipping, and varied grid sizes.

A left-edge palette contains 1-4 two-row source/frame color pairs. Every connected icon in a source color, excluding the palette swatch, gets its exterior zero region framed inside the icon bounding box expanded by one cell. Enclosed holes stay zero and frames clip at grid edges. Official-scale 20x20 and 26x26 scenes occur normally.

A 0-background grid contains one connected red(2) source shape beside a connected D4-asymmetric yellow(4) marker constellation. One to three transformed copies of that marker constellation occur elsewhere while their corresponding red footprints are empty. Match the marker constellation under every D4 transform and stamp the correspondingly transformed red shape at every match; preserve all yellow cells.

0-bg grid (size varies by difficulty) with: (a) COLUMN MARKERS — 1-5 columns in range [1, w-2] are marked by COLOR 3 (green) cells at BOTH row 0 AND row h-1 of the same column (full top+bottom pair); (b) ROW MARKERS — 1-5 rows in range [1, h-2] are marked by COLOR 2 (red) cells at BOTH col 0 AND col w-1 of the same row (full left+right pair). All marker columns and rows are interior (≥2 cells from each edge). All other cells are bg-0. Rule (AT EVERY (ROW, COL) CROSSING OF PAIRED MARKERS, PLACE COLOR 8): identify the SET of PAIRED COLUMNS (those with color-3 at both top and bottom). identify the SET of PAIRED ROWS (those with color-2 at both left and right). For EACH (r, c) with r ∈ paired rows AND c ∈ paired cols: PAINT cell (r, c) with COLOR 8 (cyan). The original markers stay; other cells stay bg-0. Net: every intersection of a marked row and marked column becomes a cyan dot, drawing the row × column lattice of crossings.

>=4 SQUARE panels (side s) separated by single full color-9 columns, each with a small motif in a non-{0,9} color. Rule: rotate the 3rd panel CW and overlay it onto the 4th panel; the rest is unchanged. Panels are square so the rotation fits the target cleanly. Panel side, count, motifs and colors vary.

0-bg grid; several rows each have exactly two same-color seeds spaced by `step`, placed left enough that the periodic pattern extends to the right edge. Rule: a row with exactly two same-color cells gets c0, c0+step, c0+2*step, ... painted rightward to the edge; other rows unchanged. Every seed-row extends (>=1 new cell); step, color, position, count and grid vary.

Color-7 (orange) BACKGROUND grid (row_count~4-7, w~8-12). Each row contains a visible RUN of 3-5 cells using two ALTERNATING non-7 colors {a, b} from a palette, where a < b. Rows alternate which color STARTS the run: even rows start with a (smaller); odd rows start with b (larger). Run start column and length vary per row. Rule: examine each row's visible run. If the run STARTS with the MAX of the two colors (the larger one), SHIFT the entire row's run ONE CELL RIGHT (i.e., the leftmost cell becomes 7-bg, the rightmost shifts into the cell right of the previous end). If it starts with the min color, leave the row unchanged. Net: max-starting rows slide right by 1; min-starting rows stay.
Return a clean odd-width 1xN row with one centered red marker. The output is the rule-intrinsic NxN red V and phase-aligned blue stripe pattern, so width is the only varying semantic feature.

A zero-background grid contains exactly one command cell (1=up, 2=down, 3=left, 4=right) and one seed cell colored 5..9. Paint every zero cell from the seed to the border in the commanded direction with the seed color, preserving both original cells. Four scheduled demonstrations cover all command meanings before the query repeats one on a new layout.

0-bg grid with several sparse non-bg cells (random colors 1-9) anywhere, INCLUDING the bottom row and some vertically stacked. Rule: SIMULTANEOUSLY (on input state) each non-zero cell at (r,c) drops to (r+1,c) iff (r+1,c) is in-bounds AND 0 in the input; cells at the bottom row or with a non-zero cell directly below STAY. Both branches (drop / stay) are exercised every instance; positions, colors, counts and grid size vary.

Construct a sparse connected graph inside gray walls, with either a tree topology or genuine alternate-route loops. Place red start 2, green checkpoint 3, and leaf goal 4 so both BFS segments are nontrivial and several traversable cells remain off the ordered route.

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-12) with 4-7 ACTIVE COLUMNS. Each active column contains 1-3 non-bg cells stacked vertically at random rows, in distinct non-bg colors per cell. Other columns are empty. Rule: for each column, find the BOTTOMMOST non-zero cell (the cell at the largest row index in that column). KEEP only that bottommost cell; erase all other non-zero cells in the same column to 0. Empty columns stay empty. Net: gravity-prune — each active column drops its upper cells and retains only the lowest one (the bottommost color survives, others vanish).

Scan non-cyan components in object order and find the first whose shape is congruent to the cyan guide under any rotation or reflection. Clear the scene, then repaint exactly the guide cells with that component's color.

Return a completely blank 5..28 by 5..28 canvas. Height and width are the only semantic inputs; the rule draws the corresponding clockwise green spiral from the top-left. A controlled default prior covers every exact public square size in every difficulty band, while the general path also teaches lawful rectangular extrapolations.

Two to four separated hollow color-4 rectangular frames have distinct interior areas.  Rank by interior area: fill only the smallest interior with 2 and only the largest with 8; middle frames stay hollow.  Scheduled shape profiles refute fixed-3x3 and widest-frame shortcuts.

Tiled lattice: tile_rows x tile_cols equal tiles separated by 1-cell color-9 divider rows/columns. Tile size varies (2x2/2x3/3x2/2x4/4x2/3x3, area<=9 so per-tile counts stay <=9, incl non-square). Each tile holds count (0..area) random non-0 cells in one colour. Rule: split on full-9 dividers and output a tile_rows x tile_cols grid where each cell = that tile's nonzero count. Tile size, counts (0..area), lattice dims and colours all vary.
skills: tile extraction, per-tile counting, reduced macro output

summary: Noisy field of {0, a single primary colour, red(2)} (like the canonical). Rule: primary = first non-0/non-2 cell (row-major). For each column: rows ABOVE its first red -> 0; rows from first..last red keep the 2s (other cells -> 0); rows BELOW its last red -> primary. Columns have varied multi-red bands so the band-preservation branch is exercised; primary colour, densities and grid size all vary.

Five square panels A|B|C|D|Q are separated by color-5 columns. B is a uniquely identifiable dihedral transform of A; D is a consistent recolor of C; apply both operations to Q. Every query uses every map key and is asymmetric, so neither operation can be skipped.

For each column independently, collect the non-zero values in their original top-to-bottom order and place them at rows 0,1,... of that same column. Fill every remaining cell with 0. Four consecutive generated examples include all canonical morphology anchors plus a mixed-order column that refutes descending-color sorting.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~10-14) with: (a) a SOLID RECTANGLE (random 2x2..3x4) in rect_color; (b) a CONNECTED NON-RECTANGULAR polyomino (random, 4-6 cells, does not fill its bbox) in shape_color, separated from the rect. Rule: locate the solid-rectangle component and the non-rectangular component, crop the shape to its bbox, recolor its cells with the rect's color, output that crop. Varied shape forms + rect colours make the recolored crop differ per sample.

A single maroon(9) marker lies on one non-corner border cell. Its side selects up/down/left/right. Remove the marker and translate every other non-zero cell exactly one step toward that side, preserving all colors, shapes, and relative positions.

A 0-background grid contains 2-5 distinct colors. Each color occurs exactly twice at opposite corners of a proper axis-aligned rectangle. The rectangles occupy disjoint bounding boxes, so their borders have no undefined color-overwrite intersections. The rule draws every rectangle border in its marker color. Grid shape, pair count, rectangle dimensions, diagonal orientation, position, and palette vary.

Orange(7) chamber inside a magenta(6) perimeter frame (11x11-heavy prior, 11..16 overall). Interior: 1..5 crosses (4 in the canonical archetype), each a 5-cell plus in its own non-{6,7} color with one arm extended (arms [1,1,1,2] canonically, [1,1,1,3] as an extension; the realized maximum arm length always equals max_arm_len). For each cross the rule clears the border cell its longest arm faces to 0 and paints the opposite border cell in the cross's color. Placement enforces the canonical collision-free invariant: horizontal-arm crosses occupy distinct rows and vertical-arm crosses distinct columns, so every cross's two border edits land on unique cells. A four-draw cycle contains one strict canonical scene, one free scene with a canonical-morphology prior, and two teaching scenes containing length-3 crosses facing both nearer and farther edges. Three demonstrations refute all three declared rivals under any query holdout.

Split at full color-9 columns. Crop the one-color template in the first panel, search each candidate for the template in any of its four rotations with template zeros acting as wildcards, and output a 1xN strip with cyan 8 under exactly the matching candidates. Reflections do not count.
skills: candidate search, rotation-tolerant matching, symbolic selection

summary: Normalize the blue(1) mask and red(2) mask. The bottom-left control chooses union(3), intersection(4), or xor(6); the bottom-right control chooses identity(7), clockwise rotation(8), or horizontal reflection(9) for the red mask. Crop the chosen result and recolor it cyan(8). Every three-example lesson covers all operation and transform controls, and generated sparse connected masks make every branch observationally distinct.

A 25x24 grid with three SOURCE frames (L-marker colors 2,3,4 in a left column) and three TARGET frames (colors 5,6,7, right column). Each source frame holds a RANDOM color-8 KEY motif in its local coordinates; each of the first two target frames holds a RANDOM color-8/9 VALUE motif. The two keys are distinct, defining a lookup A->valueA, B->valueB. The third source repeats one of the two keys and the third target starts BLANK. Rule: learn the key->value map from the first two pairs and paint the third target with the value for the third source's key. The two key motifs, the two value motifs and which key the query repeats all vary freely (was 4 hardcoded key/value sets).
skills: analogy, local motif keys, keyed value retrieval, multi-frame parsing

summary: Read transform codes from the top header and colors from the left header. Crop the single body prototype, then output every transformed × recolored copy in a gallery with one-cell separators.

0-bg grid; cell (0,0) holds a FRAME color; elsewhere a single patterned motif block (random H x W bbox spanning all four sides, with internal zeros, in 2-4 colors). Rule: crop the bbox of all nonzero cells except (0,0) and wrap it in a 1-cell frame of (0,0)'s color. Output dims = (H+2) x (W+2); motif bbox, colors, position and grid size all vary.
Count isolated red top-bar and bottom-bar T-tetrominoes into capped blue and green positions of a fixed 3x6 emblem.

Two equal-size square templates (colors 1 and 2) sit above a two-row code grid. Codes 1/2 paste the templates, codes 3/4 paste clockwise rotations, and neighboring output tiles have a one-cell background gutter. A four-profile curriculum varies tile size and active code width while retaining 25% canonical-linked 3x3/three-column examples in every difficulty band.

0-bg grid with several separated color-1 (blue) components: some touch row 0, some do not. Rule: every blue component with a cell in row 0 is recolored to 4 (yellow); interior components stay blue. Component count, shapes, positions and grid size vary; top-touching and interior counts both vary (>=1 of each guaranteed).

Project each gray L-tromino one diagonal step toward its missing corner in yellow, and each red L-tromino one step away in green; clip at edges and let green overwrite yellow on projection collisions.

Count two sparse foreground point sets on their modal background.  Use the smaller count as output height and the larger count as output width, then mark the two clipped-diamond edges in color 4 inside a color-2 block on a fixed 16x16 canvas.  Public linked profiles have a calibrated 30% prior; lawful generalized counts and backgrounds provide diversity.

A largest template shape is anchored by the same-colour singleton among a row/column of markers. Consecutive marker gaps position recoloured template copies. The cyclic curriculum includes interior anchors and non-2 template colours while hitting all four canonical profiles.

Several separated color-3 objects (plus non-{3,7} distractors). Rule: repaint the color-3 object whose bbox center is closest to the grid center as color 7. Grid size, object count, shapes and positions vary.
Multicolor objects; rule paints n green rows below each, n = distinct color count.

A 3..6 by 3..6 zero-background grid contains 2..4 distinct-colored source cells on distinct southeast diagonals.  The output is 2h by 2w. Every source at (r,c) retains its color and paints that color at (r+k,c+k) for every in-bounds k>=0.
Several non-overlapping objects on a 0 bg; rule outputs n × n cyan-diagonal where n = object count.

3-5 separated components in distinct colors (each 3-6 cells, all containing the top-left cell). Rule: crop+normalize each component to a binary mask, overlay all masks top-left-aligned, output the per-cell count mapped 1->2, 2->3, 3->4, 4+->6 (output dims = max crop size).

Several separated solid ODD-sized squares (sizes 1,3,5,7) of distinct colors on a mode-color background. Rule: redraw each square centered, with side N-2 -- EXCEPT a size-1 square GROWS to a 9x9 square. Sizes, count, positions, grid size and bg all vary.

0-bg grid with several separated color-2 components. Each component may be SOLID (no enclosed 0-regions) or have N (≥1) INTERIOR HOLES (4-conn 0-regions fully enclosed by 2-cells, not touching the grid border through 0-bg). Rule: keep only color-2 cells; compute connected components; for each component count its topological holes h; recolor its cells in the output to: h=0 → 3, h=1 → 4, h=2 → 5, h=3 → 6, h≥4 → 9. Original 2-cells are dropped (the count-based color replaces them). Empty cells stay 0.

Two contiguous crossing strands carry four distinct colors: a majority base and two equal minority markers on each strand. The crossing base selects horizontal or vertical priority. The authority fills the rectangle bounded horizontally by the two horizontal markers and vertically by the crossing plus both vertical markers with a parity-dependent woven plaid.
Two to five separated same-color components on background 0; recolor each 4-connected component by its cell-count parity (odd -> 3, even -> 4).
Reflect every red cell across both axes of the green 2x2 pivot, completing its four-cell orbit while preserving the pivot.

A black grid contains one full-height color-8 wall and 2-3 distinct colored polyominoes, each touching one direction marker: 1=left, 2=right, 3=up, 4=down. Remove every marker, then process their original positions in row-major order. At each marker, slide the currently adjacent same-color component repeatedly in the marker direction until blocked by the current grid, so an earlier move can block a later one.

0-bg grid. Several rows (varied positions) hold 1-4 non-zero cells at RANDOM columns in RANDOM colors (repeats allowed within a row, as in canonical); other rows are empty. At least one marked row has a leading gap so the slide is non-trivial. Rule: in each row, gather the non-zero values left-to-right and pack them to the left, preserving order; the rest of the row becomes 0.

Construct isolated orthogonally adjacent green-3/red-2 pairs in all four relative directions. The rule changes paired 3s to cyan 8 and paired 2s to background 0 while preserving deliberately unpaired 3s, unpaired 2s, and gray 5 distractors. A controlled default prior covers all four complete public local-adjacency profiles. Alternating default lesson slots contain preserved 3 and 2 witnesses that reject a global color-replacement shortcut.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 3-5 NON-TOUCHING BLOBS, each in a DISTINCT color from {1..9}, with SIZES from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} (each size used at most once). At least ONE EVEN-SIZED and ONE ODD-SIZED blob guaranteed (mixed parity so rule has visible effect). Rule (KEEP ONLY EVEN-SIZED OBJECTS, ERASE ODD): identify all 4-conn BLOBS. For EACH BLOB: if cell count is EVEN, KEEP. If ODD, ERASE (set cells to 0). Net: even-sized blobs survive; odd-sized vanish.

Construct one separated connected blue shape and one connected red shape. Their top-left-normalized forms overlap but differ, so the rule emits a nonempty cyan symmetric difference cropped to its own bounding box. A controlled default prior covers all five complete public shape-pair profiles while most draws vary larger polyominoes.
Measure same-color four-connected object areas, order objects by left edge/top edge/color, and draw their colors as separated bottom-aligned bars with those heights.

Grid (w>=7) with a HEADER: rows 0-2 hold two 3x3 PROTOTYPE shapes -- proto2 (color 2) in cols 0-2 and proto3 (color 3) in cols 4-6, with col 3 = 9 separator -- and row 3 is a full color-9 divider. Below the divider (rows 4+) are SEED cells: single 2s and 3s at separated positions (3x3 stamp footprint fits, non-overlapping). Rule: for each seed of color C, stamp the matching prototype's C-cells at the seed's offset; the header copies verbatim. Net: each seed expands into its color's prototype shape.

Two nonzero colors form a Cartesian lattice: a divider color occupies full row/column runs and a cell color fills every positive-size band. Count non-divider row bands and column bands, then emit a fresh rectangle of that size filled with the cell color. Divider runs may be 1-2 cells thick and may occur on any outer boundary.

Three-spaced marker chains either lie down as colored three-cell floor runs or remain/fall as vertical columns. In staggered scenes the first near-busiest row supplies the active markers, earlier red evidence sets column starts, loose lower blue cells make floor runs, and isolated red floor gaps close.

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 1-3 SAME-COLOR 5-CELL PLUS MOTIFS — each at an interior center (r, c) with 1 ≤ r ≤ h-2 and 1 ≤ c ≤ w-2, occupying the 5 cells {(r, c), (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1)} all painted in a RANDOM non-{0, 8} color from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9}. Pluses are SEPARATED by ≥1-cell padding (no shared cells in the 3×3 footprint guard). Rule (HIGHLIGHT EACH PLUS CENTER WITH CYAN 8): For EACH 5-CELL PLUS-PATTERN of color C — i.e., a cell (r, c) with (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1) all equal to C: RECOLOR the CENTER cell (r, c) from C to COLOR 8 (cyan). Arms stay at C. Net: each plus becomes a cross of color C with a cyan dot in the middle.

Rows are independent on a zero background. Exactly two separated nonzero cells of the same color are valid endpoints; the Racket rule fills their inclusive interval on a fresh grid. Ordinary samples also contain one two-color pair and one three-cell outer-match row, both of which must vanish, so every grid teaches the exact-two-and-same-color discriminator.

A square zero-background grid contains 2..4 disconnected objects in one foreground color. Nested rectangular rings preserve the canonical visual family. Scattered examples contain a sparse 3x3-bbox object and a denser 2x3-bbox object, so bbox-area ranking and cell-count ranking disagree. The authority recolors components by descending bbox area as 2,3,4,...

A 6..14 by 7..18 background-0 grid contains exactly one full-height color-5 vertical guide. Exactly 2..8 color-2 source cells lie wholly on one side, form either one connected component or two separated components, and have empty in-bounds mirror destinations. The output preserves the input and paints color 8 at (r, 2*guide_col-c) for every color-2 source.

skills: cross-tile comparison, counting, same-size selective recoloring
summary: Color-9 divider lines form a 2x2..4x4 lattice of 3x3 tiles. Count each tile's nonzero cells, find the unique maximum, and recolor only that tile's occupied cells to color 8. Every default three-example lesson contains a canonical {2,3,4,5} anchor, a unique maximum of 4 with no five-cell tile, and a unique maximum of 7 with a five-cell distractor.
Find every 2x2 window containing exactly three equal non-zero cells and one zero cell. Fill that zero corner with the shared colour, preserving all other cells.

A 6..14 by 6..14 zero-background grid contains exactly two blue (1) cells at different rows and columns.  They are opposite corners of an inclusive 3..6 by 3..6 rectangle, in either diagonal orientation.  The answer is not placed back into the input canvas: return a freshly cropped rectangle of exactly that height and width, with every cell color 8.
Blue(1) cells activate rows and red(2) cells activate columns. A fresh same-size output paints green(3) at every active-row/active-column intersection and black(0) elsewhere.

Build a sparse odd-coordinate marker lattice on a zero background. In the doubled output, a marker at (r,c) becomes a clipped 4x4 tile whose top-left is (2r-2,2c-2). Odd-coordinate markers therefore map to non-overlapping 4x4 cells on an aligned logical grid. A controlled prior covers all four linked public marker/color profiles.

A unique color-2 anchor supplies a (border-touch, symmetry-class) key. Recolor every other object to 8 iff both parts of its key match the anchor.  Every generated lesson contains true matches plus touch-only and symmetry-only counterexamples.

An 8..11 by 9..11 zero-background grid contains one to three green cardinal crosses.  A target cross is either an isolated five-cell plus or has one additional connected corner cell, so component boundaries cannot be used as a proxy for the rule.  Every input also contains a separate five-cell green non-plus decoy.  The rule recolors exactly the center and four cardinal neighbours of every all-green cross from 3 to 7, preserving attached and decoy cells.  Default sample indices alternate isolated and attached contexts, so every three-demo lesson contains a counterexample to the strongest canonical-fitting shortcut.

Grid partitioned by full COLOR-9 divider rows and cols into a tr x tc lattice of EQUAL-SIZED tiles (th x tw, evenly spaced single dividers). Each tile holds 2-4 scattered non-9 cells whose bbox is non-trivial (spans more than the cells). Rule: for each tile, fill the bbox of its non-zero cells solid with 8; reassemble with the 9-dividers. Net: each tile's scattered cells become a solid 8-filled bounding box.
skills: object enclosure, local geometry, same-size output

summary: Place equal red bars on the left and right edges in separated row bands. Put one to five cyan dots on distinct rows beside exactly one bar. Each dot selects a bar-relative row offset: join that dot inward to its red bar and paint the matching row beside the plain bar.

Two equal-size panels (h x pw) separated by one full vertical 9-col. Each panel holds sparse non-zero cells (one color per panel; color is irrelevant to the rule). The patterns are built with GUARANTEED PARTIAL overlap: >=1 position occupied in BOTH panels (cancels) and >=1 position unique to each side (survives). Rule: split on the 9-col; output (panel size) is 8 at every position where EXACTLY ONE panel is occupied (XOR of occupancy). Partial overlap makes XOR distinguishable from OR/AND.
skills: panel extraction, boolean XOR, same-size synthesis

summary: One color-9 marker at TL/TR/BL/BR selects identity/rotate-CW/flip-left-right/rotate-180 for a cropped monochrome asymmetric blob. Consecutive four-sample lesson blocks hold the blob scene fixed while cycling every marker corner; the following block changes blob geometry.
Interior horizontal same-color triples are removed and replaced by vertical triples centered on their middle columns; all other cells remain.
Hollow every solid monochrome rectangular component independently, preserving its coloured border and clearing its strict interior to 0.

Build a color-8 bordered maze with interior wall dividers and one to three pairs of colored endpoints. Each pair remains connected when all walls and other endpoints are treated as blockers. The output paints the canonical shortest path for each color on the original maze.

Place one singleton paint-color key at a canvas corner and one closed rectangular frame of the more frequent nonzero color, with at least one blank cell between the frame and every canvas edge. The output preserves the scene and fills the frame interior with a paint-color checkerboard starting at the interior top-left cell.

Gray(5) bottom-anchored vertical bars of pairwise-distinct heights (1..h, incl full-height); rule keeps the TALLEST bar (->blue 1) and SHORTEST bar (->red 2), erases the rest. Distinct heights make tallest/shortest unambiguous (rule tie-breaks leftmost).

On a zero background, fill every zero whose immediate horizontal neighbours are the same non-zero color. Read all matches from the original input. Unequal horizontal neighbours, vertical matches, wider gaps, and already occupied midpoints remain unchanged.

Two to five distinct color bands with zero holes. Each hole selects its first nonzero neighbor in up/down/left/right order and compares original row and column counts of that color or zero. Row >= column clears matching column cells; otherwise matching row cells. Includes inactive bands, edge holes, independent canvas aspect ratios, and varied multi-band extent/tie witnesses that defeat the retained profile-gated shortcut.
A 0-background grid with 1-9 isolated 2x2 L-trominoes. Each block has exactly three corners in its own distinct nonzero color; fill the missing corner with that same color.

0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~6-8) with 1-5 COLORED MARKER CELLS placed ONLY in the BOTTOM ROW (h-1) at DISTINCT random columns, each in a DISTINCT non-zero color from 1..9. The rest of the grid (rows 0..h-2) is entirely 0. Rule (UP-LEFT DIAGONAL RAY): for EACH BOTTOM-ROW MARKER at (h-1, c) with color C, EMIT a DIAGONAL UP-LEFT RAY in color C — paint cells at (h-1, c), (h-2, c-1), (h-3, c-2), ... until the ray exits the grid (hits row -1 or col -1). The marker stays at (h-1, c). Net: each bottom-row colored marker draws an upper-left diagonal line in its color.

Small LR-ASYMMETRIC multicolor tile (w>=2); rule tiles 3x3, with the MIDDLE row-block LR-mirrored (top/bottom straight). Output is 3h x 3w. Asymmetry is enforced so the middle (mirrored) block differs from the straight blocks -- the rule's distinguishing feature stays visible.

Generate a fixed 3x3 multicolor input. Apply scale-map with row scales (2, 1, 2) and column scales (2, 1, 2): duplicate the top/bottom rows and left/right columns while leaving the middle row/column single. The result is 5x5. Every ordinary scene has distinct adjacent row and column signatures so the non-uniform scale is directly identifiable.

A 0-background grid contains adjacent seed+direction emitter pairs. Codes 1/2/3/4 point up/down/left/right; when the cell behind a code is a colour 5..9, that seed colour is painted from the seed through the code to the boundary on a fresh output grid. Isolated markers disappear and rays pass through unrelated input markers.

0-bg grid (h in [6, 19], w in [6, 20]) with 2-5 non-bg colors. Each color owns a contiguous ROW BAND whose height is that color's bar height; within its band the color fills one contiguous run per row. Blocks may STACK: a later block's rectangle can carve an earlier block from an edge (never splitting a row into two runs), but every color keeps at least one cell in its band's top and bottom rows, so the bbox height of every color is exactly its band height. Band heights are DISTINCT across colors. Rule (BAR CHART OF BBOX HEIGHTS, SORTED DESC): for each non-bg color compute bbox-height = max_row - min_row + 1 over all its cells; sort colors by height DESC; output a (max_height) x N chart where column c is a vertical bar of height_c cells of color_c at the top, 0 below.

A 0-background grid has a transform key at (0,0) and one connected nonzero content shape elsewhere. Clear the key, crop all remaining nonzero content, then apply 1=rotate-cw, 2=rotate-180, 3=flip-lr, 4=flip-ud, or identity for 5/6/7. Generated lessons use exact keyed controls and strong connected non-rectangular shapes; the validator also accepts the less-asymmetric and key-color-reusing canonical cases.

0-bg grid (h~9-13, w~10-14) with: (a) ONE COLOR-9 (maroon) ANCHOR cell at a random interior position; (b) 2-4 BLOBS in DISTINCT colors (sampled from [1..8]) of size 2-5 cells each. Each blob is at a STRICTLY DISTINCT Manhattan distance from the anchor (the min cell-to-anchor distance differs for every blob; no ties, so 'nearest' is unambiguous). Rule: identify the COLOR-9 ANCHOR and the non-9 BLOBS (color-keyed 4-connected components). For each blob, COMPUTE its MIN Manhattan distance to the anchor cell. KEEP only the BLOB with the SMALLEST distance, repainted in its original color on a BLANK grid; the anchor and all other blobs are ERASED to BG (0). Net: output is ONLY the nearest blob to where the 9-anchor was (no 9 in the output).

Place 2-4 equal solid rectangles of transparent zero and colored payload on a nonzero background. Align their bounding boxes and overlay them in row-major object order, taking the first nonzero payload at every local coordinate. Every generated scene contains a distinct-color overlap that makes first-object priority observable. Default even-index scenes also distinguish row-major object order from column and fixed color priorities.

A solid color-8 outer frame, optionally crossed by 0-2 full-height vertical walls and 0-1 full-width horizontal wall, partitions a 0-bg grid into rectangular chambers.  Six to eight pebbles use every color 2..7, with at least one pebble in each chamber.  In every chamber, each column's pebbles compact upward independently while retaining their top-to-bottom order; all color-8 walls stay fixed.

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~7-10) with 4-7 scattered MARK CELLS placed in the UPPER HALF (rows 0..h//2-1, excluding cells on the exact midline if h is odd) in various non-zero colors from {1..9}. The LOWER HALF (rows h//2..h-1) and the midline (if odd h) are entirely BACKGROUND. Rule: REFLECT the grid across the HORIZONTAL MIDLINE — for every cell (r, c) with a non-zero value v, also paint cell (h-1-r, c) with v (its mirror across the horizontal axis). Original upper-half cells STAY in place. If the midline row exists (odd h), it stays. Net: input is upper-half marks; output is the same marks ALSO appearing reflected in the lower half, creating a vertically symmetric pattern.
2-3 distinct-color, non-skinny shapes with distinct interior-hole counts (0/1/2); verified full placement.
Cycle the top row's first two nonzero colors along four zero-only rays from the first color-9 seed.

0-bg grid with K (3-7) singleton non-zero cells, each in some color (1-9). The cells are placed so most have an empty cell at (r+1, c+1) (where they'd move) but ≥1 cell sits at the right or bottom edge — its (r+1, c+1) would be out of bounds, so it stays. Rule: scan all non-zero cells. For each, if (r+1, c+1) is in bounds AND empty in the input, write the value to (r+1, c+1) on a fresh output canvas. Otherwise, write it to (r, c) on the output. Output is a fresh 0-bg grid with the moved/staying cells.

A 0-background grid contains exactly three 1-ring-isolated, differently coloured, 4-connected objects. Exactly one object has a non-solid crop whose binary mask is left/right mirror-symmetric. Crop that object to its bounding box without recolouring it. Four scheduled scene profiles keep canonical U/T examples common while refuting largest-object, reading-order, any-axis-symmetry, and fixed last-object shortcuts.

0-bg grid (h, w ~5-12) with 2-5 SPARSE non-bg SEEDS in distinct colors at random positions NOT in the last row or last column. Rule: for each non-bg seed at (r, c) with color k: PAINT every cell in row r from c to col w-1 (extending rightward to the last column) with color k. Then for the cell (r, w-1) — also paint every cell in col w-1 from r to row h-1 (extending downward to the last row) with color k. Net: each seed traces an L-shaped path right to the right edge, then down to the bottom-right corner.

A zero-background tree of touching monochrome components has singleton blue(1) and red(2) endpoints, a unique 4..6-object route between them, and 1..2 attached dead-end branches. Paint every cell of the unique blue-to-red component path color 8 and erase all off-path components.

A 0-background grid contains two or three blank centers whose four diagonal neighbors share one nonzero color. The output fills every such center with that color and preserves all other cells. Each generated lesson also contains one controlled non-answer: either only three matching diagonals, four nonzero but mismatched diagonals, or a nonzero center surrounded by four matching diagonals. Positive motifs move across the grid, two of every three examples reuse one color, and one example adds a symmetric orthogonal context pair that must not block the fill.

A 0-background grid contains one or more closed rectangular outlines and at least one connected incomplete rectangular frame. Fill the full bounding box of each complete outline with its color; leave incomplete frames and other non-outline components unchanged.

0-bg grid (h, w ~10-18) with 1-3 RED(2) OUTLINE shapes — rectangular outlines (or blob/nested/U/irregular variants), each enclosing ≥1 bg cell. Outlines have ≥2 bg-cell margin from grid edges. Optional sparse decoration cells (non-{0, 2, 3}) outside outlines. Rule: (1) fill all bg(0) regions enclosed by non-bg-reachable-from-border with color 3 (green) — i.e., any bg region NOT touching the grid border gets painted 3. (2) Recolor all 2(red) cells to 0 (bg). Net effect: outlines disappear, their enclosed interiors become green; outside-the-outline decoration cells remain unchanged.

A canonical 14/15 by 22-24 canvas holds two distinct color-7/8/9 rectangular frames. Each frame contains both candidate templates (colors 1 and 2), a selector cell choosing one candidate, and transform code 3/4/5/6 for identity/rotate-CW/rotate-180/flip-LR. Transform the selected tight crop, recolor it to the frame border, and h-stack the two pieces in frame reading order, vertically centered with a one-cell gap.

Drop monochromatic 4-connected objects to the bottom, packing their bounding boxes left-to-right by distinct cell count; discard whole-canvas-bbox frames. Varied 10..18 canvases, 2..6 shapes, zero-inclusive/repeated object colors, rectangles and irregular blobs up to 12 cells, optional frames, real overrides, and measured area-sort/color-group/background/frame-preservation shortcuts.

Color-8 scenes contain separated gray (5) and pink (6) rectangles with one or more adjacent exterior color-9 dots. Gray rectangles are erased while their dots are copied to the adjacent inner edge; pink rectangles remain while their dots move to the center row/column and their exterior sources clear. Scheduled 3x3 anchors plus non-3x3 and even-axis witnesses distinguish center/edge geometry, fixed inward steps, and midpoint tie-breaking.
Blank-grid output: largest 6-blob stamped in 6 at each isolated 2-marker.

0-bg grid (h~9-11, w~11-13) with exactly 3 SINGLE-CELL MARKERS in distinct non-zero colors. Markers are placed with Manhattan distance ≥ 3 from each other (so they don't touch and the L-paths are visible). They should not all share the same row/column (non-collinear). Rule: for each color-object, compute its bbox center (integer midpoint). Sort markers by color value ascending. For each consecutive PAIR of sorted centers (a, b): draw a HORIZONTAL segment from (r_a, c_a) to (r_a, c_b) painted with color_a, then a VERTICAL segment from (r_a, c_b) to (r_b, c_b) painted with color_a (the FIRST marker's color of the pair = smaller color). Finally re-paint each original marker on top. Net effect: L-paths connect color-sorted markers, each L colored by the smaller of the pair.

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with 3 BLOBS of STRICTLY DISTINCT SIZES drawn from {2, 3, 4, 5, 6} via blob-walk, each in a DISTINCT non-rank color from {4, 5, 7, 9} (rank colors are {1, 2, 3} so input colors don't overlap output ranks). Blobs placed at non-overlapping positions. Rule (RANK BLOBS BY AREA ASCENDING, RECOLOR BY RANK 1, 2, 3): identify all BLOBS. SORT by SIZE ASCENDING (smallest first). RECOLOR the i-th smallest blob to COLOR i+1 (i.e., smallest → 1, next → 2, largest → 3). Net: blobs ranked small→large, recolored 1→2→3.

2N+1 by 2N+1 grid with one full color-9 row (separator row) and one full color-9 column (separator col), splitting the grid into 4 N×N panels. Top-left has a small shape A in some color cA. Top-right is t(A) for some transform t in {rot-cw, rot-180, rot-ccw, flip-lr, flip-ud}. Bottom-left has a different shape Q in color cQ (cQ ≠ cA possibly). Bottom-right is empty. Rule: find separators, split into panels, detect transform t. Apply t to Q. Paste t(Q) into bottom-right. Output = input + filled bottom-right.

1 8-color rect frame somewhere in the grid; output = strict interior crop (interior pattern preserved). Frame + outside region vanish. Interior is filled to a density with a small repeated palette (matching canonical patterns), so the crop content scales with frame size.

0-bg grid with several POSITIVE diagonal pairs (2 same-color cells at opposite corners of a 3x3, center 0 -> rule fills the center with that color), plus NEGATIVES: LONE cells (no diagonal partner -> no fill) and CROSS-ambiguous centers (TL/BR one color, TR/BL another -> two hits -> no fill). Rule: a 0-cell is filled iff EXACTLY ONE diagonal pair matches. Pattern counts, colors, positions and grid shape vary.

Two exact red 2x2 blocks in canonical-scale noisy cyan scenes. Return 8 iff one 8-connected cyan component touches both block rings, else 0. A four-profile cyclic curriculum constructively refutes 4-connectivity, bounding-box, any-contact, and largest-component shortcuts.

Create a rectangular 3..25 grid containing color 5 and exactly one other nonzero color X.  Both colors occupy at least two cells and the binary pattern has at least three 4-connected color components, excluding rule-hiding monochrome, singleton, and single-bar scenes.  The output places X exactly where the input contains 5 and places 0 everywhere else.  Thirty percent of default draws reproduce a canonical pattern morphology up to rotation/reflection and color renaming; the remainder are controlled multi-component generalizations whose four-sample windows contain both sparse and dense novel color-5 masks.

Three or four separated monochrome objects have distinct bounding-box perimeters and a controlled row-major rank order. Crop each object, rotate tall crops clockwise, sort by perimeter descending (row-major on ties), and stack them vertically with one zero row between crops. Every generated input contains an asymmetric tall crop that distinguishes clockwise from counterclockwise rotation.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE color-2 (red) PIVOT (interior, clear of edges) and 1-5 color-1 (blue) cells in ONE quadrant relative to the pivot (off both pivot axes, within reflectable range). Rule: reflect each 1-cell 4-fold about the pivot (self + vertical + horizontal + both mirrors), painting 1 at every in-bounds reflection. The grid size, pivot position and the 1-cells all vary freely (was a fixed center pivot + 3 fixed cells, ~9 distinct).

0-bg grid (h~7-9, w~9-11) with COLOR-4 (yellow) OUTER WALL BORDER. Interior holds: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) START cell and ONE COLOR-3 (green) GOAL cell at Manhattan distance ≥4; (b) optionally (use_k1=1) ONE COLOR-5 KEY1 and ONE COLOR-6 DOOR1; (c) optionally (use_k2=1) ONE COLOR-7 KEY2 and ONE COLOR-8 DOOR2; (d) 0-2 EXTRA INTERIOR WALL cells (color-4). Rule (BFS WITH 2-KEY MAZE): search shortest path from RED START to GREEN GOAL via 4-conn 0-cells. WALLS (4) block. DOORS (6, 8) block UNLESS the matching KEY (5 or 7) has been picked up earlier on the path. PAINT every cell on the shortest valid path with COLOR 9 (maroon). Net: 2-key maze shortest-path traced in color 9.

Fixed 5x13 grid with THREE 3x3 blocks at rows 2-4, cols starting 1/5/9. Each block is a varied 3x3 pattern in a distinct color, with a COMMAND code above its center (g[0][start+1]) chosen INDEPENDENTLY from {1,2,3,4}: 1=identity, 2=rotate-cw, 3=flip-lr, 4=rotate-180. Rule: transform each block by its command and pack the three left-to-right with a 1-col gap (output 3x11). Commands vary independently (repeats allowed, all 4 covered); block patterns and colors vary. (Was a fixed L-tetromino in each block and consecutive-distinct commands.)

0-bg grid with several separated CLOSED RECTANGULAR ROOMS (color-8 outlines, sizes vary). Each room has 0 or 1 SEED (a non-{0,8} color) at an interior cell. Rule: every seed floods its room interior (4-connected 0-cells bounded by the 8 walls) with its color; rooms without a seed stay empty. Room count/sizes/positions, seed colors, and which rooms are seeded all vary. (Was a single plus-divider with 4 corner seeds.)

Several separated RED(2) blobs (varied size/position) plus 0-2 distractor blobs in other colors, on a 0-bg grid. Rule counts the red 4-connected components and emits a 1xN alternating 8/4 bar (8 first), N = count. The distractors exercise the rule's color filter (only red is counted). Red count spans 1..8 across difficulties; output is intrinsically the count-encoding so distinct outputs = number of distinct counts.

0-bg grid (h, w~8-11) with EXACTLY ONE COLOR-8 (cyan) ANCHOR cell at interior position (ar, ac) (not at grid edge, so reflections fit). Plus 2-7 non-{0, 8} CELLS in various colors from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9} placed at scattered positions such that their point-reflection through the anchor lands IN-BOUNDS at currently empty cells. Rule: TREAT the COLOR-8 ANCHOR as the FIXED REFLECTION CENTER. For every non-{0, 8} cell at (r, c) with value v, COMPUTE its POINT-REFLECTION (2*ar - r, 2*ac - c). If that reflected position is in-bounds, PAINT it with the SAME COLOR v. ORIGINAL CELLS STAY. The anchor stays color 8. Net: every colored cell gets a same-color twin point-mirrored across the cyan anchor; output is input + all reflected copies.

Grid (h, w in [3,18], square or non-square) whose COLUMN 0 is painted a BG color (any of {0..9} except 2 and 4, and nonzero so it is visible), with the rest of the grid 0 — matching the canonical clean-column input. Rule: output column 0 = bg (g[0][0]), the anti-diagonal (r+c==h-1) = 2, the last row = 4, else 0. The output depends only on dims and the corner color; bg color and dimensions vary.

0-bg grid with scattered single-cell markers in several distinct colors, each color appearing 1-3 times. Rule: tally non-bg cells, sort colors ascending, emit each color repeated by its count -> a 1xN row. Color set, per-color counts (so the tally varies), palette and grid size all vary. (Adjacency is irrelevant to the rule; cells just need distinct positions.)

0-bg grid with a SOURCE local frame (L-marker colors 2,3,4 defining an origin + 2 perpendicular cardinal axes) carrying a color-8 motif in frame-LOCAL coordinates, and a TARGET frame (colors 5,6,7) with its own orientation. Rule: read the 8-motif in source-local coords (radius<=3) and paint it into the target frame -> the copy is rotated/reflected by the target's orientation. Motif cells span all four local quadrants (incl. negative offsets), counts/positions/orientations and grid size vary.
skills: multi-point offset copy, frame-relative transport, same-size output

summary: 0-bg grid with FOUR hollow 5x5 COLOR-8 frames in a 2x2 reading-order layout (positions/spacing vary). Each frame's 3x3 interior holds: a CONTROL KEY at the bottom-right corner (value in {1,2,3,4}) and an asymmetric MOTIF (2-4 cells, distinct non-{0,8} color) in the other cells. Rule: per frame, transform the motif by the key (1=identity, 2=flip-lr, 3=flip-ud, else=rotate-cw), center each in a 3x3 tile, assemble a 7x7 output. Keys are a permutation of {1,2,3,4} so all four transforms appear; motifs, colors and frame positions vary.

A canonical-size 0-background canvas contains one connected red (2) mask and one connected green (3) mask. Crop each mask to its own bbox, align their top-left corners, XOR occupancy into cyan (8), then crop the XOR. Consecutive lessons alternate crop-required and crop-noop counterexamples.

Sparse 4x4 to 6x6 square grids drawn from four canonical morphology profiles. The output is the main-diagonal transpose; every generated example visibly and uniquely distinguishes transpose from the other D4 transforms.

On a 0-background grid, preserve every monochrome 4-connected component that touches the outer border and erase every strictly interior component. Every ordinary draw contains both roles. Counts, dimensions, edge sides, shapes, sizes, and palettes vary; consecutive lessons include same-color and same-shape components in opposite roles to rebut color/shape shortcuts.

0-bg grid with 1..3 two-color TEMPLATES (bar3/plus5/diamond5, disjoint color pairs) and isolated single-cell PARTIALS matching template colors. Rule: stamp each template onto each partial of its color.

0-bg grid with 2-4 POSITIVE diagonal-corner pairs (each a distinct color, rect >=3 in each dim so its outline differs from the 2-corner input) plus 0-2 NEGATIVE colors (collinear pair / single cell) the rule leaves unchanged. Rule: for each color with EXACTLY 2 cells at diagonal corners (different row AND col), draw the rectangle border in that color. Rect count, sizes, colors, positions and grid shape all vary.

A 0-background grid contains multiple vertical color-2 guides.  Each guide has a color-4 pattern on one side and a differently colored marker on the opposite side; the marker occupies one location obtained by reflecting a pattern cell across that guide.  Reflect every far-side 4-cell across its matched guide and paint the reflected cells with that marker's color.

Find the full-height gray divider. Preserve the input and reflect every non-zero, non-gray cell from its left source panel to the equal-distance cell on the right, preserving color. The divider may be centered or may have one to three extra blank columns beyond the reflected right panel.

Color-9 walls form 2..5 horizontal lanes.  Every same-color 4-connected component moves east independently and rigidly on a static board made of the walls plus its original footprint, so vacated source cells can stop a gapped shape before the wall.  Width, lane count, lane height, all movable colors 1..8, placements, witness lane roles, connected profiles, and both diagonal orientations vary.  Every ordinary draw distinguishes one-step motion, row-wise alignment, merged components, and wall-only docking.

0-bg grid with exactly 2 non-bg colors, each having exactly 2 separated 4-connected pieces (curated + random shapes, bbox <=3x3, halo-separated). Rule: per color, stack its two pieces bottom-anchored in one column (originally-leftmost piece on the bottom, rightmost on top, 1-row gap); the color owning the overall-leftmost piece stacks in column 0, the other offset right by left-width+1. Colors (palette_kind), shapes, sizes vary.

For each nonzero color with exactly three cells on exactly two rows and two columns, fill its missing fourth rectangle corner in the same color. Other per-color configurations remain unchanged. Four linked profiles include canonical anchors plus bent triples, diagonal pairs, collinear triples, complete rectangles, larger target counts, and long-span targets.
Decode five gap-separated binary pieces as straight, left, or right moves and trace their two-cell steps from (1,3) in a fixed 8x7 output, with path color 2 and start marker 3.

Construct a compact square border frame first, cut it into top-left, top, bottom-left, bottom-right, and side roles, then scatter the five distinctly coloured pieces on a nonzero modal-background grid. The canonical rule must recover role geometry and repack the pieces into the source frame.

Build an even rectangular grid from four equal quadrants, each using one distinct foreground color over zero background. The output overlays corresponding cells with fixed priority TR > BL > BR > TL. General lessons force witnesses for all five outcomes: all-zero, TL, BR, BL, and TR.

A blue (color-1) template (cropped to its bbox) is replicated once per singleton color dot, each copy recolored to that dot's color. Dots all in ONE column -> vertical stack (th*n x tw); dots spread across columns -> horizontal concat (th x tw*n). Templates are both curated and randomly generated (varied shape/size, not necessarily 4-connected, as in canonical); dot count, colors (palette_kind), grid shape all vary.

0-bg grid with: (a) color-1 DIAGONAL 2x2 pairs (the positives the rule fills solid 8), (b) NEGATIVE blue configs — horizontal/vertical pairs, single dots, full 2x2 blocks — that must stay unchanged, and (c) other-color decoy shapes the rule ignores. Every blue feature is moat-separated so no cross-feature 2x2 window accidentally forms a diagonal. Counts, sizes, colors, both diagonal orientations and grid shape (incl. non-square) all vary; some instances have 0 diagonal pairs (identity output, matching canonical).

Square solid background with one interior dot. Paint color 1 vertically through the dot column, preserving the dot itself. If row == column, extend the top endpoint to the top-right corner and the bottom endpoint to the bottom-left; otherwise extend top-left and bottom-right. Generated lessons break the canonical anti-diagonal, center-column, and background-parity and dot-successor correlations.

0-bg grid with: (a) one DIRECTION marker (color 1/2/3/4) at a corner — 1=up, 2=down, 3=left, 4=right; (b) one connected OBJECT in a non-{0,1,2,3,4,8} color (3-6 cells); (c) a color-8 WALL LINE perpendicular to the sweep, placed so the object hits it after >=2 steps. Rule: translate the object in the marked direction until the next step would hit a wall or the boundary; output = union of all swept positions + the walls, marker removed. (Was: a single 8-cell wall.)
Drop each monochrome 4-connected object of size at least four to the bottom on a fresh color-7 canvas.

A singleton shape key (1=L, 4=plus) chooses one of two GREEN object families, while a singleton color key (2/6/8) gives the replacement color. Recolor every object of the selected family and preserve the other family. A cyclic three-profile curriculum includes selected-family minority counterexamples to the canonical majority-family shortcut.

Find every 2x2 window with exactly three cells of one non-background colour and one zero, then fill that zero with the same colour. Windows are evaluated from the original input. Scenes include isolated motifs, connected multi-window components, repeated colours across components, and mixed-colour near-matches that must stay unfilled.

One connected 4..9-cell color-2 template and one color-1 marker on zero. Mirror the template inside its tight bbox, then stamp it in color 8 with the bbox top-left at the marker on a fresh zero grid. Clip overflow. Sample symmetric and asymmetric shapes, canonical and larger canvases, and both complete and partial stamps. No palette relabeling is valid: the reference uses literal colors 0, 1, 2 and 8.

3 panels split by full-9 columns: a TEMPLATE (plus of color 5), a SELECTOR (one fill color != 5/9), and a BOARD holding several plus-of-5 shapes. Rule: recolor every exact template match in the board to the selector color. (Was: hardcoded multicolor 3x3 block template.)
skills: exact matching, metadata extraction, color transfer

summary: Fill initially empty 45-degree gaps for colors occurring exactly twice. Read eligibility from the original input; later colors in input reading order win at crossings. A three-draw schedule supplies one compact example and two examples teaching non-diagonal, blocker, cardinality and order guards.

A KEY ROW of 3x3 color-1 rings (at any row) defines stamp columns; the leftmost key ring's column holds ROW ICONS (above and/or below the key row). Rule: stamp an 8-ring at each row icon's row x each stamp column. Key row position, grid size, icon counts vary.

On a zero background, find each maximal vertical run of blue (1) cells. Recolor every run whose length is exactly four to red (2), including runs touching an edge, touching another target horizontally, or sharing a column with a separately gapped run. Leave all shorter and longer vertical runs blue.

Build a sealed color-5 wall lattice with two to four chamber rows and columns plus optional isolated wall blockers. Each connected chamber region has one, two, or on harder generalized lessons three distinct markers. A singleton fills solid; multiple colors fill a bbox-anchored checkerboard using only the numeric minimum and maximum.
One color-6 marker + 2-6 color-1 blobs (varied shapes) at strictly distinct Manhattan distances from the marker. Rule recolors the nearest blob to 7. Grid size and blob count/positions vary.

0-bg grid (h~4-6, w~5-7) with 1-3 NON-ZERO SEED CELLS in DISTINCT non-0 colors from {1..9}. Each seed is a single cell at a random interior position (not in the last row or column so there's room for the diagonal to extend). Rule (EACH SEED PAINTS A DOWN-RIGHT DIAGONAL OF ITS COLOR UNTIL THE GRID EDGE): For EACH SEED at (r, c) with color C: PAINT cells (r+1, c+1), (r+2, c+2), ..., (r+k, c+k) with color C until r+k or c+k goes out of bounds. The seed itself stays at C. Net: each seed emits a down-right diagonal ray of its color reaching the bottom or right edge.

0-bg grid (h, w~10-16) with one filled two-color rectangular region. The outer color fills the bbox and the inner color forms a centered solid block, an off-center block, a connected non-solid mask, or a hollow ring, always strictly inside the bbox. Rule: crop the nonzero bbox and swap the outer and inner colors everywhere in the crop.

One rect-frame (4x5 up to ~9x13) with a single seed inside (a different color). Rule checker-fills the interior 0-cells at the seed's (r+c) parity in the seed color. Frame/grid size and seed position vary.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~8-14 by ~11-16) with 3 connected BLOBS normally and 3-4 at hard difficulty, in distinct non-zero colors, varied shapes (2-4 cells each). Blobs 8-conn isolated. Rule: detect all components. Sort by bbox top-left (row asc, then col asc). For each blob, crop to its bbox. Horizontally concatenate the crops (left-to-right in sort order) with 1-col gaps. Output height = max(crop heights); width = sum(crop widths) + (n-1) gaps. Each blob's color preserved in its slot.

Colors occurring exactly twice define aligned segments. Measure each segment's Chebyshev span plus one, sort the lengths, and draw left-aligned color-8 bars. Scheduled singleton and 3-cell distractor colors teach that only exact pairs contribute rows.

Even grid (~24x24) with a full lr+ud symmetric multicolor pattern and one solid 5x5 blue(1) marker placed corner-flush or crossing exactly one center axis; oracle reconstructs the occluded 5x5 from clean mirrors.
All-2 separator row; same-color contiguous bars above and below. Columns present in BOTH bars fill with 4 between the wider bar and the separator.

Column 0 rows 0..2 encode a permutation of three equal-height row blocks. Drop the header column and stack the blocks in that order. Block geometry, width, sparse contents, and foreground colors vary; scheduled palettes break the canonical color-rank shortcut.
Paint zero cells visible orthogonally from any red seed unless a blue blocker lies strictly between.

0-bg grid: (a) ONE color-2 (blue) TEMPLATE (3-6 cell connected shape) in the upper-left area; (b) ONE color-9 (maroon) ANCHOR with room for the stamp; (c) bottom row holds 1-3 transform CODES (1=rot90, 2=rot180, 3=flip-h, 4=flip-v) at distinct columns, read left-to-right. Rule: compose the codes onto the template, stamp the result at the anchor in COLOR 3 (green) on a blank grid. (Was: fixed L-template/anchor and codes {1,3,4} -> code 2 never generated.)

0-bg grid (h~7-10, w~8-11) with 2 NON-ZERO BLOBS in 2 distinct colors from {1..9}, located in the INTERIOR — at LEAST 1 all-zero row above and below the content, and at LEAST 1 all-zero col left and right of the content.
