Blobs are 2-4 cells each, placed at non-touching interior positions. Rule (CROP TO THE BBOX OF ALL NON-ZERO CELLS): COMPUTE min_r = minimum row of any non-zero cell, max_r = maximum row, min_c = minimum col, max_c = maximum col. OUTPUT is the SUBGRID from (min_r, min_c) to (max_r, max_c) INCLUSIVE — i.e., the rectangle tightly wrapping all non-zero content (cell colors preserved). Output dimensions = (max_r - min_r + 1) × (max_c - min_c + 1). Net: input is trimmed to its active bbox, dropping zero-padding.

Rotate each single-color object inside a blue rectangular frame by (key-2)*90 degrees clockwise, then center its bounding box. All keys 2..5, rectangular and square interiors, and 1..3 separated frames occur.

Two distinct key-color markers occupy row zero above a blank separator. The body contains one connected blob of each key color plus non-key distractors; output is the tight crop around all key-colored body cells.

0-bg grid with 3-4 connected blobs in distinct non-zero colors at scattered positions, each a STRICTLY DISTINCT size (so 'largest' is unambiguous). Blobs are placed with a >=1-cell buffer so they stay separate components. Rule: collect non-zero 4-connected components (connectivity is color-blind), find the largest by cell count, and crop the input to its bbox. Output = that subgrid (the largest blob's cells in their color plus any interior zeros).

0-bg grid with 2-4 ISOLATED irregular connected blobs (4-8 cells, often non-square bbox) in distinct non-0 colors at scattered positions. Each blob reserves a square region (side = max bbox dim) so its 90 deg CW rotation fits. Rule: rotate each object's cells CW and paint at its original top-left on a fresh grid, in its color. Net: every blob rotates CW in place. (Was: 2 fixed 4x4 patterns at fixed corners.)

0-bg grid with ONE multi-cell TEMPLATE shape (3-5 cells, color A) and 2-4 SINGLE-cell MARKERS (color B != A) at scattered isolated positions. Rule: on a blank canvas, stamp the template's shape at EACH marker (template's top-left aligned to the marker), recolored to the first marker's color; out-of-bounds cells clip. Net: the template is replicated at every marker in the marker color. (Was: 3-4 blobs, no markers -> rule returned a blank grid.)
Apply row-zero transform commands left-to-right to the first lower nonzero component's rectangular crop.

0-bg grid with exactly: (a) ONE control cell in {6, 7, 8, 9} at some scattered position; (b) ONE color-2 template (4-connected blob of 3-5 cells); (c) ONE color-1 anchor cell at some position. Layout is randomized: template, control, and anchor are placed at varied positions with 1-cell buffer between them. Rule: find control → rot_count = control - 6. Find template, normalize its cells, rotate 90° CW rot_count times. Paint the rotated cells at offset (anchor) in color 4 onto a copy of the input. Stamps must fit within grid bounds.

0-bg grid (h~6-9, w~8-12) with: (a) 3-5 ACTIVE ROWS — for each active row, a SEED CELL placed at COLUMN 0 painted in a row-specific non-0 color drawn from a 4-6 color palette; (b) WITHIN SOME ACTIVE ROWS (with 50% probability): a BLOCKER CELL placed at a random column c ∈ [3, w-1] painted in a DIFFERENT non-0 color (drawn from the next color in the palette). The remaining cells stay bg-0. Each active row has the seed at col 0 and optionally a blocker further right. Rule (EACH LEFT-BORDER SEED BEAMS RIGHTWARD THROUGH ZEROS UNTIL THE FIRST NONZERO BLOCKER OR THE GRID EDGE): for EACH ACTIVE ROW with a color-C seed at (r, 0): SCAN columns 1..w-1 left-to-right. PAINT each bg-0 cell with COLOR C until you hit a NON-0 BLOCKER cell — the blocker stays unchanged, and the beam STOPS at the cell BEFORE the blocker (the blocker is not overwritten). If no blocker exists, the beam extends to col w-1. The seed stays at col 0. Other rows are unchanged. Net: each active row becomes a horizontal colored beam from the left edge until its blocker (or the right edge).

0-bg grid (h×w, ~9-12 by ~9-12) with: (a) EXACTLY ONE color-9 PIVOT cell placed roughly in the center; (b) a SOURCE shape of 1-3 non-{0, 9} cells in some single color, placed off-center so its 4 rotations land at distinct positions and stay in bounds. Rule: find pivot. For each non-zero non-9 cell at (r, c), compute offset from pivot. Generate 4 rotational offsets (90° turns: (dr, dc), (dc, -dr), (-dr, -dc), (-dc, dr)). Paint each rotated position with the cell's color (if in bounds). Output: input + 3 rotated copies of each source cell.

A zero-background canvas contains one hollow color-5 rectangular frame. Equal, aligned markers on top/bottom fill their interior column; equal, aligned markers on left/right fill their interior row. Unmatched and misaligned border markers remain inert. Colors paint in ascending order (column then row within a color), so the numerically largest crossing color wins. Default lessons explicitly refute marker-without-mate and orientation-priority shortcuts.

0-bg grid with 1-4 BORDER-TOUCHING blobs across random edges (top/bottom/left/right, varied connected shapes) and 1-3 fully-INTERIOR blobs, all in distinct colors and separated by a 1-cell ring. Rule: erase any 4-connected component whose bbox touches a grid border; keep interior components on a blank canvas. (Was: a single top-edge L-tromino border blob.)

Build a color-5 outer frame and a recursive guillotine partition with three through six rectangular rooms. Partial wall segments terminate in T-junctions rather than forcing a Cartesian lattice. Place one colored seed in one room; only that connected room fills with the seed color.
Find the isolated nonzero objects, sort them by cell-area ascending (reading order breaks ties), and keep only the middle object on a same-size zero background.

0-bg grid with scattered ISOLATED single cells (no 4-neighbour) and several 4-CONNECTED CLUSTERS (random connected polyominoes, size 2-4), all in mixed non-0 colors and separated by a 1-cell ring. Rule: any cell with no non-0 orthogonal neighbour recolors to 8 (cyan); cells in a 4-connected cluster stay. (Was: 2 fixed tromino clusters.)

Read the contiguous non-zero keys in row 0 from left to right. Select the unique largest connected body object, crop it, and emit a horizontal gallery containing the original shape followed by every cumulative transform stage. Key 2 rotates clockwise, 3 flips left/right, 4 transposes, and 5 rotates 180 degrees. Adjacent gallery stages are separated by one background column. Generated three-demo windows expose all four keys, cumulative composition, placement irrelevance, and the largest-object selection rule.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE full-column color-9 (maroon) AXIS and 1-4 colored BLOBS on the LEFT side (colors from {1..8}, placed within mirror range so their reflections land in-bounds), none on the right. Rule: mirror each left blob across the axis to the right (copy the left color into the empty mirror cell). The grid size, axis column, and the blobs' shapes/colors/positions all vary freely (was a fixed axis + 2 fixed blobs, ~9 distinct).

0-bg grid with a single KEY MARKER cell in the BOTTOM ROW (color = key), one same-color NON-RECTANGULAR target blob in the body, and 1-4 distractor blobs in other colors. Blobs are non-touching (grow_blob padding) and stay off the bottom row. Rule: key = first non-zero in bottom row; target = the body object of that color; output = its bbox crop rotated 90deg CW. (Was: key at top-left corner -> off-distribution.)

0-bg grid (h~11-16, w~13-18) with: (a) EXACTLY ONE HOLED component — an IRREGULAR polyomino with exactly one enclosed 0-hole (a rectangular ring grown with random outward bumps); (b) 1-4 SOLID distractor components with no holes. Each in a distinct non-0 color, non-touching (1-cell padding). Rule: find the unique component with exactly one enclosed hole, crop it to its bbox and recolor to 8. Output = that crop. (Was: plain rectangular ring -> only 9 distinct outputs and off-canonical.)

CYAN(8)-bg grid (8-16) with 1-4 PAIRS of a BLUE(1) anchor and a MAGENTA(6) marker at a small offset (Manhattan<=2). Blues are >=5 apart so each magenta's nearest blue is its own. Rule: recolor each magenta to 8 (blends into bg) and paint the 90deg-rotated blue->magenta offset cell (br-dc, bc+dr) ORANGE(7); blue stays 1. Net: blue + an orange at the rotated offset; magenta vanishes into the cyan field. (Was: bg 0, blues locked to 4 corners.)

Single colored seeds (one per column, distinct columns) cast same-color shadows straight down to the bottom row. Grid size and seed count vary; every seed has >=1 blank cell below. (Was: 7-10 grids, 2-5 seeds.)

A zero-background grid contains three or four separated, distinctly colored domino components. Three components form a horizontal or vertical A-B-C line: adjacent pairs have clear line of sight, while the middle component blocks the two outer components. Sort components by centroid column then centroid row and emit an N×N matrix whose diagonal is the component colors and whose off-diagonal entries are 8 exactly for unobstructed row/column visibility, otherwise 0.

For every nonzero color appearing exactly twice, connect the two cells when they share a row or column. Process colors in ascending order, so the numerically larger color wins at a segment crossing. Diagonal pairs and colors appearing three or more times remain unchanged.

0-bg grid (possibly NON-SQUARE) with: (a) 1-3 SOLID color-5 (gray) squares (2x2 to 4x4) at well-separated positions; (b) 4-10 colored DOT cells (each a singleton in some non-{0, 5} color) scattered, each at least 2 cells away from any gray square perimeter. Rule: process dots in reading order. For each dot, find the gray square at minimum L1 distance from its row/col axis. Compute target = one cell outside the square along the dot's axis (clamped to dot's row/col). Place the dot at target on a fresh canvas keeping gray squares.

0-bg grid (h~8-13, w~7-11). Contains: (a) matching VERTICAL ENDPOINT PAIRS — two same-color cells at (r,c) and (r+2,c) with exactly one bg cell between; (b) DISTRACTORS the rule leaves alone — lone single cells (no vertical partner) and mismatched endpoint pairs (x 0 y, x!=y). All structures have a >=2-row vertical clearance so none interfere. Rule: for interior (r,c), if input[r][c]==0 AND input[r-1][c]!=0 AND input[r-1][c]==input[r+1][c] -> set output[r][c]=input[r-1][c]. Net: only the MATCHING 1-cell gaps fill; lone cells and mismatched pairs stay. (Canonical includes such distractors; prior version emitted matching pairs only.)

0-bg grid (h~10-16, w~12-20) with 2-4 NON-BG OBJECTS at non-touching positions, each in a DISTINCT color from draw_distinct_colors. Each object has min_object_w ≥ 3 (rectangles, L/T/U shapes, tall_rect, or wide_rect). Objects placed with margin ≥1. Rule (ERASE TWO LEFTMOST COLUMNS OF EACH OBJECT): for EACH non-bg CONNECTED COMPONENT, COMPUTE its BBOX. For columns c = bbox_c1 and c = bbox_c1+1 (the two LEFTMOST columns of the bbox), CLEAR every cell of the object in those columns to BG (0). The remaining object cells (cols c1+2..c2) stay. Net: each object loses its 2 leftmost bbox columns, trimmed from the left.
A hollow color-5 frame contains a sparse top header and left header. Every interior crossing whose two header colors match is filled with that shared color; nonmatching crossings remain background.

Recolor each monochrome 4-component by its bounding-box aspect: tall->2, wide->3, square->4. Varied connected shapes, repeated colors across aspects, 8..20 canvases, 3..6 objects; all bands retain canonical-scale support.

Four-connected non-gray chambers with exactly two red cells fill their original zeros cyan. Framed rooms retain canonical support; diagnostic chambers distinguish connectivity, counting, shape, reach, and preservation.

Treat each same-color 4-connected nonzero component independently. Keep it in place when any cell touches the top, bottom, left, or right grid border; erase components that remain strictly inside the grid.
Two same-dim crops of one picture; mark zero/nonzero disagreements in differing rows.

Exactly three separated monochrome objects on background 0. Crop each to its tight bbox, sort by (bbox width ASC, bbox height ASC, full crop lexicographic contents ASC), then pack left-to-right, top-aligned, with one background column between crops. Generated lessons explicitly cover width-primary, height-tie, geometry-driven lex, and color-driven lex comparisons.

One or two separated 4x4 hollow frames are selected by color-1 strips on the grid edge. Each marker repeats its overlapping frame toward that edge in 4-cell steps, clipping the final copy. A four-profile cycle adds a combined witness so every three-of-four lesson rotation teaches both partial-overlap selection and per-frame color.

0-bg grid (size varies) with several solid monochrome RECTANGLES (2x2 up to 5x6) in full 1-9 palette, each with a few cells ERODED (a Chebyshev-spaced independent set) so every hole sits in a 2x2 with 3 same-color neighbours. Blocks are separated by a 1-cell halo. Rule: fill any 2x2 with 3-same + 1-zero (single pass). Net: each eroded block heals to a solid rectangle. (Was: 2-3 isolated L-trominoes on a tiny grid.)

Pairs of 2s define horizontal row spans and pairs of 3s define vertical column spans. Return a new zero grid with 8 only at row/column pairs that satisfy both inclusive span-containment tests; ignore all distractors.

Grid of color-5 WALLS forming an RxC lattice of sealed COMPARTMENTS (rooms), sizes/counts vary. Each room holds ONE marker cell in a non-{0,5} color. Rule: for each compartment with exactly one such color, fill its empty cells with it. Net: each room floods with its marker's color, bordered by gray walls. (Was: fixed 9x11 grid, fixed 2x2 lattice of 4 rooms.)

Place a nontrivial 2x2 through 5x5 pattern inside a zero canvas whose height and width equal the squared crop dimensions. The output has the same dimensions and is a self-tile fractal: a nonzero pattern cell emits one complete pattern block and a zero pattern cell emits a blank block.

Read command 1..6 from the top-left cell, clear it, tightly crop the remaining colored object, then apply identity / rotate-cw / rotate-180 / transpose / flip-left-right / flip-up-down respectively.  A deterministic six-slot lesson cycle exposes every command and anchors every canonical input profile.

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (1-4) COLORS, each appearing as EXACTLY 2 separated motifs in non-overlapping regions. Rule: for each color with exactly 2 components, fill the combined bounding box of the two with that color. Net: each color-pair becomes a solid rectangle spanning its two markers. (Was: a single color-pair per grid -> one filled bbox.)

0-bg grid with EXACTLY ONE blue(1) cell on the BOTTOM ROW. Rule: launch a ball from the blue cell upward on a diagonal (up-right from column 0, up-left otherwise), bouncing off the left/right walls until it exits the top edge. Paint every path cell 1 and every other cell 8.
For every nonzero cell, paint gray(5) at (r+1, c+1) if that cell is bg.

0-bg SMALL grid (h, w ~ 3-10) with SPARSE NON-BG CELLS painted in non-{0, 8} colors drawn from a palette of 1-4 distinct colors. Cell placement follows one of 7 density patterns (sparse / medium / dense / checker / diagonal / corners / stripes) with cell counts scaled to grid area (roughly h*w/8 to h*w/2). The constraint: at least one non-bg cell; no cell uses color 8 (reserved for output). Rule (TILE 2×2 THEN PAINT DIAGONAL HALOS WITH COLOR 8): produce an OUTPUT of dimensions (2*h, 2*w) by REPLICATING the input as a 2×2 TILE GRID (output[r][c] = input[r mod h][c mod w] for all r, c). Then, for EACH 0-CELL in the tiled output: CHECK if any of its FOUR DIAGONAL NEIGHBORS (positions (r-1, c-1), (r-1, c+1), (r+1, c-1), (r+1, c+1)) contains a non-0 value. If YES: PAINT this 0-cell with COLOR 8. Otherwise stay 0. Non-bg input-tile cells stay their original color. Net: a 2×2-tiled output where each non-bg cell gets a halo of 8s painted in the 4 diagonal directions, while cardinal neighbors stay 0.
Odd-width colored grid; rule keeps only the middle column.
0-bg grid with TWO irregular hollow CONTAINERS plus 4..10 small solid PIECES that exactly tile the containers' holes; the rule reassembles the pieces inside the containers.

A 0-background grid contains exactly one full-height magenta (6) divider, one connected asymmetric orange (7) motif entirely to its left, and non-orange decorations on both sides. Mirror every orange cell across the divider and paint the empty reflected location cyan (8). Preserve the divider, source motif, background, and all decorations.

Three or four separated monochromatic objects have 0, 1, or 2 enclosed holes. Normalize each object, sort by (hole_count, color), and pack the objects left-to-right with one zero column between neighbours. Ordinary draws explicitly refute color-only, stable-input-tie, and area-order shortcuts while retaining canonical 11x15 and 14x15 profiles.

Two EQUAL-WIDTH panels separated by a full vertical color-9 column. The LEFT panel is a STENCIL (cells of one non-0 color marking which positions to keep; the rule treats it as binary). The RIGHT panel is fully colored content. Rule: output the right panel's value at each cell where the stencil is non-0, else 0. Net: the content is viewed through the stencil's holes. Stencil color varies (rule ignores it); panels up to ~12 wide. (Was: 4-5 wide, mask color 1.)

Construct one simple orthogonal beam route from a non-corner edge source through one to three active 6/7 mirrors. The ray ends at the boundary or, less often, immediately before an active 5 stopper. Up to three off-route mirrors or stoppers may act as genuine decoys.

Color-7 background grid. Row 0 contains a lawful 2/5 seed pattern and all lower rows start as 7. For each row r>0 and column c, read the two diagonal parents lp=(r-1,c-1) and rp=(r-1,c+1), using 7 outside the grid. If either parent is 7, keep 7. If lp==rp, write the opposite 2/5 color; otherwise write rp. Generated lessons always contain at least one active parent pair, so the output is never identical to the input.

In a mostly-7 grid, find maximal straight runs of 7-cells that touch the connected 0-region cardinally. Select the run nearest the single gray(5) marker, breaking equal run distance by longer length. Move gray to the nearer endpoint for horizontal/vertical runs but to the farther endpoint for diagonal runs; restore the old marker cell to 7.

0-bg grid (h = n, w = 3n+2 where n ∈ {4..8}) split into 3 EQUAL-WIDTH N×N PANELS by 2 full-height COLOR-9 (maroon) DIVIDER columns at cols n and 2n+1. Panel A (cols 0..n-1) contains a small connected MULTI-COLOR SHAPE using 2-4 colors from a SOURCE PALETTE drawn from {2..8}; every source-palette color appears at least once. Panel B (cols n+1..2n) contains the SAME SHAPE at the same positions, but each cell is recolored via a fixed bijection src→tgt (the cmap) where tgt-palette is disjoint from src. Panel C (cols 2n+2..3n+1) contains an INDEPENDENT shape using only SOURCE-PALETTE colors. Rule: infer the A→B color MAPPING (a permutation/bijection) by scanning corresponding cells. CROP panel C to its content and RECOLOR every non-bg cell via that A→B mapping. Output the mapped C. Net: A→B teaches a color permutation; output is C with that permutation applied.

Three sparse 4x4 panels separated by full color-9 columns. Panel 1 is the unique canonical transform of panel 0, and panel 2 is an independently placed motif in a different color. Infer the panel-0→panel-1 transform and apply it to panel 2. Defaults cycle through all seven transforms.

Canonical M130-style grid: 5 rows by 7 or 8 columns, one 3-cell non-1 L-template, and two color-1 anchors. Rule: take the largest non-1 component as the template and stamp it at each anchor on a blank grid. The generator keeps default samples close to the original train distribution instead of emitting large free-form motif galleries.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 9-18) with: N_FRAMES ∈ 3-6 NESTED COLOR-1 RECTANGULAR FRAMES (concentric, each smaller than the last) with RANDOMIZED OUTER POSITION and OFFSETS — outermost frame anchored at random (or0, oc0) with size (oh, ow), each inner frame inset by a random (dr, dc) ≥ 1 from the previous on each side. All frames have STRICTLY DISTINCT bbox areas. Rule (SORT 1-FRAMES BY BBOX AREA DESCENDING; ASSIGN EACH FRAME (BY DEPTH RANK 0 = OUTERMOST) A COLOR FROM PALETTE [2,4,6,7,3,9]; RECOLOR EVERY CELL OF THAT FRAME TO THE ASSIGNED COLOR): EXTRACT all 1-frames. SORT by bbox area descending. For rank i: RECOLOR frame i with palette[i] ∈ [2,4,6,7,3,9]. Net: nested 1-frames recolored by nesting depth.

Find every separated color-5 rectangular outline.  Each strict interior contains exactly one colored dot.  Fill that entire interior with its own dot color while preserving the color-5 border and all exterior background.

A 0-background grid contains 2-8 uniquely colored singleton markers on distinct interior rows.  Sorting markers by row defines horizontal bands; the oracle draws each marker color across its row and along that band's left/right borders, closing the first and last bands at the grid edges.

A gray-bordered floor is split by a full vertical wall, a full horizontal wall, or both, plus a partial internal branch that hides a same-side pocket. Exactly one wall cell has an accent color and one adjacent chamber contains the red seed. Flood cardinally from the seed through colors 0 and 2, recoloring reached zeros to 8. Ordinary draws use an unseen accent wall color (1 or 9) and an internal pocket, rejecting both palette memorization and coarse half/quadrant filling.

A room MAZE: a grid of rectangular rooms (0 interiors) separated by color-1 WALLS, connected by color-7 DOORS placed along a random spanning TREE so the room-adjacency graph is a tree. Rule: build the room graph from the doors, find its articulation-point rooms (whose removal disconnects the graph) and paint them color 8; leaf rooms stay 0; walls and doors stay. Net: the 'cut-vertex' rooms light up. A tree guarantees both painted (internal) and unpainted (leaf) rooms. (Was: random scattered motifs unrelated to the rule.)
skills: graph connectivity, cut vertices, same-size highlight

summary: A 7..24 by 7..24 zero-background grid contains 2..6 distinct nonzero colors. Each color occupies exactly the four corners of one axis-aligned rectangle. Draw every full rectangle border on a fresh zero canvas in ascending color order; larger colors overwrite smaller colors where borders cross. The scheduled curriculum includes canonical two-cell-wide rectangles, hollow interiors, overlapping outlines, and >2 colors.

Construct one through three bands of three-wide shape sections. Section colors remain fixed, while each successive band moves every shape one section left cyclically. The output continues that sequence for one more three-row band.

Extract the normalized 4-neighbour boundary of the unique red (2) template.  Every isolated code cell stamps that boundary in cyan (8): 1 keeps the orientation, 3 rotates 90 degrees clockwise, 4 rotates 180 degrees, and 6 rotates 270 degrees.  The code cell is the normalized top-left anchor and cells beyond the bottom or right edge are clipped.

A 0-background grid contains isolated singleton markers. Every row with one blue (1) or green (3) marker is filled with that marker color. Every column with one red (2) marker is filled red, except intersections with marked blue/green rows retain the row color (row precedence). Normal draws always contain both horizontal colors and at least one red column.

Draw the outline of the bounding box of ALL same-color nonzero markers on a fresh same-size zero grid. Inputs have 2..7 distinct markers and a bbox at least 3x3. Default lessons mix three-corner canonical profiles with distributed extrema and interior markers; positions, aspect ratios, border contact and colors vary. Exact size, color and count overrides are honored in every band.

0-bg grid (size varies, up to ~24) with exactly ONE rectangular cyan(8) FRAME floating at a random position. Its interior (2..12 in each dim) is filled at a varying density with non-8 colors. Rule: find the 8 rectangular frame and crop/return its interior contents. Net: output = whatever is inside the frame; output SHAPE = the interior size. (Was: interior capped 3-6, grids <=13.)

Square 20/25/30-cell scenes contain one to four isolated mono-color wall rings. Their non-wall interiors are notches. The globally rarest color shared by every notch is selected; only notches of size at least three are filled with it. Linked profiles expose short-notch evidence, a single-notch case, and a non-unique common-color rarity tie-break.

On a 0-background grid, find the unique red (2) and blue (1) endpoints. From red toward blue, take one diagonal step, then the required straight steps along the dominant axis, then the remaining diagonal steps. Paint only intermediate path cells green (3); preserve both endpoints. Every four consecutive generated demonstrations cover both dominant axes, compact and extended separations, all four directions, and at least two canonical-size anchors. Across sixteen slots, every direction crosses every axis/distance pair and the query recombines its repeated direction.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several FIRING motifs per row — A-0-A (a same-color pair flanking one gap) and A-0-A-0-A chains (two gaps) — PLUS non-firing DECOYS: A-0-B (mismatched colors), A-0-0-A (two-cell gap), adjacent A-A, and isolated singletons. Each group is horizontally isolated by a 1-cell halo. Rule: bridge every A-0-A by setting the middle cell to A; decoys are left untouched. Net: single-cell gaps between equal colors close; everything else stays. (Was: only A-0-A motifs, no decoys -> selectivity never tested.)

0-bg grid. The first two rows are a color LEGEND: at several columns, row 0 holds a source color and row 1 holds its target (keys and values are drawn from the FULL 1-9 palette and are disjoint, matching canonical). The body (rows >=2) is filled with the source colors. Rule: keep rows 0-1, and for every body cell that equals a legend key, replace it with that key's value. Net: the legend recolors the body. (Was: sources fixed to 1-5, targets 6-9.)

A 0-background grid contains two to four complete copies of one connected polyomino and exactly one connected defective strict subset. Canonical-profile anchors are monochrome; contrast examples give the defect a distinct color. Output the full normalized polyomino painted in the defective copy's color.

An 8..20 by 8..20 black grid contains 2..4 mutually separated straight blue(1) lines, with at least one horizontal and one vertical line, plus 1..2 color-5 distractor cells. Recolor exactly the two endpoint cells of each blue line to orange(7). Preserve every blue interior cell, every color-5 distractor, and the background.
veto_reason: production teaching ambiguity: max_length_six fits all three demos but fails a validator-accepted length10 query; source cb8958815b2eaf8769d5e60d464581153b85409c98b1bdb2e5446b7e4a35e0d7; see generators/f7072db3091a/evidence/audit-reopen-review-ef7ec83f4fb64030-v0001.json

summary: 0-bg grid (size varies) holding N isolated color-1 components (count varies widely, ~2-15). Each component is a singleton OR a small varied blob (any shape counts as ONE component); components are spaced so each is a distinct 4-connected piece. Rule: count the color-1 components and emit a single row of that many 1s. Net: output width = component count. (Was: 2-6 isolated singletons -> only 5 distinct output widths.)

8-bg grid (size varies) with several color-6 shapes (some hollow). Rule: around each shape's bbox paint a 1-cell background halo of 3, and fill the background cells inside the bbox with 4; the shape stays color 6. The grid size, shape count/forms and positions vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).
Separate closed blue rectangular frames contain zero, one, or two red interior seeds. Fill every remaining interior background cell green in each seeded frame; leave empty decoy frames unchanged.

A zero-background grid contains nonzero colours, each appearing at exactly two diagonally opposite corners of a rectangle. For every colour, draw the complete rectangle border in that colour on a same-size zero background. Generated lessons use one to five disjoint, interior-bearing rectangles.

Two full color-5 columns form source, worked-result, and query panels. Infer row-span versus column-span closure from the first two panels, apply that closure to the query object, crop it, and recolor it orange (8).

0-bg grid (size varies). (a) LEGEND color at (0,0) from {1..9}. (b) ONE big BODY BLOB in the legend color (5-25 cells, LR-asymmetric so the flip is visible), away from the corner. (c) Optional smaller SAME-COLOR decoy blobs (strictly smaller, so the rule's 'largest' pick is unambiguous). (d) Several DISTRACTOR blobs in other colors. Rule: read legend L=g[0][0], clear (0,0), take the largest color-L object, crop to bbox, flip left-right; emit the flipped crop. Net: the legend color's body blob is extracted and horizontally mirrored. (Was: 3-4 cell body blob -> tiny fixed output.)

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE red(2) exemplar object and several blue(1) objects. The exemplar has a topology signature (concavities, holes). SOME blue objects share that signature (different shapes/sizes/orientations allowed — topology is rotation/scale invariant); OTHERS have a different signature. Rule: recolor every signature-matching blue object to red; non-matching blues stay blue. Net: blue shapes topologically equal to the exemplar unify under red. (Was: all blues were the exemplar's shape, so every blue was recolored and the match/no-match distinction was never shown.)

Canonical-sized zero-background grids. An isolated command at (0,0) selects identity, clockwise, 180-degree, or counter-clockwise rotation. Choose the uniquely largest component by cell count, crop its bounding box, and rotate it. A smaller reading-order-first component has the same bounding-box area and explicitly refutes largest-bbox-area selection.

A black grid contains one to four isolated singleton gray (5) seeds. Replace every seed by a clipped 3x3 blue (1) block centered on that seed; overlapping blocks merge. Default lessons stay at the canonical 9x9 scale with three or four seeds and cycle through canonical-lattice, off-lattice, edge-clipping, and overlapping-halo profiles.

Generate a clean even-sized square or rectangle filled by concentric rings. Every ring has a distinct color from 1..9. The Racket rule keeps the geometry and reverses the ring-color order (outermost <-> innermost). A controlled square prior covers the exact canonical sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14 in their corresponding difficulty bands; the remaining draws add lawful even rectangular extrapolations.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several solid monochrome RECTANGLES (2x2 up to ~5x6) in colors from the full 1-9 palette, each with a few cells ERODED (removed to 0) as a Chebyshev-spaced independent set so every hole has 3 same-color neighbours in some 2x2. Blocks are separated by a 1-cell halo. Rule: iteratively fill any 2x2 with 3 same + 1 zero (cascades). Net: each eroded block heals back to a solid rectangle. (Was: 2-3 isolated single L-trominoes that each fill one corner.)

Fill a blank midpoint only between equal nonzero endpoints exactly two diagonal steps apart, reading the original grid once. Mix sparse pairs, counterexamples to overgeneralization, and clutter on 7..18 canvases with 3..9 foreground colors; preserve a canonical 8x8/three-color component.

0-bg grid (size varies, up to ~16x20). Several single-cell colored SEEDS in distinct non-{0,5} colors, plus color-5 WALLS placed as short segments and dots. Rule: from each seed, BFS through open 0-cells (blocked by walls and other colors); paint every reachable 0-cell at EVEN BFS distance with the seed's color. Seeds and walls stay; overlapping halos resolve in row-major seed order. Net: each seed emits an every-other-ring halo that wraps around the walls. (Was: 8-10x9-11, 1-2 seeds, <=3 dot walls.)

0-bg grid (size varies, up to ~14x20). Each row holds one contiguous non-bg block in a varied color; exactly ONE row has the STRICT maximum non-bg count (other rows may tie among themselves). Rule: rank rows by non-zero count and output the top row. Net: the densest row is extracted without teaching a noisy singleton-scatter prior.

A hollow nonzero frame floats on a 0 background. Color-2 cells on the left bbox edge mark rows and color-3 cells on the top bbox edge mark columns; the rule paints color 7 at every marked interior crossing. Bottom-edge 2s and right-edge 3s are lawful distractors: they preserve the bbox rule while refuting an anywhere-marker shortcut.

0-bg grid (size varies) with several solid monochrome 2x2 SQUARES at isolated interior positions in distinct colors, plus NON-2x2 DISTRACTOR objects (single cells, dominoes, L/I/T shapes — no solid 2x2). Rule: for each solid 2x2 block, draw the surrounding 4x4 RING (its border ring of cells) in the block's color; the 2x2 itself stays. Non-2x2 objects are left untouched. Net: each square blooms into a 4x4 outline. (Was small grids, no distractors.)

0-bg grid (size varies) with several complete monochrome 3x3 RINGS (8 same-color border cells, 0 center) in distinct colors, plus DECOY rings the rule must NOT fill: broken (one border cell missing), filled (center already non-0), or two-color borders. Rule: for each 3x3 window whose 8 border cells are one non-0 color and whose center is 0, fill the center with that color. Net: complete monochrome rings get their centers filled; decoys are left untouched.

Isolated color-3 beacon cells on a 0-bg grid. Rule: every 0-cell that is a DIAGONAL (Chebyshev distance 1, Manhattan distance 2) neighbor of a 3-cell becomes color 7. Cardinal neighbors stay 0; beacons themselves stay 3. Out-of-bounds diagonals are ignored.

PERIODIC-TILED grid: a random p × p TILE (p ∈ {3, 5, 7}) populated with colors from a palette of 2-4 distinct non-{0,1} colors drawn from {2..9}, then REPEATED across an h × w grid where h = p * h_factor and w = p * w_factor (h_factor, w_factor each ∈ {3, 4}, so h, w both divisible by p). After tiling, 1-3 RECTANGULAR CORRUPTION BLOCKS of size 2..5 × 2..5 are placed at positions determined by a position_bias (scattered / centered / corners / spread), and every cell inside each block is OVERWRITTEN with COLOR 1 (blue) — corrupting the periodic pattern there. Rule (DETECT THE PERIODIC TILE, RESTORE OVER COLOR-1 CELLS): find the smallest period p such that the non-1 cells obey period p in both axes (grid[r][c] = grid[r mod p][c mod p] for every non-1 cell). RECONSTRUCT the p × p tile by reading any non-1 representatives at each (r mod p, c mod p) offset. REPAINT every COLOR-1 cell with the tile's value at its (r mod p, c mod p) offset. Non-corruption cells stay unchanged. Net: the 1-block corruption vanishes, leaving a clean periodic tiling.

Zero-background grids contain two or three incomplete plus motifs whose zero centers have four equal non-zero cardinal arms; the rule fills only those centers. A four-profile curriculum also supplies exact negative controls: 3+1 arm colors, 2+2 opposite-pair colors, and three-arm partial pluses. Repeated-color targets and isolated noise prevent per-color and object-count shortcuts.

A 6..20 by 6..24 zero-background grid contains a 2..5 by 2..5 motif whose nonzero bounding box starts at the upper-left corner. Crop that motif and tile it periodically in both dimensions to fill the output.

0-bg grid (size varies) with 2-7 SCATTERED connected MOTIFS, each a random polyomino (3-8 cells) in a DISTINCT non-bg color, placed at non-overlapping isolated positions. Rule: extract every 4-connected non-bg component, crop each to its bbox, SORT by (cell-count DESC, then color ASC), and PACK the crops LEFT-TO-RIGHT, TOP-ALIGNED, with a 1-column gap between them. Output height = max motif height, width = sum of motif widths + (n-1) gaps. Net: scattered colored motifs collected into a horizontal gallery, biggest first.

0-bg grid (size varies) with ONE single-cell MARKER and ONE connected multi-cell SHAPE (distinct non-0 colors). The marker sits beyond the shape's bounding box along one axis, with a gap. Rule: locate the size-1 marker and the larger shape; SLIDE the shape toward the marker along the axis where the marker is outside the shape's bbox, until the shape's leading edge is one cell short of the marker. OUTPUT a blank grid with the marker at its original position and the shape at its slid position. Net: the shape moves to dock against the marker. (Was mis-modelled as panels.)

A 0-background grid is divided by complete wall rows and columns into rectangular rooms. Walls are colors 1/7/9 and each room contains green (3) markers. Compare marker density (3-count divided by room area), then preserve all walls and fill the unique densest room completely with cyan 8. Ordinary generated scenes include a larger room with more markers but lower density, explicitly refuting count-only and largest-room shortcuts.
skills: ratio comparison, room area, weighted selection

summary: Read row 0 as an ordered color cycle; preserve rows 0 and 1, then overwrite each later row with the corresponding cycle color.

0-bg grid (size varies). One color-2 START and one color-3 GOAL, 0-N color-5 WALL cells (sparse, non-blocking), and 0-3 WAYPOINT cells in distinct colors from {4,6,7,9}. Rule: BFS over all non-5 cells; the path must go START -> the waypoints in ASCENDING color order -> GOAL. Paint the intermediate route cells that are 0 with color 8 (start, goal, walls and waypoints are preserved). Net: a shortest route threading the waypoints in order, drawn in color 8. (Was mis-modelled as 8-walls + 4-portals.)
Complete every colored seed across the vertical center line, preserving its color and original cell; left, right, mixed and centerline seeds are supported without conflicting mirrored colors.

Sparse 0-background grids contain 1-5 active rows.  Each active row has one colored emitter followed by a gray (8) blocker, with an empty gap. The rule fills only that gap with the emitter color.  Optional cells after the blocker are preserved.  Generated lessons always include a one-cell gap and visible background after a blocker, separating the authority from two plausible shortcuts.

Per color: exactly 2 cells form a non-degenerate diagonal pair (different row AND different col). Rule fills the OTHER TWO corners of the implied axis-aligned rectangle with the same color, if those positions are currently 0. Multiple colors are independent. Cells on the same row or same column do not pair.
1-bg grid with non-1 cells; rule extracts bbox and converts 1s to 0.

Construct a branching color-8 route network between two color-9 markers. Color-7 obstacles disable adjacent 8 cells and thereby alter the route. The selected route is shortest first and fewest-turns second; lessons cover both a unique shortest route and an equal-length tie with one uniquely straightest route.

0-bg grid: vertical PANELS separated by color-9 divider columns. The first panel is the KEY (its single color is the key color). The remaining CANDIDATE panels each hold a RANDOM shape in a distinct color; exactly one candidate's color equals the key color. Rule: split by color-9 dividers; read the key color from the first panel; find the FIRST candidate panel whose color matches; OUTPUT that panel's shape recolored to 8 (same panel size). Because each candidate has its own random shape, the matched panel's output shape varies widely. Candidate/key shapes are compact connected polyominoes rather than scattered singleton noise, keeping object-count near the canonical task. (Was all panels sharing one fixed 3-cell shape -> a near-constant output.)
skills: legend decoding, panel selection by color, same-size recolor

summary: A 0-background 9-11 square-ish grid contains 3-4 distinct-colored, 4-connected objects. Select by (bbox width DESC, cell count DESC), then crop the original grid to that object's tight bbox. The crop preserves the selected shape's holes and any foreign-colored cells inside the bbox.

Several 4-connected colored components on a 0-bg grid with distinct (size, height, width) signatures. Rule sorts by (cell_count ASC, bbox height ASC, bbox width ASC, color ASC), crops each to its tight bbox, then horizontally packs them top-aligned with 1-cell 0-gaps. Output height = max bbox height, width = sum widths + (n-1) gaps.

0-bg grid (size varies). Row 0 is a LEGEND of 2-4 distinct colors (from {1..6,8,9}) in some column order. The BODY (below row 0) has the same number of color-7 BLOBS of DISTINCT sizes, placed apart. Rule: sort the blobs by size ascending (tie-break top-left) and recolor each by the next legend color (smallest blob -> first legend color). The grid size, legend colors, and blobs' sizes/shapes/positions all vary freely (was a fixed 3-legend + 3 fixed blobs, ~9 distinct).

On a zero-background grid, several solid monochrome 2x2 components are mixed with non-2x2 distractor components.  For every solid 2x2 target, clear its top-right and bottom-left cells and keep its top-left and bottom-right cells.  Leave every distractor unchanged.  Targets may touch different-colored targets, so a full 2x2 window is not enough: all four cells must have the same nonzero color.

Zero background; 2-6 monochromatic 4-connected components. Sort by leftmost column then top row, take raw input bbox crops (including neighboring colors), and stack with one blank row and floor-centered horizontal padding. Two fifths of default draws are canonical-like three-object 10x10 scenes; other draws deliberately separate raw cropping, tied-left ordering, floor centering, right-edge ordering, color grouping and connectivity rivals. Inputs and outputs remain within 30x30.

0-bg grid (size varies) with one SHAPE in a single non-zero color (not 3). Half the time the shape is LR-symmetric with ODD bbox height; half the time it is asymmetric. Rule: find the mode non-bg color, crop to its bbox; if the crop is LR-symmetric AND (not UD-symmetric OR odd height) draw a full HORIZONTAL middle row of color 3 across the grid, otherwise draw a full VERTICAL middle column of color 3. The shape is preserved. So LR-symmetric odd-height shapes yield a horizontal 3-line; asymmetric shapes yield a vertical 3-line; the line sits at the grid's middle (which moves with the grid size). (Was a fixed 10x10 grid -> a single in/out shape.)

0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with ONE TARGET MARKER FRAME — a 3-cell L-shape anchored at a chosen origin (orig, vx, vy) painted in 3 marker colors {5, 6, 7} (per helpers/local_frame). The frame establishes a LOCAL COORDINATE SYSTEM where (2, 0) (2 cells along the x-axis from the origin) is IN-BOUNDS and INITIALLY BLANK. Rule (DRAW A 3-CELL X-AXIS BAR IN THE LOCAL FRAME): interpret the marker frame's 3 cells as (origin, x-direction vector, y-direction vector). Compute the LOCAL COORDINATE (2, 0) — i.e., origin + 2*vx + 0*vy. PAINT cells at LOCAL (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0) (a 3-cell run along the local x-axis starting from origin) with the FRAME's color or a specific color per puzzle convention. Net: the marker frame extends into a 3-cell bar in its declared x-direction.
skills: directed extension, local axes, same-size output

summary: Complete the sole connected sparse color-6 component to its solid bounding box and erase every distractor.

Fill an interior zero cell exactly when its four cardinal neighbors have one common nonzero color. Canonical-style sparse crosses are mixed with three-plus-one color near misses, occupied centers, partial arms, and diagonal-only decoys. Counts and dimensions are exact; zero stays background.

0-bg grid (size varies) with 2-4 color-3 (green) BLOBS, EXACTLY ONE of which has a color-2 (red) MARKER cell cardinally adjacent to it (1-2 markers). The grid may also hold DECOY objects in other colors (ignored by the rule). Rule: find the first color-3 blob with a cell cardinally adjacent to a color-2 marker; OUTPUT just that blob cropped to its bounding box, painted color 3 (markers and all other blobs/decoys are dropped). Net: the marker selects which green blob to extract. (Was 2 tiny blobs with one marked.)

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0,0) holds the OP KEY: 1=union, 2=intersection, 3=symmetric-difference. Elsewhere are TWO LARGE partially-overlapping component shapes (when each is cropped to its bbox top-left they share some cells and each has private cells) plus 0-2 SMALLER distractor components. Every component is a distinct color != the key. Rule: read the key at (0,0); zero out all key-valued cells; find the TWO LARGEST remaining components; crop each to its bbox; apply the set op of their cell sets (union / intersection / symmetric difference); CROP to the result bbox and paint it color 8. Smaller distractors are ignored. (Was two tiny 3-5 cell shapes with no guaranteed overlap.)
Color-2 emitters cast color-7 beams rightward through zeros until any nonzero obstacle or the edge.

A variable 0-background grid contains one solid rectangular canvas in the modal non-zero color. Two through five distinct marker colors occur once inside the canvas. Isolated outside pieces contain one matching marker cell plus a small color-2 shape; translating each piece so its marker lands on the same-colored canvas marker stamps that shape into the canvas crop. Some lessons also include one unmatched-marker outside piece, which is a distractor and must be ignored. Endpoint and diagonal pieces teach full eight-connected object extraction.

Find every cyan object. Within that object's bounding box, count the connected regions whose cells are not cyan. Recolor the whole object by that count: 1->blue(1), 2->red(2), 3->green(3), 4->orange(7); any other count leaves the object cyan. Sequential sample indices form a linked lesson: demonstrations cover 0,1,2 then 3,4 then 1,5,6; the next query uses only the already-demonstrated 2,3,4 branches.

Grid (size varies) with ONE color-9 (maroon) PIVOT cell and 1-8 other colored cells (colors 1-8) scattered around it. Rule: take the (first) color-9 cell as the PIVOT. For EACH non-0/non-9 colored cell, compute its offset from the pivot and stamp the cell (keeping its color) at all FOUR 90-degree ROTATIONS of that offset about the pivot — 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees — dropping any copy that falls outside the grid. OUTPUT a fresh grid containing the 9 pivot plus the 4-fold rotational orbit of every colored cell. Net: the scattered cells are completed into a 4-fold-rotationally-symmetric pattern around the maroon pivot.

Every nonzero color appears as two aligned endpoints. If the endpoints are exactly three cells apart, fill the two intervening zero cells with that color. Pairs at distance two or four are distractors and stay unchanged. Horizontal bridges are written first and vertical bridges second from the original input, so a perpendicular gap crossing takes the vertical bridge color. Four-example schedules include canonical scale, both distractor distances, both orientations, and crossing precedence.

On a black background, recolor only blue (1) components that are exact three-cell 2x2 L-triominoes. The replacement color is determined by the missing corner: missing southeast -> 2, southwest -> 3, northeast -> 4, northwest -> 8. Blue non-L components and non-blue components remain unchanged. Five linked profiles expose every orientation plus size, color, and border counterexamples.

A 0-background grid contains 2..6 connected monochrome panels separated by one or two blank columns.  For each panel compute (area, enclosed 4-connected holes).  Output the N×N relation matrix: 5 on the diagonal, 6 for equal area and holes, 2 for equal area only, 3 for equal holes only, and 0 otherwise.  A four-sample cyclic curriculum constructively teaches every relation, including equal-area/different-hole code 2.

Grid filled with a DOMINANT CANVAS color (the most-frequent non-zero color) on which 2-5 colored 6x6 HEX OUTLINES (a fixed 12-cell hexagon stencil) are drawn, each a distinct color != canvas. The hexes may OVERLAP: drawn back-to-front, a front hex overwrites cells of hexes behind it, so back hexes appear PARTIALLY OCCLUDED. A little NOISE (stray <4-cell fragments) may also appear. Rule: bg = the dominant canvas color; detect every other color's hex outline (fit remaining cells to the stencil; colors with <4 cells or no fit are dropped as noise); infer the occlusion z-order from which color covers each hex's missing cells (blocker dependencies); and OUTPUT the hexes restacked as COMPLETE outlines — an (n*6) x 6 grid on the canvas color, one full hex per 6-row band, ordered so blockers follow the hexes they occlude. (Was a 0-bg fixed 17x18 grid with 3 complete non-overlapping hexes.)

0-bg grid (h~8-11, w~9-12) with: (a) ONE CONNECTED COLOR-3 (green) BLOB of 2-4 cells (the PROTOTYPE) at a random interior position; (b) 1-3 SINGLE COLOR-1 (blue) ANCHOR cells placed so that stamping the PROTOTYPE (with anchor as top-left of stamp's bbox) stays in-bounds and doesn't overlap existing non-0 cells. Rule (STAMP PROTOTYPE IN COLOR 3 AT EACH 1-ANCHOR): identify the 3-BLOB PROTOTYPE (its normalized cell offsets). For EACH 1-ANCHOR at (ar, ac), STAMP the prototype's cells in COLOR 3 with (ar, ac) as the bbox top-left. EMIT a clean 0-grid with only the stamps (and the original prototype, or output may drop it). Net: each blue anchor sprouts a copy of the green prototype shape.
A zero-background grid contains isolated monochrome L triominoes in 2x2 windows. Complete every L by filling its unique missing corner with the same color; leave all other cells unchanged.

A 0-background grid contains exactly three separated monochrome 4-connected objects with strictly distinct cell counts. Sort the objects by ascending area and repaint their unchanged cells on a blank grid: the smallest object becomes 2, the middle object 3, and the largest object 4. Input colour, top-left scan order, shape, and absolute area are distractors.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 6-14, by difficulty) with: N_BLOCKS ∈ 1-4 SOLID 2×2 COLOR-5 (GRAY) BLOCKS, each placed at non-overlapping interior positions with ≥BLOCK_SEPARATION (default 5) cells between block top-lefts, ensuring ≥2-cell buffer from all grid edges. Position biases ∈ {scattered, diagonal, row_aligned, centered}. Rule (FOR EACH 0-CELL (R, C), CHECK THE 4 DIAGONAL 2×2-RELATIONS TO 5-BLOCKS: IF A 2×2 5-BLOCK SITS AT (R+1..R+2, C+1..C+2) (BOTTOM-RIGHT DIAG): PAINT (R,C) = COLOR 1; IF AT (R+1..R+2, C-2..C-1) (BOTTOM-LEFT): COLOR 2; IF AT (R-2..R-1, C+1..C+2) (TOP-RIGHT): COLOR 3; IF AT (R-2..R-1, C-2..C-1) (TOP-LEFT): COLOR 4; PICK THE FIRST MATCHING IN BR/BL/TR/TL ORDER): For EACH 0-cell, check the 4 diagonal relations to gray 2×2 blocks. PAINT with the first-matching corner marker (1, 2, 3, or 4). Blocks preserved. Net: each 2×2 block gains 4 distinct-colored corner markers at its diagonal 2-cell offsets.

Grid (h, w ~8-14) where TOP-LEFT 2×2 holds 4 distinct non-zero KEY COLORS: ka=(0,0), kb=(0,1), kc=(1,0), kd=(1,1). Body (rest of the grid) contains cells in mixed colors including the key colors. Rule: read keys ka, kb, kc, kd. For each cell (r, c) outside the top-left 2×2, if v == ka → swap to kb; if v == kb → swap to ka; if v == kc → swap to kd; if v == kd → swap to kc. Other colors unchanged. The top-left 2×2 is preserved. The body also contains NON-KEY colors, which the rule leaves UNCHANGED (so the swap is shown to be selective, not a global remap). Net effect: two PAIRED color swaps (ka↔kb, kc↔kd) applied only to body cells matching a key color.

Generate a 5..18 by 5..18 grid whose Chebyshev-depth rings are each uniform.  Four scheduled ring grammars are used: all distinct colors, innermost repeats outermost, innermost repeats its neighbor, and a two-color alternation.  A six-step schedule covers every grammar; every three consecutive demonstrations contain both an all-distinct and an outer/inner repeated-ring witness.  Zero is alternately included and excluded.  The oracle lists diagonal ring colors outer-to-inner, removes duplicate colors preserving first occurrence, and repaints every color with the preceding unique color cyclically.

A rectangular 0-background grid contains one contiguous horizontal maroon (9) support segment in the lower half and 3-8 non-maroon colored cells strictly above it. Treat every non-0/non-9 cell as one rigid ensemble, including separated components and multiple colors. Shift the complete ensemble straight down by one shared delta until its global bottom row is exactly one row above the support. Preserve the support, every color, every column, and all relative offsets. Scheduled multi-component/multi-color lessons distinguish this from dropping components independently or moving only one selected component/color.

A zero-background grid contains one or two nonzero components inside a larger frame. The answer is the tight joint bounding-box crop of every nonzero cell, preserving colors, interior zero holes, and any gap between disconnected components.

0-bg grid (size varies) with: (a) K (2-5) COPIES of a FREQUENT random polyomino SHAPE (4-7 cells); (b) 1-4 DISTRACTOR shapes, each a random polyomino with a DIFFERENT normalized shape (and distinct from each other), each appearing exactly ONCE. Every blob is painted a DISTINCT non-0 color drawn without replacement from {1..9} (the rule is COLOR-BLIND). Blobs are placed with 4-adjacent buffer separation. Rule (FIND THE MOST-FREQUENT NORMALIZED SHAPE, COUNT ITS FREQUENCY K, OUTPUT THAT SHAPE SCALED K× IN COLOR 8): GROUP all blobs by NORMALIZED SHAPE (color-blind, exact orientation). FIND the most-frequent class (tie-break top-most, left-most). Let K = its frequency. UPSCALE that shape by K (each cell -> K×K block) and PAINT every block color 8 on a bg-0 canvas of size (sh*K, sw*K). Input colors are DROPPED. Net: the dominant shape's mass × frequency yields a cyan-8 scaled output. (Was a fixed 9-shape bank; now shapes are generated randomly.)

A blue shape (1) and red shape (2) are placed apart with a control cell at a varying corner. Control 3/4/6 selects union/intersection/XOR after each shape is independently normalized to its own top-left bounding-box corner. Partial-overlap and either-subset relations are generated, and the shared normalized support may include or omit coordinate (0,0).

A 16..23 by 16..23 zero-background grid contains one solid 3x3 cyan(8) square and 20..64 gray(5) obstacles. Red(2) rays leave the four square corners on the outward diagonals, stopping before a diagonal gray cell or before a diagonal cell pinched by gray cells on both inward orthogonal sides. Yellow(4) rays leave the corners in the clockwise-adjacent diagonal directions as alternating staircases: gray at the start suppresses the ray, gray on an intermediate step stops before it, and gray on the next diagonal cell preserves the intermediate step before stopping. Gray and cyan cells remain unchanged. Ordinary draws use open/mixed/mixed profiles with opposite mixed orientations and variable blocker depths, so every three-example lesson exposes free travel, all blocker branches, and a downward corner-pinch.

On a 0-background grid, treat each nonzero monochrome 4-connected component as an object. Normalize each object to its own bounding box. Keep it at the same cells and in the same color exactly when its occupied mask is invariant under a 180-degree rotation; erase every other object. Generated lessons include point-symmetric-only objects and matched asymmetric decoys, so reflection-axis, size, aspect, position, and canonical-prototype shortcuts disagree with the intended labels.

0-bg grid (size varies). Rows 0-1: a LEGEND mapping seed 1/2/3 to an output color. The r>=2 area is partitioned by color-5 walls into rooms, each holding color-1/2/3 markers. Rule: fill each room's empty cells with the legend color of its STRICT-majority marker (ties stay 0). The grid size, legend colors, room layout and each room's marker counts/positions vary freely (was a fixed layout, ~17 distinct).

A zero-background grid contains isolated connected yellow (4) target objects with nondegenerate bounding boxes and optional isolated nonyellow distractors.  Mark the four bounding-box corners of every yellow object blue (1); leave distractors unchanged.

0-bg grid (size varies). Several ACTIVE rows each contain exactly one color-9 AXIS marker plus 1-5 other colored cells (colors 1-8) placed on EITHER side of the axis; each such cell has an in-bounds, currently-empty MIRROR slot across the axis. Some grids also include DECOY rows that hold stray colored cells but NO 9 axis. Rule: for each row, find the LEFTMOST 9 (the axis). For every non-0/non-9 cell in that row, copy it to its mirror column (2*axis - c) when that destination is in-bounds and still empty. Rows without a 9 are left unchanged. Net: every axis row becomes left-right symmetric about its 9; decoy rows pass through untouched. (Was tiny grids, 2-3 rows, cells on one side only, near-fixed colors.)

Rows 0 and 1 encode a two-stage query. Count the color-1 cells in row 0 to select an exact symmetry class: 1=left/right only, 2=up/down only, 3=both axes, and 4=no reflection symmetry. Count the color-2 cells in row 1 to select area rank 1 or 2. Filter the body objects to the requested class, sort them by decreasing area (top-left breaks ties), crop the ranked object to its bounding box, and recolor its occupied cells cyan (8).

Find dense-noise 3x3 red/gray candidates, rank them by red count and reading order, greedily reject candidates that reuse covered red cells, then recolor selected gray cells orange with yellow centers.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~14-18). ROW 0 is a LEGEND: 2-3 NON-ZERO cells at distinct columns (in left-to-right column order). Below row 0 (starting at row 2) the body contains EXACTLY ONE connected 4-conn SHAPE per legend color, each in the matching color, sized 3-5 cells. Shapes are 4-conn isolated from each other. Rule: (1) For each legend color, locate its body shape and CROP it to its bounding box. (2) CANONICALIZE the crop by taking the lex-min over six dihedral variants: identity, rotate-CW, rotate-180, transpose, flip-LR, flip-UD. (3) CONCATENATE the canonical crops horizontally in LEGEND ORDER (left-to-right column order of the row-0 cells) with a 1-cell gap of bg-0 between each pair. Output: a wide gallery strip of canonical shapes arranged in the legend's order.

0-bg grid divided into 2-6 ADJACENT VERTICAL COLOR REGIONS (left to right), each a distinct color (adjacent regions differ so boundaries are detectable) with a small per-region decoration cell. Region widths are randomized: SOMETIMES all distinct, sometimes with a repeat. Rule: detect the regions by per-column modal color; if ALL region widths are unique, REVERSE the region order; otherwise ROTATE the regions LEFT by one. Columns (including decorations) are copied wholesale. Net: regions flip or cyclically shift depending on whether their widths are all unique.

0-bg grid: row 0 holds K color-1 cells (K = the target articulation count). Below row 0 are one or more CHAINS of touching cells in distinct colors — a chain of m cells is a path of m objects with m-2 ARTICULATION objects (cut vertices of the object-adjacency graph). Exactly one chain has m-2 == K. Rule: count the row-0 ones (K); group body objects into clusters by adjacency; find the cluster whose articulation count equals K; OUTPUT its union (bbox crop) recolored to 8.

On a zero background, find every nonzero center whose four in-bounds cardinal neighbours contain exactly three cells of the center colour and one zero. Fill that one zero with the center colour, completing the plus; leave every other cell unchanged. Generated targets use distinct colours. Scheduled lessons also include isolated two-arm decoys and non-downward missing arms so the demonstrations identify the exact precondition rather than a canonical-template shortcut.

0-bg grid (h 5..14, w 12..22): row 0 is a legend listing 2..5 distinct non-zero colors by default (1..5 including the one_color edge) at scattered columns (left-to-right = pack order, always different from the below reading order when >=2 colors); row 1 is empty; rows 2..h-1 hold one 4-connected polyomino piece (1..5 cells canonical, up to 6 on generalized draws; bbox <= 3x3) per legend color, plus optional duplicate-color pieces (rule selects the LAST per color) and non-legend distractor pieces (rule ignores them). Output: the last piece per legend color cropped to its bbox and packed horizontally in legend order with 1-column zero gaps.

Build a nontrivial 2x2 through 5x5 source tile with one through three foreground colors. The output repeats the entire source tile in an n-by-n array, so every source cell appears at all coordinates with the same row and column residues modulo n.

0-bg grid: row 0 has 2-8 color-1 MARKERS at distinct columns (at least one column unmarked); rows below row 0 hold dense colored content (colors 1-9). Rule: take the columns marked with a 1 in row 0; output the rows below row 0 restricted to exactly those columns (a (h-1) x n_marks sub-grid). Net: the marked columns of the body are extracted in order.

On a blank output, fill the axis-aligned bounding rectangle of every nonzero color that occurs exactly twice. Generated pair rectangles are non-overlapping; scheduled slash pairs, 3-4 pair scenes, and one 1- or 3-cell decoy teach what the canonical backslash-only two-pair examples do not distinguish.

A zero-background grid contains one connected asymmetric color-1 template, one reflection control 2/3, one rotation control 4/5/6/7, and one color-9 anchor.  The rule transforms the normalized template and adds a color-8 copy at the anchor while preserving the input.

0-bg grid with two separated multicolor source shapes. Each source has a strict-majority main color plus three isolated non-main spec cells in distinct colors. For every spec cell, an isolated same-color marker is placed at the corresponding offset under a D4 transform in a clear target region. Rule: identify each source, align its colored spec cells to the matching markers, and stamp the transformed source on a blank grid.

0-bg grid with 1-4 color-8 TRAPEZOIDS (narrower top/bottom row, wider middle body), each in varied size and position, mutually isolated. Rule: for EACH color-8 object, compute a DIAMOND from its top-row width, bottom-row width and top-row center (apex top-width//2 above the top row, bottom-width//2 below the bottom row) and paint that diamond in color 4 on the background 0-cells (the 8-shape is preserved). Net: each trapezoid gains color-4 apex extensions above and below.

Two color-5 separator columns create equal before, after, and query panels. The after panel copies the before object and adds 1..4 color-8 cells. Transfer those additions by offsets from the before object's bbox top-left to the query object's bbox top-left; in-bounds additions overwrite any query cell they land on.

0-bg grid (h~8-10, w~10-12) structured as a small dungeon: (a) ONE COLOR-2 (red) START cell at random position; (b) ONE COLOR-3 (green) GOAL cell at another position with Manhattan distance ≥4 from start; (c) 0-4 COLOR-5 (gray) WALL cells at random empty positions; (d) 0-1 COLOR-6 (magenta) KEY cell; (e) 0-2 COLOR-7 (orange) DOOR cells. Rule (BFS PATH WITH KEY/DOOR): find the SHORTEST PATH from start to goal using BFS where WALLS (5) block movement; DOORS (7) block UNLESS the KEY (6) has been picked up earlier on the path. PAINT every cell on the shortest path with COLOR 4 (yellow). If unreachable, output = input. Start/goal/key/door/walls stay. Net: BFS shortest path → yellow trace, with key→door unlock logic.

0-bg grid (size varies) with: (a) TOP-ROW COLOR SWATCHES — 2-6 cells in row 0 at distinct columns, each a distinct color from {1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9} (color 2 is excluded, it is the shape color); (b) ROW SHAPES — 2-5 connected COLOR-2 random polyominoes placed in rows 1+, mutually isolated. Rule (CARTESIAN PRODUCT GALLERY): list the row-0 swatch colors left-to-right and the color-2 shapes top-to-bottom; output a gallery grid where cell-block (i, j) is shape i recolored from 2 to swatch color j, blocks separated by 1-cell gaps. Net: every shape is instantiated in every swatch color in a 2D grid.

Two-half grid (size varies, h odd -> vertical split). The denser LEFT half holds multi-color objects, each with a unique anchor color; the sparser RIGHT half holds one matching anchor marker per object. Rule: stamp each object onto its marker (aligning the anchor cell), on a half-width output. The grid size, object shapes/colors, anchor colors and marker footprints vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~23 distinct).

A 0-background grid contains exactly two differently colored connected objects, with the left object's bounding box strictly left of the right object. They advance inward simultaneously (left object rightward, right object leftward). Both stop at the last common step before either object would collide with the other or a full-height color-8 wall. The output preserves the wall and recolors both final objects to 7.

Place a sparse 3x3 or 4x4 multicolor key beside a cyan silhouette whose logical occupancy is the key rotated 90 degrees clockwise and expanded into uniform tiles. Recolor each cyan tile with its corresponding rotated key color while leaving the key unchanged.

Distinct colored top-row markers recolor each monochrome four-connected body below an empty row 1. Choose the marker nearest the body's horizontal bounding-box center; exact ties choose the smaller column. Markers and background remain unchanged. Body colors are disjoint from marker colors.

0-bg grid split by a full gray (color-5) row: ABOVE it a LEGEND of three glyphs in colors 2, 3, 4 (each a random polyomino, the three pairwise NON-rotation-equivalent so matching is unambiguous); BELOW it a SCENE of several COLOR-7 objects, each a random rotation of one of the legend glyphs, placed isolated. Rule: split on the gray divider; read each legend color's glyph shape; for each color-7 scene object, find the legend glyph it matches UP TO ROTATION and recolor that object to the legend color (legend and divider preserved).

0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-10, w ∈ 9-12) with: ONE SMALL MOTIF of DIMENSIONS mh × mw (mh ∈ 2-4, mw ∈ 2-5) embedded at a random INTERIOR position (top ∈ 1..h-mh-1, left ∈ 1..w-mw-1) with ≥1-CELL MARGIN of 0s all around. The motif's CORNER CELLS (0,0) and (mh-1, mw-1) are always painted (so the bbox is well-defined). Additional interior cells of the motif painted randomly in 1-3 DISTINCT non-bg colors drawn from {1..9}. Some motif interior cells may stay 0. Rule (CROP THE GRID TO THE MINIMAL BOUNDING BOX CONTAINING ALL NON-BG CELLS): COMPUTE the BOUNDING BOX of all non-bg cells (rmin, cmin, rmax, cmax). EXTRACT the subgrid g[rmin..rmax][cmin..cmax]. OUTPUT this cropped subgrid. Net: the surrounding 0-border is stripped; only the embedded motif remains, preserving its internal pattern.

A three-column left panel shows the red 3×3 V template (left arm plus bottom arm), followed by one full-height color-9 divider and a zero-background board. The board contains two or three exact copies of the shown orientation and exactly one rotated same-color V decoy. Mark color 8 at the center of every true copy on an otherwise zero board-sized output.
skills: template extraction, exact window matching, center marking

summary: 0-bg grid with 2-12 ISOLATED SINGLETON cells in varied non-zero colors, placed ANYWHERE (interior OR on the edges/corners) with a 2-cell buffer between any pair so radius-1 plus expansions never overlap. Rule: produce a FRESH same-size empty grid; for each non-zero source cell at (r, c), paint a plus — the cell itself + its 4 cardinal neighbors — in the same color, keeping only in-bounds cells (edge/corner pluses are clipped). Net: each singleton expands into a radius-1 plus of its color.

Each row has exactly one gray selector among columns 0, 1, and 2. The selector column chooses the row's solid output color: column 0 -> red 2, column 1 -> yellow 4, and column 2 -> green 3. Optional extra gray decoys may appear only in columns 3 and beyond, so the leftmost gray cell remains the selector. The default curriculum retains a substantial exact 3x3, black-background, no-decoy prior while also varying dimensions, backgrounds, row patterns, and decoy counts.

A control marker at (0,0) selects the closure axis: 2 means close each occupied row and 3 means close each occupied column. Ignore the marker, then on a blank same-size grid paint color 8 from the first through last non-marker cell of every occupied line. Endpoint colors do not determine the output color. Ordinary draws include exact canonical-profile anchors and three disjoint color-agnostic variants.

Replace every same-colour 4-connected component by the same-colour outline of its own tight axis-aligned bounding box on a fresh zero background. Canonical-size scenes are interleaved with repeated-colour and connectivity counterexamples.

0-bg grid (h~10-18, w~10-16) with 3-5 RECTANGULAR BARS anchored at a SHARED BASELINE (a varied row, not always the bottom). Each bar has: (a) WIDTH (1-4 cells, from width_dist uniform_1/uniform_2/all_2/mixed/wide); (b) HEIGHT from height_dist (ascending/tight_spread/wide_spread/shuffled), with 2*h_b ≤ grid_h. Bars don't overlap horizontally; spacing 0-2 cells between them. Each bar uses a DISTINCT color from 1..9. Rule (JUMP EACH BAR UP BY OWN HEIGHT): for EACH BAR with height h_b at columns c0..c0+w_b-1 TRANSLATE the bar UPWARD by h_b cells — paint the bar's cells at the new top position one bar-height above its current baseline. Net: each bar doubles its vertical extent by jumping up its own height.

skills: multiple arbitrary stencils in one grid
summary: A 3--6 row top library holds 2--4 color-keyed stencils, each defined relative to its visible color-9 anchor and separated by full-height 9-columns.  A blank row precedes 4--8 body seeds.  On a blank output, stamp each seed's matching anchor-relative stencil, clipping in-bounds.

A sparse 9..11 by 12..15 grid contains one connected blue (1) object, one red (2) marker, and one green (3) marker. The vector from 2 to 3 is applied to every blue cell, and the translated copy is painted cyan (8). Canonical-linked profiles cover axis-aligned and diagonal vectors, positive and negative directions, and both overlapping and disjoint copies.

Column 0 is a top-to-bottom palette. In the body, color-8 objects whose component size equals their bounding-box perimeter count as rectangular frames; overfilled lookalikes do not. Fill each zero cell by its number of strictly containing qualifying frames, leaving depths beyond the palette unchanged.

0-bg grid with: (a) one CODE cell in row 0 with value 1 or 3 (the Manhattan radius k); (b) one RED (color-2) SEED cell anywhere below row 0 — the radius-k Manhattan diamond around it may run off the grid edges (a clipped/partial ring); (c) scattered decoration cells in colors {1,3,4..9} (never 2, never in row 0, never exactly on the ring). Rule: find the first 1/2/3 cell in row 0 → k. Find the first color-2 seed. For each cell, if its value is 0 OR 2 AND its Manhattan distance from the seed equals k, set it to 8. Other cells preserved.

Row 0 holds K nonzero 'marker' cells (any colors, any columns) — the rule reads K = the count of nonzero cells in row 0. Below row 0 are 2-5 connected objects, each a random polyomino of a DISTINCT size in a distinct color. Rule: K = nonzero count in row 0; take everything below row 0, sort those objects by size DESC (tiebreak top-row then left-col), and OUTPUT the bbox crop of the K-th largest.

0-bg grid with 2-5 4-connected non-bg objects, each a distinct color and a DISTINCT number of interior holes (so the most-holes pick is unambiguous). Objects are solid rectangles of varied size with k single-cell interior holes punched (each hole fully enclosed and separated so it is its own bg component). Objects are non-touching. Rule: count each object's interior holes (bg components inside the bbox padded by 1 that don't touch the padded border); pick the object with the MOST holes (tiebreak size DESC, then top-row, then left-col) and OUTPUT its bbox crop.

On a sparse zero-background grid, fill a zero midpoint only when equal nonzero endpoints are exactly two cells apart horizontally or vertically. Every draw has two color motifs: one or two active pairs, and—when only one is active—a longer-span, diagonal, or blocked near miss that stays unchanged.
Exactly three separated, differently-sized nonzero components are recolored by descending cell count as 1/4/2. The default schedule alternates straight bars with a bounding-box counterexample.

0-bg grid split by ONE full-width row of 5s (the divider). ABOVE it: 'key' shapes, each a random polyomino (2-6 cells) in a distinct non-{3,5} color. BELOW it: 'target' shapes in color 3. Each target is paired to one key by SIGNATURE = (cell count, sorted bbox dims {min,max}) — orientation-independent — and the key/target shapes may DIFFER (e.g. transposed) so long as the signature matches. Key signatures are pairwise distinct so each match is unique. The grid may also include DECOY keys (signature used by no target) and UNMATCHED targets (signature matched by no key). Rule: for each color-3 object, find the non-{3,5} key with equal size and equal sorted bbox dims; if found, recolor the 3-object to that key's color, else leave it as 3.

Generate a canonical-scale zero-background scene with one uniquely largest 4-connected monochromatic component and crop to its bounding box. Ordinary lessons alternate split-distractor and split-target color-frequency counterexamples, with a periodic canonical-structure bridge. Aggregate-color, conditional color-ranking, and density shortcuts cannot explain the lessons.

4 PANELS in fixed 5-wide column windows [0..4], [6..10], [12..16], [18..22] of a 23-col grid (5-7 rows). Each panel holds ONE asymmetric shape (3-9 cells, all 8 dihedral images distinct) jittered to a random position inside its window, in an arbitrary color (the rule is COLOR-BLIND — it works on the binary crop). Panels are assigned to 1-4 shape CLASSES (each class a distinct cell-count so classes are pairwise dihedrally-inequivalent); each panel applies one of 8 dihedral transforms to its class base. Rule: binary-crop each panel; emit a 4x4 matrix where cell (r,c) is 8 on the diagonal, 2 if shape c is a ROTATION of panel r, 6 if it is a REFLECTION (dihedral, non-rotation) of panel r, else 0.

0-bg grid with 2-6 BLOBS, each a random 4-connected shape in a DISTINCT COLOR from {1..9} and a STRICTLY DISTINCT SIZE (so the area-sort is unambiguous). Blobs are placed at NON-TOUCHING positions (1-cell orthogonal gap). Rule (CROP EACH BLOB TO ITS BBOX, VSTACK SORTED BY AREA, ASCENDING): find all 4-CONNECTED non-0 COMPONENTS (color-blind connectivity). Compute each component's BBOX CROP and AREA (cell count). SORT crops by area ascending, tiebreaking by bbox top-row then left-col. VERTICALLY STACK the bbox crops top-to-bottom in that order, left-aligned, with a 1-row gap between them; width = max crop width (0-padded). Net: blobs are gathered into a vertical gallery sorted small-to-large.

On an 8-10 by 10-12 zero-background grid, place two or three colors as several isolated 4-connected components.  Component counts vary by color, and at least one color mixes a singleton with a multi-cell component.  Sort the non-background colors in ascending numeric order.  For each color, count its connected components and output a left-aligned bar of that color with one cell per component.  Pad shorter rows with zero to the largest component count.
Horizontal monochrome runs reduced to middle cell; vertical/diagonal shapes erased.

0-bg grid (size varies). Cell (0, 0) holds a COMMAND in {1, 2, 3, 4}. Rest of grid has 2-4 4-connected random polyomino objects in distinct colors, with PAIRWISE-DISTINCT size, bbox-width, and bbox-height (so every command is unambiguous). Rule: clear (0, 0) to 0. Compute objects of the cleared grid. Pick one object per command — 1: smallest size, 2: largest size, 3: widest bbox, 4: tallest bbox; tiebreakers go to top-most then left-most then smallest color. Output = bbox crop of the chosen object (paint its cells in its color over an empty grid sized to the bbox).

Horizontally-assembled 0-bg grid: n (4-7) PANELS (each panel_w 4-5 cols wide, panel_h 4-6 tall) separated by FULL-HEIGHT COLOR-9 1-col DIVIDERS. PANEL 0 holds a QUERY motif (1-5 connected cells in a non-{0,9} color); EXACTLY ONE other panel holds the SAME shape (any color/position); every remaining panel holds a DISTINCT-shape distractor. Rule: split on the 9-dividers; take panel 0's normalized occupied-cell shape; find the first later panel whose normalized shape matches; OUTPUT that matched panel recolored to 8 (or an empty grid if none matches).

0-bg grid (size varies) with: (a) TOP-LEFT CONTROL at (0, 0) — a SIZE RANK in {1=smallest, 2=middle, 3=largest}; (b) TOP-RIGHT CONTROL at (0, w-1) — a TRANSFORM in {4=identity, 5=mirror, 6=rotate-CW}; (c) THREE candidate objects, each a RANDOM polyomino of a DISTINCT size, in a shuffled size->color assignment over {7, 8, 9}, scattered at random positions. Rule: read the rank, pick that size-ranked 7/8/9 object, crop it tight, apply the transform from the top-right control, and OUTPUT the transformed crop in the object's color (other objects and controls discarded).

Grid (h, w ~ 5-12) FILLED with DOMINANT COLOR dom_color ∈ {1, 2, 3} (drawn uniformly) at density dom_count_ratio (0.6..0.8). The remaining cells are scattered with OTHER COLORS — 1-4 distinct values from {0, 4..9} (excluding dom_color) — placed via one of 7 LAYOUTS (scattered / blob / diagonal / row_dominant / col_dominant / checker / frame) at spread / center / edge bias. The MODE COLOR is strictly the most-common non-bg value (post-verified). Rule (READ THE DOMINANT COLOR — A VALUE IN {1, 2, 3} — AND OUTPUT THE CORRESPONDING 3×3 SHAPE FROM A FIXED MAPPING): COUNT each non-zero color's frequency. find the MODE — the value with the strict maximum count. The mode is in {1, 2, 3} by construction. LOOK UP the corresponding 3×3 SHAPE: 1 → S-shape, 2 → plus, 3 → L-shape (per demos). OUTPUT is that fixed 3×3 shape (in some color per demos, possibly the mode color). The input grid's size and content beyond mode color are dropped. Net: a small 3×3 output encoding one of 3 fixed shapes based on the mode value. Flagged intrinsic-low (uniq_out=3): only 3 possible output shapes.

Large 0-bg grid with N (3-4) connected components of varied thicknesses. Each component is a solid RECTANGLE (shorter side 2d-1 or 2d -> distinct onion depths d=1..N) in its own color from {1..8}; an optional color-9 square is a decoy the rule ignores. Rule: for each component, compute max onion depth (how many concentric layers peel away). Sort components by (depth ascending, color ascending). Output is 1×N grid of the colors in sorted order.
skills: component ranking, color extraction, symbolic ordering

summary: A 0-background grid contains one to five separated monochrome components. Choose the unique largest object by cell count.  Build its left-justified row histogram and top-justified column histogram, intersect them, and paint the resulting object cyan(8).  One quarter of ordinary draws are exact canonical-scale one-object anchors; the rest add lawful distractors.
