Each nonempty row has a unique most-frequent nonzero color; the unchanged Racket rule keeps only cells of that row-local mode. Ordinary inputs include a 2/1/1 three-color plurality row, varied mode counts, repeated color roles, and scheduled canonical-size/eight-foreground-color anchors.

A sparse 9..11 square-or-near-square grid contains two to four isolated colored singleton markers. Each singleton gains its in-bounds diagonal neighbors in the same color, forming a full or boundary-clipped X. Some profiles also contain one separated 2..3-cell connected decoy, which is not isolated and therefore remains unchanged.

Place one or two multicolor templates, each with one uniquely occurring anchor color and a repeated carrier color. Isolated cells matching each anchor request complete copies of that template; anchor color 2 mirrors the copy horizontally, while all other anchor colors preserve it.

0-bg grid (h~4-12, w~6-16) where each row starts with a contiguous non-zero PREFIX of random length 1-6 and random colors from {1..9} (some rows may be blank), followed by zeros to the row end. Rule: for each row, identify the leading non-zero prefix pattern. TILE that prefix REPEATEDLY across the full row width (modular index — the prefix pattern repeats c mod prefix_len). Net: each row becomes a periodic tiling of its initial prefix.
Separated components are replaced by cyan bounding-box borders.

On a colour-0 background, rows containing colour 1 are active and columns with colour 2 in row 0 are active. Paint their Cartesian-product intersections colour 3. Colour-2 cells below row 0 and a separate neutral colour are distractors and remain unchanged.
In each row, exactly two nonzero cells of the same color fill their inclusive horizontal span; every other row is unchanged.

0-bg grid (h×w, ~8-13 by ~8-13) with 2-5 COLOR PAIRS. Each pair: 2 cells of the same non-zero color sharing a ROW or a COLUMN with ≥1 empty cell between them. Different pairs use distinct colors. Pairs are placed so they don't interfere with each other. Plus 1-2 isolated decoration cells (no partner) to test selectivity. Rule: for each color, find its cells. If exactly 2 cells share a row, fill the row segment between them inclusive with that color. If they share a column, fill the column segment. Isolated cells with count != 2 are unchanged.

0-bg grid (size varies) laid out as ONE color-9 SOURCE FRAME plus 1-5 color-8 TARGET FRAMES (all square, interior k in 3-4), arranged in a grid of slots. The source frame's interior holds a random MULTICOLOR pattern (2-4 colors from {1..7}). Each target frame has a COMMAND CELL directly above its top-left corner with a value in {1..4} (1=identity, 2=rotate-CW, 3=rotate-180, 4=flip-UD). Rule: extract the 9-frame interior as the SOURCE. For EACH 8-frame, read the command above its top-left corner, TRANSFORM the source by that code, and PAINT the result centered in the target's interior (clearing it first). The frames, command cells, and source stay. Net: every target frame fills with a transformed copy of the multicolor source.

Count only row-0 maroon (9) cells, remove only those cells, crop the remaining scene and rotate clockwise by count modulo four. Default four-example windows cover counts 1, 2, 3, 4. One to four separated, distinct-color nonrectangular blobs have four different whole-scene rotations; canonical-scale single objects remain present in every band.
Sparse multicolor mirror orbits.  Complete each left/right pair using the nonzero member, with the left color winning occupied conflicts.

A 0-background grid contains three to five isolated objects, each in a different colour from 2 through 6. Exactly one translation-normalized shape occurs two to four times; one differently shaped object is a decoy. Crop the first row-major occurrence of the repeated shape to its bounding box and recolour its cells 8. A four-profile lesson schedule varies whether colour 2 and the first object are winner or decoy, so neither colour nor position identifies the answer.
Pack every row or column of blue(1) cells toward the edge identified by the unique cyan(8) marker. On the marker's own line, paint the vacated gap between the old and new blue blocks maroon(9).
Match a transformed query support to one of three prototype panels.
Dock scattered jagged pieces into matching bites on a full-span band, stacking interlocking layers until each local surface is flat while leaving unmatched one-cell decoy notches open.

gen1: workspace pieces sorted into edge-keyed bands.

Scene: a workspace (top or bottom region) holds 2-5 monochrome pieces —
solid blocks, rings with a decoration inside (the decoration is its own
piece), bars — each colored like one band's interior. Below/above sit
2-3 full-width bands (uniform interior, distinct 1-wide edge columns),
separated by workspace-bg rows. Transform: wipe the workspace; drop each
piece into its color-matched band, bottom-aligned, columns preserved,
recolored to the band's edge color.

gen1: icon towers over a red/green bar legend; red's count moves to green.

Scene: a non-zero background holds 3-5 towers of identical icons (one
shared icon shape per pair, distinct tower colors) in separate column
slots. The last row carries exactly one GREEN (3) and one RED (2) bar
under two different towers. Transform: stack red-tower-count copies of
the green tower's icon on top of the green tower (pitch = icon height +
1), gray out the red tower, erase both bars.

gen1: box lattices wired by a sequence strip.

Scene: a sparse lattice of framed boxes (one frame color; size 3 = single
core, 4 = 2x2 core, 5 = single core inside a frame-colored interior),
core colors mostly distinct with occasional duplicates; a strip of
isolated cells spells a non-revisiting WALK over the boxes. Transform:
bridge each consecutive pair through the clear gap along the earlier
box's core band, painted in the earlier entry's color. Scenes resample
until the rule's first-fit backtracker reproduces the intended walk.

gen1: diamond rings on a checkerboard; flanking segments fire rays.

Scene: a two-color CHECKERBOARD field holds 1-3 diamond rings (|r-cr| +
|c-cc| = k). Each ring gets 1-4 of its sides flanked by a parallel diagonal
SEGMENT one step outward, each segment in its own color. Transform: every
free chain end (exactly one same-color diagonal neighbor) fires rays
perpendicular to its chain in each diagonal direction that opens onto
background, painting its color over the checkerboard to the edge (shapes
block). Rings never fire (no free ends); segment middles never fire.

gen1: cloudy fields swept by an edge bar.

Scene: a dominant background with random cloud blobs in one color, and a
4-colored bar (width 3-6) on the top or bottom edge. Transform: clear all
cloud cells in the bar's column channel (except the bar row), then stamp
the bar every 2 rows marching away from its edge; every 3rd stamp is
green and additionally paints every maximal cloud run in its row green.

gen1: staircase corridors walked with repeating patterns.

Scene: a bg terrain holds 1-2 one-wide staircase CORRIDORS of a second
terrain (segments >= 3, non-consecutive cells kept >= 2 apart) plus a few
detached corridor-colored blobs; a legend row of 2x2 swatches (pattern),
a 2x2 turn-marker square, and a pattern[0]-colored single cell at each
corridor's border mouth. Transform: walk each corridor painting the
pattern, stamp the marker color ahead at each turn, dissolve the legend
squares. Scenes resample until the walk covers the constructed corridor
exactly.

gen1: header-programmed cursor excursion scenes.

Scene: a 6-row header of nb boxes (bar side = turn hand, bar color =
target); a field with 3-4 rects and a 2x2 cyan cursor. Sequence colors
are axis-aligned targets with clear legs (plus occasionally an absent or
unaligned color -> straight-up excursion). Transform: paint each
excursion (leg, hand turn, bounce runs to an edge). Scenes resample
until the mirror terminates within a step cap and every leg reaches its
intended target.

gen1: in-grid demo pair teaches f; apply f to the query box.

Scene: a dense >=4-color noise field carries four one-cell-thick boxes of
equal interior size: a DEMO pair (X, f(X)) far from an EMPTY answer slot,
and a QUERY box adjacent to the slot (so the nearest-to-empty rule picks
it). f is drawn from the library (complement / connect-aligned-dots /
flip-lr / flip-ud / rotate-180); scenes are resampled until the detector
finds exactly the four intended boxes, classifies the query correctly,
and the demo pair identifies the INTENDED f unambiguously.

gen1: LEARN A COLOR REMAP and apply it across a fully-colored grid.

Transform: every cell's color is mapped through a fixed bijection over the
palette (`recolor-map`), applied simultaneously to the whole grid. The input is
a 100%-filled grid of a few large contiguous color regions; the output is the
same grid with every color swapped per the learned map. The model must infer the
bijection from the demo pairs and apply it to the query.

Density concept: a DENSE (fully colored), LOW-component field — directly closes
the eval fill-density gap (eval ~73% filled vs the pool's old ~12%).

gen2: MIRROR a fully-colored grid left<->right.

Transform: `(flip-lr g)` — reflect the dense field horizontally. The input is a
100%-filled grid of a few large contiguous color regions; the output is its
mirror. Teaches a geometric transform on a DENSE field (models routinely fail
geometry once the grid is fully colored rather than sparse).

Density concept: same high-fill / low-component envelope as gen1.
Crop a fully colored dense field to exactly its left half.

gen4: DENSE DOWNSCALE — collapse a zoomed-in, fully-colored field.

Transform: the input is a 100%-filled grid built of uniform K x K blocks (a
small dense partition upscaled by K); the rule downscales by K, recovering the
small grid. Program: `(downscale g K)` (no fn -> takes each block's top-left
cell, which is the block color since blocks are uniform -> byte-exact parity).

Why this gen (vs resize/gen2's downscale): resize/gen2 fills its small grid only
~60% (40% background), so its INPUT is sparse. This one's input is FULLY filled
by a few large regions, so it closes BOTH gaps at once -- fill DENSITY (eval ~73%
vs pool's old ~12%) AND the size-SHRINK gap (output smaller than input, ~0 in the
pool) -- while keeping a LOW component count (eval-like, not pixel noise). The
hard tier reaches the large-grid tail (input up to ~27 wide, fully colored).
Slide every nonzero 4-connected object straight down until its own bottom touches the floor, preserving each object's color and exact shape.

gen2: slide every object to a wall — direction FIXED per task, varying across
seeds (one of up / down / left / right). Whole-object `move-to-wall`, shape
preserved (NOT per-cell gravity).

Layout adapts to the motion axis so objects never collide:
  - up / down   -> DISJOINT COLUMN LANES (no two objects share a column)
  - left / right-> DISJOINT ROW LANES    (no two objects share a row)
Component count is therefore preserved exactly.

Program (one rule, shared by all pairs; DIR is the per-task direction):
    (let ([objs (objects g)])
      (foldl (lambda (o acc) (move-to-wall acc (obj-cells o) 'DIR)) g objs))

gen3: magnetism to a central bar. A full-height WALL line (one fixed color)
splits the grid; every object slides HORIZONTALLY toward the wall until it is
flush against it (whole-object `slide-until-contact`, shape preserved).

Layout: objects live in DISJOINT ROW LANES (no two share a row) and each sits
entirely on one side of the wall with a >=1 column gap. Direction per object is
derived in the rule from its side of the wall, so objects on the left slide
right and objects on the right slide left. The wall is a single component; the
object count + 1 (the wall) is preserved exactly.

Program (one rule, shared by all pairs; W is the wall color, B is background):
    (let* ([wallcol (for/first ([c (in-range (cols g))]
                       #:when (andmap (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) W))
                                      (range 0 (rows g)))) c)]
           [wall-cells (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))]) (list r wallcol))]
           [objs (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) W))) (objects g B))])
      (foldl (lambda (o acc)
               (let ([dir (if (< (second (obj-bbox o)) wallcol) 'right 'left)])
                 (slide-until-contact acc (obj-cells o) wall-cells dir B)))
             g objs))

gen1: per-object recolor by SIZE EXTREMES.

Transform: among the objects on the field, the UNIQUE largest one becomes
colour BIG, the UNIQUE smallest one becomes colour SMALL, and every other
object becomes colour MID. Input objects all share ONE neutral colour, so
the output reads as "rank the blobs by area, paint the extremes".

Racket: pick-max / pick-min over obj-size locate the extremes (object
identity via eq?); foldl + recolor-cells repaints each object's cells.

Object sizes are drawn DISTINCT so the max and min are unambiguous (a
prerequisite for pick-max/pick-min == the Python `size==max/min` test).

gen2: per-object recolor by SHAPE CLASS.

Transform: each object is repainted by what KIND of shape it is —
  - a solid square (N x N filled)        -> colour SQ
  - a straight line (1 row or 1 column)  -> colour LN
  - anything else (rectangles, L/T/blobs)-> colour OT
Input objects all share ONE neutral colour, so the rule is "sort the
blobs into square / line / other and colour by class".

Racket: foldl over (objects g); per object a cond on (square? o),
(or (hline? o) (vline? o)), else; recolor-cells repaints the cells.
Classification is per-object and order-independent.

gen3: per-object recolor by EXACT CELL-COUNT (size -> colour map).

Transform: a fixed mapping size->colour is applied to every object —
all 4-cell objects become one colour, all 5-cell objects another, etc.
Objects of the same area end up the same colour regardless of shape or
position. Input objects share ONE neutral colour, so the rule is
"count each blob's cells and look the colour up".

Racket: foldl over (objects g); per object a cond on (obj-size o)
selecting the mapped colour; recolor-cells repaints. Order-independent.

Generation only ever uses sizes present in the map, so every object is
covered (the cond `else` is a safety fallback that is never reached).
Keep only the unique 4-connected object with the greatest cell count.

gen2: KEEP ONLY THE SOLID SQUARES, erase every non-square object.

Transform: among the same-color 4-connected components on a dense field, keep
those whose cells form a solid N×N block (`square?`) and erase the cells of
every other shape. The input plants a mix of solid 2×2 / 3×3 squares and
irregular non-square blobs of varied colors; the output keeps only the squares.

Selection concept: keep the objects satisfying a shape predicate.

gen3: KEEP ONLY THE ODD-ONE-OUT shape, erase the repeated ones.

Transform: the field holds several identical copies of one base shape (varied
colors) plus exactly one object of a DIFFERENT shape. `pick-unique` with
`same-shape?` returns that lone object — the one whose shape-equivalence class
is a singleton — and we erase every other object, leaving only the odd one.

Selection concept: keep the unique object that differs from all the rest.

gen1: recolor base noise (A->B), then draw a FULL CROSS (row+col) in a NEW
color centered on every marker cell -- markers (a distinct color) drive WHERE
each cross is drawn; the cross color is absent from the input.

Transform: (pipe (recolor g A B) -> for each marker (r,c): (draw-cross g r c NEW)).
Composes a color recolor with the draw-from-markers cross step.

gen2: recolor markers (marker_color -> NEW), then SMEAR that NEW color in a
fixed direction -- from each marker a ray of the NEW color shoots until it hits
a wall or a base-noise obstacle. Markers (a distinct color) drive WHERE rays
originate; NEW is absent from the input. Composes recolor + ray/smear.

Transform: (smear-color (recolor g marker NEW) NEW dir).

gen3: recolor base noise (A->B), then CONNECT each aligned marker pair with a
straight LINE in a NEW color. Markers come in pairs sharing a row (or a column);
each pair's two cells are joined by a segment of the NEW color, which is absent
from the input. Composes a recolor with the draw-line-between-markers step.

Transform: recolor A->B, then for each marker line/col draw-line between its two
markers in NEW.

gen1: keep-only ONE target color, then crop-to-content.

Transform: `(crop-to-content (keep-only g TARGET))` — from a large
multi-color noisy field, erase every color except TARGET (filter), then
crop to the tight bounding box of the surviving TARGET cells
(extraction). Output is the small TARGET-shaped patch; distractor
colors are scattered everywhere else and vanish.

gen2: recolor one distractor color, then extract-largest.

Transform: `(extract-largest (recolor g SRC DST))` — first recolor every
SRC cell to DST (a global color swap on the scattered distractors), then
crop to the bounding box of the largest 4-connected object (extraction).

The input is a large field of many small distractor components plus ONE
strictly-largest solid rectangle (a unique color, untouched by the
recolor, so it stays the unique argmax). Output = that rectangle's bbox
patch, recolored. SRC/DST are chosen so the swap never creates a
component larger than the rectangle and never touches the rectangle's
color, keeping the Racket `argmax obj-size` deterministic.

gen3: remove a pervasive noise color, recolor-map two colors, crop-to-content.

Transform:
  `(crop-to-content (recolor-map (remove-color g NOISE) (hash A B C D)))`
A large grid is flooded with a pervasive NOISE color (scattered far beyond
the meaningful shape's bounding box). remove-color erases NOISE to bg, a
recolor-map swaps the shape's two structural colors (A->B, C->D), and
crop-to-content extracts the tight bounding box of the surviving shape.
Output is the small, recolored shape pulled out of the noisy field.

gen1: frame-keyed horizontal gravity scenes.

Scene: 4-8 framed square pieces (uniform ring in cyan-8 or red-2, solid
core in another color) scattered on a uniform background. Transform:
cyan-framed pieces slide fully left, red-framed fully right, keeping
rows, stacking only against same-direction pieces (left lane settles
leftmost-first, right lane rightmost-first), lanes merged left-over-right.

gen1 — GATHER via single-axis ``gravity`` pack (packs all non-bg cells to one
edge, collapsing a scattered field into a dense bar), optionally composed with a
pre-recolor map (recolor one source color before the pack).

gen2 — GATHER via two-axis corner pack ``(gravity (gravity g d1 bg) d2 bg)``: a first
gravity packs to one edge, a second (perpendicular) gravity packs that into a
corner, collapsing a scattered field into one dense corner mass. Optionally
composed with a pre-recolor map.  The generator deliberately uses a sampled
nonzero modal background; ARC-AGI-2 eval often does, and keeping every gather
task on black-background fields was a systematic distribution shortcut.

gen3 — GATHER via panel ``overlay``-merge: the two halves of the grid are
superimposed into one half-size panel ``(overlay (left-half g) (right-half g))``
(or top/bottom), collapsing the scattered components of two panels into one
denser merged panel. Optionally composed with a pre-recolor map.

gen1: framed boxes of solid squares + glyph samples + pair legends.

Scene: a 1-thick frame encloses a grid of solid s x s squares in 2-3
source colors; outside sit one s x s sample GLYPH per source color (a
connected pattern in that color) and one two-color legend chunk per
source (source cells touching target cells). Transform: output the box
with every square replaced by its glyph in the mapped target color.
Read a legend of pierced rectangle keys as hole-count -> color, recolor each gray field blob by its enclosed-hole count, and erase unmatched blobs.

gen1: icon word-search boards with verdict strips.

Scene: an n x n board (n = 3-4) of pairwise-distinct random 3x3 icons on
a 5-cell pitch, a query strip above the first separator, a verdict strip
below the second. Scenarios: the query is a permutation of one row / one
column (success: strip + line + verdict green, swap sub-rule applies) or
a non-collinear icon set, sometimes with one icon absent from the board
(fail: matches boxed, verdict red).

gen1: reverse-built jigsaw scenes.

Scene: a random connected blob is partitioned into 3-6 connected pieces
by multi-source BFS growth; the blob (one color) sits on one side of the
grid, the pieces (distinct colors, occasionally two-toned) scatter on
the other side (different background). Transform: solve the exact tiling
and output the blob bbox padded by 1 with the pieces docked in place.
Scenes resample until the solver reproduces the intended tiling.

gen1: off-center doubly-mirrored mosaic occluded by an 8-rectangle.

Scene: value(r,c) is drawn per symmetry ORBIT under the group generated by
c -> al - c and r -> au - r (both axes are offset from the grid center;
reflections that land out of bounds leave those cells free), giving a dense
mosaic that is mirror-symmetric about both axes. A solid rectangle of 8s (a
color the mosaic never uses) occludes part of it, placed so every hidden cell
keeps at least one visible in-bounds mirror image. Transform: detect each axis
as the unique largest conflict-free reflection overlap on the visible cells,
then output the rectangle's hidden content.

Every training lesson contains separate witnesses that require horizontal and
vertical recovery.  The two witness demonstrations also use different offsets
for each axis and different output shapes, ruling out one-axis, centered-axis,
fixed-offset, and fixed-shape shortcuts before the query is shown.

gen1: diag + off-center double-mirror mosaic, black holes, full repair.

Scene: a square n x n mosaic drawn per symmetry ORBIT under the group
generated by transpose and the reflections c -> a - c, r -> a - r (one
shared axis parameter a >= n-1, so the group closes; reflections landing
out of bounds leave cells free). 3-7 black rectangles and a few single
black cells pock it. Transform: detect the axes (largest conflict-free
overlap; diagonal gated on conflict-freedom) and fill every hole from its
first visible image; output the whole repaired grid. Scenes resample
until the repair reproduces the clean mosaic exactly.

gen1: dotted panels dressed with hole-matched shapes.

Scene: a block of touching solid panels (2-4, sizes 6-8), each pierced
by 1-4 field-colored dots (pairwise separated so each is its own
enclosed hole); loose filled rectangles with the matching number of
enclosed holes sit isolated on the field. Transform: output the panel
block with each panel refilled solid and its count-matched shape pasted
centered, holes showing the panel color.

gen1: UPSCALE by an integer factor (ratios 2..5, fixed per task, varied
across tasks). Output = each input cell expanded to a factor x factor block.
Program: (upscale g F). A different random colored field per pair; the shared
rule is "blow up by F".

gen2: DOWNSCALE by an integer factor (ratios 2..5). The input is a
block-uniform field (each factor x factor block a single color); the rule
collapses each block to one cell. Program: (downscale g F). This is the
"downsize" task — big blocky input -> small output.

gen3: NON-UNIFORM scale — each row repeated by a per-row ratio and each
column by a per-col ratio (various ratios 1..3, fixed per task). Program:
(scale-map g (list row-ratios...) (list col-ratios...)). All pairs in a task
share input dims so the same ratio lists apply; content varies. Covers
asymmetric/stretch resizes (different vertical vs horizontal blow-up).

gen1: shape progressions + gray-bracket window, two shape families.

Scene: n=3-5 shapes march along one axis with constant gap and affine
sizes, anchored on a shared top/bottom line, colored by a 2-3 color
cycle. Families: PERIODIC TOWERS (constant width, unit rows tiled i+base
times, optional cap row) and GROWING ARMS (t-like: spine column full
height, full rows at fixed anchor-distances, width and height +1 per
step). Two gray corner brackets frame the bbox (or a row-crop of it) of
the NEXT element (or the one BEFORE the first); output = its content.
Vertical variants transpose the whole scene. Scenes resample until the
detector's output equals the intended construction.

gen1: sidebar-recipe stamp scenes.

Scene: 1-2 sidebars (5 wide, magenta-walled) each holding a 2-color 3x3
swatch, a 1-color glyph (rows 4-11), a corner dot in the first box and a
2-cell rotation bar in the second; the field carries simple stripes or
blobs. Transform: stamp each glyph x3, textured with the swapped swatch
(block-local phase), rotated per the bar, anchored at the dot's corner.

gen1: slotted template + scattered shape vote.

Scene: a big tc-colored rectangle on a bg field, pierced by 3-8 slots
drawn from 2-4 shape classes (dot / bar2 / bar3 / L3 / square / T4 / Z4 /
plus / bracket5 — pairwise distinct under D8). Outside its bbox, each
used class scatters in 2+ colors with one strictly-modal color; slots may
be any D8 orientation of their class. Transform: crop the template bbox
and recolor every slot to its class's modal scattered color.

Read the novel-color mask inside the anomalous tile motif, align that mask uniquely to the partially anomalous tile positions, and complete the same mask at tile scale while leaving separator lines unchanged.

Generate panel sequences whose oriented cursor consumes an aligned route.

Inspired by supplied evaluation task 5545f144.  Each input contains two or
three equal panels separated by a full-height color column.  A three-cell arrow
advances through a nested, shrinking set of singleton waypoints.  Consecutive
waypoints share exactly one row or column, while every nonconsecutive pair has
different row and column coordinates.  The output is the next clean state:
the arrow at the final waypoint, oriented along the final leg.

Generate ordered two-color cursors that consume an aligned waypoint route.

This second 5545f144-inspired family preserves the panel-sequence and
waypoint semantics of gen1 while replacing the geometric three-cell arrow
with a typed head/tail domino.  The head color is identified by its repeated
singleton waypoints; the tail color records orientation.  This forces color
role and relative-vector reasoning instead of the gen1 tip-shape shortcut.

gen1: donor window's icon transplanted onto receiver window's markers.

Scene: a striped field (1-wide stripes, adjacent colors differ) carries
two 1-thick framed windows. The DONOR holds 2-3 copies of a multicolor
icon (body color + exactly one anchor-colored cell); the RECEIVER holds
2-4 single cells of the anchor color. Transform: crop the receiver window
(frame included) and expand every marker into the full icon, aligned on
the icon's anchor cell. Scenes resample until the detector's output
equals the intended construction.
